reports.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
reports.description: Official consumer price index measuring changes in the prices of a basket of goods and services. Released on a regular cadence and used as the primary domestic inflation measure.

reports.title: National Accounts (GDP)
reports.description: Official national accounts estimates of gross domestic product and related aggregates, covering both oil and non-oil activity.

reports.title: Monthly Statistical Bulletin — Banking & Monetary Statistics
reports.description: Monthly compilation of monetary aggregates (M1, M2, M3), central-bank assets and liabilities, gross international reserves, bank deposits, credit and related banking indicators.

reports.title: Population estimates
reports.description: Official population estimates for the UAE, reflecting the large non-national component of the resident population. Most recently reported at approximately 11.3 million (2024) — earlier batch drafts using a ~10 million figure are stale.

reports.title: Balance of Payments
reports.description: Official balance-of-payments statistics compiled according to BPM6, covering the current, capital and financial accounts.

reports.title: Education statistics (general and higher education)

reports.title: Health services statistics

reports.title: CBUAE Base Rate decisions (Overnight Deposit Facility)
reports.description: Policy interest-rate decisions for the Base Rate applicable to the Overnight Deposit Facility. The rate is anchored to the US Federal Reserve's Interest Rate on Reserve Balances (IORB) and signals the monetary-policy stance under the dirham peg. VERIFIED: multiple 2026 reports confirm CBUAE explicitly holds/moves the Base Rate 'following Fed decision.'

reports.title: IMF Article IV Consultation — United Arab Emirates
reports.description: Annual IMF Article IV consultation staff report and press release assessing UAE macroeconomic conditions, fiscal and monetary policy. VERIFIED real and current: 2025 Article IV Consultation staff report published December 2025; a follow-up staff visit concluded July 2026. Useful both as a real recurring node and as an independent cross-check source for UAE national statistics — completely absent from all 10 batches despite this pattern (an IMF programme/consultation node) already existing for other countries in this project.

dependencies.basis: WAM (UAE's own state news agency) and OPEC's continued MOMR publication both frame the exit as a change in OPEC/OPEC+ composition that the MOMR's ongoing market analysis must account for.
The UAE's departure is explicitly framed by multiple outlets (CFR, Al Jazeera) as an exit from both OPEC and the OPEC+ Declaration of Cooperation framework, not just OPEC membership alone.
The MOMR's supply-side analysis is structured around OPEC+ production-adjustment decisions made under the Declaration of Cooperation framework.
VAT and corporate tax collection are the primary tax-revenue input to the consolidated government finance statistics.
IMF Article IV consultations are built on the member country's own official national accounts data as the primary input to the Fund's macroeconomic assessment.
IMF Article IV inflation assessments are built on the member country's official CPI series.
Overnight visitor arrivals to Dubai are structurally downstream of air-passenger arrivals at DXB, the emirate's dominant entry point.

reports.title: Federal Competitiveness and Statistics Centre (FCSC) institutional core
reports.description: Primary federal statistical office responsible for national accounts, prices, demographic, social and multi-domain statistics, and coordination with emirate-level statistical centres.
reports._notes: Foundational institutional node for the UAE federal statistical system.
reports._cadence_evidence: fcsc.gov.ae is a dataset portal: subjects are catalogued with coverage ranges (Annual National Accounts 2010-2025, CPI 2008-2025, Births 1976-2024, Air Transport 2014-2025, Climate January 2016-December 2024) rather than as issues. The site publishes no release calendar; the only schedule statement is that data 'will be updated following the official release of the review results' of the ongoing GDP review.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7) and applied 2026-08-19: a nominal releases_per_year so that absence keeps meaning 'one-off instrument' only - 250 encodes business-day updating (the live corpus's daily-FX convention), 365 genuinely all-days monitoring. It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

reports.title: Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE) institutional and reporting core
reports.description: Central bank responsible for monetary policy, the dirham peg, foreign-exchange reserves management, banking supervision and key macro-financial and external statistics. Publishes monetary, banking, BOP and related series.
reports._notes: Central-bank institutional counterpart to FCSC. Dirham peg is the monetary anchor.
reports._cadence_evidence: CBUAE site lists its reporting stack by frequency: monthly Statistical Bulletin (banking and monetary statistics), monthly 'Monetary & Banking Developments' summary and banking-operations statistics; quarterly 'UAE Monetary, Banking & Financial Markets Developments', Quarterly Economic Review and Credit Sentiment Survey; annual Central Bank Annual Report (2025 report issued April 2026) and Financial Stability Report. Monthly is the governing cadence.

reports.title: Labour force and expatriate employment statistics
reports.description: Labour-force and employment statistics by citizenship. The workforce is overwhelmingly non-national; Emiratisation policies and private-sector localisation targets are continuously tracked alongside overall employment and participation.
reports._notes: Core labour-market densification under expatriate-majority structure.
reports._url_evidence: FCSC page titled '2024, 2023, ... 2008 - Labor Force', the official UAE labour force statistics series.
reports._cadence_evidence: The FCSC labour-force document page title enumerates per-year documents: 2024, 2023, 2022, 2021, 2020, 2019, 2018, 2017, 2016, 2009, 2008; FCSC's subject index lists it as 'Labour Force 2008 - 2024'. One statistical document per reference year.

reports.title: Loi n° 11-10 du 22 juin 2011 relative à la commune
reports.description: Algeria's Communal Code, verified via direct download from the Journal Officiel (joradp.dz, N°37, 3 juillet 2011) and cross-checked against a FAOLEX mirror. Art. 173: "Les dotations financières d'équipement au titre des concours de l'Etat, du budget de wilaya ou du fonds commun des collectivités locales et autres subventions sont grevées d'affectation spéciale" — the first primary-text naming of the "fonds commun des collectivités locales" (FCCL) at commune level. Art. 195 repeats the FCCL naming for both operating- and investment-section revenue. Art. 211-212 establish the commune-level EQUALISATION mechanism, legally distinct from the wilaya-level Art. 176-179 fund already in corpus: "les communes disposent de deux fonds : — le fonds communal de solidarité ; — le fonds de garantie des collectivités locales", with Art. 212 specifying "une attribution annuelle de péréquation destinée à la section de fonctionnement du budget communal." No percentage/formula is given — implementing 'modalités' are left to a décret not independently located. Art. 188 confirms the internal 'compte administratif' adoption procedure exists in law, though it does not mandate public online disclosure. NAMING CAUTION: the fund is called "fonds commun des collectivités locales" here (2011), but "Caisse de solidarité et de garantie des collectivités locales / CSGCL" in the 2025/2026 Finance Laws' own annex tables, and "Fonds de solidarité et de garantie des collectivités locales / FSGCL" in the 2025 Finance Law's own renaming article (Art. 125) — these all appear to refer to the same Treasury special-allocation account (n°302-020, per dz-loi-finances-2025-etat-e), not three separate funds, but the naming is genuinely inconsistent across primary texts over time.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument.

reports.title: Loi n° 24-08 du 24 novembre 2024 portant loi de finances pour 2025 — État « E »: Liste des impôts et autres impositions et leurs produits affectés à l'État et aux collectivités locales
reports.description: Algeria's 2025 annual Finance Law, État 'E' annex — verified via direct download from joradp.dz (Journal Officiel N°84, 26 December 2024). This is the strongest finding of the whole round: an official annex table giving EXACT per-tax percentage formulas splitting revenue between État, Commune, Wilaya, and 'CSGCL' (the local-solidarity fund), together with real DA-denominated 2025 revenue projections attributed by name to the Commune column. Verbatim: "TVA intérieure - Hors DGE — 75% [Etat et fonds] / 10% [Commune] / — [Wilaya] / 15% [CSGCL] / 100% [Total]. Prévisions de réalisation 2025: 139 776 654 302 [Etat] / 18 636 887 240 [Commune] / — / 27 955 330 860 [CSGCL] / 186 368 872 403 [Total]." "Taxe sur les produits pétroliers TPP — 66% [Commune] / 29% [Wilaya] / 5% [CSGCL] / 100%. Prévisions de réalisation 2025: 128 852 877 110 [Commune] / 56 617 173 276 [Wilaya] / 9 761 581 599 [CSGCL] / 195 231 631 985 [Total]." Section I total across all Etat/Commune/Wilaya/CSGCL-split taxes for 2025: Commune column alone totals 139 393 198 977 DA. Art. 67 (taxe annuelle d'habitation, as amended): "Le produit de cette taxe est affecté, comme suit : • 50% aux communes ; • 50% aux wilayas." Art. 221 defines the operative Treasury mechanism: "Le compte d'affectation spécial n° 302-020 est intitulé « Fonds de solidarité et de garantie des collectivités locales. »", with recettes including "la contribution annuelle des communes et des wilayas" and dépenses including "des attributions de péréquation." État 'D' (special-account balances) shows the fund's balance at 376 944 433 056 DA as of 31/12/2023. The identical 'Soutien aux collectivités locales' État B budget line (620 696 272 000 DA for 2025) is corroborated by a companion implementing decree, Décret exécutif n°25-14 du 9 janvier 2025.
reports.cadence_note: Annual finance law; this edition is for FY2025 (see dz-loi-finances-2026-etat-e for the recurring FY2026 edition).

reports.title: Loi n° 25-17 du 14 décembre 2025 portant loi de finances pour 2026 — État « E »
reports.description: The FY2026 edition of the same État 'E' mechanism as dz-loi-finances-2025-etat-e, confirming it is a stable, recurring annual budget structure rather than a one-off — verified via direct download from joradp.dz (Journal Officiel N°88, 31 December 2025). Same formulas repeated with updated 2026 figures: "TVA intérieure-Hors DGE 75% [Etat et fonds] / 10% [Commune] / — [Wilaya] / 15% [CSGCL] / 100%. Prévisions de réalisation 2026: 170 102 250 000 [Etat] / 22 680 300 000 [Commune]..."; Section I total for 2026: Commune column 57 108 534 776 DA. TPP formula (66% Commune / 29% Wilaya / 5% CSGCL) repeated with 2026 figures: 138 600 000 000 DA to communes. État 'D' shows the special-account balance DECREASED year-over-year: 330 284 806 136,42 DA as of 31/12/2024 (down from 376.9bn a year earlier) — outflows exceeded inflows in 2024. État B's 'Soutien aux collectivités locales' line rose to 659 825 000 000 DA for 2026 (from 620.7bn in 2025). reports.title: Lei n.º 15/17 de 8 de Agosto de 2017 — Lei Orgânica do Poder Local
reports.description: Angola's organic law establishing autarquias locais (decentralized local authorities) — genuinely distinct from ao-lei-administracao-local-15-16's deconcentrated state-administration framework. Verified via OCR of the scanned Diário da República I Série N.º 134 (8 August 2017), hosted by FAOLEX. Art. 22 (Princípio da Autonomia Financeira e Patrimonial): "1. Os órgãos autónomos do Poder Local gozam de plena liberdade de decisão e gestão dos recursos financeiros e do seu património nos termos da Constituição e da lei. 2. Os recursos financeiros das Autarquias Locais devem ser proporcionais às atribuições previstas pela Constituição ou por lei... 3. A lei estabelece que uma parte dos recursos financeiros das Autarquias Locais deve ser proveniente de rendimentos e de impostos locais." Art. 30(2) mandates direct election: "A Assembleia da Autarquia é composta por representantes locais, eleitos por sufrágio universal, livre, directo, secreto e periódico." CRITICALLY, Art. 41 (Princípio do Gradualismo e da Transitoriedade) makes actual rollout contingent on further state action, not automatic: "A institucionalização efectiva das Autarquias Locais obedece ao Princípio do Gradualismo" — "consiste na faculdade dos órgãos competentes do Estado determinarem por lei a oportunidade da sua criação." This gradualism clause is the textual root of why, per ao-lei-13-20-regime-financeiro-autarquias's own dropped note below, no operational autarquia has yet been activated.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument.

reports.title: Lei n.º 13/20 de 14 de Maio de 2020 — Regime Financeiro das Autarquias Locais
reports.description: Angola's implementing financial law for autarquias — the 'lei própria' Art. 22(5) of Lei 15/17 deferred to. Verified via OCR of the scanned Diário da República I Série N.º 64 (14 May 2020). Art. 12(1) lists own-source revenue: property/urban-land taxes (Imposto Predial Urbano, Imposto de Sisa, Taxa de Circulação), licence/service fees, and tariffs. Art. 14 gives the concrete transfer formula: "3. Os recursos do Fundo das Autarquias Locais são as receitas provenientes do correspondente a 20% da receita prevista no Orçamento Geral do Estado, resultante da cobrança dos impostos seguintes: a) Imposto sobre o Rendimento do Trabalho por conta própria; b) ...por conta de outrem; c) Imposto Industrial [excluding diamonds/minerals]; d) Imposto sobre as Sucessões e Doações; e) Imposto sobre a Aplicação de Capitais" — 20% of five named central tax lines, based on "a receita líquida observada para aqueles impostos nos últimos três anos" (a 3-year trailing average). Art. 16 creates the Fundo de Equilíbrio das Autarquias Locais (FEAL), administered by the Finance Ministry, with three sub-accounts: Art. 17(2) "Constituem receitas da SEF 50% do valor das receitas definidas no artigo 14.º"; Art. 18(2) SEA gets 30%; Art. 19(2) SSA gets 20% — i.e. a 50/30/20 internal FEAL split. This is a real, specific, quantitative transfer mechanism (Angola's actual term is 'Fundo das Autarquias Locais'/'FEAL', not 'Fundo de Apoio Municipal' as one might expect by analogy to other countries).
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, implementing Lei n.º 15/17.

reports.title: Lei n.º 15/16 — Lei da Administração Local do Estado
reports.description: Angola's Law on Local State Administration. Article 21 states that provincial budgeting "está sujeita às normas em vigor que disciplinam... o Orçamento Geral do Estado" [is subject to the rules in force governing... the General State Budget] — provincial budgets are legally subordinate to, not independent of, the national OGE. Provincial governors are presidentially appointed (Constitution Art. 119(k)/125(4)), confirmed via decree citations for governor appointments as recent as 2025; Angola has never held local/autárquicas elections (a 2020 presidential quote — "Não se adiam eleições que nunca foram convocadas" [elections that were never called cannot be postponed] — and 2025-era news both confirm this remains the case). This corrects an earlier assumption in this branch's own research brief that Angola held provincial elections in 2025.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument.

reports.title: Loi n°041/98/AN du 6 août 1998 portant Organisation de l'Administration du Territoire au Burkina Faso
reports.description: Burkina Faso's 1998 decentralization predecessor law, verified via a FAOLEX mirror. Art. 96: "Le budget est proposé par l'organe exécutif de la collectivité locale, voté par le conseil et approuvé par l'autorité de tutelle." Art. 99: "Les recettes ordinaires des collectivités locales proviennent du produit des recettes fiscales, de l'exploitation du domaine et des services locaux." Art. 100: "Les collectivités locales disposent d'une compétence générale en matière de détermination des tarifs ou taxes rémunératoires du domaine et des services locaux." Art. 101: "Les fonds de dotation des collectivités locales prévus par la présente loi reçoivent un montant déterminé lors de l'adoption des lois de finances annuelles." This law was itself superseded by Loi n°055-2004/AN portant Code Général des Collectivités Territoriales (2004, amended 2018 per Loi n°012-2018/AN, confirmed via the Assemblée Nationale's own current legislative-text page), which was in turn replaced by the new code adopted 30 December 2025 (bf-alt-cgct-2025-adoption). Documents that commune-level fiscal/budget provisions have existed continuously in Burkinabè law since at least 1998, across three successive codes.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, superseded (2004, then again 2025).

reports.title: Alliance des États du Sahel : vers la création d'une Confédération
reports.description: Burkina Faso's own Ministry of Finance, in its own voice (article dated 19 February 2024, verified via raw HTML extraction), discussing both the ECOWAS withdrawal and the move toward Confederation: "élaborer un traité portant création de la confédération des Etats du Sahel"; "retrait sans délai de ces trois pays de la CEDEAO, le 28 janvier dernier"; "dénoncé les sanctions de la CEDEAO à l'encontre des pays en Transition. reports.title: Loi n°055-2004/AN du 21 décembre 2004 portant Code Général des Collectivités Territoriales au Burkina Faso
reports.description: The 2004 predecessor collectivités code — already cited by number/title inside bf-decret-2007-254-fpdct (which states FPDCT was "créé par l'article 141 de la loi n°055-2004/AN") and bf-loi-041-1998-administration-territoire's own description, but its own text was NOT independently retrieved in AF/G.18. Independently located and confirmed this round (AF/G.21, processing a import-supplied lead) via NATLEX's own PDF (a print-capture of Burkina Faso's official legal portal legiburkina.bf, page footers reading legiburkina.bf/Sommaires_JO/Loi_2004_00055.htm, header reading "JO SPECIAL N°02 DU 20 AVRIL 2005" — effectively the official gazette text), downloaded and independently parsed with pdftotext, not just an AI-summarized fetch. Article 1: "La présente loi établit le code général des collectivités territoriales au Burkina Faso. Le code général des collectivités territoriales détermine l'orientation de la décentralisation, les compétences et moyens d'action, les organes et l'administration des collectivités territoriales." Full document confirmed complete (Articles 1-338, ending with the enactment formula "Ainsi fait et délibéré en séance publique à Ouagadougou, le 21 décembre 2004," signed by Roch Marc Christian Kaboré as Président de l'Assemblée). Titre II ("Des moyens financiers des collectivités territoriales"), Articles 106-121, gives the municipal-finance detail this branch looks for: Art. 110 states resources come "soit par transfert de fiscalité, soit par dotations, soit par les deux à la fois"; Art. 115 lists ordinary revenue sources including "la répartition annuelle des fonds de dotation des collectivités territoriales"; and Art. 117 is the direct statutory root of the 2007 FPDCT decree: "Les fonds de dotation des collectivités territoriales prévus par la présente loi reçoivent un montant déterminé lors de l'adoption des lois de finances annuelles. Les fonds de dotation sont gérés conformément aux dispositions du régime financier des collectivités territoriales. Les modalités de répartition des fonds de dotation sont fixées chaque année par arrêté conjoint du ministre chargé des collectivités territoriales et du ministre chargé des finances." CAVEAT: this NATLEX copy is the 2005 vintage as originally promulgated — it does NOT reflect the 2018 amendment (Loi n°012-2018/AN) referenced elsewhere in this corpus; the amended/consolidated text was not independently retrieved this round (a droit-afrique.com mirror returned HTTP 403 on all attempts). Superseded in full by the new code adopted 30 December 2025 (bf-alt-cgct-2025-adoption).

reports.title: Loi n°1/16 du 25 mai 2015 portant modalités de transfert de compétences de l'Etat aux communes
reports.publisher: Présidence de la République du Burundi
reports.description: Burundi's organic law on the transfer of state competencies to communes. Directly verified via downloaded PDF (pdftotext extraction, OCR-degraded scan cross-checked against INSBU's own clean Annuaire Statistique citation, both agreeing on law number and date). Article 34: "Tout transfert de compétences par l'Etat à la commune s'accompagne du transfert des ressources nécessaires à l'exercice de ces compétences" [Any transfer of competencies by the State to the commune is accompanied by a transfer of the resources necessary to exercise those competencies]. Article 35: "Les ressources financières nécessaires à la commune pour l'exercice de ses compétences lui sont dévolues soit par transfert de fiscalité, soit par dotations ou par les deux à la fois... Le niveau des dotations est fixé chaque année par la loi des finances" [The financial resources a commune needs are devolved via tax transfer, grants, or both; grant levels are set annually by the finance law]. Article 36 creates a communal support fund ("fonds d'appui aux communes"). STRUCTURAL CAVEAT: this governs Burundi's 18 communes, not its provinces directly — provinces are deconcentrated administration (governor-led per Constitution Art. 143-151), not a distinct fiscal tier with their own budget, per Constitution Art. 269 ("The commune as well as other local collectivities... are created by organic law").
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument.

reports.title: Constituição da República de Cabo Verde (2ª Revisão Ordinária, 2010) — Artigos 230 e 233
reports.description: Cabo Verde is a unitary state organised into 22 municipalities (concelhos) with NO intermediate provincial/regional tier — the closest available fiscal-transfer tier is national-to-municipal. Article 233: "As autarquias locais têm património próprio e finanças autónomas, nos termos da lei" [Local authorities have their own patrimony and autonomous finances, under the terms of the law]. Article 230 separately defines autarquias locais as decentralised public entities with political, administrative and financial autonomy.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument.

reports.title: Lei n.º 79/VI/2005, de 5 de Setembro — Regime Financeiro das Autarquias Locais
reports.description: UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF lead-chase round, resolving AF/G.23's open FFM-rate caveat below): CONFIRMED the FFM rate remains 10%, NOT raised to 15%. The only law amending Lei n.º 79/VI/2005 since the 2019 15% proposal is Lei n.º 52/X/2025, de 17 de abril (Boletim Oficial I Série n.º 30, 17-04-2025; index https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/View?id=84886, download https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/DownloadAct?id=84886), enacted and in force since 18-04-2025. Its own text ("É alterado o artigo 6.º da Lei n.º 79/VI/2005... Artigo 32.º Norma revogatória — É revogada a Lei n.º 24/VIII/2013") shows it amends only Article 6 (municipal fee-charging powers, adding an exemption for electricity distributors that now pay a separate "renda especial") and revokes an unrelated law; it does not mention "FFM" or "Fundo de Financiamento dos Municípios" anywhere in its full 18-page text, leaving Article 10 §3 (the 10%-of-tax-revenue FFM formula, documented below) untouched. Corroborating context (not itself dispositive, since budget laws never restate the underlying percentage): the enacted FY2026 state budget, Lei n.º 69/X/2025, de 31 de dezembro (OE2026; Boletim Oficial I Série n.º 133, 1.º Suplemento, 31-12-2025; minted separately as cv-oe2026-budget in cv-leadchase-ffm-status.json), Artigo 13.º "Fundo de Financiamento dos Municípios", fixes the FFM at "5.387.079.168$00 CVE" for 2026 as an absolute amount only (standard budget-law drafting practice) — a figure consistent with, not contradictory to, continued 10%-of-tax-revenue math and with Olavo Correia's own June 2025 projection that the fund "ultrapassará os 5 milhões de contos em 2026" (quoted below). Both pending-revision instruments discussed below (the 2019 proposal to raise the rate to 15%, and the separate "novo Regime Financeiro dos Municípios"/"Lei de Base do Orçamento Municipal") remain unenacted as of the most recent primary statement located (governo.cv, 12 June 2025; see cv-g23-municipal.json's updated entry for the fuller quote) — that sweep of the 2025-2026 Boletim Oficial was not exhaustive, so a future round could still re-check for a later enactment. — Cabo Verde's national municipal finance law, distinct from the constitutional autarquias provisions in cv-constitution-autarquias. Full primary text located (AF/G.23) at the Assembleia Municipal da Praia's own document repository, after a prior round (AF/G.17) could only corroborate it via secondary sources. Preamble: "Por mandato do Povo, a Assembleia Nacional decreta, nos termos da alínea b) do artigo 174º da Constituição, o seguinte" — i.e. this law cites the Constitution's Article 174(b) (general National Assembly legislative-competence clause), NOT Article 230/233 (the autarquias-autonomy articles already covered by cv-constitution-autarquias), so no dependency edge is drawn to that node (see _dropped note). Article 1: "A presente lei estabelece o regime financeiro das autarquias locais." Article 10 creates the Fundo de Financiamento dos Municípios (FFM) and sets it at "10% do valor dos impostos directos e indirectos efectivamente cobrados no penúltimo ano anterior àquele a que o Orçamento se refere" (10% of direct and indirect state taxes — IUR, IVA, ICE, Imposto de Selo, Direitos Aduaneiros — actually collected two years prior), split "75% Para o Fundo Municipal Comum (FMC); 25% Para o Fundo de Solidariedade Municipal (FSM)". Article 11 sets the FMC's own internal distribution across all 22 municípios: "20% Repartidos igualmente por todos os Municípios; 50% Repartidos na razão directa da população residente de cada Município; 15% Repartidos na razão directa da população infanto-juvenil residente, dos zero aos dezassete anos, de cada Município; 15% Repartidos na razão directa da superfície do território de cada Município." Article 12 (FSM) targets poorer municípios via a fiscal-insufficiency/poverty formula ("CF = Pm*(Cni-Cmi)") and Article 12(2) restricts FSM eligibility to municípios "à luz dos critérios estabelecidos pelo Instituto Nacional de Estatística" — a real citation of INE, but of INE's poverty-statistics criteria generally, not of the CPI report specifically, so also not linked as an edge to cv-ine-ipc (see _dropped note). UPDATE (AF/G.23): a 21 August 2019 Council of Ministers press release on the Government's own site (governo.cv) states a draft bill would raise the FFM share "dos 10% atuais para 15%" and that "o FFM esteve 14 anos sem qualquer alteração, situação nunca antes verificada desde a Independência Nacional" — corroborating the 2005 origin of the 10% figure. A later governo.cv press release (12 June 2025), quoting Vice-Prime Minister/Minister of Finance Olavo Correia, states it remains "urgente aprovar ... o novo Regime Financeiro dos Municípios" — i.e., as of mid-2025 the government's own language still treats a comprehensive revision as pending, so the operative FFM rate cannot be confirmed at 15% rather than the original 10% text found on ampraia.cv; flagged as an open TENSE/current-rate caveat rather than resolved. The same June 2025 release states the FFM "respondeu por 32,8 M contos" of the ~42,6 million contos transferred to municípios January 2016-May 2025, growing at "4% ao ano" and projected to "ultrapassar[á] os 5 milhões de contos em 2026" — aggregate, not per-município, figures.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument (with at least one documented 2019 amendment proposal and, per a 2025 ministerial statement, a further revision still pending as of mid-2025).

Too weak to satisfy the branch's citation standard; not force-linked. The same ENDE document does contain a substantive sentence naming ECOWAS (CEDEAO) as a sub-regional funding source, but that is about project financing, not statistical methodology, so also not minted as an edge.

The same ENDE 2022-2026 document states Cabo Verde had NOT ratified the African Charter on Statistics as of 2022 ("Não ratificação da CAE pelo país") — recorded as a negative finding for future reference, matching the pattern used for Sudan and Comoros this same round.

SUPERSEDED 2026-08-13 (AF/G.23) — see below. A national Local Government Finance Law (Lei n.º 79/VI/2005, "Lei das Finanças Locais") was corroborated by two independent secondary sources (a UCLG country profile, and an "Estatuto dos Municípios" PDF) as establishing a two-fund municipal transfer mechanism (Fundo Municipal Comum, 75%, and Fundo de Solidariedade Municipal, 25%) — but the primary text of the law itself could not be located that round despite multiple targeted FAOLEX searches, all of which returned unrelated Cabo Verdean laws. AF/G.23 subsequently located the full primary text (hosted by the Assembleia Municipal da Praia, not FAOLEX or the Boletim Oficial's own site) and minted it as report node cv-lei-financas-locais-79-2005; the original secondary-source figures (75%/25% split) are independently confirmed correct by the primary text's own Article 10(4).

Lei n.º 79/VI/2005's own preamble cites the Constitution, but specifically Article 174(b) (the National Assembly's general legislative-competence clause: "a Assembleia Nacional decreta, nos termos da alínea b) do artigo 174º da Constituição") — not Articles 230/233 (the autarquias-autonomy provisions that cv-constitution-autarquias documents). Per this branch's standing rule against assuming a topical match constitutes the same citation, no dependency edge is drawn between these two nodes; recorded as a note only since no edge actually exists in the `dependencies` array.

Lei n.º 79/VI/2005 Article 12(2) restricts Fundo de Solidariedade Municipal (FSM) eligibility to municípios meeting poverty criteria "estabelecidos pelo Instituto Nacional de Estatística" — a genuine, substantive citation of INE, but of INE's general poverty-statistics criteria, not of the Índice de Preços no Consumidor (CPI) that cv-ine-ipc specifically documents. Structurally the same situation as the AFRISTAT-acronym-glossary near-miss noted elsewhere in this file: a real agency mention that does not correspond to the specific report already in corpus, so not force-linked. No edge exists in `dependencies`; recorded as a note only.

reports.title: Loi n°2019/024 du 24 décembre 2019 portant Code Général des Collectivités Territoriales Décentralisées (CGCTD)
reports.publisher: Ministère de la Décentralisation et du Développement Local (MINDDEVEL) / Assemblée Nationale du Cameroun
reports.description: Cameroon's general decentralization code, verified by direct PDF download and full-text extraction (123 pages, 501 articles). Art. 11(1): "Les Collectivités Territoriales disposent de budgets et de ressources propres...elles: élaborent et votent librement leur budget; disposent de ressources propres." Art. 12: resources come "soit par transfert de fiscalité, soit par dotations, soit par les deux à la fois." Art. 25(1)-(3) creates a state-wide transfer floor: "Il est institué une Dotation Générale de la Décentralisation destinée au financement partiel de la décentralisation...La fraction [des recettes de l'Etat]...ne peut être inférieure à quinze pour cent (15%)." Art. 26-27 mandate fiscal compensation for any new unfunded competence transferred to a CTD. Art. 168(10) gives municipal councils rate-setting power "dans le respect des fourchettes arrêtées par la loi." Art. 390-392 taxonomizes commune-level own-source revenue as "impôts locaux" (impôts communaux, centimes additionnels communaux, taxes communales, impôts et taxes des Régions). KEY FINDING — Art. 240 establishes the Communauté Urbaine (CU) as a collectivité of at least two constituent "communes d'arrondissement," and Art. 395-396 mandates a legally-required INTRA-CITY transfer from the CU down to its communes d'arrondissement: "Une dotation générale de fonctionnement est allouée aux communes d'arrondissement par la Communauté Urbaine de rattachement...indexée sur certaines recettes de la Communauté Urbaine," with implementing modalities delegated to ministerial arrêté (not independently located). FEICOM is confirmed ABSENT from this law's entire 501-article text (verified by full-text grep): the only incidental appearance of "péréquation" is Art. 454(2), a generic treasury-operations clause, not a FEICOM-specific provision.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument.

reports.title: FEICOM — Code d'Intervention du FEICOM (C.I.F.) and institutional self-description
reports.publisher: FEICOM (Fonds Spécial d'Equipement et d'Intervention Intercommunale)
reports.description: FEICOM's own site and its 'observatoire' regulatory-documents subdomain, verified via raw HTML extraction. Legal lineage, in FEICOM's own voice: "le Fonds Spécial d'Equipement et d'Intervention Intercommunale (FEICOM) a été créé par la loi n°74/23 du 05 décembre 1974 portant organisation communale au Cameroun et rendue opératoire par le décret d'application n°77/85 du 22 mars 1997," reorganized several times, "la dernière étant intervenue le 31 octobre 2018, suite au Décret présidentiel N°2018/635." Mission, in FEICOM's own words: "Le FEICOM centralise et procède à la redistribution des impôts et taxes régionaux soumis à péréquation...Le FEICOM met à la disposition des régions, des communes...les quotes-parts correspondantes de la Dotation générale de la décentralisation arrêtée par le gouvernement." 2025 year-end aggregate, from the Director General's own message: "nous avons mobilisé 235,749 milliards de FCFA...177,7 milliards de FCFA redistribués aux communes camerounaises...214 concours financiers accordés à 154 Communes et Régions." FEICOM's own Code d'Intervention (C.I.F.) gives the closest thing to a transfer FORMULA it publishes — not a uniform block-transfer percentage, but project-category-specific splits between commune own-contribution / solidarity-contribution / loan: social projects Art.18 ("l'apport en ressources définitives...est de 10%; la contribution de solidarité est de 60%"), non-revenue social projects Art.20 ("l'apport...est de 10%; la contribution de solidarité est de 90%"), operating loans Art.22 ("le prêt est de 100%"). A separate PACARF programme caps low-revenue-commune support: "un montant n'excédant pas 2% de son budget d'investissements communaux."
reports.cadence_note: Standing regulatory instrument (Code d'Intervention) plus a recurring annual institutional report (the Director General's year-end message).

dependencies.basis: FEICOM's own 'À propos' page states its redistribution role puts "à la disposition des régions, des communes...les quotes-parts correspondantes de la Dotation générale de la décentralisation arrêtée par le gouvernement" — directly referencing the Dotation Générale de la Décentralisation that Loi n°2019/024 Art. 25 creates and sets at a minimum 15% floor. FEICOM is the disbursing conduit for a mechanism the CGCTD legally establishes, even though FEICOM itself (as an institution) is not created or governed by that law.

The only relationship the two documents share is that FEICOM disburses a mechanism (DGD) the CGCTD creates — captured as the 'cites' dependency above, in the opposite direction.

reports.title: Loi de Finances pour l'exercice 2025
reports.publisher: Ministère des Finances et du Budget (République Centrafricaine)
reports.description: CAR's FY2025 budget law, downloaded directly from the Ministry of Finance and Budget's own site (155MB scanned PDF, 608 pages, no embedded text — OCR'd in full this round). Total budget (Art. 35, page numbered 16 in-document): "1- Ressources : 345 200 000 000 FCFA ... 2- Charges : 365 917 975 000 FCFA", with Art. 36 declaring a deficit of "20 717 975 000 de FCFA". Art. 31 repeals the prior commune tax-sharing mechanism, which had explicitly split shares between "a- Commune de Bangui" and "b- Autres Communes" (citing "l'article 85 de la Loi de Finances 2003, modifiant et complétant les dispositions l'article 25 de la loi de Finances Rectificative de 2001"), replacing it with a discretionary system: Art. 32 "Les communes et les autres unités administratives bénéficient des subventions dans les limites des crédits ouverts dans le Budget Général de l'Etat", with Art. 34 delegating practical modalities to "Un arrêté du Ministre des Finances et du Budget". Under Ministry 14 (Ministère de l'Administration du Territoire, de la Décentralisation et du Développement Local), budget line 14.00.00.00.390000 "Dépenses non-reparties des administrations territoriales" (Titre IV, Dépenses de transfert, 1 506 000 thousand FCFA for 2025) itemizes named transfers: "Transferts aux conseils généraux des préfectures" (75 000, code .6423.11, -16.67% vs 2024), "Transferts aux conseils généraux des sous-préfectures" (51 000, code .6424.11, +34.21%), "Transferts aux conseils généraux des quartiers et villages" (200 000, code .6426.11) annotated in the source table as "Appui à la Mairie de Bangui", "Transferts aux conseils généraux des régions" (900 000, code .6422.11) annotated "Appui aux autres Communes", and "Autres transferts aux collectivités locales" (280 000, code .6429.11). NOTE: the pairing of the descriptive labels "Appui à la Mairie de Bangui" / "Appui aux autres Communes" with specific coded lines is the source PDF's own table layout (each amount line is immediately followed on the next row by a plain-text sub-label); read literally the labels sit under the quartiers/villages and régions lines respectively, but this may be an artifact of the two-row cell format rather than a precise 1:1 amount attribution — flagged as an interpretive caveat rather than resolved. Separately, and unambiguously, all sixteen of CAR's prefectures are individually named with FY2025 operating budgets under Ministry 40 (Éducation Nationale), as "Inspection Académique de [prefecture]" lines (pages numbered 312-317 in-document), each budgeted at 3 500 thousand FCFA for 2025: Ombella M'poko, Lobaye, Mambéré Kadéï, Mambéré, Sangha Mbaéré, Nana Mambéré, Ouham, Ouham Fafa, Ouham Pendé, Kémo, Nana Gribizi, Ouaka, Haute Kotto, Vakaga, Bamingui Bangoran, Mbomou, Basse Kotto, Haut Mbomou (one entry, OCR'd as "Inspection Académique de Lim Péndé", could not be confidently matched to a standard prefecture name and is treated as a probable OCR error, not a 17th unit). A further named-prefecture line under Ministry 92 (Agriculture et Développement Rural, page numbered 541) reads: "Projet d'appui à la résilience à la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle dans les préfectures de la Kémo et la Ouaka (PARSANKO)". Searched specifically for the phrase "dotation globale de fonctionnement" (the term the 2020 decentralization law mandates for state-to-collectivité transfers) across the full OCR'd text — NOT FOUND anywhere in this 608-page document; the actual transfer lines use different, older terminology ("conseils généraux", a pre-2020 administrative term) rather than the 2020 law's "Conseil Régional"/"Conseil Municipal" vocabulary or its DGF mechanism.
reports.cadence_note: Annual budget law (loi de finances), one per fiscal year; ministry's site lists equivalents back to 2000.

reports.title: Loi portant organisation et fonctionnement des Collectivités Territoriales (2020)
reports.publisher: Présidence de la République / Assemblée Nationale (République Centrafricaine)
reports.description: CAR's 2020 decentralization framework law, establishing Régions and Communes as the two tiers of Collectivité Territoriale. Downloaded as a scanned 43-page PDF (no embedded text; OCR'd in full this round) from an NGO-run local-development resource site (devlocal-rca.org, linked to the French NGO IRAM), NOT a .gouv.cf government host — the document itself, however, bears the CAR presidential letterhead and promulgation formula and is signed "Faustin Archange TOUADERA"; its exact law number and promulgation date are blank/illegible in this scanned copy ("Loi N°" and "Fait à Bangui le" both show no visible number/date at 300dpi), so authenticity is inferred from format and signature rather than a citable number. Chapitre 7 ("DU REGIME FINANCIER DES COLLECTIVITES TERRITORIALES") Art. 46 lists Collectivité resources including "(d) les quoteparts des Collectivités Territoriales des recettes qui leur sont affectées par l'Etat" and "(e) les subventions fournies par l'Etat". Art. 49: "La loi de finance prévoit chaque année une dotation globale de fonctionnement au profit des Collectivités Territoriales. La dotation globale de fonctionnement est repartie entre les Collectivités Territoriales selon des critères fixés par un Arrêté conjoint du Ministre en charge de l'Administration du Territoire et du Ministre des Finances... les facteurs relatifs à la population, l'étendue géographique et au niveau du développement... notifiées aux Maires et présidents des Conseils Régionaux au plus tard trois (3) mois avant le début de l'année budgétaire". Art. 50 provides a parallel investment-side "dotation globale régulièrement inscrite dans la Loi de finances". Art. 71 (Titre II, Des Régions): "La Région est une Collectivité Territoriale composée d'au moins deux (2) préfectures" — confirming Région (the elected/decentralized tier) and préfecture (the deconcentrated, prefect-headed administrative tier) are distinct, with Régions built by grouping préfectures. Art. 215-216 (Titre IV, Dispositions transitoires) set deadlines from the law's adoption: "des élections Municipales sont organisées" within 2 years (Art. 215) and "des élections régionales sont organisées" within 3 years (Art. 216). No independent confirmation was found this round (within the primary-source-only search performed) that these elections have in fact been held; the FY2025 budget law's own transfer-line vocabulary ("conseils généraux" rather than "Conseil Régional"/"Conseil Municipal") is circumstantial evidence the 2020 framework's elected-council structure may not yet be operative in ordinary budget practice, but this is an inference, not a confirmed fact, and is flagged as such.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational framework law.

_dropped.why: The two documents are obviously in the same policy area (state transfers to Collectivités Territoriales) and the 2020 law's Art. 49 explicitly instructs the annual finance law to carry a 'dotation globale de fonctionnement', but the 2025 finance law's own text (Art. 31-34, and the Ministry 14 transfer lines) never cites the 2020 law by title, number, or date — it cites only the 2003 and 2001 finance laws by year. Per the standing evidence rule (verbatim textual basis required per edge), this is a genuine NOT FOUND for a documented citation edge, despite the strong topical relationship. Also, the 2025 law's transfer mechanism (discretionary 'subventions dans les limites des crédits ouverts') does not use the 2020 law's mandated DGF terminology or its population/geography/development-based formula language, so even a 'methodology_depends_on' or 'mandates' edge would overstate what the primary texts actually show.

Attempted to find the law's official number and promulgation date via (a) the finances.gouv.cf site (not hosted there), (b) FAOLEX (guessed record ID, wrong document), (c) a secondary RJDH news article that appeared in search results (URL returned 404 on fetch), and (d) the devlocal-rca.org page itself (gives only 'promulguée en 2020', no number). Genuine NOT FOUND for an exact citable number/date this round.

pefa.org lists three CAR PEFA assessments (2008, 2010, 2023). The 2023 report is marked 'Non-public' on pefa.org (node https://www.pefa.org/node/5186) and could not be accessed. The 2010 report (https://www.pefa.org/sites/default/files/assessments/reports/CAR-Jul10-PFMPR-Public.pdf) is public and was fetched per the task's angle 5 instruction, but it is donor/PEFA-Secretariat-authored, not a CAR government document, so per the evidence rule it cannot itself be a cited primary source. It does describe a joint ministerial-order transfer mechanism ('arrêtés conjoints du Ministre chargé des collectivités territoriales et du MFB') consistent with the 2020 law's Art. 49 DGF mechanism, and describes local budgets as chronically finalized late due to information reaching collectivités up to three months behind schedule — but names no specific CAR government document by number, so it yields no independently citable primary edge.

Checked both the CEMAC Commission's 2024 inflation note and AFRISTAT's CEMAC IHPC methodology documents (APA04 methodology guide and the 2017 IHPC-CEMAC methodological guide) for CAR-specific sub-national fiscal allocation content per the task's angle 4. Both name Centrafrique as 1 of 6 CEMAC member states and BANGUI specifically as the CPI observation city ('BANGUI pour la CENTRAFRIQUE'), confirming/extending the existing cf-icasees-ihpc <-> cemac-ihpc-regulation edge already in af-cemac.json — but neither document contains any CAR-specific sub-national (prefecture/region) budget or transfer content. Genuine NOT FOUND for a CEMAC-to-CAR-subnational edge; this is a CPI-methodology relationship only, already captured upstream.

reports.title: Règlement N° 03/21-CEMAC-UEAC-CM-36 portant modalités d'élaboration, de calcul et de publication de l'indice harmonisé des prix à la consommation
reports.publisher: CEMAC (Communauté Économique et Monétaire de l'Afrique Centrale)
reports.region: CEMAC (Cameroon, Central African Republic, Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea, Chad)
reports.description: The CEMAC-wide binding regulation establishing the harmonized CPI, dated 27 January 2021. The CEMAC Commission's own 2024 inflation note (page 5) describes it as covering "modalités d'élaboration, de calcul et de publication de l'indice harmonisé des prix à la consommation" [procedures for developing, calculating and publishing the harmonized consumer price index], with "a methodological guide attached to this regulation." This closes three existing _dropped leads sitting unresolved in cm-cpi-social-protection.json, ga-cpi-social-protection.json and td-cpi-social-protection.json, all of which had already identified this exact regulation number by title but not fetched or minted it. A companion instrument, Regulation N°04/21-UEAC-115-CM-36, covers "modalités d'élaboration, de calcul et de diffusion de l'inflation sous-jacente" [underlying/core inflation] — not minted this round, flagged below. AFRISTAT's own CEMAC methodology document (APA04, 'Fondements Méthodologiques de l'Indice Harmonisé des Prix des Etats Membres de la CEMAC') independently confirms the six covered states by name: "Cameroun, Centrafrique, Congo, Gabon; Guinée Equatoriale et Tchad," and identifies itself as published by AFRISTAT, though it does not itself state the regulation number — the regulation number comes from the CEMAC Commission's own note, not the AFRISTAT guide.

reports.title: Loi Organique N°014/CNT/2024 du 30/31 juillet 2024 portant Statuts des Collectivités Autonomes
reports.publisher: Conseil National de Transition (CNT), République du Tchad
reports.description: Chad's current organic law establishing commune-level government, verified independently via two sources: a FAOLEX mirror of the official gazette text and a Journal Officiel copy (65ème année, N°07, numéro spécial, juillet 2024). This 2024 reform reduced Chad's territorial tiers from four (Régions, Départements, Communes, Communautés rurales, under the superseded 2000 law) to two (Provinces, Communes) — Art. 8: "les Collectivités autonomes de la République du Tchad sont: les Provinces; les Communes." Art. 2: "Leur autonomie administrative, financière, patrimoniale et économique est garantie par la Constitution." Art. 142 lists commune own-source revenue: locally-voted taxes/centimes additionnels, state dotations/subventions, borrowing, gifts/legacies, patrimoine revenue, and "le pourcentage sur le produit des ressources du sol et du sous-sol exploitées sur leur territoire" (a share of subsoil-resource revenue). Art. 143: fiscal-legality principle — "le Conseil communal ne peut instituer aucune taxe, ni aucun impôt qui n'ait été au préalable créé par la loi de finances." Art. 144 lists specific state taxes whose product is attributed to communes (taxe foncière, taxe sur la valeur locative, contribution des patentes/licences, taxe civique). Art. 147: these taxes "sont liquidées et recouvrées directement par le receveur communal."
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, currently in force.

reports.title: Séminaire National sur la Décentralisation — Les Mécanismes de Financement des Collectivités Autonomes
reports.publisher: Inspecteurs du Trésor et des Impôts, Ministère des Finances du Tchad, presented at an official Séminaire National sur la Décentralisation
reports.description: A presentation authored by named Chad Treasury/Tax Ministry inspectors (EHBA ABRAHAM, Inspecteur Principal du Trésor; NGARLENAN DOCDJENGAR, Inspecteur Principal des Impôts) at an official government decentralization seminar. Constitutional péréquation basis: "Selon l'article 265 de la constitution de la 5ieme République, la péréquation est un dispositif juridique et institutionnel visant à réduire les disparités de ressources et de charges entre les collectivités territoriales." KEY NEGATIVE FINDING: Chad has NO operational FEICOM/ANICT-equivalent equalization/investment fund as of this 2025 seminar — one is only PROPOSED: "Création d'une Agence Nationale d'Investissement des Collectivités Autonomes...qui sera un établissement public à caractère administratif...Gérer les dotations, les subventions d'équipement et les contributions des partenaires au développement en assurant la péréquation des ressources allouées aux Collectivités Autonomes." The seminar's own conclusion: "La plupart des communes du Tchad éprouve de sérieuses difficultés à dégager une épargne suffisante pour financer ses projets de développement." reports.title: Constitution de l'Union des Comores du 23 décembre 2001 (révisée 2009, 2013, 2018)
reports.description: UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.23, Article 104 enrichment -- Union/island financial-convention power): Article 104, immediately preceding the already-captured Articles 105/106, provides: "Dans le respect de la Constitution et dans la limite de leurs compétences respectives, l'Union et les îles autonomes ou les îles autonomes entre elles peuvent conclure des conventions à caractère social, économique ou financier. ... Les conventions mentionnées à l'alinéa 2 du présent article, ne peuvent être conclues sans l'accord préalable de l'État." [In keeping with the Constitution and within the limits of their respective competences, the Union and the autonomous islands, or the autonomous islands among themselves, may conclude conventions of a social, economic or financial nature ... conventions mentioned in paragraph 2 of this article may not be concluded without the prior agreement of the State.] This names the specifically *financial* dimension of the Union/island relationship and reinforces the centralization pattern already described below (State-set grants, State-approved island budgets) by requiring prior State approval even for financial conventions among the islands themselves. The consolidated Comorian Constitution (2001, as amended through the 2018 revision), hosted via ILO NATLEX. Directly verified via pdftotext extraction. Article 105: "Compte tenu de la solidarité nationale et du développement socio-économique équilibré des iles, les ressources de celles-ci comprennent la dotation versée par l'État et le produit des droits, impôts, taxes locaux, dont les montants et les taux sont fixés par la loi de finances" [In view of national solidarity and balanced socio-economic development of the islands, island resources comprise the grant paid by the State and the proceeds of local duties, taxes and levies, whose amounts and rates are set by budget law]. Article 106: "Le budget de l'Ile doit être en équilibre et approuvé par l'État" [The Island's budget must be balanced and approved by the State]. The 2018 revision is widely reported to have significantly centralised power relative to the original 2001 framework (ending the rotating Union presidency among islands) — Articles 105/106 show the fiscal relationship is asymmetric/centralised (State-set grants, State-approved budgets), not co-equal federalism, despite the three islands each retaining their own elected government. No separate annual budget law itemising actual per-island transfer amounts was located this round.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument (consolidated through the 2018 revision).

dependencies.basis: An AU/StatAfric Pan-African Statistics Programme peer review of Comoros's national statistical system (hosted on INSEED's own domain, visit dated 21-22 October 2018) states verbatim: "L'INSEED adapte les nomenclatures développées par AFRISTAT et les méthodologies et méthodes internationales de collecte et de traitement des données" [INSEED adapts the nomenclatures developed by AFRISTAT along with international methodologies and methods for data collection and processing]. This is AU-authored (a third-party peer review of INSEED, not INSEED's self-published methodology note), but hosted on INSEED's own site and states a direct, specific methodology-adaptation relationship — matching the strength standard used elsewhere in this corpus for `methodology_depends_on` edges. `afristat-ihpc-guide-2014` reused per the branch's node-id discipline.

The full text of the AU peer-review document (36 pages) was searched for "Commission de l'Océan Indien," "COI," and "Indian Ocean Commission" — zero mentions found. Genuine NOT FOUND despite being the single best-positioned candidate document searched so far.

reports.title: Annexe 8 : Concours Financiers aux Collectivités Territoriales et aux Districts Autonomes — Loi de Finances 2026
reports.publisher: Direction Générale du Budget et des Finances (DGBF), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et du Budget de Côte d'Ivoire
reports.description: DGBF's own annual budget-law annex governing state transfers to collectivités territoriales, verified by direct PDF download (2026 edition; 2025 edition independently cross-checked). Cover: "LOI DE FINANCES N°2025-987 DU 19 DECEMBRE 2025 PORTANT BUDGET DE L'ETAT POUR L'ANNEE 2026 — ANNEXE 8." For 2026: "il est prévu un montant de 479,70 milliards FCFA comprenant 255,01 milliards FCFA de recettes affectées et 224,69 milliards FCFA au titre des dotations budgétaires" (up from 396,09 milliards FCFA total in the 2025 edition). KEY FINDING: "toutes les Collectivités Territoriales bénéficient des dotations budgétaires à l'exception des dix (10) principales communes du district autonome d'Abidjan compte tenu de l'importance des quotes-parts d'impôts qui leur sont reversées" — Abidjan's ten main communes (Cocody, Plateau, Yopougon, Marcory, Treichville, Abobo, etc.) are structurally EXCLUDED from the DGF precisely because they receive larger tax-retrocession quotes-parts instead, funded under "l'arrêté interministériel n°0772/MBPE/MIS/MEF du 26 juillet 2022." The 2026 edition carves out one named exception: "pour l'année 2026, la Commune d'Attécoubé, compte tenu de ses difficultés de mobilisation de ressources propres, bénéficie d'un appui budgétaire." Distribution formula: "leur répartition s'effectue sur la base d'une proportion ventilée de manière égalitaire entre les collectivités de même type, permettant d'obtenir une part minimale. Le reste de la dotation est réparti au prorata de la population de chaque collectivité. A ce critère s'ajoute le taux de pauvreté déterminé par l'Enquête Harmonisée sur les Conditions de Vie des Ménages (EHCVM) pour ce qui concerne la répartition de la dotation d'investissement." A separate annual interministerial arrêté sets equalization terms: "il est pris chaque année, un arrêté interministériel qui détermine les modalités de péréquation en vue de réduire les disparités entre différentes communes, régions et districts autonomes" — the only place across all documents checked this round where "péréquation" appears in Ivorian primary material, as an adjective describing this annual mechanism rather than a named 'Fonds de Péréquation' (that exact term does not appear anywhere in Ivorian primary law found this round). The governing statute is cited as "la loi n°2020-885 du 21 octobre 2020 portant régime financier des Collectivités Territoriales et des Districts Autonomes," whose own full text was NOT independently retrieved this round (two hosting attempts failed with connection errors) — its existence, title and date are corroborated by this primary DGBF document, but its own text is NOT FOUND.

reports.title: Loi n°2020-885 du 21 octobre 2020 portant régime financier des Collectivités Territoriales et des Districts Autonomes
reports.description: Côte d'Ivoire's governing fiscal-regime law for collectivités, previously known in this corpus only by title/date via a citing document (ci-dgbf-annexe8-2026) — its own text was NOT FOUND in AF/G.18 after two failed hosting attempts. Independently re-verified this round (AF/G.21, processing a import-supplied lead): the import's exact cited URL (commons.laws.africa) is a dead 404, but the actual law text was independently located and confirmed via a third-party document-host mirror (Scribd), since the known official mirrors (agp.africanlii.org, juriafrica.com, dcf.ci) remained unreachable. Article 1: "La présente loi fixe les règles et principes fondamentaux régissant le cadre financier et comptable des collectivités décentralisées : les collectivités territoriales et les districts autonomes." Article 2: "Les collectivités territoriales sont des entités décentralisées qui s'administrent librement par des conseils dont les membres sont élus. Elles sont dotées de la personnalité morale et de l'autonomie financière. Les districts autonomes sont des entités territoriales de type particulier qui s'administrent par un conseil composé de membres élus et nommés. Ils sont dotés de la personnalité morale et de l'autonomie financière." On the DGF mechanism already cited (but not quoted) via ci-dgbf-annexe8-2026: Article 59 lists "la dotation globale de fonctionnement," "la dotation générale de décentralisation," "les subventions d'équilibre," and "les subventions d'équipement" as the four state transfer instruments; Article 60 and 61 create the DGF and the dotation générale de décentralisation respectively; but Article 62 explicitly delegates the actual calculation/allocation formula to a SEPARATE decree, not the law itself: "Les modalités de fixation, de calcul et de répartition de la dotation globale de fonctionnement et de la dotation générale de décentralisation sont fixées par décret pris en Conseil des ministres." CAVEAT (sourcing): the verified text comes from a non-official third-party upload, not a government-hosted or Journal Officiel copy — content is corroborated as accurate against the law's own citing documents (title, date, and Article 1/2 substance all consistent with how ci-dgbf-annexe8-2026 already describes it), but a government-domain mirror was not reachable this round. CAVEAT (completeness): the readable text truncates mid-Article-125 (the law's own signature/promulgation block was not reached), so no "péréquation" fund name or explicit tax-retrocession quotes-parts formula was found WITHIN the law's own text — this is inconclusive due to truncation, not a confirmed absence; see updated `_dropped` entries.

reports.title: Constitution de la République de Djibouti (1992)
reports.description: Djibouti's 1992 Constitution, Titre X ("Des collectivités territoriales"). Resolves this file's own earlier `_dropped` note — the import located and this session independently re-fetched the primary text (MJP Digithèque, a French academic constitutional-text mirror, the same hosting tier already used elsewhere in this branch for constituteproject.org/WIPO Lex texts). Directly verified via curl + HTML extraction. Article 85: "Les collectivités territoriales sont créées et administrées dans les conditions définies par la loi. Ces collectivités s'administrent librement par des conseils élus et dans les conditions prévues par la loi" [Territorial collectivities are created and administered under conditions defined by law. These collectivities are freely self-administered by elected councils, under conditions provided by law]. Article 86: "Dans les collectivités territoriales, le délégué du Gouvernement a la charge des intérêts nationaux, du contrôle administratif et du respect des lois" [In the territorial collectivities, the Government's delegate is responsible for national interests, administrative oversight, and compliance with the law]. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the import's own paraphrase: the import's response described these articles as stating the collectivities "enjoy administrative and financial autonomy" — that specific phrase does NOT appear anywhere in the actual French text of Article 85 or 86; the primary text establishes self-administration by elected councils, not a financial-autonomy guarantee. the import also cited "Articles 85-87" as Titre X, but Article 87 is actually the FIRST article of Titre XI ("De la révision de la Constitution"), unrelated to territorial collectivities — a real citation error, caught by independent re-verification of the primary text rather than taken on the import's word. No fiscal-transfer mechanism or percentage is specified anywhere in this Titre; the detailed financing regime is left entirely to ordinary law, consistent with dj-loi-174-territorial (still not independently located this round, per the dropped note below).
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument.

reports.title: Loi organique n°08/016 du 07 octobre 2008 portant composition, organisation et fonctionnement des Entités Territoriales Décentralisées — Titre IV: Des ressources financières
reports.description: DRC's organic law establishing the fiscal regime of Entités Territoriales Décentralisées (ETDs — communes, secteurs, chefferies), the tier below province. Cross-verified against two independent hostings (leganet.cd, a Congolese legal-reference portal, and FAOLEX, the FAO's national-legislation database — neither a .gouv.cd host itself). Art. 104: "Les finances d'une entité territoriale décentralisée sont distinctes de celles de la province" [An ETD's finances are distinct from the province's]. Art. 105 lists ETD resource categories: own resources, a share of nationally-sourced revenue allocated to provinces, resources of the national equalisation fund, and exceptional resources. Art. 108-109: own resources include "l'impôt personnel minimum" (minimum personal tax), perceived "au profit exclusif des communes, des secteurs ou des chefferies" [exclusively for the benefit of communes, secteurs, or chefferies]. KEY FINDING — Art. 115: "Les entités territoriales décentralisées ont droit à 40% de la part des recettes à caractère national allouées aux provinces" [ETDs are entitled to 40% of the share of nationally-sourced revenue already allocated to the provinces] — a second, cascading 40% rule, legally distinct from (even though numerically identical to) the province-level 40% retrocession already in the corpus (cd-constitution-provinces-revenue, Constitution Art. 175). Art. 116: distribution among ETDs is based on "critères de capacité de production, de la superficie et de la population" [production capacity, territorial area, and population], with the exact mechanism left to provincial edict (édit) — not independently located this round.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument.

dependencies.basis: Article 105 of the organic law explicitly lists 'la part provenant des recettes à caractère national allouées aux provinces' among ETD resource categories, directly presupposing the Constitution's Article 175 province-level 40% retrocession mechanism as the source pool that Article 115's own commune-level 40% cascades from.

Deliberately minted isolated (no dependency edges to ng-cpi-pension-safety-net or gh's CPI node): the report's own Acknowledgements state its data source as "data and other useful information provided by member central banks" — an AGENCY ONLY attribution to central banks specifically, not to the national statistical offices (Nigeria's NBS, Ghana's GSS) whose own CPI releases are already minted in this corpus. Forcing an edge from a central-bank-sourced convergence report to a statistics-office CPI node would be exactly the kind of unsupported inference this branch's rules forbid — a real near-miss, honestly reported rather than stretched.

reports.title: Constitution of the Arab Republic of Egypt (2014), Articles 176-178 — Local Administration
reports.description: Egypt's 2014 Constitution's local-administration and local-finance provisions, not previously minted in this corpus (which already has Egypt's provincial-tier documents — eg-cairo-citizen-budget-2024-2025 and eg-local-administration-law-43-1979 — from an earlier session, but not the constitutional text itself). Directly verified via PDF extraction. Article 176: "The state ensures support for administrative, financial, and economic decentralization. The law organizes empowering administrative units in providing, improving, and managing public utilities well, and defines the timeline for transferring powers and budgets to the local administration units." Article 177: "The state guarantees that it will satisfy the local units' needs in terms of scientific, technical, administrative and financial assistance, and ensures the equitable distribution of facilities, services and resources." Article 178: "Local units have independent financial budgets. Local units' resources include, in addition to the resources allocated to them by the state, original and additional taxes and fees of a local nature." IMPORTANT: the Constitution's own 5-year deadline (January 2019) to pass a NEW Local Administration Law implementing Articles 175-183 has lapsed — Law No. 43 of 1979 (already minted as `eg-local-administration-law-43-1979`) remains the operative statute, with a replacement still an unpassed draft before Parliament (resubmitted April 2026) — consistent with this corpus's EXISTING dropped note on eg-cairo-municipal-finance.json ("New/replacement Local Administration Law (post-43/1979) -> Cairo Governorate finance, deferred"). No new edge is drawn between this Constitution node and the pre-1979 law given the chronological mismatch (the operative law predates this Constitution).
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument.

reports.title: Loi n° 12-07 du 21 février 2012 relative à la wilaya (Code de la Wilaya)
reports.publisher: République Algérienne / Journal Officiel de la République Algérienne (JORADP)
reports.description: Algeria's Wilaya Code, establishing the fiscal relationship between the central state and Algeria's 58 wilayas (provinces). Directly verified via curl + pdftotext extraction of the official Journal Officiel PDF (bypassing a 403-blocked mirror and a dead government-site link). Article 5: "L'Etat affecte à la wilaya, en sa qualité de collectivité territoriale, les ressources destinées à la couverture des charges et des compétences qui lui sont dévolues par la loi... tout transfert de missions par l'Etat à la wilaya s'accompagne de l'affectation des ressources financières nécessaires à leur couverture permanente" [The State allocates to the wilaya the resources to cover the charges and competences devolved to it by law; any transfer of missions is accompanied by the necessary financial resources]. Article 151 lists wilaya budgetary resources including state grants ("dotations") and tax proceeds. Article 154: "La wilaya reçoit de l'Etat des subventions et des dotations de fonctionnement, compte tenu, notamment, de : — l'inégalité des revenus des wilayas ; — l'insuffisance de son revenu par rapport à ses missions" [The wilaya receives operating subsidies and grants from the State, taking into account revenue inequality among wilayas and revenue insufficiency relative to its missions] — a direct equalisation clause. Articles 176-179 (Chapitre 1er, "De la solidarité financière") establish two dedicated equalisation funds: "le fonds de solidarité des collectivités locales" and "le fonds de garantie des collectivités locales," the former paying wilayas "une attribution annuelle de péréquation destinée à la section de fonctionnement du budget de la wilaya" [an annual equalisation allocation for the wilaya's operating budget]. Article 155 separately names the "fonds commun des collectivités locales (FCCL)" for earmarked equipment financing — the historic name (per a secondary, not independently verified, Wikipedia summary) for what appears to now operate as the two Article-176 funds. No specific Loi de Finances line item labelled "transferts aux wilayas" was independently located this round.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument.

reports.title: نظام الادارة المحلية (Local Administration System) — State Information Service
reports.publisher: State Information Service (SIS), Arab Republic of Egypt
reports.description: Egypt's official state information/media agency's own restatement of the Constitution's local-administration provisions, corroborating (from a genuine Egyptian government agency, not the OHCHR unofficial-translation mirror used for the Constitution's own text) that the independent-budget/elected-council design exists in law: "الدولة إلى وحدات إدارية تتمتع بالشخصية الاعتبارية، منها المحافظات، والمدن، والقرى" [The state is divided into administrative units enjoying legal personality, including governorates, cities, and villages]; "تنتخب كل وحدة محلية مجلساً بالاقتراع العام السرى المباشر، لمدة أربع سنوات" [Each local unit elects a council by direct secret public ballot for a four-year term]; "يكون للوحدات المحلية موازنات مالية مستقلة" [Local units shall have independent financial budgets]. IMPORTANT: this describes the system AS DESIGNED, not as currently operating — Local Popular Councils have been dissolved since 2011 (Law No. 116 of 2011) with no successor body elected since, so no independent local-unit budget publication exists in practice (consistent with eg-local-administration-law-43-1979's finding that sub-governorate 'resources' are statutorily governorate-allocated transfers, not autonomous budgets).
reports.cadence_note: Standing institutional/legal-system description page, not dated to a specific edition.

reports.title: Eritrea: Selected Issues and Statistical Appendix (IMF Country Report No. 03/166)
reports.description: The most recent IMF document with substantive Eritrea CPI content locatable this round (2003; report data through 2002). Directly extracted via OCR (the PDF is a scanned image with no text layer) from Chapter V, paragraph 87: "Until recently, the authorities have used two measures of inflation, one produced by the Bank of Eritrea (BE) and the other established by the National Eritrea Statistics and Evaluation Office (SEO)... The SEO began compiling its own measure of the CPI in January 1996." Table V.1 sources line: "Sources: Bank of Eritrea; Eritrea Statistical and Evaluation Office; Ethiopian authorities; and IMF staff estimates." PAST TENSE and flagged accordingly: this describes 1994-2002 practice with no confirmation it continues. No live NSEO (National Statistics and Evaluation Office) website was found — only third-party aggregator profile pages (knoema.com, ghdx.healthdata.org). A 2019 IMF Article IV mission occurred but its end-of-mission press release contains no CPI figures or agency citation, and no full Board-approved staff report after 2003 could be confirmed as published — Eritrea has a documented history of delayed/absent Article IV consultations.
reports.cadence_note: One-off country report; no evidence of a current recurring Eritrean CPI publication was found this round.

reports.title: Constitution of Eritrea (1997)
reports.description: Eritrea's 1997 Constitution, ratified but never fully implemented/promulgated into force. Article 1(5): "Eritrea is a unitary State divided into units of local government. The powers and duties of these units shall be determined by law." Verified directly via PDF text extraction. No implementing body or fiscal mechanism is named — the constitutional mandate is general and, per er-un-coi-proclamation-86-1996, was never given fiscal substance at the regional (zoba) level.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument.

reports.title: UN Commission of Inquiry on Human Rights in Eritrea — Chapter V (quoting Proclamation No. 86/1996)
reports.publisher: UN Human Rights Council Commission of Inquiry on Eritrea
reports.description: A UN Commission of Inquiry report (A/HRC/29/CRP.1) that quotes Eritrea's own Proclamation No. 86/1996 verbatim with paragraph/article numbers; the proclamation itself is not independently available online in full text, so this UN document is the best available evidence. Directly verified via PDF text extraction. Paragraph 260: "In April 1996, Proclamation No. 86/1996 was adopted. It abolished the historical nine provinces of Eritrea and established six administrative regions or zobas... Southern Red Sea; Northern Red Sea; Anseba; Gash-Barka; Southern; and Central." Paragraph 263: "Article 13(1) of the Proclamation states that baito zobas are to prepare regional development programmes... Regional assemblies do not have fiscal authority but are mandated to collect local revenues." This last clause is the key finding: Eritrea's regional (zoba) tier has NO fiscal transfer mechanism analogous to other African countries' provincial equalisation/dotation systems — a genuine structural negative finding, not a research gap.
reports.cadence_note: One-off report (2015), quoting a one-off 1996 legislative instrument.

reports.title: 2016 Fiscal Year (2023/24) Federal Government Budget Proclamation No. 1297/2023
reports.publisher: House of Peoples' Representatives, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
reports.description: Ethiopia's federal budget proclamation, published in Federal Negarit Gazette No. 38 (14 September 2023) and directly downloaded from the Ministry of Justice's own site. Article 7 ('Subsidies to Regions') lists Addis Ababa City Government and Dire Dawa Administration as separate, numbered line items structurally parallel to the 11 regional states, not nested under them: "441 Addis Ababa City Government 5,254,541,684 ... 442 Dire Dawa Administration 1,837,611,323", alongside "431 The State of Tigray 12,591,813,948 ... 439 The State of the Harari People 1,587,027,961". Sub-article 7.10 breaks Addis Ababa's own subsidy into External Loan (5,215,724,800 Birr) and External Assistance (38,816,884 Birr); sub-article 7.11 breaks Dire Dawa's into Domestic Source (1,811,501,996 Birr) and External Assistance (26,109,327 Birr). Note an asymmetry: Article 8 ('Support for Achievement of SDGs') lists a Dire Dawa line (8.10) but no separate Addis Ababa line, unlike Article 7. This is a fixed itemized appropriation, not a percentage formula.
reports.cadence_note: Annual federal budget proclamation; this edition covers Ethiopian FY2016 (Gregorian 2023/24).
