_slice: Alberta energy royalties and price benchmarks
_note: Alberta's royalty system is not one formula but two parallel chains that meet only in the budget. Conventional oil and gas run on prices the province itself manufactures: the Alberta Petroleum Marketing Commission sets monthly oil par prices and the Alberta Natural Gas Reference Price as netbacks to the wellhead, and the Modernized Royalty Framework writes its post-C* rate tables directly in those numbers ($/m3 brackets for oil, $/GJ brackets for gas). Oil sands runs on a price Alberta has no hand in at all: the Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009 makes the royalty rate an explicit linear function of the NYMEX prompt-month WTI futures settlement price converted at the Bank of Canada's daily USD/CAD rate — a Chicago exchange and a federal central bank jointly determine the largest line in Alberta's revenue. The interesting shape here is how much of the chain terminates in privately published commercial price assessments (WCS-WTI broker indices, Argus Mexico Maya, ICE Brent, AECO) that are named in Alberta regulations but are not public statistical releases; those became dropped edges. The chain also runs sideways into property tax: the same Alberta Energy Regulator well records that underpin the sector feed the Linear Property Assessment Minister's Guidelines field by field, so a well's assessed value is literally read out of AER General Well File record types.

reports.title: Oil Par Prices
reports.publisher: Alberta Energy and Minerals / Alberta Petroleum Marketing Commission
reports.description: Monthly par prices for the four density categories of conventional Alberta crude oil (light, medium, heavy and ultra-heavy), plus par prices for pentanes plus, butanes, propane and ethane. Set by the Alberta Petroleum Marketing Commission to represent arm's-length netback market prices at the producing battery, and published in numbered Alberta Energy Information Letters. These are the prices the conventional oil royalty formulas are written in terms of.
reports.cadence_note: Published as a numbered Information Letter roughly six weeks after the production month.

As of the check date (2026-08-11), par-price documents were already posted through September 2026 (IL-2026-26), while October, November and December 2026 were listed as text only (not yet linked) -- confirming a consistent one-document-per-month cadence that matches the corpus's releases_per_year=12. Exact day-of-month for each posting could not be determined (PDF fetch blocked by robots.txt), so entries use month precision only.

reports.title: Alberta Natural Gas Reference Price
reports.publisher: Alberta Energy and Minerals / Alberta Petroleum Marketing Commission
reports.description: The monthly representative market price ($/GJ) for natural gas bought and sold within Alberta, calculated by the APMC on a simplified netback model. Published alongside monthly reference prices for methane, ethane, propane, butanes, pentanes plus and sulphur. The reference price is the input that values the Crown's natural gas royalty volume, and the budget forecasts it by name.
reports.cadence_note: Continuous monthly series from 1994; average market prices published for 1988-1993 on the same page.

entries.covers: June 2026 monthly reference price added to table
July 2026 monthly reference price added to table

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar or stated-rule found on alberta.ca. The page (open.alberta.ca/opendata metadata confirms 'Monthly' maintenance/update frequency) is updated monthly with a new month's reference price. As of the page's last-modified timestamp (2026-07-15), the table showed data through May 2026 - an observed lag of roughly 6 weeks after month-end before that month's value is posted. Applying that same observed lag going forward implies June 2026 data should appear around mid-August 2026 and July 2026 data around mid-September 2026. This is an inferred pattern, not a stated publication rule.

reports.title: Alberta Modernized Royalty Framework Guidelines: Principles and Procedures
reports.description: The operating manual for the Modernized Royalty Framework governing wells drilled on or after 1 January 2017 under the Petroleum Royalty Regulation, 2017 and the Natural Gas Royalty Regulation, 2017. Sets out the Drilling and Completion Cost Allowance (C*), the 5% flat royalty until cumulative revenue reaches C*, and the post-C* royalty rate as a price component (rp) plus a quantity component (rq), with worked examples and rate-bracket tables keyed to par and reference prices for each hydrocarbon.
reports.cadence_note: Reissued when the framework, its rate formulas or its programs change rather than on a fixed calendar.

release_schedule.note: This is a policy/program guidelines document (principles and procedures for Alberta's Modernized Royalty Framework), not a periodic statistical report. Alberta Energy and Minerals has issued revised versions at irregular intervals since 2020: v1.1 (2020-05-28), v2.0 (2020-06), v2.1 (2022-02), v2.2 (2023-01), v2.3 (2023-10), v2.4 (2024-11-21). No new version has been published since v2.4 as of 2026-08-11 (checked; dataset metadata last touched 2026-03-31 with v2.4 still the current/active resource). No calendar or stated rule governs when the next revision will appear — updates occur when Alberta Energy and Minerals changes MRF program parameters or procedures.

reports.title: Oil Sands Monthly Royalty Rates Information
reports.description: The monthly determination of oil sands royalty rates under the Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009: the pre-payout gross revenue royalty percentage, the post-payout gross revenue royalty percentage and the post-payout net royalty percentage factor. Each release also publishes the WTI price and exchange rate used. Alberta Energy posts the percentages by the fifth business day following the production month.

Publish OS Monthly Royalty Rates - October 2026
Publish OS Monthly Royalty Rates - November 2026
Publish OS Monthly Royalty Rates - December 2026

release_schedule.note: Alberta Energy and Minerals publishes an annual 'Oil Sands Royalty Reporting Calendar' PDF that lists a specific 'Publish OS Monthly Royalty Rates' date for each month. The PDF itself notes it is 'prepared as a courtesy only' and that the Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009 and departmental guidelines govern actual requirements, but it gives concrete dates each year. The August 2026 entry (Aug 10) has already passed as of 2026-08-11, so the next occurrence is September 8, 2026. The landing page https://www.alberta.ca/oil-sands-royalty-rates links to the Open Government Portal where each month's report/CSV is actually posted (open.alberta.ca was returning server errors during this check, so exact historical posting dates on that portal could not be independently verified, but the reporting calendar's dates align with a monthly cadence consistent with releases_per_year=12).

reports.title: Bitumen Valuation Methodology (BVM) Components and Floor Price
reports.description: Monthly publication of the component values and the Floor Price used to compute a deemed bitumen value under the Bitumen Valuation Methodology (Ministerial) Regulation. Operators whose bitumen is not sold at arm's length must value it at the BVM price rather than a sales price, so this release fixes the gross revenue on which oil sands royalty is charged. Accompanied by a downloadable BVM model calculator.

entries.covers: June 2026 update to cumulative BVM components report (adds May 2026 production month data)
July 2026 update to cumulative BVM components report (adds June 2026 production month data)
August 2026 update to cumulative BVM components report (expected to add July 2026 production month data)

release_schedule.note: Publisher (CKAN metadata on open.alberta.ca) states updatefrequency = 'Monthly'. The report is a single cumulative annual PDF per year (e.g. em-bvm-components-2026.pdf) that is republished each month with the newly available production month's data appended; only the latest version is kept ('published cumulatively'). Using the CKAN package_activity_list API for dataset id f5f003e9-bdb2-42a7-9ed5-a2ee207dcd7e, update timestamps for the 2026 file show a highly consistent monthly cadence, generally landing between the 20th and 26th of each month: 2026-01-21, 2026-02-23, 2026-03-23, 2026-04-23, 2026-05-21/26, 2026-06-22, 2026-07-22. The same pattern holds in prior years (e.g. 2025-08-21, 2024-08-22, 2023-08-23 for the August update specifically). As of 2026-08-11 no August 2026 update has yet appeared, so the next release is projected for roughly 2026-08-17 to 2026-08-24 based on this pattern, adding July 2026 data. The downloaded 2026 PDF (last-modified 2026-07-22) currently contains monthly rows through June 2026 (WCS settlement price, oil sands par price, exchange rate, etc.), confirming the June data was the most recent addition as of that update.

reports.title: NYMEX Light Sweet Crude Oil (WTI) Futures Daily Settlement Prices
reports.description: The daily settlement price of the prompt-month West Texas Intermediate light sweet crude oil futures contract traded on NYMEX, published each trading day by CME Group. Named by Alberta regulation as the single price series that sets oil sands royalty rates and the bitumen floor price, which makes a commodity exchange's daily settlement the largest single driver of Alberta's provincial revenue.
reports.cadence_note: One settlement per exchange trading day; roughly 252 per year. Alberta averages the daily settlements over a month.

release_schedule.rule: Daily settlement prices for NYMEX Light Sweet Crude Oil (WTI) futures are determined every trading day, based on trading activity during the settlement period of 14:28:00 to 14:30:00 Eastern Time (14:00:00-14:30:00 ET on front-month expiration day), per the NYMEX Energy Futures Daily Settlement Procedure.

entries.covers: Daily settlement price for the 2026-08-11 trading session

release_schedule.note: This is a continuous daily release published after the close of every CME/NYMEX trading day (the exchange trades Sunday evening through Friday afternoon ET, closed on exchange holidays), not a single dated 'next release' in the usual sense. 2026-08-11 is an ordinary trading day (Tuesday, no US/CME holiday), so it is the next (in-progress or upcoming) settlement date; the pattern then repeats each subsequent trading day. The corpus's releases_per_year of 252 is consistent with one settlement per NYMEX trading day per year.

reports.title: Bank of Canada Daily Exchange Rates
reports.description: The Bank of Canada's daily indicative exchange rates, published each business day at 16:30 ET. Alberta's oil sands royalty regulation and its bitumen valuation regulation both name the Bank of Canada's daily USD/CAD rate as the conversion that turns a US-dollar crude price into the Canadian-dollar price the royalty formulas run on, and both contain fallback clauses in case the Bank stops publishing it.
reports.cadence_note: Every business day; the regulations still say 'noon' rate, a series the Bank replaced in 2017 with a single daily rate.

release_schedule.rule: The daily average exchange rates are published once each business day by 16:30 ET.
release_schedule.note: This is a daily recurring release on every business day (Mon-Fri, excluding Bank of Canada holidays), published by 16:30 ET, not an annual/periodic report with a small number of releases_per_year. The entry above is the next expected business-day release (today); no fixed multi-date calendar is posted since it is effectively continuous. releases_per_year=250 on file is consistent with roughly one release per business day (~250-252 business days/year) and appears reasonable, though not explicitly stated by the publisher as a count.

reports.title: AER General Well Data Report (General Well File)
reports.description: The Alberta Energy Regulator's authoritative record of every oil, gas, oil sands and water well licensed in Alberta, updated daily and distributed as fixed-format record types carrying licence number, well status, total depth, shoe set depth, plug intervals, material and operating pressure. It is the master register the province's regulated well and pipeline assessment reads from.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously maintained and updated daily; assessment freezes it at October 31 of the assessment year.

reports.title: ICE Brent Crude Futures Daily Settlement Prices
reports.description: The daily settlement price of the prompt-month Brent crude futures contract on ICE. Named verbatim in Alberta's Bitumen Valuation Methodology regulation, where the gap between Brent and WTI enters the monthly Floor Price directly. A commercial exchange's settlement price, written into provincial law as a term in a royalty formula.
reports.cadence_note: One settlement per exchange trading day; roughly 252 a year. Alberta averages the daily settlements over a month.

entries.covers: Daily settlement price for the next ICE Futures Europe trading day

release_schedule.rule: Daily settlement price for ICE Brent Crude Futures is calculated as the weighted average price of trades during a two-minute settlement period from 19:28:00 London time, and is published on each trading day the exchange is open (London trading hours 01:00-23:00, Mon-Fri, with holiday closures per the ICE Futures Europe trading calendar).
release_schedule.note: This is a continuously traded futures contract; ICE publishes a new daily settlement price at the close of every trading day, not on a periodic release calendar. releases_per_year of 252 is consistent with the approximate number of annual trading days, which matches this daily-settlement rule.

reports.title: Argus Mexico Maya Spot Price, FOB US Gulf Coast
reports.description: Argus Media's daily price assessment for Mexican Maya heavy crude delivered FOB at the US Gulf Coast. Alberta's bitumen valuation regulation names Argus as the publisher by company name and uses the assessment as the MMSP term in the Floor Price formula, so a proprietary heavy-crude assessment sets the floor under the province's bitumen royalty base.
reports.cadence_note: Assessed each trading day and averaged monthly for the BVM calculation. The assessment is paywalled; only the regulation naming it is public.

entries.covers: Next daily Argus Americas Crude price report (Maya FOB USGC assessment)

release_schedule.rule: "At the end of each trading day we publish a PDF report containing the latest prices, news and market commentary" (Argus Americas Crude, which includes the Argus Mexico Maya Spot Price, FOB US Gulf Coast assessment) — i.e. published daily on each business day, excluding the holidays listed in Argus's annual publishing schedule.
release_schedule.note: This is a daily spot price assessment published every trading day as part of the Argus Americas Crude report/PDF, consistent with the corpus's releases_per_year=252 (roughly the number of US business days in a year). Argus publishes an annual 'Publishing Schedule' PDF (e.g. https://www.argusmedia.com/-/media/project/argusmedia/mainsite/english/documents-and-files/publishing-schedule/publishing-schedule-2026-pdf.pdf) listing specific holiday non-publication dates, but that PDF was blocked by robots.txt and could not be fetched directly to confirm exact 2026 holiday gaps.

dependencies.basis: The MRF Guidelines state that Alberta Energy determines a well's monthly revenue by 'multiplying volumes of all the hydrocarbons produced, including test production, by their respective par/reference prices as published in the Information Letters available on the Alberta Energy website' (Revenue = Production * Par Price), and that 'the price component of oil is determined by using the monthly oil par price (PP) based on density'. The rate brackets are literal par-price thresholds: PP <= 251.70, 251.70 < PP <= 409.02, 409.02 < PP <= 723.64, 723.64 < PP. The Petroleum Royalty Regulation, 2017 s.5 gives the Minister the power to 'determine an amount per cubic metre as the par price' for light, medium, heavy and ultra-heavy oil, and its Schedule sets rp% = [(par price - 251.70) x ...].
dependencies.evidence_quote: The price component of oil is determined by using the monthly oil par price (PP) based on density.

dependencies.basis: Under MRF the post-C* royalty rate is rp% + rq%, where 'the price component (rp) is the percentage rate based on the par/reference price for each hydrocarbon'. C* is drawn down each month by revenue 'valued using the respective hydrocarbon par/reference price', and the gas rate tables in the guidelines are indexed on the monthly reference price in $/GJ. The Natural Gas Royalty Regulation, 2017 correspondingly requires the Minister to prescribe a Gas Reference Price 'for January, 2017 and for each subsequent' production month along with the methane, ethane, propane, butanes and pentanes plus ISC reference prices.

reference_period.stated_as: Gas Reference Price prescribed 'for January, 2017 and for each subsequent' production month; C* is drawn down each month at that month's reference price.

dependencies.evidence_quote: the price component (rp) is the percentage rate based on the par/reference price for each hydrocarbon

dependencies.basis: Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009 (AR 223/2008) s.29 sets the gross royalty rate as RG% = 1% + [FG (A - B)], where FG is '8% divided by $65 per barrel', A is 'the lesser of the WTI price for the given month ... and $120 per barrel' and B is 'the lesser of A for the month and $55 per barrel'. s.29(3)(a) defines the monthly WTI price as 'the simple average of the WTI prices for the trading days of the preceding month, excluding any days where the trading price was at or below $0 per barrel', and s.29(4)(a) defines the daily WTI price as 'the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract of West Texas Intermediate crude futures as traded on NYMEX'. The same A term drives the post-payout net royalty percentage factor, NRPF = 25% + (FN (A - B)).

reference_period.stated_as: 'the simple average of the WTI prices for the trading days of the preceding month' — Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009 s.29(3)(a).

dependencies.evidence_quote: the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract of West Texas Intermediate crude futures as traded on NYMEX

dependencies.basis: Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009 s.29(3) makes the Canadian-dollar WTI price 'the product of' the average US-dollar NYMEX settlement price and 'the simple average of the daily actual USD/CAD (noon) exchange rates for that month'. s.29(4)(c) specifies that 'the actual USD/CAD (noon) exchange rate for a day is that published in relation to that day by the Bank of Canada', and s.29(7) provides a substitution mechanism 'if the Bank of Canada no longer publishes' it.
dependencies.evidence_quote: the actual USD/CAD (noon) exchange rate for a day is that published in relation to that day by the Bank of Canada

dependencies.basis: Bitumen Valuation Methodology (Ministerial) Regulation (AR 232/2008) s.1(3)(g) provides that 'the WTI price for a month shall be the simple average of the WTI prices for the trading days of the current month expressed in U.S. dollars', where a daily WTI price is 'the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract West Texas Intermediate crude futures as traded on NYMEX'. That WTI term enters the monthly Floor Price directly: Floor Price = greater of $10/m3 and MMSP - $250/m3 - A, where A is the greater of $0 and (BRENT - WTI).

reference_period.stated_as: 'the WTI price for a month shall be the simple average of the WTI prices for the trading days of the current month' — BVM (Ministerial) Regulation s.1(3)(g).

dependencies.evidence_quote: the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract West Texas Intermediate crude futures as traded on NYMEX

dependencies.basis: BVM (Ministerial) Regulation s.1(5) requires the Mexico Maya spot price, the Brent price, the WTI price, the synbit premium and the BVM Dilbit Value all to be 'converted from U.S. dollars per barrel to Canadian dollars per m3' using a conversion factor of 6.29234 barrels per m3 and 'the simple average of the daily actual USD/CAD (noon) exchange rates for the month published by the Bank of Canada, rounded to 5 decimal places'.
dependencies.evidence_quote: the simple average of the daily actual USD/CAD (noon) exchange rates for the month published by the Bank of Canada, rounded to 5 decimal places

dependencies.basis: The Economic Outlook chapter forecasts the WTI benchmark by name in its Fiscal Year Assumptions table and treats it as the driver of the fiscal position: 'The West Texas Intermediate oil price is expected to average US$60.50 per barrel', with the differential to WCS at Hardisty forecast separately from US$11.20/bbl in 2025-26 to US$14.30/bbl by 2028-29. The revenue chapter attributes the $3.1 billion fall in non-renewable resource revenue to 'a combination of lower WTI prices and a wider light-heavy differential', and the budget notes a US$1/bbl move in the differential is worth roughly $670 million.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The West Texas Intermediate oil price is expected to average US$60.50 per barrel

dependencies.basis: The Fiscal Plan's Fiscal Year Assumptions table carries an 'Alberta Reference Price (Cdn$/GJ)' row beside WTI and WCS, and the footnote to that table states that 'The Alberta Reference Price (used in natural gas royalty calculations) represents the average field price of all Alberta gas sales which normally follows the Western Canada regional benchmark.' The revenue chapter then forecasts natural gas and by-product royalties off that assumption — the ARP is forecast at C$3.00/GJ in 2026-27, up from C$1.70/GJ in 2025-26, with royalties rising from $0.7 billion to $0.9 billion.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The Alberta Reference Price (used in natural gas royalty calculations) represents the average field price of all Alberta gas sales which normally follows the Western Canada regional benchmark.

dependencies.basis: The Fiscal Plan reports the in-year revision against the same energy price assumptions the Economic Outlook set at budget: non-renewable resource revenue is 'a $0.8 billion decrease from budget', because 'The West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price is expected to average US$61.50 per barrel (/bbl) in 2025-26, a US$6.50/bbl decrease from the Budget 2025 estimate' and 'the light-heavy differential is expected to average US$11.20/bbl for 2025-26, US$5.90/bbl narrower than budgeted'. The in-year statements exist to restate revenue against a revised version of the budget's price forecast.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price is expected to average US$61.50 per barrel (/bbl) in 2025-26, a US$6.50/bbl decrease from the Budget 2025 estimate

dependencies.basis: The 2025 Alberta Linear Property Assessment Minister's Guidelines define 'AER means the Alberta Energy Regulator' and then read assessment inputs straight out of its records: for pipelines and wells licensed by the AER 'the assessment must reflect the characteristics and specifications as of October 31 of the assessment year, as contained in the records of the AER'. Pipeline assessment classification codes are set by 'pipeline material, outside diameter, and the maximum operating pressure ... as contained in the records of the AER', and well depth is taken field by field — 'Total depth (field WELL-TOTAL-DEPTH of AER General Well File record type 010)', 'Deepest shoe set depth (field SHOE-SET-DEPTH of AER General Well File record type 040)', plug tops from record type 055. The guidelines also rely on the AER Insolvency List.

reference_period.stated_as: 'the assessment must reflect the characteristics and specifications as of October 31 of the assessment year, as contained in the records of the AER'.

dependencies.evidence_quote: Total depth (field WELL-TOTAL-DEPTH of AER General Well File record type 010)

dependencies.basis: Bitumen Valuation Methodology (Ministerial) Regulation (AR 232/2008) s.1(3)(f) defines the Brent price as 'the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract of the Brent crude futures as traded on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE)'. That term enters the monthly Floor Price through A = greater of $0 and (BRENT - WTI), alongside the WTI term already recorded. Promoted from _dropped in V0.5 under the commercial-source decision: the evidence is exactly as strong as the WTI edge and was only ever held back because ICE is a commercial exchange.

reference_period.stated_as: Daily ICE prompt-month Brent settlements entering the monthly Floor Price determination under BVM (Ministerial) Regulation s.1(3)(f).

dependencies.evidence_quote: the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract of the Brent crude futures as traded on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE)

dependencies.basis: Bitumen Valuation Methodology (Ministerial) Regulation (AR 232/2008) s.1(3)(e) states that 'the daily Mexico Maya Spot Price FOB at the U.S. Gulf Coast shall be as published by Argus Media Inc.' The MMSP is the leading term in the Floor Price: Floor Price = greater of $10/m3 and MMSP - $250/m3 - A. Alberta legislation names a private price-reporting agency by company name, which is as explicit as evidence gets.

reference_period.stated_as: Daily Argus Mexico Maya assessments entering the monthly Floor Price determination under BVM (Ministerial) Regulation s.1(3)(e).

dependencies.evidence_quote: the daily Mexico Maya Spot Price FOB at the U.S. Gulf Coast shall be as published by Argus Media Inc.

_dropped.why: The Budget 2026 Fiscal Plan says the Alberta Reference Price 'normally follows the Western Canada regional benchmark' (AECO), which is suggestive, but 'normally follows' is a correlation statement, not a calculation. The APMC's 'simplified netback model' inputs are not published as a formula, and AECO itself is a commercial index (ICE NGX) rather than an official statistical release, so it does not qualify as a graph node.

_dropped.edge: ab-bvm-components -> WCS-WTI broker index / CAPP Equalization Steering Committee values
_dropped.why: BVM Regulation s.1(3)(c) sets the WCS index as 'the weighted average, based on trading volumes, of the "WCS-WTI" index published for that month by the commodity brokers specified', and s.1(3)(d) takes the Condensate Allowance Price and CRW density from 'the Equalization Steering Committee and as published on the website of the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers'. Both are named in law but neither is a stable, identifiable public release; the broker list is even set by ministerial order.

_dropped.edge: ab-oilsands-royalty-rates -> AER ST3 / ST98 production statistics
_dropped.why: Intuitive but wrong in direction of causation. Royalty is computed from operator volumetric submissions through Petrinex, not from the AER's published statistical series; ST3 and ST98 are downstream summaries of the same raw volumes. No royalty document names an AER statistical report as an input.

The budget forecasts 'WCS @ Hardisty (Cdn$/bbl)' as a named assumption row, but the WCS assessment is produced by commercial brokers and price reporting agencies with no official publisher, so there is no report node to point at. The WTI edge captures the same relationship at the point where an identifiable publisher exists.

_dropped.edge: ab-bvm-components -> WCS-WTI broker index / CAPP Equalization Steering Committee values
_dropped.why: Still out after the V0.5 commercial-source decision, and for a different reason than ICE and Argus were. Those two failed the old officialness rule and the rule bent. This one fails identifiability, which no rule change fixes: BVM Regulation s.1(3)(c) sets the WCS index from 'the commodity brokers specified' in a list the Minister sets by order, so there is no stable publication to point a node at, and the CAPP Equalization Steering Committee values in s.1(3)(d) are committee outputs rather than a recurring release. A node needs a real, named, recurring publication; commercial is now allowed, unidentifiable is not.

reports.title: Local Government Fiscal Framework — Capital Funding Allocations
reports.description: Annual allocation of provincial capital funding to Alberta local governments, calculated by a formula set out in the Local Government Fiscal Framework Act. $800 million in 2026.
reports.cadence_note: Aggregate amounts must be communicated by September 30 two years in advance; individual allocations follow some weeks later.

entries.covers: Future LGFF capital funding levels for the 2028 funding year

release_schedule.rule: The LGFF Act requires that information on future funding levels is shared by September 30, 2 years prior to the funding year.
release_schedule.note: Page (updated/published March 23, 2026) states the statutory disclosure deadline; the most recent occurrence (Sept 30, 2025, covering the 2027 funding year) has already passed, so the next occurrence is Sept 30, 2026. No published multi-year release calendar was found beyond this stated statutory rule.

reports.title: Local Government Fiscal Framework — Operating Funding
reports.description: Annual operating funding component of the Local Government Fiscal Framework, $60 million per year, distributed to Alberta local governments.

entries.covers: 2027 LGFF Operating funding payment to municipalities

release_schedule.rule: Funding is allocated annually after legislative approval of the program budget, and authorization of program funding and individual allocations by the Minister of Municipal Affairs. Payments to municipalities occur by approximately June 30, following provincial budget approval (conditional on certification of the prior year's Statement of Funding and Expenditures, matching reported expenditures to the allocation, and submission of the executed Memorandum of Agreement).
release_schedule.note: Date is described by the publisher's own guidelines as 'approximately June 30' — an annual target, not a guaranteed fixed date. The June 30, 2026 payment for the current cycle has already passed relative to today (2026-08-11), so the next occurrence is projected for June 30, 2027. Sourced from the LGFF Operating Program Guidelines PDF (dated 2023-12-12, last modified 2024-03-12), linked from the publisher's 'Local Government Fiscal Framework program guidelines' Open Government page. Underlying allocation formula/amounts themselves are set via the provincial budget process (irregular relative to any fixed calendar date) but the annual payment-to-municipalities deadline is the stated recurring rule.

reports.title: Municipal Affairs Population List (MAPL)
reports.description: Annual official population counts for Alberta municipalities, Metis Settlements and First Nations communities, drawn from municipal or federal census results. Used by provincial ministries to determine municipal grants.
reports.cadence_note: Discontinued in 2020 with the repeal of the Determination of Population Regulation; resumed in 2023 under the Municipal Census Regulation.

release_schedule.note: The CKAN metadata for this dataset states 'updatefrequency: Annual' and shows resource creation dates for the last three editions: the 2023 population list was posted 2024-02-16, the 2024 population list was posted 2025-04-11, and the 2025 population list (most recent, current as of this query) was posted 2026-01-21. The list was discontinued after 2019 and publication resumed with the 2023 edition. Each numbered edition (e.g. '2025 population list') is published roughly a year after its reference year, but the exact month varies (Jan/Feb/Apr), so no single stated day exists. Next expected release would be the '2026 population list', likely appearing sometime between roughly January and June 2027 based on this pattern.

reports.title: Municipal (Census Subdivision) Population Estimates
reports.publisher: Alberta Treasury Board and Finance, Office of Statistics and Information
reports.description: Annual population estimates for Alberta census subdivisions by year, age and gender, including permanent and non-permanent residents.

entries.covers: Municipal (Census Subdivision) Population Estimates, next annual update (2016-2026)

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar found on Alberta.ca or the open.alberta.ca/open.canada.ca dataset pages. The dataset's own resource-update history shows the CSD-level municipal population estimates file has been refreshed in mid-January in the years for which we have confirmed dates: updated January 11, 2023 (covering 2016-2022) and updated January 14, 2026 (covering 2016-2025), consistent with a once-a-year January update pattern (releases_per_year=1 on file is consistent with this). No intervening years' exact update dates could be confirmed via search, so the pattern is based on two confirmed data points plus the current 'most recent update' timestamp; the office could be contacted directly (780-427-2071) to confirm exact cadence. The open.canada.ca dataset record lists overall dataset maintenance frequency as 'Quarterly', but that reflects the combined dataset (which also bundles a separate quarterly provincial-level population series updated June 17, 2026) rather than this specific municipal/CSD-level component, which itself only shows January updates.

reports.title: Municipal Financial Information Return (FIR)
reports.description: Standardised annual return summarising each municipality's audited financial statements — assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses, long term debt and property taxes. Required from every Alberta municipality by May 1.
reports.cadence_note: Due May 1 for the preceding financial year.

release_schedule.rule: Each municipality and each regional services commission must prepare annual audited financial statements and a financial information return (FIR). Both reports must be returned to Alberta Municipal Affairs by May 1 of each year, as required by the Municipal Government Act.
release_schedule.note: The 2026-05-01 deadline (for the 2025 fiscal year FIR) has already passed relative to today's date (2026-08-11), so the next occurrence is 2027-05-01. Extensions to this deadline can be requested and are evaluated by Municipal Affairs (see ma-financial-reporting-extension-requests.pdf), so an individual municipality's actual submission date could shift, but the standard statutory deadline is May 1.

reports.title: Municipal Financial and Statistical Data
reports.description: Annual compilation of every Alberta municipality's financial and statistical returns, including tangible capital assets, accumulated amortization, road length, assessment and tax rates.

entries.covers: Statutory deadline for municipalities to submit FY2026 audited financial statements, FIR and SIR to Alberta Municipal Affairs, which Municipal Affairs then compiles into the next edition of this report

release_schedule.rule: A municipality is required to submit to Alberta Municipal Affairs, by May 1 of each year, its financial statements and auditor's report pertaining to the previous year, as well as a financial information return (FIR) that is a summary of information from the audited financial statements. Municipalities also submit statistical information returns (SIR) each year as required under the Municipal Government Act.
release_schedule.note: This is the statutory submission deadline that feeds the compiled dataset, not a publication date Municipal Affairs itself commits to. CKAN metadata (open.alberta.ca API, checked 2026-08-11) confirms updatefrequency='Annual' and shows the 2025 financial-year resource already has real content as of last_modified 2026-08-05 (following the May 1, 2026 deadline for FY2025 data). Historically the compiled dataset resource for a given fiscal year has appeared/been substantively updated anywhere from ~1 to ~6+ months after the following May 1 deadline (e.g. FY2022 resource created 2023-06-05, FY2023 resource created 2024-08-29, FY2024 last substantively updated 2026-07-16), so the exact month the FY2026 edition appears cannot be pinned down beyond 'sometime after 2027-05-01'.

reports.title: Provincial Equalized Assessment Report
reports.description: Annual adjustment of every municipality's taxable assessment to a common basis, producing a uniform provincial measure of property wealth. Determines each municipality's share of requisitions.

release_schedule.note: Alberta Municipal Affairs publishes this annual series ('Provincial equalized assessment report', ISSN 2368-657X) on the Open Government portal every year, consistently in late October/early November. CKAN resource-creation timestamps for the last several editions: Provincial 2022 report created 2021-10-29; Provincial 2023 report created 2022-10-31; Provincial 2024 report created 2023-10-31; Provincial 2025 report created 2024-11-01; Provincial 2026 report created 2025-10-30 (this is the current/most-recent edition as of 2026-08-11). No formal forward-looking release calendar or stated statutory publication date was found — the pattern is inferred purely from past posting dates. The dataset's own metadata field 'updatefrequency' is listed as 'Annual'. Based on this pattern, the next edition (Provincial 2027 equalized assessment report) is expected in late October/early November 2026. NOTE: the corpus's existing url (open.alberta.ca/opendata/equalized-assessment-report) actually resolves to a different, related dataset titled 'Updated Equalized Assessment' (a supplemental mid-cycle update resource), not this annual 'Provincial equalized assessment report' series — see url_correction.

entries.covers: Provincial 2026 equalized assessment report (current/most recent edition)
Provincial 2027 equalized assessment report (next expected edition)

reports.title: Education Property Tax Requisition Comparison Report
reports.description: Annual statement of the education property tax requisition levied on each Alberta municipality, split between residential/farm and non-residential. Municipalities are obliged to collect it on the province's behalf. $3.1 billion in 2025.

release_schedule.note: Late-February window, 5 years running. Candidate edge, not yet added: this report methodologically depends on Alberta's 'equalized assessment' dataset, a separate Municipal Affairs publication — needs a proper basis before becoming a real edge.

dependencies.basis: Calgary and Edmonton allocations weight population at 48 per cent, and the fact sheet names Municipal (Census Subdivision) Population Estimates as the data source.
Calgary and Edmonton allocations weight education property tax requisitions at 48 per cent, sourced from the Education Property Tax Requisition Comparison Report.
Allocations to local governments other than Calgary and Edmonton weight population at 65 per cent, taken from the Municipal Affairs Population List.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Data for Other Local Governments 2026 calculations are based on the 2023 Municipal Affairs Population List (MAPL), 2023 book value of tangible capital assets (excluding electricity and gas distribution systems, machinery and equipment, and land), average annual cumulative amortization (excluding electricity and gas distribution systems, machinery and equipment, and land) for the 2019-2023 period, and 2023 length of local roads.

dependencies.basis: Tangible capital assets (15 per cent), five-year average cumulative amortization (10 per cent) and length of local roads (10 per cent) are all drawn from named schedules of the Municipal Financial and Statistical Data.
Needs-based funding eligibility is set by comparing a municipality's equalized assessment per capita, or per kilometre of road, against the provincial average.
dependencies.evidence_quote: For example, if average provincial equalized assessment per capita is $150,000, then the 80 per cent threshold is $120,000 (0.8 x $150,000), meaning any municipality with a population less than 10,000 and equalized assessment per capita below $120,000 receives needs-based funding based on its weighted population.

dependencies.basis: The dataset is compiled from the financial information return and statistical information return submitted annually by every Alberta municipality.

Alberta's education property tax page states the mechanism directly: 'Municipal Affairs establishes the provincial mill rate used to determine each municipality's share of the provincial education tax. The provincial equalized assessment base used to determine education property taxes this year reflects 2024 property values.' It gives the rates in force: 'Education property tax rates will increase to $2.84 per $1,000 of equalized assessment for residential/farmland properties and $4.17 per $1,000 of equalized assessment for non-residential properties in 2026-27', raising the requisition 'from $3.1 billion in 2025-26 to $3.6 billion in 2026-27'. Both figures verified verbatim. [Basis moved here 2026-08-07 from ontario-ompf-mpac.json, where it lived as a deliberately-superseding duplicate copy; see that file's _dropped note.]

reference_period.stated_as: Annual, with a two-year lag stated outright: 'The provincial equalized assessment base used to determine education property taxes this year reflects 2024 property values.' The reading is once a year against a base two years stale, which is a documented lag rather than an inferred one.

dependencies.evidence_quote: Municipal Affairs establishes the provincial mill rate used to determine each municipality's share of the provincial education tax. The provincial equalized assessment base used to determine education property taxes this year reflects 2024 property values.

_note: The hub layer. The Local Government Fiscal Framework Act indexes municipal capital funding to provincial revenue from three years prior — a statutory link running straight from Alberta's fiscal position to every municipality's road-repair budget. This slice also closes the detached education pair by connecting the K-12 funding manual to the budget that sets its grant rates.

reports.title: Alberta Budget — Fiscal Plan
reports.description: The centrepiece of Alberta's annual budget, setting out revenue, expense and the fiscal position across a three-year horizon. Contains the economic outlook, capital plan and tax plan chapters, and is the source of the provincial revenue figures that statutory funding formulas key off.
reports.cadence_note: Tabled in late February for the fiscal year beginning 1 April.

release_schedule.note: Alberta has tabled its fiscal plan in the last week of February in every recent year (27 February 2020, 28 February 2023, 27 February 2024). The Fiscal Planning and Transparency Act is believed to set a statutory deadline of 28 February, but no citation for that provision has been read yet, so this stays observed rather than stated-rule and the whole month is claimed rather than a day. Tighten to 'stated-rule' with a day once the section is quoted.

reports.title: Fiscal Update and Economic Statement
reports.description: In-year revision of Alberta's revenue, expense and deficit forecasts against the tabled budget. The vehicle by which future municipal funding envelopes are communicated in advance.
reports.cadence_note: Three per year — on or before the last day of August, November and February. A Final Results year-end report follows by the end of June.

entries.covers: 2026-27 First Quarter Fiscal Update and Economic Statement
2026-27 Mid-year Fiscal Update and Economic Statement

release_schedule.rule: Quarterly fiscal and economic updates on the budget are provided 3 times a year – on or before the last day of August, November and February. (Alberta Treasury Board and Finance, alberta.ca/budget-documents)
release_schedule.note: As of 2026-08-11 the 2026-27 First Quarter update has not yet been posted on alberta.ca/budget-documents or open.alberta.ca. Historical Q1 releases confirm the pattern: 2023-24 Q1 released Aug 31 2023, 2024-25 Q1 released Aug 29 2024, 2025-26 Q1 released Aug 28 2025, so the actual 2026-27 Q1 release will likely land within the last few days of August 2026 rather than precisely on the 31st. In practice only Q1 and Mid-year 'Fiscal Update and Economic Statement' documents are produced each fiscal year (plus a June 'Final Results' year-end report, matching releases_per_year=3 on file); a distinct 'last-day-of-February' third-quarter update, referenced in the government's general 3x/year description, has not been produced as a separate document under this title since ~2019-20 — that slot is effectively superseded by the annual Budget tabling.

reports.title: Alberta Economic Outlook
reports.description: The province's forecast for growth, employment, inflation, population and energy prices. Published as a chapter of the fiscal plan; the assumptions underneath every provincial revenue projection.

entries.covers: Budget 2026 Economic Outlook (tabled Feb 26, 2026, current edition on alberta.ca/economic-outlook)

release_schedule.note: The 'Alberta Economic Outlook' is not a standalone report with its own publication calendar; it is the economic-outlook chapter/page of the province's annual Budget Fiscal Plan, published by Treasury Board and Finance alongside the provincial budget. Alberta budgets have consistently been tabled in late February each year (e.g., Feb 25 2021, Feb 27 2025, Feb 26 2026), so the next edition is expected around late February 2027. This is an observed pattern (no explicit publisher-stated release-date rule was found), consistent with releases_per_year=1 already on file. Quarterly fiscal updates (e.g., Q1/Q2 fiscal updates) also touch on the economic outlook but the alberta.ca/economic-outlook page itself appears tied to the annual budget cycle.

dependencies.basis: The LGFF Act sets a Revenue Index Factor comparing provincial revenue three years prior against four years prior, and municipal capital funding rises or falls by exactly that percentage. 2025 funding rose 13.6% to $820 million on the strength of 13.6% revenue growth between 2021-22 and 2022-23.
Aggregate LGFF funding amounts must be communicated to municipalities two years in advance, and are announced through the quarterly fiscal update.
The economic outlook is a chapter of the fiscal plan and supplies the growth, employment, inflation and energy price assumptions from which every revenue line is forecast.
Each quarterly update revises the revenue, expense and deficit forecasts set out in the tabled fiscal plan, and is reported against it.

reference_period.stated_as: 'Each quarterly update revises the revenue, expense and deficit forecasts set out in the tabled fiscal plan' — three updates a year despite the name.

dependencies.basis: Grant rates in the Funding Manual for School Authorities are set by the K-12 education allocation voted in the provincial budget; the manual distributes the envelope the fiscal plan establishes.

Exports and imports (especially minerals and gas) that enter the national accounts are taken from the merchandise-trade statistics compiled from customs and specialized mineral/gas export registers. Evidence: "Brindar las estadísticas de exportaciones de bienes para el diseño, implementación y monitoreo de políticas públicas o privadas, así como para la elaboración de las Cuentas Nacionales y Balanza de Pagos"
dependencies.evidence_quote: Brindar las estadísticas básicas de importaciones de bienes para el diseño, implementación y monitoreo de políticas públicas o privadas, así como para la elaboración de las Cuentas Nacionales y Balanza de Pagos, entre otros usos.

dependencies.basis: The 2017 reference-year revision of Bolivia’s national accounts incorporates the recommendations of the System of National Accounts 2008. Evidence: "actualizar la metodología para incorporar las recomendaciones del Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales 2008 (SCN 2008) ... uso de las medias encadenadas de volumen y la medición de los servicios de intermediación financiera medidos indirectamente (SIFMI) en línea con las recomendaciones del SCN 2008."
dependencies.evidence_quote: Este trabajo para implementar los lineamientos metodológicos internacionales del Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales 2008 recomendado por Naciones Unidas, fue acompañado técnicamente por organismos de reconocida experticia y trayectoria que velaron por la calidad y rigurosidad metodológica del mismo.

dependencies.basis: Colombia’s balance of payments is produced according to the sixth edition of the IMF Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual. Evidence: "La balanza de pagos de Colombia registra los flujos ... de acuerdo con el Manual de Balanza de Pagos y Posición de Inversión Internacional del FMI, versión 6."
dependencies.evidence_quote: La balanza de pagos de Colombia registra los flujos reales y financieros que el país intercambia con el resto de las economías del mundo, de acuerdo con el Manual de Balanza de Pagos y Posición de Inversión Internacional del FMI, versión 6.

dependencies.basis: Colombia’s national accounts currently follow the methodological recommendations of the 2008 System of National Accounts. Evidence: "Actualmente, el DANE sigue las recomendaciones metodológicas del SCN2008. ... El sistema actual de cuentas nacionales del DANE se basa en el SCN2008."
dependencies.evidence_quote: En general los trabajos de cuentas nacionales se basan en acuerdos y recomendaciones internacionales. El que rige actualmente es el Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales 2008 (SCN 2008), preparado bajo los auspicios del Grupo Intersecretarial de trabajo sobre Cuentas Nacionales

dependencies.basis: Colombia’s IPC uses the international COICOP classification structure. Evidence: "el impacto del uso de la nomenclatura basada en el estándar internacional COICOP en el IPC vigente desde enero de 2019 ... El estándar internacional COICOP define la caracterización de las clases de gasto"
dependencies.evidence_quote: El uso de una nomenclatura basada en el estándar internacional COICOP (Clasificación del consumo individual según su propósito, por sus siglas en inglés).

dependencies.basis: Weights of the Industrial Production Index are derived from value-added / gross-production ratios of the Annual Manufacturing Survey (EAM). Evidence: "Es un índice ponderado por la relación de valor agregado sobre la producción bruta de la EAM del año 2017 y se presenta en año base 2018."
dependencies.evidence_quote: Es un índice ponderado por la relación de valor agregado sobre la producción bruta de la EAM del año 2017 y se presenta en año base 2018.

dependencies.basis: Ecuador’s balance of payments is compiled according to the sixth edition of the IMF Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual. Evidence: "IMPLEMENTACIÓN DEL NUEVO MANUAL DE BALANZA DE PAGOS Y POSICIÓN DE INVERSIÓN INTERNACIONAL SEXTA EDICIÓN (MBP6) ... El BCE compila y divulga las estadísticas de la balanza de pagos del país ... presenta los resultados con cifras a partir de 2016"
dependencies.evidence_quote: El Banco Central del Ecuador consciente de estos cambios metodológicos y estándares en las estadísticas del sector externo, presenta los resultados con cifras a partir de 2016, en forma anual y trimestral.

dependencies.basis: Oil extraction and related activities in the production approach draw directly on production, price and export data supplied by EP Petroecuador. Evidence: "Información petrolera: producción, precios, entre otros EP Petroecuador ... Extracción de petróleo, gas natural y actividades de servicio relacionadas ... Información directa de Petroecuador, Exportaciones de Comercio Exterior"
dependencies.evidence_quote: Información petrolera: producción, precios, entre otros

dependencies.basis: Value-added estimates for many market activities rely on sales declared in the IVA form administered by the Internal Revenue Service (SRI). Evidence: "las ventas declaradas en el formulario del Impuesto al Valor Agregado (IVA) administrado por el Servicio de Rentas Internas (SRI)"
dependencies.evidence_quote: las ventas declaradas en el formulario del Impuesto al Valor Agregado (IVA) administrado por el Servicio de Rentas Internas (SRI)

dependencies.basis: Ecuador’s national accounts follow the conceptual framework of the 2008 System of National Accounts. Evidence: "The methodology applied in the production of CBE statistics follows international guidelines, such as the 2008 System of National Accounts (SNA 2008), recommended by the United Nations and the International Monetary Fund. ... CBE follows methodological recommendations of the 2008 System of National Accounts (SNA 2008)"
dependencies.evidence_quote: CBE follows methodological recommendations of the 2008 System of National Accounts (SNA 2008)

dependencies.basis: ENEMDU supplies labour-market and income information that feeds the national accounts compiled by the Banco Central del Ecuador. Evidence: "A su vez, permite alimentar el Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales, administrado por el Banco Central del Ecuador (BCE)." (Direction flipped 2026-09-04: the basis names ec-cuentas-nacionales as the consumer of ec-enemdu; the edge was minted the other way round — Thomas's ruling on HANDOFF item 1, list in Claude outputs/direction-suspect-jp-kr-2026-09-03.json.)
dependencies.evidence_quote: A su vez, permite alimentar el Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales, administrado por el Banco Central del Ecuador (BCE).

dependencies.basis: The IPC basket and classification structure follow the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP/CCIF). Evidence: "Adaptar la estructura de la Canasta Básica de Bienes y Servicios a la Clasificación del Consumo Individual por Finalidades (CCIF), para asegurar la comparabilidad internacional del indicador."
dependencies.evidence_quote: Adaptar la estructura de la Canasta Básica de Bienes y Servicios a la Clasificación del Consumo Individual por Finalidades (CCIF) que permita así, la comparabilidad internacional.

dependencies.basis: NBI structural poverty is calculated from ENEMDU (and census) housing, education and service variables; ENEMDU is the official annual source. Evidence: "se oficializó a la Encuesta Nacional de Empleo, Desempleo y Subempleo (ENEMDU) como su fuente oficial. ... El documento de homologación incluyó los datos del período 2008–2010, y la serie se actualiza cada diciembre con base en esta misma encuesta."
dependencies.evidence_quote: El NBI se calcula desde el 2008 con la fuente ENEMDU por razones metodológicas.

dependencies.basis: Official poverty and extreme-poverty lines (originally estimated from consumption surveys) are updated monthly/periodically by the Consumer Price Index so that current-period incomes can be compared to real lines. Evidence: "A partir de diciembre de 2007, la pobreza por ingresos se obtiene actualizando la línea oficial de pobreza por consumo mediante el Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC)."
dependencies.evidence_quote: A partir de diciembre de 2007, la pobreza por ingresos se obtiene actualizando la línea oficial de pobreza por consumo mediante el Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC).

dependencies.basis: Tax collection (administered by SRI) constitutes the largest non-oil revenue source incorporated into the national budget proforma. Evidence: "En las fases de programación y formulación de la proforma de ingresos del Presupuesto General del Estado, los servicios tributario y aduanero deberán remitir ... los planes de gestión y metas de recaudación de los ingresos tributarios que administran"
dependencies.evidence_quote: En las fases de programación y formulación de la proforma de ingresos del Presupuesto General del Estado, los servicios tributario y aduanero deberán remitir en los plazos que se fijarán en las directrices presupuestarias, los planes de gestión y metas de recaudación de los ingresos tributarios que administran

dependencies.basis: Exports and imports of goods that enter the expenditure-side national accounts and quarterly GDP are taken from foreign-trade statistics (customs/SUNAT). Evidence: "statistics on Foreign Trade and tax collection from SUNAT are used. ... SUNAT Imports and Exports"
dependencies.evidence_quote: The BCRP's Balance of Payments Division provides data on exports and imports of goods and nonfinancial services in nominal terms.

dependencies.basis: Peru’s national accounts with base year 2007 incorporate the recommendations of the 2008 System of National Accounts. Evidence: "se han incorporado nuevos elementos conceptuales recomendados por la Organización de las Naciones Unidas en el Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales de 2008. ... de acuerdo a las recomendaciones establecidas en el Manual del Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales 2008 de Naciones Unidas."
dependencies.evidence_quote: elaborado en el marco de la actualización de las Cuentas Nacionales con año base 2007, considerando las recomendaciones establecidas en el Manual del Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales 2008 de Naciones Unidas.

dependencies.basis: Peru’s CPI is classified according to the Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP). Evidence: "Product coverage: The data covers 586 products, under 276 headings, 151 subclasses, 89 classes, 43 groups, and 12 divisions according to the Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP)."
dependencies.evidence_quote: The data covers 586 products, under 276 headings, 151 subclasses, 89 classes, 43 groups, and 12 divisions according to the Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP).

dependencies.basis: Canon and related mining transfers are distributed through the public-sector budget framework administered by MEF, based on income-tax and royalty collections from mining activity. Evidence: "el Canon Minero está constituido por el 50% del total de ingresos y rentas obtenidos por el Estado en la actividad minera ... se transfiere a los gobiernos regionales y gobiernos locales a partir del mes siguiente de recibir la información de la Superintendencia Nacional de Aduanas y de Administración Tributaria (SUNAT)"
dependencies.evidence_quote: El Canon Minero, está constituido por el 50% (cincuenta por ciento) del Impuesto a la Renta que obtiene el Estado y que pagan los titulares de la actividad minera por el aprovechamiento de los recursos minerales, metálicos y no metálicos.

dependencies.basis: The monthly national production index is a weighted aggregate of sectoral indices that uses the annual percentage structure of value added from the national accounts base year as fixed weights. Evidence: "El Índice Mensual de la Producción Nacional, se obtiene mediante la agregación ponderada de los índices sectoriales ... utilizando como factores de ponderación, la estructura porcentual anual del año base de las Cuentas Nacionales."
dependencies.evidence_quote: El Índice Mensual de la Producción Nacional, se obtiene mediante la agregación ponderada de los índices sectoriales que están comprendidos en el campo coyuntural, utilizando como factores de ponderación, la estructura porcentual anual del año base de las Cuentas Nacionales.

dependencies.basis: Fishing and aquaculture physical output is one of the direct sectoral indicators that enter the monthly production index. Evidence: "Sectores considerados: - Sector Agropecuario - Sector Pesca - Sector Minería e Hidrocarburos - Sector Manufactura"
dependencies.evidence_quote: Sectores considerados: Sector Agropecuario Sector Pesca Sector Minería e Hidrocarburos Sector Manufactura

reports.title: Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC)
reports.publisher: Australian Bureau of Statistics and Statistics New Zealand (Tatauranga Aotearoa)
reports.description: The single industry classification used by both Australian and New Zealand official statistics, and the structural twin of `naics` — a classification agreed and maintained jointly by the statistical agencies of more than one country, from which each publishes national statistics. Its Preface is signed by both national statisticians: "Dennis Trewin / Brian Pink — Australian Statistician / Government Statistician — Australian Bureau of Statistics, Statistics New Zealand". Catalogue no. 1292.0; hierarchical, four levels (Division, Subdivision, Group, Class), 19 divisions and 86 subdivisions in the 2006 edition. Replaced two separate national classifications, the Australian Standard Industrial Classification (ASIC, 1969/1978/1983) and the New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (NZSIC, 1970/1975/1987), both of which were themselves derived from ISIC.
reports.cadence_note: Two editions in thirty-plus years — 1993 and 2006 — with a Revision 1.0 (Feb 2006) and Revision 2.0 (26 June 2013) of the 2006 edition. Next release listed by the ABS as 'Unknown'. Not an annual release; releases_per_year is nominal, and deliberately lower than `naics`'s 0.2 because ANZSIC has no five-year cycle.

release_schedule.note: ANZSIC is a joint ABS/Stats NZ industry classification standard revised only as needed, not on a fixed cycle. History: ANZSIC 1993 (original), ANZSIC 2006 Revision 1.0, ANZSIC 2006 Revision 2.0 (released 26 June 2013). The ABS 'latest-release' page itself lists 'Next release: Unknown'. No stated rule or calendar for a future revision was found; the ANZSCO (occupation) classification has an active comprehensive review underway, but that is a separate standard from ANZSIC (industry).

reports.title: International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC)
reports.description: The United Nations' industry classification and the acknowledged parent of most national industrial classifications, including ANZSIC and its two predecessors. Its absence from this corpus was a hole of the same shape as the missing `gasb-standards` that the associated-states pass had to fill: `naics` was present with eight inbound edges while the classification NAICS itself is aligned to was not represented at all. Adopted 1948; revisions 1 (1958), 2 (1968), 3 (1990), 3.1 (2002), 4 (2007) and 5 (endorsed 2023, publication forthcoming).
reports.cadence_note: Six revisions in seventy-five years. Rev. 5 was endorsed by the UN Statistical Commission at its 54th session in 2023 and, as of this session's read of the UNSD page, is 'forthcoming' in published form while being distributed as introduction, explanatory notes and structure files. releases_per_year is nominal.

release_schedule.note: ISIC has no publication calendar or fixed revision cycle. Revisions occur irregularly and infrequently (Rev.3: 1989, Rev.3.1: 2002, Rev.4: 2008, Rev.5: endorsed by the UN Statistical Commission at its 54th session in March 2023). National adaptation of Rev.5 is targeted by 2025, business register updates by 2026, and statistical program implementation from 2027, but these are implementation milestones for the already-published Rev.5, not a future release date. The UN Committee of Experts on International Statistical Classifications recommended a five-year revision cycle for ISIC/CPC (raised at the 55th Statistical Commission session, 2024), but as of the 56th session (2025) documents, this had not been formally adopted -- a new Standing Task Team on ISIC and CPC was instead tasked with developing a revision-cycle strategy proposal. No computable next revision date exists yet.

reports.title: Australian Industry
reports.description: The ABS's annual industry-performance release — employment, industry value added, sales and income by ANZSIC division — compiled from the Economic Activity Survey and Business Activity Statement data supplied to the Australian Taxation Office. Minted here for one purpose: it is the Australian end of the ANZSIC bridge, and the first `AU` node in this corpus that is not part of the government-finance pass.

release_schedule.note: ABS labels this publication 'Annual' but does not publish a dated release calendar or a stated rule for exactly when the annual edition appears each year. Observed past editions cluster in late May to mid June. Note: the '18/09/2026' (or 17/09/2026 per the ABS industry release calendar) date shown as 'Next release' on the latest-release page is NOT the next annual edition — it is a supplementary datacube/article release ('Additional detailed article and datacube for Wholesale trade and Retail trade') for the same 2024-25 financial year edition, confirmed via https://www.abs.gov.au/release-calendar/future-releases-calendar/202609/rcc_industry. The next full annual edition (covering 2025-26 financial year) is therefore projected for around May-June 2027 based on the observed pattern, not September 2026.

reports.title: Annual Enterprise Survey
reports.description: Stats NZ's annual financial-performance and financial-position survey of New Zealand businesses, running since the 1985/86 survey year and covering, on its own account, around 80% of GDP. The New Zealand end of the ANZSIC bridge. Its DataInfo+ metadata is unusually forthcoming about its own downstream use — it names the national accounts, the Tourism Satellite Account, the Non-profit Institutions Satellite Account, Business Price Indexes and Regional GDP as consumers — which makes it a promising source node for a later Stats NZ pass; see `_dropped`.

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ does not publish a fixed release-calendar date far in advance for AES, but the provisional AES release has landed consistently in late June for the past three years: 2023 FY (provisional) released 1 Jul 2024, 2024 FY (provisional) released 27 Jun 2025, and 2025 FY (provisional) released 25 Jun 2026. Based on this pattern the 2026 FY (provisional) release is projected for late June 2027; a final (non-provisional) AES release also follows later in the year but no consistent date pattern was found for it.

Preface: "International comparability has been enhanced by aligning the classification, as far as possible, with the upcoming revision of the International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) (Revision 4)." However, the degree of alignment able to be achieved is sometimes adversely affected by competing classification principles e.g. a different organisation or structure of Australian or New Zealand industry, or a lack of significance of some internationally recognised economic activities in the two economies." The parentage is stated for the predecessors too: the 1969 ASIC "was based at the broader levels on the ISIC", the 1970 NZSIC was "based on ISIC, Rev.2", and the driver for a single joint classification was "the need to update each country's classifications to align with ISIC, Rev.3 issued in 1990." The joint ABS/Stats NZ authorship — "The Australian Bureau of Statistics and Statistics New Zealand jointly developed this classification to improve the comparability of industry statistics between the two countries and with the rest of the world", verified directly by this session in the volume's Preface — is a property of the node's `publisher` field, and this corpus draws no edge from an authorship fact. `Research.1.md`'s one rule is that an edge is a documented statement that one report uses another as an input, and a classification does not take its own authors as inputs. The tie exists only because this session also minted `au-abs-australian-industry` and `nz-statsnz-aes`, one citing release on each side, so that a path now runs AU release -> anzsic <- NZ release. The direction is the other way and the target is not the right node. The AES DataInfo+ item states, under 'Main users of the data': "The Annual Enterprise Survey data forms the basis of Statistics New Zealand's national accounts statistics including: Production/Industry Accounts, Institutional Sector Accounts, Inter-Industry Study, Provisional National Accounts." And in the objectives: the AES provides "the main accounting aggregates needed to compile the National Accounts estimates", including "annual benchmarks for the reconciliation of quarterly and annual Gross Domestic Product (GDP) estimates" and "annual updates of Input - Output tables". That is a producer-side claim of a real edge running national accounts -> AES, but the corpus holds only `nz-statsnz-national-accounts-income`, which is the quarterly institutional-sector income release, and the passage names four national-accounts products of which that is at best one. Minting `nz-statsnz-national-accounts-income -> nz-statsnz-aes` off a list that does not name it by release title would be exactly the kind of loose match this branch has been catching in external research. The AES is designed and published not at ANZSIC level but at NZSIOC level 4 — "The AES data is to be used with caution below industry design level (NZSIOC level 4). The survey is not designed to support analysis below this level", and "Additional tables were released at level 4 of the New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification (NZSIOC)" (2011). _dropped.edge: anzsic -> isic, at a named revision (caveat on a minted edge, not a dropped one)
_dropped.why: The edge is minted but the revision is deliberately not pinned, and the reason is worth recording because it is a general hazard for classification nodes. ANZSIC 2006's Preface aligns it to "the upcoming revision of the ISIC (Revision 4)" — that is, to a document that did not yet exist when ANZSIC 2006 was published in February 2006, ISIC Rev.4 having been expected in 2007. The volume's own shipped correspondences are to a different revision again: "Correspondences (or concordances) between ANZSIC 2006 and ANZSIC 1993 are shown in the Correspondences section, together with correspondences between ANZSIC 2006 and ISIC Rev. 3.1." So the classification is designed against Rev.4 and machine-mapped to Rev.3.1, while ISIC itself is now at Rev.5 (endorsed 2023) and ANZSIC has not been re-based. `isic` is therefore modelled as one node covering the classification across revisions, on the same convention as `naics`, and the revision detail is left in this note rather than forced into the edge.

ANSWERED 2026-08-09 (cheap-check pass), and the entry's own instinct was right: ANZSCO IS NOT A BRIDGE NODE AND SHOULD NOT BE MINTED AS ONE. The governance question the entry insisted on asking first turns out to be the whole answer -- joint management has ENDED. The ABS media release 'ANZSCO Change' (8 October 2024, abs.gov.au/media-centre/media-releases/anzsco-change, fetched this session) announces that Australia replaced ANZSCO with the "Occupation Standard Classification for Australia (OSCA), 2024, version 1.0", released 6 December 2024, and that New Zealand introduced its own tailored occupational classification effective 20 November 2024; the two agencies agreed that "the benefits of joint management are no longer compelling" given the growing differences between the two labour markets, and will instead "develop concordances to map between classifications to maintain comparability, data continuity and time-series analysis". So the structure that makes `anzsic` genuinely bi-national -- one classification, two national statisticians -- has no occupational counterpart as of December 2024. The drift was visible in the last joint edition too: the ABS's own ANZSCO 2022 Introduction says ANZSCO "was jointly developed by the ABS, Stats NZ and the then Australian Government Department of Education, Employment and Workplace Relations" but describes both recent revisions as Australia-only -- "In 2021, a targeted revision related to selected areas of the Australian labour market was undertaken by the ABS. Another revision related to different selected areas of the Australian labour market has been undertaken by the ABS in 2022." Jointly developed once, unilaterally maintained since. ON THE ISCO HALF, which the entry correctly ranked second: what the ANZSCO 2022 Introduction offers is a "description of the comparability between ANZSCO and ISCO-08" -- comparability language, which is `Research.1.md` sec.5a's trap by name, not a parentage claim. That is not enough for a `methodology_depends_on` edge even if ANZSCO were minted. Distinct from the ANZSIC case, where the volume states derivation outright. NOT ADJUDICATED, flagged for whoever picks up occupational classifications properly: what replaced ANZSCO on the New Zealand side is reported in secondary immigration-sector coverage as Immigration New Zealand's 'National Occupation List (NOL)', in force 20 November 2024. That is an immigration instrument and may or may not be the same thing as the statistical classification the ABS release refers to; no Stats NZ primary source was read this session and the two should not be assumed identical. OSCA, by contrast, is unambiguously an ABS statistical classification and is a clean single-country node candidate whenever occupations are worked. ORIGINAL ENTRY BELOW. Item 26c of `research-input/the import-Research-Brief-XI.md`: ANZSCO, the occupational twin of ANZSIC, and whether its front matter names ISCO as parent. Not attempted this session — the ANZSIC work took the available fetching budget. Flagged rather than assumed: this session did not open ANZSCO and does not know whether it is still jointly maintained by both agencies. If it is not, it is not a bridge node and should not be minted as one — so the first question for a successor is the governance, not the ISCO parentage. Left on the list.

reports.title: Sistema Estadístico Nacional (SEN) / National Statistical System of Argentina
reports.description: The organised set of statistical services of national, provincial and municipal bodies that produce official statistics. Coordinated by INDEC under normative centralisation and executive decentralisation. Each province has a Dirección Provincial de Estadística (DPE).
reports._notes: Institutional framework node. Continuously referenced as the organisational architecture within which INDEC and the DPEs operate. Static in the sense that it is not a periodic statistical release, but load-bearing and recurringly cited.
_referenced_by: Relevamiento del Sistema Estadístico Nacional publications

reports.title: Dirección Provincial de Estadística de la Provincia de Buenos Aires
reports.publisher: Gobierno de la Provincia de Buenos Aires
reports.description: Provincial statistical office (DPE) that coordinates the Sistema Estadístico Provincial of Buenos Aires and participates in national operatives. Produces or compiles provincial and, where relevant, municipal-level indicators.
reports._notes: Provincial counterpart to IDECBA. Part of the SEN architecture established by Ley 17.622. Capacity is real but thinner and more dependent on INDEC frameworks than the CABA institute for the densest urban indicators.

reports.title: Dirección General de Estadística y Censos de la Provincia de Córdoba
reports.publisher: Gobierno de la Provincia de Córdoba
reports.description: Provincial statistical office that coordinates the Sistema Estadístico Provincial of Córdoba and produces or compiles provincial indicators under the SEN framework.
reports._notes: One of the stronger provincial statistical services. Explicitly listed in SEN directories and maintains an active web presence.

reports.title: Instituto Provincial de Estadística y Censos de Santa Fe (IPEC)
reports.publisher: Gobierno de la Provincia de Santa Fe
reports.description: Provincial statistical institute responsible for coordinating and producing official statistics for Santa Fe under the SEN architecture.
reports._notes: Strong provincial counterpart to IDECBA and the Córdoba DGEC. Maintains public statistical products and participates in national operatives.

reports.title: Dirección de Estadística y Censos de la Provincia del Chaco
reports.publisher: Gobierno de la Provincia del Chaco
reports.description: Provincial statistical service of Chaco. Exists within the SEN but with thinner independent publication cadence than Córdoba, Santa Fe or CABA institutes.
reports._notes: Homogeneity test: the office exists and is listed in SEN directories, yet most high-frequency and poverty indicators used analytically remain the national EPH/IPC cuts. Local packaging capacity is limited.

reports.title: Dirección de Estadística de la Provincia de Tucumán
reports.publisher: Gobierno de la Provincia de Tucumán
reports.description: Provincial statistical office (one of the older ones, founded 1881). Produces provincial indicators and participates in national operatives; also publishes local products such as the Canasta de Crianza.
reports._notes: Noroeste example with a long-standing provincial office and some original local products (e.g. Canasta de Crianza). Still operates inside the SEN framework and relies heavily on national survey infrastructure.

reports.title: Índice de Producción Industrial Minero (IPI minero)
reports.description: Monthly volume index of mining and hydrocarbon extraction activities. Covers crude oil, natural gas, metallic and non-metallic minerals, including lithium. Published with original and cumulative series.
reports._notes: Key short-term indicator for the energy and mining boom. First-half 2026: +8.4% cumulative. Driven by non-conventional oil (+35% range) and lithium carbonate (+49% range). Complements the manufacturing IPI.

reports.title: Vaca Muerta / producción de hidrocarburos no convencionales (Neuquén)
reports.description: Statistical representation of the Vaca Muerta shale play and non-conventional hydrocarbon production, concentrated in Neuquén. Dominates national crude-oil growth and is visible in the IPI minero and provincial export origin statistics.
reports._notes: Transformative energy node. Without Neuquén/Vaca Muerta, national crude production would be at multi-decade lows; with it, 2025 set records. Appears in IPI minero (non-conventional oil), provincial export origin (Neuquén rising share), and energy-balance analysis.

reports.title: Producción de litio / carbonato de litio (estadísticas mineras)
reports.description: Physical and index measures of lithium carbonate and related lithium minerals production, published within the IPI minero framework.
reports._notes: High-growth critical-mineral series. First-half 2026 lithium carbonate production +49% cumulative; monthly physical volumes regularly published. Completes the mining layer alongside hydrocarbons.

reports.title: Exportaciones de combustibles y energía / complejo petrolero-petroquímico
reports.description: Trade statistics for the fuels & energy large rubric and the oil-petrochemical export complex. Directly linked to Vaca Muerta production growth.
reports._notes: Trade counterpart to the production indices. Oil-petrochemical complex was the second-largest export complex in 2025 (~13.5% of total goods exports).
