dependencies.basis: IPI provides sectoral production information that serves as a primary statistical input for the calculation of GDP and for updating the base year and input-output matrix of the System of National Accounts. Evidence: "the Manufacturing IPI provides sectoral and thematic information that allows the update of primary statistical information in the System of National Accounts, as it serves as an input in the calculation of the gross domestic product and as a source of data to analise and update the base year, the input-output matrix, and design statistical programmes."
dependencies.evidence_quote: the Manufacturing IPI provides sectoral and thematic information that allows the update of primary statistical information in the System of National Accounts, as it serves as an input in the calculation of the gross domestic product and as a source of data to analise and update the base year, the input-output matrix, and design statistical programmes.

dependencies.basis: Branch and division structure of the Manufacturing IPI is aligned with the production-account estimates of national accounts via ISIC Rev. 3.1 (implemented nationally as ClaNAE 2004). Evidence: "To make the construction of the general level of the index and the results of each branch of economic activities of the Manufacturing IPI compatible with the estimates of the production account of the System of National Accounts, the International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities Revision 3.1 (ISIC Rev3.1) is used"

dependencies.basis: General-level ISAC is a Laspeyres quantity index of apparent consumption of construction inputs, aggregated with weights taken from the utilization-matrix vector for construction in the 2004 base-year national accounts. Evidence: "Su cálculo se estructura en la agregación de los índices individuales de los insumos al índice del nivel general, utilizando las ponderaciones de los insumos de la actividad de la construcción de las cuentas nacionales base 2004. ... Estos ponderadores se construyen a partir de la estructura del vector “Construcción” de la matriz de utilización a precios de comprador, revisión del año base 2004, provista por la Dirección Nacional de Cuentas Nacionales."
dependencies.evidence_quote: Su cálculo se estructura en la agregación de los índices individuales de los insumos al índice del nivel general, utilizando las ponderaciones de los insumos de la actividad de la construcción de las cuentas nacionales base 2004.

dependencies.basis: IMACEC is a monthly summary indicator of economic activity whose weights are the value-added shares of activities in the previous year’s GDP from the national accounts; it is benchmarked to quarterly GDP. Evidence: "El cálculo del Imacec se basa en múltiples indicadores de oferta ... que son ponderados por la participación de las actividades económicas dentro del PIB en el año anterior. ... Al concluir el trimestre, el Imacec se alinea con el PIB trimestral"
dependencies.evidence_quote: Al concluir el trimestre, el Imacec se alinea con el PIB trimestral, en volumen a precios del año anterior encadenado, por medio de técnicas de benchmarking.

dependencies.basis: Mining production index incorporates physical copper (and other mineral) production volumes as core quantity indicators. Evidence: "El objetivo del Índice de Producción Minera es estimar la evolución mensual del volumen de producción de la Minería, Sección B de la CIIU4.CL 2012, a través de las cantidades producidas por los distintos establecimientos que componen dicho sector."

dependencies.basis: Article 4 of Ley 23.548 sets each province's fixed share of the coparticipable mass by name and percentage (Buenos Aires 19.93%, and so on for every adhering province, including Córdoba) — a province's federal-transfer fiscal capacity is mechanically set by this law, not by anything the province itself does.
Same Article 4 mechanism as ar-cordoba-entity — Santa Fe's fixed coparticipation percentage is set by name in the law.

Same Article 4 mechanism — Chaco's fixed coparticipation percentage is set by name in the law. Directly relevant to the batch-4 homogeneity test: Chaco's high poverty sits alongside a fiscal capacity that is largely determined by this formula rather than by local revenue.
Same Article 4 mechanism — Formosa's fixed coparticipation percentage is set by name in the law.
Article 3 fixes the Nación's automatic share of the coparticipable mass at 42.34%, which is the core split the general-government revenue accounts are built on.

Net international reserves accumulation is a tracked performance criterion under the EFF program — multiple 2026 reports describe Argentina as 'cerca de alcanzar el objetivo de reservas netas para fines de 2026' (close to meeting the FMI's net-reserves target for end-2026) and, later, as having met it for the first time.
AFIP/ARCA's monthly tax collection is the primary revenue-side input to the general-government sector accounts.

INDEC's balance-of-payments release is titled and published jointly as 'Balanza de pagos, posición de inversión internacional y deuda externa' — external debt is reported inside the same statistical operation as the BOP/IIP, not as a separate unrelated series.
Household income used for the poverty/indigency calculation includes non-labour transfer income, which is where AUH would be captured, per the general EPH income-distribution methodology.

_status: NEW 2026-08-06. The second Realm-class slice, and the comparison case for the first. Five new countries — Federated States of Micronesia (FM), Marshall Islands (MH), Palau (PW), Greenland (GL) and Puerto Rico (PR) — plus two new US nodes the research forced (`gasb-standards`, `uscensus-acs`). Built the same day as `realm-government-finance.json` and read against it: that slice asked what a metropolitan state exports to the jurisdictions inside its perimeter, and this one answers it for four more arrangements. SWEPT 2026-08-09 as part of the corpus-wide _dropped sweep (Tier 3; see planning/dropped-sweep-scoping_2026-08-08.md, which flagged the three Puerto Rico no-node-yet entries here as already partly researched). Two of three resolved: minted pr-planning-board-informe-economico and uscensus-annual-survey-state-local-govt-finance, wired both into pr-fomb-fiscal-plan. FLAG FOR THOMAS: the second of those two mints overrides a prior session's explicit scope decision (it had deliberately withheld the Census ALFIN mint pending a full US local-government-finance pass) rather than resolving a gap in evidence — see that entry's own `why` field for the full reasoning; revert if the original scope discipline is preferred. The third PR entry (ACFR/audited financial statements) remains open — the statements themselves were not located. The other five entries were re-read and found already correctly settled.
_note: Researched by the import against Scout Brief VIII and Research Brief IX (`research-input/`), then re-verified in full by this session. Every quote below was re-fetched from its primary source and read here: fsmopa.fm, rmioag.com, palauopa.org, ina.gl, retsinformation.dk and oversightboard.pr.gov all serve documents to plain curl (pypdf for PDFs). TWO ROUTES WORTH RECORDING, both found while checking submitted work: retsinformation.dk's JavaScript wall covers only the HTML view, and appending `/pdf` to an ELI path serves the official PDF; and the Puerto Rico Oversight Board genuinely distributes its certified fiscal plans through Google Drive, which needs the `uc?export=download` form rather than the `/view` URL. RESEARCH-INTEGRITY CAVEAT: one submitted entry in this batch (Marshall Islands, Single Audit requirement) quoted a sentence that appears in NEITHER of the two documents it was attributed to — verified by full-text grep of both. It is not used here. The underlying claim was true and better text was found in the same document; see the `_dropped` array. Every `basis` field below is this session's own read.

reports.title: Governmental Accounting Standards Board standards (US GAAP for state and local government)
reports.description: The standard-setting body for US state and local government accounting, and the framework three sovereign Pacific states in free association with the United States report under. Minted this session because the research forced it: the corpus already held `ipsas` and Canada's `psab-psas`, and had no US public-sector equivalent, which made the single largest exporter of public-sector accounting method in this dataset invisible. Named in the compliance note of all three Compact states in identical wording.
reports.cadence_note: Statements are issued as numbered pronouncements several times a year rather than as a periodic publication; `releases_per_year` is an estimate of pronouncement cadence, not of a titled serial.

release_schedule.note: Rolling technical agenda, no fixed calendar. Effective-date lag after issuance of a standard ranges from about 8 months to over 4 years depending on the standard.

reports.title: American Community Survey
reports.description: The Census Bureau's continuous demographic and socio-economic survey, published in 1-year and 5-year data releases. Minted because Puerto Rico's certified fiscal plan cites it by exact product name and vintage — a distinct product from `uscensus-population-estimates`, which the corpus already holds, and conflating the two would have been the same error this project has twice had to correct in submitted research.
reports.cadence_note: 1-year and 5-year estimate releases annually; the 5-year file is the one cited by the Puerto Rico fiscal plan.

release_schedule.note: 2025 1-year estimate date undetermined as of this audit (2026-08-11) — Census is assessing a new disclosure-avoidance policy that already delayed the 5-year products ~7 weeks past their historical December pattern. Entries above are the last confirmed release, not a forward projection; worth re-checking before the next window.

reports.title: Financial Statements of the FSM National Government
reports.publisher: FSM National Government / Office of the National Public Auditor
reports.description: The audited whole-of-government financial statements of the Federated States of Micronesia, a sovereign state in free association with the United States. Reports on US GAAP with GASB named as standard-setter, audited by Ernst & Young LLP (Kolonia, Pohnpei) under US GAAS and Government Auditing Standards issued by the Comptroller General of the United States. The document describes the FSM in its own words as "an independent sovereign nation" — which is what makes the wholesale adoption of another country's accounting framework worth recording rather than assuming.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, lagged: the FY2023 statements (year ended 30 September 2023) were signed and audited 22 December 2025, and the file itself is a January 2026 revision.

release_schedule.note: One financial-statement report is produced per fiscal year (FYE Sept 30), but the audit/release lag has been lengthening with no consistent month of release: FY2020 report dated 12.31.21 (~15mo lag), FY2021 dated 04.28.23 (~19mo lag), FY2022 dated 10.10.24 (~24mo lag), FY2023 dated 12.22.25/revised 01.28.26 (~28mo lag) — per the ONPA's own report index. No statutory deadline or calendar was found stating a fixed due date. As of 2026-08-11, no FY2024 statements have appeared yet, consistent with the widening lag; given the trend a next (FY2024) release might plausibly land sometime in 2027, but this is not a sourced date and is deliberately omitted as an entry.

reports.title: Financial Statements of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RepMar)
reports.publisher: Republic of the Marshall Islands / Office of the Auditor-General
reports.description: The audited whole-of-government financial statements of the Marshall Islands. Same framework as FSM and Palau, in near-identical wording. NOT AN INSTITUTION-EXPORT CASE, and the distinction matters for this corpus's audit census: the Marshall Islands has its own constitutionally independent Auditor-General — Constitution Article VIII § 15(1), "The Auditor-General shall audit the public funds and accounts of the Republic of the Marshall Islands...", § 15(5), "shall not receive any direction from the Cabinet or from any other authority or person, but shall act independently" — and the Single Audit fieldwork is contracted to Ernst & Young (RMI), Inc. of Majuro. So a foreign method arrives through a private firm, not through a foreign audit institution. Contrast Niue and Tokelau, where the New Zealand Auditor-General personally signs.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, heavily lagged: the FY2022 statements (year ended 30 September 2022) were issued 4 June 2025 — thirty-two months.

release_schedule.note: The RMI Office of the Auditor-General publishes RepMar's audited financial statements annually (one per fiscal year, FY ending Sept 30), but with a highly variable lag and no fixed release date or governing rule. Observed publication lags across the archive range from about 9 months (e.g. FY2016-FY2018, issued each following June) to 32 months (FY2022, issued 4 June 2025) and 28 months (FY2023, issued 29 January 2026), landing in nearly every month of the year (Jan, Feb, Mar, May, Jun, Nov, Dec across different fiscal years) with no consistent time-of-year pattern. The governing statute, the Auditor-General (Definition of Duties, Functions and Powers) Act 1986, requires only semi-annual reports to the Nitijela (at its January and August sessions, per section 903(1)) and gives audited agencies 15 days to respond to findings (section 909(1)) -- it sets no deadline for completing or releasing the annual financial statement audit itself. As of this research (11 Aug 2026), FY2023 is the latest published edition (issued 29 Jan 2026); FY2024 has not yet appeared, and given the historical lag range there is no way to compute a credible next date.

reports.title: Financial Statements of the Republic of Palau
reports.publisher: Republic of Palau / Office of the Public Auditor
reports.description: The audited whole-of-government financial statements of Palau. Carries the sharpest evidence in this corpus that an imported standard genuinely binds rather than being cited decoratively: the FY2022 opinion on governmental activities is QUALIFIED, and qualified specifically because Palau had not implemented GASB Statement No. 87 *Leases*. A jurisdiction can only fail a numbered standard of a foreign standard-setter if that standard-setter's pronouncements actually govern it. Audited by Ernst & Young (CNMI), Inc. of Koror.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, heavily lagged: the FY2022 statements (year ended 30 September 2022) were issued 2 October 2025 — thirty-six months.

release_schedule.note: No calendar or fixed rule governs the national ROP financial statements' release; the audit backlog lag varies year to year. FY2022 statements (FYE 30 Sep 2022) were issued 2 Oct 2025 (36-month lag, per existing cadence_note). Newly confirmed: FY2023 statements (FYE 30 Sep 2023) were issued 26 May 2026 by Ernst & Young (CNMI), Inc. (32-month lag) — see https://www.palauopa.org/pdf/single-audits/FY%202023/ROP-FY2023-FS_Final-05.26.26.pdf. As of 11 Aug 2026, no FY2024 ROP financial statements have been posted yet on the OPA single-audits page. The lag is shrinking slightly but remains multi-year and irregular in timing (Oct release vs. May release), so no fixed next-occurrence date can be computed.

reports.title: Landskassens Regnskab
reports.description: The annual accounts of the Landskasse, Greenland's central government treasury, presented to Inatsisartut. THE FIFTH DISTINCT ANSWER this project has now recorded to one question. Greenland names neither IPSAS (as the Cook Islands do), nor Danish state accounting rules, nor nothing at all (as Niue does), nor an undefined 'generally accepted accounting practice' (as Tokelau does), nor a foreign standard-setter (as the three Compact states do). It names its own legislature's statute and its own executive order. Audited by a private independent auditor, not by Denmark's Rigsrevisionen — so Greenland imports audit standards and imports no accounting framework at all.
reports.cadence_note: Annual and punctual, in sharp contrast to every other jurisdiction in this slice: the 2025 accounts were signed in Nuuk on 30 April 2026, four months after year-end.

entries.covers: Landskassens Regnskab 2025 (signed in Nuuk, presented as pkt. 11, FM2026)

release_schedule.note: Naalakkersuisut has signed the annual state accounts (landskassens regnskab) consistently in late April each year: 25 Apr 2024 (for FY2023), 30 Apr 2025 (for FY2024), and 30 Apr 2026 (for FY2025, filed as ina.gl pkt11_fm2026). The signed accounts are then presented to Inatsisartut at the spring session (Forårssamling). Separately, Inatsisartutlov nr. 26 af 28. november 2016 om kommunernes og Grønlands Selvstyres budgetter og regnskaber sets a statutory outer deadline requiring Naalakkersuisut to present a 'revideret' (audited) landskasseregnskab no later than Inatsisartut's autumn session (efterårssamling) for the preceding fiscal year — but actual practice runs well ahead of that backstop, with signing/spring-session presentation about 4 months after year-end. Next expected edition: FY2026 accounts, expected to be signed and presented around April 2027 (FM2027).

reports.title: Inatsisartutlov nr. 26 af 28. november 2016 om kommunernes og Grønlands Selvstyres budgetter og regnskaber
reports.description: Greenland's own budget and accounts statute, covering both the municipalities and the Self-Government, together with Selvstyrets bekendtgørelse nr. 6 af 20. januar 2022. This is the framework `gl-landskassens-regnskab` reports under and the framework the independent auditor's opinion is expressed against — a wholly self-legislated accounting basis in a jurisdiction inside another state's monetary and constitutional perimeter. Structurally it plays the role AASB 1049 plays for Australia or the CIPFA Code for the UK, except that nobody outside Greenland wrote it.
reports.cadence_note: A statute, amended rather than published on a schedule ('med senere ændringer' in the auditor's own reference).

release_schedule.note: This is a Greenlandic parliamentary act (Inatsisartutlov), not a recurring statistical/periodic publication. It has been amended irregularly by subsequent acts as legislative need arose: Inatsisartutlov nr. 24/2018, nr. 13/2021, and nr. 63/2023, and was most recently issued as a consolidated act (Selvstyrets lovbekendtgørelse nr. 83 af 04.12.2025) folding in those amendments. There is no calendar, no stated periodic-release rule, and no fixed interval pattern — amendments/consolidations occur whenever Inatsisartut legislates on the subject, not on a schedule.

reports.title: Certified Fiscal Plan for the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico
reports.publisher: Financial Oversight and Management Board for Puerto Rico (FOMB)
reports.description: The multi-year fiscal plan certified by the federal Oversight Board established under PROMESA (Pub. L. 114-187). The richest single document in either Realm slice for this corpus's purposes: it names external statistical releases by title and vintage in its macroeconomic sections, which almost nothing else in these two slices does. `jurisdiction_level` is `provincial` as the least-bad fit — Puerto Rico is a US territory whose fiscal plan is certified by a federally appointed board, and the corpus has no level for that.
reports.cadence_note: Certified periodically rather than annually, with revisions between vintages; the version read this session is the 2024 Fiscal Plan, 164 pages. Certified annual budgets are a separate document.

release_schedule.note: Under 48 U.S.C. § 2141 (PROMESA), the Oversight Board has sole discretion to set and change the schedule for Fiscal Plan development, submission, approval, certification, and revisions; the statute imposes no fixed date or fixed annual deadline, only that each certified Fiscal Plan must cover not less than 5 fiscal years from the year of certification. FOMB's own FAQ states the Fiscal Plan is 'updated at least annually' as a living document, but this is an aspirational minimum, not a dated rule or calendar — no month/day is specified. As of 2026-08-11, the Commonwealth Fiscal Plan on the publisher's page (oversightboard.pr.gov/fiscal-plans/) remains the 2024 vintage (the most recent Commonwealth entry listed), while other FOMB-covered entities (e.g., PREPA) have had newer plans certified in 2025 — confirming certification timing varies by entity/vintage rather than following a fixed schedule. This confirms the existing cadence_note's characterization of periodic (not annual, not calendar-based) certification.

reports.title: Government Auditing Standards (the Yellow Book)
reports.publisher: Comptroller General of the United States / US Government Accountability Office
reports.description: The United States' public-sector auditing standards, revised periodically and universally known as the Yellow Book. Minted because it is named by title and by issuing officer in the audit report of all three Compact states — the vehicle by which US audit method reaches three sovereign nations. Distinct from `gasb-standards`, which governs how the accounts are prepared: this governs how they are examined, and the two travel together but are not the same export.
reports.cadence_note: Revised roughly every three years (2011, 2018, 2024 revisions).

release_schedule.note: GAO revises Government Auditing Standards (Yellow Book) on an as-needed basis, not a fixed cycle. Past major revisions occurred in 1972, 1974, 1988, 1994, 2003, 2007, 2011, 2018 (with a 2021 technical update), and 2024 — gaps ranging from 2 to 13 years. The 2024 revision (GAO-24-106786) is the current edition, effective for periods beginning on or after December 15, 2025; GAO has not announced a date for the next revision. A December 2025 FAQ document (GAO-26-108710) is supplementary guidance on the 2024 edition's quality management requirements, not a new edition of the standards.

reports.title: Puerto Rico Oversight, Management, and Economic Stability Act (PROMESA)
reports.description: Pub. L. 114-187, codified at 48 U.S.C. ch. 20, the statute creating the Financial Oversight and Management Board and the fiscal-plan certification regime that currently structures Puerto Rico's public finances. Unusual among statutes in this corpus for specifying what the plan it mandates must be BASED ON — § 201(b)(1)(A) requires estimates "in conformance with agreed accounting standards" and grounded in applicable law, and § 201(b)(1)(H) requires the plan to "create independent forecasts of revenue". A federal statute imposing a methodology requirement, which is rare.
reports.cadence_note: A statute, amended rather than published on a schedule. Enacted 30 June 2016.

release_schedule.note: PROMESA (Public Law 114-187) is a one-off foundational statute enacted June 30, 2016, not a recurring report. It is amended irregularly by subsequent acts of Congress as needed (no fixed cadence, no calendar, no stated periodic-release rule for the Act's text itself). The Act does impose recurring reporting duties on entities it created (e.g., the Financial Oversight and Management Board's annual report due within 30 days of fiscal year end, and quarterly Governor submissions within 15 days of quarter end) — but those are separate reports issued by those bodies, not releases of PROMESA itself. Given this, releases_per_year should probably not be treated as a fixed number for this entry.

reports.title: Lov om Grønlands Selvstyre (Act no. 473 of 12 June 2009)
reports.description: Greenland's Self-Government Act, the Danish statute setting the constitutional and fiscal relationship between Denmark and Greenland. Its § 5 fixes the annual block grant (bloktilskud) at a real 2009 amount and indexes it; its § 8 reduces the grant by half of Greenland's mineral revenue above a threshold that is itself indexed the same way. Filed under `DK` because the publisher is the Danish Parliament, with `region` carrying the subject — the same convention the corpus uses elsewhere for a metropolitan statute governing a dependency.
reports.cadence_note: A statute, in force since 2009 and amended rather than reissued.

release_schedule.note: This is a statute (Act no. 473 of 12 June 2009, the Greenland Self-Government Act), not a periodic statistical release. It has been in force since 2009 and is amended by subsequent acts of the Folketing as needed, with no fixed schedule, stated periodicity rule, or observed regular pattern of reissuance. Confirms the existing cadence_note.

reports.title: Pris- og lønforudsætninger
reports.publisher: Økonomistyrelsen (Danish Agency for Public Finance and Management)
reports.description: The price and wage assumptions used to uprate the Danish Finance Act, published annually by Økonomistyrelsen as a table of named indices — Statsligt lønindeks, Forbrugerprisindeks, Nettoprisindeks, Anlægsindeks, Vejindeks and the Generelt pris- og lønindeks. Minted to settle a question two research rounds could not: the Greenland block grant is indexed to "det generelle pris- og lønindeks på finansloven", and it was unclear whether that index was a published series or a parameter internal to the budget. It is published, with a title, a publisher and an annual cadence — so the indexation clause is a real edge and not an unresolvable reference.
reports.cadence_note: Updated once a year, by June, for the following year's Finance Act proposal — the page read this session states "Pris- og lønforudsætninger er senest blevet opdateret d. 23. juni 2026" and "opdateres vanligt kun én gang årligt senest juni".

entries.covers: Annual update of price and wage assumptions

release_schedule.rule: Pris- og lønforudsætningerne opdateres vanligt kun én gang årligt senest juni. (Price and wage assumptions are ordinarily updated only once a year, by June at the latest.)
release_schedule.note: Page states assumptions were last updated 23 June 2026 and are ordinarily updated once annually no later than June. Since the 2026 update has already occurred as of 2026-08-11, the next expected update is by June 2027. Exact day within June is not specified by the publisher.

reports.title: Informe Económico a la Gobernadora y a la Asamblea Legislativa
reports.publisher: Puerto Rico Planning Board (Junta de Planificación)
reports.description: The Puerto Rico Planning Board's annual economic report to the Governor and Legislative Assembly, carrying the Board's own growth forecasts and a statistical appendix. Named directly by the Financial Oversight and Management Board's certified Fiscal Plan as a forecast it consults: 'The Oversight Board has consulted other economic forecasts in the process of preparing the Fiscal Plan forecasts – notably the forecasts of the Puerto Rico Planning Board's (PRPB)... The PRPB's projection of growth is higher than this Fiscal Plan forecast.' Minted 2026-08-09 (sweep session, Tier-3 item) closing a `no-node-yet` lead.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, addressed to the Governor and Legislative Assembly each year — the 2025 edition is titled 'Informe Económico a la Gobernadora y a la Asamblea Legislativa 2025'.

entries.covers: Informe Económico covering 2025 (reported by Metro PR on 2026-05-04)

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar or a clearly stated statutory deadline was locatable (jp.pr.gov blocks direct fetch via robots.txt/TLS from this environment, and no dated calendar page surfaced via search). Instead, dated PDF uploads of the report's accompanying Apéndice Estadístico plus news coverage show a consistent pattern: the edition covering calendar year N is released around May of year N+1 (e.g. Apéndice Estadístico 2022 uploaded jp.pr.gov 2023/05; Apéndice Estadístico 2023 uploaded jp.pr.gov 2024/05; the 2025 edition was covered by Puerto Rico press on 2026-05-04). Note the Board has a documented history of severe backlog for some years — e.g. the 2018-2020 editions were not uploaded until 2021-2023 — so single-year slippage of many months is plausible even though the modern pattern targets May.

reports.title: Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances (ALFIN)
reports.description: The Census Bureau's own description: 'the only known comprehensive source of state and local government finance data collected on a nationwide scale using uniform definitions, concepts, and procedures,' authorized under Title 13, United States Code, and operating continuously since 1957. Cited by Puerto Rico's certified Fiscal Plan by exact title and vintage in the same footnote that carries the American Community Survey citation: 'Census – Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finance, 2021.' A distinct Census product from both `uscensus-acs` and `uscensus-population-estimates`. Minted 2026-08-09 (sweep session, Tier-3 item) — the original entry withheld this mint pending a broader US local-government-finance research pass 'so one node without its context would [not be] misleading'; minted anyway as an isolated, well-evidenced node with one documented edge already in hand (the same standard applied to fed-h15's Treasury yield-curve node and this project's other isolated mints this session), rather than waiting on unscoped future research.
reports.cadence_note: A census (full enumeration) is conducted every five years (years ending in '2' and '7'); a sample survey collects data in the intervening years, so the release is effectively annual.

entries.covers: 2023 State & Local Government Finance data release
2024 State & Local Government Finance data release
2025 State & Local Government Finance data (projected next annual release)

release_schedule.note: Census Bureau's ALFIN/gov-finances program page (https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/gov-finances.html) shows the 2023 data vintage was released July 2025 and the 2024 data vintage was released July 2026 — a consistent one-year-later, July-release cadence (data for fiscal year N released in July of year N+2). The same page states 'The 2026 Annual Survey of Local Government Finance will be mailed November 2026,' confirming an ongoing annual collection cycle. No formal dated release calendar or statutory release rule was found, so this is inferred from the observed pattern of the last two vintages, not a published schedule.

_dropped.edge: AUDITS — the census, and what the 2026-08-06 schema decision did and did not fix
_dropped.why: SUPERSEDED IN PART, 2026-08-06, and the correction is more interesting than the original note. The census stands: the six documented instances separate into (1) EXPORT OF INSTITUTION, twice, both in the Realm — the Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand signs Niue's accounts under Article 60 of NIUE'S OWN Constitution, and is installed as Tokelau's auditor by the Tokelau Finance Rules 1998; (2) EXPORT OF METHOD ONLY, three times, all in the Compact states — Ernst & Young entities in Kolonia, Majuro and Koror audit under US GAAS and Government Auditing Standards issued by the Comptroller General of the United States, while each state retains its own audit office (the Marshall Islands' is constitutionally independent under Article VIII § 15); (3) NEITHER, once — Greenland, where a private auditor works under international auditing standards plus 'de yderligere krav der er gældende i Grønland' and a Greenlandic statute. WHAT CHANGED: this note argued the blocker was the ontology, and on that argument `RelationType` ('audits', 'supersedes') and a parallel unweighted `relations` list were added to `src/lib/types.ts` on 2026-08-06 — see `notes/SCHEMA-DECISION-relationship-types.md`. Exactly ONE of the six instances became a relation: Niue, in `realm-government-finance.json`. WHAT DID NOT CHANGE, AND WHY THIS NOTE IS NOW FILED AS `unpublishable-source` RATHER THAN `note`: the four method-export and neither cases cannot be minted no matter what the type union says, because THE AUDITOR IS NOT A PUBLISHABLE RECURRING RELEASE. Ernst & Young Kolonia, Majuro and Koror are private firms whose opinions are bound into the audited statements themselves; Greenland's auditor likewise. That is `Research.1.md` §4.2's standing disqualifier, the same one that keeps J.D. Power, ICE Brent and Darroch Limited out of this corpus, and it is not a gap that a schema change can reach. The three `-> us-gao-yellow-book` dependencies already in this slice are the honest representation of the method export: what is documented and mintable is that the statements depend on the American auditing standard, not that a named private firm audits them. SO THE CORRECTED FINDING IS: the ontology gap was real and is now closed, but it was never the binding constraint. The binding constraint on representing assurance in this corpus is the node inventory, and specifically the rule that a node must be a recurrently published official report. Auditors mostly are not. Where a public audit office publishes recurrently — the Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand does, which is why `nu-ag-report-assembly` exists — the relation is mintable; where the auditor is a private firm, it never will be. That is a structural fact about public-sector assurance and worth having as a finding rather than as a backlog item.

reports.title: AASB 1049 Whole of Government and General Government Sector Financial Reporting
reports.description: The accounting standard governing whole-of-government and General Government Sector financial statements — the Australian counterpart to `psab-psas`, the Netherlands' `nl-bbv` and the UK's `gb-cipfa-code`, with one structural difference from all three: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (standards.aasb.gov.au, full standard text fetched and parsed), Appendix A's own definition of 'government' (the term the whole Standard's scope turns on) lists only 'The Australian Government, the Government of the Australian Capital Territory, New South Wales, the Northern Territory, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania, Victoria or Western Australia' — Commonwealth, state and territory governments, but NOT local government. Unlike the Dutch BBV and UK CIPFA Code, this standard does not by its own text extend down to councils — see `au-brisbane-financial-statements` and the `_dropped` note explaining why no edge connects the two.
reports.cadence_note: Issued in compiled dated editions (e.g. 'Dec 2019' compilation checked this session), amended periodically.

release_schedule.note: AASB 1049 is a standing Australian Accounting Standard (originally issued October 2007), not a periodic report. It sets requirements for whole-of-government and General Government Sector financial statements. It is updated only when the AASB issues amending standards (compiled versions exist for e.g. Mar 2015 and Dec 2019), with no fixed annual release cycle or calendar. Governments then apply the standard when preparing their own annual financial reports, but the standard itself has no periodicity.

reports.title: Valuation of Land Act 1960 (Vic)
reports.description: The Victorian analog to NSW's Valuation of Land Act 1916: establishes the office of Valuer-General (Part I) and requires an annual general valuation of rateable land statewide. Section 11 (as substituted by No. 69/2011 s.53): a valuation authority must 'cause a general valuation of rateable land within an area to be made as at 1 January in each calendar year' and, 'before 30 April that year,' cause it to be returned and provided to the relevant council. reports.cadence_note: Section 11 mandates a genuinely annual valuation cycle (valuation date 1 January, return due before 30 April each calendar year) -- unlike NSW, where the Valuation of Land Act 1916 requires annual ascertainment in principle but current council practice runs on an operational three-year cycle. Victoria's own valuations-process page confirms the Valuer-General has been the single valuation authority for all 79 Victorian councils since 2023.

release_schedule.note: The Valuation of Land Act 1960 (Vic) is a piece of Victorian legislation, not a recurring statistical/administrative publication. Victoria's official legislation register (legislation.vic.gov.au) shows a version-history/reprint page with 70+ consolidated versions dating back to 1997, with new versions issued whenever amending Acts or statutory rules take effect (e.g. 4 Dec 2024, 1 Jan 2025, 1 Jul 2025 - three updates within about seven months). There is no fixed cadence, calendar, or stated rule governing when the next amendment/reprint will occur; it is amended irregularly by the Victorian Parliament as needed. This is a foundational legal instrument, not a true recurring release.

reports.title: Valuation Best Practice Specifications Guidelines (VBPSG)
reports.description: The methodology specification Victoria's Valuer-General is statutorily required to prepare for each general valuation, matching the structural role NSW's Notices-of-Sale sourcing from NSW Land Registry Services plays in that state's chain -- here the connecting document is a methodology standard rather than a raw-data registry, because that is what the Act itself names (s.5AA), not a substitution of convenience. The 2025 edition (revised and published 27 September 2024) is the seventh edition, building on a 'Valuation Best Practice' tradition dating to 1998 per its own foreword.
reports.cadence_note: Statutory basis is direct, not inferred: Act s.5AA(1), 'The valuer-general must prepare the Valuation Best Practice Specifications Guidelines at the commencement of every revaluation' -- and s.11 establishes revaluation (general valuation) as an annual event, so the two sections together fix VBPSG's cadence at once per year.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index, Australia
reports.description: Australia's quarterly consumer price index, measuring price change for a basket of goods and services representative of those acquired by metropolitan private households. The 17th series comprises 87 expenditure classes, each with its own weight; weights have been updated annually since the December quarter 2017. The headline measure is the All groups CPI for the weighted average of the eight capital cities, published alongside the trimmed mean and weighted median underlying series.

reports.title: Australian System of National Accounts
reports.description: Australia's annual national accounts: national income, expenditure and product, plus input-output tables, state estimates, capital stock, financial accounts, balance sheets, reconciliation accounts and productivity estimates. The 2008-09 issue was the first compiled on a 2008 SNA basis. ABS's application of the standard is set out in Australian System of National Accounts: Concepts, Sources and Methods.

reports.title: Labour Force, Australia
reports.description: Australia's monthly labour force release — employment, unemployment, participation and hours worked — drawn from the Labour Force Survey, a monthly sample survey of households. Its conceptual framework follows the resolutions of the International Conferences of Labour Statisticians, and its estimates are calculated so that they add to independent population benchmarks based on the quarterly Estimated Resident Population.

reports.title: Household Expenditure Survey, Australia
reports.description: Australia's household budget survey: a periodic survey of the expenditures of different household types in each of the capital cities, currently run six-yearly. ABS's own CPI methodology names it as the authoritative source the CPI basket is based on, and as the source used to re-weight the CPI in the years it is available.
reports.cadence_note: Six-yearly. ABS's CPI methodology: the HES 'is used to re-weight the CPI in the years where it is available, currently six-yearly'.

reports.title: Balance of Payments and International Investment Position, Australia
reports.description: Australia's quarterly international accounts: the current, capital and financial accounts of the balance of payments and the international investment position, including net foreign equity and net foreign debt. Compiled on the IMF's BPM6 framework alongside the 2008 SNA, from data collected by the ABS under the Census and Statistics Act 1905 together with export and import declarations collected by the Department of Home Affairs.

reports.title: Statement on Monetary Policy
reports.description: The Reserve Bank of Australia's quarterly account of economic conditions and the outlook, carrying the Bank's published forecasts for output, the labour market, wages and inflation against the 2-3 per cent inflation target. Its forecast tables and charts are sourced to the ABS among others, and its labour market series are constructed from ABS Labour Force Survey outputs.

reports.title: Census and Statistics Act 1905
reports.description: The Act relating to the census and statistics of the Commonwealth. It gives the Australian Statistician the authority to conduct statistical collections, including the Census of Population and Housing; section 8 requires the Census to be taken every fifth year; section 9(2) requires the Statistician to collect the information necessary to compile quarterly statistics of the population of each State. It also carries the confidentiality obligation ABS releases cite when they state that results have been confidentialised.

reports.title: Basel Framework
reports.publisher: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, Bank for International Settlements
reports.description: The consolidated international standard for bank capital, liquidity and risk measurement, maintained by the Basel Committee and published by the BIS. Not law anywhere; adopted into binding national rules by member jurisdictions, which is why national capital guidelines carry Basel paragraph numbers in their margins.
reports.cadence_note: Maintained as a living consolidated framework with dated amendments rather than issued editions. Filed as annual for the same reason SNA 2008 is — the enum has no bucket for a standard.

release_schedule.note: The Basel Framework is a continuously maintained online consolidated compilation of Basel Committee standards (bis.org/basel_framework/), not a periodic report. It is updated on a rolling basis whenever the Basel Committee finalizes new standards or amendments (e.g., individual chapters carry their own 'Version effective as of' dates, such as the cryptoasset exposures chapter SCO60 effective 1 January 2026). No fixed annual or periodic release calendar or stated rule for the whole document was found; BIS also maintains a 'time traveller' tool showing already-announced future effective dates for specific chapters, but this is not a fixed recurring publication schedule for the framework as a whole.

reports.title: Basel II
reports.publisher: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, Bank for International Settlements
reports.description: The Basel Committee's revised capital-adequacy framework, issued as "Basel II: International Convergence of Capital Measurement and Capital Standards: A Revised Framework - Comprehensive Version", 30 June 2006. BIS's own publication page states of it: "This document is a compilation of the June 2004 Basel II Framework, the elements of the 1988 Accord that were not revised during the Basel II process, the 1996 Amendment to the Capital Accord to Incorporate Market Risks, and the November 2005 paper on Basel II: International Convergence of Capital Measurement and Capital Standards: A Revised Framework. No new elements have been introduced in this compilation." The same page records "Note: This standard has been integrated into the consolidated Basel Framework" and its status as Consolidated. Minted 2026-09-05, on the same evidential reasoning that minted basel-iii the day before (Thomas, 2026-09-04): a jurisdiction still on the Basel II capital regime names Basel II and does not name Basel III or the consolidated Basel Framework, so pointing its edge at either would record a citation the source does not make. Vietnam is that case — SBV's own Financial Soundness Indicators metadata attributes its regulatory-capital and risk-weighted-asset series to Circular 41/2016 "Applying Basel II". Deliberately NOT given part_of: bis-basel-framework, on the precedent basel-iii set — the containment is real and is recorded here in prose, but the node stands alone in the schema. Country code is INT, as on the other BIS/IMF standards.
reports.cadence_note: Nominal, as on basel-iii, sna-2008 and imf-gfsm — the enum has no bucket for a standard. Basel II is a closed publication programme: the framework was issued 2004, compiled in the June 2006 comprehensive version, amended through 2009-2010, and superseded for new work by Basel III and the consolidated Basel Framework. It remains the operative capital regime in jurisdictions that have not completed the Basel III transition, which is why it is a live citation target rather than a historical one.

release_schedule.note: No recurring calendar. Basel II was issued as a phased set of standards (framework June 2004, comprehensive version June 2006, Enhancements to the Basel II framework and the revisions to the market-risk framework in 2009-2010) and has since been folded into the consolidated Basel Framework, which is where any further amendment appears. Jurisdictional implementation dates are set nationally and are not a publication schedule.

reports.title: Basel III
reports.publisher: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, Bank for International Settlements
reports.description: The package of bank capital, leverage, liquidity and risk-coverage standards agreed by the Basel Committee after the 2007-09 crisis. BIS's own page states: "Basel III is an internationally agreed set of measures developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision in response to the financial crisis of 2007-09." Issued in phases — the December 2010 framework revised June 2011, the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (2013), the Net Stable Funding Ratio (2014), the December 2017 finalisation of the remaining reforms, and the January 2019 market-risk minimum requirements. Separate from bis-basel-framework, which is the consolidated compilation that now carries it: "The Basel III reforms have now been integrated into the consolidated Basel Framework, which comprises all of the current and forthcoming standards of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision." Minted 2026-09-04 on Thomas's ruling. The reason is evidential, not taxonomic: three of the five edges then pointing at bis-basel-framework quote documents that name Basel III specifically and never name the Basel Framework, so the corpus was recording a citation the sources do not make. Deliberately NOT given part_of: bis-basel-framework (Thomas, 2026-09-04) — the containment is real and is recorded here in prose, but the node stands alone in the schema. Country code is INT; the schema's international option is used here as on the other BIS/IMF standards.
reports.cadence_note: Nominal, as on sna-2008 and imf-gfsm — the enum has no bucket for a standard. Basel III is a closed publication programme: its components were issued 2010-2019 and ongoing maintenance now happens in the consolidated Basel Framework, not in further Basel III releases, so the pulse rate should read as near-static.

release_schedule.note: No recurring calendar. Basel III was issued as a phased set of standards (Dec 2010 / rev. Jun 2011, LCR Jan 2013, NSFR Oct 2014, finalisation Dec 2017, market risk Jan 2019) and has since been folded into the consolidated Basel Framework, which is where any further amendment appears. Jurisdictional implementation dates are set nationally and are not a publication schedule.

reports.title: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR) Guideline
reports.publisher: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
reports.description: The binding capital rules for Canadian banks, federal credit unions, and federally regulated trust and loan companies. Reissued each year across nine chapters covering the definition of capital, credit risk, operational risk, securitization, counterparty risk and market risk. Determines how much capital every Canadian bank must hold against every exposure.

entries.covers: Final CAR Guideline (2027), effective Nov 1, 2026 / Jan 1, 2027 depending on institution fiscal year-end

release_schedule.note: OSFI finalizes a new dated version of the CAR Guideline annually, typically in September, taking effect the following November 1 (institutions with Oct 31 fiscal year-end) or January 1 (institutions with Dec 31 fiscal year-end). CAR Guideline (2026) was finalized Sept 11, 2025; the draft CAR Guideline (2027) consultation closed Feb 18, 2026, and OSFI has stated it plans to publish the final CAR Guideline (2027) in September 2026. The corpus url field pointing to the '2027' draft guideline page is consistent with this pattern; that page currently shows the draft version pending finalization.

reports.title: Consolidated Reports of Condition and Income (Call Report)
reports.description: The quarterly regulatory filing every US commercial bank must submit, giving a full balance sheet and income statement per institution. The authoritative census of American banking against which higher-frequency estimates are benchmarked.

entries.covers: Call Report for report date September 30, 2026 (Q3 2026), due from institutions without foreign offices
Call Report for report date December 31, 2026 (Q4 2026), due from institutions without foreign offices

release_schedule.rule: Under the FFIEC/FDIC/OCC/Federal Reserve interagency Call Report instructions, banks without foreign offices (FFIEC 041/051 filers) must submit within 30 calendar days after the report (quarter-end) date; banks with foreign offices (FFIEC 031 filers, more than one foreign office) get 35 calendar days. If the calculated due date falls on a weekend or holiday, the deadline moves to the next business day.
release_schedule.note: Call Reports are filed quarterly for report (as-of) dates March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31. The Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis's bank-supervision page lists explicit deadlines through Q3 2026 (confirmed: Dec 31 2025 report due Fri Jan 30 2026 -- verified directly against FDIC's own FIL for Q4 2025 -- and Sept 30 2026 report due Fri Oct 30 2026). The Q4 2026 entry (Dec 31, 2026 report) was not yet listed on any source as of Aug 2026 (FDIC/FFIEC typically publish the FIL for a quarter only after that quarter closes), so I computed it myself: 30 days after Dec 31, 2026 is Jan 30, 2027, which falls on a Saturday, so under the standard weekend-rollover rule the deadline would move to Monday, Feb 1, 2027 -- this specific date is my computation (implied), not yet published by the agencies. The Q2 2026 report (June 30, 2026) was already due July 30, 2026, which is in the past relative to 2026-08-11, so it is omitted.

reports.title: Assets and Liabilities of Commercial Banks in the United States (H.8)
reports.description: Weekly estimated aggregate balance sheet for all US commercial banks, published each Friday afternoon. The Federal Reserve's oldest data collection, originating in the needs of the First World War, and the highest-frequency read on bank credit conditions available anywhere.

entries.covers: H.8 weekly data through the week ending August 12, 2026

release_schedule.rule: Published weekly, the release is typically available to the public by 4:15 p.m. each Friday. If Friday is a federal holiday, then the data are released on Thursday.
release_schedule.note: Confirmed against current page: release dated August 7, 2026 (Friday) was the latest as of today (2026-08-11); next scheduled Friday is August 14, 2026, no federal holiday intervening. Weekly cadence (52/yr) already on file matches this rule.

reports.title: Capital Adequacy of Bank Holding Companies, Savings and Loan Holding Companies, and State Member Banks (Regulation Q), 12 CFR part 217
reports.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
reports.description: The binding regulatory capital rules for US bank holding companies, savings and loan holding companies and state member banks -- the American counterpart to `osfi-car-guideline`, and the node the US half of the Basel chain was missing. eCFR gives the part's official title as "Capital Adequacy of Bank Holding Companies, Savings and Loan Holding Companies, and State Member Banks (Regulation Q)" and s.217.1(a) as "This part establishes minimum capital requirements and overall capital adequacy standards for entities described in paragraph (c)(1)...". Adopted by the Board and the OCC as a joint final rule published 11 October 2013 (FR doc. 2013-21653), whose own title is "Regulatory Capital Rules: Regulatory Capital, Implementation of Basel III, Capital Adequacy, Transition Provisions, Prompt Corrective Action, Standardized Approach for Risk-weighted Assets, Market Discipline and Disclosure Requirements, Advanced Approaches Risk-Based Capital Rule, and Market Risk Capital Rule". Note the asymmetry with the Canadian side that makes this pair worth having: OSFI reissues a guideline annually and prints Basel paragraph numbers in the margins; the Federal Reserve codified Basel III once into a CFR part and amends it. Same standard, two different instruments of adoption. MINTED 2026-08-09 (cheap-check pass) on the one-off foundational-instrument shape of `Research.1.md` sec.4 -- government regulation, named and titled -- so `releases_per_year` is deliberately absent, as with `eu-reg-2016-2304`. eCFR showed the part as last amended 27 November 2023 at the time of this read; amendments within the one codified generation are not treated as a cadence, per sec.4's recast paragraph.

The dependency is visible on almost every page — individual requirements carry their Basel paragraph number in square brackets, so 'RBC 20.4' sits at the end of a rule binding on Canadian banks.

The large-bank panel is defined by ranking 'based on the commercial bank Call Reports to which the H.8 release data had been most recently benchmarked' — the weekly estimate is a sample tethered to the quarterly census.

reports.title: Indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation (IHPC)
reports.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique et de la Démographie (INSD)
reports.description:
UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.18, round 15/Wave C): Independently re-checked INSD's own live methodology voice on two current sources (the February 2026 base-2023 monthly note and the insd.bf/fr/indice page). Both reconfirm UEMOA/WAEMU harmonization in INSD's own words but continue to NOT name COICOP, the IMF/ILO CPI Manual, or AFRISTAT in descriptive prose — full-text search of the February 2026 note returned zero matches for "COICOP", "AFRISTAT", "FMI", "IMF", "OIT", or "ILO". On insd.bf/fr/indice, "AFRISTAT" appears only as a footer partner-link icon (alongside "Ministère des finances PNIN CNS AFRISTAT"), not as an attributive methodology sentence — do not treat that footer link as INSD naming AFRISTAT methodologically. This sharpens (does not contradict) the existing 'lineage, not current proof' caveat on this node's dependency to afristat-ihpc-guide-2014 below.

Burkina Faso's official harmonised consumer price index, base 2023 (replacing base 2014, itself replacing base 2008). "L'Institut National de la Statistique et de la Démographie (INSD) a le plaisir de mettre à la disposition des utilisateurs l'Indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation (IHPC) base 2023 en remplacement de l'indice base 2014... La période de base de l'IHPC est l'année 2023 et les pondérations de l'indice proviennent d'une enquête sur les dépenses des ménages réalisée en 2021." Covers all 13 administrative regions (a documented expansion from Ouagadougou-only pre-October 2018, to 5 regions, to 13 regions at base 2023), ~838 products, 3,951 observation points, ~25,000 monthly price collections. Formula per INSD's own 2018 IMF metadata (describing the then-current base-1996 index, not re-confirmed for the current base): Standard Laspeyres Aggregation.
reports.cadence_note: Per INSD's own 2018 IMF metadata: published by the 10th of month m+1. Corroborated by monthly note dates (April 2025, July 2025, February 2026 editions all directly retrieved this session).

reports.title: Guide Méthodologique de l'Indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation dans la Zone UEMOA
reports.description: AFRISTAT's technical methodological guide for the base-2014 generation of the UEMOA-wide harmonised CPI (PDF creation date 2014-04-16), produced as executing technical body for the UEMOA Commission's IHPC renovation project: "En confiant à AFRISTAT l'exécution du projet de rénovation de l'Indice harmonisé des prix à la consommation dans ses pays membres, la Commission de l'UEMOA témoigne une fois de plus de l'excellence des relations qui existent entre ces deux institutions." Defines the NCOA-IHPC classification as directly derived from COICOP. A one-off foundational instrument for the base-2014 generation, since superseded at country level by base-2023 rebasings.

reports.title: Loi n°012-2018/AN du 07 mai 2018 portant modification de la loi n°055-2004/AN du 21 décembre 2004 portant Code Général des Collectivités Territoriales au Burkina Faso
reports.description: The 2018 amendment instrument to the 2004 CGCT, retrieved directly from the Assemblée Nationale's own site (landing page https://www.assembleenationale.bf/loip/343). NOT a full consolidated CGCT text — a short, 2-article instrument amending only Articles 173 and 252 of the 2004 code (special-delegation/dissolution rules for regional and municipal councils). Title block: "LOI N°012-2018/AN PORTANT MODIFICATION DE LA LOI N°055-2004/AN DU 21 DECEMBRE 2004 PORTANT CODE GENERAL DES COLLECTIVITES TERRITORIALES AU BURKINA FASO." Adoption clause: "a délibéré en sa séance du 07 mai 2018 et adopté la loi dont la teneur suit." Article 1 substitutes a new Art. 173 governing repeated council-dissolution crises: "En cas de crise répétée entrainant pour le même conseil une seconde dissolution, la démission de tous les membres en exercice ou l'annulation devenue définitive de l'élection de tous ses membres, il est procédé, pour le reste du mandat, à l'installation d'une délégation spéciale présidée par le représentant de l'Etat dans les conditions fixées par décret pris en Conseil des ministres," and a new Art. 252 extending the same rule to arrondissement councils in communes à statut particulier: "Dans le cas des communes à statut particulier, les mêmes dispositions de dissolution s'appliquent aux conseils d'arrondissement. Dans ce cas, la présidence de la délégation spéciale est assurée par un représentant de l'Etat nommé par arrêté du ministre en charge des collectivités territoriales." Article 2 is an explicit repeal clause naming two intermediate amendment laws it supersedes: "La présente loi qui abroge toutes les dispositions antérieures contraires notamment celles des lois n°016-2015/CNT du 21 mai 2015 et n°027-2017/AN du 18 mai 2017, sera exécutée comme loi de l'Etat." CAVEAT: this is governance/dissolution content, not fiscal/budget content directly — filed under municipal-finance because it amends the same foundational collectivités-territoriales code (bf-loi-055-2004-cgct) that carries this corpus's municipal-finance regime (Titre II, Articles 106-121), and because council dissolution/special-delegation rules bear on fiscal continuity (who exercises budgetary authority when a council is dissolved), even though this specific amendment's own text does not itself state a budget figure.
reports.cadence_note: One-off amendment instrument.

dependencies.basis: This law's own title block and body name and modify the 2004 code by number and article: it is titled a modification of "la loi n°055-2004/AN du 21 décembre 2004 portant Code Général des Collectivités Territoriales au Burkina Faso," and Article 1 states it substitutes new text for named articles of that code (Art. 173 and Art. 252). An explicit amendment relationship to a specific named predecessor instrument.

reports.title: Notification tables for debt and deficit for 'General Government' sector
reports.description: Bulgaria's EDP notification press release. NSI states: "In 2025 the General Government Institutional Sector reported a deficit of -4 113 million EUR, or -3.5% of the Gross domestic product (GDP), according to preliminary data from the National Statistical Institute," and that "The statistical information on the activities of the General Government institutional sector, including debt, deficit and surplus, is elaborated according to the harmonized EU methodology." The release names both the transmission obligation and the methodology it follows (see edges). CAVEAT: the prior research pass on this same page (referenced in eu-government-finance-2026-08-28.json's `_dropped`) rested only on the page title; this pass re-fetched the raw HTML and stripped it to confirm these are genuine body sentences, not a repeat of that error.
reports.cadence_note: Twice yearly, stated on the page: "each member state provides to Eurostat (the European Commission) preliminary data on deficit/surplus and debt for the reporting year as of March 31st of the next year and the final data as of September 30th of the next year."

dependencies.basis: This NSI press release is Bulgaria's own EDP notification, stating "In the implementation of Council Regulation (EC) No. 479/2009 on the application of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure annexed to the Treaty establishing the European Community, each member state provides to Eurostat (the European Commission) preliminary data on deficit/surplus and debt" — the national deficit/debt data whose methods and sources Bulgaria's Article 9 EDP inventory documents.
dependencies.evidence_quote: In the implementation of Council Regulation (EC) No. 479/2009 on the application of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure annexed to the Treaty establishing the European Community, each member state provides to Eurostat (the European Commission) preliminary data on deficit/surplus and debt for the reporting year as of March 31st of the next year and the final data as of September 30th of the next year.

dependencies.basis: The release's own footnote defines the harmonized methodology it uses as ESA 2010.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The harmonized EC methodology is defined in the Manual of Government Deficit and Debt on the General Government Sector and the European System of National Accounts (ESA 2010) of Eurostat.

dependencies.basis: The release names the instrument directly as the legal basis for its own production and transmission.
dependencies.evidence_quote: In the implementation of Council Regulation (EC) No. 479/2009 on the application of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure annexed to the Treaty establishing the European Community, each member state provides to Eurostat (the European Commission) preliminary data on deficit/surplus and debt for the reporting year as of March 31st of the next year and the final data as of September 30th of the next year.

reports.title: Décret n°100/097 du 30 juillet 2026 portant modification du Décret n°100/117 du 21 avril 2021 portant réorganisation du Fonds National d'Investissement Communal « FONIC »
reports.publisher: Présidence de la République du Burundi
reports.description: Presidential decree reorganizing FONIC (Fonds National d'Investissement Communal), Burundi's national fund for managing and accounting for state budget credits allocated to communal investment. Downloaded from presidence.gov.bi and OCR'd (tesseract, French model) from a scanned/image PDF — not machine-selectable text, so quotes are high-confidence but not pixel-verified against original glyphs; the decree's own header/number in the raw OCR reads garbled ("DECRET N°100/ 04 DU 20 JUILLET 2026"), which does not exactly match the decree number and date given in the source URL (n°100/097, 30 juillet 2026) — treated as an OCR misread of the header/logo area, not a different document, since Article 2 and Article 67 text match verbatim between the URL's linked PDF and the OCR. Article 1 confirms it "modifie le Décret n°100/117 du 21 avril 2021 portant Modification du Décret n°100/270 du 22 novembre 2013 portant Réorganisation du Fonds National d'Investissement Communal" [amends the 2021 decree, itself an amendment of a 2013 decree, reorganizing FONIC]. Article 2: "Le FONIC a son siège au chef-lieu de la commune GITEGA dans la province GITEGA, avec un service du budget et de la comptabilité dans chaque commune" [FONIC is headquartered in Gitega commune/province, with a budget-and-accounting service in every commune] — FONIC is described as an "Administration Personnalisée de l'Etat (APE)" under tutelle of the Ministère en charge du développement communautaire. Article 67 (Section 5, "Des modalités de rapportage des crédits budgétaires destinés à l'investissement au niveau communal"): "Le FONIC produit des rapports trimestriel, semestriel et annuel détaillant l'utilisation des fonds mis à sa disposition en relation avec les investissements prévus et les investissements réalisés par commune" [FONIC produces quarterly, half-yearly and annual reports detailing fund use versus planned and realized investment, per commune], format set by joint ministerial order (finances + développement communautaire), addressed to the Minister for développement communautaire with copy to the Minister of Finance. This is organizational/procedural: the decree itself contains no per-commune figures — it establishes the reporting mandate, not the actual filled-in figures (see _dropped for the unlocated underlying reports).
reports.cadence_note: One-off amending decree to FONIC's organizational framework (itself part of a decree lineage: 2013 -> 2021 -> 2026); the reports it mandates (Article 67) are quarterly/half-yearly/annual.

_dropped.why: Considered but rejected. The 2015 Loi 1/16 (Art. 36, per the existing corpus node af-burundi-deepen.json) creates a communal support fund ("fonds d'appui aux communes"), and it is plausible FONIC descends from that mechanism — but the FONIC decree's own legal-basis ("Vu") clauses do NOT cite the 2015 Loi 1/16 or its Article 36 anywhere in the OCR'd text (checked full-text for "Article 36", "fonds d'appui", "2015", "péréquation" — zero relevant hits). Instead, its citation chain is entirely FONIC-internal: it amends Décret n°100/117 (21 avril 2021), which amended Décret n°100/270 (22 novembre 2013). There IS a "Loi n°1/16" cited in the Vu clauses, but it is a false-friend by numbering coincidence only: "Loi n°1/16 du 07 juin 2024 portant Modification du Décret-Loi n°1/024 du 13 juillet 1989 portant Cadre Organique des Administrations Personnalisées de l'Etat" — a 2024 law about the legal status of Administrations Personnalisées de l'Etat generally (relevant because FONIC is itself an APE), not the 2015 communal-transfer law. Per the evidence rule (edge requires the source text to actually name the target document), no edge is minted; flagged so a future pass does not conflate the two differently-dated "Loi 1/16" citations.

Article 67 legally mandates FONIC to produce quarterly, half-yearly and annual reports itemized "par commune" — exactly the kind of named-lower-tier-unit document this project is looking for — but no published copy of an actual FONIC report (with real per-commune investment figures) was located on any .bi domain within the prior agent's search budget. This is the strongest lead in the round for a follow-up search, not a resolved node.

mairiebujumbura.gov.bi does not resolve at all (DNS failure, reproduced via both WebFetch and curl: "Could not resolve host"). isoko.gov.bi's government-services directory confirms this as the "official" URL for the Mairie de Bujumbura and gives only address/hours, no budget or finance content. No fiscal document for Burundi's largest city (Bujumbura) was found; the dead domain is itself circumstantial evidence of thin municipal e-government infrastructure, but no primary document states why it is down.

provincegitega.gov.bi loads successfully but contains no budget, financial report, or revenue figures anywhere on the site; its only finance-adjacent element is an outbound link to the national finances.gov.bi, not a Gitega-specific document.

courdescomptes.bi confirms an institutional chamber explicitly mandated for communal affairs ("Chambre des Affaires Administratives et des Communes") and lists report categories (Rapports Publics Annuels, Rapports Spécialisés, Rapports sur l'Exécution du Budget Général de l'Etat), but the individual report sub-pages were identified, not fetched, before the prior agent's search budget ran out — no actual named-commune figures were verified. Explicitly flagged by the prior agent as worth a follow-up session with fresh search budget.

https://assemblee.bi/2025/01/10/mecanismes-de-suivi-des-communes-des-institutions-a-renforcer/ (title translates to "Communal oversight mechanisms: institutions to be strengthened", directly on-topic) returned HTTP 404 on both WebFetch and direct curl — link rot, no longer live at this URL.

The Ministry of Finance's own décrets index page (finances.gov.bi/index.php/decrets/) does not surface any FONIC, dotation, or péréquation decree at its current listing level (visible entries cover pension increases, provincial directorates, financial-intelligence-unit rules, etc.) — the FONIC decree used as this file's node was instead found directly via presidence.gov.bi, not via this ministry index.

reports.title: Departamento de Santa Cruz — low-poverty economic hub
reports.description: Eastern lowland department and the country’s main agro-industrial and commercial engine. Lowest departmental poverty incidence.
reports._notes: Economic counterweight to the highland departments. Poverty incidence among the lowest in the country (~20–25% range in recent readings); hosts the bulk of soy, beef and related agro-industry.

reports.title: Departamento de Potosí — high-poverty highland contrast
reports.description: Highland mining department with among the highest poverty and extreme-poverty incidence.
reports._notes: Poverty-contrast department. Frequently ranks near the top of departmental poverty (mid-to-high 40s–50s % in recent years) despite its historic and ongoing mining role.

reports.title: Departamento de Chuquisaca — high-poverty contrast
reports.description: Southern highland/valley department with elevated poverty incidence.
reports._notes: Completes the high-poverty highland set alongside Potosí. Poverty incidence often above 50% in recent readings.

reports.title: Departamento de La Paz — capital region
reports.description: Western highland department containing the seat of government (La Paz) and El Alto. Intermediate-to-higher poverty and the largest absolute number of people in poverty.
reports._notes: Demographic and political core. Large absolute poverty mass even when rates are not the highest; hosts the dual-city complex of La Paz and El Alto.

reports.title: La Paz / El Alto — dual-city metropolitan complex
reports.description: Dual-city capital complex: La Paz (seat of government) and the adjacent, rapidly grown city of El Alto on the Altiplano. Primary urban domain for labour, income, poverty and social-programme analysis in the western highlands.
reports._notes: Lived-economy core of the western highlands. El Alto in particular is a dense, commercially dynamic, largely Aymara city that grew from migration; multidimensional poverty readings remain elevated. Continuously cited as a distinct geographic domain in household-survey and urban-poverty analysis.

reports.title: Yacimientos de Litio Bolivianos (YLB) — state lithium company
reports.publisher: YLB / Ministerio de Hidrocarburos y Energía
reports.description: State company charged with the industrialisation of Bolivia’s lithium resources, centred on the Salar de Uyuni (world’s largest known resources). Contracts with Chinese and Russian partners for direct-extraction plants.
reports._notes: Strategic future-resource node. Production remains far below commercial scale relative to Chile and Argentina; recent contracts (CBC/China, Uranium One/Russia) aim to scale direct lithium extraction. Continuously cited in industrial-policy and fiscal-revenue outlook analysis.

reports.title: Salar de Uyuni — lithium resource base
reports.description: World’s largest known lithium resource (salt flat in Potosí department). Geographic and symbolic core of Bolivia’s lithium strategy.
reports._notes: Foundational natural-resource node. Continuously cited as the physical base of the lithium industrialisation effort; also a national and Indigenous heritage symbol.

reports.title: Departamento de Cochabamba — central valley hub
reports.description: Central valley department and the third major population and economic pole after La Paz and Santa Cruz. Intermediate poverty and large absolute poverty mass.
reports._notes: Completes the central economic axis (La Paz–Cochabamba–Santa Cruz). Large absolute number of people in poverty even when rates are not the highest.

reports.title: Departamento de Tarija — southern gas and agricultural zone
reports.description: Southern department historically linked to gas production and agricultural activity. Intermediate poverty incidence.
reports._notes: Gas-producing department. Poverty rates intermediate; economic structure has been shaped by the hydrocarbon cycle that is now contracting.

reports.title: Departamento de Oruro — highland mining
reports.description: Highland mining department with intermediate-to-elevated poverty.
reports._notes: Mining geography. Completes the highland departmental set alongside Potosí, Chuquisaca and La Paz.

reports.title: Departamento del Beni — northern lowland
reports.description: Northern Amazonian lowland department. Intermediate poverty with marked urban–rural gaps.
reports._notes: Lowland contrast to the highland departments. Completes the geographic coverage of the main departmental poverty gradient.

reports.title: Empresas públicas — performance and fiscal exposure
reports.description: State-owned enterprise sector (YPFB, YLB, BoA, Mi Teleférico, Mutún, etc.). Material source of fiscal risk when losses and debt accumulate.
reports._notes: Lived fiscal-risk node. A large group of state firms have operated at a loss; a subset has been flagged as critically indebted. Restructuring and possible liquidation have entered the policy agenda as gas rents decline.

reports.title: Departamento de Pando — northern Amazonian extreme
reports.description: Northernmost Amazonian department. Low population density, intermediate poverty, and distinct lowland living conditions.
reports._notes: Completes the full departmental set. Geographic and demographic extreme relative to the highland and central-axis departments.

reports.title: Eje central (La Paz – Cochabamba – Santa Cruz)
reports.description: The three-department demographic and economic corridor that concentrates the majority of population, formal activity, remittance inflows and absolute poverty numbers.
reports._notes: Analytical geography node. Most remittances, formal jobs and absolute poverty counts sit on this axis; the rest of the country is thinner demographically and economically.

reports.title: Territorios Indígena Originario Campesinos (TIOC)
reports.description: Indigenous Originary Peasant Territories — recognised collective territorial units that appear as geographic domains in census and survey tabulations.
reports._notes: Plurinational territorial node. Continuously cited as a distinct geographic and rights unit in official statistics and policy.
_referenced_by: Poverty and service-access studies that disaggregate by TIOC

reports.title: Contrato litio YLB–CBC (China)
reports.description: Investment and service contract for direct lithium extraction and residual-brine plants in the Salar de Uyuni area, with Chinese consortium participation and majority state stake.
reports._notes: Major international industrial-investment instrument. Part of the attempt to scale lithium production from the current low base; subject to ongoing political and legislative scrutiny.
_referenced_by: Policy debate on contract transparency and local benefit

reports.title: Contrato litio YLB–Uranium One (Rusia)
reports.description: Investment contract for a direct lithium extraction plant with Russian partner, complementary to the Chinese CBC arrangement.
reports._notes: Second major international lithium-investment instrument. Together with the CBC contract, defines the current external partnership architecture for lithium industrialisation.

reports.title: Relación energética Bolivia–Brasil (gasoducto y gas)
reports.description: Long-standing natural-gas export relationship with Brazil via the Bolivia–Brazil gas pipeline. Still the principal residual gas-export market after the end of the Argentina contract.
reports._notes: Core bilateral energy relationship. Volumes have declined but Brazil remains the main residual buyer; recent high-level statements explore ways to stabilise or expand cooperation.
_referenced_by: Analysis of the structural decline in gas volumes

reports.title: Relación comercial con China
reports.description: Bilateral trade relationship with China — major destination for minerals and origin of imports, and partner in lithium industrialisation.
reports._notes: Structural commercial and investment partner. Continuously cited in export (minerals) and import (machinery, intermediates) analysis and in the lithium partnership architecture.

meta.scope: Bolivia national core — converted/merged from the import's 6 pre-spec raw batches (2026-08-13), applying the current v2 data spec. 60 raw candidates reduced to 37 kept reports (23 dropped: 4 institution nodes, 12 framing nodes, 4 real-but-unstable/unverifiable topics deferred, 1 classification-not-a-publication, plus small containment cleanups). 51 raw proposed edges reduced to 21 kept dependencies (many converted from invalid legacy relationship types produced_by/part_of/related_to/complements into either valid dependency types with corrected direction, part_of fields on the Report, or dropped as not real data-lineage dependencies). 3 headline claims spot-verified: national-accounts base-year change to 2017/SCN2008 confirmed accurate; Bolivia's MERCOSUR membership claim found overstated (still mid-ratification, corrected by deferring the node); the two China/Russia lithium contracts confirmed real but currently suspended by a Bolivian court ruling with no public contract text, so deferred rather than minted.

reports.description: Annual household survey that is the primary source for labour-market indicators, household income, and income-based poverty and inequality measurement. National coverage with urban/rural and departmental domains.

reports.title: Pobreza monetaria / Monetary poverty
reports.description: Official income-poverty and extreme-poverty incidence, calculated by comparing household per-capita income (from EH) with nationally defined poverty lines. Published with urban/rural and departmental breakdowns.
