reports.title: Finanças do Brasil — Dados Contábeis dos Municípios (FINBRA), via SICONFI
reports.publisher: Secretaria do Tesouro Nacional (STN), Ministério da Fazenda
reports.description: The national consolidation of every Brazilian federative entity's accounting and fiscal declarations, collected through SICONFI (Sistema de Informações Contábeis e Fiscais do Setor Público Brasileiro) and published by the Tesouro Nacional. STN's own Cartilha defines it and names its statutory origin in one sentence, quoted directly: "O Finbra é o nome do banco de dados formado pelas informações das declarações recebidas pelo Tesouro Nacional por determinação da Lei Complementar 101/2000, a Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal – LRF. Tal banco de dados contém um conjunto de informações contábeis e fiscais enviadas pelos entes da Federação sobre a sua execução orçamentária e financeira." Its history and the tense shift, both quoted directly: "O Finbra nasceu como uma série de volumes publicados anualmente pelo Tesouro Nacional, intitulada 'Finanças do Brasil – Dados Contábeis dos Municípios'. Cada volume continha os dados consolidados da execução orçamentária de quase 5.500 municípios brasileiros, referentes ao exercício financeiro anterior" — note "nasceu como", past tense: the printed annual volume series is historical. The live form is stated in the same document: "Em 2014, com a criação do Siconfi ... o novo Finbra passou a ser disponibilizado em formato CSV, atualizado de maneira automática e online, sem a necessidade de processamentos adicionais. É uma consulta pública e que fica disponível para qualquer usuário que tenha acesso à internet." What it now contains is stated twice: "Com o aumento da quantidade de relatórios recebidos no Siconfi em 2015, o Finbra foi consequentemente aprimorado para trazer, além de todos os dados da Contas Anuais, também os dados do Relatório Resumido de Execução Orçamentária – RREO e do Relatório de Gestão Fiscal – RGF", and "A tela mostrará três opções de consultas de acordo com os relatórios recebidos: Contas Anuais, RGF e RREO." This makes FINBRA the aggregation point for br-rreo and br-rgf (br-fiscal-responsibility-law.json), which until this round had no downstream at all. The Cartilha PDF was fetched with plain curl at TIER A (HTTP 200, 952,735 bytes, a genuine text PDF extracted with pdftotext -layout); the STN product page and the SICONFI consultation page were both independently confirmed reachable at TIER A. The gov.br/tesouronacional contabilidade-e-custos/siconfi page suggested as an alternative route returns a genuine HTTP 401 ("Conteúdo Restrito É necessário autenticar para visualizar essa página") and is not used.
reports.cadence_note: Two cadences, and the document is explicit about which is which. The original series was annual — "uma série de volumes publicados anualmente pelo Tesouro Nacional", one volume per exercício financeiro — but STN's own text puts that in the past tense ("nasceu como"). Since 2014 the live product is a continuously-updated public CSV consultation ("atualizado de maneira automática e online"), which has no discrete release event to count. releases_per_year is kept at 1 because the underlying declarations remain organised by exercício and the Contas Anuais consultation is annual by construction; it should be read as the reporting cycle, not as a publication event, and the continuous form means the true figure is either much higher or undefined.

reports.title: Manual de Demonstrativos Fiscais (MDF)
reports.publisher: Secretaria do Tesouro Nacional (STN), Ministério da Fazenda
reports.description: STN's standing methodological manual for the LRF's fiscal demonstratives — the direct sibling of br-mcasp (Manual de Contabilidade Aplicada ao Setor Público, br-fpm-population.json), covering the fiscal reports where MCASP covers the accounting standards. Its scope is defined verbatim in STN's own FINBRA Cartilha: "O RREO deve ser elaborado seguindo as regras contidas no Manual de Demonstrativos Fiscais – MDF. O MDF estabelece regras de harmonização a serem observadas, de forma permanente, pela Administração Pública para a elaboração do Anexo de Riscos Fiscais (ARF), do Anexo de Metas Fiscais (AMF), do Relatório Resumido da Execução Orçamentária (RREO) e do Relatório de Gestão Fiscal (RGF), e define orientações metodológicas, consoante os parâmetros definidos pela LRF." That single sentence names all four instruments it governs, two of which are already nodes (br-rreo, br-rgf), and states its own subordination to the LRF (br-lc-101-2000). Its reissue rule, also verbatim: "O MDF é constantemente atualizado, e a observância da edição vigente deve ser dada seguindo o exercício financeiro..." HONEST LIMITATION ON THIS NODE, stated rather than glossed: the MDF's own document and its own STN landing page were NOT fetched this round. Every quotation above is STN's description of the MDF inside the FINBRA/SICONFI Cartilha (TIER A, plain curl, genuine text PDF) — an authoritative first-party source for what the MDF is and what it governs, written by the same Secretaria that publishes it, but not the manual's own text. The `url` below therefore points at that Cartilha rather than at an unverified MDF URL. A future round should re-source this node from a specific numbered edition of the MDF itself, which would also give the node a real edition history in the shape br-mcasp already has.
reports.cadence_note: Inferred, not stated. STN says only "O MDF é constantemente atualizado, e a observância da edição vigente deve ser dada seguindo o exercício financeiro" — one binding edition per exercício financeiro, which implies an annual reissue without stating a periodicity. Same convention and the same honesty flag as br-mcasp's own cadence_note in br-fpm-population.json ("Not stated as a fixed periodicity by STN. Estimated, not stated"), except that here not even a list of dated editions was observed, so the estimate is weaker than br-mcasp's.

reports.title: Contas Nacionais Trimestrais (CNT)
reports.publisher: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)
reports.description: The quarterly national accounts, and the release that carries Brazil's headline GDP figure. Its international basis is stated verbatim on IBGE's own page: "As estimativas das CNT seguem as recomendações internacionais reunidas no mais recente manual das Nações Unidas - Sistema de Contas Nacionais (SNA 2008). Todas as transações definidas no SNA para a produção (transações mercantis e não mercantis) são registradas em regime de competência, exceto as receitas do governo, que são registradas em regime de caixa." Its dependence on the annual accounts is stated equally plainly, and mechanically: "Os dados trimestrais são ajustados para os totais anuais (Sistema de Contas Nacionais Anuais - SCN), usando o procedimento estatístico de benchmarking (Denton)." That sentence is the basis for this node's edge to br-scn — the quarterly series is constrained to sum to the annual totals by a named statistical procedure, not merely cross-referenced. The page's current edition at the time of research was "Tabelas - 1º trimestre 2026". Fetched with plain curl at TIER A (HTTP 200, 151,398 bytes).
reports.cadence_note: IBGE's own metadata block states: "Tipo de operação estatística: Sistema de contas nacionais | Tipo de dados: Outro tipo de dados | Periodicidade de divulgação: Trimestral".

reports.title: Lei nº 8.213, de 24 de julho de 1991 (Planos de Benefícios da Previdência Social) — art. 41-A
reports.description: The statute governing Brazil's general social-security benefit regime (RGPS), "Dispõe sobre os Planos de Benefícios da Previdência Social e dá outras providências", used here in its consolidated (texto compilado) form. Art. 41-A, inserted by Lei nº 11.430/2006, is the provision that closes br-ipca-fpe.json's own open lead on INPC's statutory downstream use, quoted directly: "Art. 41-A. O valor dos benefícios em manutenção será reajustado, anualmente, na mesma data do reajuste do salário mínimo, pro rata, de acordo com suas respectivas datas de início ou do último reajustamento, com base no Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor - INPC, apurado pela Fundação Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística - IBGE." The statute names the index by name and names IBGE by name as its producer — the exact combination br-ipca-fpe.json searched for and did not find. Its interaction with the minimum wage is also stated, § 4º: "Para os benefícios que tenham sido majorados devido à elevação do salário mínimo, o referido aumento deverá ser compensado no momento da aplicação do disposto no caput deste artigo, de acordo com normas a serem baixadas pelo Ministério da Previdência Social." Present tense and in force. One-off foundational instrument per Research.1.md §4 — a standing statute defining a method, amended in place rather than reissued, so no releases_per_year is given; same convention as br-lc-101-2000 and br-lc-62-1989. Fetched at TIER A from planalto.gov.br (HTTP 200, 753,510 bytes) with a browser User-Agent header; the identical header-less request returns "curl: (52) Empty reply from server", which is a request-shaping requirement rather than a content workaround and is recorded rather than hidden.
reports.cadence_note: A statute, amended rather than reissued — same convention as br-lc-101-2000 (br-fiscal-responsibility-law.json) and br-lc-62-1989 (br-ipca-fpe.json). The annual cadence lives in the instrument that executes it, br-portaria-reajuste-inss, not here.

reports.title: Portaria Interministerial MPS/MF de reajuste dos benefícios do INSS (edição em vigor: nº 13, de 9 de janeiro de 2026)
reports.publisher: Ministério da Previdência Social / Ministério da Fazenda
reports.description: The annual joint ministerial instrument that actually applies the RGPS benefit readjustment art. 41-A of Lei 8.213/1991 commands. Ementa, quoted directly: "Dispõe sobre o reajuste dos benefícios pagos pelo Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social - INSS e demais valores constantes do Regulamento da Previdência Social - RPS e dos valores previstos nos incisos II a VIII do § 1º do art. 11 da Emenda Constitucional nº 103, de 12 de novembro de 2019..." Its preamble names its own legal basis chain verbatim: "OS MINISTROS DE ESTADO DA PREVIDÊNCIA SOCIAL E DA FAZENDA, no uso da atribuição que lhes confere o inciso II do parágrafo único do art. 87 da Constituição, e tendo em vista o disposto na Emenda Constitucional nº 20, de 15 de dezembro de 1998; ... no art. 41-A da Lei nº 8.213, de 24 de julho de 1991; na Lei nº 14.663, de 28 de agosto de 2023; no Decreto nº 12.797, de 23 de dezembro de 2025; e no Regulamento da Previdência Social - RPS, aprovado pelo Decreto nº 3.048, de 6 de maio de 1999, resolvem:" Art. 1º states the result: "Os benefícios pagos pelo Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social - INSS serão reajustados, a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2026, em 3,90% (três inteiros e noventa centésimos por cento)." IMPORTANT NEGATIVE, CARRIED ON THE NODE SO IT CANNOT BE QUIETLY FILLED IN LATER: the full DOU text of this Portaria contains ZERO occurrences of "INPC" and names no price index at all. It states the resulting percentage and not the index that produced it. The INPC naming is exactly one hop upstream, in art. 41-A of Lei 8.213, which this preamble cites by article number — so this file wires portaria -> br-lei-8213 -> br-inpc and deliberately does NOT draw a direct portaria -> br-inpc edge, which would overstate the evidence. Published metadata, verbatim: "Publicado em: 12/01/2026 | Edição: 7 | Seção: 1 | Página: 58". Fetched at TIER A from the Imprensa Nacional's own DOU page (HTTP 200, 104,885 bytes), located by extracting `urlTitle` from the in.gov.br search endpoint's embedded JSON. The Ministry's own PDF of the same Portaria is a scanned raster with no extractable text and was not usable; a bibliotecadigital.gestao.gov.br mirror returned a genuine 403.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, and the periodicity is an inference from the series rather than a verbatim statement inside the instrument — flagged rather than asserted. One Portaria Interministerial per year, published each January, fixing that year's readjustment percentage. The statutory basis for the annual rhythm is art. 41-A's own "será reajustado, anualmente, na mesma data do reajuste do salário mínimo", which this Portaria executes; the instrument itself states only its own effective date ("a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2026"). No release_schedule is given: only one dated instance was observed this round, which is thinner than the two-point pattern br-ipca-fpe.json required before projecting br-fpe-dn-tcu's calendar.

reports.title: Lei nº 14.663, de 28 de agosto de 2023 (política de valorização permanente do salário mínimo)
reports.description: The statute establishing Brazil's permanent minimum-wage valorisation policy, and the cleanest live INPC dependency located in this corpus. Art. 1º, quoted directly: "Esta Lei define o valor do salário mínimo a partir de 1º de maio de 2023, estabelece a política de valorização permanente do salário mínimo a vigorar a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2024, e altera os valores da tabela mensal do Imposto sobre a Renda da Pessoa Física (IRPF)..." Art. 3º caput sets the two-term formula: "Ficam estabelecidas as diretrizes para a política de valorização do salário mínimo a vigorar a partir de 2024, inclusive, a serem aplicadas em 1º de janeiro do respectivo ano, considerado que o valor decorrerá da soma do índice de medida da inflação do ano anterior, para a preservação do poder aquisitivo, com o índice correspondente ao crescimento real do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) de 2 (dois) anos anteriores, para fins de aumento real, conforme apuração nos termos deste artigo." § 1º names the index and its producer: "Os reajustes para a preservação do poder aquisitivo do salário mínimo corresponderão à variação do Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor (INPC), calculado e divulgado pela Fundação Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), acumulada nos 12 (doze) meses encerrados em novembro do exercício anterior ao do reajuste." § 4º names IBGE for the GDP term as well — "a taxa de crescimento real do PIB do segundo ano anterior ao da fixação do valor do salário mínimo, apurada pelo IBGE até o último dia útil do ano e divulgada no ano anterior ao de aplicação do aumento real" — but names no titled release, which is why no GDP edge is minted from this node (see _dropped). The statute also fixes what happens when the index is late, §§ 2º–3º: "Na hipótese de não divulgação do INPC referente a um ou mais meses compreendidos no período do cálculo até o último dia útil imediatamente anterior à vigência do reajuste, o Poder Executivo federal estimará os índices dos meses não disponíveis" and "os índices estimados permanecerão válidos para os fins do disposto nesta Lei, sem qualquer revisão, e os eventuais resíduos serão compensados no reajuste subsequente, sem retroatividade" — a documented fallback rule for a missing input, which is the kind of method fidelity this corpus exists to capture. One-off foundational instrument per Research.1.md §4, so no releases_per_year. Fetched at TIER A from planalto.gov.br (HTTP 200, 36,354 bytes) with a browser User-Agent header.
reports.cadence_note: A statute defining a method, applied each 1 January by a separate annual decree (br-decreto-salario-minimo). Art. 3º fixes the application date verbatim — "a serem aplicadas em 1º de janeiro do respectivo ano" — but the statute itself is not reissued.

reports.title: Decreto anual de fixação do salário mínimo (edição em vigor: Decreto nº 12.797, de 23 de dezembro de 2025)
reports.description: The annual decree that fixes the minimum wage the following year, executing the formula Lei 14.663/2023 defines. Ementa, quoted directly: "Dispõe sobre o valor do salário mínimo a vigorar a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2026." Preamble, naming its statutory basis: "O PRESIDENTE DA REPÚBLICA, no uso da atribuição que lhe confere o art. 84, caput, inciso IV, da Constituição, e tendo em vista o disposto na Lei nº 14.663, de 28 de agosto de 2023, e na Lei nº 15.077, de 27 de dezembro de 2024, DECRETA:" Art. 1º and its parágrafo único give the result: "A partir de 1º de janeiro de 2026, o valor do salário mínimo será de R$ 1.621,00 (mil seiscentos e vinte e um reais)" and "Em decorrência do disposto no caput, o valor diário do salário mínimo corresponderá a R$ 54,04 (cinquenta e quatro reais e quatro centavos) e o valor horário, a R$ 7,37 (sete reais e trinta e sete centavos)." The R$ 1.621,00 figure reappears verbatim inside Portaria Interministerial MPS/MF nº 13/2026 art. 2º ("não poderão ser inferiores a R$ 1.621,00 (mil seiscentos e vinte e um reais)"), independently confirming this decree's downstream use from a second document rather than from the decree's own claim about itself. Publication note, verbatim: "Este texto não substitui o publicado no DOU de 24.12.2025." Fetched at TIER A from planalto.gov.br (HTTP 200, 10,327 bytes) with a browser User-Agent header.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, and the periodicity is a series-level inference rather than a statement inside the instrument — flagged rather than asserted, same as br-portaria-reajuste-inss. VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A (planalto.gov.br, plain curl with a browser User-Agent, HTTP 200, 36,354 bytes). Lei 14.663/2023 art. 3º § 1º: "Os reajustes para a preservação do poder aquisitivo do salário mínimo corresponderão à variação do Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor (INPC), calculado e divulgado pela Fundação Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), acumulada nos 12 (doze) meses encerrados em novembro do exercício anterior ao do reajuste." A second, independent statutory INPC dependency alongside br-lei-8213 -> br-inpc, and the more precisely specified of the two: it names the index, names IBGE as producer, and fixes the exact accumulation window. `calculated_from` because the inflation term of the minimum wage is arithmetically the accumulated INPC variation, not a contextual reference. reference_period.stated_as: "acumulada nos 12 (doze) meses encerrados em novembro do exercício anterior ao do reajuste" — Lei 14.663/2023 art. 3º § 1º. INPC publishes monthly; this edge carries a reading once a year, over a twelve-month window closing at the end of November.

dependencies.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A (STN's own FINBRA/SICONFI Cartilha PDF). The MDF's scope sentence ends by subordinating its own methodology to the LRF's parameters: "O MDF estabelece regras de harmonização a serem observadas, de forma permanente, pela Administração Pública para a elaboração do Anexo de Riscos Fiscais (ARF), do Anexo de Metas Fiscais (AMF), do Relatório Resumido da Execução Orçamentária (RREO) e do Relatório de Gestão Fiscal (RGF), e define orientações metodológicas, consoante os parâmetros definidos pela LRF." `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`: the MDF is not merely authorised by the LRF, its content is derived from it — the demonstratives it standardises are the ones LC 101/2000 arts. 52–55 require, and the limits and defined terms they test against are the statute's own. CAVEAT, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: this quotation is STN's description of the MDF inside the FINBRA Cartilha, not the MDF's own text. It is a first-party source (same Secretaria, same publisher) but not the dependent document itself, which is the strict form of the project's rule. See the node description on br-mdf and the caveat entry in _dropped.

VERIFIED, TIER A SOURCE BUT NOT FROM THE DEPENDENT DOCUMENT'S OWN TEXT — the weakness is stated here rather than in a footnote. STN's FINBRA/SICONFI Cartilha states the obligation directly and by name: "O RREO deve ser elaborado seguindo as regras contidas no Manual de Demonstrativos Fiscais – MDF." The MDF's own scope sentence names the RREO again from the other side: "O MDF estabelece regras de harmonização a serem observadas, de forma permanente, pela Administração Pública para a elaboração do ... Relatório Resumido da Execução Orçamentária (RREO) ... e define orientações metodológicas, consoante os parâmetros definidos pela LRF." So the relationship is asserted twice in the same first-party document, in both directions. `methodology_depends_on` is the right type — the MDF is exactly a method manual, and "o RREO deve ser elaborado seguindo as regras contidas no MDF" is a compliance obligation, not a reference. What it is NOT is a statement from an actual RREO instance about its own inputs, and the project's rule asks for the dependent document's own text. A purist should re-source this edge from a filed RREO or from the MDF itself; it is minted at MEDIUM confidence rather than dropped because the source is the Secretaria that publishes all three documents. This edge sits alongside, and does not replace, br-rreo -> br-lc-101-2000 in br-fiscal-responsibility-law.json: statute supplies the required content, manual supplies the harmonised form.

_dropped.edge: br-fpe-dn-tcu -> br-pnad-continua (PNAD Contínua as the source of TCU's 'renda domiciliar per capita (rdpc)' column in the FPE Decisão Normativa)
_dropped.why: REJECTED, AND THE REJECTION IS ONE OF THIS ROUND'S MOST VALUABLE FINDINGS. br-ipca-fpe.json's strongest open lead was that PNAD Contínua supplies the rdpc figures TCU uses to compute the FPE coefficients. It was tested at three independent levels of the chain and failed at all three, and a fourth, numeric test failed as well. (1) THE TCU SIDE. TCU's DN 209/2024 (FPE-2025) was re-read in full. Its Anexo column notes source the population column to a statutory hook — "Coluna B: população da UF fornecida pela Fundação Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) com data de referência em 31/7/2022 e malha territorial de 30/4/2023 (art. 102, inciso I, da Lei 8.443, de 16/7/1992)" — but source the income column to the agency and nothing else: "Coluna F: renda domiciliar per capita (rdpc) da UF fornecida pelo IBGE, relativa ao exercício de 2023." The table header says the same: "Renda domiciliar per capita (rdpc) (fonte: IBGE, ref. 2023)". PNAD CONTÍNUA IS NOT NAMED ANYWHERE IN THE DN — no survey name, no titled release, no statutory hook. (2) THE STATUTE SIDE, checked as an alternative route. LC 62/1989 art. 2º § 3º (redação da LC 143/2013) does not even name IBGE: "Para efeito do disposto neste artigo, serão considerados os valores censitários ou as estimativas mais recentes da população e da renda domiciliar per capita publicados pela entidade federal competente." The contrast inside the same statute is instructive — art. 3º does name the agency ("...com base no resultado do Censo de 1991, realizado pela Fundação IBGE") — so the generic wording in § 3º is a drafting choice, not an oversight. (3) THE IBGE SIDE. PNAD Contínua is solidly documented as a release and is minted as a node on its own merits, but nothing on IBGE's side claims TCU as a consumer. (4) THE NUMERIC CORROBORATION TEST, run because no document connects the two, AND IT CAME BACK NEGATIVE. TCU's own Anexo gives the national figure it used: "Na observação, apresenta-se o valor da rdpcn, também fornecido pelo IBGE (R$ 1.892,75), a partir do qual se calcula o valor de referência (72% da rdpcn = R$ 1.362,78)". PNADC's published 2023 headline, from the "Rendimento de todas as fontes: 2023" release itself: "...ainda maior (11,5%), alcançando o valor de R$ 1 848, o maior da...". R$ 1 848 ≠ R$ 1.892,75. The published series is real (deflated); TCU's appears to be nominal or otherwise differently based. A query to IBGE's own SIDRA/servicodados aggregate metadata API (api/v3/agregados?pesquisa=PD, HTTP 200) found NO PNADC aggregate publishing a national mean renda domiciliar per capita at all — the PNADC tables expose rdpc only as classes/faixas, never as a national mean level. CONCLUSION, STATED PLAINLY SO IT IS NOT QUIETLY RE-OPENED: the most likely real-world mechanism is a direct, unpublished data supply from IBGE to TCU, which would mean there is no document node behind that column at all and br-ipca-fpe.json's 'gap' is a genuine structural feature of the Brazilian FPE process rather than a research failure. If a future round confirms that, the right modelling is a terminus (TerminalReason 'unpublishable') on the TCU side, not an edge to PNADC. Verification: TCU at TIER B (portal.tcu.gov.br returned HTTP 200 and ~50KB that were a JS bot-challenge page, not the PDF — confirmed by inspecting the bytes: `<!DOCTYPE html> ... window["bobcmn"]`), LC 62/1989 and the PNADC release PDF at TIER A.

_dropped.edge: Resolução CMN nº 2.615, de 30 de junho de 1999 -> br-ibge-ipca (the resolution that first named IPCA as Brazil's inflation-target index)
_dropped.why: FOUND, VERIFIED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED — this resolves br-ipca-fpe.json's own open question about the number while producing a negative on the node. Resolução CMN 2.615/1999 was fetched at TIER A from the Banco Central's own normativo repository (bcb.gov.br/pre/normativos/res/1999/pdf/res_2615_v2_L.pdf, HTTP 200, 18,544 bytes, genuine text PDF). THE NUMBER br-ipca-fpe.json DECLINED TO ASSERT IS CORRECT. Ementa: "Fixa as metas para a inflação e seus respectivos intervalos de tolerância, bem como o índice de preços a que se aplicam, para os anos 2001, 2000 e 1999." Art. 1º, verbatim, is exactly the provision that was being looked for: "Determinar que o índice de preços relacionado às metas para a inflação, referido no art. 1º, parágrafo 1º, do Decreto nº 3.088, de 21 de junho de 1999, é o Índice de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo (IPCA), calculado pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)." Its preamble names the parent decree: "...tendo em vista o disposto no Decreto nº 3.088, de 21 de junho de 1999, RESOLVEU". Signed "Brasília, 30 de junho de 1999 / Arminio Fraga Neto / Presidente". WHY IT IS STILL NOT A NODE: it is revoked, and the revocation was independently verified rather than taken from the face of the document alone. The BCB PDF carries the flag "Documento normativo revogado pela Resolução nº 4.367, de 11/9/2014", and Res. 4.367/2014 was fetched separately (TIER A, HTTP 200, 19,020 bytes); its Art. 1º lists the revoked instruments verbatim and 2.615 is among them: "Ficam revogadas as Resoluções ns. 38, de 15 de outubro de 1966; ... 2.615, de 30 de junho de 1999; 2.776, de 3 de outubro de 2000; ...", under the ementa "Revoga resoluções sem função por decurso de prazo ou por regulamentação superveniente". Its parent, Decreto 3.088/1999, is also revoked (effective 1 January 2025 — see br-decreto-12079-2024 in br-ipca-fpe.json). This project does not mint discontinued or superseded instruments as live nodes, so no br-resolucao-cmn-2615 node and no historical IPCA edge is created; the live equivalent, br-resolucao-cmn-5141, is already in the corpus and already carries that edge. Recorded in full here because the finding is genuinely useful in both directions: it confirms the historical claim (IPCA has been the target index by CMN resolution continuously since 30 June 1999) and it closes the lead permanently, so no future round re-opens it expecting a live node.

_dropped.edge: br-lc-62-1989 -> a national GDP release (the '75% da variação real do Produto Interno Bruto nacional' term in the FPE floor)
_dropped.why: WEAK, FLAGGED BY THE RESEARCH AND NOT MINTED. LC 62/1989 art. 2º, inciso II (redação da LC 143/2013) states the term verbatim, at TIER A from planalto.gov.br: "a partir de 1º de janeiro de 2016, cada entidade beneficiária receberá valor igual ao que foi distribuído no correspondente decêndio do exercício de 2015, corrigido pela variação acumulada do Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo (IPCA) ou outro que vier a substituí-lo e pelo percentual equivalente a 75% (setenta e cinco por cento) da variação real do Produto Interno Bruto nacional do ano anterior ao ano considerado para base de cálculo." The IPCA half of that sentence is already minted (br-lc-62-1989 -> br-ipca, br-ipca-fpe.json). The GDP half is not, and the reason is precise: the statute names the CONCEPT "Produto Interno Bruto nacional" and names neither an agency nor a titled release. This is structurally the same gap as the rdpc column in TCU's FPE Decisão Normativa — an indicator reference, not a document-to-document dependency. It is deliberately not upgraded on the reasoning that 'everyone knows IBGE produces the PIB', which is exactly the inference the evidence standard exists to exclude. Note also that even granting the agency, the corpus now holds two candidate targets, br-scn (annual) and br-cnt (quarterly, which is where the headline annual growth rate actually lands), and nothing in the statute chooses between them. A future round could close this from the implementing side — TCU's own DN or an STN/Tesouro instrument may name the release it reads the GDP variation from, and that would be the document to look for, not another reading of LC 62.

_dropped.edge: br-lei-14663 -> a titled IBGE GDP release (the 'taxa de crescimento real do PIB ... apurada pelo IBGE' term in the minimum-wage formula)
_dropped.why: MEDIUM, AND STILL NOT MINTED — recorded separately from the LC 62 GDP entry above because the evidence is strictly stronger and the distinction is the finding. Lei 14.663/2023 art. 3º § 4º, TIER A from planalto.gov.br: "Para fins de aumento real, será aplicado, a partir de 2024, o percentual equivalente à taxa de crescimento real do PIB do segundo ano anterior ao da fixação do valor do salário mínimo, apurada pelo IBGE até o último dia útil do ano e divulgada no ano anterior ao de aplicação do aumento real." Unlike LC 62/1989, THIS STATUTE DOES NAME IBGE, and it fixes the reference period and the publication deadline. What it still does not name is a titled release. The blocker is therefore not 'which agency' but 'which of that agency's two national-accounts products': br-scn (Sistema de Contas Nacionais, anual) and br-cnt (Contas Nacionais Trimestrais) are both now nodes in this file, both publish real GDP growth, and the annual rate for a calendar year is in practice carried by the quarterly programme's fourth-quarter release while being consolidated by the annual one. Nothing in § 4º chooses between them, and picking one would be inventing the half of the citation the statute omitted. The corpus does hold a precedent for minting an agency-level edge — br-fpe-dn-tcu -> br-ibge-estimativas-populacao (br-ipca-fpe.json), where the DN also named only "fornecida pela ... IBGE" — but that case had exactly one plausible target and this one has two, which is the difference. A future round should look for the Executive's own calculation memo or the Decreto's exposição de motivos, which would name the release actually read.

_dropped.edge: br-scn -> br-pia-empresa / br-paic / br-pac / br-pas (the four IBGE annual surveys the national accounts name as their own inputs)
_dropped.why: A GENUINE LEAD, blocked only by the targets not existing. IBGE's own SCN page names its domestic inputs verbatim, at TIER A: "O Sistema de Contas Nacionais Anuais - SCN, como sistema síntese, reúne informações de várias pesquisas do IBGE tais como a Pesquisa Industrial Anual - Empresa - PIA-Empresa, a Pesquisa Anual da Indústria da Construção - PAIC, a Pesquisa Anual de Comércio - PAC e a Pesquisa Anual de Serviços - PAS. Reúne ainda informações econômicas de registros fiscais e administrativos como a Escrituração Contábil Fiscal - ECF e dados de agências reguladoras." This is the strongest form of evidence the project recognises — the dependent document naming its own inputs by title, in its own words — and four edges are available the moment the four survey nodes are researched. Each is a titled, recurrent IBGE annual release, so each qualifies as a node under the ordinary rule; none was researched this round because the round's budget went to the FINBRA and national-accounts clusters. The same sentence also names the Escrituração Contábil Fiscal (ECF), a Receita Federal tax-return record rather than a publication, which on the corpus's own rules is a terminus candidate (TerminalReason 'unpublishable') rather than a report — the same shape as the CRA PD7 accounts behind SEPH. Worth doing together, since the four surveys plus the ECF terminus would give br-scn a complete documented input set, which almost no node in this corpus has.

_dropped.edge: br-finbra -> the SICONFI 'Contas Anuais' / Declaração de Contas Anuais (DCA)
_dropped.why: A LEAD, and the third of FINBRA's three input streams. STN's Cartilha names all three together — "A tela mostrará três opções de consultas de acordo com os relatórios recebidos: Contas Anuais, RGF e RREO" — and two of the three are now minted as edges (br-finbra -> br-rreo, br-finbra -> br-rgf) because br-rreo and br-rgf already existed as nodes from br-fiscal-responsibility-law.json. The Contas Anuais / DCA has no node, and none was created from a single descriptive mention: the Cartilha names it as a consultation option, not as a titled recurring release with a publisher, cadence and URL of its own. It is a real annual filing obligation under LC 101/2000 art. 51 ("Os Estados e os Municípios encaminharão suas contas ao Poder Executivo da União até 30 de abril"), so the node is almost certainly buildable from a Tesouro Nacional instrument or the MDF itself — a tractable target for a future Brazilian fiscal round, alongside re-sourcing br-mdf from its own text.

_dropped.edge: br-rgf -> br-mdf (methodology citation sourced from STN's Cartilha rather than from the RGF's own text)
_dropped.why: AN ANNOTATION ON A MINTED EDGE, not a rejection. Both MDF edges in this file (br-rreo -> br-mdf and br-rgf -> br-mdf) rest on STN's FINBRA/SICONFI Cartilha describing the RREO and the RGF, not on an actual RREO or RGF instance stating its own methodological source. The project's rule asks for the dependent document's own text, and this is one step short of that. Two reasons they are minted anyway rather than dropped: the source is the Secretaria do Tesouro Nacional, which publishes all three documents, so it is first-party for every end of the relationship; and the relationship is asserted from both directions inside it ("O RREO deve ser elaborado seguindo as regras contidas no Manual de Demonstrativos Fiscais – MDF" from the report's side, and the MDF's own scope sentence naming the RREO and the RGF among the four demonstratives it governs). The RGF edge is the weaker of the two by one further step: only the RREO-specific "deve ser elaborado seguindo" sentence was reproduced verbatim from the extracted Cartilha text this round, so the RGF edge rests solely on the MDF scope sentence. Both should be re-sourced from a filed RGF/RREO or from the MDF's own front matter when br-mdf is re-researched from its own document.

HYPOTHESIS APPEARS FALSE, not merely unverified — which is a stronger and more useful answer than the one br-ipca-fpe.json's own _dropped entry recorded. That entry paired two hypothesised INPC uses, INSS benefit readjustment and FGTS correction. The INSS half is now closed with a real edge (br-lei-8213 -> br-inpc, minted in this file, and the round-1 entry rewritten as resolved). The FGTS half is not, and the reason is that FGTS accounts are remunerated by TR plus 3% a.a. under Lei 8.036/1990, not by any consumer price index — so there is probably no instrument to find. Stated at the confidence it deserves: no primary text of Lei 8.036/1990 was fetched this round to quote that provision verbatim, so this is recorded as 'the hypothesis looks incorrect rather than merely unsourced', not as a verified negative. A future round wanting to close it properly should read Lei 8.036/1990 art. 13 directly rather than searching for an INPC instrument that the mechanism suggests does not exist.

reports.title: Real Property Tax Act Regulations (EC512/72 et seq.)
reports.description: One-off foundational regulatory instrument made under the Real Property Assessment Act, setting out the annual property-assessment-list and tax-notice process PEI municipalities' own tax bills and financial statements depend on. Section 3 requires the Minister to forward each municipality an annual real-property list by March 31, and deems an annual assessment list under the Real Property Assessment Act sufficient to meet that requirement.

reports.title: Maximum Benefit Amounts and Related Figures — Canada Pension Plan and Old Age Security (Quarterly)
reports.description: Official quarterly report giving Canada Pension Plan maximum benefit amounts alongside Old Age Security (OAS) pension and Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) monthly payment amounts, including GIS top-up tables by marital status and income level. Successor to the OAS payments page's discontinued rate tables, which now point here for combined OAS/GIS figures.

reports.title: Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor (INPC)
reports.publisher: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)
reports.description: IBGE's narrower consumer price index, tracking the purchasing power of wages for lower-income salaried households rather than general inflation. Its own methodology statement, quoted directly: "O INPC tem por objetivo a correção do poder de compra dos salários, através da mensuração das variações de preços da cesta de consumo da população assalariada com mais baixo rendimento. Esta faixa de renda foi criada com o objetivo de garantir uma cobertura populacional de 50% das famílias cuja pessoa de referência é assalariada e pertencente às áreas urbanas de cobertura do SNIPC." And: "Atualmente, a população-objetivo do INPC abrange as famílias com rendimentos de 1 a 5 salários mínimos, cuja pessoa de referência é assalariada..." -- against IPCA's 1-40 salários mínimos from any income source and no salaried restriction. Both indices are monthly and produced by IBGE under the same SNIPC (Sistema Nacional de Índices de Preços ao Consumidor). Fetched this session via the r.jina.ai rendering proxy after direct curl returned a 403 Cloudflare challenge on www.ibge.gov.br; the underlying document is IBGE's own product page.
reports.cadence_note: IBGE's own page states: "Periodicidade de divulgação: Mensal".

reports.title: Decreto nº 12.079, de 26 de junho de 2024
reports.description: Brazil's current decree establishing the inflation-targeting regime, in force since replacing Decreto nº 3.088/1999 (revoked effective 1 January 2025). It does not itself name a price index -- Art. 4º delegates that choice, quoted directly: "O índice de preços a ser adotado para fins do disposto neste Decreto será escolhido pelo Conselho Monetário Nacional..." -- the same structure as its 1999 predecessor, whose own Art. 3º read: "O índice de preços a ser adotado para os fins previstos neste Decreto será escolhido pelo CMN, mediante proposta do Ministro de Estado da Fazenda." The index the CMN actually chose under this decree is IPCA, named not here but in Resolução CMN nº 5.141/2024, issued the same day (see br-resolucao-cmn-5141). Fetched this session via plain, unmodified curl (HTTP 200) from planalto.gov.br -- no proxy involved.

reports.title: Resolução CMN nº 5.141, de 26 de junho de 2024
reports.publisher: Conselho Monetário Nacional (CMN) / Banco Central do Brasil
reports.description: The instrument that actually names IPCA as Brazil's inflation-targeting price index, issued the same day as Decreto 12.079/2024, which delegated the choice to the CMN without naming an index itself. Art. 1º, quoted directly: "O índice de preços a ser adotado para fins da nova sistemática de meta para a inflação... é o Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo – IPCA, calculado pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística – IBGE." The Banco Central's own historical-targets page confirms compliance is measured this way, reporting results as "Variação do IPCA" and linking each year's target resolution (CMN Resolutions 2842 through 5141) back to the same normativo repository. Fetched this session via the r.jina.ai rendering proxy: both bcb.gov.br/estabilidadefinanceira/exibenormativo and bcb.gov.br/controleinflacao/historicometas are JS-rendered and return no content to raw curl. The underlying documents are the Banco Central's own normativo pages, not third-party mirrors.

reports.title: Decisão Normativa-TCU — coeficientes individuais de participação no Fundo de Participação dos Estados e do Distrito Federal (FPE)
reports.description: The annual normative decision fixing every Brazilian state's and the Federal District's individual coefficient in the Fundo de Participação dos Estados, the constitutional transfer under art. 159, I, alínea "a" of the Federal Constitution -- a correction from an initially hypothesised art. 159 II, which is in fact a different fund (the IPI-Exportação fund, apportioned by export value, unrelated to population or income). Verified directly against the Constitution's own compiled text: "a) vinte e um inteiros e cinco décimos por cento ao Fundo de Participação dos Estados e do Distrito Federal; (Vide Lei Complementar nº 62, de 1989)" under art. 159, I -- FPE and FPM (alínea "b") are siblings under the same inciso, not parallel incisos. TCU's authority to calculate the coefficients comes from art. 161, parágrafo único, confirmed a third time verbatim in the DN itself: "a atribuição que lhe confere o art. 161, parágrafo único, da Constituição Federal" and "o constante no art. 159, inciso I, alínea 'a', da Constituição Federal". Unlike the FPM, the FPE formula includes a per-capita-income term (see br-lc-62-1989); DN 215/2025's own Anexo III (Nota Explicativa da Metodologia) works this through per state, with columns for population, "renda domiciliar per capita (rdpc)", inverse rdpc and the resulting coefficient. Anexo I gives the individual result, e.g. Acre 4,241365%, São Paulo 1,519448%, summing to 100%. As with the parallel FPM instrument (br-fpm-dn-tcu, in br-fpm-population.json), the population figure is sourced to the agency but not to a titled release, quoted directly from Anexo III: "Coluna B: população da UF fornecida pela Fundação Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) com data de referência em 1º/7/2024 (art. 102, inciso I, da Lei 8.443, de 16/7/1992)... Coluna F: renda domiciliar per capita (rdpc) da UF fornecida pelo IBGE, relativa ao exercício de 2024... Coluna K: excesso da rdpc... valor de referência – que corresponde a 72% da renda domiciliar per capita nacional (rdpcn)...". Fetched this session via the r.jina.ai rendering proxy for the TCU coefficients index page (portal.tcu.gov.br returned a TLS reset to direct curl); the DN 215/2025 and DN 221/2026 PDFs themselves were downloaded with plain, unmodified curl (HTTP 200, verified as real PDF binaries via pdftotext) -- the strongest verification tier, no proxy involved.
reports.cadence_note: One decision per exercise, parallel to the FPM DN series published on the same TCU page. Two dated instances observed this session: DN 215/2025 (19 de março de 2025, for exercício 2026) and DN 221/2026 (18 de março de 2026, for exercício 2027) -- a March cadence, distinct from FPM's observed November pattern in br-fpm-population.json.

entries.covers: Expected DN for coeficientes FPE 2028, projected from the two-instance March pattern

release_schedule.note: Only two dated instances were confirmed this session (DN 215/2025 and DN 221/2026), both in March -- thinner evidence than the FPM series' multi-year November pattern in br-fpm-population.json, but a real and internally consistent two-point pattern rather than a single date.

reports.title: Lei Complementar nº 62, de 28 de dezembro de 1989 (alterada pela Lei Complementar nº 143, de 17 de julho de 2013)
reports.description: The statute defining the FPE distribution formula, binding since 1989 and rewritten from 2016 onward by Lei Complementar nº 143/2013. Art. 2º III, quoted directly, defines the population-plus-inverse-income formula used above the statutory floor: "a parcela que superar o montante especificado no inciso II será distribuída proporcionalmente a coeficientes individuais de participação obtidos a partir da combinação de fatores representativos da população e do inverso da renda domiciliar per capita da entidade beneficiária... a) o fator representativo da população corresponderá à participação relativa da população da entidade beneficiária na população do País, observados os limites superior e inferior de, respectivamente, 0,07... e 0,012...; b) o fator representativo do inverso da renda domiciliar per capita corresponderá à participação relativa do inverso da renda domiciliar per capita da entidade beneficiária na soma dos inversos da renda domiciliar per capita de todas as entidades." The same article ties the FPE's own statutory floor to IPCA, quoted directly: "cada entidade beneficiária receberá valor igual ao que foi distribuído no correspondente decêndio do exercício de 2015, corrigido pela variação acumulada do Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo (IPCA)... e pelo percentual equivalente a 75% da variação real do Produto Interno Bruto nacional..." -- directly connecting the FPE mechanism back to IPCA (see br-ipca). Art. 2º § 3º sources the underlying population and income figures generically rather than naming IBGE: "serão considerados os valores censitários ou as estimativas mais recentes da população e da renda domiciliar per capita publicados pela entidade federal competente" -- the pre-2013 wording of the companion provision (Lei 8.443/1992 art. 102) did name IBGE explicitly; the current, LC 143/2013-amended text also generalises to "entidade competente do Poder Executivo federal". The original 1989 version of this law (superseded for distribution purposes from 2016) set a fixed 85%/15% regional split with an Anexo Único of 27 individual state/DF coefficients based on 1960s-era data; background reporting associates this frozen table with the STF's partial-unconstitutionality ruling in ADI 875/2010, which forced LC 143/2013 -- not independently verified from the STF's own text this session, so treated as historical context only (see _dropped). Fetched this session via plain, unmodified curl (HTTP 200) from planalto.gov.br -- no proxy involved.
reports.cadence_note: A statute, amended rather than reissued -- same convention as br-lei-8443 (br-fpm-population.json) and br-lc-101-2000 (br-fiscal-responsibility-law.json).

_dropped.edge: br-fpe-dn-tcu -> a titled IBGE release naming its own population and renda domiciliar per capita inputs
_dropped.why: HARDENED, NOT RESOLVED, 2026-08-13 (BRICS/G.2) — the round chased this lead and came back with a stronger negative than it started with. PNAD Contínua was found and minted (`br-pnad-continua`, in `br-g2-pnadc-siconfi-scn.json`) as the obvious candidate source for TCU's 'renda domiciliar per capita' column, and the edge was REJECTED on three independent grounds. (1) TCU's own DN still says only 'rdpc da UF fornecida pelo IBGE' — agency, never a titled release. (2) LC 62/1989 §3º does not even name IBGE, saying only 'entidade federal competente'. (3) DECISIVE: the numbers do not match. PNADC's published 2023 headline household per-capita income is R$ 1 848 against TCU's R$ 1.892,75, so TCU is not simply lifting the published PNADC figure. The most likely mechanism is an UNPUBLISHED IBGE-to-TCU data supply, which would mean there is no document node behind that column at all — a structural finding about the corpus's own limits, not a search that ran out of time. Compare the near-identical shape found in India the same round: FC16 names MoSPI for the GSDP behind its largest weighted criterion and likewise never names a publication. ORIGINAL BLOCKER, kept: The FPM pattern repeats at the state level. DN 215/2025's Anexo III names the agency and gives a reference date for both inputs -- "Coluna B: população da UF fornecida pela ... (IBGE) com data de referência em 1º/7/2024" and "Coluna F: renda domiciliar per capita (rdpc) da UF fornecida pelo IBGE, relativa ao exercício de 2024" -- but never a titled release (no 'Estimativas da População', no named income survey/product). For population, the gap is partly closed by minting the edge to br-ibge-estimativas-populacao (br-fpm-population.json) directly, on the same reasoning that instrument's own methodology note supplies from the producer's side. For renda domiciliar per capita, there is no equivalent: no primary source located this session gives IBGE's per-capita household income product a title or URL, so no node exists to point to at all -- a harder gap than the population one. Enabling statutes use deliberately generic language throughout: LC 62/1989 Art. 2º § 3º says only "entidade federal competente", and Lei 8.443/1992 Art. 102 (as amended by LC 143/2013) says "entidade competente do Poder Executivo federal" -- neither names IBGE. Only TCU's own implementing DN names the agency, and only by name and reference date, never by titled release.

reports.title: Oslo Manual
reports.description: International standard guidelines for collecting and interpreting data on business innovation activity, jointly published by the OECD and Eurostat as part of the Frascati Family of manuals. OECD's own page states: "The Oslo Manual is the foremost international source of guidelines for the collection and use of data on innovation activities in industry." Brazil's IBGE cites the 3rd edition (2005) by name in the technical notes of its own innovation survey, PINTEC: "A referência conceitual e metodológica da PINTEC é baseada na terceira edição do Manual de Oslo (OSLO..., 2005)."

reports.title: Rose Angina Questionnaire (WHO)
reports.description: A standardized angina-symptom screening instrument, first published by Geoffrey Rose in the WHO's own journal and subsequently recommended by WHO as a general population-survey tool, internationally known as the "WHO/Rose angina questionnaire." Original citation: Rose GA, "The diagnosis of ischaemic heart pain and intermittent claudication in field surveys," Bulletin of the World Health Organization, v.27, n.6, p.645-658, 1962.

reports.title: Global School-based Student Health Survey (GSHS)
reports.description: WHO's collaborative surveillance methodology and standardized questionnaire for measuring youth health behaviours. WHO's own page states: "The Global school-based student health survey (GSHS) is a collaborative surveillance project designed to help countries measure and assess the behavioural risk factors and protective factors in 10 key areas among young people aged 13 to 17 years."

reports.title: World Population Prospects — Methodology
reports.publisher: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division
reports.description: The UN Population Division's methodology for its global population estimates and projections series, "World Population Prospects" (WPP) — covering fertility age-patterns, mortality model life tables, and migration methods used to produce official population estimates and projections for every UN member state. Brazil's IBGE names four distinct WPP/UN Population Division methodological choices directly in its own population-projection report: the WPP2024 fertility age-pattern, the UN(2015) old-age mortality adjustment expanding Wilmoth et al. (2012), the UN(2011) West Model Life Tables, and UN Manual VI (1970) for internal migration.

reports.title: World Programme for the Census of Agriculture (WCA)
reports.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
reports.description: FAO's decadal international programme (running since 1950) establishing recommended concepts, definitions and methodology for national agricultural censuses, so results are internationally comparable. IBGE's own English-language page for its 2017 Census of Agriculture states: "the Institute used premises from the Programa del Censo Agropecuario Mundial 2020 (World Programme for the Census of Agriculture), implemented by the United Nations Organization and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)... The results of the 2017 Census of Agriculture, as of those of previous editions, are in accordance with the recommendations and the basic concepts adopted by FAO."

reports.title: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA)
reports.publisher: United Nations Statistics Division / UN Committee of Experts on Environmental-Economic Accounting
reports.description: UN international statistical standard framework for compiling environmental-economic accounts, comprising the SEEA Central Framework (2012), SEEA Experimental Ecosystem Accounting / SEEA-EEA (2012), its 2021 successor SEEA Ecosystem Accounting (SEEA-EA), and SEEA-Water. IBGE's own methodology page for its environmental-economic accounts states: "A metodologia da contabilidade econômica e ambiental vem sendo estabelecida pelas Nações Unidas por meio do Sistema de Contas Econômicas Ambientais - SCEA (System of Environmental-Economic Accounting - SEEA)," naming SEEA-EEA 2012 and SEEA-Water specifically for its ecosystem and water accounts.

reports.title: Monetary and Financial Statistics Manual and Compilation Guide (2016)
reports.description: The IMF's 2016 manual (successor to the 2000 Monetary and Financial Statistics Manual) setting the international methodological standard for compiling monetary and financial statistics — the monetary base, monetary aggregates, and the monetary-authority survey of assets and liabilities. Brazil's Banco Central do Brasil describes it, in its own words, as "referência metodológica de melhores práticas para a produção de estatísticas monetárias e financeiras" (methodological reference of best practices for producing monetary and financial statistics), citing "o padrão definido no Manual de Estatísticas Monetárias e Financeiras e Guia de Compilação (MEMF), edição 2016, do Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI)" for its "crédito ampliado" statistic.

reports.title: International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th Revision (ICD-10)
reports.description: WHO's international standard diagnostic classification for epidemiology, health management and cause-of-death/morbidity statistics, adopted by the World Health Assembly in 1990 and in effect for member states from 1993 (superseded internationally by ICD-11, effective 2022, though ICD-10 remains in wide concurrent use). China's National Health Commission states in its own China Health Statistical Yearbook: "2000 年采用 ICD-9 国际疾病分类统计标准。2002 年起，采用 ICD-10 国际疾病分类统计标准。" ("In 2000, the ICD-9 international disease-classification statistical standard was adopted; from 2002 onward, the ICD-10 international disease-classification statistical standard has been used.")

_note: One cross-source tension, weaker than Tanzania's three-way conflict but the same shape. The older SSA/ISSA country profile (Social Security Programs Throughout the World: Africa, 2018-2019 vintage, ssa.gov) states for Botswana's universal old-age pension and War Veteran's Allowance: 'Benefits are adjusted periodically based on changes in the cost of living.' No document fetched this session corroborates that claim for the *current* system: the government's own Old Age Pension allowance page (gov.bw) states only the current amount and administering department, with no adjustment mechanism named; the discretionary jump from P830 to P1400 (dailynews.gov.bw, effective 1 April, announced in the Vice President/Finance Minister's budget speech) was framed as accommodated 'through reprioritisation and budget cuts within the existing allocations' -- budget language, not CPI or cost-of-living language; and the government's own 2020 National Social Protection Recovery Plan (bw-national-social-protection-recovery-plan-2020) recommends introducing automatic indexation for the Older Persons Grant precisely because, as a recommendation rather than a description of existing practice, it implies no such mechanism currently exists. Per Research.1.md S3, this is reported as an unresolved conflict rather than adjudicated -- it reads as though the ISSA profile's 'cost of living' claim was either loose paraphrase of ad-hoc discretionary increases (P530 in the 2018-2019 profile itself, since risen to P830 and then P1400) or described an arrangement not documented anywhere else found this session, but that is inference. Neither the 2018-2019 ISSA/SSA profile nor a newer vintage (none was found for Botswana specifically -- see _open_questions) is minted as a corpus node, matching Tanzania's precedent for the same source series.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Botswana's official monthly Consumer Price Index release. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via the June 2026 edition: the base period is held at 'December 2018 = 100.0' across all tables -- the same base year Statistics Botswana's own CPI Technical Report established (see bw-statsbots-cpi-technical-report-2018), which this release does not itself restate ('the primary CPI calculation methodology is not detailed in this publication'). Statistics Botswana's own Prices Statistics webpage separately states 'Consumer Price Index (CPI) is computed using the Modified Laspeyres method which is in line with regional and international recommendations' -- website copy, quoted separately from the Technical Report's own elementary-aggregate formula (geometric mean/Jevons) because the two are different documents making distinct-but-compatible claims about different levels of the same index construction. The June 2026 release also documents Statistics Botswana's core-inflation method: it 'attempts to remove 8 percent (by weight) of the commodity subgroups price changes at each of the ends of an ordered series' (trimmed mean), alongside a separate administered-prices-exclusion measure.

release_schedule.note: Statistics Botswana maintains a published release calendar at statsbots.org.bw/release-calendar listing dated CPI releases (typically 2-3 weeks after the reference month ends), consistent with the on-file releases_per_year=12 (monthly) cadence.

reports.title: National Social Protection Recovery Plan, Part 1: Analysis and Recommendations
reports.publisher: Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development (Botswana), with UNDP, UNICEF, ILO, FAO and UNFPA
reports.description: Botswana's government-published, UNDP-supported social protection review, 30 June 2020. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Section 5.1 of the Executive Summary (p.xi) recommends: 'The value of the combined Older Persons Grant should be re-evaluated and benchmarked against the poverty line or consumption needs, so that the transfer value would be automatically adjusted each year to retain or increase its purchasing power over time.' Framed as a recommendation rather than a description of current practice, this is the document affirmatively implying the absence of an automatic adjustment mechanism for the Old Age Pension (the 'Older Persons Grant') -- the same shape as Tanzania's National Social Protection Policy 2023 (tz-national-social-protection-policy-2023): a government social-protection review whose own proposed fix reveals what does not yet exist, rather than a document simply silent on the question. The document does not name Statistics Botswana or the CPI as an input anywhere; its own recommended benchmark is a poverty line/consumption-needs standard, not an existing CPI series.

reports.title: Botswana Social Protection Programs and Systems Review: Policy Brief
reports.description: World Bank policy brief reviewing Botswana's social protection system. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. On the Old Age Pension: 'The OAP yields the highest contribution to the fight against poverty', covering 5.5% of the population, with no statement anywhere in the brief of how the benefit amount is set or adjusted. On the Ipelegeng public-works programme: 'The value of the Ipelegeng wage rate is 81 to 93 percent of the minimum wage in 2019 (not including the meal)' -- a relative-to-minimum-wage benchmark, not a CPI or price-index link -- and the brief criticises the wage as 'high in comparison with international benchmarks for public works programs' without proposing an indexation formula of any kind. No document located this session ties either programme's amount-setting to Statistics Botswana's CPI.

reports.title: Local Government Act, 2012 (Act No. 18 of 2012, Cap 40:01)
reports.description: Botswana's organic law establishing Councils' revenue base and the Auditor-General's mandate to audit them. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Section 64 (Part X, 'Revenues of Councils, Accounts and Audits') states: 'The revenues of a Council shall consist of - ... (h) the grants as the Government may make to the Council'. Section 68(3) states: '[t]he accounts under subsection (2)... shall be audited by the Auditor General' -- the exact provision the Auditor-General's own reports cite as their mandate to name and audit all Town/City and District Councils (see bw-auditor-general-report-2018-2019 and bw-auditor-general-report-2019-2020). A separate provision (Part V, Rating) states: 'It shall be lawful for the Minister in his or her discretion to make a grant to the revenue of the Council in lieu of an owner's rate, on property vested in Government... not exceeding the amount which would have been payable except for the provisions of subsection 4 (a) and (c)' -- the exact statutory mechanism behind the Auditor-General's finding of a P23,246,480 unpaid grant-in-lieu-of-rates to Gaborone City Council. Hosted on botswanalaws.com, a private Botswana legal-database mirror, not gov.bw directly; treated as adequate per this branch's established sourcing precedent for verbatim government Act text. Supersedes the pre-2012 Local Government (District Councils) Act, Cap 40:01, whose section 44 carried the same revenue-list wording ('such grants as the Government may make to the council') under older section numbering -- the predecessor was not independently minted as a corpus node since current Auditor-General reports cite the 2012 Act's section numbering, not the older instrument's.

reports.title: 2024/2025 Budget Speech
reports.description: Botswana's national budget speech, delivered by Peggy O. Serame, Minister of Finance, 5 February 2024. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Paragraph 99 (p.29): 'Mr. Speaker, Revenue Support Grants to District and Urban Councils constitute the largest portion of the Ministry's projected Recurrent Budget, amounting to five billion, one hundred and ninety million Pula (P5.19 billion) or 55.5 percent of the total budget.' This confirms the operative name and scale of the national-to-council transfer mechanism ('Revenue Support Grant', not the 'District Development Fund' name hypothesized going into this round's search -- that specific name does not appear to be the current Botswana instrument; see _dropped). The speech gives only this single aggregate figure: it does not break the P5.19 billion down by individual named council, and no allocation formula is stated anywhere in the document. Paragraph 98 (p.28-29) adds: 'Nine hundred and twenty-four million Pula (P924 million) of this budget is allocated for Councillors termination benefits, the operational expenses of upgrading Sub-Districts into fully-fledged Districts, and the projected growth in the number of Council Members and Council Wards...', confirming an active sub-district-to-district upgrading process. Hosted on bankofbotswana.bw (a mirror), not the Ministry of Finance's own site, but is unambiguously the Minister of Finance's own budget speech text.

dependencies.basis: Article 1 (اولا) of Iraq's Federal Budget Law No. 13 of 2023, published by the Ministry of Justice, states: "احتساب الإيرادات المخمنة من تصدير النفط الخام على أساس معدل سعر تصدير قدره (٧٠) دولار للبرميل الواحد ومعدل تصدير قدره (٣,٥٠٠,٠٠٠) برميل يومياً" (Estimated crude oil export revenues are calculated on the basis of an assumed export price of $70 per barrel and an export rate of 3,500,000 barrels per day), yielding the law's oil revenue figure of 117,252,500,000 thousand dinars. Oil revenue is a stated arithmetic function of the export volume. THIS REPLACES the secondary analyst PDF that the first pass rejected: the source here is the law itself on moj.gov.iq.

The revenue table in Article 1 of Law No. 13 of 2023 states total budget revenue as the sum of its oil and non-oil components — "اجمالـــي الايـــرادات = ( أ + ب )", where (أ) النفطية [oil revenues] = 117.25 trillion IQD and (ب) [non-oil revenues] = 17.3 trillion IQD — reaching the law's stated total: "تقدر إيرادات الموازنة العامة الاتحادية للسنة المالية (٢٠٢٣) بمبلغ (١٣٤,٥٥٢,٩١٩,٠٦٣) ألف دينار" (Federal budget revenues for FY2023 are estimated at 134,552,919,063 thousand dinars).

COSIT's own preliminary and quarterly GDP report for 2022 states in its introduction: "ونود الإشارة إلى إن تم أستخدام التصنيف الدولي للأنشطة الاقتصادية التنقيح الثاني (ISIC 2) في جداول التقرير" (We note that the International Standard Industrial Classification, Revision 2 (ISIC Rev. 2), was used in the report's tables). WORTH FLAGGING: ISIC Rev. 2 dates from 1968 and was superseded in 1989, 2002 and 2008 — Iraq's national accounts are classified on a vintage six decades old. That is a substantive finding about the corpus, not a transcription error; the report says Revision 2 explicitly.

The ILO's own article on Vietnam's labour statistics states: "The standards were adopted in 2013 by the 19th International Conference of Labour Statisticians, or ICLS19"; "In 2014, with ILO's technical support, Viet Nam became one of the 10 pilot countries that tested them in their Labour Force Surveys"; and "Viet Nam officially adopted the new standards in January this year and applied them in its report of the first quarter." All three sentences were obtained by the orchestrating session re-fetching the page — the researching agent had reported only the middle one and had explicitly hedged that ICLS was not named in its quote, which turned out to be an artefact of what its fetch returned rather than of the page.

MODELLING QUESTION FOR THOMAS, not a research failure. SCI's national-accounts page does state "Classification of individual consumption by purpose (COICOP), for classification of household final consumption expenditures" — verified verbatim by the orchestrating session. But it names COICOP with no revision, and the corpus has only revision-specific nodes: `un-coicop-2018` and `un-coicop-hbs-1999`. Wiring a source that says 'COICOP' to the 2018 edition asserts an edition the document does not assert, and Iran's accounts are on the SNA 1993 vintage, which makes a pre-2018 COICOP the more likely referent. Not minted. The fix is a decision, not more research: either mint a revision-neutral `un-coicop` parent node that the revisions hang off, or accept that generic-COICOP citations cannot be wired at all.

CONTRADICTION FLAGGED, NOT RESOLVED — this needs Thomas's ruling, and it is the reason Iran contributed one edge to this round instead of seven. _meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED into src/data/index.ts. Round 5 of Thomas's 'go for 10 rounds' request, 2026-08-12. DR Congo — entirely new to the AF branch until now (flagged 'no-document' in af-synthesis.json's _dropped list, item 3). A strong constitutional decentralization story (26 provinces since a 2015 redivision, a documented 40%-retention rule) but the actual fiscal-transfer paper trail linking federal and provincial documents to each other was not found this round — an honest partial result, not a completed thread.

reports.title: Constitution de la République Démocratique du Congo, 2005 (rev. 2011) — Articles 2 et 175
reports.description: Article 2, verbatim: "The Democratic Republic of the Congo consists of the city of Kinshasa and 25 provinces which possess legal personality" (26 territorial divisions total, naming all 25 provinces individually). Article 175, verbatim: "The percentage of national revenues allocated to the provinces is fixed at 40%. It is retained at the source (retenue à la source)." This is DRC's version of the same federal-to-province fiscal-transfer question already documented for Ethiopia (Proclamation 1250/2021) and Kenya (CRA formula, Equalisation Fund) this round — a constitutionally fixed percentage rather than a discretionary formula, and unusually explicit that the money is retained at the province of origin rather than routed through the capital first.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument (a constitution).

reports.title: Note de Conjoncture (Institut National de la Statistique, RDC)
reports.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique (INS), République Démocratique du Congo
reports.description: AGENCY-attributed via press citation, not a directly located primary PDF: opinion-info.cd, reporting DRC's July 2026 inflation, states verbatim: "Selon la note de conjoncture de l'Institut national de la statistique (INS), le taux d'inflation s'est établi à 0,195%, contre 0,186% enregistré la semaine précédente" — implying a weekly cadence. INS's own site (insrdc.cd) is confirmed live but explicitly under construction ("Prochainement: Catalogue de données, Calendrier de diffusion..."), so a direct primary link was not available this round despite the agency and publication name both being real and specifically named. Closes the 'DR Congo CPI -> no node minted' gap flagged in af-synthesis.json's _dropped list, though not as cleanly as a directly-fetched bulletin would.
reports.cadence_note: Implied weekly, per the press citation's own week-over-week comparison; not independently confirmed against a primary masthead.

reports.title: Édit budgétaire du Gouvernement provincial de Kinshasa, exercice 2026
reports.description: Adopted by the provincial assembly late December 2025. Verbatim total: "3 223 milliards 567 millions 945 mille 514 francs congolais, soit près de 1,111 milliard de dollars américains" (~US$1.111 billion). Press coverage (DeskEco) describes the budget as resting on "une approche pragmatique et réaliste, fondée... sur les capacités réelles de mobilisation des ressources provinciales" (provincial resource-mobilization capacity) rather than citing the constitutional 40% retrocession rule directly — checked specifically and confirmed absent from this source.
reports.cadence_note: Annual provincial budget edict.

reports.title: Cadre Budgétaire à Moyen Terme 2024–2026
reports.publisher: Ministère du Budget, République Démocratique du Congo
reports.description: Published September 2023. Contains a consolidated "Provinces ETD Consolidé" (Provinces + Entités Territoriales Décentralisées) budget line aggregating transfers to all provinces and decentralized entities together, without itemizing by individual province — so it cannot itself be used to link to Kinshasa's own budget edict. Does not cite Article 175 or the 40% figure directly, checked specifically and confirmed absent. DRC's own national medium-term fiscal framework, structurally the same genre already minted for Nigeria (MTEF) and Kenya (CFSP), but with materially less transparency about the province-by-province breakdown.
reports.cadence_note: Rolling medium-term framework (this is the 2024-2026 edition; a 2025 Loi de Finances also exists at the same publisher).

_dropped.why: The CBMT's own "Provinces ETD Consolidé" budget line is exactly the kind of figure Article 175's 40% rule would produce, but the document was checked directly for an Article 175 or '40%' citation and neither was found — the two are almost certainly related in substance but not documented as connected in this specific text. Flagged for a import follow-up: dense French-language government budget PDFs like this are exactly where this session's fetch tooling has underperformed before.

Kinshasa's own 2026 budget edict, per the press coverage checked, frames its revenue base as provincial resource-mobilization capacity rather than citing the constitutional retrocession mechanism or the national medium-term framework by name. The primary édit budgétaire text itself (as opposed to press coverage of it) was not located this round — worth a direct search for the provincial assembly's own published text.

reports.title: Loi de Finances pour l'année 2026 (Loi n°42-2025 du 31 décembre 2025)
reports.publisher: Ministère des Finances, du Budget et du Portefeuille Public (République du Congo)
reports.description: Congo-Brazzaville's FY2026 national budget law, published in the Journal Officiel N°3-2026 (5 janvier 2026). Chapitre 6 "Dotations aux collectivités locales", Article cinquante-quatrième: "Au titre de l'année 2026, les collectivités locales bénéficient des dotations de l'Etat, conformément aux dispositions de l'article 22 de la loi n° 30-2003 du 20 octobre 2003 portant institution du régime financier des collectivités locales" — a direct citation of the 2003 decentralization-finance law as legal basis for departmental dotations (full text of Loi n°30-2003 itself could not be located online this round; see _dropped). Article 23 (redevance de crédits carbone / carbon-credit royalty, Section 9 "Recouvrement et répartition du produit de la redevance"): "Le produit de la redevance de crédits carbone est réparti comme suit : • 70 % au trésor public ; • 30 % aux collectivités locales du lieu de l'implantation des projets. La part destinée aux collectivités locales est exclusivement destinée à la réalisation des projets sociaux de la collectivité" — generic reference to "collectivités locales du lieu de l'implantation", no individual department named. Article trente-neuvième nouveau (judicial-document fee split): "Le produit issu de la vente des bulletins du casier judiciaire et du certificat de nationalité est affecté ainsi qu'il suit : - 50% au budget des collectivités locales ; - 50% à l'administration centrale." Ministry budget table, "Code 23 Intérieur et décentralisation": total 181 546 346 898 FCFA, of which a dedicated "029 Décentralisation" program line of 50 726 550 428 FCFA — confirms a national decentralization budget program exists but breaks down no further by individual department.
reports.cadence_note: Annual budget law (loi de finances), one per fiscal year.

reports.publisher: Ministère des Finances, du Budget et du Portefeuille Public (République du Congo)
reports.description: Congo-Brazzaville's FY2020 budget document, downloaded from the Ministry of Finance's own site. The cover is labeled "PROJET DE LOI DE FINANCES POUR L'ANNEE 2020" with the law-number/date fields blank ("Loi n° __________ du_________________"), so this may be an unsigned draft copy rather than the enacted text — flagged, not resolved. Annexe budgets annexes/comptes spéciaux, "12- Fonds de développement des collectivités locales": "Le Fonds de développement des départements est alimenté par : - 50% de la taxe de superficie perçue par l'administration de l'économie forestière (Cf. loi n° 16-2000 du 20 novembre 2000) ; - le produit de la taxe superficiaire perçue par l'administration des hydrocarbures (Cf. loi n° 28-2016 du 13 octobre 2016) ; - les frais de délivrance des autorisations de transports routiers ou d'activités connexes au transport automobile (Cf. loi n° 18-89 du 31 octobre 1989)." Ministry-by-ministry budget table, "Code 34 Intérieur et décentralisation": "Titre 4 : Transferts …….. 25 103 678 980 FCFA / dont collectivités locales 20 080 000 000 FCFA". Titre VII "Des modalités des concours financiers de l'Etat aux collectivités locales", Article trente-septième: "Conformément aux dispositions de l'article 22 de la loi n° 30-2003 du 20 octobre 2003 portant institution du régime financier des collectivités locales, des dotations sont accordées à celles-ci pour leur fonctionnement. Au titre de l'année 2020, il n'est accordé, au profit des collectivités locales, aucun concours financier par l'Etat." — documents that the legal basis for state dotations to collectivités locales existed but was explicitly not exercised in FY2020, despite the same-year ministry table showing a 20.08bn FCFA "collectivités locales" transfer line under a different budget code (Intérieur et décentralisation), an apparent internal tension in the source document that is reported as found rather than reconciled.

reports.title: Arrêté n°15948 du 10 septembre 2019 portant organisation et fonctionnement du fonds de développement local de la série de développement communautaire de l'Unité Forestière d'Exploitation Ngongo-Nzambi
reports.publisher: Ministère de l'intérieur et de la décentralisation / Ministère de l'économie forestière (République du Congo)
reports.description: Joint arrêté signed by the Minister of the Interior and Decentralization (Raymond Zéphirin Mbouloou) and the Minister of Forestry Economy (Rosalie Matondo), published in the Journal Officiel de la République du Congo N°38-2019 (pp. 1036-1037). This is a national-government instrument about a specific department, not a document published by/for the Niari department as its own governing body, so it is classed federal rather than provincial. Article 2: "Le fonds de développement local est alimenté par : - la redevance de 200 FCFA par m3 sur le volume commercialisable exploité annuellement par la société Asia Congo Industries dans l'assiette annuelle de coupe (AAC) de l'unité forestière d'exploitation Ngongo-Nzambi ; - les subventions du conseil départemental de Niari, selon un pourcentage de son budget annuel. Ce pourcentage est fixé par délibération du conseil départemental de Niari ; - les dons et legs de différentes natures." This is a sectoral forestry-fund instrument (not itself an economic/statistical report) but is solid primary evidence that Niari department has a legally defined, budget-percentage-linked subvention relationship with a local fund. Hosted as a verbatim scan on FAOLEX (FAO's legal database); could not be independently confirmed as mirrored on Congo's own sgg.cg archive, so government authorship is clear (signed ministers, JO citation, cross-checked against the local pdftotext extraction) but the hosting location is secondary/mirrored.
reports.cadence_note: One-off sectoral arrêté, not a recurring series.
