reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) / Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index measuring changes in the prices of a representative basket of goods and services. National coverage with city-level detail for major urban centres.
reports._notes: Flagship price statistic. July 2026: monthly variation 0.17%, year-to-date 4.94%, annual 6.03%. Direct input into monetary-policy analysis by the Banco de la República and into the updating of poverty lines.

reports.title: Gran Encuesta Integrada de Hogares (GEIH) / Great Integrated Household Survey
reports.description: Continuous household survey that is the primary source for labour-market indicators (employment, unemployment, informality, underemployment) and for the income data used in monetary-poverty measurement. National, urban-rural, regional and capital-city domains.
reports._notes: Central social and labour survey. Moving-quarter and monthly releases. Official source for both labour statistics and the income side of monetary poverty and inequality (Gini). Microdata regularly disseminated.

reports.title: Pobreza monetaria y pobreza monetaria extrema / Monetary poverty
reports.publisher: DANE + Comité de Expertos en Pobreza
reports.description: Official income-poverty and extreme-poverty incidence, calculated by comparing household per-capita income (from GEIH, augmented with administrative transfers) with nationally defined poverty lines. Annual publication with urban/rural and city breakdowns.
reports._notes: Headline social indicator. 2025 results published June 2026 with joint DANE–Expert Committee statement. Poverty lines updated with IPC; income concept includes labour, transfers and other sources. Series have undergone methodological empalmes after GEIH frame changes.

reports.title: Líneas de pobreza monetaria y pobreza extrema
reports.description: Monetary values of the poverty and extreme-poverty lines (per capita and for reference households), updated with the IPC and differentiated by geographic domain.
reports._notes: Direct input into the poverty measurement. 2025 national per-capita extreme-poverty line ~$236,580; poverty line ~$482,041 (monthly). Domain-specific lines published for cabeceras and centros poblados/rural disperso.

reports.title: Cuentas Nacionales / National Accounts of Colombia
reports.description: Full system of national accounts producing GDP by production, expenditure and income, supply-and-use tables and institutional sector accounts. Quarterly and annual releases.
reports._notes: Core macroeconomic statistical system. DANE is the primary compiler (unlike Chile where the central bank leads). Quarterly GDP and annual institutional accounts are the headline products.

reports.title: Censo Nacional de Población y Vivienda / National Population and Housing Census
reports.description: Decennial population and housing census. Provides the demographic baseline, sampling frames for household surveys, and small-area population estimates.
reports._notes: Foundational demographic product. Continuously cited by GEIH design, poverty analysis and departmental statistical work. Latest major census cycle and subsequent projections are the current reference.

reports.title: Índice de Producción Industrial (IPI) / Industrial Production Index
reports.description: Monthly volume index of industrial production (manufacturing, mining, electricity). Principal short-term activity indicator for the industrial sector.
reports._notes: Core short-term industrial indicator. Complements the broader activity measures and feeds into quarterly national accounts.

reports.title: Coeficiente de Gini / Income inequality
reports.description: Official Gini coefficient of income inequality, calculated from the same GEIH income concept used for monetary poverty. Published annually with the poverty results.
reports._notes: Companion inequality indicator to the poverty series. Released jointly with monetary poverty and extreme poverty under the Expert Committee process.

reports.title: Índice de Producción Industrial (IPI) — sector detail
reports.description: Monthly volume index of industrial production covering manufacturing, mining & quarrying, electricity & gas, and water. Published with sector contributions and year-to-date rates.
reports._notes: Core short-term industrial indicator. February 2026: 0.0% year-on-year overall; manufacturing +1.4%, electricity & gas +1.8%, water +2.2%. Built from EMMET and administrative registers.

reports.title: Encuesta Mensual Manufacturera con Enfoque Territorial (EMMET)
reports.description: Monthly sample survey of manufacturing establishments measuring production, sales, employment, wages and hours. Source for the manufacturing component of the IPI and for territorial industrial indicators.
reports._notes: Primary high-frequency manufacturing survey. Covers 39 CIIU domains and selected departments/metropolitan areas. Direct input into monthly IPI and quarterly national accounts.

reports.title: Encuesta Anual Manufacturera (EAM)
reports.description: Annual structural survey of manufacturing establishments providing production, intermediate consumption, value added, employment and energy use. Structural counterpart to the monthly EMMET.
reports._notes: Structural manufacturing baseline. 2024 provisional: ~6,583 establishments, production ~COP 444 trillion, value added ~COP 148 trillion. Used for national-accounts benchmarking and industrial structure analysis.

reports.title: Balanza de Pagos y Posición de Inversión Internacional
reports.description: Quarterly balance of payments and international investment position. Covers current account, capital/financial account, and the stock of external assets and liabilities.
reports._notes: Core external-accounts product. Q4 2025: current-account deficit USD 3.9 bn (3.1% of quarterly GDP). Full-year 2025 deficit ~USD 10.9 bn (2.4% of GDP). Net IIP negative ~USD 200 bn.

reports.title: Estadísticas de Comercio Exterior / Merchandise Trade
reports.description: Monthly and annual statistics of exports and imports of goods, by product, partner and customs regime. Primary real-side input into the goods account of the balance of payments.
reports._notes: Trade data feed both the BOP and the national accounts. Mining-energy exports remain a large share; recent years have seen widening goods deficits driven by stronger import growth.

reports.title: Informe de Política Monetaria (Banrep)
reports.description: Periodic Monetary Policy Report of the central bank. Explains the inflation outlook, the policy framework and the implications for the intervention interest rate.
reports._notes: Flagship policy communication product. Complements the post-meeting statements and minutes of the Junta Directiva. Central reference for the 3% inflation target and the path of the policy rate.

reports.title: Tasa de interés de intervención / Policy interest rate
reports.description: Main monetary-policy instrument of the Junta Directiva. The rate at which the central bank intervenes in the money market to manage liquidity and steer inflation toward the 3% target.
reports._notes: Operational policy rate. Recent levels in the low-to-mid teens after the post-2022 tightening cycle; path is the primary signal of the monetary stance.

reports.title: Reservas Internacionales del Banco de la República
reports.description: Stock of international reserves managed by the central bank under constitutional and legal mandate. Published at high frequency and analysed in the BOP and Board reports to Congress.
reports._notes: Key external-buffer indicator. End-2025 net reserves ~USD 66.4 bn (up ~USD 3.9 bn year-on-year). Adequacy metrics (IMF-style) regularly reported.

reports.title: Marco de metas de inflación (3%) — Banco de la República
reports.description: Operational monetary-policy framework: inflation targeting centred on 3% annual CPI inflation. Derived from the constitutional and legal mandate of the central bank.
reports._notes: Core policy-framework node. Continuously cited as the reference against which inflation outcomes and policy actions are evaluated.
_referenced_by: Every IPoM and monetary-policy decision statement
IPC and inflation analysis that refers to the target

reports.title: Informe de la Junta Directiva al Congreso de la República
reports.description: Statutory twice-yearly report of the central-bank Board to Congress covering economic conditions, policy decisions, reserves, the Bank’s financial situation and outlook.
reports._notes: Accountability product required by law. March and July editions are the main formal channel from the Junta Directiva to the legislature.

reports.title: Bogotá D.C. — capital statistical identity
reports.description: Capital district and largest urban economy. Primary domain for GEIH labour and poverty cuts, with lower informal employment and lower monetary-poverty incidence than the national average.
reports._notes: Dominant metro node. Recent GEIH: unemployment ~8.8% (below national); informal employment among the lowest of the 23 cities (~33%). Monetary poverty incidence also lower than the national urban average. Continuously published as a distinct geographic domain.

reports.title: 13 ciudades y áreas metropolitanas — statistical domain
reports.description: Standard high-frequency geographic domain of the GEIH comprising Bogotá and the main metropolitan areas (Medellín, Cali, Barranquilla, etc.). Core urban labour and poverty reporting frame.
reports._notes: Workhorse urban domain. Informal employment and unemployment rates for the 13 cities are the main urban benchmarks published monthly/quarterly alongside the national total.

reports.title: Medellín Área Metropolitana — statistical profile
reports.description: Second-largest metropolitan area. Regularly published as a distinct GEIH and poverty domain with intermediate informal-employment and poverty outcomes.
reports._notes: Key secondary metro. Completes the capital–second-city contrast inside the national urban hierarchy.

reports.title: Producción y exportaciones de petróleo / Mining-energy exports
reports.publisher: DANE / Ministerio de Minas y Energía / Banrep
reports.description: Statistics of crude-oil and broader mining-energy production and exports. Structurally important component of merchandise exports and of the external accounts.
reports._notes: Commodity backbone of the export basket. Mining-energy share of total exports remains large; recent years have seen volume and price swings that dominate the goods-trade balance.

reports.title: Café — producción y exportaciones
reports.publisher: DANE / Federación Nacional de Cafeteros / MinCIT
reports.description: Statistics of coffee production and exports. Iconic non-mining agricultural export and a recurring line in trade and rural-economy analysis.
reports._notes: Signature soft-commodity export. Appears in both the agricultural and the non-mining-energy export aggregates and is continuously cited in rural and trade-policy discussion.

reports.title: Encuesta Nacional de Calidad de Vida (ECV)
reports.description: Periodic multi-purpose household survey measuring living conditions, housing, education, health affiliation, subjective well-being and access to services. Complements GEIH on non-labour dimensions of welfare.
reports._notes: Key living-conditions survey. 2024 results cover health-service perception, education, housing deficit and subjective poverty. Published for national, Bogotá and departmental domains.

reports.title: Pruebas Saber / ICFES learning assessments
reports.description: National standardised assessments of student learning outcomes (Saber 11 and related). Principal learning-quality indicator for the school system.
reports._notes: Flagship education-quality statistic. Complements enrolment and attainment data from ECV and administrative sources. Continuously cited in education-policy evaluation.

reports.title: Departamento del Chocó — highest-poverty contrast
reports.description: Pacific department with the highest monetary-poverty incidence in the 2025 departmental results. Tests the statistical hierarchy under extreme marginalisation.
reports._notes: Poverty-contrast department. 2025 monetary poverty 65.3% (highest of the 23 reported departments); extreme poverty also the highest. National survey infrastructure reaches the department; independent local statistical density is thin.

reports.title: Departamento de La Guajira — high-poverty Caribbean contrast
reports.description: Northern Caribbean department with the second-highest monetary-poverty incidence. Completes the periphery contrast alongside Chocó.
reports._notes: 2025 monetary poverty 60.2%. Extreme poverty also elevated. Illustrates the Caribbean–Pacific poverty belt under a common national measurement framework.

reports.title: Departamento de Sucre — secondary high-poverty node
reports.description: Caribbean department ranking third in monetary poverty in the 2025 results.
reports._notes: 2025 monetary poverty 51.8%. Reinforces the Caribbean high-poverty cluster.

reports.title: Departamento de Cundinamarca — low-poverty contrast
reports.description: Andean department surrounding Bogotá with the lowest departmental monetary-poverty incidence in 2025.
reports._notes: 2025 monetary poverty 15.1% — lowest of the reported departments. Completes the capital-region low-poverty pole opposite Chocó/La Guajira.

reports.title: Departamento de Antioquia — core statistical identity
reports.description: Major Andean department centred on Medellín. Intermediate-to-low monetary poverty and a relatively dense urban statistical presence via the Medellín AM domain.
reports._notes: 2025 monetary poverty 19.2%. Hosts the second-largest metro and a significant share of manufacturing and services activity.

reports.title: Pobreza monetaria por departamento (DANE)
reports.description: Official departmental tabulations of monetary poverty and extreme poverty. Primary source for the inter-departmental poverty gradient.
reports._notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2025 ranking (selected): Chocó 65.3%, La Guajira 60.2%, Sucre 51.8%, … Antioquia 19.2%, Bogotá 17.8%, Cundinamarca 15.1%. National average 28.0%.

reports.title: DIAN — recaudo tributario y aduanero
reports.publisher: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
reports.description: Tax and customs administration. Publishes gross and net tax collection by type of tax (income withholding, VAT, customs, etc.) and performance against annual targets.
reports._notes: Primary revenue-side fiscal statistic. 2025 gross collection ~COP 296 trillion (96.9% of target). Links the real-side economy to the central-government budget.

reports.title: Sistema General de Regalías / Royalties from hydrocarbons and mining
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Hacienda / DNP / Agencia Nacional de Hidrocarburos
reports.description: Royalties generated by hydrocarbon and mineral extraction and their distribution to producing and non-producing territorial entities. Major sub-national fiscal transfer mechanism.
reports._notes: Critical sub-national fiscal node. 2025 hydrocarbon royalties caused ~COP 8.5 trillion. Concentrated in Meta, Casanare, Santander, Arauca and Huila. Directly links the oil/mining production statistics to territorial budgets.

reports.title: Presupuesto General de la Nación / National Budget
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Hacienda y Crédito Público
reports.description: Annual national budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues and expenditure of the central government.
reports._notes: Operational fiscal framework. Links tax collection (DIAN), royalties and other revenues with functional spending on education, health, social protection and investment.

reports.title: Departamento del Valle del Cauca — core statistical identity
reports.description: Major Pacific-Andean department centred on Cali. Intermediate monetary poverty and a significant metropolitan domain (Cali AM).
reports._notes: 2025 monetary poverty 21.8%. Completes the set of large departmental economies alongside Antioquia, Cundinamarca/Bogotá and the Caribbean departments.

The EAM methodology, by contrast, never mentions the EMMET.

_slice: County of Grande Prairie No. 1 — the template tested
_note: The second municipality, researched to find out whether the Grande Prairie template replicates. It does: the same six documents exist, published under the same statute, naming their inputs in the same places. A rural municipality adds two things a city does not have in quantity — regulated property assessment (farmland, machinery and equipment, linear) valued under provincial Minister's Guidelines rather than by the local assessor, and a seniors housing requisition large enough to appear as its own line. Both are additions to the pattern, not departures from it. The template holds.

reports.title: Property Tax Bylaw (Rates of Taxation)
reports.description: Annual bylaw setting tax rates for each property class in the county, passed under the Municipal Government Act. States the total to be raised by taxation, the assessment behind each class including farmland, machinery and equipment and linear property, and every requisition collected for another body — with prior-year under-levies carried forward and corrected.

entries.covers: 2025 Property Tax Bylaw (Bylaw #3250) third and final reading
2026 Property Tax Bylaw third and final reading

release_schedule.note: County of Grande Prairie No. 1 council passes its annual Property Tax Bylaw (Rates of Taxation) in April each year after finalizing its budget and receiving provincial education/Grande Spirit Foundation requisition figures. No fixed statutory day is published (Alberta's Municipal Government Act does not set a specific date), and no public release calendar exists, but the two most recent confirmed adoption dates (April 17, 2025 and April 24, 2026) show a consistent mid-to-late April pattern. The 2026 bylaw has already been passed as of the 2026-08-11 reference date, so the next expected occurrence is April 2027.

reports.title: County Budget
reports.description: Annual operating and capital budget adopted at a dedicated budget council meeting, setting the net funding requirement that the tax rate bylaw then raises. The 2025 budget set that requirement at $154,133,907.

release_schedule.rule: "The County approves an interim budget in the fall annually for the following year." "The finalized budget and municipal tax rates are approved once the Province sets the final property tax levy for education requisitions, and when property assessment values have been confirmed through final budget deliberation meetings in April."
release_schedule.note: The County actually publishes budget documents twice per year, not once: an interim budget adopted in fall/December (2025 interim approved 2024-12-13; 2026 interim approved 2025-12-13) and a finalized budget adopted in April once provincial education tax levies and assessments are confirmed (2025 final approved 2025-04-17; 2026 final approved 2026-04-25). Dates for the December interim entry are estimated (implied) from the consistent Dec 13 precedent in the two most recent years; exact 2026 dates were not on a published calendar.

reports.title: Property Assessment Roll
reports.description: Annual valuation of every assessable property in the county, notices mailed by the end of May. Unlike a city roll, most of its value sits in classes the local assessor does not value at market: $2.27 billion of machinery and equipment, $2.46 billion of linear property, and $122 million of farmland, all valued under provincial Minister's Guidelines.

release_schedule.rule: Property Assessment Notices are mailed to County of Grande Prairie No. 1 property owners by the end of May of each year.
release_schedule.note: The 2026 assessment roll/notices were already mailed by end of May 2026 (confirmed by a June 2026 County news post: 'Property Tax Notices Mailed; Payment Deadline June 30, 2026', https://www.countygp.ab.ca/news/posts/property-tax-notices-mailed-payment-deadline-june-30-2026/). Since today (2026-08-11) is past that, the next occurrence is projected to end of May 2027. The complaint deadline for the 2026 roll was July 14, 2026 (per https://www.countygp.ab.ca/home-property-environment/property-assessments/appealing-an-assessment/), consistent with a ~60-day window after a May mailing.

reports.title: Consolidated Audited Financial Statements
reports.description: Annual audited statements required by the Municipal Government Act and returned to Municipal Affairs by May 1. Schedule 3 separates real property taxes from linear property taxes and nets out each requisition collected for an external body.

entries.covers: County of Grande Prairie No. 1 consolidated audited financial statements for fiscal year ended December 31, 2026

release_schedule.rule: Under the Municipal Government Act, each municipality (and each regional services commission) must prepare annual audited financial statements and a financial information return, both of which must be returned to Alberta Municipal Affairs by May 1 of each year.
release_schedule.note: The County's FY2025 (year ended Dec 31, 2025) consolidated audited financial statements were approved by Council/Management on April 24, 2026 and the independent auditor's report (RSM Canada LLP) is dated April 28, 2026, consistent with the province-wide May 1 statutory deadline. The next report (for FY2026) would follow the same annual cycle, due by May 1, 2027. The county's own financial documents page (given url) does not itself list a calendar but confirms statements are prepared annually on a calendar-year basis.

reports.title: Municipal Census
reports.description: Municipal population count conducted at the county's discretion under the Municipal Government Act, most recently in 2024, and reported to Municipal Affairs for the population list.
reports.cadence_note: Irregular and discretionary, like the city's. Two adjacent municipalities both happened to count in 2024, which is coincidence rather than a cycle.

release_schedule.note: County of Grande Prairie municipal censuses were conducted in 2006, 2012, and 2024 (6-year then 12-year gaps). The County's own FAQ explicitly states there is no fixed schedule: 'The County conducts municipal censuses based on population changes, community needs, and Council's direction. Any future censuses will be determined by these factors.' No next date or interval is announced as of 2026-08-11.

reports.title: Grande Spirit Foundation Seniors Housing Requisition
reports.description: Annual requisition levied on member municipalities in the Grande Prairie region to fund seniors housing, collected through their property tax bylaws. A housing management body under the Alberta Housing Act — neither a government nor a department, but able to requisition tax from one.

release_schedule.note: Grande Spirit Foundation (a regional Alberta 'management body' under the Alberta Housing Act) requisitions operating funds annually from its member municipalities (City/County of Grande Prairie and several surrounding towns/counties/MDs). The Housing Act provision found only specifies that a municipality must pay its agreed contribution within 90 days of the Foundation mailing the invoice -- it does not fix a date by which the Foundation must issue the requisition. Board meeting minutes show requisition percentage increases being approved at a mid-year (June 2024) meeting for the following fiscal year's budget, but no calendar, fixed statutory date, or consistent multi-year pattern for the requisition's own issuance could be confirmed -- the Foundation's public board-minutes archive (2023-2025) contains no dedicated 'requisition schedule' document, and the Alberta Housing Act / Housing Regulation full text could not be retrieved (qp.alberta.ca, kings-printer.alberta.ca, canlii.org, and open.alberta.ca all blocked or errored on fetch). Member-municipality budget documents (e.g. County of Grande Prairie) show the requisition amount folded into municipal interim/final budgets each Nov-Dec, but that reflects the municipality's own budget cycle, not a documented Foundation release date.

reports.title: Regulated Property Assessment Minister's Guidelines
reports.description: The Minister's Guidelines that set assessed values for regulated property — farmland, machinery and equipment, linear property and railway. These classes are not valued at market by the local assessor; the province prescribes the procedure and the rates, and the municipality applies them. Issued as ministerial orders and updated for each assessment year.
reports.cadence_note: Published as a set of four guidelines per assessment year. Modelled as one node because Alberta publishes and revises them together as 'regulated property minister's guidelines'; splitting them would add three nodes with identical edges.

release_schedule.note: "Regulated Property Assessment Minister's Guidelines" is the alberta.ca landing-page category covering four separate annual Ministerial Order documents: Linear Property, Railway Property, Machinery & Equipment, and Farm Land Assessment Minister's Guidelines. Each is republished annually via Ministerial Order (e.g. MAG:016/23, MAG:017/24) and the Open Government publication pages show a clear multi-year December pattern: 2025 editions of the Linear, Machinery & Equipment, and Farm Land guidelines were posted/updated December 12, 2025, and the Railway guideline December 17, 2025; prior editions (2015-2024) follow the same annual cadence. No statute/regulation text was found specifying an exact statutory deadline (the Matters Relating to Assessment and Taxation Regulation, 2018 just requires assessors to follow whichever guidelines are in effect), so this is classified as an observed pattern rather than a stated rule. The next edition (2026 guidelines) is expected mid-December 2026 based on this pattern; the exact day is not yet published as of 2026-08-11.

_slice: Canadian credit, mortgage and lending infrastructure
_note: This slice covers the plumbing that sits between the Bank of Canada's policy rate and what a Canadian household or small lender actually pays: the CORRA benchmark family, the mortgage stress test, government-backed mortgage insurance, and deposit insurance pricing. Its shape is unusual. The benchmark side (CORRA, Term CORRA) is exceptionally well documented because IOSCO benchmark principles force administrators to publish methodology, so those edges are precise and mechanical. The mortgage side is documented in bursts: the rules are public, but the ONLY places that state what feeds what are the transition documents written when a rule changed - the Department of Finance's February 2020 backgrounder replacing the Bank of Canada 5-Year Benchmark Posted Mortgage Rate, and OSFI's 2020-21 letters replacing the same rate with a fixed 5.25 percent floor. Both of those edges are historical: Canada has spent the last five years deliberately cutting the mortgage stress test loose from any published market rate, so the current stress test for uninsured mortgages depends on nothing at all - it is a number OSFI announces. The provincial credit union chain is the darkest corner: Alberta's Credit Union Deposit Guarantee Corporation publishes a full Standards of Sound Business and Financial Practices that never once names Basel, OSFI, or a federal guideline, so it could not be attached to the graph on evidence and was dropped. The two documents that actually bind bank prudential regulation to the macroeconomic graph turned out to be CMHC's Residential Mortgage Industry Report (which footnotes the national accounts and defines the stress test by reference to OSFI B-20) and CDIC's Differential Premiums Manual (which reads its capital inputs out of OSFI's BCAR return).

reports.title: Canadian Overnight Repo Rate Average (CORRA)
reports.description: CORRA is Canada's designated risk-free reference rate, measuring the cost of overnight general collateral funding in Canadian dollars using Government of Canada treasury bills and bonds as repo collateral. The Bank of Canada has calculated and published it since June 15, 2020, as a daily trimmed volume-weighted median of eligible overnight repo transactions reported to CIRO through the Market Trade Reporting System. It became Canada's principal interest rate benchmark after CDOR ceased publication in June 2024.
reports.cadence_note: Published each Canadian business day by 10:00 ET, postponable to 11:00 ET.

entries.covers: CORRA value for August 10, 2026 (previous business day), published on the next business day, August 11, 2026

release_schedule.rule: Published every business day between 9:00 and 11:00 ET.
release_schedule.note: CORRA is a daily benchmark rate published every business day (excluding weekends and statutory holidays), not a periodic report with a fixed number of yearly editions in the usual sense. The releases_per_year value of 250 is roughly consistent with the number of Canadian business days in a year (about 252 minus a few statutory holidays), so it appears reasonable and was not corrected.

reports.title: Term CORRA
reports.publisher: CanDeal Benchmark Administration Services (distributed by TMX Datalinx)
reports.description: Term CORRA is Canada's forward-looking term reference rate for 1- and 3-month tenors, created on CARR's recommendation to give the loan and trade finance market a CDOR replacement. It is calculated by CanDeal Benchmark Administration Services from transactions and executable bids and offers in the central limit order book of One-Month (COA) and Three-Month (CRA) CORRA Futures on the Montreal Exchange, and published at 13:00 ET each business day. Its approved use cases are deliberately narrow: loans, trade finance, and single-currency derivatives hedging Term CORRA loans.
reports.cadence_note: Published same-day (T+0) at 13:00 ET each Canadian business day.

release_schedule.rule: Term CORRA is published same-day (T+0) at 1:00 PM ET on each Canadian business day, calculated using transactions, executable bids and offers in the central limit order book (CLOB) of CORRA Futures contracts traded on the Montréal Exchange.
release_schedule.note: Published every Canadian business day (not weekends/holidays) at 13:00 ET; no dated publication calendar is posted since it recurs daily. Next entry given is the next Canadian business day after 2026-08-11.

reports.title: Residential Mortgage Underwriting Practices and Procedures – Guideline B-20
reports.publisher: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
reports.description: Guideline B-20 sets OSFI's expectations for prudent residential mortgage underwriting by all federally regulated financial institutions engaged in residential mortgage underwriting or the acquisition of residential mortgage loan assets in Canada. It is organised around five principles covering governance, borrower due diligence, collateral valuation, loan-to-value ratio management, and credit and counterparty risk management including mortgage insurance. It is the instrument through which the minimum qualifying rate (mortgage stress test) for uninsured mortgages is imposed.
reports.cadence_note: The guideline itself is revised only occasionally (2012, 2017, 2018, 2021, 2023); OSFI commits to reviewing the qualifying rate calibration at least annually.

release_schedule.note: Guideline B-20 is a supervisory guideline, not a periodic statistical release. It was originally published October 17, 2017 (effective January 1, 2018) and substantively revised once since, effective March 30, 2023, following a public consultation. OSFI's own consultation-response page states it will 'continue reviewing our expectations relating to real estate secured lending through 2023 to 2024' and will sequence/prioritize any further debt-serviceability changes, but gives no fixed timetable or next-update date. The guideline itself contains no revision-cycle commitment (the only periodic-review language found is OSFI's separate commitment to review the mortgage qualifying-rate calibration 'at least annually,' which is a distinct, narrower item, not a schedule for republishing the guideline as a whole). No calendar, no stated fixed-interval rule, and only two editions in ~9 years (an irregular gap), so this does not support published-calendar, stated-rule, or observed-pattern classification.

reports.title: Minimum Qualifying Rate for Uninsured Mortgages
reports.publisher: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
reports.description: The MQR is the mortgage stress test rate OSFI requires federally regulated lenders to apply to uninsured (down payment of 20 percent or more) residential mortgage borrowers. It has two separately calibrated components: a buffer, currently 2 percent above the contract rate, and a floor, currently 5.25 percent. OSFI reviews and announces both components at least annually.
reports.cadence_note: OSFI committed in 2021 to review and communicate the qualifying rate at a minimum annually, every December.

release_schedule.note: OSFI's own MQR page (osfi-bsif.gc.ca/en/supervision/financial-institutions/banks/minimum-qualifying-rate-uninsured-mortgages) states OSFI reviews the minimum qualifying rate (floor and buffer) for uninsured mortgages 'at least annually,' but gives no fixed date or month. Actual historical announcement dates confirm irregular timing rather than a fixed cadence: Dec 15, 2022 ('OSFI maintains Minimum Qualifying Rate for uninsured mortgages'), Dec 12, 2023 ('OSFI confirms Minimum Qualifying Rate for uninsured mortgages'), Nov 21, 2024 (Fall Quarterly Release, which also touched on MQR for straight switches), and then no 2025 announcement — the next decision (keeping the rate at 5.25%/contract rate+2%) was announced Jan 29, 2026, per OSFI news and Canadian Mortgage Professional/Canadian Mortgage Trends coverage. Given the >14-month gap between the Nov 2024 and Jan 2026 announcements and the shifting month (Dec, Dec, Nov, Jan), there is no reliable next date to project. Most recent decision: Jan 29, 2026, rate maintained at 5.25% or contract rate + 2 percentage points, whichever is higher.

reports.title: CMHC Mortgage Loan Insurance – Homeowner and Small Rental Programs (eligibility requirements and premium schedule)
reports.description: CMHC's published mortgage loan insurance product rules set the eligibility criteria and premium schedule for government-backed mortgage default insurance, which is required by law on residential mortgages with a loan-to-value ratio above 80 percent. The rules define maximum Gross Debt Service (39 percent) and Total Debt Service (44 percent) ratios, minimum down payments, maximum property values and amortization limits, and a premium table running from roughly 0.60 to 4.50 percent of the loan amount by loan-to-value band. These are the operative underwriting standards for the insured segment of the Canadian mortgage market.
reports.cadence_note: Revised as government mortgage insurance policy changes rather than on a fixed schedule.

release_schedule.note: CMHC does not publish a release calendar or stated periodic-update rule for this eligibility/premium schedule. The quick-reference guide page (published June 20, 2022) and premium information page (published March 31, 2018) both carry only a page-publication date and a disclaimer that terms are 'subject to change at any time' with no fixed review cycle. Historically, premium rate changes occurred irregularly (e.g., 2011, 2014, March 2015, March 2016, March 2017) tied to policy/risk decisions rather than a fixed annual or quarterly schedule, and premiums have reportedly been unchanged since 2017. This does not support treating it as an annual (releases_per_year=1) publication.

reports.title: Mortgage Qualifying Rate (Benchmark Rate for Insured Mortgages)
reports.description: Since April 6, 2020 the Bank of Canada has published a weekly benchmark rate used to determine the minimum qualifying rate for government-backed insured mortgages. It is calculated as the weekly median 5-year fixed insured mortgage rate drawn from federally backed mortgage insurance applications adjudicated by mortgage insurers, plus a buffer set by the Minister of Finance (initially 200 basis points). It is published on a Wednesday and takes effect the following Monday, replacing the older Bank of Canada 5-Year Benchmark Posted Mortgage Rate for this purpose.

entries.covers: Weekly benchmark/mortgage qualifying rate update (effective Monday 2026-08-17)

release_schedule.rule: The new benchmark rate for insured mortgages (based on the weekly median 5-year fixed insured mortgage rate from federally-backed mortgage insurance applications, plus a 200 bps buffer) is published by the Bank of Canada every Wednesday, effective the following Monday.
release_schedule.note: Confirmed by Department of Finance's Feb 2020 announcement establishing the new benchmark rate methodology and weekly Wednesday publication schedule (effective April 6, 2020, replacing the prior 5-Year Benchmark Posted Rate). Corroborated by Bank of Canada's related posted-interest-rates page, which is also 'Typically published on Wednesdays by 14:30 ET' with the most recent data as of research date (2026-08-11) being from Wednesday 2026-08-05, consistent with a next release on Wednesday 2026-08-12. Could not directly confirm on bankofcanada.ca which exact page hosts the insured-mortgage benchmark rate series itself (searches only surfaced the Department of Finance policy announcement and BoC's general posted-rates page), so no url_correction is made without direct citation.

reports.title: Interest Rates Posted for Selected Products by the Major Chartered Banks
reports.description: A weekly Bank of Canada table of the interest rates posted by the six major Canadian chartered banks on conventional mortgages (1- through 5-year terms), GICs, personal loans and deposit products. The published figure for each product is the statistical mode of the rates posted by the six largest banks, so it is a compilation of commercial bank submissions rather than a market-transaction rate. Its 5-year conventional mortgage series was the Bank of Canada 5-Year Benchmark Posted Mortgage Rate that governed the Canadian mortgage stress test until 2020-21.

release_schedule.rule: Typically published on Wednesdays by 14:30 ET (weekly update of posted interest rates by the major chartered banks).
release_schedule.note: The Bank of Canada page states the data is typically published weekly on Wednesdays by 14:30 ET; the most recent observation at time of check was dated 2026-08-05 (a Wednesday). The 2026-08-12 date is the next expected weekly Wednesday update, computed from that stated cadence, not read off a dated calendar. This matches the corpus's existing releases_per_year=52.

reports.title: Residential Mortgage Industry Report
reports.description: CMHC's semi-annual survey of the Canadian residential mortgage market, covering originations, renewals, arrears, and the traditional (chartered bank, credit union, mortgage finance company) and alternative (mortgage investment corporation, private) lending segments. It is assembled from CMHC's own NHA MBS issuer reporting and Survey of Non-Bank Mortgage Lenders together with Statistics Canada and Bank of Canada series, Equifax credit data and Canadian Bankers Association data. It is the main published bridge between mortgage-market outcomes and the prudential rules that govern them.
reports.cadence_note: Published twice a year (spring and fall editions); the companion Residential Mortgage Industry Data Dashboard updates quarterly.

release_schedule.note: CMHC's own Reports Calendar page lists this report's 'Last published' date as May 12, 2026 (the Spring 2026 edition) and 'Next published' as 'Fall 2026' with no specific day given; the calendar states release dates are subject to change. Prior editions follow a Spring/Fall pattern (Fall 2025, Spring 2026 confirmed), consistent with the corpus's releases_per_year=2.

reports.title: CDIC Differential Premiums Manual and Differential Premiums By-law
reports.description: CDIC's annual manual implements the Differential Premiums By-law, which sorts every CDIC member institution into one of five premium categories and sets the deposit insurance premium each pays. Scoring is split between quantitative factors (capital ratios, leverage, asset concentration, earnings, liquidity) and qualitative factors (OSFI's supervisory Overall Risk Rating and stage of intervention). Members file a Differential Premiums Return each April, largely auto-populated from returns already filed with OSFI through the Regulatory Reporting System.
reports.cadence_note: Manual reissued each March for the premium year; returns due April 30.

entries.covers: By-law Amending the CDIC Differential Premiums By-law finalized (Canada Gazette Part II)
By-law Amending the CDIC Differential Premiums By-law finalized (Canada Gazette Part II)
New comprehensive Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation Differential Premiums By-law (SOR/2025-165) finalized, in force April 29, 2026
March 2026 Differential Premiums Manual published ahead of the 2026 premium year (May 1, 2026 - April 30, 2027)
Projected next annual update of the Differential Premiums Manual (and any related by-law amendment) ahead of the 2027 premium year (May 1, 2027)

release_schedule.note: CDIC's own Forward Regulatory Plan states the Differential Premiums By-law 'must be reviewed annually,' historically pre-published (Canada Gazette Part I) each October and finalized (Part II) the following February-April, timed to the premium year that runs May 1 - April 30. The Differential Premiums Manual is reissued each year dated March (the 2026 edition PDF is headed 'MARCH 2026'), just before the May 1 premium-year start. However, CDIC completed a comprehensive by-law overhaul (SOR/2025-165, pre-published 2025-01-18, finalized 2025-09-10, in force 2026-04-29) rather than a routine annual amendment, and CDIC's 2025-2027 forward plan suggests the routine annual amendment cadence may be paused while the new framework beds in, so the exact 2027 date is a projection based on the historical pattern rather than a confirmed one.

reports.title: Minimum Qualifying Rate for Insured Mortgages (Government-Backed Mortgage Insurance Guarantee Framework)
reports.description: The Minister of Finance, not OSFI, sets the qualification rules for insured mortgages under Canada's government-backed mortgage insurance guarantee framework. Since April 6, 2020 the minimum qualifying rate for an insured mortgage has been the greater of the borrower's contract rate or the Bank of Canada's published Benchmark Rate. The Minister retains authority to adjust the buffer built into that benchmark.
reports.cadence_note: Changed by ministerial decision rather than on a schedule; major changes in 2016, 2020.

release_schedule.note: This is a policy framework/rule, not a periodic statistical report. The Feb 2020 announcement set the minimum qualifying rate formula (weekly median 5-year fixed insured mortgage rate + a 200bp buffer set by the Minister of Finance, with authority to adjust the buffer as needed). While the underlying benchmark RATE VALUE is republished weekly (Wednesdays, effective the following Monday) by the Bank of Canada, the FRAMEWORK/RULE itself (what this Dept of Finance report/announcement documents) has only been amended irregularly and unpredictably since 2020: e.g. Dec 2022 and Dec 2023 ministerial statements on the housing market, the Sept 2024 'Boldest Mortgage Reforms in Decades' announcement, the Dec 2024 in-force announcement, and a March 2025 Canada Gazette regulatory amendment (Insurable Housing Loan Regulations / Eligible Mortgage Loan Regulations). There is no stated cadence or fixed review interval for buffer/framework changes -- the Minister simply 'will have the authority to adjust the buffer' at will. This looks like a foundational policy instrument amended irregularly rather than a true recurring publication.

reports.title: Interest Rates Charged for New and Existing Lending by Chartered Banks
reports.description: The Bank of Canada's own 'month-end statement of interest rates charged vis-a-vis new and existing loans, booked in Canada, in Canadian dollars only, to Canadian households and corporate sectors by chartered banks.' Rates are a volume-weighted average across reporting institutions, cross-sectioned for a given month. It breaks residential mortgages out by rate type, with a 'Residential variable rate mortgages' section ('Total variable rate mortgages, Total', further split into closed non-convertible, closed convertible, and open variable rate mortgages) alongside the fixed-rate breakdown. This is the missing near-end node flagged in this file's own _dropped entry and in rate-transmission.json: not an individual lender's commercial rate sheet (which cannot be a node), but the Bank's own aggregated published series of what banks actually charged, including on the variable-rate segment. Also redistributed by Statistics Canada as table 10-10-0006-01, 'Funds advanced, outstanding balances, and interest rates for new and existing lending, Bank of Canada', which states its source as the Bank of Canada.
reports.cadence_note: Typically published within the third week of the month.

release_schedule.rule: Typically published within the third week of the month.
release_schedule.note: The Bank of Canada page states the data is 'Typically published within the third week of the month' but does not give exact calendar dates. Cross-check via Statistics Canada table 10-10-0006 (which republishes this BoC series) showed a most recent release date of 2026-07-14, roughly consistent with a monthly cadence though slightly earlier than 'third week'.

dependencies.basis: CORRA's published methodology defines a contingency fallback computed directly from the Bank's policy rate: "The fallback rate is equal to the Bank of Canada target for the overnight rate for that day plus the mean spread over the previous five business days between CORRA and the Bank of Canada target on those days." If technical issues prevent calculation by 11:00 ET, CORRA is set at this fallback rate. The methodology page works a numeric example beginning "Bank of Canada target for the overnight rate: 1.75 percent". Note the causality is unusual: the Bank targets the overnight rate that CORRA measures, so CORRA normally depends on the policy rate only economically - but the documented, mechanical dependency is this fallback.

The CanDeal Term CORRA Methodology states Term CORRA "is a forward-looking measurement of overnight CORRA for 1- and 3-month tenors, based on market-implied expectations from CORRA derivatives markets. The rate is calculated from 1- and 3-month CORRA futures trading on the Montreal Exchange", and that it "is designed to complement both overnight CORRA and the CORRA Compounded Index that are administered and published by the Bank of Canada." The contract specifications annexed to the methodology close the loop mechanically: the futures' "final settlement price... is 100 minus the compounded daily CORRA rate over the reference quarter" (and over the reference month for the one-month contract).

Section IV "Other guidance" of Guideline B-20 states: "This Guideline is complementary to, and should be read in conjunction with, other OSFI guidance" and then lists, among others, the "Capital Adequacy Requirements Guideline" and the "Leverage Requirements Guideline". B-20 also provides that where a lender fails to control residential mortgage risk, "OSFI can take, or require the FRFI to take, corrective measures... including... the discretionary authority to adjust the FRFI's capital requirements or authorized leverage ratio".

Guideline B-20 defers to CMHC's published insurance rules for the debt-serviceability standard on insured mortgages: "for insured mortgages, the Canada Mortgage Housing Corporation (CMHC) defines GDS and TDS ratios and sets maximum GDS and TDS limits." It adds that "For insured residential mortgages, OSFI expects FRFIs to meet mortgage insurers' requirements in regard to debt serviceability" and that B-20 "complements... the Government of Canada's mortgage insurance guarantee framework, which establishes the rules for government-backed insured mortgages."

B-20 does not itself contain the stress-test number; it points at OSFI's separately announced calibration: "At a minimum, the qualifying rate for all uninsured mortgages should be the greater of the contractual mortgage rate plus a buffer, as set by the Superintendent or the minimum (or 'floor') rate, as set by the Superintendent", and "OSFI will review the calibration of the qualifying rate (both the buffer and floor) at least annually and will issue announcements if there are any calibration changes."

Historical but explicitly documented. OSFI's February 18, 2020 news release states: "OSFI's mortgage underwriting guideline (B-20) sets the minimum qualifying rate for uninsured mortgages... currently the minimum qualifying rate is the higher of the contractual mortgage rate plus two percent, or the five-year benchmark rate published by the Bank of Canada." That five-year benchmark rate was the Bank of Canada 5-Year Benchmark Posted Mortgage Rate from the posted chartered bank rate table. The link was severed on June 1, 2021 when OSFI replaced the Bank of Canada benchmark with a fixed 5.25 percent floor.

Department of Finance Canada backgrounder: "The minimum qualifying rate for insured mortgages will now be the greater of: The borrower's contract rate... or The new Benchmark Rate." "The new Benchmark Rate for insured mortgages will be published weekly on the Bank of Canada's website, and will be based on submitted mortgage insurance application contract rates."
dependencies.evidence_quote: The minimum qualifying rate for insured mortgages will now be the greater of: The borrower's contract rate... or The new Benchmark Rate.

dependencies.basis: Historical but explicitly documented in the same backgrounder, which describes the rule it was replacing: "borrowers taking on an insured mortgage must qualify at the greater of the: Borrower's Contract Rate... or Bank of Canada 5-Year Benchmark Posted Mortgage Rate, which is the mode of the posted 5-year conventional mortgage rates offered by the six largest banks." The document gives OSFI's and Finance's reason for dropping it: the posted rate "is also less representative of average contract rates as it only considers Canada's six largest banks, and the 'posted', and not 'actual' rates offered to borrowers by those banks."

CMHC does not set its own qualification rules for insured mortgages; the Minister of Finance does. OSFI's May 2021 MQR letter states plainly: "The Minister of Finance sets the qualification rules for insured mortgages." The Department of Finance backgrounder describes the same framework: "Mortgage insurance standards include requirements for a minimum down payment, and maximum mortgage amortization period, along with other factors such as minimum credit scores and maximum debt servicing levels. The standards also include minimum qualifying rates for insured mortgages", and notes the review was conducted by Finance "in consultation with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions, the Bank of Canada, and the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation."
dependencies.evidence_quote: The Minister of Finance sets the qualification rules for insured mortgages.

dependencies.basis: The Bank of Canada does not observe these rates itself; the benchmark is built from mortgage insurers' application files. Department of Finance backgrounder: "The new Benchmark Rate will be: The weekly median 5-year fixed insured mortgage rate as calculated by the Bank of Canada from federally-backed mortgage insurance applications adjudicated by mortgage insurers; plus a buffer of 200 basis points to be set by the Minister of Finance." CMHC is the dominant federally backed insurer adjudicating those applications.

CDIC's premium scoring reads its capital inputs straight out of OSFI's capital framework. The 2026 Manual instructs: "1.1.4 Supervisory Target CET1 Capital Ratio (%) - Indicate the supervisory target CET1 capital ratio (including the capital conservation buffer, DSIB surcharge and domestic stability buffer as applicable) as set by the regulator for the member institution in accordance with the Capital Adequacy Requirements guideline (i.e., OSFI Target CET1 capital ratio (%) as set out in Schedule 10.010 - Ratio Calculations of the BCAR form)". Members must file with CDIC "the Basel Capital Adequacy Return (BCAR)" and "the Leverage Requirements Return (LRR form)" that they submitted "to the Superintendent... in accordance with the financial reporting instructions published by OSFI", and CDIC states that returns already filed with OSFI "by means of the RRS system" need not be refiled.

A similar stress test was required for insured loans beginning in 2016." The glossary further defines chartered banks and federally regulated financial institutions by OSFI's supervisory perimeter, and the report's lender taxonomy separates "Non-bank OSFI regulated" lenders.

The Bank of Canada's own explainer states the mechanism: 'What's behind your mortgage rate' (bankofcanada.ca, May 27, 2020) -- 'These include the prime rate, which is used by the banks as a basis for pricing variable-rate mortgages.' Typed uses_data_from rather than calculated_from, matching this file's own boc-prime-rate -> boc-policy-rate precedent: the explainer describes a market convention (prime plus or minus a lender-set spread), not a formula stated by the published series' own methodology page, and the published aggregate is a volume-weighted average of what banks actually charged rather than a recalculation of prime itself.

_dropped.why: Alberta's Credit Union Deposit Guarantee Corporation is the obvious provincial counterpart to OSFI, and its capital standards are widely described as Basel-influenced. But its published Standards of Sound Business and Financial Practices (2016 and 2026 editions, ~220KB of text) contain zero occurrences of 'Basel', 'OSFI' or 'Superintendent'. Every capital and liquidity requirement is referred only to 'the Credit Union Act and Regulations' - provincial legislation, not a report. CUDGC's own annual report financial statements are prepared under IFRS Accounting Standards, not PSAS, so there is no accounting-standards edge either. No CUDGC node was created rather than leave a permanently isolated one. This is the single biggest documented gap in the slice: Canada's provincial credit union supervisory chain is genuinely disconnected in public documents from the federal one.

OSFI describes its MQR-setting inputs only in the abstract: 'We factor in data collected from Canada's financial institutions. We also consider a range of vulnerability indicators in the housing market and the economic environment. Lastly, we consult with the Department of Finance Canada and the Bank of Canada.' Consulting an institution is not depending on a release, and no specific published series is ever named. Since June 2021 the MQR floor has been a fixed 5.25 percent with no formula behind it.

CAR Guideline Chapter 4 does recognise mortgage insurance as a credit risk mitigant and gives special treatment where 'a mortgage is comprehensively insured by a private sector mortgage insurer that has a backstop guarantee provided by the Government of Canada'. But it treats mortgage insurance generically and never cites CMHC's published product rules as a document, so this reads as a legal-status reference rather than a report dependency. The equivalent edge from Guideline B-20, which names CMHC explicitly as the source of the GDS and TDS limits, was kept instead.

This is the most important dependency in CORRA's methodology, but MTRS is a confidential regulatory data feed, not a published statistical release, so there is no node to point at.

_dropped.why: The Bank of Canada states the published figure for each product is 'the most typical of those offered by the six major chartered banks', computed as the statistical mode of the six largest banks' posted rates. The underlying inputs are commercial rate sheets from RBC, TD, BMO, CIBC, Scotiabank and National Bank, which have no stable public landing pages and are not reports in this graph's sense. This is the general shape of the problem in this slice: commercial lenders publish far less than governments do.

CDIC's $100,000 per-category coverage limit looks like the kind of threshold that would be indexed, but it is fixed in the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation Act and changed only by Parliament (last raised in 2005, with new eligible categories added in 2020 and 2022). It is not indexed to CPI or to any published series, so there is no dependency to record.

reports.title: IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard Plus (SDDS Plus)
reports.description: Highest tier of the IMF Data Standards Initiatives, established 2012. Builds on the SDDS with nine additional data categories (sectoral balance sheets, general government gross debt, and others) and stricter coverage, periodicity and timeliness requirements. Adherents publish an enhanced National Summary Data Page monitored on the Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board. Sits beside the existing imf-sdds and imf-e-gdds nodes as the third rung of the same initiative.
reports.cadence_note: A standard, not a periodical: revised rarely (legal text amendments). Nominal releases_per_year matching the existing imf-sdds/imf-e-gdds convention so the pulse reads as near-static.

reports.title: ASEAN Community Statistical System (ACSS)
reports.description: Regional statistical cooperation framework established 2011 under the ASEAN Framework of Cooperation in Statistics. Comprises the national statistical systems of the ten ASEAN Member States plus relevant sectoral bodies; harmonises concepts, definitions and classifications and produces comparable regional statistics via the ASEAN Statistical Indicators and the ASEANstats portal. ASEANstats (ASEAN Secretariat Statistics Division) is its technical arm.
reports.cadence_note: A standing framework, not a titled release: no releases_per_year on purpose, so it renders as a standing instrument (hollow), same as statutes.

reports.title: APEC Statistics (StatsAPEC)
reports.description: APEC's statistical databases (Key Indicators Database and Bilateral Linkages Database), compiling comparable economic and trade indicators across the 21 APEC member economies from national statistical offices and international sources. Its glossary names each economy's source agency, including Chinese Taipei's DGBAS.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7): a nominal releases_per_year so the pulse rate reads as continuous rather than one-off.

Round 7's corpus-wide sweep found six LIVE edges standing on exactly that same null, which meant the corpus said a null-NSDP row supports an edge six times and refuses it three times. Thomas ruled the refusal, not the allowance. THE REASON, in the IMF's own words rather than ours: IMF Country Report 25/270 says of a country in this same class, 'Algeria participates in the Enhanced General Data Dissemination (e-GDDS) and first posted its metadata in April 2009 but is yet to disseminate the data recommended under the e-GDDS.' Participation and implementation are two facts, and the null ComplianceDate is the second one in data form. `methodology_depends_on` asserts that the source's METHODOLOGY depends on the target; a country that has never disseminated what the e-GDDS recommends has a membership, not a methodology dependency. A ROUTE THAT WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: the evidence for all six predates the e-GDDS (which took effect 2015-07-01) and names the GDDS, so this looked at first like a wrong-target call answerable by minting a separate `imf-gdds` edition node under the §7 edition rule. It is not: the same Algeria sentence shows the IMF treating a 2009 GDDS-era posting as e-GDDS participation, because participants rolled over rather than rejoining. There is no edition split to make here, and `imf-e-gdds` was the right node all along — the edge is simply not a dependency. MEASURED, not assumed: 33 of the 34 null-ComplianceDate participants posted their DSBB metadata before 2015-07-01; Aruba (2017-08-16) is the sole country that joined under the e-GDDS itself and still never posted an NSDP. THE FACT IS NOT LOST, it is just not an edge: this country IS on the 110-country e-GDDS participant list, and its Important Dates row reads 'Iraq | December 15, 2009 | [blank]' with the NSDP column blank. To re-mint: find a document from this country's own statistical system stating that a release follows the e-GDDS, or wait for a non-null NSDP date to appear in the table. _meta: AF/G.23 (2026-08-13) — Cabo Verde municipal-tier synthesis pass. The raw research file for this round (cv-lei-financas-locais-79-2005's primary text via ampraia.cv, plus corroborating governo.cv press releases on the FFM 10%->15% proposal and 2016-2025 transfer totals) had already been folded into /tmp/rc/src/data/research/af-cabo-verde.json's cv-lei-financas-locais-79-2005 node and _dropped array by the time this synthesis pass began (verified line-for-line against the raw findings file — no discrepancies, nothing left un-synthesized there). This file captures the remaining negative/deferred findings from that same research pass that were not yet recorded anywhere: a distinct pending municipal-budget-law instrument, a per-município transfer breakdown that could not be located, and a CPLP-methodology search that came up empty. No new report nodes minted this round — no primary document was found that isn't already represented in af-cabo-verde.json.

_dropped.edge: cv-lei-financas-locais-79-2005 -> cv-lei-base-orcamento-municipal (target has no node yet)
_dropped.why: UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF lead-chase round): reason code changed from 'deferred' to 'note' — this is now a confirmed negative finding as of a specific date, not an open unknown awaiting a future search. A governo.cv press article (20.04.2023, quoting Minister of State/Territorial Cohesion Janine Lelis) describes a proposed revision to a distinctly-named instrument, the 'Lei Base do Orcamento Municipal' ('a proposta de revisao da Lei Base do Orcamento Municipal... esta-se tambem a introduzir os principios orcamentais que decorrem, tanto da Lei Base do Sistema Nacional de Planeamento, bem como a propria Lei Base do Orcamento do Estado'), separate from Lei n.º 79/VI/2005. The lead-chase round re-fetched the same governo.cv, 12.06.2025 article (Vice-PM/Minister of Finance Olavo Correia) and captured the fuller sentence this time: "Para o próximo ciclo, Olavo Correia defendeu que 'é urgente aprovar a Lei de Base do Orçamento Municipal, o novo Regime Financeiro dos Municípios e adotar o Índice de Coesão Territorial'" — the Minister names BOTH the 'Lei de Base do Orçamento Municipal' AND the 'novo Regime Financeiro dos Municípios' together, in present/future-obligation tense ('é urgente aprovar'), directly confirming (not merely implying, as this entry's original text had to infer from a partial quote) that NEITHER instrument had been enacted as of 12 June 2025. Separately, a full-text check of Lei n.º 52/X/2025 (Boletim Oficial I Série n.º 30, 17-04-2025; https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/DownloadAct?id=84886) — the only law amending Lei n.º 79/VI/2005 located in the 2025-2026 window — confirms it is not this instrument either: it amends only Article 6 (an unrelated municipal fee-charging exemption), not the FFM formula or a comprehensive municipal-budget-law revision. No enacted law number was found for the 'Lei de Base do Orçamento Municipal' or the 'novo Regime Financeiro dos Municípios' in this round's search either; that sweep of the Boletim Oficial was not exhaustive (search budget exhausted before a full 2025-2026 sweep could be completed), so a future round could still check for a later enactment. Still no node minted for either instrument for lack of a citable primary text of the enactment itself.

_meta: AF lead-chase round, 2026-08-13 — follow-up to AF/G.23's cv-cabo-verde municipal-tier synthesis. Task: resolve the open question left by cv-lei-financas-locais-79-2005's description (governo.cv, June 2025) of whether Cabo Verde's Fundo de Financiamento dos Municípios (FFM) rate had been raised from 10% to 15% per a 2019 draft proposal. RESOLVED: still 10%, not raised. Two primary Boletim Oficial instruments were located: (1) Lei n.º 52/X/2025, de 17 de abril — the only law amending Lei n.º 79/VI/2005 since the corpus baseline, and it does not touch the FFM rate (amends only Article 6, an unrelated fee-charging provision) — judged too narrow to warrant a standalone report node and instead cited by URL directly within cv-lei-financas-locais-79-2005's updated description (see _dropped entry below for the reasoning). (2) Lei n.º 69/X/2025, de 31 de dezembro (OE2026, the enacted FY2026 state budget) — a genuinely new, independently citable national budget document, minted below as cv-oe2026-budget with a cites edge to cv-lei-financas-locais-79-2005. This file also documents (via a dependency-free note, since no new edge was created) that the same research pass re-confirmed, with a fuller quote, that both pending municipal-finance revision instruments flagged by cv-g23-municipal.json remain unenacted as of the most recent primary statement located (governo.cv, 12 June 2025) — the fuller quote and reason-code change were applied directly to cv-g23-municipal.json rather than duplicated here.

reports.title: Lei n.º 69/X/2025, de 31 de dezembro — Orçamento do Estado para 2026 (OE2026), Artigo 13.º (Fundo de Financiamento dos Municípios)
reports.description: Cabo Verde's enacted FY2026 state budget law, published as a 1.º Suplemento to the Boletim Oficial (I Série, n.º 133, 31-12-2025). Chapter V ("Autarquias Locais"), Article 13.º, "Fundo de Financiamento dos Municípios": "O montante do Fundo de Financiamento dos Municípios (FFM) é fixado em 5.387.079.168$00 CVE... para o ano de 2026, distribuído conforme constante do Mapa X, anexo à presente lei." [The FFM amount is fixed at 5,387,079,168 CVE for 2026, distributed as per Map X annexed to this law.] Consistent with — but does not itself restate — the 10%-of-tax-revenue FFM formula set by Lei n.º 79/VI/2005 Article 10 §3 (see cv-lei-financas-locais-79-2005); Cabo Verdean budget laws follow the standard practice of fixing the fund at an absolute escudo amount each year rather than reciting the underlying percentage. The ~5.39 billion CVE figure lines up with Vice-Prime Minister/Minister of Finance Olavo Correia's own June 2025 projection (governo.cv) that the FFM would "ultrapassar[á] os 5 milhões de contos em 2026" [surpass 5 million contos in 2026] — 5 million contos = 5 billion CVE, so the enacted figure is squarely in the range the Minister was already projecting under continued 10% math, not a jump consistent with a 15% rate (which would imply a materially larger figure). Per-município distribution not independently verified this round (Mapa X annex not fetched — flagged for a future round if a per-município breakdown is needed; see cv-g23-municipal.json's existing unresolved per-município _dropped entry, which this does not supersede).
reports.cadence_note: Annual state budget law; this is the FY2026 instalment. A recurring series could be modelled with releases_per_year: 1 in a future round if prior/subsequent years' OE laws are minted, but left unset here since only this one year's law has been located.

dependencies.basis: OE2026 Article 13.º restates and funds the Fundo de Financiamento dos Municípios (FFM) that Lei n.º 79/VI/2005 Article 10 established and formula-defines (10% of certain state tax revenue, penultimate-year lookback); the budget law names the fund by its statutory acronym and fixes its annual amount under that pre-existing legal framework, without re-legislating the formula itself.

_dropped.why: Lei n.º 52/X/2025, de 17 de abril (Boletim Oficial I Série n.º 30, 17-04-2025; https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/DownloadAct?id=84886) is the only law located that amends Lei n.º 79/VI/2005 since the corpus baseline, and its full 18-page text was checked end-to-end for any mention of "FFM" or "Fundo de Financiamento dos Municípios" — none found. It amends only Article 6 (adding a municipal fee-charging exemption for electricity distributors that now pay a separate "renda especial") and revokes an unrelated law, Lei n.º 24/VIII/2013. Judged too narrow in substantive content to warrant a standalone report node (unlike cv-oe2026-budget, which independently states a citable national budget figure); instead cited directly by URL within cv-lei-financas-locais-79-2005's updated description as the evidentiary basis for confirming the FFM rate is unchanged at 10%. Recorded here as a note only since no report node or dependency edge was created for it.

reports.title: Financial Accounts (Gesamtwirtschaftliche Finanzierungsrechnung)
reports.description: Quarterly balance sheets of financial flows and outstanding amounts by institutional sector and financial instrument, published in press releases, the Bundesbank's Monthly Report, and its dedicated Statistical Series. Bundesbank's own page: 'The Bundesbank compiles the financial accounts on a quarterly basis... Their methodological basis is the latest version of the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010).' Passed on to the ECB, which uses it (with other euro-area countries' contributions) to compile the euro-area financial accounts.
reports.cadence_note: Live-verified directly on bundesbank.de/en/statistics/macroeconomic-accounting-systems/financial-accounts -- 'The Bundesbank compiles the financial accounts on a quarterly basis.'

release_schedule.note: Bundesbank's statistical release calendar lists each quarterly financial-accounts (Finanzierungsrechnung) release individually, each on its own dated page. Releases follow a consistent ~4-month lag after quarter-end (e.g. Q2 data released end of October, Q3 data released end of January, Q4 data released end of April, Q1 data released end of July), confirming the on-file releases_per_year=4. As of 2026-08-11 the Q1 2026 release (expected ~end July 2026) has already occurred, so the next upcoming release is the Q2 2026 data on 2026-10-31.

reports.title: National Accounts — Domestic Product (Fachserie 18)
reports.description: The German national accounts, scoped by Destatis's own quality report as 'national accounts of the Federation (EVAS No 81)' and covering 'domestic product calculation (production, use, and distribution approaches), input-output accounts, national wealth accounts, employment accounts'. Published as Fachserie 18, whose quarterly strand is Reihe 1.2 ('National Accounts – Domestic Product – Quarterly results') and whose seasonally adjusted strand is Reihe 1.3. First results for a quarter appear as a press release at t+30 days, with detail at about t+55. Compiled under ESA 2010, which Destatis states was 'implemented in Germany as part of the 2014 general revision'.
reports.cadence_note: Destatis Quality Report, General information on the statistics: 'Periodicity: quarterly, annual'. The quarterly strand is taken as the release rate. Publication timing is documented separately in the QNA inventory: 'First quarterly results of GDP without particular breakdown are published as press release 30 days after the end of a reporting quarter. The more detailed figures are published … around 55 days after the end of the reporting quarter.'

entries.covers: Detailed results on gross domestic product, 2nd quarter 2026 (Fachserie 18, Reihe 1.2)

release_schedule.note: Destatis's Fachserie 18 Reihe 1.2 (quarterly national accounts detailed results) is published quarterly (~4x/year), consistent with the corpus's releases_per_year=4. The publisher's own 30 July 2026 press release (PD26_269) explicitly states: 'Detaillierte Informationen zu den Revisionen stellt das Statistische Bundesamt mit der Veröffentlichung der ausführlichen Ergebnisse zum Bruttoinlandsprodukt im 2. Quartal 2026 am 25. August 2026 zur Verfügung' (detailed Q2 2026 GDP results will be published 25 August 2026). Past pattern of detailed-results releases in 2026: 22 May 2026 (Q1 2026, PE26_173). No published full-year release calendar with all future dates was found; only the next single date is documented directly by the publisher.

dependencies.basis: Destatis states ESA 2010 as the legal basis of the German national accounts in the structured metadata of its own quality report: 'Scope of the statistics: national accounts of the Federation (EVAS No 81) … Legal bases: Regulation (EC) No 549/2013, European System of National and Regional Accounts (ESA) 2010, and supplementary and amending regulations … Periodicity: quarterly, annual'. The same report sets out the mechanism: 'The ESA 2010 is a European Regulation, which is binding for all EU member states as of 1 September 2014 (Council Regulation (EU) No. 549/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 21 May 2013, published in the Official Journal on 26 June 2013). It was implemented in Germany as part of the 2014 general revision. This regulation was amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/734 …'. Two further documents say the same in their own words: the GNI inventory ('in compliance with the European System of National Accounts (ESA) 2010' and 'based on the European System of Accounts (ESA) 2010') and the QNA inventory ('in compliance with the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)'). relationship_type is methodology_depends_on rather than uses_data_from: ESA 2010 supplies no figures, it supplies the 'common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables' (Regulation 549/2013, Article 1(2)(a)).
dependencies.evidence_quote: The national accounting system is based on harmonised European rules that are laid down in a legally binding form in the European System of National and Regional Accounts (ESA 2010).

reports.title: Consumer Price Index for Germany
reports.description: Germany's national consumer price index, EVAS register no. 61111, listed as one of the German GNI calculation's main data sources (production, expenditure and income approaches) in the GNI inventory's own Chapter 10 table. Confirmed live on Destatis's own site: a flash/expected estimate near month-end followed by the confirmed rate roughly ten days into the following month (e.g. 'Inflation rate of +2.8% expected in July 2026' on 30 July 2026, followed by 'Inflation rate at +2.3% in June 2026' on 10 July 2026 for the prior month).
reports.cadence_note: Live-verified on destatis.de/EN/Themes/Economy/Prices/Consumer-Price-Index -- a monthly press-release series, two releases per reference month (flash estimate, then confirmed figure), same two-stage pattern already seen for eurostat-hicp.

release_schedule.note: Destatis publishes both a preliminary estimate (around the last working day of the reference month) and final results (mid-following month) for the German CPI/HICP each month. The August 12, 2026 date is directly confirmed in the July 30, 2026 press release (PD26_270_611): 'Die endgültigen Ergebnisse für Juli 2026 werden am 12. August 2026 veröffentlicht.' Subsequent dates through end of 2026 are taken from Destatis's own release calendar search tool (Terminsuche) filtered for 'verbraucherpreisindex', consistent with the standard preliminary/final monthly pattern.

reports.title: Labour Cost Survey
reports.description: EVAS register no. 62411, listed in the GNI inventory's Chapter 10 table as a production- and income-approach source. The GNI inventory's own text: 'The labour cost survey (EVAS 62411) takes place every 4 years (also 2020) and asks for the private use of car companies (benefit in kind)...' -- used among other things to allocate gross wages and salaries per employee and private use of company cars.
reports.cadence_note: Stated directly in the source document itself (the GNI inventory, p. 152 of the extracted text): 'takes place every 4 years (also 2020)'. Not independently re-verified on a separate Destatis page this session -- the GNI inventory is itself a Destatis publication and the primary source for this fact.

release_schedule.rule: The Labour Cost Survey (Arbeitskostenerhebung) is conducted every four years under EU law (Council Regulation (EC) No 530/1999 and Commission Regulation (EC) No 1737/2005) and Germany's Verdienststatistikgesetz, covering reference years 2000, 2004, 2008, ..., 2020, 2024, 2028. Eurostat's LCS metadata states 'Data for LCS2024 will be published in 2nd half of 2026,' and Destatis's April 2026 press release (PD26_148_624) states the 2024 survey results 'werden voraussichtlich im Juli 2026 veröffentlicht' (are expected to be published in July 2026).
release_schedule.note: As of the research date (2026-08-11), no press release or dataset confirming the actual July 2026 publication of AKE2024 detailed results could be located via search — the target month has just passed and the release may have slipped slightly (Destatis used 'voraussichtlich' = 'expected'). The prior cycle (LCS2020) was published July 2022 (PD22_280_624), i.e. about 2 years after the reference year, consistent with the 2024→2026 pattern. If AKE2024 has already been published by the time this is read, the next occurrence would instead be AKE2028, expected to be published in the second half of 2030.

reports.title: Quality Report -- National Accounts
reports.description: Destatis's own quality report on the German national accounts (EVAS No 81), covering 'domestic product calculation (production, use, and distribution approaches), input-output accounts, national wealth accounts, employment accounts, volume of labour accounts and financial accounts'. States its own legal basis as 'Regulation (EC) No 549/2013, European System of National and Regional Accounts (ESA) 2010, and supplementary and amending regulations'. Voluntary: nothing in EU regulation compels a member state to publish a report of this kind (esa2010-quality-reporting.json _second_finding); Destatis produces one on its own initiative.
reports.cadence_note: Document's own cover page: reference period '10/2024-09/2025', 'Periodicity: annual', 'Published: 24/10/2025'. release_schedule.note: This is a methodological 'Quality Report' (part of Destatis's SIMS-style quality reporting framework offered 'since 2005' for all federal statistics), not a periodic statistical release. The current PDF is dated 29 October 2025 (per its own title page), but neither the report's landing/introduction page (https://www.destatis.de/EN/Methods/Quality/QualityReports/National-Accounts-Domestic-Product/einfuehrung.html) nor the general quality-reports overview page (https://www.destatis.de/EN/Methods/Quality/quality-reports.html) states any fixed update frequency, review cycle, or publishes a release calendar for it. No prior editions with dates could be located to establish an observed annual (or other) pattern within the available tools (web search budget was exhausted and archive.org access was blocked by the proxy). Given the absence of any calendar, stated rule, or confirmable pattern, this is classified as irregular; the corpus's releases_per_year=1 could not be confirmed or refuted with direct evidence.
