reports.title: Balance of Payments Statistics
reports.description: Deutsche Bundesbank's balance of payments statistical series -- the German GNI inventory names it as the source for taxes on production and imports paid to the rest of the world and for cross-border property income. Read live on bundesbank.de/en (Statistics > External sector > Balance of payments > Balance of payments statistics): a table series (Major items of the balance of payments; Current account; International investment position and external debt; Trade in services; Direct investments) updated through 2026, most recently 31 August 2026 at the time of research.
reports.cadence_note: The table series updates monthly (component tables carry different dates within the same month, e.g. 12.08.2026 and 31.08.2026 for different table sets); not independently cross-checked against a stated periodicity on a separate methodology page this round.

reports.title: Microcensus
reports.description: EVAS register no. 12211, Germany's core household survey -- the GNI inventory names it directly as a source for allowances in the labour-market/national-accounts calculation and for average household size used in staff-sales estimation. Destatis's own EN methods page (read live 2026-09-07): 'The microcensus is the largest annual household survey of official statistics in Germany... roughly 810,000 people in about 370,000 households and collective living quarters, that is approximately one percent of Germany's population, are asked about their working and living conditions.' The same page states the EU Labour Force Survey has been folded into it since 1968 ('Since 1968... EU-wide questions about labour market participation (Labour Force Survey, LFS) have been an integral part of the microcensus') -- a lead for a future EU-LFS edge, not pursued this round (no EU LFS Regulation node exists in the corpus yet).
reports.cadence_note: Destatis's own page: 'the largest annual household survey'. Distinct from EVAS 12212 (the microcensus's housing supplementary programme), which remains an unminted lead in de-destatis-source-surveys.json's own _dropped block.

reports.title: Turnover Tax Statistics (Advance Returns)
reports.description: EVAS register no. 73311 -- per de-destatis-source-surveys.json's own prior count, the single most-cited source statistic in the whole GNI inventory (35 mentions). Used to supplement household final consumption expenditure (HFCE) with VAT, to cross-check production-approach results for almost all industries, and as one of the main data sources (with quarterly production statistics and monthly ITGS) for machinery/equipment capital formation. Destatis's own EN page ('Turnover tax', read live 2026-09-07) confirms it as a live, regularly updated release: e.g. an 18 March 2026 update reporting 2024 advance-return results, and a 25 September 2025 update reporting 2021 assessment results. The GNI inventory's own abbreviations table gives the German original: 'UStSt Umsatzsteuerstatistik (VAT statistics)'.
reports.cadence_note: Destatis's page presents results by reference year (annual updates, e.g. the 2024 advance-return results reported 18 March 2026); not independently cross-checked against a stated periodicity document this round.

reports.title: Federal Statistics Act (Bundesstatistikgesetz)
reports.description: The framework law establishing the Statistisches Bundesamt (Destatis) and governing federal statistics in Germany (Gesetz über die Statistik für Bundeszwecke). Originally enacted 1987; current consolidated text as of the 2016 recast, last amended 2024, read live on gesetze-im-internet.de (the Federal Ministry of Justice's official consolidated-law portal) 2026-09-07. Section 3(1) sets out the Statistisches Bundesamt's statutory tasks, including compiling and publishing national accounts (No. 13) -- the German counterpart of the UK's Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007 (gb-srsa-2007) already in the corpus.

reports.title: Building and Housing Census
reports.description: EVAS register no. 31211 (Gebäude- und Wohnungszählung). A full survey of Germany's housing stock, conducted alongside the population census -- most recently 2022 and 2011. The GNI inventory names it directly and repeatedly as the primary data source for housing services (imputed and actual rent) in the production/expenditure accounts: 'With the results of the 2022 building and housing census (EVAS 31211), data on rental income per square metre and the corresponding floor area are available for the first time from a full survey', and its results are the 'current benchmark' for the housing-services calculation between census years.
reports.cadence_note: GNI inventory: conducted 2011 and 2022, an 11-year interval -- entered as a nominal rate (1/11) rather than guessed, per the corpus's own 'a number can say once a generation' convention for the decennial US census (0.1) and SNA 2008 (0.05). Not independently cross-checked against a stated future schedule on a separate Destatis page this round.

reports.title: Microcensus Additional Survey on the Housing Situation of Households
reports.description: EVAS register no. 12212 -- the microcensus's housing supplementary programme, distinct from the core annual microcensus (EVAS 12211, minted in de-national-core-2026-09-07.json). The GNI inventory names it by its full official title directly: 'Information on service charges (excluding energy) is available from the Microcensus Additional Survey on the Housing Situation of Households (EVAS 12212). The most recent surveys were conducted in 2018 and 2022.' Also used, per the same document, to extrapolate housing floor-area data between building-census years.
reports.cadence_note: GNI inventory: 'The most recent surveys were conducted in 2018 and 2022' -- a 4-year interval, matching the microcensus's own broader supplementary-survey rotation. Not independently cross-checked against a stated future schedule this round.

reports.title: Tax Revenue Statistics
reports.description: EVAS register no. 71211 (Steuerhaushalt / Kassenmäßige Steuereinnahmen). Destatis's own EN page titles this 'Tax revenue' and reports cash tax revenue by type of tax. The GNI inventory's Chapter 10 summary table glosses the same EVAS number 'Tax revenue statistics'; its body text cites the identical EVAS number twice as 'public finance statistics' (land transfer tax revenue for the housing-services and real-estate-services calculations) and once as 'fiscal statistics' (the second-home tax added to housing services) -- three English glosses for one release inside the same document, recorded here as title_aliases sourced from that document rather than picked for the node.
reports.cadence_note: Destatis publishes both annual (Fachserie 14 Reihe 4) and quarterly ('Statistischer Bericht Steuerhaushalt') releases; not independently cross-checked against a stated periodicity document this round -- entered as quarterly (4) since that is the more frequent, live-confirmed release cadence (destatis.de lists quarterly 'Statistischer Bericht Steuerhaushalt' reports through 2024).

_note: DE thin-coverage round 4. Works the 37 genuinely-open Chapter 10.1 rows that de-destatis-source-surveys.json's own _dropped note lists (round 10 made that note accurate: four rows resolved, two REFUSED, so 37 open and not 43). Method is round 3's: the German GNI inventory (esa-2010-methods.pdf, 372pp, 4.4MB) fetched live in the cloud sandbox and read for BODY-TEXT sentences that name a source statistic by title AND by EVAS number AND say what the accounts do with it. Chapter 10's table row alone was never treated as sufficient -- see the first open question for why that is a ruling and not a research gap. 21 rows had such a sentence; 16 did not and stay open, each with its reason. Node titles are the publisher's own words for the artefact taken from this same document (PLAYBOOK-CORPUS §7c), with the Chapter 10 register gloss recorded as a title_alias where the two differ -- the same multi-gloss handling round 3 used for EVAS 71211. One title_alias was deliberately NOT recorded (EVAS 71712's register gloss, see that node). Node urls are the publisher's canonical per-statistic GENESIS-Online pages, all verified 200 this round; they are Angular shells, so they are a node url and never evidence.
_headline: DE: +21 nodes, +21 edges, all off one document already cited in this corpus. Chapter 10.1's open rows go from 37 to 16.
_open_questions: THE RULING THIS ROUND KEPT HITTING, and it is Thomas's, not a research pass: 8 of the 16 rows left open appear in Chapter 10's table and NOWHERE in the 372-page body -- 12111 Population census, 21372 (higher-education finance, quarterly), 31141 Statistics of demolition of buildings and dwellings, 44241 (annual survey, finishing trade and property developers), 71512 and 71517 (quarterly cash results), 71811 Annual accounts of extra budgets, 79931 Energy tax statistics. PLAYBOOK-CORPUS §7a admits a methodology table cell that names a source as caption-equivalent and grades it A, and Chapter 10 is exactly such a table -- its title is 'Main data sources used'. What it discloses per row is an X against the Production/Expenditure/Income column, i.e. WHICH APPROACH the source feeds, not what the accounts compute from it. Every mint in rounds 2, 3 and 4 rested on a body sentence instead. Reading the table row as sufficient would move all eight at once, on one decision; refusing it leaves them permanently unwirable from this document. Neither is a research question.

The other 8 open rows are refused on evidence, not left unread. Five are cited ONLY inside an EVAS BUNDLE the document never separates: 43211 appears only as 'EVAS 43211 and 43221', 23121 only as 'the annual hospital statistics (EVAS 23111, 23112, 23121)', 51141 and 51231 only as 'the monthly ITGS (EVAS 51141, 51231)' / 'the external trade statistics (EVAS 51141, 51231)', 44221 only as 'the annual business and investment survey (EVAS 44211, 44221)'. Wiring one member of a bundle asserts a division of labour the sentence does not make. Three more are named only in a phrasing too generic to carry a node title: 42252 is cited twice as 'the annual structural survey (SE)', 71711 as 'the budgets of the Federal Government, the federal states and the municipalities' with no artefact title at all, and 31121 only as 'the construction activity statistics', which is the family name covering EVAS 31111 as well. The ITGS pair is the most valuable of the eight -- 'monthly ITGS' would be a real node if minted as ONE international-trade-in-goods node rather than split across two EVAS rows, and this corpus already carries ITGS nodes elsewhere; that is a scoping question, not an evidence one.

Chapter 10.2 (16 other official sources) is untouched by this round and its own note in de-destatis-source-surveys.json is the accurate worklist: KBA motor vehicle statistics, BaFin insurance and pension statistics, banking statistics, EMU interest rate statistics, Economic Accounts for Agriculture and the Bundesnetzagentur telecommunications annual report are still open; the Bundesbank Monthly Report and Annual Report are refused, twice, and must not be opened a third time. Chapter 10.3 (7 non-government sources) is still lowest priority and untouched.

The 47415 -> 47410 and 45341/45342 -> 47410 successions are real and are NOT minted here. Both are `supersedes`, which is a Relation and not a dependency edge, and no round has opened that shape for this branch. All five nodes carry the succession in their descriptions so the lead survives.

reports.title: AfA tables (Absetzung für Abnutzung)
title_aliases: Depreciation table for generally usable fixed assets
reports.description: Chapter 10.2 row 16 of the German GNI inventory ('Depreciation table for generally usable fixed assets, Federal Ministry of Finance'). BMF's depreciation tables giving the ordinary useful life of fixed assets for tax purposes: one table for generally usable assets ('AfA-Tabelle AV', applying to assets acquired after 31 December 2000) plus around a hundred branch-specific tables. The inventory calls them the main reference points for the average service lives used in the national accounts' capital stock estimates, while saying plainly that the figures have to be augmented by 20% to 100% because fiscal service lives are set on a precautionary basis. BMF's own page says the tables are not a binding legal norm, which is why this is a publication and not an instrument.
reports.cadence_note: Nominal, not measured. The inventory calls them 'regularly updated' and states no interval; BMF's own page shows the generally-usable-assets table applying unchanged to everything acquired after 31 December 2000, with the branch tables revised occasionally. 0.05 is the corpus's once-a-generation convention (as used for SNA 2008), entered rather than guessing a real rate.

_dropped.edge: de-destatis-national-accounts -> BaFin insurance and pension statistics (GNI inventory Chapter 10.2 rows 5 and 6)
_dropped.why: REFUSED 2026-09-07 (DE round 5), and refused on the strongest ground available: what the accounts use is not a publication. Chapter 10.2 row 5 is titled 'Statistics for primary insurance, reinsurance undertakings and pensions funds, Bundesanstalt für Finanzdienstleistungsaufsicht' and row 6 is BaFin's own budget, so the register makes them look like titled releases. The body says otherwise. Paragraph 3.369: 'Data sources here are the forms and records made available to the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority ... in line with the Regulation on Reporting by Insurance Undertakings to the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (Versicherungsberichterstattungs-Verordnung - BerVersV) and/or the Regulation on Reporting by Pension Funds (Pensionsfondsberichterstattungs-Verordnung - BerPensV). They are made available to the Federal Statistical Office by the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) as so-called internal accounting documents.' Regulatory returns passed between two agencies as internal documents are not a published recurring release, so PLAYBOOK.md rule 2 refuses the node however well evidenced the usage is. The later body sentences that DO name something ('based on data of the insurance statistics from the Financial Supervisory Authority', 3.374 and 3.379) describe the same pipeline and do not turn the internal documents into a publication. THE LEAD THAT SURVIVES, and it is a real one: BerVersV and BerPensV are both named by full title in 3.369 and are genuine legal instruments of the kind PLAYBOOK-CORPUS §7c keeps. They are the legal basis of the INSURERS' reporting to BaFin, not of Destatis's compilation, so wiring them to de-destatis-national-accounts would assert one step more than the document says. Whoever opens this should mint them against BaFin's data collection if that ever becomes a node, not against the national accounts.

_dropped.edge: de-destatis-national-accounts -> Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt motor vehicle statistics (GNI inventory Chapter 10.2 row 3)
_dropped.why: REFUSED 2026-09-07 (DE round 5) on PLAYBOOK-CORPUS §7a's agency-not-artefact bar, after a real attempt to clear it. The inventory uses KBA data heavily and says so in at least six body sentences, but every one attributes it to the AGENCY with a descriptive phrase rather than naming a release: 'the registration statistics of the Federal Motor Transport Authority', 'the re-registration statistics of the Federal Motor Transport Authority', 'notifications of new registrations and re-registrations from the Federal Motor Transport Authority'. Chapter 10.2's own row is 'Motor vehicle statistics, Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt', which is the agency plus a category. A node could be forced through the matcher by titling it 'Registration statistics', which the body would run-match — but that is not a title the publisher uses, and §7c says a node carries the publisher's own title. KBA's German pages name the products Neuzulassungen (new registrations, https://www.kba.de/DE/Statistik/Fahrzeuge/Neuzulassungen/neuzulassungen_node.html, 200 this round) and Besitzumschreibungen (change of ownership, 200 this round), and its English site has no statistics section naming either. So the honest position is: two distinct KBA products, the inventory citing them as one undifferentiated agency source, and no publisher's-own English title to carry. Reopen it by minting the two KBA products from KBA's own pages FIRST and wiring the inventory to them second — not by inventing an English title to satisfy the run rule.

reports.title: Loi n°174/AN/02/4ème L du 7 juillet 2002 portant décentralisation et statut des régions
reports.description: Djibouti's national décentralisation law, creating the country's five régional collectivités territoriales. Article 2, verbatim: "Il est crée en République de Djibouti cinq collectivités territoriales régionales dénommées : Régions d'Arta, d'Ali Sabieh, de Dikhil, d'Obock et de Tadjourah...". Article 80, verbatim (on régional budget composition): "Le budget de la région est composé : Des dotations et transferts de État / Des ressources fiscales / Des produits de l'exploitation des services et domaines..." [the article "l'" before "État" is missing in this extraction — likely a PDF-extraction artifact of the mirror copy rather than a genuine textual variant; flagged for a cleaner-OCR re-check]. Article 93, verbatim: "Une dotation globale sera consentie par État pour assurer le fonctionnement des régions décentralisées" — the textual basis for the state-to-région fiscal-transfer mechanism (literal future-tense "sera consentie" in the original French; treated as prescriptive/statutory language per corpus convention). Article 4, verbatim: "Les Districts et Région d'Arta, dans leurs limites territoriales, ne comprennent pas Djibouti-Ville qui fera l'objet d'un statut spécial..." — the textual link establishing that Djibouti-Ville is carved out of the régional system and separately governed by its own statute (later enacted as Loi n°122/AN/05, see dj-loi-122-2005-ville-statut). Corroborated by Djibouti's own e-government portal (egouv.dj), which independently paraphrases the same law and states in its own text: "La région est dotée de la personnalité morale et de l'autonomie financière" [source rendering showed an encoding artifact in place of the apostrophes; corrected here] — though that portal's régional population figures for the same nominal 2021 reference year disagree with figures on presidence.dj (see _dropped note below, not resolved this round).
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument (organic decentralization law).

reports.title: Loi n°122/AN/05/5ème L du 1er novembre 2005 portant statut de la Ville de Djibouti
reports.description: Djibouti-Ville's own organic statute law, fetched directly from the Ministère Délégué Chargé de la Décentralisation's own .gouv.dj domain. Article 2, verbatim (defining the city's three communes): "La ville de Djibouti comprend trois communes : - la commune dénommée «Ras-Dika» dont le territoire correspond à celui du 6ème Arrondissement, - la commune appelée «Boulaos» recouvre l'ensemble des territoires de premier, deuxième et troisième arrondissement, - et la commune dite «Balbala» sous le nom duquel se regroupent les territoires du 4ème et du 5ème arrondissement." Article 99, verbatim (on the Conseil de Djibouti's budget composition): "Le budget du Conseil de Djibouti est composé : - des donations et transferts de l'État ; - des ressources fiscales locales ; - des produits de l'exploitation des services et domaines ; - des taxes rémunératrices sur les services rendus ; - des participations des autres collectivités ; - des produits financiers ; - des produits de dons, legs et subventions ; - des produits de l'aliénation des biens de la collectivité." This is a direct structural analogue to the régions' Article 80 in Loi n°174/AN/02 (dj-loi-174-2002-decentralisation) — the same enumeration pattern/order, evidencing a consistent national budget-composition template across both régional and Djibouti-Ville tiers. Also confirmed on the same page: the budget must be voted "avant le 1er janvier" of the fiscal year, accounts reported by July 1, and deficits exceeding 5% of operating revenue trigger court intervention; Article 52 gives the Council authority to set local taxes within legal limits.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument (organic municipal statute).

reports.title: Loi n°107/AN/00/4ème L du 29 octobre 2000 relative aux lois des Finances
reports.description: Djibouti's organic public-finance/budget law, as described on the Ministère du Budget's own site (budget.gouv.dj). Verbatim quote on scope: "Elle s'applique à l'État, aux collectivités régionales et aux établissements publiques" [sic, "établissements publiques" as printed on the source page] — establishing that this organic law's public-accounting rules apply to régional collectivités as well as the État, the general statutory framework that the Plans de Développement Régional (see dj-pdr-* series) and Loi 174's Article 80/93 budget provisions sit underneath. Article 1, verbatim: "fixe les règles fondamentales relatives à la nature, au contenu, à la procédure d'élaboration, de présentation et d'adoption des lois de finances." Article 4 identifies three types of finance laws: loi de finances de l'année (initiale), loi de finances rectificative, and loi de règlement.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument (organic finance law).

reports.description: Government-authored five-year regional development/budget plan for Obock, one of the five régions created by Loi n°174/AN/02 (dj-loi-174-2002-decentralisation). Revenue table, TOTAL by year, verbatim as extracted: "152 505 000 Fdj 169 645 000 Fdj 149 645 000 Fdj 59 645 000 Fdj 59 645 000 Fdj 591 085 000 Fdj" (2021-2025 figures followed by the grand total). Implementation-status admission, verbatim: "à ce jour, seule celle de l'Etat Civil est réellement effective au niveau du Chef-lieu" — a rare, directly quotable primary-government admission that of the nine competencies formally decentralized to régional councils by decree in 2007, only civil-status registration is actually operative, and only at the chef-lieu (regional capital), not in sub-prefectures — a candid, present-tense statement of the gap between Djibouti's decentralization law-on-paper and its practice.

dependencies.basis: Loi n°174/AN/02 Article 4 explicitly anticipates and names Djibouti-Ville's carve-out from the régional system: "...Djibouti-Ville qui fera l'objet d'un statut spécial." Loi n°122/AN/05, enacted three years later, is precisely that special statute — the two laws share the same subject entity (Djibouti-Ville) and a direct sequential textual reference from the earlier law to the later one.

The Tadjourah PDR's financial mobilization table includes a named, quantified "Dotation de l'État" line item (270 000 000 FDJ, ~41% of total mobilized resources) that is the region's own budgeted instantiation of the "dotation globale" state-to-région fiscal-transfer mechanism created by Loi n°174/AN/02 Article 93 ("Une dotation globale sera consentie par État pour assurer le fonctionnement des régions décentralisées").

The Conseil Régional Ali-Sabieh, author/subject of this PDR, is one of the five régional collectivités territoriales explicitly created by name in Loi n°174/AN/02 Article 2 ("...Régions d'Arta, d'Ali Sabieh, de Dikhil, d'Obock et de Tadjourah"); the PDR is a planning/budget product of that legally-created entity.

The Conseil Régional de Dikhil, author/subject of this PDR, is one of the five régional collectivités territoriales explicitly created by name in Loi n°174/AN/02 Article 2; the PDR is a planning/budget product of that legally-created entity.

The Conseil Régional d'Obock, author/subject of this PDR, is one of the five régional collectivités territoriales explicitly created by name in Loi n°174/AN/02 Article 2; the PDR is a planning/budget product of that legally-created entity.

Djibouti's March 2023 PEFA public-finance-management assessment ("RÉPUBLIQUE DE DJIBOUTI — ÉVALUATION DE LA PERFORMANCE DU SYSTEME DE GESTION DES FINANCES PUBLIQUES SUIVANT LA METHODOLOGIE PEFA," URL: https://www.pefa.org/sites/pefa/files/2023-07/DJ-Mar23-PFMPR-Public%20with%20PEFA%20Check.pdf) verbatim-confirms the '6 collectivités territoriales = 5 régions + Djibouti-Ville' structure already independently established via Loi 174 Article 2 and Loi 122 ("Les collectivités territoriales au nombre de 6 comprennent 5 régions et la ville de Djibouti composée de trois communes"), but per its own framing was prepared 'at the request of the Government of Djibouti and financed by the World Bank, European Union and French Development Agency' with PEFA Secretariat quality assurance — mixed authorship, not a clean primary-government document per this branch's evidence rule. reports.title: Loi n°149/AN/11/6ème L du 8 décembre 2011 portant modification de la loi n°174/AN/02/4ème L portant décentralisation et statut des régions et de l'article 6 de la Loi n°122/AN/05/5ème L portant sur le statut de la ville de Djibouti
reports.description: Djibouti's 2011 amendment law, restructuring regional and Djibouti-Ville council terminology, composition and governance rather than fiscal mechanics. Title/promulgation, verbatim: "Loi n°149/AN/11/6ème L portant modification de la loi n°174/AN/02/4ème L portant décentralisation et statut des régions et de l'article 6 de la Loi n°122/AN/05/5ème L portant sur le statut de la ville de Djibouti. L'ASSEMBLEE NATIONALE A ADOPTE LE PRESIDENT DE LA REPUBLIQUE PROMULGUE LA LOI DONT LA TENEUR SUIT :". Preamble (VU clauses), verbatim: "VU La Constitution du 15 septembre 1992 ; VU La Loi n°92/AN/10/6ème L portant révision de la Constitution ; VU La Loi n°174/AN/02/4ème L portant décentralisation et statut des régions ; VU La Loi n°122/AN/05/5ème L portant sur le statut de la ville de Djibouti ; VU La Loi n°139/AN/06/5ème L modifiant la Loi n°174/AN/02/4èmeL portant décentralisation et statut des régions ; ... Le Conseil des Ministres entendu en sa séance du 15 novembre 2011." Article 1, verbatim: "Le terme «Assemblée Régionale» contenu dans la Loi n°174/AN/02/4ème L est modifié par «Conseil Régional»." Article 2, verbatim (adding an alinéa to Loi 122/AN/05 Article 6): "Il est ajouté un alinéa supplémentaire à l'article 6 de la Loi n°122/AN/05/5ème L portant sur le statut de la Ville de Djibouti ... Le nombre de membres de chaque conseil est calculé sur la base d'un élu pour mille (1000) électeurs inscrits ... Le Conseil communal est composé de neuf (9) élus au minimum." Article 4, verbatim (replacing Loi 174/AN/02 Article 7): "L'article 7 de la loi n°174/AN/02/4ème L est modifié ainsi : «Le Conseil régional, composé de conseillères et de conseillers régionaux élus, est l'organe chargé de formuler les politiques et d'agir comme un corps délibérant au niveau de la région. Le conseil élit en son sein un bureau composé d'un président, d'un vice-président et de deux secrétaires.»" Article 24 (execution clause), verbatim: "La présente Loi sera exécutée et publiée au Journal Officiel de la République de Djibouti dès sa promulgation. Fait à Djibouti, le 08 décembre 2011 Le Président de la République, chef du Gouvernement ISMAÏL OMAR GUELLEH." Confirms this is a two-parent amendment: it modifies both dj-loi-174-2002-decentralisation (multiple articles, including Articles 1, 3-24) and dj-loi-122-2005-ville-statut (Article 6). NOTE ON DOMAIN SCOPE: the quoted operative articles (1, 2, 4) restructure council terminology, composition and internal governance/bureau structure, not fiscal formulas or budget composition — unlike Article 80/93 of Loi 174 or Article 99 of Loi 122 (see those nodes' own descriptions), no finance/budget article of either target law is quoted here. ACCESS-METHOD CAVEAT: the government's own domain (decentralisation.gouv.dj) still has a broken TLS certificate chain for direct tooling access, confirmed again this round — the text above was retrieved via a text-extraction reader-proxy (r.jina.ai) fetching the exact government URL, then cross-validated against an independent WebFetch AI-summarization pass of the same URL, which matched verbatim wherever both quoted the same passage; treated as reliable, not hallucinated, but the underlying access constraint is unresolved and would block any future attempt at direct verbatim re-extraction. A secondary academic source (Rochegude & Plançon, "Cadre juridique et institutionnel — Djibouti," Comité technique Foncier & développement, June 2023) independently quotes Articles 1 and 4 near-verbatim (one tiny wording difference: "modifié comme suit" vs. the government PDF's actual "modifié ainsi"), used here only as a cross-check that the primary text is not fabricated — not cited as this node's evidentiary URL.

meta.note: First mints from the DSBB option-E worklist (Claude outputs/dsbb-pilot-2026-09-09/e-slice-tier1.json), on Thomas's 2026-09-09 ruling: take only the pairs whose IMF Summary of Methodology names the country's OWN publication by title, so the node is minted on a named publication rather than on a DSBB category label. Each node's title comes from the SoM's dissemination sentence and was then CONFIRMED against the publisher's own site, which is also what supplies `url` and the cadence — no node here rests on the SoM alone. Two of the four Eastern Caribbean candidates are minted; the other two are in _dropped with the reason, and both are host problems rather than evidence problems. NOT wired, deliberately: the MET00 rows for Dominica, Grenada, St Kitts and St Vincent each name SITC Rev.3 alongside HS and would suit the `sitc` node minted earlier today, but their SoMs name no publication for the trade series, so under option E they have no source node to hang on. Saint Vincent's own Annual Trade Report exists on the Office's publications page — but the SoM does not name it, and pairing them would be this researcher's inference, which is the exact source-match error the 2026-09-05 DSBB review flagged. Left as a lead. EDITION NOTE: both quotes name ISIC Rev 3.1 while `isic` is a family-level node; that is the corpus's established shape for ISIC (see `ar-scn -> isic`, minted on 'ISIC Revision 3.1' in the 2026-09-05 import) and is not a new call. JURISDICTION_LEVEL: 'federal', which is this corpus's value for a national-level publisher — there is no 'national' in the JurisdictionLevel union and 2,429 existing nodes use 'federal' for exactly this, including Jamaica's and Trinidad's national releases. Recorded because the word reads wrong for a unitary Caribbean state and the next person will wonder. meta.source: research round 2026-09-09 (round 34) — DSBB option-E slice, second batch
meta.note: Continues the option-E worklist begun in round 33. Same bar: the IMF Summary of Methodology must NAME the country's own publication, and the publisher's own site must then CONFIRM it and supply the url and cadence. Three minted here (Kyrgyzstan, Azerbaijan, Moldova); the candidates that failed the second half are in _dropped, and the reasons are worth reading because none of them is an evidence failure. AZERBAIJAN, A CHECK WORTH RECORDING: its quote is the DQAF-shaped sentence 'The methodological soundness dimension is assessed against the guidelines outlined in...', which reads like framework boilerplate and would be worthless if it were. It is not — grepping all 684 cached SoMs for that phrase returns exactly ONE file, Azerbaijan's own. Checked rather than assumed, because if it had turned up in two hundred countries the edge would have been the IMF's template talking, not Azerbaijan. All three quotes were confirmed unique across the 684-file cache the same way. MOLDOVA, ONE EDGE NOT TWO: BOP00 and IIP00 both name BPM6 and both resolve to the same yearbook, which would be a duplicate (source, target) pair; the BOP00 quote is the stronger of the two (it names the manual in full) and is the one wired. No registry work this round — KG, AZ and MD were already in regions.ts and palette.ts, unlike round 33's DM and VC.

_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Algeria is the first of three North Africa countries researched this session (AF/G.9 priority 1) -- Morocco and Tunisia alongside it, Libya researched separately after being retested rather than assumed thin. Researched by a subagent this session against the branch's full Research.1.md discipline; several official Algerian domains (dz.cnr.dz, dgfp.gov.dz) refused or reset direct connections, so some findings rest on Wayback Machine snapshots or news-outlet quotations of Journal Officiel text rather than a direct primary fetch -- flagged inline and in _open_questions. Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review, following the established DRAFT-then-import pattern.
_note: Algeria's own CPI documents are explicit about NOT following the frameworks this branch has come to expect: three ONS bulletins spanning 2013-2026 all classify goods and services 'conformément à la classification conseillée par les Nations Unies dans le système de comptabilité nationale de 1970' -- the 1970 UN system of national accounts, not COICOP 2018 and not even SNA 2008. The IMF's own 2025 Article IV report draws the same distinction sharply: Algeria's national accounts WERE rebased in December 2023 to follow the 2008 SNA, but the CPI is a separate ONS product that still runs on 2000-survey weights the IMF itself calls 'severely outdated.' On pensions, the CNR's own 2018 and 2026 revaluation announcements both frame pension increases as presidential/ministerial decisions under a wage-actualisation article (Loi 83-12, Art. 43) rather than a price-indexation formula -- and a named CASNOS official, quoted on the record by a Chatham House research paper, states that a comparable social-insurance benefit (health-insurance reimbursement tariffs) 'has not been updated for almost 40 years,' explicitly invoking inflation as the cause of erosion. A secondary legal-commentary source's claim that the minimum wage (SNMG) is set partly by reference to the CPI could not be corroborated against the primary decree text, which contains no such formula -- reported as an unresolved conflict rather than minted as an edge.

_open_questions.question: The CNR's own site (dz.cnr.dz) and the pension ministry site (dgfp.gov.dz) both refused or reset connections this session. Article 43 of Loi 83-12's full statutory language was read only as quoted secondhand in news reporting of the 2018 and 2026 arrêtés, not directly from the Journal Officiel or CNR's own text.

A private legal-commentary site (legal-doctrine.com) claims the SNMG (minimum wage) is set partly by reference to 'l'indice des prix à la consommation,' but the claim is internally inconsistent (cites 'trois principes' and lists two) and the primary decree (Décret exécutif n° 15-59 du 8 février 2015) contains no such formula in the text this session could access. Worth checking Loi n° 90-11's Article 87 and the 2015 finance law directly.

The ISSA country profile for Algeria (issa.int) blocked direct PDF download (403) both with and without a browser user-agent; its corroborating quote on CNR/CNAS benefit adjustment came through a WebFetch read of the live page only, not independently verified against raw bytes the way the SSA.gov quote was.

reports.title: Indice des Prix à la Consommation
reports.description: Algeria's official monthly Consumer Price Index bulletin. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via the May 2026 edition (No. 365), cross-checked against 2012 and 2016 editions for stability of wording. 'L'année de base est 2000 et l'année de référence (100 pour les calculs) est 2001... Formule de calcul de l'indice: I m/2001 = Σi (w i / Σi w i)(p m i / p 2001 i)' (a Laspeyres-type weighted arithmetic mean). Classification is 'proche de celle recommandée (par l'ONU) dans le système de comptabilité nationale de 1970' -- explicitly the 1970 UN system of national accounts, not COICOP 2018. All three editions read (2012, 2016, 2026) were searched in full for 'COICOP', 'Manuel'/'FMI', 'SCN 2008', 'Arabe' and 'Maghreb' -- none appear anywhere.

release_schedule.note: ONS Algeria's own 2025 publication calendar (Calendrier des Publications Année 2025) shows the CPI (IPC) released monthly with roughly a one-month lag: e.g. December 2024 data -> released January 2025; January 2025 -> February 2025; February -> March; March -> April; April -> May; May -> June; June -> July; July -> August; August -> September; September -> October 2025 (all documented rows in that PDF). However, the ONS homepage's latest actual news item (dated 26/7/2026) announces the May 2026 IPC release (matching the corpus's existing IPC_mai2026.pdf), which is a ~2-month lag from the reference month, indicating the cadence has slipped from the nominal 1-month lag seen in the 2025 calendar. No 2026 calendar PDF was found on the site (only 'Calendrier des Publications Année 2025' is linked), so future dates are projected from the most recently observed real cadence (2-month lag) rather than taken from a published 2026 calendar.

reports.title: Arrêté portant revalorisation des pensions et allocations de retraite
reports.publisher: Ministère du Travail, de l'Emploi et de la Sécurité Sociale / Caisse Nationale des Retraites (CNR), Algeria
reports.description: Annual ministerial order revaluing CNR old-age pensions under Article 43 of Loi 83-12 du 2 juillet 1983. VERIFIED via news reporting of the Journal Officiel text (direct CNR/JORT access blocked this session -- see _open_questions). The 2018 arrêté set tiered fixed percentages by pension-amount bracket (5% below 20,000 DA down to 0.5% at or above 80,000 DA); the 2026 CNR Director-General confirmed the pattern continues, framing it explicitly as 'application des instructions du président de la République... conformément aux dispositions de l'article 43 de la loi 83-12 relative à l'actualisation des salaires servant de base au calcul de la pension' -- an administrative wage-base updating mechanism, not a CPI formula. Corroborated by the SSA/ISSA country profile: 'Benefits are adjusted annually on May 1 by ministerial decree.'

release_schedule.note: Algeria's pension/allowance revaluation is grounded in Article 43 of Law n°83-12 of 2 July 1983 on retirement (as amended), which establishes the annual revaluation mechanism, but the law text itself does not fix a specific calendar date. In practice, the Ministry of Labour/CNR has consistently issued an annual arrêté setting the revaluation effective as of 1 May each year (2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 all confirmed at 1 May), even though the order's signature date and the actual payment date (which has varied: mid-May, June, first week of May) differ year to year. The 2026 order was dated 16 April 2026 and effective 1 May 2026, matching the pattern; the next occurrence is projected for 1 May 2027 by extrapolation of this pattern, not from a published calendar or an explicit statutory date.

reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (Journal Officiel N° 08, hosted via ILO NATLEX). Issued under Article 87 of Loi n° 90-11 du 21 avril 1990, the decree's three articles define only which pay components count toward the SNMG (national guaranteed minimum wage) -- base salary plus certain bonuses, excluding others. Searched in full for 'indice des prix', 'inflation', 'coût de la vie': none appear. Contradicts a private legal-commentary site's claim (unresolved, see _open_questions) that the SNMG is set partly by reference to the CPI.

reports.title: Algeria: 2025 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report
reports.description: IMF Country Report No. 25/270. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Annex XI ('Data Issues') states Algeria's CPI weights are 'based on a 2000 household survey and severely outdated, which could lead to errors in the measurement of inflation,' while separately confirming Algeria's national accounts (a distinct ONS product) 'have been rebased in December 2023 with 2001 as a base year, and now follow the 2008 SNA recommendations.' Also states: 'Algeria participates in the Enhanced General Data Dissemination (e-GDDS) and first posted its metadata in April 2009 but is yet to disseminate the data recommend[ed] under the e-GDDS.'

No ONS CPI document mentions COICOP anywhere.

IMF Country Report 25/270 confirms it is Algeria's national accounts, not the CPI, that were rebased in Dec. 2023 to follow 2008 SNA. The CPI's own classification remains tied to the 1970 system of national accounts through the May 2026 release.
Full-text search of the ONS CPI methodology documents (2012, 2016, 2026 editions) for 'Manuel', 'FMI', 'IMF' found no reference to the IMF CPI Manual anywhere.

_dropped.edge: dz-ons-ipc-monthly cites an Arab/Maghreb regional statistical body
_dropped.why: No ONS CPI document accessed this session mentions AITRS/AITSR, the Arab Monetary Fund, or the Union du Maghreb Arabe. No new regional node is proposed.

Both the 2018 arrêté and the 2026 CNR statement frame the revaluation as a fixed, tiered percentage set by ministerial arrêté 'en application des instructions du président de la République', under Article 43 of Loi 83-12 (which governs updating of the wage base used in the pension formula, not indexation of the pension payment to a price index). No document ties the percentage to CPI/inflation. Corroborated by SSA's SSPTW Algeria profile: 'Benefits are adjusted annually on May 1 by ministerial decree.'

_dropped.edge: CASNOS/CNAS health-insurance reimbursement tariffs indexed to CPI
_dropped.why: A named CASNOS official, quoted on the record by a Chatham House research paper, states reimbursement tariffs have 'not been updated for almost 40 years' and that 'with the rate of inflation experienced by the country during this long period... the level of reimbursement is insignificant' -- an explicit admission of erosion with no adjustment mechanism, CPI-based or otherwise. Corroborated by an academic paper hosted on cnese.dz (Algeria's own National Economic, Social and Environmental Council site) citing medical-procedure reimbursement 'sur la base des tarifs de 1987'.

The primary decree (Décret exécutif n° 15-59, Journal Officiel N° 08) contains no CPI/inflation reference anywhere in its text -- it only defines which pay components count toward the SNMG. A secondary legal-commentary site (legal-doctrine.com) claims the SNMG is set per 'l'indice des prix à la consommation' among 'trois principes' but the claim is internally inconsistent (lists only two) and unsupported by the primary decree text accessed this session. Reported as an unresolved conflict, not asserted as a real edge.

reports.title: Encuesta Nacional de Empleo, Desempleo y Subempleo (ENEMDU)
reports.description: Continuous household survey that is the primary source for labour-market indicators (adequate employment, underemployment, unemployment) and for income-based poverty and inequality measurement. National, urban and rural domains.
reports._notes: Central social and labour survey. Monthly and quarterly releases. Official source for both labour statistics and monetary poverty. Recent (Dec 2025): national poverty 21.4%, extreme poverty 8.3%; unemployment ~2.6–3.6%.

reports.title: Pobreza por ingresos y pobreza extrema / Income poverty
reports.description: Official income-poverty and extreme-poverty incidence, calculated by comparing household per-capita income (from ENEMDU) with nationally defined poverty lines updated by the IPC. Published with urban/rural breakdowns.
reports._notes: Headline social indicator. Dec 2025: national poverty 21.4% (down sharply from 28.0% a year earlier); extreme poverty 8.3%. Large urban–rural gap (urban ~13.8%, rural ~37.6%).

reports.title: Líneas de pobreza y pobreza extrema
reports.description: Monetary values of the poverty and extreme-poverty lines (per capita), updated with the IPC.
reports._notes: Direct input into the poverty measurement. Dec 2025: poverty line ~USD 92.40 per person; extreme poverty line ~USD 52.07.

reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) / Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index measuring changes in the prices of a representative basket of goods and services.
reports._notes: Flagship price statistic. Used to update the poverty lines and as the primary inflation indicator for the dollarized economy and for BCE analysis.

reports.title: Cuentas Nacionales / National Accounts of Ecuador
reports.description: System of national accounts producing GDP by production, expenditure and income. Quarterly and annual releases.
reports._notes: Core macroeconomic statistical system. In Ecuador the Banco Central plays a larger role in national accounts compilation than in pure INEI/DANE-style systems.

reports.title: Empleo adecuado / pleno empleo (ENEMDU)
reports.description: Key labour-market indicator from ENEMDU measuring the share of the employed who work full-time at or above the minimum wage. Central quality-of-employment metric in the Ecuadorian system.
reports._notes: Distinctive Ecuadorian labour indicator. Dec 2025: national adequate employment 37.1% (up from 33.0% a year earlier). Large urban–rural gap (urban ~46%, rural ~20%).

reports.title: Censo de Población y Vivienda / Population and Housing Census
reports.description: Decennial population and housing census. Provides the demographic baseline and sampling frames for household surveys.
reports._notes: Foundational demographic product. Continuously cited by ENEMDU design and poverty analysis.

reports.title: Coeficiente de Gini / Income inequality
reports.description: Official Gini coefficient of income inequality, calculated from the same ENEMDU income concept used for monetary poverty.
reports._notes: Companion inequality indicator to the poverty series. Recent values in the mid-0.44 to 0.47 range.

reports.title: Balanza de Pagos / Balance of Payments
reports.description: Quarterly and annual balance of payments covering the current account, capital/financial account and changes in reserve assets.
reports._notes: Core external-accounts product. 2025 current-account surplus reached a historical high of ~USD 7.7 bn, driven by the goods surplus and secondary income (remittances).

reports.title: Estadísticas de Comercio Exterior / Merchandise Trade
reports.description: Monthly and annual statistics of exports and imports of goods, with a sharp analytical split between oil and non-oil trade.
reports._notes: Trade data feed the BOP and national accounts. Non-oil exports (shrimp, cocoa, banana, mining) have become the main growth engine; oil remains important but has lost relative weight.

reports.title: Exportaciones e ingresos petroleros / Oil exports & fiscal contribution
reports.description: Statistics of crude-oil and derivatives production, exports and related fiscal revenues. Historically the dominant export and a major source of public revenue.
reports._notes: Structural but declining relative weight. 2025 oil exports ~USD 7.8 bn (down ~19% year-on-year). Still a key fiscal and external-sector variable, but non-oil exports now exceed oil by a wide margin.

reports.title: Exportaciones no petroleras (camarón, cacao, banano, minería)
reports.description: Non-oil merchandise exports, led by shrimp, cocoa & elaborates, banana/plantain and mining products. Principal recent driver of the trade surplus and of export diversification.
reports._notes: 2025 non-oil exports ~USD 29.4 bn (+18%). Shrimp, cocoa and banana are the headline traditional non-oil lines; mining has also grown. Central to the narrative of export diversification under dollarization.

reports.title: Reservas Internacionales del Banco Central del Ecuador
reports.description: Stock of international reserves managed by the central bank. Critical liquidity buffer in a fully dollarized economy.
reports._notes: Key external-buffer indicator under dollarization. End-2025 reserves reached record levels (~USD 9.8 bn). Cover deposits of the financial system and provide confidence in the dollarized regime.

reports.title: Régimen de dolarización oficial (desde 2000)
reports.publisher: Banco Central del Ecuador / Marco legal
reports.description: Official dollarization of the Ecuadorian economy (US dollar as legal tender since 2000). Defines the monetary regime: no independent national currency or classic policy interest rate.
reports._notes: Foundational institutional regime node. Continuously cited as the framework that constrains monetary policy and elevates the importance of fiscal discipline, reserves and external competitiveness.
_referenced_by: Every major BCE macroeconomic and monetary report
Analysis of inflation, reserves and financial stability

reports.title: Índice Nacional de Precios al Productor (INPP)
reports.description: Monthly producer price index, published with and without oil. Measures price changes at the producer level across agriculture, mining, manufacturing and utilities.
reports._notes: Complements the IPC. The oil/non-oil split mirrors the trade and production analysis. Useful for cost-push and industrial-price monitoring.

reports.title: Canasta Familiar Básica y Canasta Familiar Vital
reports.description: Official cost of the basic and vital family baskets, published monthly with the IPC. Used for living-cost and wage-reference analysis.
reports._notes: High-visibility living-cost indicator. Linked to the IPC and frequently cited in wage and social-policy discussion.

reports.title: Remesas de trabajadores / Secondary income (remittances)
reports.description: Statistics of worker remittances received from abroad. Major component of the secondary-income account and a stabilising factor in the balance of payments.
reports._notes: Structurally important inflow. Contributed to the record current-account surplus in 2025. Complements the goods-trade surplus in the external accounts.

reports.title: Camarón, cacao y banano — leading non-oil export products
reports.description: Product-level export statistics for the three largest non-oil traditional export lines: shrimp, cocoa & elaborates, and banana/plantain.
reports._notes: These three products dominate non-oil traditional exports. Shrimp has overtaken oil in some recent periods as the single largest export earner; cocoa has seen exceptional value growth.

reports.title: Quito / Distrito Metropolitano de Quito — capital statistical identity
reports.description: Capital city and primary highland urban economy. Core of Pichincha province. Lower income-poverty incidence than the national average.
reports._notes: Dominant highland metro. Pichincha records among the lowest provincial income-poverty rates (~11%). Continuously published as a key urban domain in ENEMDU labour and poverty analysis.

reports.title: Guayaquil / Área metropolitana de Guayaquil — coastal statistical identity
reports.description: Largest coastal city and main commercial/port economy. Core of Guayas province. Intermediate-to-higher poverty incidence relative to the capital.
reports._notes: Dominant coastal metro. Guayas carries a large absolute number of poor households. Completes the capital–port-city contrast inside the national urban hierarchy.

reports.title: Provincia de Pichincha — low-poverty contrast
reports.description: Highland province containing Quito. Among the lowest income-poverty rates in the 2025 provincial results.
reports._notes: 2025 income poverty ~11.2%. Completes the low-poverty pole opposite the Amazonian and some coastal provinces.

reports.title: Provincia de Morona Santiago — highest-poverty Amazon contrast
reports.description: Amazonian province with the highest income-poverty incidence in recent provincial results. Tests the statistical hierarchy under extreme marginalisation.
reports._notes: Poverty-contrast province. 2025 income poverty reported in the mid-70% range; also among the highest in multidimensional and NBI poverty. National survey infrastructure reaches the province; local independent statistical density is thin.

reports.title: Provincia de Orellana — high-poverty Amazon contrast
reports.description: Amazonian oil-producing province that previously recorded the highest poverty rates and saw a sharp decline in 2025.
reports._notes: 2025 income poverty fell dramatically (from ~76% to ~44%). Illustrates both the high-poverty Amazon cluster and the volatility of provincial estimates in smaller domains.

reports.title: Pobreza por ingresos por provincia (INEC)
reports.description: Official provincial tabulations of income poverty and related indicators. Primary source for the inter-provincial poverty gradient.
reports._notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2025 ranking extremes: Morona Santiago highest; Tungurahua and Pichincha among the lowest (~11%). National average ~21.8%.

reports.title: Presupuesto General del Estado / National Budget
reports.description: Annual national budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues (including oil) and expenditure of the central government.
reports._notes: Operational fiscal framework. Links oil and non-oil revenues with functional spending on education, health, social protection and investment. Critical under dollarization because monetary financing is constrained.

reports.title: Cuentas Satélite de Educación (CSE)
reports.description: Satellite accounts of education measuring the value added, expenditure and production of the education sector (public and private). Complements the national accounts with a sectoral view of education.
reports._notes: 2024 education VAB ~5.5% of GDP (USD 6.8 bn). Higher education is the largest single industry within the satellite. Links the education budget to the real-side accounts.

reports.title: Encuesta Nacional de Ingresos y Gastos de los Hogares (ENIGHUR)
reports.description: Periodic household income and expenditure survey. Updates the structure of household consumption, provides the weights for the IPC, and supports living-conditions and inequality analysis.
reports._notes: Structural survey (latest 2024-2025 after a 12-year gap). Average monthly household income ~USD 1,135; expenditure ~USD 930. Directly feeds the IPC basket and complements ENEMDU on the expenditure side.

reports.title: Pobreza por Necesidades Básicas Insatisfechas (NBI)
reports.description: Structural poverty indicator based on unsatisfied basic needs (housing quality, overcrowding, access to services, education, economic dependence). Calculated primarily from census data and updated with survey information.
reports._notes: Complementary structural poverty measure to income poverty. 2022 census: 39.8% of the population with at least one NBI. Provincial extremes remain large (Amazonian provinces highest).

reports.title: Instituto Ecuatoriano de Seguridad Social (IESS) — coverage and finances
reports.description: Main social-security institution covering pensions, health insurance and other benefits for formal workers and their dependents. Major fiscal counterpart and health-system actor.
reports._notes: Central social-protection node. Large and growing claims on the national budget (state contribution to pensions and health). Continuously cited in fiscal and health-system analysis; historical arrears are a recurring policy issue.

reports.title: Sistema de salud pública / Ministry of Health statistics
reports.description: Public-health service statistics, coverage indicators and related expenditure. Complements IESS and household-survey health modules.
reports._notes: Public provider side of the dual health system (MSP + IESS). Linked to the health functional budget and to household access indicators from ENEMDU/ENIGHUR.

reports.title: Gasto público en educación
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / INEC CSE
reports.description: Public expenditure on education as reflected in the national budget and in the education satellite accounts.
reports._notes: Education is a constitutionally prioritised function. CSE and budget execution together track the resource side of the education system.

reports.title: Gasto público en salud y seguridad social
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / IESS
reports.description: Public expenditure on health and social security, including the state contribution to IESS pensions and health benefits.
reports._notes: Health and social-security spending are major and growing budget items. The state–IESS financing relationship is a structural fiscal issue under dollarization.

reports.title: Encuesta Nacional sobre Desnutrición Infantil (ENDI)
reports.description: Specialised survey on child malnutrition, early childhood development and related household conditions. Complements the broader health and living-conditions system.
reports._notes: High-priority social indicator survey. Tracks chronic malnutrition and early-childhood development outcomes; used for targeted social-policy monitoring.

reports.title: Provincia de Tungurahua — low-poverty highland contrast
reports.description: Highland province with among the lowest income-poverty rates in the 2025 results. Completes the low-poverty set alongside Pichincha.
reports._notes: 2025 income poverty ~11%. Useful as a second low-poverty highland node.

reports.title: Provincia de Manabí — large coastal province
reports.description: Major coastal province with elevated poverty and a large absolute number of poor households. Completes the coastal provincial set alongside Guayas.
reports._notes: Significant coastal population and poverty mass. Frequently appears in both absolute and relative poverty rankings.

reports.title: Camarón — producción y exportaciones
reports.publisher: Cámara Nacional de Acuacultura / BCE / INEC
reports.description: Statistics of shrimp aquaculture production and exports. Ecuador’s leading export product by value, surpassing oil in recent years. Concentrated in Guayas and other coastal provinces.
reports._notes: Structural export success story. 2025 exports reached record levels (~USD 8.4 bn), overtaking oil as the single largest export earner. ~225–230k hectares in production; major employment generator (especially female labour). China, EU and US are the main markets.

reports.title: Sector acuícola / Aquaculture statistics
reports.publisher: Cámara Nacional de Acuacultura / MAG / BCE
reports.description: Broader aquaculture sector statistics, dominated by shrimp but also covering other cultured species. Complements the product-level shrimp series.
reports._notes: Industry association and official statistics track production area, employment, export volumes and values. Guayas accounts for ~60% of shrimp production area.

reports.title: Servicio de Rentas Internas (SRI) — tax collection
reports.description: National tax administration. Publishes gross tax collection by type of tax (VAT, income tax, ICE, etc.) and performance against annual targets.
reports._notes: Primary non-oil revenue-side fiscal statistic. 2025 collection ~USD 21.5 bn (record). VAT is the largest single tax. Critical under dollarization because monetary financing is unavailable.

reports.title: Impuesto al Valor Agregado (IVA) / Value-added tax
reports.description: Main consumption tax. Rate and base changes are high-visibility fiscal policy instruments; collection is published monthly by the SRI.
reports._notes: Largest single tax revenue. Recent rate/base adjustments (including expansion of the taxable base) have been material drivers of collection growth.

reports.title: Deuda pública / Public debt statistics
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / BCE
reports.description: Stock and flow statistics of central-government and public-sector debt (external and domestic). Key sustainability indicator under dollarization.
reports._notes: Critical fiscal-sustainability node. Continuously monitored because dollarization removes the option of monetary financing of deficits.

reports.title: Provincia de El Oro — shrimp and coastal production
reports.description: Coastal province that is the second-largest shrimp-producing area after Guayas. Completes the coastal aquaculture geography.
reports._notes: ~15% of national shrimp production area. Links the commodity (shrimp) to the provincial production and poverty geography.

reports.title: Provincia de Esmeraldas — northern coastal contrast
reports.description: Northern coastal province with elevated poverty and a significant share of shrimp and other coastal production.
reports._notes: Elevated poverty incidence relative to the highland core. Completes the set of major coastal provinces (Guayas, Manabí, El Oro, Esmeraldas).

reports.title: Cacao y elaborados — producción y exportaciones
reports.description: Statistics of cocoa production and exports (beans and elaborates). One of the three leading non-oil traditional export products alongside shrimp and banana.
reports._notes: Strong recent value growth. Completes the product-level view of the non-oil traditional export triad (shrimp–cocoa–banana).

reports.title: Banano y plátano — producción y exportaciones
reports.description: Statistics of banana and plantain production and exports. Long-standing traditional export and a major employer in coastal provinces.
reports._notes: Classic traditional export. Still a large volume and value line; frequently cited alongside shrimp and cocoa in non-oil export analysis.

reports.title: Provincia del Guayas — core coastal statistical identity
reports.description: Largest coastal province, containing Guayaquil and the majority of national shrimp production area. Intermediate-to-higher poverty incidence and the largest absolute poverty mass.
reports._notes: ~60% of shrimp production area; hosts the main port and commercial economy. Completes the provincial set with the largest economic and demographic weight on the coast.

dependencies.basis: ENDI does not use Ministry of Health statistics: INEC's 'Documento Metodologico ENDI' builds its sample from the household Marco Maestro de Muestreo (2010 pre-censo plus 2011-2018 cartographic updating), and the MSP appears only as a provider of methodological/training support and blood-sampling facilities, and in the users table ('Ministerio de Salud Publica: Informacion actualizada que de cuenta del impacto de los programas'). The flow runs the other way: the MSP publishes the national chronic child malnutrition figure sourced to ENDI — 'La medicion reflejo tambien que... se ha reducido esta problematica en 3,5 %, pasando del 23,6 % de menores de dos anos con DCI al 20,1 %', from 'la primera Encuesta Especializada sobre Desnutricion Infantil (ENDI) 2022-2023... la encuesta disenada por el Instituto Ecuatoriano de Estadistica y Censos (INEC)'.

_headline: ARTICLE 9 DOES WHAT ANNEX B COULD NOT, AND STILL DOES NOT REVERSE THE ASYMMETRY. EU/slices/README.md records two binding instruments followed to the national boundary and both stopping at AGENCY ONLY — Annex XI and ESA 2010's Annex B. Annex B failed for a structural reason: it obliges DATA. Article 9 of Regulation 479/2009 obliges a DOCUMENT ('a detailed inventory of the methods, procedures and sources'), requires it to be updated, and — the nine words that matter — 'Member States shall make their inventories public.' Eurostat's own page carries a live Inventory link for every EU member state. So the supranational layer here CREATES a published national document class rather than naming an existing publication. That is a third shape, alongside the README's 'legislative layer names nobody' and G.50's 'self-regulatory layer names its sources freely'. BUT THE DIRECTION IS UNCHANGED: the Regulation still names no member state's inventory by title (AGENCY ONLY, Article 9(1)), and the edge, if it were mintable, would still run national -> EU. The asymmetry finding survives. What changes is the mechanism, not the direction.

reports.title: Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 on the application of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure
reports.description: The EDP Regulation — the instrument that turns the Treaty's excessive deficit procedure into a statistical reporting regime, and the second EU Regulation in this corpus to be modelled as a node after esa-2010. It matters here for Article 9, which compels into existence a published national document class that no other instrument this branch has followed produces: 'Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat) with a detailed inventory of the methods, procedures and sources used to compile actual deficit and debt data and the underlying government accounts' (Art. 9(1)), 'The inventories shall be updated following revisions in the methods, procedures and sources adopted by Member States' (Art. 9(3)), and 'Member States shall make their inventories public' (Art. 9(4)). Eurostat's own EDP inventories page states the consequence — 'Pursuant to Article 9 of Council regulation 479/2009 (as amended), all EU Member States are required to prepare and publish an EDP inventory' — and carries a live Inventory link for each of the 27. EUR-Lex titles it a '(Codified version)', codifying Council Regulation (EEC) No 3605/93. Note that the Regulation names no member state's inventory by title: AGENCY ONLY at exactly the point where a title would have produced a downward edge.
reports.cadence_note: Derived from an observed amendment record, not from a stated rate — see _open_questions. Adopted 25 May 2009; EUR-Lex lists exactly two consolidated versions, 19/08/2010 and 01/09/2014, with 01/09/2014 flagged as the current version. Two amendments across the 17 years to 2026.

release_schedule.note: April notification is provisional, October carries the revised annual figures. The underlying legal deadline (Reg. 479/2009 Art. 3(1)) is fixed at before 1 April and 1 October each year, so future cycles can be projected from that even without the exact transmission date.

reports.description:
Germany's Article 9 inventory -- the national document Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 compels every EU member state to prepare, keep updated and publish, describing the methods, procedures and sources used to compile Germany's Maastricht deficit and debt data and the underlying government accounts. RESOLVED 2026-08-09 (dropped-sweep, Tier 1): the cadence blocker this file's own _dropped entries flagged as 'the main cost of this slice' is closed. Eurostat's EDP-inventories page carries a live 'Inventory' link for Germany that resolves, in a real browser session (CIRCABC gates non-interactive HTTP clients, the same gate already documented elsewhere in this corpus for EUR-Lex), to a CIRCABC library item titled 'DE EDP Inventory 2025', uploaded 2026-01-08 -- and the document's own title page reads 'Germany' / 'October 2025'. Destatis's own copy is still headed 'December 2015'. Same title, same 188-page structure, same institutional-responsibilities matrix, confirming a revised edition of the same document class rather than a one-off. Its own background section: 'Compilation and publishing of the Inventory of the methods, procedures and sources used to compile actual deficit and debt data is foreseen by Council Regulation 479/2009, as amended... In line with the provisions of the Regulation set up in Article 9, "Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat) with a detailed inventory of the methods, procedures and sources used to compile actual deficit and debt data and the underlying government accounts."'

TABLE 1 READ DIRECTLY, 2026-08-09 (closing G.64.md cheap check 7). Page 17 names the three institutions crossed against Table 1's columns in full: 'The official names of the German institutions involved are: NSI: Statistisches Bundesamt (Destatis) – English: Federal Statistical Office (FSO), MOF: Bundesministerium der Finanzen (BMF) – English: Federal Ministry of Finance, NCB: Deutsche Bundesbank – English: German Central Bank.' The table itself splits the work rather than naming one compiler: Destatis (NSI) compiles the nonfinancial national accounts (annual and quarterly) and the EDP tables' actual deficit/surplus and other variables; Deutsche Bundesbank (NCB) compiles the financial accounts, Maastricht debt, and the EDP tables' actual debt figures; the Ministry of Finance (MOF) supplies the planned-data column across all three EDP table 1 rows. 'The completed EDP tables are transmitted to Eurostat by the Federal Statistical Office via electronic form (EDAMIS). An affidavit does not exist.' Publisher field updated from the prior generic 'jointly compiled per the inventory's own institutional-responsibilities matrix' description to name the three institutions directly.
reports.cadence_note: ESTIMATED from an observed interval, not stated by the document itself -- Article 9(3) gives only an event trigger ('The inventories shall be updated following revisions in the methods, procedures and sources'), no periodicity. Two dated editions confirmed at source this session: December 2015 (Destatis's own copy) and October 2025 (the current CIRCABC edition, uploaded 2026-01-08) -- 9.83 years apart. 0.1 (1/9.83) is that observed interval, the same estimation-from-observed-interval treatment Thomas's Q2 ruling applied to the ESA 2010 German GNI/QNA inventories in esa-2010.json.

release_schedule.note: This EDP Inventory (required under Article 9 of Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009, as amended) has no fixed publication calendar or stated periodic-review rule. The regulation only requires member states to compile, publish, and keep the inventory available; it does not specify a review/update interval. In practice, EDP inventories (hosted centrally by Eurostat on CircaBC, one document per member state) are revised irregularly, whenever there are material changes to the compilation methods/sources/procedures for government deficit and debt data, not on a schedule. This is distinct from Germany's twice-yearly EDP notification tables (April/October actual data transmissions under Reg. 479/2009 Art. 3), which follow a fixed biannual calendar but are a separate report. I was unable to load the CircaBC document page itself (https://s-circabc.europa.eu/...) directly -- it is an Angular SPA that returns HTTP 404 to non-browser clients on any deep-linked route (even https://s-circabc.europa.eu/ui/welcome 404s the same way), so this looks like a client-side-routing/access limitation rather than proof the document is gone. Eurostat's live EDP inventories landing page (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/government-finance-statistics/excessive-deficit-procedure/edp-inventories), fetched directly today, still lists this exact URL as the current 'Inventory' link for Germany, corroborating that it remains the publisher's designated location for this report. Destatis's own mirrored copy of the inventory (https://www.destatis.de/DE/Themen/Wirtschaft/Volkswirtschaftliche-Gesamtrechnungen-Inlandsprodukt/Tabellen/eu-stabilitaetspakt-eurostat-edp-info.html) is a stale ESA95-vintage PDF dated 2014-02-18 with no stated update cadence, consistent with this being an irregularly-revised methodological document rather than a periodic release.

dependencies.basis: Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009, consolidated text of 01/09/2014, Article 1(1): 'For the purposes of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure and of this Regulation, the terms in paragraphs 2 to 6 are defined according to Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 of the European Parliament and the Council of 21 May 2013 on the European system of national and regional accounts in the European Union (hereinafter referred to as ESA 2010). The codes in brackets refer to ESA 2010.' The dependence is operative, not decorative: Article 1(2) defines 'Government' as 'the sector of general government (S.13)... as defined in ESA 2010', Article 1(3) defines 'Government deficit (surplus)' as 'the net borrowing (net lending) (B.9) of the sector of general government (S.13), as defined in ESA 2010', and Article 1(5) defines 'Government debt' by ESA 2010 categories 'currency and deposits (AF.2); debt securities (AF.3) and loans (AF.4)'. 'Are defined according to' is derivation language and is not on Research.1.md section 5a's watchlist. Direction: the EDP Regulation is the dependent, ESA 2010 the depended-on. Re-fetched and re-read from EUR-Lex 2026-08-07 after G.50.md Finding 4 recorded the site serving nothing; the outage was transient. Quoted with EUR-Lex's in-line amendment markers stripped — the unstripped Article 1(1) reads with the whole clause inside a M2 insertion marker, because the original 2009 text referred to ESA 95.

_dropped.why: Two German statutes named by the inventory as the legal basis for the data it compiles, neither a publication on a cadence. 'In Germany, the Law on the Statistics of Public Finance and Public Service Personnel (Finanz- und Personalstatistikgesetz - FPStatG) regulates the statistical collection and compilation of national fiscal data, which are the main data source for the general government sector in national accounts. The national responsibility for the provision of government finance statistics (GFS) data according to ESA 2010 is set out in the Federal Statistics Law (Gesetz ueber die Statistik fuer Bundeszwecke - BStatG). According to section 3(1) No. 7 BStatG it is the duty of the Federal Statistical Office to compile and to publish national accounts data for national purposes. According to section 19 BStatG the Federal Statistical Office has to compile national accounts data for purposes of the European Union and of international organisations and to transmit these data to the European Union.' BStatG section 19 is the national mirror of ESA 2010 Article 3(1) — a domestic statute obliging transmission to the EU — and it is absent from the staged records entirely, recovered only by re-reading the source. Worth knowing that the obligation is doubly grounded, in EU and national law, even though neither statute is a node.

'For the compilation of GFS data, the public finance statistics as unique data source is not sufficient. Examples are data directly provided by the Ministry of Finance, annual and quarterly business reports, balance of payments data, reports from the budget committee, direct information from certain units, Working Party on Tax Revenue Estimates, Zentrale Datenstelle der Landesfinanzminister (ZDL) etc.' Seven named inputs, not one of them a titled publication: two bodies, four descriptions, and an 'etc.' that declines to claim the list is complete.
