_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Third municipal-level slice in the AF branch (G.13). Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review.
_note: This slice is a documented NEGATIVE finding rather than a network of dependencies, and is reported honestly as such rather than stretched. Across every document actually opened, Cairo Governorate's fiscal relationship to the center runs top-down: the center (Ministry of Planning, Ministry of Local Development, the national Cabinet, Parliament's Plan and Budget Committee) prepares, allocates and approves; Cairo's own Executive Council/governor prepares proposals and executes. No primary document was found showing Cairo Governorate independently setting a tax, fee, or tariff rate, and no primary document was found linking any Cairo/governorate-level fiscal instrument to CAPMAS's CPI. The one genuine, quotable statutory fiscal link between national instruments and governorate-level money is the Real Estate Tax Law's Article 28, earmarking 25% of tax collected within a governorate's jurisdiction for that governorate -- itself administered 'in a manner regulated by Cabinet decision.' All three reports below are correspondingly isolated (no dependencies drawn among them or to other corpus nodes) -- per this project's V0.12 convention, an isolated node is not an absence of information but the documented statement that nothing published names this level's inputs, which is exactly the Cairo finding.

_open_questions.question: News reporting (Al-Masry Al-Youm, Al-Watan News) confirms a distinct 'General Diwan' operating budget exists for Cairo Governorate (EGP 8bn for FY2026/2027 vs 5.68bn prior year, approved by Parliament's Plan and Budget Committee), with the governor quoted seeking to 'diversify financing sources.' No primary document (the budget text, committee record, or a Cairo Governorate financial statement) was reachable this session to quote directly.

A April 2026 news item indicates a draft new Local Administration Law was under legislative discussion, which could eventually supersede Law 43/1979's budget-preparation/control provisions. The draft text itself could not be fetched (proxy blocked it) -- worth checking again in a future session.

HCWW's own site hosts a page purporting to reproduce the Official Gazette text of a Cabinet decree amending water tariffs, but the content is embedded in a non-extractable interactive document. Existence confirmed, content not verified.

reports.title: Citizen Budget Plan for Cairo Governorate (FY2024/2025)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Planning, Economic Development & International Cooperation (Egypt)
reports.description: A central-government 'citizen budget' document produced by Egypt's national Ministry of Planning, presenting the public investment plan allocated to Cairo Governorate (EGP 100.5 billion, 21% of national public investment, across 1,284 projects) for FY2024/2025. Not a Cairo-authored fiscal document: discloses no locally-raised revenue, no transfer structure, and no CPI/inflation adjustment. One of a nationwide set of governorate-level plans the ministry issues, illustrating that even Cairo's most visible public 'budget' artifact is a central-ministry product describing money allocated TO Cairo, not one Cairo itself raises revenue for or controls.
reports.cadence_note: Published annually per fiscal year as part of the Ministry of Planning's 'Citizen Budget' series covering all governorates, not just Cairo.

reports.title: Local Administration Law No. 43 of 1979 (as amended), and 2014 Constitution Article 178 (local units)
reports.publisher: Arab Republic of Egypt (People's Assembly / Constitution)
reports.description: Egypt's foundational local-government statute structuring how governorates including Cairo are administered. Article 178 of the 2014 Constitution nominally grants local units 'independent financial budgets' funded partly by 'taxes and duties of a local nature,' but Law 43/1979 assigns budget preparation to each governorate's Executive Council (Art. 33) while vesting control and performance evaluation of governorates in the central Cabinet (Art. 133: 'The Cabinet shall take charge of control of the work of the governorates, and evaluate their performance'). No primary evidence was found that Cairo Governorate raises or manages revenue independently of central-government allocation and oversight -- consistent with news evidence that Cairo's own operating budget is approved by Parliament's Plan and Budget Committee, not an elected local body. UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.18, municipal-tier round): independently re-verified against the statute's own Arabic text (cross-confirmed across two legal-database mirrors, lawyeregypt.net and lawhub.info -- neither a .gov.eg host, flagged as a sourcing caveat). Article 1 confirms sub-governorate units DO have legal personality: "وحدات الحكم المحلى هى المحافظات والمراكز والمدن والأحياء والقرى، ويكون لكل منها الشخصية الاعتبارية" [Local government units are the governorates, markaz, cities, hay/districts, and villages, and each of them shall have legal personality] -- notably 'qism' (police-district unit) is NOT among the named units. But Articles 43 and 51 show this legal personality does not extend to independent budgeting: Art. 43, "ما يخصصه المجلس الشعبى المحلى للمحافظة من موارده لصالح المركز" [what the governorate's Local Popular Council allocates from its resources in favor of the markaz]; Art. 51, "ما يخصصه المجلس الشعبى المحلى للمحافظة لصالح المدينة من الموارد المقررة للمحافظة" [what the governorate's Local Popular Council allocates in favor of the city from resources established for the governorate] -- markaz/city 'resources' are statutorily governorate-ALLOCATED transfers, not autonomous revenue-raising budgets. No 'General Diwan' (الديوان العام) budget mechanism appears anywhere in the law's text as reproduced, despite that term's use in news coverage of Cairo's own operating budget.

reports.title: Real Estate Tax Law No. 196 of 2008 (as amended, incl. 2026 amendments)
reports.publisher: Egyptian Real Estate Tax Authority / Ministry of Finance
reports.description: Egypt's national property-tax law (10% of net annual rental value, less 30-40% deduction for expenses), administered by the Real Estate Tax Authority -- a federal-level input to Cairo's local finances rather than a Cairo-specific document. Article 28 earmarks 25% of tax collected within each governorate's jurisdiction for that governorate (plus a further 25% of the national total for informal-settlements development). Valuations are fixed for a statutory five-year cycle with revaluation increases capped at 30% (residential) / 45% (non-residential) per cycle -- a fixed administrative cap, not a CPI or inflation-indexed adjustment. Exemption thresholds (raised to 100,000 EGP annual rental value per 2026 amendments) change only by discretionary Council of Ministers/Parliament action, with no automatic price-index linkage found in the law's text.

The law's valuations are fixed for five-year cycles with flat percentage caps (30%/45%), and exemption thresholds move only via discretionary Council of Ministers/Parliament decisions -- not via any CPI or inflation index. A documented absence, not an inference.

reports.title: General Consumer Price Index (CAPMAS), 10th series
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Egypt's official monthly CPI. CAPMAS's role as publisher was independently verified this session via Law 148/2019's own statutory definition (see eg-social-insurance-pensions-law-148-2019). The 10th series' base period (FY2018/2019) and release date (October 2019, with September 2019 data) are independently confirmed this session via CAPMAS's own metadata catalog for the 10th-series bulletin itself. That same fetch also confirms the classification standard directly: 'COICOP-HBS 2000/1999' -- Egypt's CPI runs on the 1999 vintage of the UN's individual-consumption classification, not the 2018 vintage South Africa and Nigeria both cite (see un-coicop-hbs-1999 below). Weights are sourced from the FY2017/2018 Household Income, Expenditure and Consumption Survey (HIECS), covering 945 items across 12 sections/47 groups/116 classes priced monthly at roughly 14,442 outlets; the index is a Modified Laspeyres formula with Jevons-type (unweighted geometric mean) elementary aggregation. Egypt complies with the IMF's SDDS, releasing on the 10th day after the reference month. Per Thomas's standing instruction on import-sourced verification, this is accepted from the IMF's own DSBB DQAF page for Egypt (dsbb.imf.org/sdds/dqaf-base/country/EGY/category/CPI00), whose live metadata (certified 2026-02-25) the import re-confirmed on a second pass -- the page's detailed sections are JS-collapsed for every tool tried against it, including the import's own, so no fuller primary text than this exists to quote.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly CPI release; weights refreshed roughly every two years per the household expenditure survey cycle.

release_schedule.rule: تصدر فى اليوم العاشر من الشهر التالى لجمع البيان (Issued on the 10th day of the month following the data-collection month; prices are gathered monthly from urban and rural areas between the 1st and 28th of each month).
release_schedule.note: Confirmed by real-world observation: the July 2026 CPI release was published by CAPMAS on 2026-08-10 (reported in multiple Egyptian news outlets on 10 Aug 2026, e.g. Masrawy, Al-Balad, Amwal Al Ghad), consistent with the stated 10th-of-following-month rule. Next release (August 2026 data) is therefore expected 2026-09-10, rolled forward from the just-completed July cycle.

reports.title: Social Insurance and Pensions Law No. 148 of 2019
reports.description: Egypt's unified pension and social insurance statute, replacing several prior fragmented schemes; effective 1 January 2020, executive regulations issued via Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2437 of 2021. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (Andersen's published official English translation of the Act) -- Article 35: 'Pensions due as of June 30 of each year shall be increased starting from July 1 by a percentage not less than the rate of inflation and not exceeding 15%', with 'the value of the increase must not exceed the proportionate increase relative to the maximum monthly contributory wage.' 'Inflation Rate' is defined in the Act itself as 'the relative change in the general consumer price index across the Republic for a given year, as published by [CAPMAS], determined each April.' Independently corroborated by the US Social Security Administration's own International Update (February 2020): 'The pension amount is automatically adjusted in July of each year based on changes in the national consumer price index, with a maximum annual increase of 15 percent.' The strongest statutory CPI-to-benefit link found in the corpus's Africa branch so far -- a genuine floor formula, not a Gazette-notice discretion.

reports.title: Social Security Law No. 12 of 2025
reports.description: The statute that legally anchors Takaful and Karama as Egypt's primary social safety net, resolving an open question left by the first draft of this slice (the docx's citation could not initially be confirmed against an official source). INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED this session via a legal-reference summary (lawhub.info) quoting the Act directly: Article 3, 'the Takaful and Karama Fund... shall succeed to the Central Social Security Fund [established under Law No. 137 of 2010]... shall assume all its assets, rights and liabilities'; Article 4, 'The Social Security Law issued by Law No. 137 of 2010 is hereby repealed', with existing beneficiaries retaining current benefits through a transition period of up to two years. Article 39 (per the same source) formally establishes the Fund itself, with resources drawn from budget allocations, donations, recovered overpayments, investment returns, and penalties/fees (Article 40). Issued 4 Shawwal 1446 AH / 3 April 2025 CE, effective three months after Official Gazette publication. Multiple independent Arabic-language legal and news sources (a July 2026 Ministry of Social Solidarity executive-regulation notice among them) corroborate the citation and continued currency of this law.

reports.title: Takaful and Karama Programme
reports.description: Egypt's flagship cash-transfer programme: Takaful (conditional, families with children) and Karama (unconditional, covering elderly persons, persons with disabilities, and orphans). VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via the ILO's own GIMI country profile for Egypt: no automatic indexation or adjustment mechanism is mentioned anywhere in the profile for Takaful/Karama. Funding figures independently confirmed via Daily News Egypt, quoting Prime Minister Madbouly directly: 'we are allocating EGP 41bn in the current FY 2025, up from EGP 24bn the previous year', rising to roughly EGP 55bn for FY 2025/26 -- that reporting gives no inflation rationale for the increase. A second, independent search this session (vian import, checking specifically for a Ministry of Social Solidarity or Ministry of Finance document tying benefit increases to a CAPMAS CPI formula) also came back negative -- 'no primary source linking increases to a CPI formula does not appear to exist' -- reinforcing rather than merely repeating the first session's finding. Unlike eg-social-insurance-pensions-law-148-2019, nothing found across two independent search passes ties this programme's benefit levels to CPI by formula.

reports.title: Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP-HBS 1999/2000)
reports.description: The 1999/2000 household-budget-survey vintage of COICOP -- an older edition than the COICOP 2018 already in the graph (un-coicop-2018, minted for South Africa). INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED this session via CAPMAS's own metadata catalog for its 10th CPI series bulletin (2019, current series): 'تصنيف الاستهلاك الفردى حسب الغرض الوارد بنظام الحسابات القومية، COICOP-HBS 2000/1999' (Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose included in the System of National Accounts, COICOP-HBS 2000/1999). Minted as a distinct node from un-coicop-2018 deliberately: they are different editions of the same UN standard, and the corpus's own precedent (Canada/US) treats COICOP as governing a release only when a national document says so for that release specifically -- CAPMAS's metadata for the *current* series is exactly that document, for the older vintage.
reports.cadence_note: Revised on a multi-decade cycle; not an annual release. Matches the treatment already given to un-coicop-2018 and sna-2008.

release_schedule.note: COICOP-HBS 1999/2000 (Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose, adapted for Household Budget Surveys) is a UN statistical classification standard, not a periodic statistical release. It has already been superseded by COICOP 2018, published after a 19-year gap with no fixed revision cycle. The UNSD classification family page lists a 'Next Review: 2017' which is stale/outdated and was in fact followed by the 2018 revision rather than a recurring scheduled update. No release calendar or stated periodicity rule exists; revisions occur on an as-needed basis driven by international statistical standards review processes (e.g., UN Statistical Commission), not a fixed schedule.

dependencies.basis: Article 35 sets the pension increase floor directly equal to 'the rate of inflation', and the Act's own definitions section defines 'Inflation Rate' as the change in CAPMAS's General Consumer Price Index, determined every April. CAPMAS's CPI print is a direct, named input into the statutory floor of the calculation (capped at 15%), not merely referenced as context.

CAPMAS's own metadata catalog entry for the 10th-series (current) CPI bulletin names 'COICOP-HBS 2000/1999' as the classification the index's item structure is built on -- independently fetched this session, not taken from the import's extraction alone.

REGISTER: The IMF's own DSBB DQAF page for Egypt's CPI states SDDS-compliant release timing (10th day after the reference month) among other prescribed dissemination-methodology fields -- reusing the `imf-sdds` node first minted for South Africa's equivalent edge (za-fiscal-federalism.json), on the same reasoning: SDDS prescribes coverage, periodicity, timeliness and advance-release-calendar practice, which is a dissemination-methodology obligation rather than mere context.

reports.title: Law No. 35 of 1960 concerning Statistics and Censuses (as amended)
reports.description: Foundational legal instrument governing the conduct of statistics and censuses in Egypt. Establishes the framework for official statistical work, confidentiality of individual data, obligations to supply data, and coordination of statistical operations. Amended by Law No. 28 of 1982. Remains the primary statutory basis for official statistics production and is repeatedly cited in CAPMAS publications and data-access policies.
reports.cadence_note: One-off / amending legal instrument; still in force as the core statistics statute

reports.title: Presidential Decree No. 2915 of 1964 establishing the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.publisher: Arab Republic of Egypt (Presidency of the Republic)
reports.description: Presidential Decree establishing the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) as an independent authority adjunct to the Presidency of the Republic. Assigns CAPMAS the technical jurisdictions under Law No. 35 of 1960, including the power to conduct statistics and censuses required by the State, set dates and methods, disseminate results, and ensure coordination. Foundational institutional instrument for the Egyptian national statistical system.
reports.cadence_note: One-off founding decree; still the organisational foundation of CAPMAS

reports.title: Egypt Statistical Yearbook (كتاب الإحصاء السنوي)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Long-running comprehensive annual statistical yearbook published by CAPMAS. Presents detailed multi-domain national statistics covering population and demography, labour force, national accounts and prices, agriculture, industry, trade, education, health, transport, environment and related fields. Principal single-volume official reference for Egyptian official statistics; typically released around September–December.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: Egypt in Figures (مصر في أرقام)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Annual concise statistical booklet issued by CAPMAS presenting key demographic, social and economic indicators for Egypt in a compact format with recent time series and governorate highlights. Complements the more detailed Statistical Yearbook; typically released mid-year. Serves as a rapid-reference official summary for decision-makers and the public.
reports.cadence_note: Annual (often March–June window)

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI) – Egypt (الرقم القياسي لأسعار المستهلكين)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Official Consumer Price Index and related inflation statistics for Egypt, compiled monthly by CAPMAS. Covers urban, rural and national series; primary official measure of consumer price inflation used for monetary-policy monitoring, living-standards analysis and indexation. Weights derive from household expenditure surveys. Monthly press releases and detailed bulletins are issued.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly

reports.title: Population and Housing Census of Egypt / General Census of Population, Housing and Establishments
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Decennial (or periodic) Population and Housing Census of Egypt, most recently conducted in 2017 as the General Census of Population, Housing and Establishments. Provides the official population base, demographic structure, housing characteristics and establishment counts. Subsequent annual population estimates and projections published by CAPMAS are derived from the census framework updated with vital registration (births and deaths).
reports.cadence_note: Decennial census with continuous inter-censal population estimates and projections

reports.title: Labour Force Survey / Quarterly Labour Force Survey (بحث القوى العاملة)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Official quarterly (and annual) labour-force statistics produced by CAPMAS. Provides nationally representative data on labour-force participation, employment, unemployment, underemployment and related indicators by sex, age, urban/rural residence and governorate. Principal official source for unemployment rates and labour-market analysis in Egypt; results released quarterly with annual summaries.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly with annual aggregates

reports.title: Household Income, Expenditure and Consumption Survey (HIECS / بحث الدخل والإنفاق والاستهلاك)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Periodic large-scale household survey programme producing detailed statistics on household income, expenditure, consumption patterns, living standards and poverty. Conducted roughly every two years (recent rounds include 2017/18, 2019/20, 2021/22). Provides the micro-data foundation for CPI weights, poverty measurement, inequality analysis and national-accounts household consumption estimates.
reports.cadence_note: Approximately every two years (multi-wave field collection)

reports.title: Egypt National Accounts / GDP Statistics (Ministry of Planning series)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Planning, Economic Development and International Cooperation (MPED)
reports.description: Official national accounts and GDP statistics for Egypt, compiled and disseminated primarily by the Ministry of Planning, Economic Development and International Cooperation (MPED). Includes GDP by production (value added by economic activity at factor cost) and expenditure approaches at current and constant prices, quarterly and annual series, and regional/governorate accounts. CAPMAS contributes source data and maintains related supply-use tables; the consolidated national-accounts responsibility has rested with MPED since the late 1990s. Core macroeconomic measure of economic activity and growth.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly releases with annual final estimates; base-year revisions periodically

reports.title: Central Bank of Egypt Monthly Statistical Bulletin
reports.description: Flagship monthly statistical publication of the Central Bank of Egypt. Compiles and disseminates comprehensive monetary, banking, fiscal, external-sector and selected real-sector statistics, including reserve money, domestic liquidity (M2), credit, interest rates, international reserves, exchange rates, balance of payments summaries, and selected CAPMAS/MPED indicators (CPI, GDP). Primary official source for high-frequency monetary and external statistics.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly

reports.title: Central Bank of Egypt Balance of Payments and External Sector Statistics
reports.description: Official Balance of Payments, International Investment Position, external debt and related external-sector statistics compiled by the Central Bank of Egypt in accordance with IMF standards (BPM6). Covers the current account (goods, services including Suez Canal, income, transfers), capital and financial accounts, reserve assets and external debt. Disseminated through the Monthly Statistical Bulletin, dedicated BoP releases, SDDS and the Annual Report. Primary official source for Egypt’s external accounts.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly BoP with monthly reserves and related indicators

reports.title: Producer Price Index (PPI) – Egypt (الأرقام القياسية لأسعار المنتجين)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Official monthly Producer Price Index compiled by CAPMAS covering agriculture, forestry & fishing, mining & quarrying, manufacturing, electricity & gas, water supply, construction, and selected service activities (including accommodation and food services). Base year January 2016 = 100 (updated series). Primary official measure of producer-level price change used for national-accounts deflation and inflation analysis alongside the CPI.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly

reports.title: Annual Agricultural Statistics / Crop Area and Plant Production / Agricultural Income Estimates
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Annual CAPMAS bulletins on cultivated and cropped areas, plant production quantities and values, agricultural income estimates, and related farm-gate statistics. Covers major field crops (wheat, rice, maize, potatoes, tomatoes, etc.), permanent crops, and value of agricultural production by component (plant, animal, fish). Core source for the agriculture sector contribution to GDP and food-security indicators.
reports.cadence_note: Annual (agricultural year)

reports.title: Annual Livestock Statistics (إحصاءات الثروة الحيوانية)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Annual CAPMAS bulletin on livestock numbers (cattle, buffalo, sheep, goats, camels), slaughtered animals, red-meat production, milk production, poultry meat and egg output. Complements plant-production statistics and feeds the animal-production component of agricultural income and GDP by activity.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: Foreign Trade Statistics / Merchandise Trade (إحصاءات التجارة الخارجية)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Official merchandise trade statistics compiled by CAPMAS from customs declarations. Covers exports and imports by commodity group, partner country, and economic use; published in monthly and annual bulletins. Primary customs-based trade series used alongside the banking-based trade figures that appear in the CBE Balance of Payments.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly bulletins with annual aggregates

reports.title: Tourism Statistics / Tourist Arrivals and Nights (إحصاءات السياحة)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) / Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities
reports.description: Official statistics on inbound tourist arrivals, tourist nights, and related tourism indicators. CAPMAS publishes tourism data series and integrates them into the Statistical Yearbook; the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities and CBE also report tourism receipts that feed the services account of the Balance of Payments. Key sector for services exports and employment.
reports.cadence_note: Periodic / quarterly and annual releases

reports.title: Industrial / Total Production Index components (Manufacturing, Electricity, Construction, Tourism, etc.)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Planning, Economic Development and International Cooperation (MPED) / CAPMAS
reports.description: Short-term production indices covering manufacturing, natural gas, oil products, electricity, construction, transportation (including Suez Canal), and tourism. Compiled and disseminated under the national accounts / real-sector monitoring framework; used as high-frequency indicators of sectoral activity that feed into quarterly GDP estimates.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly

reports.title: Energy / Petroleum and Electricity Production Statistics
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) / relevant energy authorities
reports.description: Official statistics on petroleum (crude and products), natural gas, and electricity production and related energy indicators that appear in CAPMAS yearbooks and specialised bulletins and feed the extractive and utilities components of national accounts and the PPI.
reports.cadence_note: Annual aggregates with higher-frequency production indices

reports.title: GDP / Gross Regional Product by Governorate (National Accounts – Regional)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Planning, Economic Development and International Cooperation (MPED)
reports.description: Official estimates of GDP (value added) by governorate and economic region produced within the national accounts framework. Provides the principal measure of economic size and structure at subnational level and the vertical link from governorate activity into national GDP.
reports.cadence_note: Annual (with lag)

reports.title: Population Estimates by Governorate
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Annual mid-year or 1 January population estimates by governorate derived from the 2017 Population and Housing Census updated with vital registration (births and deaths). Core demographic base for all governorate-level analysis and for weighting of national surveys.
reports.cadence_note: Annual estimates; continuous population clock on CAPMAS site

reports.title: Cairo Governorate Statistical Profile / Key Indicators
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) / Cairo Governorate
reports.description: Aggregated official statistics for Cairo Governorate drawn from CAPMAS national products (population estimates, labour force, household surveys) and governorate-level administrative data. Cairo is the largest governorate by population and a major contributor to national GDP; serves as the core metropolitan node.
reports.cadence_note: Annual / continuous updates via national series

reports.title: Giza Governorate Statistical Profile / Key Indicators
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) / Giza Governorate
reports.description: Aggregated official statistics for Giza Governorate. Second-largest by population and integral to Greater Cairo; includes significant industrial, residential and tourist (Pyramids) activity. Provides metropolitan contrast to pure urban Cairo.
reports.cadence_note: Annual / continuous updates via national series

reports.title: Alexandria Governorate Statistical Profile / Key Indicators
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) / Alexandria Governorate
reports.description: Aggregated official statistics for Alexandria Governorate, Egypt’s principal Mediterranean port and second major metropolitan centre after Greater Cairo. Captures coastal / port-city economic structure (trade, industry, services).
reports.cadence_note: Annual / continuous updates via national series

reports.title: Minya Governorate Statistical Profile / Key Indicators (Upper Egypt contrast)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Aggregated official statistics for Minya Governorate in Upper Egypt. Provides inland / Upper Egypt demographic and economic contrast to the coastal and Greater Cairo metropolitan governorates; significant agricultural base.
reports.cadence_note: Annual / continuous updates via national series

reports.title: Sohag Governorate Statistical Profile / Key Indicators (Upper Egypt contrast)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Aggregated official statistics for Sohag Governorate in Upper Egypt. Complements Minya as a second Upper Egypt contrast node with substantial rural and agricultural population.
reports.cadence_note: Annual / continuous updates via national series

reports.title: Aswan Governorate Statistical Profile / Key Indicators (Upper Egypt / frontier contrast)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Aggregated official statistics for Aswan Governorate at the southern end of the Nile Valley. Serves as Upper Egypt / frontier contrast (tourism, High Dam, lower population density relative to Delta and Cairo).
reports.cadence_note: Annual / continuous updates via national series

reports.title: Ministry of Finance Financial Monthly Bulletin / Fiscal Performance Statistics
reports.description: Monthly fiscal bulletin published by the Ministry of Finance presenting budget execution (revenues, expenditures by economic and functional classification), overall and primary balance, domestic and external financing, and related public-finance indicators. Primary official high-frequency source for Egypt’s fiscal accounts; data also feed CBE monetary and below-the-line analysis.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly

reports.title: State Budget / Final Accounts (الموازنة العامة / الحساب الختامي)
reports.description: Annual State Budget law and subsequent Final Accounts (approved by Parliament) presenting the full fiscal framework: revenues, expenditures by economic and functional classification, deficit/surplus, and financing. Constitutional targets for health, education and scientific research spending are monitored against these accounts. CAPMAS also issues a related annual bulletin on public expenditure drawn from MoF sources.
reports.cadence_note: Annual budget + final accounts cycle

reports.title: Education Statistics (Pre-university and Higher Education)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) / Ministry of Education and Technical Education / Ministry of Higher Education
reports.description: Official statistics on pre-university education (schools, classes, pupils, teachers) and higher education (enrolment, graduates by type of institution). Published in CAPMAS specialised bulletins and the Statistical Yearbook; primary source for education indicators used in human-development and labour-force analysis.
reports.cadence_note: Annual (academic year)

reports.title: Egypt Family Health Survey / Demographic and Health Indicators
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) / Ministry of Health and Population
reports.description: Periodic large-scale household survey programme (Egypt Family Health Survey / related DHS-style rounds) producing fertility, maternal and child health, nutrition, family-planning and related demographic-health indicators. Most recent major round referenced around 2021; results feed population projections, health policy and the Statistical Yearbook.
reports.cadence_note: Periodic multi-year survey cycle

reports.title: Health Statistics / Health Facilities and Services Indicators
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) / Ministry of Health and Population
reports.description: Official statistics on health facilities, hospital beds, medical personnel, selected service utilisation and related indicators published by CAPMAS in specialised bulletins and the Statistical Yearbook. Complements the Family Health Survey micro-data with administrative health-system statistics.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: Vital Statistics (Births, Deaths, Marriage, Divorce)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Official civil-registration-based statistics on births, deaths, marriages and divorces. Used to update inter-censal population estimates and to compile crude rates that appear in the Statistical Yearbook and Egypt in Figures.
reports.cadence_note: Annual with continuous registration

reports.title: Egypt / CAPMAS Contribution to BRICS Joint Statistical Publication and NSO Cooperation
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Thin institutional contribution node representing Egypt’s provision of national statistical series (national accounts, prices, population, labour, external trade, etc.) to the BRICS Joint Statistical Publication (JSP) and related BRICS National Statistical Offices cooperation mechanisms (Heads of NSOs meetings, technical working groups). Egypt joined BRICS as a full member in 2024; CAPMAS participates in the statistics track (including the 2026 Lucknow NSO Heads meeting). No separate freestanding titled annual ‘Egypt BRICS Statistical Report’ is required; the contribution is evidenced by data appearing in successive JSP editions and by CAPMAS public statements on BRICS statistical cooperation.
reports.cadence_note: Aligned with BRICS JSP and NSO meeting cycle

reports.title: CAPMAS Study: Egypt and the BRICS Countries (2013–2024 / subsequent updates)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Analytical statistical study issued by CAPMAS examining trade, investment and selected economic indicators between Egypt and BRICS member states over a multi-year window (explicitly referenced for 2013–2024 with later updates). Provides tabulated trade values, partner rankings and growth rates; supports public communication of Egypt’s BRICS economic engagement. Complements the regular foreign-trade bulletins.
reports.cadence_note: Ad-hoc / periodic analytical release

reports.title: Annual Bulletin of Water Purification and Sanitation Statistics (النشرة السنوية لإحصاءات المياه النقية والصرف الصحي)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Annual CAPMAS bulletin on potable water production, distribution networks, sanitation/sewerage coverage, treatment plants and related service indicators by governorate. Primary official source for water and sanitation access and infrastructure statistics used in living-standards, health and environmental analysis.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: Bulletin of Housing in Egypt / Housing Units Statistics (نشرة الإسكان في مصر)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Annual CAPMAS bulletin on housing units executed by public, public-business and private sectors, investments in housing, new-city projects and related residential construction indicators. Provides the principal official measure of housing supply and is used for urban-policy and construction-sector analysis.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: Construction and Building Statistics / Construction Sector Indicators
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) / Ministry of Planning
reports.description: Official statistics on construction activity, building permits or completed works, and the construction component of GDP and investment. Complements the Housing bulletin with broader construction-sector coverage that feeds national accounts and the industrial/production index framework.
reports.cadence_note: Annual with higher-frequency production-index components

reports.title: Annual Bulletin of Vehicles and Trains Accidents / Transport Safety Statistics
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Annual CAPMAS bulletin on road-vehicle and railway accidents, casualties and related transport-safety indicators. Complements broader transport and warehousing statistics that appear in national accounts and the Statistical Yearbook.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: Annual Bulletin of Transportation Means of Petroleum Products and Natural Gas
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Annual CAPMAS bulletin covering transport modes and volumes for petroleum products and natural gas. Links energy production statistics to the transport and logistics component of the economy.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: Quarterly Industrial Production Statistics / Manufacturing Production Index (إحصاء الإنتاج الصناعي الربع سنوي)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Quarterly CAPMAS statistics on industrial production covering public/public-business and private-sector establishments. Provides short-term indicators of manufacturing output, employment and related variables that feed the monthly/annual industrial production index and quarterly GDP estimates.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly

reports.title: Economic Census of Egypt (التعداد الاقتصادي)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Periodic Economic Census enumerating establishments by economic activity, employment size, legal form and geographic location. Provides the structural baseline for industrial, trade and services statistics, sample frames for enterprise surveys, and detailed activity-level data used in national accounts and productivity analysis. Most recent major rounds referenced in the 2010s–2020s programme.
reports.cadence_note: Periodic multi-year census cycle

reports.title: Poverty Statistics / National and Multidimensional Poverty Indicators (from HIECS)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) / Ministry of Planning / Ministry of Social Solidarity
reports.description: Official poverty measurement programme based primarily on the Household Income, Expenditure and Consumption Survey (HIECS). Includes monetary poverty rates (national poverty line) and the national Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) developed with partners (dimensions covering education, health, housing, services, employment, social protection and food security). Primary official source for poverty incidence, depth and regional disparities.
reports.cadence_note: Aligned with HIECS rounds (approximately every two years) plus periodic MPI analytical releases

reports.title: Dakahlia Governorate Statistical Profile / Key Indicators (Delta contrast)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Aggregated official statistics for Dakahlia Governorate in the Nile Delta. Provides Lower Egypt / Delta agricultural and demographic contrast to the metropolitan (Cairo/Giza/Alexandria) and Upper Egypt nodes already covered.
reports.cadence_note: Annual / continuous updates via national series

reports.title: Sharqia Governorate Statistical Profile / Key Indicators (Delta contrast)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Aggregated official statistics for Sharqia (Sharkia) Governorate in the eastern Delta. Complements Dakahlia as a second major Delta agricultural/population node.
reports.cadence_note: Annual / continuous updates via national series

reports.title: Qalyubia Governorate Statistical Profile / Key Indicators (Greater Cairo periphery)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Aggregated official statistics for Qalyubia Governorate, immediately north of Cairo and part of the broader Greater Cairo economic zone. Provides peri-urban / industrial-agricultural contrast within the metropolitan system.
reports.cadence_note: Annual / continuous updates via national series

reports.title: Annual Bulletin of Patents and Trademarks Statistics (النشرة السنوية لبراءات الاختراع والعلامات التجارية)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Annual CAPMAS bulletin on patents granted, trademark registrations and related intellectual-property indicators. Thin but real official series supporting innovation and business-environment analysis; appears in the Statistical Yearbook and specialised releases.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: CAPMAS Monthly Informatics Bulletin (النشرة المعلوماتية)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
reports.description: Monthly concise statistical bulletin issued by CAPMAS presenting the latest available indicators across key demographic, social and economic domains in a compact, graph-supported format. Serves as a rapid-update companion to the more comprehensive Statistical Yearbook and specialised annual bulletins.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly

_dropped.why:
RESOLVED 2026-08-08 (Thomas, Q1, Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx): 'these situations call for a node... it's sole role is broadcasting and that needs represented... doesn't need cadence.' Minted as statcan-system-macroeconomic-accounts in statcan-macro-accounts.json (evergreen, no releases_per_year). Two edges built here covering all four citations in this entry's own quotes (the three s. 3.1 capital-formation terms collapsed into one edge, since they cite the framework identically; the s. 5(b)(i) corporate-profits term as a second, independent edge) -- not four separate edges, since the first three are the same statutory sentence repeated for three aggregates rather than three distinct dependencies. The general question this entry raised -- 'whether a node may be a named series or framework rather than a release' -- is answered for this framework specifically; the sibling statcan-hfce / statcan-national-accounts duplication and the bea-gdp -> bea-pce question are NOT resolved by this ruling and remain open on their own terms. Original entry follows.

The most frequently named product in the Regulations and the one this graph is least able to represent. Named in the DIVISION 1 definitions at s. 3.1 three times over, for the three capital-formation aggregates: 'gross fixed capital formation in intellectual property products, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'; 'gross fixed capital formation in machinery and equipment, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'; 'gross fixed capital formation in non-residential structures, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. And in the DIVISION 1 revenue base at s. 5(b)(i): 'the portion of the aggregate of corporate profits in Canada, before the payment of income taxes and without any deduction of the aggregate of corporate losses in Canada, that is attributable to any of the 10 provinces for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. The CSMA is an accounting framework, not a release with a cadence, so it cannot become a node under the current model — but four separate revenue-base components depend on it definitionally, so leaving it unrepresented understates the Equalization Program's real input set. This is the same problem as the statcan-hfce / statcan-national-accounts duplication and the same problem as bea-gdp -> bea-pce, arriving from a third direction. THREE THINGS ARE NOW BLOCKED ON ONE DECISION: whether a node may be a named series or framework rather than a release.

_dropped.edge: SOR/2007-303 — table-number vintages disagree between divisions
_dropped.why: A corpus fact that will matter when these nodes are built. The same instrument cites Statistics Canada tables under two incompatible numbering systems, split by division. The Nova Scotia division uses retired CANSIM numbers: s. 8(1)(j) cites 'CANSIM table 183-0024, Sales of alcoholic beverages by volume, value and per capita 15 years and over, fiscal years ended March 31' for spirits, wine and beer in three separate subparagraphs; s. 8(1)(z) cites 'CANSIM table 002-0020'; s. 8(1)(h) and (i) cite 'CANSIM table 405-0004'. The Territorial Formula Financing part uses the current numbering for the same subject matter: s. 19(1)(f) cites 'table 10-10-0011-01, Value of sales of alcoholic beverages of liquor authorities and other retail outlets, by beverage type (× 1,000)' for the same three beverages. And the general Interpretation at s. 1(1) uses the current numbering too, at 'table 23-10-0066-01'. CANSIM was retired in favour of the current product-identifier scheme around 2018, so DIVISION 2 is citing tables under numbers Statistics Canada no longer publishes under. Two consequences. Any node built from a CANSIM citation has to be matched to its modern successor by hand, and that match is a judgement, not a quotation. And it corroborates the scope caveat on the SEPH edge: DIVISION 2 was not revised when the rest of the instrument was, which is consistent with its role as a legacy calculation for the Nova Scotia accords rather than a live all-provinces formula.

_dropped.edge: SOR/2007-303 — which division each citation lives in
_dropped.why: Recorded because a section number alone hides it, and it determines how much any of this is worth. Of the twenty-four provisions returned in this round, twelve sit in s. 8 — DIVISION 2 — Nova Scotia, which defines revenue base 'For the purpose of sections 3.71 to 3.9 of the Act', the Nova Scotia additional-equalization provisions, and retains the pre-2007 thirty-three-source revenue structure with paragraphs running (a) to (z.5). Ten sit in s. 3.1 and s. 5, which are DIVISION 1 — Fiscal Equalization to the Provinces, the live all-provinces formula with five revenue sources. Two sit in the general Interpretation at s. 1(1). THE DIVISION 1 CITATIONS ARE THE VALUABLE ONES and they are the minority. The s. 3.1 definitions in particular are what makes Tier 2's thesis true as originally stated — every province's revenue base runs through the same handful of named products — because they are definitions and not per-province measurements. The s. 8 citations are real, verified and narrower than they look. Also worth noting on packaging: the s. 3.1 definitions carry no paragraph numbers of their own, being definitions in an interpretation section, so they are citable only as 's. 3.1, definition of X'. That is the correct answer for them and is what NO CITABLE LOCATION was meant to elicit.

reports.title: Territorial Formula Financing
reports.description: The federal unconditional transfer to Yukon, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut that closes the gap between what a territory could raise on its own and what it needs to provide services comparable to those in the provinces, calculated under Part I.1 of the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act and Part 1.1 of SOR/2007-303. The fourth major federal transfer alongside the Canada Health Transfer, the Canada Social Transfer and Equalization, and until this entry the only one of the four with no node in this graph. Its revenue-base formula at s. 19 mirrors the DIVISION 2 Nova Scotia formula at s. 8 term for term in several places (SEPH, the System of Macroeconomic Accounts wage terms, Government Finance Statistics), which is what made this pass cheap once the equalization-named-products cluster had already verified the parallel citations.
reports.cadence_note: Entitlements are announced in December for the fiscal year beginning the following April 1, alongside Equalization, from the same certificate process.

entries.covers: TFF entitlements for fiscal year 2027-28 (beginning April 1, 2027)

release_schedule.rule: Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. F-8), s. 4.3: "The territorial formula financing payment payable to a territory for a fiscal year shall be calculated, at a time determined by the Minister, no later than three months before that fiscal year begins."
release_schedule.note: Statutory deadline is 3 months before the fiscal year starts (i.e., no later than Dec 31), but in practice Finance Canada has announced TFF and Equalization entitlements earlier in December each year via a joint news release: FY2022-23 announced Dec 16, 2021; FY2023-24 announced Dec 2022; FY2024-25 announced Dec 2023; FY2025-26 announced Dec 23, 2024. The next occurrence (for FY2027-28) is therefore expected around mid-to-late December 2026, with Dec 31, 2026 as the hard statutory backstop.

reports.title: Census of Agriculture
reports.description: The quinquennial census of Canadian farms, aligned with the population census years (2021, 2026, ...), producing farm land and building values among its outputs (IMDB record 3438). SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(h) names it explicitly as a publication — 'the value of farm land and buildings in a province or territory ... as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its publication entitled Census of Agriculture' — for the farm sub-base of the Territorial Formula Financing property-tax revenue base, the counterpart to the Nova Scotia division's use of the agricultural balance sheet (CANSIM 002-0020 / table 32-10-0056-01) for the same conceptual measure.
reports.cadence_note: Every five years, in the same years as the Census of Population (2021, 2026); not an annual release.

entries.covers: 2026 Census of Agriculture, first data release

release_schedule.rule: The Census of Agriculture is conducted every 5 years (quinquennial), coinciding with the Census of Population. 2026 Census of Agriculture collection runs May 4 to August 9, 2026 (Census Day May 12, 2026); first data release scheduled for May 12, 2027 (first in a series of releases).
release_schedule.note: Data is released in multiple phases over time following the census; May 12, 2027 is the first scheduled release date for 2026 Census of Agriculture results. Next full cycle after that would be 2031.

reports.title: Gasoline and Other Petroleum Fuels Sold
reports.description: The annual survey of gasoline, diesel, aviation and other petroleum fuel volumes sold by province and territory (IMDB record 2746), reported each year in The Daily as 'Motor vehicle fuel sales'. SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(d)(ii) and s. 19(1)(e)(ii)(A) both name the survey by title for the aviation-fuel and railway-fuel components of the Territorial Formula Financing motive-fuel tax base, distinct from the general fuel-volume definition in s. 1(1) that runs through the fixed table 23-10-0066-01 (statcan-road-fuel-sales) instead.

release_schedule.note: StatCan's IMDB survey page (SDDS 2746) lists collection as ongoing/monthly for internal purposes, but public release via The Daily is annual, each September, covering the prior calendar year's data. No forward-looking release calendar with a confirmed 2026 date was found; the September 2026 entry is projected from five consecutive years of September releases (2021-2025).

reports.title: Report on Energy Supply and Demand in Canada
reports.description: Statistics Canada's annual publication (catalogue 57-003-X) reconciling Canadian energy supply and demand by fuel type and province. SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(e)(ii)(B) names it as the fallback source for the railway-fuel component of the Territorial Formula Financing motive-fuel tax base, used 'in any other case' where the primary railway fuel tax data is incomplete — the same statutory-fallback shape as the Oil Sands Royalty Regulation's provision for a discontinued Bank of Canada exchange rate.
reports.cadence_note: Published with a lag behind its reference year; catalogue 57-003-X was still being issued as of the 2025 edition. The regulation cites it as a named fallback publication, not as the primary source for this revenue base.

entries.covers: Energy supply and demand, 2025 (projected next release)

release_schedule.note: No formal published release calendar found for this specific product; StatCan lists it as an annual publication. Observed pattern from 'The Daily' release bulletins: releases have landed in mid-to-late November for the past three years (2023-11-20, 2024-11-21, 2025-11-13), though slightly earlier than the 2021-2022 editions which released in December (2021-12-13 for 2020 data, 2022-12-06 for 2021 data). Next release (covering 2025 data) is projected for November 2026 based on this pattern, but no exact date is confirmed.

dependencies.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 8(1)(y), the payroll-tax revenue base, makes SEPH a named term in a statutory formula: 'P is the gross dollar value, before deductions, of the payrolls of all employers in the province for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of its Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours, other than the payrolls of (i) employers not included in that survey, and (ii) employers in the following industry classifications, as defined by the North American Industry Classification System: (A) the elementary and secondary schools industry group, (B) the hospitals subsector, (C) the nursing and residential care facilities subsector, (D) the provincial and territorial public administration subsector, and (E) the local, municipal and regional public administration subsector'. `calculated_from` because P is a term in the formula, not a consideration — the same test that makes boc-bank-rate calculated_from the policy rate. Note the provision also carves out its own exclusions by NAICS classification, so the edge to `naics` is stated in the same sentence. SCOPE, stated because the section number alone overstates it: s. 8 sits in DIVISION 2 — Nova Scotia, and defines revenue base 'For the purpose of sections 3.71 to 3.9 of the Act', which are the Nova Scotia additional-equalization provisions. SEPH does NOT appear in the DIVISION 1 all-provinces revenue base at s. 5 — the phrase 'payrolls' occurs nowhere in ss. 1 through 8(1)(j), because the 2007 reform folded payroll taxes into the personal-income base. So this is the Equalization Program depending on SEPH through one division of the Regulations, not through the general formula.

reports.title: Delayed Article IV Consultation with the State of Eritrea (IMF Press Release No. 18/262)
reports.description: IMF Press Release No. 18/262, dated June 28, 2018. Title (independently confirmed): "Delayed Article IV Consultation with the State of Eritrea." Only the title, press-release number, and date could be confirmed this round — the release's body text could not be retrieved (IMF's site renders press-release content via client-side JavaScript; both WebFetch and direct curl attempts returned 503/403). The title itself is significant: it establishes on the record that Eritrea's routine Article IV consultation cycle was delayed, consistent with the roughly fifteen-year gap between the 2003 Country Report (er-imf-cr03166-cpi) and the Fund's next substantive Eritrea engagement in 2019 (see er-imf-2019-article-iv-eb). Flagged as a partial finding: title/metadata confirmed, body content NOT FOUND.
reports.cadence_note: One-off press release announcing a specific delayed Article IV cycle; not a recurring publication.

reports.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2019 Article IV Consultation with the State of Eritrea (Press Release; Board Document EBM/19/67-3)
reports.description: Press release reporting the conclusion of the IMF Executive Board's 2019 Article IV Consultation with Eritrea, dated July 24, 2019 (verified via the africa-newsroom.com syndicated mirror; the direct imf.org URL, pr19288, could not be fetched in this environment — see _dropped). Executive Board Assessment section quote: "Directors stressed the need for capacity building tailored to country circumstances, particularly the production and analysis of data." Independently corroborated via the IMF Archives Catalog (https://archivescatalog.imf.org/Details/archive/125319451), which lists the underlying document as "The State of Eritrea – 2019 Article IV Consultation," Board Document ID EBM/19/67-3, dated July 22, 2019 — an internal Executive Board Meeting document, not a released Country Report. No CR/19/xxx Country Report exists in the IMF eLibrary for Eritrea for this consultation (confirmed via direct elibrary.imf.org subject-page search returning no Eritrea entries for this period; the IMF's own Publications-series filter for Eritrea Country Reports likewise showed zero results, "Page 1 of 0"). A separate End-of-Mission press release (No. 19/179, May 22, 2019) confirms an IMF staff mission occurred that spring, though only its boilerplate genre-description text was retrievable ('End-of-Mission press releases include statements of IMF staff teams that convey preliminary findings after a visit to a country.'), adding no further data — not minted as its own node (see _dropped). CORRECTION TO EXISTING CORPUS: er-imf-cr03166-cpi (IMF Country Report No. 03/166, 2003) was previously treated as the most recent IMF document on Eritrea; this is not accurate — the IMF resumed Article IV engagement with Eritrea in 2018-2019 (see also er-imf-pr18262-delayed-article-iv), but that 2019 cycle never produced a published Country Report, only this press release. CR/03/166 therefore remains the most recent *published Country Report*, but it is not the most recent IMF *engagement*. No textual citation links this press release to CR/03/166 or to PR 18/262, so no formal dependency edge is recorded (see _dropped).
reports.cadence_note: One-off press release concluding a specific Article IV cycle; no Country Report was published for this cycle, so no recurring-publication cadence exists.

_dropped.why: Both press releases concern the same 2018-2019 Article IV consultation cycle (18/262 announces the delay, the 2019 Executive Board release reports its conclusion), but neither release's confirmed text cites the other by number or title. Per the standing evidence rule (verbatim textual basis required per edge), this is a real narrative/temporal relationship but not a documented citation, so no formal dependency edge is added — recorded here for context instead.

This file's central finding is that the 2018-2019 IMF material postdates and corrects the prior assumption that CR/03/166 (2003) was Eritrea's most recent IMF document. However, neither the 2019 Executive Board press release nor PR 18/262 textually cites CR/03/166 by number or title — the relationship is a corpus-level correction, not a documented citation between the two texts. No 'cites' or 'methodology_depends_on' edge is added; the correction is instead recorded in prose in er-imf-2019-article-iv-eb's description and in this file's _meta.

All attempts to reach the direct imf.org URL for the 2019 Executive Board conclusion (https://www.imf.org/en/News/Articles/2019/07/25/pr19288-eritrea-imf-executive-board-concludes-2019-article-iv-consultation) failed: direct curl and WebFetch returned repeated 403 (Akamai bot-block) / 503 across multiple retries and user agents; the r.jina.ai reader-proxy workaround also returned 403 (blocked by this environment's outbound proxy); the archive.org Wayback Machine API returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited) on repeated attempts, so no independent archive verification was possible either. The scratch file /tmp/eri_pr.html is the saved response from one of these direct-fetch attempts and confirms the failure mode: its <TITLE> is literally "Access Denied", with body text "You don't have permission to access ... pr19288 ... on this server" (Akamai edgesuite.net error page). This is a confirmed dead end, not a source — the same press release content was instead obtained via the africa-newsroom.com syndicated mirror, used as the url for er-imf-2019-article-iv-eb.

IMF Press Release No. 19/179 ("Eritrea: IMF Staff Completes 2019 Article IV Mission", May 22, 2019, https://www.imf.org/en/News/Articles/2019/05/22/pr19179-eritrea-imf-staff-completes-2019-article-iv-mission) suffered the same access limitation as PR 18/262 — only generic boilerplate genre-description text loaded; the substantive mission-findings text did not. Confirms only that a 2019 IMF staff mission occurred; adds no data beyond er-imf-2019-article-iv-eb, so it was not minted as a separate node.

Checked http://www.nseoeritrea.org and http://nseoeritrea.gov.er — both DNS resolution failures ("Could not resolve host"). Web searches for "Eritrea National Statistics Office CPI" and "National Statistics and Evaluation Office site" returned only third-party aggregators (Knoema, GHDx, DHS Program) describing NSEO as a historical data source cited by others (e.g. the 2002 DHS survey), never a live NSEO web presence or current release. No functioning NSEO domain exists; no current CPI, population, or budget release could be located under Eritrean government attribution.

https://mof.gov.er and https://www.mof.gov.er — connection reset by peer / CONNECT tunnel failure (502) / ConnectTimeout, no working site. https://www.eritrea.gov.er — DNS resolution failure, domain does not exist. Web search "Eritrea Ministry of Finance national budget 2024 2025" returned only World Bank Macro Poverty Outlook PDFs (World Bank-authored, not primary Eritrean government) and an unrelated business-directory page with no linked government document. No live Ministry of Finance or Ministry of National Development website, and no locatable national budget document of any vintage hosted by the Eritrean government itself.

Web search "Asmara municipality official document budget" returned: the UNESCO heritage nomination document (non-financial — see separate dropped entry below), a Wikipedia article on "Administrations of Asmara" (excluded as non-primary), an unrelated South African municipality (Metsimaholo), an Archnet architecture-database entry, and a private Dutch enthusiast site (asmera.nl) — none primary/government-financial. No Asmara city government website, no municipal budget, no municipal statistical release found anywhere.

No dedicated zoba-by-zoba search was completed this round beyond the general searches above — the WebSearch tool hit its per-session call cap partway through the task. Eritrea's six zobas (Maekel, Debub, Anseba, Gash-Barka, Semienawi Keyih Bahri, Debubawi Keyih Bahri) returned no results in any general query, and no zoba-specific web domain surfaced. Per the findings file, this should be flagged as incompletely checked rather than a confirmed absence (unlike the Ministry of Finance and NSEO items above, which had multiple independent negative signals) and revisited in a future round.

A genuine Eritrean-government-authored primary document does exist: the State Party submission to UNESCO/ICOMOS, "Interim Report Responses for: Nomination of Asmara: Africa's Modernist City" (compiled to February 2017, https://whc.unesco.org/document/156800), quoting "The justification for Criteria (ii) was made in the formal submission to UNESCO in January 2016 and augmented in November 2016..." and attributed to the State Party of Eritrea via the Department of Public Works Development / Asmara Heritage Project. It shows Eritrea's government is capable of producing documents for international bodies, but it is a heritage/urban-planning nomination dossier confirmed to contain "no budget information, municipal financial data, or detailed governance statistics" over 100+ pages. Not usable as a fiscal/municipal-finance node; its absence of financial content, if anything, reinforces the no-funded-municipal-disclosure conclusion already recorded via er-un-coi-proclamation-86-1996.

_headline: DISCLOSURE RUNS UPWARD, NOT DOWNWARD. Two EU instruments have been followed to the national boundary and neither names a member-state publication (Annex XI, Annex B — both recorded as _dropped in eu-draft-budget.json). But member-state documents DO name the EU instrument: two German inventories each state they compile GDP/GNI 'in compliance with' ESA 2010, which is an obligation and not Research.1.md 5a agreement language. The asymmetry is the result — the supranational layer does not name its inputs, and the national layer does name its obligations.
_open_questions: CADENCE for the two Destatis inventories is not stated by either document, so neither is minted — see the no-node-yet entries. Evidence exists for a five-year cycle (HERP benchmark revisions at reference years ending 0/5 and implementation years ending 4/9; 'most recent major revision took place in 2024, and the next is scheduled for 2029'; 'Eurostat GNI verification cycle 2020 to 2024') but that is the REVISION cycle, not a stated publication cadence for the inventories, and the two inventories in hand are Edition 2025 and Edition 2024 — one year apart, which the five-year reading does not explain. Deliberately not guessed: ISSAI 300/400 were refused on the same ground in eu-draft-budget.json and consistency is worth more here than one extra node.

ESA 2010's releases_per_year of 0.05 mirrors sna-2008 exactly (also 0.05, also a generational standard). Observed ESA intervals are shorter than that implies — ESA 1995 to ESA 2010 is 15 years, and a further revision is already named in an ESAC opinion ('the revised European System of Accounts (ESA) in line with the newly endorsed System of National Accounts (SNA 2025)'). 0.067 would fit the observed intervals better. Matched to the corpus precedent rather than the arithmetic; flag if the precedent is the thing that is wrong.

reports.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.
reports.cadence_note: A generational standard, revised roughly once every fifteen to twenty years: ESA 1995 preceded it, and a further revision is already anticipated. releases_per_year matches sna-2008 (0.05) so the two read at the same pulse rate; see _open_questions.

release_schedule.note: 2030 is Eurostat's stated aim, not a locked legal date — the ESA 2030 proposal is still in consultation.

reports.title: ESA 2010 Methods and Sources for the German GNI (Gross National Income) and Its Components
reports.description: Destatis's own detailed inventory of the methods and sources used to compile Germany's GDP and GNI 'in compliance with the European System of National Accounts (ESA) 2010'. Its own colophon states 'Periodicity: non-recurring', Research.1.md 4.2's exact one-off disqualifier -- but the same document has a section headed 'Revisions policy and major revisions since the 2021 inventory', and the landing page's 'Older editions' heading links a 2016 edition, so at minimum three editions demonstrably exist (2016, 2021, 2025 -- current edition, published 12 March 2026). Minted as a regular node 2026-08-08 on Thomas's ruling (Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx Q2): treat 'non-recurring' as a per-publication metadata label rather than a hard disqualifier, and estimate a cadence from the observed interval for the pulse animation.
reports.cadence_note: ESTIMATED, not stated: the document's own colophon says 'Periodicity: non-recurring' and names no publication schedule. The 2021-to-2025 gap between its own cited predecessor and the current edition is the only observed interval (4 years, releases_per_year 0.25); the landing page's separate 2016 edition is noted but not used for the estimate, since the 2016-to-2021 gap (5 years) and 2021-to-2025 gap (4 years) are not the same length and this project does not average intervals from different revision regimes without evidence they are the same cycle. Per Thomas's Q2 ruling this is an estimate for the pulse visualisation, not a documented cadence.

release_schedule.note: Destatis's ESA 2010 Methods and Sources page shows only two editions on record: 'Edition 2016' (previous) and 'Edition 2025' (current, dated 12 March 2026). No release calendar, no stated periodicity rule, and no consistent multi-point pattern was found (only two data points, ~9 years apart). This document is Germany's GNI Inventory required for EU 'own resources' GNI verification; such inventories are typically revised/updated when the European Commission's GNI Committee runs a verification cycle, which occurs at irregular multi-year intervals rather than a fixed schedule. releases_per_year=0.25 (implying a 4-year cycle) does not match the observed ~9-year gap between the only two known editions.

reports.title: Quarterly National Accounts Inventory Based on ESA 2010 Methodology
reports.description: Destatis's companion inventory for the quarterly national accounts, stating it 'contains the detailed description of the quarterly methods and sources used for the compilation of the gross domestic product of Germany in compliance with the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)' and that 'the structure of the description follows a uniform European standard that was developed by the Statistical Office of the European Communities'. Current edition dated 12 September 2024 ('Edition 2024'); an earlier, differently-numbered publication in the same territory (Fachserie 18 Reihe S.31, 'Edition 2017') is marked as its own series' last issue and may or may not be a true predecessor to the present standalone document -- not confirmed either way. Minted as a regular node 2026-08-08 on Thomas's ruling (Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx Q2), same as the GNI inventory.
reports.cadence_note: ESTIMATED, not stated: unlike the GNI inventory, this document carries no periodicity statement at all and names no confirmed predecessor edition -- the Fachserie 18 Reihe S.31 'last issue' (2017) found this session may be an unrelated, discontinued series rather than a true predecessor, and that was not run to ground. The 0.25 estimate is carried over from the GNI inventory's demonstrated interval on the reasoning that both inventories sit under the same Eurostat GNI-verification-style revision cycle, per Thomas's instruction to estimate for the pulse visualisation -- flagged as the weaker of the two estimates in this file.

release_schedule.note: The document is a methodological 'inventory' describing sources and methods for German Quarterly National Accounts under ESA 2010, published as numbered editions (current: 'Edition 2024', dated 12 September 2024). Neither the PDF itself nor the surrounding Destatis publication pages state an update frequency, edition history, or next planned release date. It appears to be revised irregularly, as needed when compilation methodology changes, rather than on a fixed schedule -- analogous to other EU member states' ESA 2010 national-accounts-inventory documents submitted to Eurostat, which are updated on an as-needed basis rather than a calendar.

dependencies.basis: The inventory states its own legal basis twice, in obligation and derivation language rather than 5a agreement language: 'The present document contains the detailed description of the methods and sources used for the compilation of the gross domestic product and the gross national income of the Federal Republic of Germany in compliance with the European System of National Accounts (ESA) 2010', and 'describes the methods and statistical sources used to calculate GDP and GNI at market prices for the Federal Republic of Germany based on the European System of Accounts (ESA) 2010'. 'In compliance with' and 'based on' name ESA 2010 as the rulebook the inventory's own compilation follows, the same relationship already established from the release side by de-destatis-national-accounts -> esa-2010.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The present document contains the detailed description of the methods and sources used for the compilation of the gross domestic product and the gross national income of the Federal Republic of Germany in compliance with the European System of National Accounts (ESA) 2010

dependencies.basis: RE-CITED 2026-09-05 (Round C): evidence_url moved from the Destatis landing page (3,943 chars, names ESA 2010 only in the file title) to the inventory PDF itself (54 pp, read live from the bridge VM), which is where the quoted sentence is. 'The present document contains the detailed description of the quarterly methods and sources used for the compilation of the gross domestic product of Germany in compliance with the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010).' A second sentence in the same document adds a further, distinct dependency not modelled as its own edge here: 'The structure of the description follows a uniform European standard that was developed by the Statistical Office of the European Communities' -- the inventory's own STRUCTURE, not just its content, is set by Eurostat.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The present document contains the detailed description of the quarterly methods and sources used for the compilation of the gross domestic product of Germany in compliance with the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010).

_dropped.why: A PREDICTED EDGE, REFUTED BY Research.1.md 5a. ESA 2010's own text says: 'The ESA 2010 is consistent with the worldwide guidelines on national accounting set out in the System of National Accounts 2008 (2008 SNA)' (Annex A, Chapter 1, paragraph 1.05). 'Consistent with' is verbatim on 5a's watchlist and is agreement between two frameworks, not derivation of one from the other. Two further records say it the same way and were already flagged by the original extractor: the supply-and-use manual — 'The ESA 1995 is fully consistent with the world-wide System of National Accounts (SNA 1993)' — and Eurostat's national accounts page — 'This system is fully consistent with the worldwide guidelines on national accounting, the System of national accounts (SNA).' Three independent statements, all agreement language, none a dependency. Per 5a this is worth recording precisely because the link is plausible enough to be re-proposed every few months; it was re-proposed this session.
