The substantive finding this entry chases — a documented member-state-to-ESA-2010 dependency — is already built, via a different German document: de-destatis-national-accounts (releases_per_year 4, 'National Accounts — Domestic Product (Fachserie 18)') carries a live methodology_depends_on edge to esa-2010, sourced from the same Destatis quality report and inventories. This specific methods-INVENTORY document (as opposed to the release it describes) is still not itself a node, and the conflict below is still unresolved on its own terms — nothing here adjudicates it. THE BEST CROSS-LAYER CANDIDATE FOUND SO FAR, and the direction is the surprise. Destatis: 'The present document contains the detailed description of the methods and sources used for the compilation of the gross domestic product and the gross national income of the Federal Republic of Germany in compliance with the European System of National Accounts (ESA) 2010.' A second record from the same document: 'describes the methods and statistical sources used to calculate GDP and GNI at market prices for the Federal Republic of Germany based on the European System of Accounts (ESA) 2010.' 'In compliance with' and 'based on' are obligation and derivation language, NOT 5a agreement language — a real methodology_depends_on running from a member-state publication to the EU instrument. NOT MINTED, and the cadence question was looked up on 2026-08-05 rather than left open. THE ANSWER IS A DOCUMENTED CONFLICT, reported per 3 and not adjudicated. The publication's own colophon states 'Periodicity: non-recurring' (Statistisches Bundesamt, published March 2026), which is Research.1.md 4.2's exact disqualifier — 'something published once is not a node'. But the SAME DOCUMENT names its own predecessor: section 1.2 is headed 'Revisions policy and major revisions since the 2021 inventory', and the Destatis landing page carries an 'Older editions' heading. So a 2021 edition and a 2025 edition demonstrably exist, four years apart, consistent with the Eurostat GNI verification cycle documented elsewhere in the corpus ('Eurostat action points from the GNI verification cycle 2020 to 2024'). Reading: 'non-recurring' is most likely a per-publication metadata label meaning 'not a scheduled series release' rather than a claim that no further inventory will appear — but that is an inference about what the publisher meant, and 6 says do not guess a cadence to make the JSON validate. If the other end of the process reads 'non-recurring' as a metadata artefact, releases_per_year 0.25 is the number the observed 2021->2025 interval supports.

_headline: The corpus's biggest documented classification gap (esa2010-quality-reporting.json's dropped 'esa-2010 -> NACE, CPA, COICOP, COFOG, NUTS' entry, itself declined for citing a bulleted list rather than programme-level prose) now has its first resolved member: CPA is a real node, reached the way §7 prescribes -- not by reading CPA's own documentation for edges, but by reading a downstream programme (ESA 2010's own Annex A, a specific numbered paragraph, not a bulleted summary list) stating in flowing prose that it uses CPA for products.
_open_questions: The esa-2010 -> cpa edge rests on ESA 2010 Annex A, Chapter 1, paragraph 1.22 as staged in EU/slices/_staging -- NOT independently re-verified live this session (a WebFetch attempt against the consolidated ESA 2010 PDF, eur-lex.europa.eu CELEX 32013R0549, could not locate paragraph 1.22 within the tool's read window; the document is long enough that this is inconclusive rather than a failed check). UPDATE: the same paragraph was independently staged THREE times, in three different batches, on the same original 2026-08-02 extraction session -- batch 8 (record esa2010-cpa-ref, the shorter form quoted in the dependency's basis), and batches 6 and 7 (records esa2010-a-1.22 / esa2010-nace-1.22, a longer form that includes a first sentence the batch-8 version omits: 'The ESA 2010 employs concepts and classifications (e.g. Statistical classification of economic activities in the European Union "NACE rev. 2" ...) that are used for other social and economic statistics of Member States ... Furthermore, the concepts and classifications in the ESA 2010 are harmonised with those of the United Nations. ...'). All three stagings agree verbatim on the operative sentence used as this edge's basis. Cross-batch agreement across three independent extraction passes is not the same as live re-verification, but it is real corroboration, and is noted here as such rather than left as a single unverified data point.

Judgement call, flagged for a future session to revisit rather than silently made: this dependency is structurally similar in kind (a document naming multiple classifications together, one of which was declined before) to the bundled-list entry esa2010-quality-reporting.json already declined to mint from -- e.g. 'contains EU-specific classifications, e.g. Classification of products by activity (CPA) ... for products and NACE Rev. 2 for industries'. The distinction drawn here: that declined entry came from a Eurostat *quality report about* ESA 2010 (a third document) citing a bulleted, multi-item heading with no per-item location; this one comes from ESA 2010's *own* Annex A text, in prose, at one specific numbered paragraph -- closer in kind to §7's naics precedent ('every edge into NAICS came from a survey's methodology page saying it classifies its respondents by NAICS') than to the declined list. If a future session judges this distinction wrong, this edge should be moved to _dropped with the same reasoning already on file for its four siblings (NACE, COICOP, COFOG, NUTS).

reports.title: Statistical Requirements Compendium (SRC)
reports.description: Catalogue number KS-01-26-011 (2026 edition). Eurostat's own foreword: 'Eurostat, the statistical office of the European Union, publishes each year the Statistical Requirements Compendium (SRC), an essential reference document for the EU statistical acquis... It offers a comprehensive overview of the key reference elements required for the production of European statistics, including applicable legal acts, documentation needed for data compilation, methodological guidelines, data and metadata transmission requirements, and cooperation frameworks with international organisations across different thematic areas.' Its own summary adds it 'also serves as the framework for conducting compliance monitoring of the enlargement countries... in the field of statistics.' The item this file's own subject (item 5 of Research.1.md §8) was originally named for -- 'Eurostat's own structural publications. The Statistical Requirements Compendium and its data-requirement tables' -- now minted.
reports.cadence_note: Explicit annual cadence, stated directly by the document's own foreword ('publishes each year') and confirmed by the edition number (2026 edition, catalogue KS-01-26-011, following a 2024/2025 sequence the document's own summary references).

entries.covers: Statistical requirements compendium – 2027 edition (projected next release)

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar exists for this title, but Eurostat has issued a new edition every year for two decades (editions found dating back to 2005), each released in the first third of the year (mid-March to mid-April in the four most recent years). The 2026 edition (KS-01-26-011) was released 20 March 2026. Next edition (2027, likely catalogue KS-01-27-0xx) is projected for around Q1 2027 based on this pattern; exact date not published in advance.

reports.title: Handbook on Quarterly National Accounts
reports.description: Eurostat's own methodological guidance for compiling quarterly national accounts (QNA), catalogue number KS-GQ-13-004. Its own introduction: 'This handbook is an update of the 1999 edition... including the update of ESA 2010 and associated transmission programme.' States that 'Chapter 12 of ESA 2010 describes and defines the major principles and characteristics of QNA' and that QNA's coverage 'is the same as that of ANA [annual national accounts]: they encompass the entire sequence of accounts and the corresponding aggregates as well as the supply and use framework.'
reports.cadence_note: Two editions confirmed by the document's own text: 1999 (original) and 2013 (the current, 'update' edition, catalogue KS-GQ-13-004). 14-year observed interval, releases_per_year 1/14 ≈ 0.07 -- the same 'latest observed interval' convention used elsewhere in this corpus for irregular recurring documents. Only one interval is known; a third edition would sharpen this.

release_schedule.note: No update schedule stated by Eurostat. The 2013 edition (KS-GQ-13-004) is explicitly described as an update of the 1999 original, motivated by ESA2010 adoption and 14 years of practical experience -- not by a fixed periodicity. No third edition or revision timeline has been announced as of 2026-08-11.

reports.title: Quarterly Non-Financial Accounts for General Government
reports.description: Eurostat's own ESMS metadata page (dataset gov_10q_ggnfa): 'The data correspond to quarterly non-financial accounts for the general government sector which are conceptually consistent with the corresponding annual data compiled on a national accounts (ESA 2010) basis.' Primarily derived from 'administrative and other records of general government', benchmarked against annual GFS data once more detailed annual information is available.
reports.cadence_note: Eurostat's own ESMS Timeliness section: 'Quarterly data are to be delivered three months after the end of the quarter to which the data relate. Quarterly data are released at around t+112 days after the reference quarter.'

entries.covers: Q2 2026 quarterly government finance statistics (deficit/debt and non-financial accounts)

release_schedule.rule: Quarterly data are to be delivered three months after the end of the quarter to which the data relate. Quarterly data are released at around t+112 days after the reference quarter.
release_schedule.note: Eurostat's ESMS Timeliness section states the t+112 day rule; the corpus's own euro-indicators press releases confirm the pattern (e.g. 21 July 2026 release covered Q1 2026 data, ~112 days after 31 March 2026 quarter-end). A Eurostat/KSH mirrored press release document explicitly states 'Next release: 21 October 2026' for the euro indicators series that includes this quarterly government data, which aligns with the t+112 rule applied to the Q2 2026 reference quarter (30 June 2026 + ~112 days).

reports.title: Manual on Quarterly Non-Financial Accounts for General Government
reports.description: Methodological guidance and Member-State compilation-practice reference for the quarterly non-financial general-government accounts. Eurostat's own ESMS page (data compilation section): 'A Manual on Compilation of Taxes and Social Payments on a Quarterly Basis was first published in 2002. A Manual on Quarterly Non-Financial Accounts for General Government (2006) replaces the first manual providing methodological guidance and describing Member States' compilation practices for all ESA95 transactions. An updated Manual on Quarterly Non-Financial Accounts for General Government (2011 edition) was released in September 2011.' Treated here as the lineage beginning with the 2006 title (the 2002 predecessor carries a different title and is recorded as historical context, not the same node).
reports.cadence_note: 2006 (first edition under this title) to 2011 (updated edition): 5-year observed interval, releases_per_year 1/5 = 0.2. The 2002 predecessor (different title, 'Manual on Compilation of Taxes and Social Payments on a Quarterly Basis') is not used in the interval calculation.

release_schedule.note: This is a methodological/compilation manual, not a periodic statistical release. Eurostat's own metadata (gov_10q_ggnfa_esms.htm) documents editions in 2002, 2006, and 2011 (2011 edition released September 2011, product code KS-RA-11-017), and states an ESA2010-methodology update 'is planned' -- but no such update has been found published as of August 2026, 15 years after it was announced as planned. There is no release calendar and no stated rule with a computable next date; updates occur ad hoc when major accounting-standard revisions (e.g. ESA95->ESA2010) occur, not on a fixed schedule.

reports.title: Manual on Quarterly Financial Accounts for General Government
reports.description: Catalogue number KS-GQ-17-012. Eurostat's own publication summary: 'The second edition of the Manual on Quarterly Financial Accounts for General Government provides a detailed insight into the sources and methods used by countries to compile the data on quarterly financial accounts for general government... It integrates ESA 2010 concepts and documents improvements in compilation practices achieved since the first edition... compiled under the supervision of the Government Finance Statistics Task Force and validated by the Excessive Deficit Procedure Working Group.' The manual's own preface: 'reflecting the change from ESA95 to ESA2010.' Background section: the material 'was later used to produce, in 2008, the first version of the Manual on sources and methods for quarterly financial accounts for general government. This version, the 2017 version, is the first update of the manual.'
reports.cadence_note: Two editions confirmed by the manual's own text: 2008 (first version) and 2017 (second edition, 'the first update'). 9-year observed interval, releases_per_year 1/9 ≈ 0.11.

release_schedule.note: Only two editions have ever been published: 2008 (first version, KS-RA-08-006) and 2017 (second edition, KS-GQ-17-012, released 17-11-2017, described in its own text as 'the first update'). As of 2026-08-11 (nearly 9 years after the 2nd edition), no third edition, revision, or update has been published, and Eurostat's product page and the Government Finance Statistics publications listing show no stated revision cycle or announced next edition. With only two historical data points and no confirmed third edition despite the prior ~9-year gap having already elapsed, this is better classified as irregular than as a reliable observed-pattern with a computable next date.

reports.title: Manual on Government Deficit and Debt – Implementation of ESA 2010 (MGDD)
reports.description: Catalogue number KS-GQ-23-002 (2022 edition, current). Its own preface: 'Eurostat publishes the Manual on Government Deficit and Debt – ESA Implementation (MGDD) complementing or interpreting the general rules of ESA 2010... The MGDD, first published in 1999, provides guidance on the appropriate statistical treatment of specific government operations as well clarifications on the issues raised in the European Union regarding government finance statistics. It is an indispensable complement to ESA 2010.' Sets out that 'the reference values for deficit and debt are based on concepts defined in the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010)', that the government surplus/deficit is 'in national accounts referred to as the net lending (+)/borrowing (–) (B.9)', and that debt is 'the total consolidated gross debt at face value' in categories 'defined in ESA 2010'. States ESA 2010 records transactions 'on an accrual basis, i.e., when the economic activity takes place, rather than when the cash is paid.'
reports.cadence_note: First published 1999; current edition 2022 (KS-GQ-23-002). Live-checked this session (not in the staged batch) for intermediate editions, since a 1999-to-2022 span alone would be a poor cadence estimate: confirmed editions found at 2014 (KS-GQ-14-010), 2016 (KS-GQ-16-001), 2019 (KS-GQ-19-007), 2022 (KS-GQ-23-002). Using the latest observed interval (2019 to 2022, 3 years) per this corpus's standing convention: releases_per_year 1/3 ≈ 0.33.

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar and no stated periodicity rule exists for the MGDD. Eurostat's own product page for the 2022 edition (KS-GQ-23-002) describes it only as 'an updated version of the edition published in August 2019' with no indication of a next-edition date or fixed cycle. Web search in August 2026 found no announcement of a forthcoming edition. This confirms the existing cadence_note's characterization: releases occur irregularly whenever ESA 2010 methodological guidance needs updating, and the corpus's convention of using the latest observed interval (2019 to 2022 announcement, ~3.5 years) for releases_per_year ≈ 0.33 remains the best available estimate — no new evidence to correct it.

reports.title: Statistical Classification of Products by Activity in the European Economic Community (CPA)
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: Established by Regulation (EC) No 451/2008. Article 1(1): 'This Regulation establishes a new common CPA within the Community in order to ensure relevance with respect to the economic reality and comparability between national, Community and international classifications and hence national, Community and international statistics.' Article 3: 'The Commission shall use the CPA for all statistics classified according to products by activity.' A six-level hierarchical structure (Article 2(1)): sections, divisions, groups, classes, categories, subcategories. CPA Version 2.2 has applied for data transmissions since 1 January 2025. One-off foundational instrument per Research.1.md §4 (a classification standard, same shape as naics/isic/anzsic already in this corpus) -- amended periodically (2.1, 2.2) but read here from its current consolidated form, not as a recast lineage with its own cadence.

A catalogue entry naming ESA 2010 as the legal basis for one of its own reference sections, not a computational input the SRC's own content is derived from -- cites, the same treatment eu-manual-mgdd's Regulation 479/2009 reference above received, for the same reason (a reference/index document's own legal-basis citations describe what it catalogs, not what it is built from).

dependencies.evidence_quote: The reference values for deficit and debt are based on concepts defined in the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010).

Cited as the legal framework the manual operates under, not a source the manual's own content is derived from -- cites, not methodology_depends_on.

dependencies.basis: ESA 2010, Annex A, Chapter 1, paragraph 1.22 (as staged, not independently re-verified live this session -- see _open_questions): 'The ESA 2010 contains EU-specific classifications, e.g. Classification of products by activity (CPA) ... for products and NACE Rev. 2 for industries (both are harmonised with the corresponding UN classifications).' The 'harmonised with the corresponding UN classifications' clause is the §5a trap (not a dependency, not used as one); the operative clause -- ESA 2010 'contains' and uses CPA for products -- is read as the dependency, on the same footing as a survey's methodology page stating it classifies respondents by NAICS.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The ESA 2010 contains EU-specific classifications, e.g. Classification of products by activity (CPA) ... for products and NACE Rev. 2 for industries (both are harmonised with the corresponding UN classifications).

The blocker this entry recorded was the missing node, not the missing evidence: `nace-rev2` was minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round, and the edge `esa-2010 -> nace-rev2` is now live at A, `methodology_depends_on`. What this entry asked for was 'NACE's own Article text (or a national/EU release's own methodology page stating it classifies by NACE)'. NEITHER WAS WHAT CLOSED IT. The evidence is ESA 2010's own Annex A, Chapter 2: 'The classification used for grouping local KAUs into industries is the NACE Rev. 2.' — the source document speaking about itself, which is stronger than either route this entry proposed, and which was inside the document the whole time. The retrieval problem it describes is also gone but not the way it expected: EUR-Lex still serves this container nothing (an AWS WAF challenge, HTTP 202, zero bytes), and Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 was read from CELLAR, the Publications Office's own repository, at http://publications.europa.eu/resource/cellar/41239b25-9bba-4c36-9b25-926d90511bb3.0007.02/DOC_1 . Original entry follows.

Per Research.1.md §6 a confirmed title is not a substitute for a verbatim quote. The same ESA 2010 Annex A 1.22 paragraph names NACE Rev. 2 for industries in the same sentence that supports the cpa edge above -- once NACE's own Article text (or a national/EU release's own methodology page stating it classifies by NACE, the way r3-netherlands-poland.json's SBR register already does in passing for a different node) is in hand, this edge is one step away, not a fresh search.

EUR-Lex summary, Key points: 'The CPA is connected to the United Nations' products and services classification, the Central Product Classification (CPC), via a correspondence table.' A correspondence/comparability table between two classifications, not a dependency -- same §5a shape as CPA's own 'consistent with'/'harmonised with' language toward NACE (see the minted edge's basis note). CPC is not a node in this corpus and this quote would not be grounds to mint one even if it were: correspondence tables document alignment, not derivation.

No edge between cpa and nace is minted from this material; the two classifications' relationship is structural/taxonomic (CPA products map onto NACE activities down to the fourth level), not one input feeding another.

_dropped.edge: ESA 2010 Annex A -- general government sector (S.13) definition, market/non-market producer test, control criteria (batches 6+7, 15 records: esa2010-a-1.34/1.35/2.35/2.38/2.39/2.111/2.113/3.19/3.24/3.26/3.37, esa2010-50pct-3.19/1.37/3.32/3.37)
_dropped.why: All fifteen records are ESA 2010's OWN definitional text -- how the Regulation itself defines the general government sector (S.13, Annex A 2.111: 'institutional units which are non-market producers whose output is intended for individual and collective consumption... financed by compulsory payments'), its four subsectors (2.113: S.1311-S.1314), the market/non-market boundary (the 50% cost-coverage-by-sales test, 3.19/3.32/1.37), and the control-criteria checklist that pulls a government-controlled corporation into or out of general government (2.38's eight indicators, 2.39's five non-profit indicators). No OTHER document is named anywhere in this material -- it is entirely ESA 2010 describing its own classification apparatus, the same shape Research.1.md §7 warns produces almost nothing when read for edges ('Do not research a classification standard by reading the classification'). Kept as one bundled entry rather than fifteen, per the same convention esa2010-quality-reporting.json's own classification-gap entry used, because it is one finding (this material yields no edges) rather than fifteen separate findings. Genuinely useful as corroborating detail for esa-2010's own description if a future session wants to enrich it, and as the primary-source backing for the 50% market/non-market rule that other EU-branch files already invoke by name (e.g. eurostat-edp-gfs-ecb-statistics.json's cadence notes reference 'general-government exposure breakdowns'); not pursued further here since enriching an existing node's description is not this item's task.

_dropped.edge: ESA 2010 Annex A accrual-basis / time-of-recording rules and their government/tax exceptions (batches 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 -- 8 distinct paragraphs, staged five times with heavy overlap)
_dropped.why: The fundamental accrual principle (1.101: flows recorded 'when economic value is created, transformed or extinguished'; 1.102: output/asset-sale/interest examples; 1.105: same-point-in-time recording across units), its explicit relaxation for government cash-basis source data (1.103), the exception for uncollectible taxes and social contributions so they do not distort net lending/borrowing (1.104), and the operational time-adjusted-cash method for taxes (4.26, 4.150(b)) are all ESA 2010's own internal accounting rules -- no other document is named anywhere across all five batches, so no edge is extractable, the same conclusion as batches 6+7's classification rules above and for the identical reason (Research.1.md §7). WORTH FLAGGING SEPARATELY FROM THE CONTENT FINDING: these five batches (11-15) are near-duplicates of one another, not five distinct threads -- all quote paragraph 1.101 identically (batches 11 and 14), all quote 1.103/1.104 identically (batches 11, 12, 13, 15), and 12/13/15 each also carry the same 4.26/4.150 time-adjusted-cash material under slightly different framing headers ('exceptions to the accrual basis', 'cash basis rules', 'exceptions to the accrual basis' again). This looks like an artifact of how the original 2026-08-02 splitting session scoped its stop conditions batch by batch rather than five genuinely different provisions -- worth knowing for whoever next reads 01-manifest.json's scope strings closely: a batch count is not the same as a distinct-content count, even within one coherent subject.

_headline: THE REGULATION WILL NOT NAME THE STANDARD; THE REPORT PUBLISHED UNDER THE REGULATION NAMES IT OUTRIGHT. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2304 recital (5) refers only to 'the European Statistical System standards on quality reporting published by the Commission (Eurostat)' — AGENCY ONLY, and a search of all 24,942 characters for SIMS, ESMS, ESQRS or Handbook returns nothing. The Eurostat report produced under that same Regulation says the assessment adheres 'to the requirements for the Single Integrated Metadata Structure'. Same standard; only the non-legislative document will say its name. That is G.50.md's two-layer finding — legislative layer names nobody, self-regulatory layer names its sources freely — reproduced inside ONE chain, with the boundary falling exactly between an instrument and the report published under it.
_second_finding: THE TWO INSTRUMENTS ARE COMPLEMENTARY FAILURES, AND THAT IS WHY NO MEMBER-STATE NODE EXISTS IN EITHER SLICE. Regulation 479/2009 Article 9(4) compels a PUBLISHED national document ('Member States shall make their inventories public') but states no interval, only an event trigger. Implementing Regulation 2016/2304 states the interval ('Member States shall provide the quality report on an annual basis') and compels NO publication — searched for 'shall be made public', 'publish', 'publication', 'public' across the whole instrument; the two hits are Eurostat's own standards and the Regulation's entry into force. Each instrument supplies exactly what the other lacks and neither supplies both. Two slices, two compelled national document classes, 54 documents in principle, and zero mintable member-state nodes — for two different and individually sufficient reasons.
_third_finding: THE EU COMPELS THE NAMING IT WILL NOT DO ITSELF. Annex 4.2 indicator 2 of 2016/2304 requires each Member State to supply a 'List of national publications on the data sources used and methodology applied containing the titles of these publications and links to them, if available' — annually, all 27. Every EU instrument this branch has followed has stopped at AGENCY ONLY at the national boundary, and this one does too on its own face. But it REQUIRES the member states to name their own publications by title. Read against EU/slices/README.md's disclosure-runs-upward finding, this is a candidate mechanism for that asymmetry: the upward disclosure may not be voluntary candour at the national end but a reporting requirement drafted at the supranational end. Offered as an observation, not a conclusion — establishing it would need a national quality report, and none is published.
_open_questions: THE CHEAPEST HIGH-VALUE TEST IN THE EU BRANCH IS NOW SPECIFIC: does any Member State publish its own ESA 2010 quality report voluntarily? Nothing compels it (see _second_finding), but nothing forbids it either, and one such document would be a list of national statistical publications by title with links — the 'document that names its own inputs in a table' that Research.1.md §7 calls the strongest evidence class there is, for one country, annually. If even one exists, the member-state layer opens by a route neither Annex B nor Annex XI nor Article 9 of 479/2009 could open. If none exists, that is a measured negative across 27 jurisdictions and worth as much.

reports.title: Quality report on national and regional accounts
reports.description: Eurostat's annual assessment of the quality of the national and regional accounts data that Member States transmit under the ESA 2010 transmission programme, produced under Article 4 of Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 and structured by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2304. In its own words: 'This document presents Eurostat's assessment of the quality of national and regional accounts data submitted by the EU Member States, as well as Iceland, Norway and Switzerland, in 2024. It also includes information on the quality of key European aggregates published by Eurostat. The assessment in this quality report is based on the national quality reports exercise for data transmissions during 2024.' Distinct from eurostat-edp-gfs-quality-report, which is the Article 8(3) report on fiscal data under Regulation 479/2009 — the two are adjacent and easily conflated. This node is the one document in the chain that names the Single Integrated Metadata Structure by name; the Regulation governing it does not.
reports.cadence_note: Stated by the publication itself — 'It is the eighth such report since the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010) was introduced in September 2014' — and corroborated by eight observed editions across 2018-2025 (KS-FT-18-004, KS-FT-19-009, KS-FT-20-007, KS-FT-21-009, KS-FT-22-008, KS-FT-23-002, KS-01-24-023, KS-01-25-052) and by ISSN 2529-3222. The underlying obligation is annual on its face: 'Member States shall provide the quality report on an annual basis' (Implementing Regulation 2016/2304, Article 1). See _open_questions on the reference-year gap.

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar or stated publication-timing rule found; Eurostat's Implementing Regulation 2016/2304 Article 1 sets an annual obligation for Member States to submit quality data to Eurostat, but does not fix when Eurostat itself must publish the resulting report. Observed publication dates of past editions cluster in November-December each year: 2025 edition published 12 Nov 2025 (KS-01-25-052); 2024 edition 13 Dec 2024 (KS-01-24-023); 2023 edition 19 Dec 2023 (KS-FT-23-002); 2022 edition 15 Dec 2022 (KS-FT-22-008); 2021 edition 17 Dec 2021 (KS-FT-21-009); 2020 edition 18 Dec 2020 (KS-FT-20-007). Based on this consistent annual Nov-Dec pattern, the next (ninth) edition is expected around November-December 2026, but no exact date can be confirmed in advance.

reports.title: Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council on European statistics
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: The framework Regulation for European statistics, and the legal spine EU/slices/README.md names alongside ESA 2010 and the EBS Regulation. Two of its articles do work across this corpus. Article 11 constitutes the European Statistics Code of Practice: 'The Code of Practice shall aim at ensuring public trust in European statistics by establishing how European statistics are to be developed, produced and disseminated in conformity with the statistical principles as set out in Article 2(1) and best international statistical practice', and 'The Code of Practice shall be reviewed and updated as necessary by the ESS Committee. The Commission shall publish amendments thereto.' Article 12(1) sets the seven quality criteria — relevance, accuracy, timeliness, punctuality, accessibility and clarity, comparability, coherence — that ESA 2010 Article 4(1) applies to transmitted data and that Implementing Regulation 2016/2304 structures the national quality reports around. Minted 2026-08-07 after G.50.md filed it deferred when EUR-Lex served nothing; the retry G.50 recommended succeeded.
reports.cadence_note: Derived from an observed amendment record, not a stated rate, on the same basis as eu-reg-479-2009 in the sibling slice. Adopted 11 March 2009; EUR-Lex lists two consolidated versions, 08/06/2015 and 26/12/2024, with 26/12/2024 flagged as current. Two amendments across the 17 years to 2026.

release_schedule.note: Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 is a standing legal act (the framework regulation governing the European Statistical System), not a periodically released publication. It has been amended irregularly as legislative need arose — e.g. by Regulation (EU) 2015/759, Regulation (EU) 2019/2152 (ESS governance regulation), and most recently Regulation (EU) 2024/... (in force from 26 Dec 2024, reflected in the consolidated text CELEX:02009R0223-20241226). No article of the regulation sets a fixed periodic review/evaluation date, and no publisher calendar exists for future amendments — the timing of the next amendment (if any) depends on future Commission legislative proposals and cannot be computed.

reports.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2304 of 19 December 2016 on the modalities, structure, periodicity and assessment indicators of the quality reports on data transmitted pursuant to Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council
reports.description: The Implementing Regulation that structures the annual national-accounts quality reports Member States submit under ESA 2010 (Regulation 549/2013) — the same instrument eurostat-national-accounts-quality-report's own description already names as what it is 'structured by'. Article 1 sets the periodicity for the underlying obligation, not for itself: 'Member States shall provide the quality report on an annual basis' with reports due no later than 31 May each year. Minted 2026-08-08 as a one-off foundational instrument under Research.1.md §4 (Thomas's ruling): adopted once (19 December 2016) and never amended — EUR-Lex shows no consolidated version — which is exactly the shape the new rule was written to admit; previously excluded under the old §4.2 language ('something published once is not a node'), recorded in this file's _dropped array until today. No predecessor is named anywhere in the instrument or in G.50/G.52's research, so it is not read as a recast — a genuine one-off, not a lineage's current edition.

dependencies.basis: Quality report on national and regional accounts, 2025 edition (KS-01-25-052), Executive summary, page 5: 'The quality report covers a number of quality indicators (completeness, revision policy and practice, punctuality, coherence and documentation on methodology), adhering to the requirements for the Single Integrated Metadata Structure, which were endorsed by the European Statistical System Committee in November 2015.' dependencies.basis: Quality report on national and regional accounts, 2025 edition (KS-01-25-052), Executive summary, page 5: 'This requires the quality of national and regional accounts data sent to Eurostat to be assessed against the quality criteria set out in the Regulation on European statistics (Regulation (EC) No 223/2009).' The information shall be presented according to the following structure: Relevance; Accuracy and reliability; Timeliness and punctuality; Accessibility and clarity; Coherence and comparability.' dependencies.basis: Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, consolidated text of 24/08/2015, Article 4(1) ('Quality assessment'): 'For the purpose of this Regulation, the quality criteria set out in Article 12(1) of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 shall apply to the data to be transmitted in accordance with Article 3 of this Regulation.' 'Shall apply' is application of one instrument's criteria by another, not comparability — §5a does not reach it. Direction: ESA 2010 is the dependent, taking its quality criteria from the framework Regulation. NOTE THAT THIS IS esa-2010'S FIRST OUTGOING DEPENDENCY IN THE CORPUS: it was imported with zero, and its only previously proposed outgoing edge (esa-2010 -> sna-2008) is refused by §5a in esa-2010.json and refused again by a fourth independent statement found this session (see _dropped). Read from EUR-Lex 2026-08-07.
dependencies.evidence_quote: For the purpose of this Regulation, the quality criteria set out in Article 12(1) of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 shall apply to the data to be transmitted in accordance with Article 3 of this Regulation.

_dropped.why: G.50.md's DEFERRED ITEM, NOW SETTLED — AND NOT THE WAY IT EXPECTED. G.50 filed this edge deferred purely on retrieval: EUR-Lex served nothing, and the staged Article 11(1)/(2) quotes 'would support both a Regulation node and this edge'. The retry G.50 recommended succeeded, both articles are verified verbatim, and the Regulation node is minted above. THE EDGE IS STILL NOT MINTED, for a reason invisible from the Regulation's side. The Code of Practice's own preamble says: 'The common quality framework of the European Statistical System is composed of the European Statistics Code of Practice, the Quality Assurance Framework of the European Statistical System and the general quality management principles … This self-regulatory common quality framework COMPLEMENTS the extensive legal framework of the European Statistical System based on the Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 on European statistics which itself derives from the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.' 'Complements' is §5a family, and it is not loose phrasing — the sentence exists to draw a line between a 'self-regulatory' framework and a 'legal framework' and to put the Code of Practice on the self-regulatory side. Against that, Regulation 223/2009 Article 11 asserts authority over the Code: 'The Code of Practice shall aim at ensuring public trust in European statistics by establishing how European statistics are to be developed, produced and disseminated in conformity with the statistical principles as set out in Article 2(1)' and 'The Code of Practice shall be reviewed and updated as necessary by the ESS Committee.' TWO DOCUMENTS POINTING OPPOSITE WAYS, BOTH QUOTED, NEITHER PICKED, per Research.1.md §3. Reason moved from 'deferred' (a retrieval problem, solved) to a documented conflict. NOT FOUND: no other citation of Regulation 223/2009 anywhere in the CoP's 11 pages, and no occurrence of 'Article 11' (strings searched: '223/2009', 'Regulation (EC) No 223/2009', 'Article 11').

DOCUMENTED PLAINLY AND BLOCKED ON PUBLICATION, WHICH IS THE SLICE'S SECOND FINDING. The report says what it is built from: 'The assessment in this quality report is based on the national quality reports exercise for data transmissions during 2024.' The Implementing Regulation compels those reports annually from all 27 — 'Every year, not later than 31 May, Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat) with the completed quality report' — and NOTHING IN THE INSTRUMENT REQUIRES THEM TO BE PUBLISHED. Strings searched across all 24,942 characters of 2016/2304: 'shall be made public', 'publish', 'publication', 'public'. The only two hits are recital 5 (standards published by Eurostat) and Article 3 (the Regulation's own entry into force on publication in the Official Journal). Compare Regulation 479/2009 Article 9(4), 'Member States shall make their inventories public', which is what made the EDP inventories a published class in the sibling slice. Research.1.md §4 requires a node to be published on a cadence; these are produced on a cadence and not published. AGENCY ONLY as to which reports, additionally: neither the Regulation nor the Eurostat report names a single Member State's quality report.

THE TEMPTING EDGE, AND IT FAILS TWICE OVER. Recital (5): 'As the information in the quality reports on national and regional accounts should be based on the European Statistical System standards on quality reporting published by the Commission (Eurostat), the Annex to this Regulation should be drawn up in line with those standards.' The standard meant is SIMS — the report published under this very Regulation says so (see the minted edge above), and Eurostat's own quality-reporting page says 'The ESS quality reporting standard is the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS)', which is what G.50.md minted ess-sims on. But the Regulation will not say it. Searched the full instrument: 'SIMS' NOT FOUND, 'Single Integrated' NOT FOUND, 'ESMS' NOT FOUND, 'ESQRS' NOT FOUND, 'handbook'/'Handbook' NOT FOUND. That is AGENCY ONLY in Research.1.md §6's sense, applied to a standard rather than to a publisher. Second and independent reason: 'should be drawn up in line with' is recital language and 'in line with' is §5a family. Recorded in full because this is exactly the edge a future session will re-propose from the recital alone.

It appears in three basis fields instead, which is where an instrument that determines a method but does not recur belongs. This is the same call, made the same way, as the corpus's treatment of one-off implementing decisions. Revisit if a future session finds it amended.

A FOURTH INDEPENDENT §5a STATEMENT ON AN EDGE ALREADY REFUSED THREE TIMES, recorded because esa-2010.json predicts it will keep being re-proposed and notes it already was once. Quality report on national and regional accounts, 2025 edition, §3.3 'Manuals and guidelines': 'ESA 2010 is broadly aligned with SNA 2008 to make comparable analysis with non-EU economies possible.' Two watchlist phrases in fourteen words — 'broadly aligned with' and 'comparable analysis'. The three already recorded in esa-2010.json are 'is consistent with' (ESA 2010 Annex A ¶1.05), 'is fully consistent with' (the supply-and-use manual) and 'fully consistent with' (Eurostat's national accounts page). Four statements, four different documents, all agreement language, none a dependency.

_dropped.why: THE STRONGEST STATEMENT YET FOR THE BRANCH'S BIGGEST CLASSIFICATION GAP, and not mintable here. Quality report on national and regional accounts, 2025 edition, §3.2, headed 'Classifications used in ESA 2010': 'Classification of institutional sectors • Statistical Classification of Economic Activities in the European Community (NACE), Rev. 2 (2008) • Statistical Classification of Products by Activity, Version 2.1 (CPA) • Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP), COICOP 2018 • Classifications of functions of government (COFOG) • Nomenclature of territorial units for statistics (NUTS), 2024 version'. Second, Research.1.md §7's counter-intuitive rule says a classification hub should be built from the programmes coded to it, not from a list that names it — 'Do not research a classification standard by reading the classification.' A bulleted list under a heading also gives no citable location per classification, which is why this is one record naming five things rather than five records. Recorded because both ends are now nodes and the citation is real, so the edge will look available. Regulation 479/2009 Article 8(2): 'Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat), as promptly as possible, with the relevant statistical information requested for the needs of the data quality assessment, WITHOUT PREJUDICE TO the provisions of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 … relating to statistical confidentiality.' A savings clause is not a dependency — it disclaims interference with another instrument rather than taking anything from it. Contrast the minted esa-2010 -> eu-reg-223-2009 edge, where Article 4(1) says the criteria 'shall apply'.

_dropped.edge: The Annex 4.2 lists of national publications
_dropped.why:
PARTIALLY ADVANCED 2026-08-09 (sweep session, Tier-3 item), still not minted. A real candidate was found: Germany's own Statistisches Bundesamt (Destatis) publishes a 'Quality Report - National Accounts' (destatis.de/EN/Methods/Quality/QualityReports/National-Accounts-Domestic-Product/) — exactly the voluntary national quality report this entry hoped might exist. But the cadence test this project requires was not cleared: the page states only a single publication date ('Date: 29 October 2025') with no reference-period or 'annual' language, and the only hint of recurrence is the PDF's own URL carrying a version parameter (`v=11`) and an external search result surfacing the same document under the label 'National Accounts - 10/2024 - 09/2025' — suggestive of a revision history and a rolling reference window, but not a stated cadence in the document's own text. Destatis's quality-reports landing page adds only that 'Since 2005, the Federal Statistical Office has offered Quality Reports on all federal statistics' — a standing practice, not a per-report frequency statement. Not minted on this evidence; the next step is opening the PDF's own text (not just its metadata) for a stated update frequency, or checking whether v=1 through v=10 are still resolvable as dated prior editions. Original entry follows.

NOT AN EDGE — A LEAD, AND THE BEST ONE EITHER SLICE PRODUCED. Implementing Regulation 2016/2304, Annex 4.2, qualitative indicator 2 ('Documentation on methodology') requires each Member State to supply: 'List of national publications on the data sources used and methodology applied containing the titles of these publications and links to them, if available'. Indicators 1 and 3 similarly require 'links to existing metadata published nationally'. So the EU compels, annually and from all 27, precisely the naming that every EU instrument this branch has read declines to do itself. If any Member State publishes its own quality report voluntarily — nothing requires it, nothing forbids it — that single document is a data-sources table in Research.1.md §7's strongest-evidence-class sense, for one country, refreshed every year. Finding one is now the cheapest high-value test in the EU branch. Note the limit of what this licenses: it makes the upward-disclosure asymmetry look like a drafting artefact rather than national candour, but establishing that needs a report in hand, and none has been read.

QUARANTINED 2026-08-31 (independent audit finding D1, Thomas's ruling 1-A: quarantine all): this edge asserted a relationship instead of citing one — its evidence_url was absent and its basis quotes no document, so nobody could check it. Original basis: "eurostat-national-accounts-quality-report's own description: 'produced under Article 4 of Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 and structured by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2304.' The Regulation sets the modalities, structure, periodicity and assessment indicators the report follows — method, not raw data input, hence methodology_depends_on rather than uses_data_from. Added 2026-08-08 alongside minting the target node; the edge was implicit in the source node's description since the file was drafted but could not be minted while the target had no node." To re-mint: find the document (methodology note, statute, release annex) that names the input, quote it verbatim, and cite that document's URL — not the homepage.

Not itself staged in EU/slices/_staging/ (found one hop outside the staged batches, via live search plus a direct PDF fetch of Destatis's own hosting page, while tracing what the staged Germany improvement-actions document was responding to). Title page, read directly at source: 'PEER REVIEW REPORT ON COMPLIANCE WITH THE EUROPEAN STATISTICS CODE OF PRACTICE AND FURTHER IMPROVEMENT AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE NATIONAL STATISTICAL SYSTEM GERMANY Jonas Markelevicius Thomas Burg Richard Laux Jean-Pierre Poncelet January 2022.' Executive summary: 'Overall, there is a good level of compliance with the European Statistics Code of Practice (ES CoP) throughout the German statistical system. However, the peer review team identified eight compliance-relevant and fifteen improvement-related recommendations grouped under six main headings.' Recommendation 1, read directly at source and later confirmed to match the staged Germany improvement-actions document word-for-word: 'The Federal Statistical Office should formalise and publish National Guidelines to ensure quality in the development, production and dissemination of European Statistics, applicable to all Other National Authorities.'

reports.title: Peer Reviewers' Recommendations and Improvement Actions of the National Statistical System of Germany
reports.publisher: Federal Statistical Office of Germany (Destatis), in agreement with Eurostat
reports.description: Germany's improvement action plan responding to the recommendations of its January 2022 ESS peer-review report -- the fourth phase of the standard ESS peer-review process (SWD(2024)136: 'the NSI drafted an improvement action plan for the NSS outlining the measures to be taken to address the recommendations of the peer-review report, setting a deadline and identifying an institution responsible'). Title/cover: 'PEER REVIEWERS' RECOMMENDATIONS AND IMPROVEMENT ACTIONS OF THE NATIONAL STATISTICAL SYSTEM OF GERMANY IN RESPONSE TO THE RECOMMENDATIONS.' Its own '1. Recommendation' restates the January 2022 report's Recommendation 1 verbatim -- 'The Federal Statistical Office should formalise and publish National Guidelines to ensure quality in the development, production and dissemination of European Statistics, applicable to all Other National Authorities. The implementation of these National Guidelines should be monitored and reviewed. The responsibility for ensuring compliance with the Guidelines rests solely with the heads of the Other National Authorities. (Compliance-relevant: ES CoP, indicator 1bis.2)' -- then sets out dated sub-actions: 'Improvement sub-action 1.1: A kick-off and 1-2 working meetings are planned by the end of 2023 to familiarize the ONAs with the applicable quality guidelines. Deadline: Q4 2023' and 'Improvement sub-action 1.2: The quality guidelines in force for the German official statistics network will be applied in at least 2 ONAs by the end of 2024. Deadline: Q4 2024.'

REASON CORRECTED 2026-08-09 (EU/G.73.md): filed as `duplicate`, which is not a DroppedReason value — the corpus's own vocabulary has no such member, and nothing caught it because the validator counted reasons without checking them. It is an observation about the corpus with null endpoints, i.e. a `note`. Original text follows.

All 139 distinct record_ids across the 11-batch cluster were read this session; itemised mapping so the cluster is not reopened. Batches 27, 39, 43, 57 (SWD(2024)136 / third-round peer-review methodology and results) are re-derived evidence for ess-peer-review-final-report, already minted in eu-meta-docx-batches.json with the same cadence conclusion (round-based, 0.13/year, three rounds 2006-2008/2013-2015/2021-2023). Batches 29, 42, 59 (ESGAB Annual Reports 2024/2025, plus the 2026 Work Programme and ESAC opinions named alongside them) are re-derived evidence for esgab-annual-report, eurostat-annual-work-programme and esac-opinion-work-programme, all three already minted in the same file. Batches 28, 41, 58 (Commission Recommendation (EU) 2023/397) match an entry eu-meta-docx-batches.json's own _dropped array already carries verbatim: 'A soft-law instrument (replacing Recommendation 2009/498/EC) inviting Member States to apply the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS). Not itself a recurrently published document -- it is a one-off legal act... no new node.' Nothing in this session's re-read of the Recommendation's recitals and operative points changes that conclusion. Only batch 40 (Slovakia peer-review report + Germany improvement-actions document) held material not already covered; see reports/dependencies above.

Eurostat's own news announcement confirms the report exists and was published (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-eurostat-news/w/cn-20230818-1, 'Peer review report on Portugal now online', 2023-08-18) and names a second location, Statistics Portugal's own site (https://www.ine.pt/xportal/xmain?xpid=INE&xpgid=ine_cont_inst&INST=623284698&xlang=en), but neither page exposes a direct PDF link retrievable by WebFetch this session (the ine.pt page also refused the fetch outright -- robots/connect-timeout), and a guessed url on Eurostat's document-store naming pattern (Peer+Review+Report+Portugal.pdf) 404'd. Per Research.1.md §6, a confirmed announcement and title are not a substitute for a verbatim quote read at its own source url, so this stays unminted rather than being promoted on the batch stub's uncited quote alone. One websearch/one direct-fetch attempt each, consistent with item 5(e)'s per-record budget; a future session should try the ine.pt page again (transient connect timeout) or search Statistics Portugal's own document library directly.

_note: The ESS's self-regulatory quality stack, which the blob had staged across twenty-two batches and no session had ever built. The Code of Practice names its own composition ('the common quality framework ... is composed of the European Statistics Code of Practice, the Quality Assurance Framework ... and the general quality management principles'), and each layer below it names the layer above in its own words, ending outside the EU entirely at the SDMX Glossary.
_headline: A five-node chain in which every link is stated by the dependent document about itself: EHQMR -> SIMS -> SDMX Glossary, with QAF -> CoP alongside, and the two existing EU governance nodes (ESGAB annual report, ESS peer review final report) attaching to the CoP. It is the EU branch's first documented chain that leaves the EU layer downward into an international standard rather than upward into a Regulation.
_open_questions: Direction is genuinely two-way between the CoP and the peer reviews and this session minted only one leg. ess-handbook-quality-metadata-reports -> eu-statistics-code-of-practice is recorded as 'cites' on 'It supports compliance with the European Statistics Code of Practice'. That is a purpose statement, and the choice between 'cites' and 'methodology_depends_on' is a judgement, flagged rather than resolved.
The EHQMR contradicts itself about its own edition inside one document: the cover says '2021 re-edition', the foreword says 'This 2020 edition'. Both quoted in Part A; not adjudicated.

sdmx-glossary is the corpus's first SDMX node and its cadence is the weakest of the five: the document says it is a 'living' document that 'will grow and be updated' but states no interval. releases_per_year is derived from observed versions, not from a stated commitment.

ess-qpi-guidelines' cadence is genuinely two-readings and not adjudicated: two revision events across 2010-2014 (roughly one every two years) versus two revisions and then twelve years of silence to 2026. releases_per_year is the second, conservative reading (0.13); the first is recorded in the cadence_note. If a Version 1.5 or a post-2014 edition exists anywhere, it was not found this session and it would change the number.

reports.title: European Statistics Code of Practice
reports.publisher: European Statistical System Committee (published by Eurostat)
reports.description: The ESS's self-regulatory quality standard, adopted by the European Statistical System Committee and applying to Eurostat and the national statistical authorities. Eurostat's own page: 'The European Statistics Code of Practice (CoP) is the cornerstone of the quality framework and sets the standards for developing, producing and disseminating European statistics. It defines 16 key principles for the institutional environment under which the EU and national statistical authorities operate, as well as for the statistical processes and output . It also includes a set of 84 indicators for the best practices and standards for each of the 16 principles.' The current edition's own title page reads 'Adopted by the European Statistical System Committee 16th November 2017'. It names its own place in a three-part framework: 'The common quality framework of the European Statistical System is composed of the European Statistics Code of Practice, the Quality Assurance Framework of the European Statistical System and the general quality management principles'.
reports.cadence_note: Revised editions, not periodic issues. Eurostat's 'History of the CoP' table gives three dated events and nothing else: '24 February 2005 Adoption of the CoP by the Statistical Programme Committee | September 2011 Revision of the CoP based on the results of the 1st round of ESS peer reviews | November 2017 Revision of the CoP based on the results of the 2nd round of ESS peer reviews'. Two revisions across twelve years is roughly one every six; 0.17 is that observed interval, not a stated commitment. Same treatment as the versioned-standard nodes (esa-2010, sna-2008).

release_schedule.note: No fixed periodicity found. Eurostat's director publicly flagged (Nov 2025) that a revision is 'urgently' being prepared, but no date has been set.

reports.title: Quality Assurance Framework of the European Statistical System
reports.publisher: European Statistical System Committee (published by Eurostat)
reports.description: The implementation-side half of the ESS common quality framework, sitting under the Code of Practice. Eurostat's own page: 'The QAF serves as complementary guidance for how to implement the CoP. Like the CoP, it applies to the statistical authorities of the ESS, which comprises the European Union Statistical Authority (Eurostat), the National Statistical Institutes (NSIs), and Other National Authorities (ONAs).' The document's own introduction: 'The current version 2.0 of the ESS QAF was prepared by the ESS Task Force QAF, a sub-group of the Working Group on Quality in Statistics, and Eurostat, and was approved by the European Statistical System Committee in May 2019.'
reports.cadence_note: Two versions on the record, tied to the CoP's own revisions: 'In 2011, when the European Statistics Code of Practice (CoP) was revised for the first time, the European Statistical System Committee (ESSC) adopted the Quality Assurance Framework (QAF) of the European Statistical System (ESS). After the revision of the CoP in 2017, the QAF was substantially enhanced and a revised version was adopted by the ESSC in 2019.' One revision across eight years; 0.13 is that observed interval, not a stated commitment.

release_schedule.note: The ESS QAF has no fixed revision schedule. The publisher's own document (Version 2.0, approved by the European Statistical System Committee in May 2019) states: "The ESS QAF remains open to further updates in the collection of methods, tools and good practices and, in this context, will closely follow the evolution of the ES Code of Practice in the future." Past editions (V1.0 ~2012, V1.2 ~2015, V2.0 2019) appear only when the underlying European Statistics Code of Practice is itself revised (e.g. 2011, 2017), not on any calendar or fixed-interval rule. Eurostat's general quality/QAF landing pages (ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/quality and .../quality/european-statistical-system) either 404'd or gave only generic navigation content when fetched directly, and this session's web-search budget was already exhausted, so I could not confirm whether a newer version (e.g. tied to a post-2023 Code of Practice revision) exists beyond V2.0. No evidence of a stated periodic rule or scheduled next release was found.

reports.title: European Statistical System handbook for quality and metadata reports
reports.description: The ESS's operational guidance for writing quality and metadata reports, and the document that turns SIMS from a structure into a reporting practice. Its own foreword: 'The ESS Handbook for Quality and Metadata Reports (EHQMR) is recognised as an ESS standard. It is included in the Catalogue of ESS standards, the collection of non-legislative normative documents underpinning the ESS.' And: 'This 2020 edition of the ESS Handbook for Quality and Metadata Reports (EHQMR) fully incorporates SIMS 2.0 and the two standards - ESQRS and ESMS - which are unified in SIMS. The document provides guidelines for producer reports and user reports within the overarching SIMS framework.' NOTE: the cover of the same PDF reads '2021 re-edition' while the foreword calls it 'This 2020 edition'; both are quoted and neither is adjudicated.
reports.cadence_note: Editions counted from the Handbook's own lineage statement: 'The first ESS quality guidelines for standard quality reports were adopted in 2003, accompanied by the first ESS Handbook on Quality Reports (EHQR), which was further extended in 2009 to cover all types of statistical processes and incorporate the standard ESS Quality and Performance Indicators.' Three editions - 2003, 2009, and this one - across roughly seventeen years. No stated review interval was found; 0.15 is the observed rate.

release_schedule.note: This is a methodological handbook, not a periodic statistical release. Editions to date: 2014 (ESS Handbook for Quality Reports, EHQR), a March 2020 edition, and a December 2021 re-edition (corrected Nov 2021) incorporating SIMS V2.0. The document itself states no fixed revision schedule; Section 3.2.5 notes SIMS/the Handbook 'will further evolve' via improvement requests reviewed by a Eurostat Task Force and the Working Group on Quality in Statistics, with possible ESS Committee approval — an ongoing but informal, on-demand revision process rather than a periodic cadence.

reports.title: Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS)
reports.publisher: Eurostat, endorsed by the European Statistical System Committee
reports.description: The ESS's single reporting structure for quality and reference metadata, formed by unifying the two earlier structures. Eurostat's own metadata-standards page: 'SIMS is the inventory and conceptual framework for all ESS quality and reference metadata concepts.' Its live status is stated in the present tense on Eurostat's quality-reporting page: 'The ESS quality reporting standard is the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS).' The two structures it absorbed remain visible as subsets rather than separate publications: 'the Euro-SDMX metadata structure (ESMS): the ESMS is a subset of SIMS' and 'the ESS standard quality report structure (ESQRS): the ESQRS is a subset of SIMS focusing on detailed quality concepts' - which is why neither is a node here.
reports.cadence_note: Versions, not issues. The EHQMR's lineage statement: 'the two standards - ESQRS and ESMS - were combined in the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS), which was published in 2013. Minor updates were made in 2015 and SIMS 2.0 was adopted by the European Statistical System Committee.' Eurostat's quality-reporting page additionally lists 'Single Integrated Metadata Structure Guidelines v2.0 (2019)'. Three dated points across 2013-2019; 0.2 is the observed rate, and no stated review interval was found.

release_schedule.note: SIMS is a metadata standard/conceptual framework endorsed by the European Statistical System Committee, not a periodic statistical release. It has been revised twice in its history: v1.0 (~2009) and v2.0 (November 2015, ESSC-endorsed). No Eurostat, CROS, or interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu page states a review cycle, revision schedule, or next planned update. Commission Recommendation (EU) 2023/397 references SIMS concepts for reference metadata reporting but does not establish a periodic revision cadence. Given the absence of any calendar or stated rule, and only two revisions in ~15+ years with no announced next version, this is best classified as irregular rather than assigning a fabricated periodicity.

reports.title: SDMX Glossary
reports.description: The terminology component of the SDMX Content-Oriented Guidelines, and the published home of the SDMX cross-domain concepts that the ESS's own metadata structure is derived from. The COG's own introduction: 'The SDMX Glossary is an SDMX guideline containing concepts and related definitions that are useful for building and understanding data and metadata exchange arrangements based on SDMX. [...] The Glossary is closely linked to the cross-domain concepts as it also contains all these concepts, stating their definitions and context descriptions.' Maintained by the SDMX Statistical Working Group: 'The development and maintenance of the content-oriented guidelines is under the responsibility of the SDMX Statistical Working Group (SWG), which is made of 20 members from national and international organisations from the statistical and central banking worlds.' The seven SDMX sponsoring institutions are referred to as a group in that document but are nowhere enumerated in the text read, so the publisher field does not enumerate them either.
reports.cadence_note: The weakest cadence in this slice, and stated as such. The Glossary says of itself only that it is updated, with no interval: 'this list will grow and be updated as the SDMX guidelines are used in more and more statistical domains. The Glossary should thus be considered as a "living" document'. sdmx.org names 'The SDMx Glossary Version 2.1 (published in December 2020)'; the same page carries a 'January 2009 version' of the subject-matter domain classification and a February 2016 COG introduction. Roughly one version per decade on the versions observed; 0.1 is that count, not a commitment.

release_schedule.note: The SDMX Glossary is a reference document maintained by the SDMX Statistical Working Group (SWG), not a periodic statistical release. The current version 2.1 was published December 2020, revising prior editions with new/clarified concept definitions. The publisher's page (sdmx.org) states the glossary is subject to ongoing review by the SWG but gives no fixed update schedule, calendar, or stated periodicity rule. Given the multi-year gaps between editions and absence of any announced cadence, this fits 'irregular' rather than a computable schedule.

reports.title: ESS Guidelines for the Implementation of the ESS Quality and Performance Indicators
reports.description: The document that defines the sixteen standard ESS Quality and Performance Indicators (QPIs) and states how each is computed. Its own title page reads 'ESS GUIDELINES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE ESS QUALITY AND PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (QPI)' and 'Version 1.4'. The ESS Handbook for Quality and Metadata Reports names it as the source of the definitions: 'The definitions and compilation methods for the QPIs are specified in the ESS Guidelines for the Implementation of the ESS Quality and Performance Indicators.' NOTE, and this is the reason the node is the Guidelines document and not 'the QPIs': the indicators themselves live inside SIMS and the ESQRS as sub-concepts ('SIMS incorporates the 16 standard ESS Quality and Performance Indicators (QPIs) within the sub-concepts (for user reports) and as sub-concepts of their own (for producer reports)'), which is the same part_of shape that keeps ESMS and ESQRS out of this slice. The indicator set is part of SIMS; the document that defines it is not.
reports.cadence_note: Versions, not issues, and the rate is a judgement between two readings that the document does not settle. Its own p.1: 'These indicators were reviewed by the Eurostat Expert Group on Quality Indicators in 2010 and then slightly updated by the Task Force on Quality Reporting in 2012-2013' - producing Version 1.4, which Eurostat's Tools and standards list dates as 'ESS Quality and Performance Indicators (2014)'. Read narrowly, that is two revision events across 2010-2014, roughly one every two years. Read across the observed lifetime, it is two revisions and then nothing at all for the twelve years to 2026. 0.13 is the lifetime reading (2 revisions / 16 years), chosen as the conservative one and the same treatment ess-quality-assurance-framework already carries; the narrow reading is recorded here rather than discarded. No stated review interval was found in the document or on Eurostat's quality-reporting page.

release_schedule.note: This is a methodological guidance document (defining the 18 ESS Quality and Performance Indicators), not a periodic statistical release. It has been revised occasionally, reproduced within the broader 'ESS Handbook for Quality Reports' / 'ESS Handbook for Quality and Metadata Reports' series: 2009 edition, 2014 edition (the version at the corpus's current URL), a 2020 edition (Feb 2020, KS-GQ-19-006), and a 're-edition 2021' (Dec 2021, KS-GQ-21-021). Gaps between editions are irregular (5 years, then 6 years, then ~1.75 years). The 2020 handbook states revisions are proposed via periodically-convened Task Forces of the Working Group on Quality in Statistics, with no fixed/stated cycle or calendar. No edition newer than the 2021 re-edition was found as of 2026-08-11.

Like the CoP, it applies to the statistical authorities of the ESS, which comprises the European Union Statistical Authority (Eurostat), the National Statistical Institutes (NSIs), and Other National Authorities (ONAs). [...] The QAF represents a collection of methods, tools and good practices that are suggested for use or are already in use in some statistical authorities of the ESS. The aim of the QAF is to accompany the CoP by providing guidance and examples in the form of more detailed methods and tools.' Deliberately NOT built on the QAF's own 'follows and aligns with the 2017 revision of the European Statistics Code of Practice' sentence, which is Research.1.md section 5a language; see the caveat entry.

dependencies.basis: Eurostat, Reference metadata reporting standards: 'The 19 high-level concepts are derived from the statistical data and metadata exchange (SDMX) cross-domain concepts published in the SDMX glossary .' The adjacent sentence in the same paragraph - 'The concepts defined in the SIMS standard are compatible with the common terminology established by the SDMX standard' - is Research.1.md section 5a language and carries nothing; the operative clause is 'are derived from'.

dependencies.basis: The ESGAB annual report's own title page (2021 edition, read in full this session): 'Thirteenth annual report by the European Statistical Governance Advisory Board to the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union on the implementation of the European Statistics Code of Practice by Eurostat and the European Statistical System as a whole'. The Code of Practice supplies the criteria the report is written against.

dependencies.basis: Eurostat's third-round peer-review page, two statements on the same page. On the exercise: 'Peer reviews form part of the European Statistical System (ESS) strategy to monitor the implementation of the European Statistics Code of Practice (CoP). Their objective is to review the compliance/alignment of the ESS with the CoP and help the statistical authorities to further improve and develop the national statistical systems.' On the report: 'As in previous rounds, Eurostat prepared a final report on the third round of the European Statistical System peer reviews, which has been transmitted to the European Parliament and the Council. This report summarises the results of the peer reviews in all members of the ESS.' This is a two-sentence chain rather than one statement inside the report itself - weaker than the ESGAB edge, and stated as such; SWD(2024) 136 was not opened this session.

The Handbook takes the definitions and the compilation methods for the indicators it requires from the named document, which is methodology_depends_on rather than cites. _dropped.edge: ESS Quality and Performance Indicators as a node
_dropped.why: RESOLVED 2026-08-08 - minted as ess-qpi-guidelines, with a methodology_depends_on edge from ess-handbook-quality-metadata-reports. NOTE FOR THE RECORD: this was NOT reopened by Research.1.md section 4's one-off-foundational-instrument rule, which is what that section's own forward pointer implied. It qualifies on the ordinary recurring shape. The original blocker ('one dated publication with no second edition and no stated review interval found') rested on a search confined to Eurostat's quality-reporting page and the EHQMR foreword; the QPI document itself states its own revision history on p.1 ('These indicators were reviewed by the Eurostat Expert Group on Quality Indicators in 2010 and then slightly updated by the Task Force on Quality Reporting in 2012-2013') and carries 'Version 1.4' on its title page. The naming evidence the original entry could not find is in the EHQMR body rather than its foreword, s. 3.2.2. The nodeable object is the Guidelines document, not the indicator set - the set is incorporated into SIMS and minting it would double-count, the same call already made for ESMS and ESQRS. ORIGINAL (covering all three candidates as one bundled entry): All three are named in Eurostat's own 'Tools and standards' list alongside the three documents minted here, and the EHQMR states that the QPIs 'have been incorporated in the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS)'. _dropped.edge: ESS Quality Glossary as a node
_dropped.why: RE-CHECKED 2026-08-08 AND STILL NOT A NODE, ON A DIFFERENT REASON THAN THE ORIGINAL. The original blocker was cadence, and cadence is not the problem: the EHQMR s. 2.5.2 says 'The ESS Quality Glossary, first published in 2003, was transferred to the Concepts and Definitions Database (CODED), where it is now available as a theme', and the Publications Office's EU Vocabularies register carries an 'ESS Quality Glossary' dataset whose latest version is 2023, maintained by Eurostat with the Working Group on Quality in Statistics - so there are dated points twenty years apart. As used by the Handbook it is an in-document supplement: 'for the purposes of this Handbook, the Glossary has been revised and expanded to become the ESS Quality and Metadata Glossary', supplied as Supplementary Document A of the EHQMR itself. Either route is part_of something else - the same reasoning that keeps ESMS and ESQRS out. And nothing read names it as an input to a report; the EHQMR mentions it descriptively. Revisit if Eurostat republishes it as a titled standalone document. ORIGINAL (bundled entry): All three are named in Eurostat's own 'Tools and standards' list alongside the three documents minted here, and the EHQMR states that the QPIs 'have been incorporated in the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS)'. Each is one dated publication with no second edition and no stated review interval found, which fails Research.1.md section 4(2). _dropped.why: SCOPED 2026-08-08 (G.56, EU/CatalogueOfESSStandards_scoping_2026-08-08.md) AND RE-CHECKED 2026-08-09 - STILL NO MINT, ON A NARROWER REMAINDER THAN THE ORIGINAL. G.56 read the catalogue itself (a SKOS dataset on ShowVoc, not a document or webpage list - CROS: 'The Catalogue of ESS Standards is currently hosted on ShowVoc'). It is 12 entries, static for at least four years (EFGS 2022: 'It currently contains 12 standards'). Two of the 12 are already nodes here (ess-handbook-quality-metadata-reports, ess-sims). Of the other 10: one (EDAMIS) is a transmission system, not a publication, same call as the ESS Metadata Handler entry in this same array. One (ISCED 2011) is a classification hub and is subject to Research.1.md section 7's rule against researching a hub by reading it - its edges come from the programmes coded to it, and none has been found yet. The remaining 8 are named and titled but none has been read at source for an edge into this graph. The strongest of the 8, ESS guidelines on seasonal adjustment, clears the recurring-cadence bar on its own (two dated editions confirmed at source, KS-GQ-15-001 2015 and ks-gq-24-012 2024 'revised guidelines', releases_per_year ~0.11) but a corpus-wide grep this session ('seasonal adjustment', case-insensitive, all of src/data/) found it named nowhere outside this note and Canada's statcan-ippi.json - no proposed edge anywhere in the graph. That is the isolated-mint case this corpus declines (the MIP-scoreboard caution: the node-only-evidence exception that covered fed-h15 or a Staat-van-de-WOZ-style mint does not apply here, because only the document's existence and cadence were confirmed at source, not its content or use). The one soft connection G.56 flagged (ess-sims -eli:based_on-> eu-reg-223-2009, asserted by the catalogue's own metadata rather than by SIMS about itself) was chased further this session: WebFetch on Eurostat's reference-metadata-reporting-standards page found no present-tense statement tying SIMS to Regulation 223/2009; the SIMS 2.0 PDF itself repeats only the already-recorded future-tense 'SIMS will be the standard for quality reporting according to Article 12 of Regulation 223/2009'; a web search for a live Eurostat quality-reporting page turned up nothing newer. Not minted. Remaining candidates (European business statistics methodological manual for business registers, ESS guidelines on temporal disaggregation/benchmarking/reconciliation, Handbook on precision requirements and variance estimation for household surveys, Methodology for data validation 2.0, GSBPM 5.1, SDMX 2.0, SDMX 2.1) have not been read at source at all - full detail and ESSC/WG approval dates in the G.56 scoping doc. ORIGINAL: The EHQMR describes itself as 'included in the Catalogue of ESS standards, the collection of non-legislative normative documents underpinning the ESS'. A named collection of normative documents is exactly the shape that produces nodes in this corpus, and none of its members other than the three minted here have been looked at. Named, not scoped - a candidate category for the rolling to-do rather than a dropped edge.
