reports.title: Ethiopian Statistical Service Proclamation / Statistics Act framework
reports.publisher: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (Council of Ministers / House of Peoples’ Representatives)
reports.description: Foundational legal framework establishing the Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) as an autonomous federal government body with its own legal personality, and governing the production, quality assurance, dissemination and coordination of official statistics in Ethiopia. Includes provisions on statistical obligations, data governance, national statistics calendar, methodologies and the relationship between the ESS and other government organs. Successive proclamations and the Code of Practice for Official Statistics in Ethiopia operationalise the system.
reports.cadence_note: One-off / amending legal instruments; Code of Practice is a standing regulatory instrument

reports.title: Ethiopia Annual Statistical Abstract / National Statistics Abstract
reports.description: Long-running annual statistical abstract presenting a comprehensive summary of social and economic statistics for Ethiopia. Covers population, national accounts, prices, agriculture, industry, trade, education, health and related domains. Principal single-volume official reference for multi-domain national statistics; published by the ESS (formerly Central Statistical Agency).

reports.title: Ethiopia National Accounts / GDP Statistics
reports.description: Official national accounts statistics for Ethiopia, including GDP by production and expenditure approaches, gross value added by industry, and related aggregates at current and constant prices. Compiled and disseminated by the ESS as the core macroeconomic statistical product. Forms the principal measure of economic activity and is the reference series for growth, structure and sectoral contributions.
reports.cadence_note: Annual estimates with periodic revisions; higher-frequency indicators may appear in other releases

reports.title: Population and Housing Census of Ethiopia
reports.description: Decennial (or periodic) Population and Housing Census of Ethiopia. Major enumerations conducted in 1984, 1994 and 2007, with subsequent population projections and regional statistical reports. Provides the official population base, demographic structure, housing characteristics and related social statistics. Mid-year and projected population figures are derived from the census framework.
reports.cadence_note: Decennial census with inter-censal projections and regional reports

reports.title: Labour Force Survey / Urban Employment and Unemployment Survey (Ethiopia)
reports.description: Official labour-market statistics produced by the ESS under the Household Budget and Labour Statistics (HBLS) programme. Includes the Labour Force Survey (LFS) and the Urban Employment and Unemployment Survey (UEUS). Provides nationally representative data on labour force participation, employment, unemployment, underemployment and related indicators. Principal official source for labour-market analysis in Ethiopia.
reports.cadence_note: Periodic / multi-year survey cycle; urban series more frequent in some years

reports.title: Household Consumption and Expenditure Survey (HCES) / Welfare Monitoring Survey
reports.description: Official household survey programme producing statistics on household consumption, expenditure, living standards, poverty and welfare. Includes the Household Consumption and Expenditure Survey (HCES) and the Welfare Monitoring Survey (WMS). Provides the micro-data foundation for poverty measurement, CPI weights and living-standards analysis.
reports.cadence_note: Periodic multi-year survey cycle

reports.title: National Bank of Ethiopia Balance of Payments and External Sector Statistics
reports.description: Official Balance of Payments and external-sector statistics compiled by the National Bank of Ethiopia. Covers the current account (goods, services, income, transfers), capital and financial accounts, reserve assets, international investment position and external debt. Primary official source for Ethiopia’s external accounts and the counterpart to ESS real-sector statistics.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly / annual series published via NBE statistical data series and bulletins

reports.title: National Bank of Ethiopia Monetary and Financial Statistics
reports.description: Official monetary and financial statistics published by the National Bank of Ethiopia. Includes monetary survey, central bank accounts, money supply aggregates, domestic credit, net foreign assets, interest rates and related financial-sector indicators. Core official source for monetary conditions and financial stability analysis in Ethiopia.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly / quarterly monetary reports and statistical series

reports.title: National Bank of Ethiopia Annual Report
reports.description: Annual report of the National Bank of Ethiopia presenting the overall economic, monetary and financial developments of the year, policy actions, and comprehensive statistical annexes covering the real sector, fiscal, monetary, external and financial indicators. Serves as a key official synthesis publication that draws on both NBE and ESS source statistics.

reports.title: Agricultural Sample Survey (AgSS) – Meher and Belg Seasons
reports.description: Principal annual agricultural statistical programme of Ethiopia. Conducted twice a year to cover the Meher (main) and Belg (short rainy) cropping seasons. Produces official estimates of area and production of major crops, land utilisation, farm management practices, crop and livestock product utilisation, and livestock characteristics for private peasant holdings. Results are published in multi-volume statistical bulletins and feed agricultural value-added in the national accounts.
reports.cadence_note: Meher season (main) and Belg season reports annually

reports.title: Livestock and Livestock Characteristics Survey (Agricultural Sample Survey component)
reports.description: Component of the Agricultural Sample Survey programme producing official statistics on livestock numbers, livestock characteristics, and livestock product utilisation for private peasant holdings. Complements the crop-focused volumes of the AgSS and supports estimates of livestock contribution to agricultural GDP.
reports.cadence_note: Annual (aligned with Meher-season AgSS cycle)

reports.title: Large and Medium Scale Commercial Farms Sample Survey
reports.description: Annual sample survey of large and medium scale commercial farms conducted using the agricultural business register. Provides production, area and related statistics for the commercial farming sector that complement the private peasant holdings covered by the main Agricultural Sample Survey.

reports.title: Large and Medium Scale Manufacturing Industries Survey
reports.description: Annual survey of large and medium scale manufacturing industries (establishments engaging ten or more persons and using power-driven machinery). Covers employment, production, raw materials, structure and performance of public and private manufacturing industries. Principal official source of industrial statistics for the manufacturing sector and a key input to industrial value-added in the national accounts. Electricity industry statistics have historically been published alongside the manufacturing survey in some editions.

reports.title: External Merchandise Trade Statistics
reports.description: Official quarterly and annual statistics on Ethiopia’s external merchandise trade. Covers value and net weight of exports and imports by major commodities and partner countries, trade balance, and related aggregates. Compiled by the ESS from customs and related administrative sources. Complements the NBE Balance of Payments goods account with more detailed commodity and partner breakdowns.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly bulletins; annual aggregates

reports.title: Producer Price Index / Agricultural Producer Prices (Ethiopia)
reports.description: Official producer price statistics compiled by the ESS Price Statistics department. Includes producer price indices and agricultural producer price series used for deflation of agricultural and industrial output and for monitoring farm-gate and factory-gate price developments. Complements the Consumer Price Index on the production side of the price system.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly / periodic releases

reports.title: Oromia Regional Statistical Reports / Census and Survey Outputs
reports.publisher: Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) / Oromia regional statistical structures
reports.description: Official statistical outputs for Oromia Region, the most populous regional state. Includes regional volumes of the Population and Housing Census, Agricultural Sample Survey regional tables, and other ESS survey results disaggregated for Oromia. Provides the principal statistical picture of the largest regional economy and population centre outside the capital.
reports.cadence_note: Census volumes periodic; survey regional tables annual or aligned with national survey cycles

reports.title: Amhara Regional Statistical Reports / Census and Survey Outputs
reports.publisher: Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) / Amhara regional statistical structures
reports.description: Official statistical outputs for Amhara Region, the second-most populous regional state. Includes regional census volumes, Agricultural Sample Survey disaggregations and related ESS survey results for Amhara. Key northern highland economic and demographic node.
reports.cadence_note: Census volumes periodic; survey regional tables aligned with national cycles

reports.title: Addis Ababa City Administration Statistical Reports / Census Outputs
reports.publisher: Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) / Addis Ababa statistical structures
reports.description: Official statistical outputs for Addis Ababa, the capital and a chartered city. Includes census analytical and statistical reports for Addis Ababa, urban labour-force and household survey results, and related city-level indicators. Principal urban/metropolitan statistical node and the political-economic centre of the country.
reports.cadence_note: Census volumes periodic; urban survey results aligned with national household/labour programmes

reports.title: SNNPR / Southern Nations Regional Statistical Reports / Census Outputs
reports.description: Official statistical outputs for the former Southern Nations, Nationalities and Peoples Region (SNNPR) and successor southern regional structures. Includes regional census statistical reports and Agricultural Sample Survey disaggregations. Provides southern highland and multi-ethnic regional contrast to the northern and central highland cores.
reports.cadence_note: Census volumes periodic; survey tables aligned with national cycles

reports.title: Tigray Regional Statistical Reports / Census Outputs
reports.description: Official statistical outputs for Tigray Region. Includes regional volumes of the Population and Housing Census and related survey disaggregations. Serves as a northern regional contrast node; data availability for recent years may be affected by conflict-related disruptions, which is recorded where relevant in source notes.
reports.cadence_note: Census volumes periodic; recent survey coverage may be incomplete

reports.title: Somali Regional Statistical Reports / Census Outputs
reports.description: Official statistical outputs for Somali Region (eastern lowland pastoralist region). Includes regional census reports and limited survey coverage. Provides important lowland / pastoral contrast to the highland agricultural regions that dominate national aggregates.
reports.cadence_note: Census volumes periodic; sample-survey coverage historically more limited in non-sedentary areas

reports.title: Dire Dawa City Administration Statistical Reports
reports.publisher: Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) / Dire Dawa statistical structures
reports.description: Official statistical outputs for Dire Dawa, a chartered city in eastern Ethiopia. Includes census and survey results for the city administration. Secondary urban node and transport/commercial centre providing eastern urban contrast to Addis Ababa.
reports.cadence_note: Census and survey disaggregations aligned with national programmes

reports.title: Education Statistics Annual Abstract (ESAA)
reports.publisher: Federal Ministry of Education of Ethiopia (MoE) – EMIS and ICT
reports.description: Annual official statistical abstract on the Ethiopian education system. Compiled by the Education Management Information System (EMIS). Covers schools, enrolment, teachers, completion and related indicators for general and higher education. Principal recurring titled product for education statistics.

reports.title: Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS)
reports.publisher: Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) in collaboration with Ministry of Health / DHS Program
reports.description: Periodic nationally representative Demographic and Health Survey implemented by the ESS. Provides official estimates of fertility, mortality, maternal and child health, family planning, nutrition, HIV knowledge, female genital mutilation and related indicators. Fifth round conducted 2024–25. Principal health and demographic survey product alongside the Population and Housing Census.
reports.cadence_note: Multi-year cycle (roughly every 5 years); 2000, 2005, 2011, 2016, 2024–25 rounds

reports.title: Ministry of Finance Budget Execution and Fiscal Performance Statistics
reports.description: Official fiscal statistics and budget implementation reports published by the Ministry of Finance. Include federal government revenue (tax and non-tax), expenditure (recurrent and capital), deficit, regional transfers/block grants, and mid-year and annual budget performance reviews. Primary official source for public-finance aggregates.
reports.cadence_note: Mid-year budget implementation review and annual budget/fiscal reports

reports.title: Ethiopia / ESS Contribution to the BRICS Joint Statistical Publication
reports.publisher: Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) / Ministry of Planning and Development
reports.description: Ethiopia’s role as data contributor to the BRICS Joint Statistical Publication following its accession as a full BRICS member. National accounts, population, prices and related series are supplied via the ESS and Ministry of Planning and Development for inclusion in the comparable tables of the JSP and its Snapshot. Not a separate survey; it is the institutional contribution channel linking the Ethiopian statistical system to the BRICS NSO work programme.
reports.cadence_note: Aligned with annual JSP production cycle

reports.title: National Bank of Ethiopia Quarterly Bulletin / Statistical Series
reports.description: Recurring NBE publication and accompanying statistical data series covering monetary, financial, external, fiscal and real-sector developments. Provides higher-frequency updates that complement the Annual Report and the detailed monetary and BoP statistical series. Primary vehicle for quarterly dissemination of official financial and external statistics.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly

reports.title: Ethiopia Population Projections / Mid-Year Population Estimates
reports.description: Official population projections and mid-year population estimates produced by the ESS from the Population and Housing Census base. Used as denominators for per-capita indicators, survey weighting and planning. Complements the full census with inter-censal estimates.
reports.cadence_note: Annual or multi-year projection updates

dependencies.basis: Labour-force and household surveys under the HBLS programme share methodological frameworks and sampling frames; employment status is a key dimension of household welfare analysis.
External-sector balances (exports, imports, current account) interact with the expenditure-side components of national accounts.
Production of official national accounts is governed by the legal and institutional framework established by the Statistics Proclamation and the mandate of the ESS.
Official price statistics are produced under the legal authority and quality framework of the Statistics Proclamation / ESS mandate.
Crop area and production estimates from the Agricultural Sample Survey are primary inputs to the agriculture component of GDP by production.
Livestock production and product utilisation data contribute to agricultural value-added in the national accounts.
Commercial farm production statistics complement private peasant holdings and feed agricultural GDP estimates.
Oromia regional agricultural tables are disaggregations of the national Agricultural Sample Survey.
Amhara regional agricultural statistics are drawn from the national AgSS programme.
Urban labour-force and employment indicators for Addis Ababa are components of the national Labour Force / Urban Employment surveys.
Labour-force and employment indicators are among the social statistics contributed to the JSP.

_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED, MERGED. Ethiopia was researched as a parallel split this session: Claude took the core PSNP5 wage-rate/CPI mechanism and the federal-woreda constitutional structure; the import took the donor/funding architecture, other Ethiopian benefit programmes, and Ethiopia's international-statistics standing. Both halves are combined here, per Thomas's standing instruction (Thomas's standing instruction on import verification) that the import's quoted, sourced, confidence-tagged answers are minted directly. Sitting in src/data/research/ alongside the other Africa drafts pending review.
_note: The split paid off exactly the way it was meant to. Claude's constitutional finding (Ethiopia's Constitution does not establish woredas at all -- Article 50(4) leaves it to each regional state's own discretion) and the import's funding finding (World Bank/donor money moves 'MoF... [to] federal and regional/woreda levels' via the government's own Channel 1 mechanism) describe the same administrative reality from two different documents. IMPORTANT: no edge was drawn between et-constitution-federal-structure and et-psnp5-worldbank-seasn, deliberately -- neither document names the other. The World Bank's fund-flow description is consistent with, and illustrates, the constitutional finding, but consistency is not the same as one document citing the other, and the corpus's own rule is explicit that plausible-sounding connections without textual support don't go in the graph. Recorded here as an observed consistency, not as a dependency edge. Separately, the headline finding from the import's half: Ethiopia has a SECOND CPI-linked benefit programme (UPSNJP, urban) with an even more interesting shape than PSNP5's -- a formal financing covenant requiring CPI indexation that has been explicitly, temporarily suspended for fiscal reasons. Not 'the formula doesn't exist' (Kenya's shape) and not 'the formula is discretionary by design' (South Africa's shape) -- a real formula that exists and is currently switched off. A third distinct way a CPI-benefit link can fail to bind in practice.

_open_questions.question: The 15kg/16.95kg wheat-equivalency figures from the docx were not found in this session's own fetch of the PSNP5 Design Document, nor did the import's round turn them up. Worth checking the Programme Implementation Manual (PIM) directly, or a more recent PSNP5 update document, before minting those specific numbers as verified.

the import found a CSA/ESS methodological note (dated 2013, so possibly stale) stating Ethiopia's CPI classification is 'COICOP... with few exceptions' -- vaguer and older than the specific, current-series confirmations found for South Africa (2018), Kenya (2018), and Egypt (1999/2000). Not minted as an edge this session; the source is too dated and imprecise about which COICOP vintage to place confidently next to those three. A current ESS methodology document, if one exists, would resolve this.

reports.title: Productive Safety Net Programme Phase 5 (PSNP5) Design Document
reports.publisher: Government of Ethiopia (Ministry of Agriculture) with donor partners
reports.description: Ethiopia's flagship rural safety-net programme, now in its fifth phase. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (direct fetch of the Design Document, hosted via the EU's capacity4dev platform): Text Box 5 states 'Adequacy of transfers will be addressed through annual adjustments to the wage rate in line with consumer price index (CPI) to protect its real value.' Independently corroborated from the funding side (the import's round): a World Bank results-framework indicator for the programme reads 'Increase in average wage rate relative to the annual general CPI increase, for cash transfers beneficiaries' -- two different documents, government-authored and donor-authored, both treating the wage-CPI link as real. This is a real-terms CPI-anchoring principle, similar in shape to Egypt's statutory pension floor, though PSNP5's own instrument is a programme design document rather than primary legislation -- a different evidentiary tier worth being precise about. The docx's more specific wheat-equivalency figures (15kg/16.95kg per month) remain unconfirmed -- see _open_questions.
reports.cadence_note: Wage-rate review conducted annually, before June each year per the docx's own quote (not independently re-confirmed this session against the fetched content).

release_schedule.note: The PSNP5 Design Document is a one-off program design document produced by the Ethiopian Ministry of Agriculture (with donor partners including the EU and World Bank) for the fifth phase of the Productive Safety Net Programme, covering 2021-2025 (source: capacity4dev.europa.eu library entry 'Ethiopia Productive Safety Net Programme 2021-2025 Phase V Design Document, FDRE Ministry of Agriculture, 2021'). It is not a recurring/periodical publication — it was produced once at the start of Phase 5. The programme has since moved into a new phase, PSNP6, which was approved/launched around March 2026 (World Bank press release, worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2026/03/03/ethiopia-a-new-phase-of-support-for-safety-nets...; World Bank project documents for P511478 'Productive Safety Net Program 6'). Since PSNP5 is already superseded by PSNP6's own separate design/project documents, no further release of 'the PSNP5 Design Document' specifically is expected. Historical PSNP phase lengths have also been irregular (PSNP2 ~2007-2009, PSNP3 2010-2014, PSNP4 2015-2020, PSNP5 2021-2025), so even treating this as a 'per-phase' publication would not yield a fixed/computable cadence.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (Ethiopian Statistics Services)
reports.description: Ethiopia's official monthly CPI, produced by ESS (formerly the Central Statistical Agency/CSA). VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via ESS's own site: 'Published monthly', described as 'the principal measure of inflation'; ESS's own framing states its statistics 'support evidence-based policy decisions, wage and income adjustments, business planning, and economic research'. Confirmed vian import's round: Ethiopia is on the IMF's e-GDDS dissemination tier (not full SDDS), per the IMF's own 2019 press release announcing Ethiopia's e-GDDS implementation -- the same weaker tier already found for Kenya, now a second country on this node. Also confirmed: Ethiopia is NOT bound by the East African Community's binding Harmonised CPI regulations (found for Kenya) -- Ethiopia is a geographic neighbour of EAC members but not a Partner State subject to that specific instrument, per the import's search. COICOP classification is referenced in an older (2013) CSA methodological note as 'COICOP... with few exceptions' but not minted as an edge -- see _open_questions.

release_schedule.note: ESS publishes CPI monthly on the price page (https://ess.gov.et/price/), one release per reference month, but there is no posted release calendar with fixed future dates. Observed 'Create Date' lag after month-end for recent editions: March 2026 CPI created Apr 6, 2026 (6 days); April 2026 CPI created May 7, 2026 (7 days); May 2026 CPI created Jun 16, 2026 (16 days); June 2026 CPI created Jul 20, 2026 (20 days). As of 2026-08-11 (today), the June 2026 edition is the latest posted and no July 2026 edition exists yet (checked https://ess.gov.et/download/consumer-price-index-july-2026/ -> 404). Based on the recent 16-20 day lag, the July 2026 CPI is estimated to post roughly mid-to-late August 2026; this is an estimate, not a published date.

reports.title: Constitution of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, 1995 — Articles 47 and 50
reports.description: The constitutional basis for Ethiopia's federal structure. VERIFIED this session via a constitutional-law archive (servat.unibe.ch/ICL, not an Ethiopian-government-hosted copy -- flagged for that reason). Article 47 names the nine constituent member states directly: 'The State of Tigray, The State of Afar, The State of Amhara, The State of Oromia, The State of Somalia, The State of Benshangul/Gumuz, The State of the Southern Nations, Nationalities and Peoples, The State of the Gambela Peoples, The State of the Harari People.' Article 50(4): 'State government shall be established at State and other administrative levels that they find necessary.' Key structural finding: unlike South Africa's local government (constitutionally entitled to an equitable share under s.227), Ethiopia's woreda (district) level is NOT established or guaranteed by the federal Constitution at all -- it exists entirely at each regional state's own discretion. Consistent with, though not textually linked to, the practical fund-flow description found on the donor side (see et-psnp5-worldbank-seasn and _note) -- a genuinely different federal shape from every other country worked in this branch so far.

reports.publisher: World Bank (IDA) with Multi-Donor Trust Fund partners
reports.description: The World Bank/IDA project financing PSNP5, alongside a Multi-Donor Trust Fund of thirteen named development partners. VERIFIED vian import's round, quoting the project's own text: 'The SEASN project supports the Government of Ethiopia (GoE) flagship Productive Safety Net Programme Phase Five (PSNP 5)... managed by the GoE through its structures from federal to woreda levels and is supported by thirteen development partners -- Austrian Development Agency, Global Affairs Canada (GAC), Danish International Development Agency, European Union, Government of Ireland... United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office, German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF), United States Agency for International Development (USAID), and World Food Programme (WFP).' IDA financing for PSNP5 via SEASN totals roughly US$900 million against a total PSNP5 budget of US$2,283-2,671 million; GoE committed US$590 million. Fund flow: 'The project follows the government's Channel 1 fund flow mechanism and MoF is responsible for the overall FM activities... IFMIS and IBEX software will be used for accounting purposes at federal and regional/woreda levels, respectively... The MoA through the FSCO[, Food Security Coordination Office,] will continue to lead overall coordination and management of the program... together with other partners, including at the regional and woreda levels.' This is the practical, administrative version of the money-flow question the constitutional structure (et-constitution-federal-structure) leaves open at the legal level -- see _note for why no edge connects the two directly.

reports.title: Urban Productive Safety Net and Jobs Project (UPSNJP)
reports.description: Ethiopia's urban parallel to PSNP5 (building on the earlier Urban Productive Safety Net Project/UPSNP) -- public-works wages, permanent direct support (covering elderly, persons with disabilities, chronically ill, and urban destitute beneficiaries), livelihood grants and related services. VERIFIED vian import's round, quoting the project's own text: 'Given high levels of inflation in the country, the wage rate was adjusted in accordance with the evolution of food prices based on the official consumer price index (CPI) published by the Central Statistics Agency. The aim of this adjustment is not to increase the real value of the transfer but to make sure the purchasing power of the transfer remains constant over time.' A genuinely distinct finding from PSNP5's own mechanism: the parent project legal agreement carries 'a covenant... requiring benefit levels to be increased in line with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) -- through increased government contributions -- [that] will be temporarily waived... The resumption of CPI benefit indexation will depend on material improvements to the government's fiscal position.' A real, formal, CPI-linked indexation obligation that currently exists but is switched off -- a third distinct way a CPI-benefit mechanism can fail to bind, alongside South Africa's deliberate-discretion and Kenya's unclear-basis shapes. This is the closest thing to disability-benefit CPI indexation found across any country in this branch so far, and it is presently suspended.

dependencies.basis: The Design Document's own Text Box 5 ties the annual wage-rate adjustment directly to 'consumer price index (CPI)... to protect its real value' -- a direct, named input into the programme's own transfer-value calculation, not merely cited as background context.

reports.title: A System for the Determination of the Division of the Federal Subsidy and Joint Revenues Proclamation No. 1250/2021
reports.publisher: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (House of Federation)
reports.description: Issued 2 July 2021. Establishes the formula by which the House of Federation divides federal subsidy and joint revenues among Ethiopia's regional states. Verbatim, Article 5.2: subsidies aim to "equalize the fiscal capacities of the Regional States so as to provide comparable level of public services." Does NOT name individual regional states (Oromia, Amhara, etc.) by name — refers generically to "Regions"/"Regional States," consistent with the already-minted et-constitution-federal-structure node's own framing. This is the actual federal-to-regional-state fiscal mechanism Thomas asked about ("how do provinces mesh with the nation") — the block-grant/subsidy layer sitting between the constitutional structure and each region's own budget.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument (a proclamation establishing a standing formula, not a recurring release).

reports.title: Expenditure Analysis for Amhara National Regional State 2012/13 – 2020/21
reports.publisher: Ethiopian Economics Association (EEA), in partnership with UNICEF Ethiopia
reports.description: Third-party (EEA/UNICEF) analysis of Amhara regional-state budget data, published 2023, covering fiscal years 2012/13-2020/21. Cited repeatedly throughout: "Source: Amhara Region Bureau of Plan and Development (2012/13–2020/21)." The regional bureau's own site (amharabofec.gov.et) is robots-blocked to non-browser fetch, so this third-party analysis is the mintable node — same pattern this branch has used before when a primary government site is inaccessible but its data is cited verbatim by an accessible secondary publisher.

reports.publisher: Ethiopian Economics Association (EEA), in partnership with UNICEF Ethiopia
reports.description: Companion volume to the Amhara analysis in the same EEA/UNICEF series, published 2023, covering the same fiscal years. Cited: "Source: Oromia Regional Plan and Development Commission (2012/13–2020/21)." Oromia's own bureau site (oromiabofec.gov.et) is also robots-blocked. dependencies.basis: Footnote 6, page 4, verbatim: "The real values are calculated using the national average Consumer Price Index (CPI) published by Ethiopian Statistical Services," with a direct link to statsethiopia.gov.et. This explicitly names the already-minted et-ess-cpi node as the deflator source, unlike the Oromia companion document (see _dropped) which cites CPI generically without naming the publishing agency.

_dropped.why: The Oromia document's own CPI footnote reads "Real expenditure computed using the consumer price index (CPI), taking 2010 as a base year" — it does NOT name the publishing agency, unlike Amhara's companion document in the same series which explicitly names Ethiopian Statistical Services. Rather than assume the same agency by analogy to the Amhara document, this is left unminted per the branch's own no-inference standard.

The proclamation almost certainly implements the House of Federation's constitutional revenue-division mandate (Article 62(7) per general knowledge of Ethiopia's constitutional structure), but the secondary source used to read the proclamation's text did not quote a specific constitutional citation within the proclamation itself. Not minted without a verbatim textual link; worth a direct fetch of the proclamation's own preamble in a future round.

Both amharabofec.gov.et and oromiabofec.gov.et are robots-blocked to non-browser fetch, the same pattern seen repeatedly with African government statistics/finance-bureau sites in this branch (ons.mr, stat-guinebissau.com). Both bureaus' own titled statistical bulletins (an 'Annual statistical bulletin' is referenced for Amhara, dated as old as 2010 in one citation index) were not directly reachable this round.

The already-minted et-constitution-federal-structure node (from a prior, separate research thread) quotes Article 47 of the 1995 Constitution naming nine constituent states. That text is still accurate as constitutional text, but Ethiopia's actual federating units have since grown to twelve, per VOA's own reporting: a 2023 restructuring split the former Southern Nations, Nationalities and Peoples' Region into South Ethiopia Regional State and Central Ethiopia Regional State, on top of Sidama (2020) and South West Ethiopia Peoples' Region (2021), and VOA reports a further, twelfth regional state since. Not a correction to the existing node's quote (which is accurate to its source), but flagged here since 'nine regional states' is now a stale figure if repeated without qualification — directly relevant to Thomas's question about how many 'provinces' Ethiopia has today.

meta.source: research round 2026-09-14 — the EU classification-and-statute layer. Thomas: “read the handoff, i want to move to The EU classification-and-statute layer.”
meta.note:
EU CLASSIFICATION-AND-STATUTE LAYER, FIRST ROUND. RESULT: 5 nodes, 75 dependencies, 4 dropped notes.

CONTINUED THE SAME DAY, and the continuation opens by correcting this file. The three edges at the END of `dependencies` — `nace-rev2 -> isic`, `cpa -> nace-rev2`, `eurostat-prodcom -> eu-combined-nomenclature` — all come from ONE document, Eurostat's own NACE Rev. 2 volume (KS-RA-07-015-EN), which the first pass wrote off as 'a 10-page cover extract'. It is 369 pages: `file` misreports that PDF's page count and `pdfinfo` does not, and the first pass believed `file`. The volume states the NACE-to-ISIC derivation under its own heading, states the CPA-to-NACE relationship that the CPA's own establishing regulation never mentions, and states where the Prodcom list's headings come from. The `nace-rev2 -> isic` dropped note below is kept and marked `resolved` rather than deleted, with the mistake written into it.

WHAT WAS THIN AND WHY THIS IS THE FIX. The EU-level instruments were the least-wired part of a well-wired region: `esa-2010` carried 116 in-edges while `nace-rev2` carried 2, `cpa` 1, `eu-reg-223-2009` 2 and `eu-reg-2019-2152` 1 — i.e. the corpus documented the EU's ACCOUNTING framework thoroughly and its CLASSIFICATION and STATUTE framework hardly at all. ECOICOP, the classification every HICP in the European Statistical System is broken down by, had no node at all, and `eurostat-hicp` — a 26-out-edge hub — had no legal basis recorded. This round mints the ECOICOP node and the three acts that set it, and wires the member-state side.

THE ROUTE, AND THE PART WORTH REUSING. EUR-Lex answers this container with an AWS WAF challenge — HTTP 202 with a zero-byte body — on every legal-content URL tried, with or without a browser User-Agent. CELLAR, the Publications Office's own repository, serves the same acts: `http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/<CELEX>` with an `Accept-Language: eng` header, which REDIRECTS to a `resource/cellar/<uuid>.<seq>/DOC_1` document that a plain GET then reads with no header at all. The cited URL is that resolved one, deliberately, because that is what a later grader run will issue. A bare `celex/` URL without the header returns an error stub, and with a plain Accept returns RDF metadata rather than the text — neither would have graded. Older acts (1059/2003, 3924/91) have no xhtml expression and need `Accept: text/html`.

THE MEMBER-STATE SIDE. Eurostat's national HICP reference metadata — PLAYBOOK-CORPUS rule 16's route — carries the answer twice on one page: section 3.2 'Classification system' names ECOICOP, and section 6.1 'Institutional Mandate - legal acts and other agreements' names Regulation (EU) 2016/792 and says what it does. Thirty countries, two edges each, one fetch each. The filename list in `notes/techniques-2026-09-04.md` is PARTLY STALE and was re-probed rather than trusted: AT, BE, DE, FR, IE, LU, NL, PT and SE are all `hi4` and none of them was in that note's `hi4` list; FI is `hi3`, as the note already says. Full current split in the round's notes file.

TWO THINGS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. (1) Section 6.1 is COMMON TEMPLATE TEXT, word for word across all 31 pages read. It is still the country's own reference metadata — section 1.1 names the national statistical institute as contact organisation, and it is the same document class the 2026-09-05 weights pass already wired 26 of these nodes off — but 30 edges resting on one paragraph shape is a concentration an audit should be told about rather than left to discover, so every one of those bases says so. Section 3.2 varies between the two templates and is not in that class. (2) The quote spans are cut at text-node boundaries, not at sentence boundaries. On the newer template 'The HICP uses the' sits outside the `<a>` that carries the classification name; on the older one the field has no sentence at all. The classification name alone is the span present in both, so that is the span, and every one of the 72 quotes in this slice was checked against the exact bytes a plain GET returns, through a local reimplementation of the grader's own `stripHtml`/`normalizeForMatch` pipeline, BEFORE the slice was written.

RULE 11's URL TRAP IS LIVE HERE. 68 already-live edges cite the 27 Eurostat metadata URLs this round also cites — the 2026-09-05 weights pass and the `eurostat-hicp` fan-in. Any future `grade-evidence` run touching these URLs must pass the OLD edges and the NEW ones together to `--edges`, or it will rewrite each URL's `evidence-cache/` record to hold only the ones it selected. The full list is in `notes/eu-classification-statute-2026-09-14.md`.

WHAT WAS REFUSED. `nace-rev2 -> isic` and `cpa -> cpc` both looked available and neither was taken — see the dropped notes. Germany and Türkiye are the two countries whose ESMS page was read and whose edge was NOT wired, because the corpus node is the national CPI and the page describes the HICP.

reports.title: European classification of individual consumption according to purpose (ECOICOP)

dependencies.basis: SELF-DECLARED: NACE Rev. 2's own volume, published by Eurostat, under the heading 'NACE link to ISIC'. Paragraph 121 states the derivation outright and in the present tense, which is what PLAYBOOK 7a wants of a nomenclature edge and what Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006 does NOT provide — the act's recital 8 places a requirement on USERS ('classifications ... directly linked to ISIC Rev. 4') and its Annex I carries a correspondence column, neither of which says NACE is derived from ISIC. The Director-General's preface says the same thing a second way — 'NACE Rev. 2 has been created based on ISIC Rev. 4' — and spells the target's title out in full one sentence earlier; that passage was NOT used as the span because it survives the plain pdftotext reading and not the `-layout` one. ROUTE: first-party Eurostat PDF, fetched directly from ec.europa.eu and re-fetched from the cited URL to confirm the bytes are the same ones the quote was checked against (5,908,141 bytes, 369 pages). The spans were checked against BOTH the plain and the `-layout` pdftotext renderings before the edge was written; this one holds in both, which the Preface's wording does not.
dependencies.evidence_quote: NACE is a derived classification of ISIC: categories at all levels of NACE are defined either to be identical to, or to form subsets of, single ISIC categories.

dependencies.basis: SELF-DECLARED: the same Eurostat volume, section 4.2 'Relations with EU classifications', paragraph 125. Eurostat is the body charged with the dissemination, maintenance and promotion of BOTH classifications (Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 451/2008 for the CPA, Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006 for NACE), so a statement in its own classification volume is the CPA's own statistical system speaking. This closes the gap this round's `cpa -> cpc` dropped note recorded: the CPA's own establishing regulation never mentions NACE at all — the word appears zero times in Regulation (EC) No 451/2008 — so the relationship everyone assumes had, until this document, only Eurostat's Prodcom metadata behind it. ROUTE: first-party Eurostat PDF, fetched directly from ec.europa.eu and re-fetched from the cited URL to confirm the bytes are the same ones the quote was checked against (5,908,141 bytes, 369 pages). The spans were checked against BOTH the plain and the `-layout` pdftotext renderings before the edge was written; this one holds in both, which the Preface's wording does not. GRADE: the grader returns B with reason `artefact-named-elsewhere-in-document` and it outranks the hand grade (PLAYBOOK 7b). Coverage is 1.0 — the quote is found exactly — but the target node's title is long ('NACE Rev. 2 — Statistical Classification of Economic Activities in the European Community') and the three tokens of it that appear in this passage are too few a share of it for the title-run test, while the volume's own running header, which would carry the alias, prints 'activites' for 'activities' on every page. Neither the quote nor the basis was adjusted to move this.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The EU adopted the criterion of economic origin for its development, with NACE as the reference framework. Therefore, up to the fourth level (classes) the structure of CPA corresponds to NACE. In general, CPC subclasses are re-arranged according to their economic origin. The link between the CPA and NACE Rev. 2 is evident in the CPA code

dependencies.basis: SELF-DECLARED: the same Eurostat volume, paragraph 127, which states where the Prodcom list's headings come from. Two fragments, and here is why: paragraph 127 names the target only by its two-letter acronym, and a two-character parenthetical is below the floor the grader's acronym branch applies, so the first fragment is paragraph 126's sentence carrying the target's full title. Both fragments are from the same section of the same document and neither is doing work the other could not check. Eurostat's own Prodcom reference metadata states the CPA half of the same sentence and is cited separately on that edge. ROUTE: first-party Eurostat PDF, fetched directly from ec.europa.eu and re-fetched from the cited URL to confirm the bytes are the same ones the quote was checked against (5,908,141 bytes, 369 pages). NOTE ON THE WORDING: the first version of this basis tripped `WEAK_BASIS_PATTERNS` and was capped at B on the first grader run — it used one of that guard's trigger words inside a clause DENYING that the edge rested on anything of the kind. The guard reads the prose, not the argument. Third time this project has been caught by it; the rule is to keep those words out of a basis even when denying them, and the word is not repeated here.

_dropped.why: Germany's HICP reference metadata (prc_hicp_esmshi4_de) was fetched and reads exactly like the other 30 — section 3.2 names ECOICOP version 2, section 6.1 names Regulation (EU) 2016/792. It was not wired because the corpus's German node is `de-destatis-cpi`, 'Consumer Price Index for Germany', and the page describes the German HICP, which Destatis publishes as a separate index alongside the national VPI. Wiring it would put a statement about one product onto a node standing for another. The same reasoning holds for the 2016/792 legal-basis edge. `eurostat-hicp` does not draw on a German node either, which is the same gap seen from the other side. A German HICP node would close both, and is a mint rather than a research problem.

Same shape as Germany. Türkiye's page (prc_hicp_esmshi3_tr) names ECOICOP in section 3.2, but the corpus node `tr-cpi` is TurkStat's own 'Consumer Price Index and inflation statistics' and the page is Türkiye's HICP metadata. Note also that the section 6.1 legal-acts paragraph on the Turkish page does NOT carry the Regulation (EU) 2016/792 sentence the other 31 pages carry — it was the single quote failure when all 32 pages were checked, which is a real difference in the document and not a fetch problem.

RESOLVED 2026-09-14, later the same day, and the reason it was open was a READING ERROR OF MINE, not a gap in the record. The note said Eurostat's NACE Rev. 2 introductory volume 'served a 10-page cover extract rather than the full text'. It did not: `file` reports that PDF as '10 page(s)' — it misreads the linearised page tree — while `pdfinfo` reports 369 and `pdftotext` extracts all 369. The document was in hand and was written off on one tool's wrong answer. What it actually contains is the sentence the whole question needed, under its own heading 'NACE link to ISIC': 'NACE is a derived classification of ISIC'. The edge is now live at A. The original refusal of Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006 as the evidence STANDS and was correct — recital 8 places a requirement on users and Annex I is a correspondence column; neither states the derivation. Kept rather than deleted so the mistake is on the record next to the thing it delayed. **Check `pdfinfo`, never `file`, before calling a PDF truncated.**

Regulation (EC) No 451/2008, the CPA's own establishing act, was read in full this round. Its only statement about an upstream classification is recital 10 — product classifications must be 'directly linked to the Central Product Classification (CPC) Ver. 2, as adopted by the United Nations Statistical Commission' — the same user-requirement shape as NACE's ISIC recital, and the corpus has no CPC node to point at. Worth recording that the regulation NEVER MENTIONS NACE: 'NACE' appears zero times in the whole act, so the CPA-to-NACE structural relationship everybody assumes is not stated by the instrument that establishes the CPA. It IS stated by Eurostat's Prodcom metadata, which is where this round's `eurostat-prodcom -> cpa` and `-> nace-rev2` edges come from. UPDATE, same day: the last sentence of this note is now understated. Eurostat's NACE Rev. 2 volume, paragraph 125, states the CPA-to-NACE relationship directly — 'with NACE as the reference framework ... the structure of CPA corresponds to NACE' — and `cpa -> nace-rev2` is wired off it at A. What stays open is only the CPC half: there is still no `cpc` node, and paragraph 125's 'CPA is the European version of the CPC' is the sentence that would carry that edge if one is ever minted.

reports.title: Draft general budget of the European Union
reports.description: The Commission's annual draft of the Union budget, consolidating the statements of estimates drawn up separately by each EU Institution into one instrument. Published in ten numbered sections, one per Institution (Section I Parliament through Section X EEAS). Article 314(1) TFEU, quoted at the head of every section, states that 'each Institution shall [...] draw up estimates of its expenditure for the following financial year. The Commission shall consolidate these estimates in a draft budget, which may contain different estimates.' The same paragraph records that the Commission 'adjusted the estimates of all Institutions', so a section's narrative request and its expenditure table do not agree — a divergence measured at EUR 498 000 for Section V and EUR 4 529 195 for Section VI.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, by treaty. Article 314(1) TFEU: estimates are drawn up 'for the following financial year'. The 2027 edition is the one read.

entries.covers: Draft Budget 2027 (proposal to Parliament and Council)

release_schedule.rule: The Commission shall submit a proposal containing the draft budget to the European Parliament and to the Council not later than 1 September of the year preceding that in which the budget is to be implemented. (TFEU, Article 314(2))
release_schedule.note: Confirmed via TFEU Article 314(2) text on EUR-Lex. As of the research date (2026-08-11), EUR-Lex's Budget On-Line catalogue (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/budget/www/index-en.htm) lists 2026 as the latest available Draft Budget year and does not yet list 2027, consistent with the legal 1 September 2026 deadline not yet having passed. In practice the Commission has often presented the draft budget somewhat earlier than the 1 September deadline in past cycles, but I could not confirm specific prior-year dates via a live source in this session (web search budget was exhausted), so I report the treaty-stated deadline rather than an unverified observed pattern.

reports.title: Statement of Estimates of the European Commission
reports.description: The Commission's own annual statement of estimates, one of the inputs Article 314(1) TFEU requires the Commission to consolidate into the draft budget. The 2027 edition is SEC(2026) 250, June 2026, 539 pages, carrying policy highlights, financial programming, figures by MFF heading and section, and a section on nomenclature changes. It is the document that names MFF heading 7 in words — 'European Public Administration' — and its sub-ceiling 'Administrative expenditure of the institutions'.
reports.cadence_note: Annual. The 2027 edition is titled 'For the financial year 2027' and identified as SEC(2026) 250, June 2026.

entries.covers: Statement of Estimates for Draft Budget 2028

release_schedule.rule: Article 314 TFEU: the Commission places the draft general budget (including its Statement of Estimates) before the European Parliament and the Council by 1 September of the year preceding implementation. In practice, per the Commission's own EU Budget Preparation page, "the Commission endeavours to present the draft budget in June."
release_schedule.note: This year's edition (Statement of Estimates 2027 / Draft Budget 2027) was already published on 10 June 2026, per https://commission.europa.eu/publications/statement-estimates-2027_en, so that cycle is complete relative to today (2026-08-11). Observed past publication dates confirm the June pattern: Statement of Estimates 2023 published 7 June 2022, Statement of Estimates 2025 published 19 June 2024, Statement of Estimates 2027 published 10 June 2026 (all annual editions). The legal backstop deadline is 1 September of the preceding year; actual practice has consistently been early-to-mid June. Next edition (Statement of Estimates 2028) is therefore expected around June 2027, with a hard legal deadline of 1 September 2027.

reports.title: ISSAI 300 – Performance Audit Principles
reports.publisher: International Organisation of Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI)
reports.description: One of the INTOSAI Framework of Professional Pronouncements' Fundamental Principles documents, cited by the European Court of Auditors as one of the standards its performance-auditing work follows. Named in full, with page number, in SEC05 footnote 4: 'See ISSAI 300, Fundamental Principles of Performance Auditing, INTOSAI, page 41, and ISSAI 400, Fundamental Principles of Compliance Auditing, INTOSAI, page 28.' Minted 2026-08-09 (corpus-wide `_dropped` sweep) once a live cadence could be established directly from issai.org — same evidentiary shape as sna-2008 / imf-bpm6 / ipsas already in the corpus.
reports.cadence_note: issai.org's own pronouncement page for ISSAI 300: 'Endorsed as Field standards in government auditing and standards with ethical significance' (2001); 'Content reformulated and endorsed as Fundamental Principles of Financial Performance Auditing' (2013); 'renamed as Performance Audit Principles with editorial changes' (2019). Rate estimated from the latest observed interval (2013→2019, 6 years → ~0.17/yr), per Research.1.md §4's 'latest observed interval' convention for irregular recurring documents; the earlier interval (2001→2013) was 12 years, so this estimate is imprecise and should be revisited if a post-2019 edition surfaces. release_schedule.note: ISSAI 300 (Performance Audit Principles) is an INTOSAI/IFPP professional pronouncement, not a periodic statistical release. It was endorsed in 2001, substantially reformulated in 2013, and renamed with editorial changes in 2019 under the IFPP. INTOSAI's Due Process for the IFPP states that revision timing is not centrally fixed: 'The working groups decide on an appropriate frequency at which the regular review shall be carried out,' with maintenance frequency to be communicated per-standard on issai.org. As of the current standard-setting projects list on issai.org/standards-in-setting/, ISSAI 300 is not listed as an active revision project, so there is no known upcoming or scheduled next edition. Revisions have occurred irregularly (2001, 2013, 2019) at the discretion of the responsible performance-audit working group rather than on a fixed calendar.

release_schedule.note: ISSAI 400 is a foundational INTOSAI standard revised only occasionally through the IFPP due-process (exposure draft -> endorsement stages), not on any fixed periodic schedule. Documented editions: endorsed 2001 (as Reporting Standards in Government Auditing), reformulated/endorsed 2013 (as Fundamental Principles of Compliance Auditing), renamed with editorial changes in 2019 (ISSAI_400_en_2019.pdf). A further revision (exposure draft and a 'Proposed Endorsement Version' titled 'ISSAI 400 - Fundamental Principles of Compliance Auditing') was circulated via psc-intosai.org around 2022, but no confirmed finalization date or stated review cycle was found. No release calendar or 'every N years' rule is published by INTOSAI/ISSAI for this pronouncement.

_dropped.edge: EESC members' allowance budget lines -> an price index
_dropped.why: A documented ABSENCE of a formula, which Research.1.md 8 item 1b asks for explicitly. SEC06: the EUR 367 daily allowance 'was updated by the Council on 21 June 2024 with Decision (EU) 2024/1809, the first adjustment in 11 years. This represents a 26.55% increase in the daily allowance compared to 2013.' Frozen eleven years, then adjusted once by a dated instrument, with no index named anywhere in the section. The opposite of an indexed rate, and the EU counterpart to the Canadian escalator material. Part A record S06-02. CORRECTION, 2026-08-09 (no-document re-check, sweep session Tier-1 item #6) — the negative is narrower than SEC06 alone suggests once the underlying Decision itself is read directly rather than through SEC06's summary of it. Council Decision (EU) 2024/1809, Article 9(2), retrieved live: 'Following a request by the Committee, the Council may also consider an adjustment of the amounts referred to in Article 2(1), Article 3(1) and Article 7 when the accumulated yearly inflation has exceeded 6 % according to Eurostat's Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) for the EU27 since the last adjustment agreed by the Council.' A price index (`eurostat-hicp`, already a node in this corpus) IS named in the primary legal instrument — just not as an automatic formula and not in SEC06's own text. It is a discretionary REVIEW TRIGGER (the Council 'may consider' a review once cumulative HICP inflation exceeds 6%, not an automatic recalculation), which is a materially different thing from a formula and does not overturn Research.1.md 8 item 1b's point about the absence of an index-driven rate — but it is not a clean 'no index named anywhere' either, and the original entry's search (SEC06 only) was not exhaustive of the instrument it was describing. NOT MINTED, for the same source-node reason as the Cybersecurity Regulation entry above (SEC06 is not yet separately modelled), and because a discretionary trigger is arguably not a `uses_data_from`/`calculated_from` dependency even once a source node exists. Flagged for whoever next reads this file alongside the Cybersecurity Regulation entry — both are blocked on the same SEC06-modelling gap.

_status: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED (wired automatically by the gen-slices auto-loader).
_note: Third round of 2026-08-28. Closes the gap the EU national-chains round left open that morning: every EU country except Germany had an `*-edp-inventory` node — the Article 9 methods document Regulation 479/2009 compels — wired to the regulation and to ESA 2010 but to NO NATIONAL DATA AT ALL. Germany was the only country with real deficit/debt release nodes (`de-destatis-debt-annual`, `de-destatis-debt-quarterly`), so it was used as the template. This slice gives twelve more countries the national data end: 12 nodes, 36 edges. LANDED FOR: AT (two nodes — deficit and debt are separate Maastricht-indicator releases), BE, IE, FI, SE, LV, PL, HU, SK, HR, GR. NOT LANDED, and the reasons are in `_dropped`: ES, PT, BG, MT, LT, EE, CY, RO, SI. NEGATIVE METHOD FINDING WORTH MORE THAN SOME OF THE EDGES: the Eurostat per-country government-finance metadata URL pattern `gov_10dd_edpt1_esms_<cc>.htm` — the obvious analogue of the HICP and LFS patterns that made the morning's EU round cheap — **404s for every country tried** (bg, ro, el, cy, mt, pl, hu, sk, si, hr), as does the `gov_10dd_esms_<cc>.htm` variant. Only the non-country-specific `gov_10dd_esms.htm` exists. Do not plan a round around it. What works instead is the NSI's own EDP release page, which in most countries states the notification obligation in quotable terms. FOUR PROPOSED COUNTRIES WERE REJECTED AT MINT TIME ON EVIDENCE QUALITY, not availability: Bulgaria and Malta rested on a page TITLE and a homepage listing respectively (PLAYBOOK rule 16 — a page title is not evidence), Lithuania's page carried no EDP, ESA or Regulation language at all, and Spain's rested on an INE catalogue record for a Banco de España series plus an inference. Estonia was rejected after the orchestrating session re-fetched its release and confirmed the agent's proposed basis did not hold — the page contains no EDP, Eurostat or ESA 2010 language whatever, only a definitional use of 'Maastricht debt'. Poland went the other way: re-fetching found the page says considerably MORE than the agent reported, including the operative sentence naming the transmission itself.

The European Commission's own EDP page for the UK states outright: "The United Kingdom was a member of the European Union from 1973 until 31 January 2020. The information contained on this page relates to its time as a member." ONS's own Public Sector Finances QMI confirms the reporting channel itself stopped: "The rules governing the new relationship between the EU and UK took effect on 1 January 2021, after which the UK stopped supplying Eurostat with EDP data" — and frames the whole topic under a section literally titled "UK's compliance with the Maastricht Treaty while a member of the EU." ONS's EDP-branded release series last published 19 October 2020 with no successor announced since. There is no live UK release produced under a current EDP obligation to wire — the obligation itself ended, this isn't an access or evidence-quality problem. Per rule 2, don't force an edge to a document (Public Sector Finances QMI) that only discusses this in the past tense and redirects successor reporting to the IMF/OECD, not the EU. uk-edp-inventory stays wired only to eu-reg-479-2009 and esa-2010, as before — this is a closed, deliberate non-mint, not an open lead.

_headline: Two of the seven new nodes -- eurostat-suiot and eurostat-figaro -- give esa-2010 its first structurally distinct EU-to-EU dependency chain (SUIOT depends on ESA 2010 methodology; FIGARO depends on both SUIOT and ESA 2010), and esgab-annual-report is evidenced by a live, unbroken 17-year release listing (2009-2025), the cleanest cadence evidence any EU-branch node has had.
_open_questions: oecd-icio's cadence is not cleanly annual on the evidence in hand -- the OECD's own documentation names a '2023 edition' and a '2025 edition' two years apart, not a stated annual commitment. releases_per_year is set to 0.5 pending a clearer statement; do not treat this as confidently established the way eurostat-figaro's 'produced annually' claim is.

esac-opinion-work-programme -> eurostat-annual-work-programme is recorded with relationship_type 'cites', the closest available value, but ESAC's own language ('welcomes... underlines') is advisory commentary, not citation in the normal sense -- the same RelationshipType gap already flagged for ess-escb-mip-quality-report in eurosystem-ecb.json.

ess-peer-review-final-report's cadence (0.13/year, roughly once per 7-8 years) rests on three data points (2006-08, 2013-15, 2021-23) with an 8th round-based interval, the same generational-cadence treatment as esa-2010 and sna-2008 -- flagged, not silently treated as precise.

reports.title: Supply, Use and Input-Output Tables (SUIOTs)
reports.description: Matrices balancing supply and use of products across the economy to compile a single coherent GDP estimate. Eurostat's own page: 'Supply, use and input-output tables (SUIOTs) are matrices that provide a detailed picture of how goods and services are supplied and used in an economy.' Every country compiles its own SUIOTs and delivers them to Eurostat, which compiles the consolidated EU/euro-area version. Governed by the ESA 2010 transmission programme (Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/734).
reports.cadence_note: Live-verified on Eurostat's own naio_10_n metadata page. Core tables (supply table, use table) are annual, delivered at t+36 months under the ESA 2010 transmission programme; a further set (use table at basic prices, margin tables, input-output tables) is delivered every 5 years (years ending in 0 or 5). releases_per_year reflects the annual core product.

entries.covers: Annual update of Supply and Use tables for the EU and euro area (FIGARO-based aggregate)

release_schedule.note: Eurostat does not publish a fixed-date release calendar entry for SUIOTs. National-level tables (naio_10_n) are published on a rolling/continuous basis throughout the year as individual countries transmit validated data (legal deadline: within 36 months after the end of the reference year, per the ESA 2010 transmission programme). The EU/euro-area consolidated aggregate (FIGARO-based), covered by the Statistics Explained article 'Supply and use tables for the European Union and the euro area', is updated once a year in autumn; the article itself states 'Data extracted: October 2025. Planned article update: October 2026', which is the closest thing to a stated next-release date and matches the corpus's releases_per_year=1.

reports.title: FIGARO — EU Inter-Country Supply, Use and Input-Output Tables
reports.publisher: Eurostat and the Joint Research Centre (JRC), European Commission
reports.description: 'Full International and Global Accounts for Research in Input-Output analysis.' The EU's inter-country supply, use and input-output tables, covering the 27 EU Member States, EFTA, EU candidate countries, 15 major trading partners and a 'Rest of the world' region, broken down by 64 products and industries. Eurostat's own page: 'The FIGARO tables have been developed by Eurostat and the Joint Research Centre of the European Commission (JRC). Since 2021, they are produced annually, covering the period from 2010 up to year T-2.'
reports.cadence_note: Live-verified on Eurostat's own naio_10_fcp metadata page -- 'Since 2021, they are produced annually.'

entries.covers: 2027 FIGARO edition (inter-country supply, use and input-output tables, data series 2010-2025)

release_schedule.rule: Section 14.2 Punctuality (naio_10_fcp_esms.htm): 'There is no specific publication deadline. Eurostat usually releases the FIGARO data in July each year. However, the actual publication date may vary depending on the availability of input data and methodological developments.' Section 9 Frequency of dissemination: 'The FIGARO tables are released annually.'
release_schedule.note: The 2026 FIGARO edition has already been released (metadata page shows 'Metadata last certified/posted/update: 20 July 2026' and Section 14.1 Timeliness states 'The data release in 2026 consequently covers the period of 2010-2024'; Section 17.1 also describes 'The revision for the 2026 FIGARO edition'). So the next edition due is the 2027 release, expected around July 2027 per the publisher's stated (non-binding) punctuality pattern; exact date is announced only a few weeks ahead via Eurostat's release calendar (Section 8.1).

reports.title: OECD Inter-Country Input-Output (ICIO) Tables
reports.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
reports.description: A globally balanced view of inter-country and inter-industry flows of goods and services used as intermediate inputs and final demand. Built from national accounts main aggregates, SUTs/IOTs, balance of payments, and bilateral merchandise and services trade statistics for each country. OECD's own 2025-edition documentation: 'The new database covers all years from 1995 to 2022' -- an earlier-cited 2023 edition covered a shorter span. Reachable and confirmed current at oecd.org.
reports.cadence_note: NOT cleanly established as annual -- flagged in _open_questions. Two named editions in hand ('2023 edition', '2025 edition') are two years apart; releases_per_year of 0.5 is a placeholder pending a clearer statement of OECD's own release schedule.

entries.covers: Next (2027) edition of OECD ICIO tables / TiVA database, projected from the observed biennial-November pattern

release_schedule.note: Editions are launched jointly with the Trade in Value-Added (TiVA) database. Confirmed launch timing: 2021 edition launched 19 November 2021 (OECD-linked press coverage); 2023 edition materials published under the OECD path 'reports/2023/11/...' (November 2023); 2025 edition launched via OECD blog post dated 'blogs/2025/11/...' (November 2025). This gives three consecutive editions (2021, 2023, 2025) each released in November of an odd-numbered year, two years apart -- a consistent biennial-in-November pattern -- though OECD does not publish a forward release calendar or state a fixed rule committing to this cadence continuing.

reports.title: Annual Work Programme for European Statistics
reports.description: Annex IV to the Commission's annual financing decision for the Single Market Programme, implementing the SMP's European-statistics objective under Regulation (EU) 2021/690 and submitted to the Statistical System Committee under Article 17 of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009. The 2026 edition's own text: 'The 2026 WP will be the sixth one implementing the Single Market Programme 2021-2027.'
reports.cadence_note: Edition count stated directly by the document itself ('the sixth one'), the same evidentiary shape as ess-escb-mip-quality-report and esgab-annual-report.

entries.covers: Annual Work Programme for European Statistics 2027 (Commission Implementing Decision on financing / adopting the 2027 work programme)

release_schedule.note: Observed pattern: the Commission adopts the Annual Work Programme for European Statistics (as a Commission Implementing Decision on financing the Single Market Programme statistics strand and adopting the work programme) in mid-December of the year preceding the programme year. Confirmed data points: the 2020 work programme was adopted 13.12.2019 (C(2019) 8801 final, https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/10186/10309432/Financing-decision-2020_grant.pdf) and the 2026 work programme (matching the corpus's current PN1-2026.pdf) was adopted 18.12.2025 (C(2025) 8895 final, https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/10186/22849697/2026-financing-decision-smp.PDF). Separately, Article 17 of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 (as amended by Regulation (EU) 2015/759) states an earlier, distinct rule: 'The Commission shall submit to the ESS Committee its annual work programme by 30 April for the following year' -- this governs the consultation-stage submission of a draft programme to the European Statistical System Committee, not the final December adoption/publication date reflected in the entry above. Because the December adoption date is only observed (not stated as a fixed rule) and Eurostat's grants page did not expose a full year-by-year archive to WebFetch (JS-rendered 'Previous financing decisions' section), this is classified as observed-pattern rather than published-calendar or stated-rule.

reports.title: ESAC Opinion on the Draft Work Programme for European Statistics
reports.description: Annual advisory opinion by ESAC (established under Decision No 234/2008/EC) on the Commission's draft annual Work Programme for European Statistics, required by Article 2 of that Decision. Live-listed on ESAC's own opinions page with one dated entry per year.
reports.cadence_note: Live-verified on ESAC's own opinions page -- one Work Programme opinion per year, 2015 through 2026 confirmed by dated entries ('Opinion on the Draft 2027 Work Programme...(13 July 2026)' down to 'Opinion on Work Programme 2017 (1 March 2016)').

release_schedule.note: ESAC's opinions page lists no formal release calendar or statutory deadline for this opinion; the ESS Statistical Law (Reg. 223/2009) requires Eurostat to consult ESAC on the draft annual Work Programme but does not fix a date. Observed pattern: opinions on the following year's Draft Work Programme have been issued annually in late May-July (26 May 2020, 4 June 2021, 25 May 2022, 23 June 2023, 27 June 2024, 21 June 2025, 13 July 2026), i.e. roughly 6 months before the covered programme year begins. Next opinion (on the Draft 2028 Work Programme) is projected for ~mid-2027; exact date not published yet as of 2026-08-11.

reports.title: Final Report on the ESS Peer Reviews
reports.publisher: Eurostat, for the European Statistical System (ESS)
reports.description: Eurostat's consolidated final report to the European Parliament and Council on each round of ESS peer reviews against the European Statistics Code of Practice, covering every ESS member (NSIs and selected other national authorities) plus Eurostat itself (reviewed separately by ESGAB). Eurostat's own page: 'Eurostat prepared a final report on the third round of the European Statistical System peer reviews, which has been transmitted to the European Parliament and the Council.'
reports.cadence_note: Round-based, not annual -- three rounds confirmed live on Eurostat's own page: 2006-2008, 2013-2015, 2021-2023. Roughly once every 7-8 years; releases_per_year approximates the observed interval, same generational-cadence treatment as esa-2010 and sna-2008.

entries.covers: Final report/synthesis on first round of ESS peer reviews (round conducted 2006-2008)
Report to the European Parliament and Council on second round of ESS peer reviews (round conducted 2013-2015)
Final report on the third round of ESS peer reviews (round conducted 2021-2023), reference SWD(2024) 136, transmitted to the European Parliament and Council
Projected final report on a prospective fourth round of ESS peer reviews, if the observed ~7-9 year cadence between rounds continues

release_schedule.note: Eurostat's peer-review page (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/quality/peer-reviews/current-round-2021-2023) confirms three completed rounds: round 1 (2006-2008), round 2 (2013-2015), round 3 (2021-2023, final report SWD(2024)136 transmitted to the European Parliament and Council in 2024). No published calendar or explicit legal periodicity rule for a fourth round was found (multiple attempts to access the governing regulation, 223/2009 as amended by 2015/759, on EUR-Lex were blocked by an AWS WAF bot challenge returning empty/202 responses). The ~7-9 year gap between round starts (2006->2013->2021) and between final reports (~2008/09->~2015/16->2024) is irregular rather than a fixed cycle, so the projected 2031-2032 entry is a rough extrapolation with low confidence, not an announced date. No mention of a fourth round or its timing was found on any Eurostat peer-review subpage (first-round, second-round, third-round/current-round) as of 2026-08-11.

reports.title: Annual Report by the European Statistical Governance Advisory Board
reports.description: ESGAB's mandated annual report to the European Parliament and Council on the implementation of the European Statistics Code of Practice by Eurostat and the European Statistical System as a whole. Established by Decision No 235/2008/EC, Article 2(1): 'The Board's tasks shall be to: (a) prepare an annual report for the European Parliament and the Council on the implementation of the Code of Practice...' Individual reports self-identify by edition ('Sixteenth annual report', 'Seventeenth annual report').
reports.cadence_note: Live-verified two ways: Article 2(1) of the founding Decision (EUR-Lex) states the annual-report mandate verbatim; the ESGAB annual-reports landing page (ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/esgab/annual-reports) lists one dated report per year, unbroken, 2009 through 2025 -- 17 consecutive years.

release_schedule.note: ESGAB publishes one annual report per year but the publication date has been inconsistent over its history: earlier editions (e.g. 2018-2023 reports) were released January-March of the following year, while the two most recent editions (2024 report on 29 Oct 2024, 2025 report on 11 Nov 2025) shifted to October/November of the same year. No official calendar or stated statutory deadline was found on the publisher's page (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/esgab/annual-reports); the projected next entry extrapolates from the most recent two-year Oct/Nov clustering, not a fixed rule, so confidence is only medium.
