_status: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED (wired automatically by the gen-slices auto-loader).
_note: EU/EEA national-chain round, 21 countries that each had exactly three nodes (EDP inventory, ESS peer review report, national accounts) and ZERO country-internal dependency edges — they hung off the Eurostat/ESA hubs and nothing else. This round mints each country's own price index, household budget survey and labour force survey, and wires the three documented domestic dependencies between them: CPI/HICP weights from national accounts household final consumption expenditure, CPI/HICP weights from the HBS, and national-accounts employment from the LFS. It also resolves the granularity question left open in eurostat-hicp.json (_open_questions, 2026-08-05: 'if a future session wants country-level granularity for HICP... this node may need to be split'): eurostat-hicp now has incoming uses_data_from edges from the national HICPs it aggregates, rather than being split. Researched by 21 parallel subagents, one per country, each told a guessed answer is worse than none and required to WebFetch and quote. FOUR load-bearing quotes were independently re-fetched and confirmed verbatim by the orchestrating session before minting: Poland's Eurostat ESMS weights sentence, Ireland's CSO CPI background-notes HFMCE/HBS sentences, Austria's std_v_vpi_hvpi.pdf Gewichtung sentence, and Greece's Eurostat ESMS weights sentence. METHOD FINDING worth reusing: the two Eurostat national reference metadata URL patterns are the highest-yield source for this whole class of question — https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/cache/metadata/EN/prc_hicp_esmshi4_<cc>.htm (HICP weights + transmission) and https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/cache/metadata/EN/employ_simslfs_<cc>.htm (whether the LFS is the national-accounts employment source, stated as an explicit Y/N field). CAUTION: the HICP filename is versioned per country and NOT uniform — esmshi4 for PL/EL/ES/HU/HR/BG/LT, esmshi3 for SK/SI/EE/LV/MT/CY/IS, and 404 for FI. Try hi4, fall back to hi3. NEGATIVE FINDINGS ARE REAL DATA here, not gaps: the employ_simslfs pages state outright that Cyprus 'doesn't make use of LFS, or makes minimal use of it' for national accounts and that Slovenia is the same, so those two countries correctly have NO national-accounts<-LFS edge — see _dropped. Spain, Hungary, Slovakia, Croatia, Latvia and Lithuania are documented as using the LFS as a main-but-not-sole source, and their edge bases quote that caveat rather than overclaiming. NOT DONE this round: no government-finance / EDP notification node was researched for any of the 21 — every agent deprioritised it in favour of the CPI/HBS/LFS core, so treat it as unresearched rather than absent. Portugal is the thinnest country here: ine.pt refused essentially every fetch (robots.txt ConnectTimeout, reproduced independently by the orchestrating session), so pt-ine-idef's url points at the INE IPC release that evidences it rather than at IDEF's own page, no Portuguese LFS node exists, and Romania lost its IAPC node to the same failure mode on insse.ro.

reports.title: Wskaźnik cen towarów i usług konsumpcyjnych / Zharmonizowany wskaźnik cen konsumpcyjnych (HICP) — Consumer Price Index / Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices
reports.description: GUS's monthly price release, covering both the national CPI and the harmonised HICP. GUS's own press-release page states prices are recorded once a month ("Ceny towarów i usług notowane są raz w miesiącu") and that the national index's weights come from the household survey: "Wagi pochodzą z Badania Budżetów Gospodarstw Domowych (BBGD) – cyklicznego badania ankietowego mierzącego wydatki i dochody ok. 37 tys. gospodarstw domowych." Eurostat's Poland national reference metadata separates the two weighting systems: "The main source of HICP weights are National Accounts while the system of weight for CPI is based on data from Household Budget Survey."
reports.cadence_note: GUS's press-release page states prices are recorded monthly; Eurostat's Poland HICP metadata confirms the full set is "published each month according to a pre-announced schedule, usually between 15 and 18 days after the end of the reference month."

reports.title: Badanie budżetów gospodarstw domowych (BBGD) — Household Budget Survey
reports.description: GUS's own survey page names as one of its purposes "tworzenia wag do obliczania indeksów cen towarów i usług konsumpcyjnych" (creating weights for calculating consumer price indices), and describes it as a continuous year-round survey ("cały rok – badanie ciągłe").
reports.cadence_note: Fieldwork is continuous ("cały rok – badanie ciągłe", GUS BBGD survey page) but the results report "Budżety gospodarstw domowych w 2023 roku" states its own publication frequency explicitly: "Częstotliwość wydania: Roczna" (annual).

reports.title: Badanie Aktywności Ekonomicznej Ludności (BAEL) — Labour Force Survey
reports.description: GUS's BAEL survey page describes it as "Jest głównym źródłem danych wykorzystywanych do konstrukcji wskaźników z zakresu rynku pracy" (the main source of data used for constructing labour-market indicators), used by among others the National Bank of Poland, the ECB, the ILO, the OECD and the World Bank.
reports.cadence_note: Survey is continuous, results quarterly: "Co kwartał dostarcza wiarygodnych danych dotyczących sytuacji osób pracujących, bezrobotnych oraz biernych zawodowo" (GUS BAEL page).

reports.title: Indicele Prețurilor de Consum (IPC) — Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Romania's national CPI. INS's own methodological notes state the weights come from the Household Budget Survey: "Ponderile utilizate pentru calculul IPC sunt obţinute din Ancheta Bugetelor de Familie (ABF)", with the current weight base set out as "începând din ianuarie 2023, calculul indicilor lunari cu bază fixă se face utilizând preţurile medii din anul 2021 (anul 2021=100) şi ponderile din acelaşi an." NOTE: this is the national IPC, NOT the harmonised IAPC — the IAPC quality report and every other insse.ro page refused to load this round, so Romania has no HICP node and no edge into eurostat-hicp.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly; INS publishes a per-month press release (source PDFs named ipc01r25.pdf, ipc05r26_0.pdf etc.) and the methodological notes describe "calculul indicilor lunari cu bază fixă".

reports.title: Ancheta Bugetelor de Familie (ABF) — Household Budget Survey
reports.description: Romania's household income-and-expenditure survey, named as the source of the IPC weights by INS's own methodological notes. The European Commission's CROS survey catalogue lists it as "Ancheta Bugetelor de Familie (ABF)"; Eurostat's EU-wide HBS metadata states the survey's core purpose across participating countries is that "The main purpose of this survey at national level is to update the weights of the basket of goods and services used for the calculation of the HICP."
reports.cadence_note: RECURRING, cadence unconfirmed — not a one-off instrument. INS's own ABF pages (quality report, manual) all failed to load from insse.ro this round. Eurostat's EU-wide HBS metadata describes the harmonised EU round as roughly five-yearly ("1988, 1994, 1999, 2005, 2010, 2015 and 2020") with Romania a participant, but that is the EU transmission round, not INS's domestic fieldwork/publication cadence. releases_per_year omitted rather than guessed.

reports.description: Eurostat's Romania LFS national reference metadata gives the "Compiling agency: National Institute of Statistics" and states plainly of national accounts that "In NA: LFS is the main data source", alongside "Country uses LFS as the only source for employment in national accounts". reports.title: Konsumentprisindex (KPI) — Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Sweden's national consumer price index. SCB's KPI service page states "KPI publiceras månadsvis i regel runt 10–14 dagar in på nästkommande månad efter redovisningsmånaden" (KPI is published monthly, typically 10–14 days into the month following the reference month). SCB's official 'Statistikens framställning' document for KPI 2024 states the weights come from the national accounts: "Underlag för vägningstalen är i första hand Nationalräkenskaperna."
reports.cadence_note: Monthly, per SCB's KPI service page ("KPI publiceras månadsvis...").

reports.title: Harmoniserat index för konsumentpriser (HIKP) — Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP), Sweden
reports.description: Sweden's EU-harmonised consumer price index. SCB's HIKP page states "It is the same price material that forms the basis for HIKP in Sweden as for CPI and other price indices SCB calculates" and that "The measure is published by SCB monthly in connection with the publication of CPI"; SCB's KPI production-of-statistics document adds "KPI är också utgångspunkt för beräkningen av det EU-harmoniserade måttet Harmoniserat Index för Konsumentpriser (HIKP)."
reports.cadence_note: Monthly, published with the KPI: "The measure is published by SCB monthly in connection with the publication of CPI" (SCB HIKP page).

reports.title: Hushållens utgifter (HUT) — Household Budget Survey
reports.description: SCB's household expenditure survey, run irregularly rather than annually. SCB's HE0201-EN page states the surveys "have been carried out since 1958" and that "The survey will be conducted in 2026 and then every five years starting in 2030" — so it is NOT discontinued. Notably, NO fetched SCB page names HUT as a source of KPI or HIKP weights; SCB attributes those to the national accounts instead (see _dropped).
reports.cadence_note: Five-yearly from 2030, per scb.se/HE0201-EN: "The survey will be conducted in 2026 and then every five years starting in 2030." Most recent full results found were for 2021, reported December 2022.

reports.title: Arbetskraftsundersökningarna (AKU) — Labour Force Surveys
reports.description: SCB's Labour Force Survey. SCB's "more about the Labour Force Survey" page states "LFS is also used in the work of Statistics Sweden, partly for national accounts work, partly for labour force analyses and prognoses."
reports.cadence_note: INFERRED, not quoted: the AKU statistics page shows a monthly series through "2026M07" and a next publication date of "2026-09-16", one month after the latest data point. No verbatim 'published monthly' sentence was found. Treat as lower-confidence than the KPI/HIKP figures — but the field is set rather than omitted because absence means 'one-off instrument' in this schema, which AKU certainly is not.

reports.title: Consumptieprijsindex / Indice des prix à la consommation — Consumer Price Index (and HICP)
reports.description: Monthly Statbel release covering the national consumer price index and Belgium's HICP. Statbel's methodology page describes an index that "objectively reflect[s] the price evolution over time for a basket of goods and services purchased by households," with results "available on the penultimate working day of the reference period," and states that "Weights are determined based on the household budget survey."
reports.cadence_note: Monthly; Statbel's CPI page states results are "available on the penultimate working day of the reference period."

reports.title: Gezondheidsindex / Indice santé — Health Index
reports.description: The legally operative Belgian index. Statbel states the consumer price index "forms the basis of another index: the health index," which excludes "alcoholic beverages (bought in a shop or consumed in a bar), tobacco products and motor fuels except for LPG," and that the smoothed four-month-moving-average version "is used as a basis for the indexation of retirement pensions, social security benefits and some salaries and wages," and that "The health index is used for the indexation of housing rents."
reports.cadence_note: INFERRED, not quoted: the health index is derived each month from the CPI (itself monthly), with a rolling four-month smoothed variant computed "since April 2016". Field set rather than omitted because absence means 'one-off instrument' in this schema.

reports.title: Huishoudbudgetonderzoek / Enquête sur le budget des ménages — Household Budget Survey
reports.description: Statbel's own HBS page describes it as "a survey on consumption expenditure of households," states "The survey is also the main source to compile the consumer price index," that "The choice of representative items and their weights in the basket are deeply reviewed every two years based on the most recent HBS," and that it serves "as input for updating the index basket and for estimating household consumption expenditure in the national accounts."
reports.cadence_note: Biennial: the survey "runs biannually (every two years) as of 2012, though it was conducted annually from 1999 to 2010" (Statbel HBS page).

reports.title: Enquête naar de arbeidskrachten (EAK) / Enquête sur les forces de travail (EFT) — Labour Force Survey
reports.description: Statbel's survey description page states its "main purpose is to classify the working-age population (15 years and older) into three groups (employed persons, unemployed, and inactive), and to provide descriptive and explanatory data on each of these categories," that "Each year, approximately 60,000 households are randomly selected," and that "This survey is also conducted in other EU Member States and is coordinated by EUROSTAT."
reports.cadence_note: RECURRING, publication cadence unconfirmed — not a one-off instrument. The fetched Statbel page confirms continuous annual sampling but states no release frequency; Statbel's annual "Labour Force Survey: publication with detailed figures" appeared only in unfetched search results. Statbel's English labour-market pages returned ROBOTS_DISALLOWED. releases_per_year omitted rather than guessed.

reports.title: Verbraucherpreisindex (VPI) — Austrian national Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Statistik Austria states "Der Verbraucherpreisindex (VPI) zeigt, wie sich die Preise für Waren und Dienstleistungen in Österreich verändern." The joint VPI/HVPI standard documentation states the basket weighting draws on two sources at once: "Die Gewichtung des Warenkorbes basiert auf den Ergebnissen der jeweils rezent vorliegenden Konsumerhebung sowie auf aktuellen Daten über den privaten Konsum aus den Volkswirtschaftlichen Gesamtrechnungen."
reports.cadence_note: "Die Veröffentlichung der beiden Indizes erfolgt monatlich, jeweils Mitte des Folgemonats und wird als Erstmitteilung in Form einer Presseaussendung und auf der Homepage am selben Tag mit Eurostat veröffentlicht" (std_v_vpi_hvpi.pdf) — re-fetched and confirmed verbatim by the orchestrating session.

reports.title: Harmonisierter Verbraucherpreisindex (HVPI) — Austria's Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices
reports.description: Statistik Austria states "Der Harmonisierte Verbraucherpreisindex (HVPI) ist die europäische Vergleichsgröße" and, in its VPI FAQ factsheet, that it "dient u. a. der Bewertung der Geldwertstabilität innerhalb der Euro-Zone." The standard documentation records the relationship to the national index: "Die beiden Indizes VPI und HVPI verwenden dieselben Preisdaten werden aber mit unterschiedlichen Gewichten berechnet."
reports.cadence_note: Published jointly with the VPI, monthly, mid-month following the reference month (std_v_vpi_hvpi.pdf).

reports.title: Konsumerhebung — Austrian Household Budget Survey
reports.description: Statistik Austria's Konsumerhebung page states: "Die Ausgabensummen und deren Verteilung auf einzelnen Ausgabengruppen bilden zudem eine wichtige Quelle für die Revision des Warenkorbes der Verbraucherpreisindizes" (the expenditure totals and their distribution across spending categories form an important source for revising the basket of the consumer price indices).
reports.cadence_note: "Die Konsumerhebung wird alle fünf Jahre durchgeführt" (conducted every five years) — statistik.at Konsumerhebung page.

reports.title: Mikrozensus-Arbeitskräfteerhebung (AKE) — Austrian Labour Force Survey
reports.description: Statistik Austria's Erwerbsstatus page publishes results as "Arbeitsmarktstatistik – 1. Quartal 2026, Mikrozensus-Arbeitskräfte-Erhebung" and states the results draw on register data alongside the survey: "Die Ergebnisse stammen aus der Mikrozensus-Arbeitskräfteerhebung (AKE) (Stichprobenerhebung) sowie der Registerzählung (RZ) und der Abgestimmten Erwerbsstatistik (AEST) (Administrativdatenabgleich)." NOTE: Austria is one of the countries where the national-accounts<-LFS edge was looked for and NOT found — see _dropped.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly; the Erwerbsstatus page lists a separate Arbeitsmarktstatistik publication for each quarter, e.g. "Arbeitsmarktstatistik – 1. Quartal 2026".

reports.title: Índice de Preços no Consumidor (IPC) — Consumer Price Index (carries the IHPC/HICP)
reports.description: INE's monthly consumer price release. The January 2024 edition states: "A estrutura de ponderação do IPC, que tem subjacente o conceito de despesa monetária de consumo final das famílias, tem como principal referência os dados detalhados (finais de 2021 e preliminares de 2022) das Contas Nacionais Portuguesas (SEC 2010)," and that the same weighting incorporates "os resultados do Inquérito às Despesas das Famílias (IDEF) realizado em 2015/2016." The IPC and IHPC weights are updated together: "os ponderadores do IPC e IHPC para 2024 foram atualizados com recurso adicional a informação preliminar das Contas Nacionais Trimestrais para 2023."
reports.cadence_note: INFERRED, not quoted: the fetched release does not state 'monthly' in so many words, but individually-dated monthly editions were located (Dec 2016, Dec 2023, Jan 2024, Dec 2024) on the same ine.pt attachment path. Field set rather than omitted because absence means 'one-off instrument' in this schema.

reports.title: Inquérito às Despesas das Famílias (IDEF) — Household Budget Survey
reports.description: Portugal's Household Budget Survey, named inside INE's own January 2024 IPC release as a weight source: "os resultados do Inquérito às Despesas das Famílias (IDEF) realizado em 2015/2016." URL CAVEAT: this node's url is that IPC release, not an IDEF page of its own — every ine.pt IDEF page refused to load (ROBOTS_DISALLOWED / robots.txt ConnectTimeout), reproduced independently by the orchestrating session, including a direct fetch of ine.pt/robots.txt itself. The domain root loaded and one deep PDF path loaded, so this reads as an intermittent robots-check fault rather than a real disallow; worth retrying in a later round to give this node its own page.
reports.cadence_note: RECURRING, cadence unconfirmed — not a one-off instrument. Editions labelled 2015/2016 and 2022/2023 appeared in unfetched search snippets, suggesting an irregular multi-year wave, but nothing was confirmed from a page that loaded. releases_per_year omitted rather than guessed.

reports.title: Δείκτης Τιμών Καταναλωτή (ΔΤΚ) — Consumer Price Index, National Index
reports.description: ELSTAT's national publication page gives the official title "Consumer Price Index (CPI) - National Index" and names a "Methodological Publication of CPI (2009=100.0)" as its reference methodology document; the current national index is compiled on a 2020=100.0 reference base. Distinct from the harmonised index gr-elstat-hicp, which has its own separately-documented weighting.
reports.cadence_note: ELSTAT's own CPI publication page (statistics.gr, publication code DKT87) states Release Frequency: Monthly.

reports.title: Εναρμονισμένος Δείκτης Τιμών Καταναλωτή (ΕνΔΤΚ) — Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices
reports.description: ELSTAT's HICP publication page gives the title "Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices (HICP)", produced by the Retail Price Indices Section. Eurostat's Greek national reference metadata sets out the two-tier weighting, re-fetched and confirmed verbatim by the orchestrating session: "The expenditures are based on National Accounts expenditure data and for and 5-digit COICOP level on HBS expenditure data, both for the year t-2."
reports.cadence_note: Monthly, confirmed on ELSTAT's own HICP page (publication code DKT90) and on Eurostat's Greek HICP metadata, which gives dissemination "between 15 and 18 days after the end of the reference month."

reports.title: Έρευνα Οικογενειακών Προϋπολογισμών (ΕΟΠ) — Household Budget Survey
reports.description: ELSTAT's own Household Budget Survey 2023 report states its purpose directly: "The main purpose of the HBS is to determine in detail the household expenditure pattern in order to revise the Consumer Price Index conducted by ELSTAT." The 2023 round sampled 5,832 private households nationwide.
reports.cadence_note: Annual and continuous: "From 2008 onwards, it was decided...that the survey should be annual and continuous" (ELSTAT HBS 2023); ELSTAT publishes a report per survey year (2017–2024 editions found).

reports.title: Έρευνα Εργατικού Δυναμικού (ΕΕΔ) — Labour Force Survey
reports.description: ELSTAT's Labour Force Survey release states: "From 1998 onwards it is a continuous quarterly survey," with monthly employment/unemployment estimates produced from a sub-sample and subsequently benchmarked so that "monthly averages" align with the finalized quarterly estimates. NOTE: Greece is one of the countries where the national-accounts<-LFS edge was looked for and not evidenced — see _dropped.
reports.cadence_note: ELSTAT publishes a named monthly release ("LABOUR FORCE SURVEY: March 2026", and Jan/Feb/Apr 2026 editions found) alongside a quarterly summary; the underlying design is "a continuous quarterly survey".

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (carries Ireland's HICP)
reports.description: Ireland's monthly Consumer Price Index release, which also carries the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices. The CSO's background notes state "Approximately 50,000 prices are collected...during the week containing the second Tuesday of each month up to and including the third Tuesday of each month." On weighting, the CSO's CPI methodology page states — re-fetched and confirmed verbatim by the orchestrating session — "Since 2012 the weights of the items in the basket have been updated annually at CPI COICOP class (4-digit) level using information on consumer expenditure from National Accounts Household Final Monetary Consumption Expenditure (HFMCE)," and "Additionally at the 2016 rebase, a more granular level update of the weights (5-digit) was possible using information from the latest Household Budget Survey (HBS) which was carried out between February 2015 and February 2016."
reports.cadence_note: Monthly; CSO CPI July 2026 background notes describe the monthly price-collection week.

reports.title: Household Budget Survey
reports.description: The CSO's technical note states the "Household Budget Survey (HBS) which is held every 5 years to fulfil a National requirement to update the weighting basis of the Consumer Price Index (CPI)", and the 2022-2023 edition's background notes state its "primary purpose... is to ensure that the Consumer Price Index (CPI), the official measure of inflation, continues to be based on up-to-date and accurate household expenditure."
reports.cadence_note: Every five years, per the CSO technical note (cso.ie/en/methods/tn/householdbudgetsurvey/): "held every 5 years".

reports.title: Labour Force Survey (LFS)
reports.description: Ireland's quarterly household survey of labour market activity, successor to the QNHS. The CSO's "About the Labour Force Survey" page states it "is designed to produce quarterly labour force estimates" and that "Each quarter the LFS will produce data on" the key labour market indicators.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly, per the CSO methodology page: "It is designed to produce quarterly labour force estimates."

reports.title: Índice de Precios de Consumo (IPC) / Índice de Precios de Consumo Armonizado (IPCA) — Consumer Price Index / Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices
reports.description: INE issues the national IPC and the harmonised IPCA in the same monthly release. INE's standardised methodological report states the index aims to "medir la evolución de los precios de los bienes y servicios de consumo adquiridos por los hogares residentes en España." Eurostat's Spain national reference metadata gives the weighting chain: "the main data source for the compilation of the HICP weights are the HFMCE data (in line with the domestic concept) from Spanish National Accounts (obtained from year t-2) further complemented with data from the Household Budget Survey and other sources."
reports.cadence_note: INE's methodological report states "El IPC se difunde mensualmente"; results appear around the 13th of the month following the reference month.

reports.title: Encuesta de Presupuestos Familiares (EPF) — Household Budget Survey
reports.description: INE's operation page describes the EPF as an operation that "suministra información anual sobre la naturaleza y destino de los gastos de consumo, así como sobre diversas características relativas a las condiciones de vida de los hogares," on a sample of roughly 24,000 households per year.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, per INE's own operation page (INEbase cid=1254736176806): "suministra información anual...".

reports.title: Encuesta de Población Activa (EPA) — Labour Force Survey
reports.description: INE's operation page describes the EPA as "a continuous investigation directed at family households" aimed at obtaining "data of the labor force and its various categories (employed, unemployed), as well as the population outside the labor market (inactive)", sampling roughly 47,500 households per quarter. CAVEAT recorded at mint time: these two quoted fragments came back from the fetch tool already in English despite the Spanish-locale source URL, so they may be an INE-provided English gloss rather than page-verbatim Spanish; the cadence and the edge evidence do not rest on them.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly, per INE's operation page (INEbase cid=1254736176918), which lists the EPA's periodicity as trimestral.

reports.title: Kuluttajahintaindeksi / Yhdenmukaistettu kuluttajahintaindeksi — Consumer Price Index / Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices
reports.description: Finland's CPI and HICP are one statistical process: the standalone HICP release ('ykhi') was discontinued 31/12/2007 and the harmonised figures are now produced inside the CPI release. Statistics Finland's CPI documentation states "the Consumer Price Index utilizes the consumption expenditures which are produced by the National Account," and the 2025 weight-structure release states "The weight structure of the Consumer Price Index 2025 is based on national accounts calculations on private consumption expenditure according to EU guidelines."
reports.cadence_note: "Consumer Price Index is published monthly. Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices is published two times a month: flash estimate and final" (stat.fi documentation of statistics, khi).

reports.title: Kotitalouksien kulutus / kulutustutkimus — Households' Consumption / Household Budget Survey
reports.description: Statistics Finland states that "The statistics on households' consumption, or the Household Budget Survey" are produced at long intervals, and — unusually explicit for this class of source — names both of its downstream consumers: "The data of the statistics on households' consumption are submitted to the Consumer Price Index, the international price comparison and national accounts," and "In national accounts, the Household Budget Survey is used for level revision of private consumption expenditure."
reports.cadence_note: "The statistics on households' consumption are produced at intervals of five years, on average" (stat.fi documentation of statistics, ktutk).

reports.title: Työvoimatutkimus — Labour Force Survey
reports.description: Statistics Finland states "Monthly data are released approximately three weeks from the end of the survey month. Quarterly data are released simultaneously with the last monthly data of each quarter," and, directly, "Statistics Finland uses the quarterly Labour Force Survey data in the compiling of national accounts."
reports.cadence_note: "Monthly data are released approximately three weeks from the end of the survey month" (stat.fi documentation of statistics, tyti); quarterly and annual releases come from the same survey.

reports.title: Fogyasztóiár-index és harmonizált fogyasztóiár-index — Consumer Price Index and Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices
reports.publisher: Központi Statisztikai Hivatal (KSH) / Hungarian Central Statistical Office
reports.description: KSH's own CPI methodology page states the weight system is built on national accounts data: "a fogyasztóiár-index súlyrendszere csoportszinten – a nemzetközi előírásoknak megfelelően – a tárgyévet két évvel megelőző év nemzeti számlájának a lakosság vásárolt fogyasztásra vonatkozó előzetes adataira épül" (the CPI weight system is based, at group level, on preliminary national-accounts data on households' purchased consumption from two years before the reference year), and that price collection is monthly ("A reprezentánsok árainak gyűjtése havonta történik"). Eurostat's Hungary metadata adds the sub-4-digit layer: "Household Budget and Living Conditions Survey (HBLS), Tourism statistics and Car Registry data are also used."
reports.cadence_note: Monthly; Eurostat's Hungary HICP metadata states the index is "published each month according to a pre-announced schedule, usually between 15 and 18 days after the end of the reference month," and KSH confirms monthly price collection.

reports.title: Háztartási költségvetési és életkörülmény adatfelvétel (HKÉF) — Household Budget and Living Conditions Survey
reports.publisher: Központi Statisztikai Hivatal (KSH) / Hungarian Central Statistical Office
reports.description: Eurostat's Hungary HICP national reference metadata names this survey as an input to the detailed weighting, below the 4-digit ECOICOP level supplied by the national accounts: "Household Budget and Living Conditions Survey (HBLS), Tourism statistics and Car Registry data are also used."
reports.cadence_note: RECURRING, cadence unconfirmed — not a one-off instrument. No KSH or Eurostat page found this round states an explicit publication frequency for the HKÉF; the KSH methodology page located for household income/consumption did not carry it. releases_per_year omitted rather than guessed. This node's evidence is Eurostat metadata rather than a first-party KSH page — worth upgrading in a later round.
title_aliases: Household Budget and Living Conditions Survey

reports.title: Munkaerő-felmérés — Labour Force Survey
reports.publisher: Központi Statisztikai Hivatal (KSH) / Hungarian Central Statistical Office
reports.description: KSH's own survey page describes the quarterly household sample: "Negyedévente körülbelül 36 ezer háztartást kérünk fel" (approximately 36,000 households are surveyed each quarter), producing internationally comparable employment and unemployment data.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly is the designated first release: Eurostat's Hungary LFS metadata gives "First release, quarterly (4x), yearly (1x), ad hoc module results (1x)". Monthly figures also exist ("Monthly results of the Hungarian LFS are published 3-4 weeks after the end of the reference month") but 4 was used rather than guessing which counts as the release.

reports.title: Index spotrebiteľských cien — Consumer Price Index and Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices
reports.publisher: Štatistický úrad Slovenskej republiky (ŠÚ SR) / Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic
reports.description: ŠÚ SR's national price metadata page gives the official title "Index spotrebiteľských cien" and notes the CPI and HICP baskets "differ partially" (imputed rent and similar). Eurostat's Slovak national reference metadata sets out the two-tier weighting: "The weights at the 4-digit COICOP level are based on annual National Accounts (NA) data Household final consumption aggregates for the year t-2 (2023)," while below that "The various sources are used for different product groups at the level of the ECOICOP 5-digit level or below - e.g., NA, Household budget survey 2021, scanner data for Food and non-alcoholic beverages, Alcoholic beverages and tobacco, information from suppliers..."
reports.cadence_note: Monthly; ŠÚ SR's metadata page (id=5068) states monthly publication and Eurostat's Slovak HICP metadata states "HICP is a monthly statistics".

reports.title: Zisťovanie rodinných účtov — Household Budget Survey
reports.publisher: Štatistický úrad Slovenskej republiky (ŠÚ SR) / Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic
reports.description: The ŠÚ SR survey page states the survey obtains information on "the amount, structure and development of monetary expenditures and income" of households, is "carried out regularly on a monthly basis," with results "processed and published annually."
reports.cadence_note: Collection monthly, publication annual: "Results are then processed and published annually" (zber.statistics.sk).

reports.title: Výberové zisťovanie pracovných síl (VZPS) — Labour Force Survey
reports.publisher: Štatistický úrad Slovenskej republiky (ŠÚ SR) / Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic
reports.description: The ŠÚ SR survey page states the LFS aims to "provide regular detailed information on the situation, structure and development on the labour market in the SR"; Eurostat's Slovak LFS metadata describes it as designed "to produce quarterly labour force estimates" by the "Statistical Office of the SR (SOSR)."
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly: Eurostat's Slovak LFS metadata gives "First release, quarterly (4x), yearly (1x), ad hoc module results (1x)"; ŠÚ SR states the survey "is conducted continuously throughout the year" with "processing and publication ... carried out quarterly."

reports.title: Indeksi cen življenjskih potrebščin (ICŽP / HICŽP) — Consumer Price Indices, national CPI and HICP
reports.publisher: Statistični urad Republike Slovenije (SURS) / Statistical Office of the Republic of Slovenia
reports.description: SURS's methodological note is unusually clean about the split: "Za pripravo uteži za izračun HICŽP uporabljamo kot glavni vir podatke o izdatkih gospodinjstev za končno potrošnjo iz nacionalnih računov" (for HICP weights, national accounts household final consumption expenditure is the main source), while "Za pripravo uteži za izračun ICŽP uporabljamo kot glavni vir podatke iz ankete o potrošnji sredstev gospodinjstev (APG)" (for the national CPI, the Household Budget Survey is the main source). Eurostat's Slovenia metadata corroborates: "for lower levels mostly data from the household budget surveys (HBS) are used (HBS data relating to 2022 are used for 2025 weights)."
reports.cadence_note: Monthly: SURS's methodological explanation states 'mesečno'; Eurostat's Slovenia metadata gives "HICP is a monthly statistic" published "usually between 15 and 18 days after the end of the reference month."

reports.title: Anketa o potrošnji sredstev gospodinjstev (APG) — Household Budget Survey
reports.publisher: Statistični urad Republike Slovenije (SURS) / Statistical Office of the Republic of Slovenia
reports.description: Named in SURS's own CPI methodological note as the primary source of national CPI weights: "Za pripravo uteži za izračun ICŽP uporabljamo kot glavni vir podatke iz ankete o potrošnji sredstev gospodinjstev (APG)."
reports.cadence_note: RECURRING, cadence unconfirmed — not a one-off instrument. Two SURS pages for the survey itself (DocSysFile 9768 and 4102) were robots.txt-blocked, so no first-party statement of its own release cadence was read; the evidence here is its named role inside the CPI methodology note. releases_per_year omitted rather than guessed.

reports.title: Aktivno in neaktivno prebivalstvo (ANP) — Labour Force Survey, Active and Inactive Population
reports.publisher: Statistični urad Republike Slovenije (SURS) / Statistical Office of the Republic of Slovenia
reports.description: SURS's methodological explanation identifies this as the survey run under the EU labour-force-survey regulation, "Uredba Sveta (ES) št. 577/98 z dne 9. marca 1998 o organizaciji vzorčne raziskave delovne sile v Skupnosti," and states "Podatki so mednarodno primerljivi in prispevajo k evropski statistiki." NOTE: Slovenia is one of the two countries in this round documented as NOT using the LFS for national accounts — see _dropped.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly on the SI-STAT portal: "Četrtletno: - Podatkovni portal SI-STAT... Objavljajo se absolutni podatki in deleži"; each household is surveyed for three consecutive quarters.

reports.title: Indeksi potrošačkih cijena — Consumer Price Index
reports.publisher: Državni zavod za statistiku (DZS) / Croatian Bureau of Statistics
reports.description: Croatia's national CPI. DZS's own methodology page states the primary weight source: "Osnovni izvor podataka za izradu pondera... jest Anketa o potrošnji kućanstava (APK)" (the primary data source for weight construction is the Household Budget Survey), and that most prices are collected monthly: "Većina cijena koje se prikupljaju na tradicionalan način snima se jedanput na mjesec." TRANSCRIPTION NOTE: the fetch of this page returned mojibake for Croatian diacritics; the quotes are reproduced with standard diacritics restored from unambiguous context, with no change of wording.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly first release; DZS's methodology page states most prices are collected "jedanput na mjesec".

reports.title: Harmonizirani indeks potrošačkih cijena — Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices
reports.publisher: Državni zavod za statistiku (DZS) / Croatian Bureau of Statistics
reports.description: Croatia is a clean example of the two indices drawing on different sources, stated on one page. Eurostat's Croatia national reference metadata: "The main data source for the HICP weights is the National Accounts data, while the main data source for the CPI weights is the Household Budget Survey." DZS's own methodology page says the same in Croatian: "Osnovni izvor podataka za izradu pondera... jesu podaci nacionalnih računa." The same Eurostat page notes "The HICP is published together with the CPI in the form of the first release, which is available on the CBS website."
reports.cadence_note: Monthly, published jointly with the national CPI first release; "Data are transmitted to Eurostat according to the Eurostat transmission timetable."

reports.title: Anketa o potrošnji kućanstava (APK) — Household Budget Survey
reports.publisher: Državni zavod za statistiku (DZS) / Croatian Bureau of Statistics
reports.description: DZS's survey page states "Podaci se primjenjuju za praćenje mjera vezanih za gospodarsku i socijalnu politiku" (data are applied to monitor economic and social policy measures); the 2026 round "provodi se tijekom cijele 2026." (is conducted throughout 2026) on a sample of 12,792 randomly selected households.
reports.cadence_note: RECURRING, publication cadence unconfirmed — not a one-off instrument. The fetched page confirms the survey runs continuously through the year but no page confirming the cadence of its results report was fetched (an apparently-annual title, "Osnovne karakteristike potrošnje kućanstava", appeared only in unfetched search snippets). releases_per_year omitted rather than guessed.

reports.title: Anketa o radnoj snazi (ARS) — Labour Force Survey
reports.publisher: Državni zavod za statistiku (DZS) / Croatian Bureau of Statistics
reports.description: DZS's survey page states "podaci se prikupljaju svakog tjedna, a objavljuju svaka tri mjeseca" (data are collected weekly and published every three months), and "Rezultati ovog istraživanja vrlo su važni za potrebe odlučivanja o gospodarskim i socijalnim pitanjima."
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly; DZS states data are collected weekly and published every three months ("objavljuju svaka tri mjeseca").

reports.title: Инфлация и индекси на потребителските цени — Inflation and Consumer Price Indices (national CPI, HICP and Small Basket Index)
reports.description: NSI bundles the national CPI, the HICP and the Small Basket Index into one monthly release. Of the national CPI's weights it states "Основен източник на информацията за разходите е изследването на бюджетите на домакинствата в страната" (the main source of information on expenditure is the household budget survey conducted in the country), and of the Small Basket Index "Източник на информацията за теглата е изследването на бюджетите на домакинствата." Eurostat's Bulgaria metadata gives the HICP side: "weights used in the current year t are based on national accounts data referring to t-2, estimated in line with the domestic concept, that are further adjusted using additional sources in order to make them representative for t-1."
reports.cadence_note: Monthly; Eurostat's Bulgaria HICP metadata states "HICP is a monthly statistics" and NSI publishes a dated monthly press release.

reports.title: Наблюдение на домакинските бюджети — Household Budget Survey
reports.description: NSI describes the survey as a "регулярно извадково статистическо изследване, провеждано от Националния статистически институт" (a regular sample statistical survey conducted by the National Statistical Institute), collecting household expenditure and living-standards data; for 2026 "извадката включва 5 580 домакинства", divided into sub-samples each observed one month per quarter.
reports.cadence_note: RECURRING, publication cadence unconfirmed — not a one-off instrument. NSI's page describes a continuous rotating sample but states no publication frequency for results. releases_per_year omitted rather than guessed.

reports.title: Наблюдение на работната сила — Labour Force Survey
reports.description: NSI states "Наблюдението на работната сила е регулярно извадково статистическо изследване" whose "Основната цел на наблюдението е да се получи актуална информация за икономическата активност на населението", with "Всяко тримесечие в изследването участват около 19.6 хил. домакинства".
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly; NSI states roughly 19,600 households participate each quarter and Eurostat's Bulgaria LFS metadata lists frequency as "Quarterly (4x), yearly (1x), ad hoc module results (1x)".

reports.title: Tarbijahinnaindeks / harmoneeritud tarbijahinnaindeks — Consumer Price Index / Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices
reports.description: Estonia's national and harmonised consumer price indices share a weight basis and are modelled here as one node. Eurostat's Estonia national reference metadata identifies the release as "IA023: HARMONIZED INDEX OF CONSUMER PRICES, 2005 = 100 (MONTHS)" and states its weights are "derived mainly from the National Accounts and Household Budget Survey data". URL REPAIRED 2026-09-15 (ECOICOP target audit): the node's own `url` was Eurostat's Estonian HICP metadata page — a real document about the right series, published by the wrong body. Statistics Estonia's own page is named inside that document at §10.3, and its opening sentence covers exactly this node's scope: "The Consumer Price Index (CPI), the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) and the Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices with Constant Taxes (HICP-CT)". The `andmed.stat.ee` database table the same section names answered HTTP 500 and was not used; the cited url is the one `www.stat.ee/en/find-statistics/methodology-and-quality/esms-metadata/20407` redirects to, because that is what a plain GET reads.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly; Eurostat's Estonia HICP metadata (prc_hicp_esmshi3_ee) gives the IA023 series' dissemination frequency as "Monthly".

reports.title: Leibkonna eelarve uuring — Household Budget Survey
reports.description: Statistics Estonia's own Household Budget Survey page names three downstream uses at once: "The data are also used in the calculation of the consumer price index, the GDP and the subsistence minimum."
reports.cadence_note: "The Household Budget Survey has been carried out in the years 1996–2007, 2010–2012, 2015–2016 and 2019–2020. From 2026 onwards, the survey will be conducted every five years" (stat.ee/en/household-budget-survey). A separate stat.ee metadata page (40203) said 'every three years'; the more specific and more recent statement was used.

reports.title: Tööjõu-uuring — Estonian Labour Force Survey
reports.description: Statistics Estonia states "Since 2000, data are collected throughout the year and results are presented on a quarterly and annual basis." Estonia is the strongest case in this round for the national-accounts dependency: Eurostat's Estonia LFS metadata states flatly "Country uses LFS as the only source for employment in national accounts."
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly; Eurostat's Estonia LFS metadata gives "First release, quarterly (4x), yearly (1x), ad hoc module results (1x)" and Statistics Estonia confirms results are "presented on a quarterly and annual basis."

reports.title: Vartotojų kainų indeksas (VKI) — Consumer Price Index
reports.publisher: Valstybės duomenų agentūra / State Data Agency (formerly Statistics Lithuania)
reports.description: Lithuania's national CPI. The State Data Agency's prices page states it "calculates and publishes the consumer price index monthly" and that, for the 986-item statistical basket, "household budget survey data on monetary consumption expenditures serves as the primary information source for weight preparation." Split from the harmonised index here because the documented weight sources differ.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly; osp.stat.gov.lt/kainos states the State Data Agency "calculates and publishes the consumer price index monthly".

reports.title: Suderintas vartotojų kainų indeksas (SVKI) — Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices
reports.publisher: Valstybės duomenų agentūra / State Data Agency (Eurostat metadata credits Statistics Lithuania, SL)
reports.description: Eurostat's Lithuania national reference metadata states "HICP is a monthly statistics," that "SL is the only institution in the country engaged in the production of the HICP," and that "At ECOICOP ver.2 5-digit level, weights used in the current year are based on annual HFMCE data of the previous year, estimated in line with the domestic concept" — i.e. the harmonised index is weighted from national-accounts household final monetary consumption expenditure, where the national VKI is weighted from the household budget survey.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly, per Eurostat's Lithuania HICP metadata: "HICP is a monthly statistics."

reports.title: Namų ūkių biudžetų tyrimas — Household Budget Survey
reports.publisher: Valstybės duomenų agentūra / State Data Agency
reports.description: Named on the State Data Agency's income, consumption and living-conditions page as the "Namų ūkių biudžetų tyrimas", governed by the methodology document "Namų ūkių biudžetų statistinio tyrimo metodika" (2025, Nr. DĮ-278), and administered by the Valstybės duomenų agentūra. Its role as the primary weight source for the national VKI is documented on the agency's prices page.
reports.cadence_note: RECURRING, publication cadence unconfirmed — not a one-off instrument. No fetched page carried an explicit release-frequency statement; an infographic page for the survey loaded but returned only a title with no body text (JS-rendered). releases_per_year omitted rather than guessed.

reports.title: Gyventojų užimtumo tyrimas — Labour Force Survey
reports.publisher: Valstybės duomenų agentūra / State Data Agency
reports.description: The State Data Agency's Labour Force Survey data page publishes results on several schedules, including "Quarterly: Labour force, employment, and unemployment indicators broken down by age groups and gender."
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly is the core cadence per osp.stat.gov.lt/gyventoju-uzimtumo-tyrimo-duomenys; Eurostat's Lithuania LFS metadata corroborates with "First release, quarterly (4x), yearly (1x), ad hoc module results (1x)."

reports.title: Patēriņa cenu indekss (PCI) un saskaņotais patēriņa cenu indekss (SPCI) — Consumer Price Index and Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices
reports.publisher: Centrālā statistikas pārvalde (CSP) / Central Statistical Bureau of Latvia
reports.description: Latvia's national and harmonised indices, modelled as one node because no fetched page distinguished separate release schedules for them. Eurostat's Latvia national reference metadata gives the weighting: "At ECOICOP 5-digit level, weights used in the current year are based on annual HFMCE data of the previous year, estimated in line with the domestic concept," that "HFMCE is obtained from provisional NA data for the first three quarters of the previous year," and that "For elementary product groups the HBS data and additional sources are used."
reports.cadence_note: Monthly; Eurostat's Latvia HICP metadata states "HICP is a monthly statistics" released 15-18 days after the reference month. CSP's own Latvian topic page lists periodicity more loosely as "Periodiskums: Ceturkšņu/mēnešu dati" (quarterly/monthly data).

reports.title: Mājsaimniecību budžeta pētījums — Household Budget Survey
reports.publisher: Centrālā statistikas pārvalde (CSP) / Central Statistical Bureau of Latvia
reports.description: CSP's official statistics portal states: "Dati par mājsaimniecību patēriņa izdevumiem tiek iegūti Mājsaimniecību budžetu apsekojumā" (data on household consumption expenditure are obtained from the Household Budget Survey).
reports.cadence_note: Annual, per CSP's page: "Periodiskums: Gada dati" (Frequency: Annual data).

reports.title: Darbaspēka apsekojums — Labour Force Survey
reports.publisher: Centrālā statistikas pārvalde (CSP) / Central Statistical Bureau of Latvia
reports.description: CSP's publication overview states "Informatīvajā apskatā apkopota informācija par Latvijas nepārtrauktā darbaspēka izlases apsekojuma rezultātiem 2024. gadā" (this overview compiles information from the results of Latvia's continuous labour force sample survey for 2024), published by the Centrālā statistikas pārvalde.
reports.cadence_note: RECURRING, cadence disputed between two documented sources — not a one-off instrument. CSP's annual 'galvenie rādītāji' overview publication states 'Reizi gadā' (once a year), while Eurostat's Latvia LFS metadata states "First release, quarterly (4x), yearly (1x), ad hoc module results (1x)". The two disagree on what counts as 'the' release, so releases_per_year was omitted rather than picked.

reports.title: Retail Price Index (RPI) and Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP)
reports.description: NSO Malta states: "The basket of consumption items considered for the RPI is reviewed periodically, in line with the Household Budgetary Survey (HBS), during which information of household consumption is collected over a 12-month period in order to obtain an estimate of the average household expenditure." Eurostat's Malta national reference metadata gives the harmonised side: "HFMCE values to derive weights up to the ECOICOP 4-digit level are obtained from quarterly National Accounts (NA) for the first three quarters of year t-1."
reports.cadence_note: Monthly, each month's data published the following month (NSO Malta RPI page); Eurostat's Malta metadata states flash HICP estimates are transmitted "at end of reference month" with full data "between 15 and 18 days after the end of the reference month."

reports.title: Household Budgetary Survey
reports.description: NSO Malta describes the survey as illustrating "patterns in household expenditure and how these are distributed among different goods and services."
reports.cadence_note: Approximately every five years, per NSO Malta's HBS page; the round used for current weights was 2015/16 per Eurostat's Malta HICP metadata.

reports.title: Labour Force Survey (LFS)
reports.description: Eurostat's Malta LFS national reference metadata is unusually specific about the division of labour with administrative data: "Total employment in persons is based on administrative sources in case of full-time employment and on LFS in case of part-time employment" and "LFS is the only source used by National Accounts when compiling hours worked. Data on hours worked have been used since 2002."
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly; Eurostat's Malta LFS metadata gives "First release, quarterly (4x), yearly (1x), ad hoc module results (1x)."

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP)
reports.description: CyStat's CPI general information document states: "The compilation of the CPI is based on goods and services included in the shopping basket, which are derived primarily from the Household Budget Survey. This survey is conducted by the Statistical Service of Cyprus every 5 years and it records the daily expenses of households." That document does not name national accounts; the national-accounts weight source comes instead from Eurostat's Cyprus HICP metadata: "The usual sources of the expenditure data used for the calculation of the weights of HICP items are mainly the NA and HBS data."
reports.cadence_note: Monthly: "The main CPI index and relevant price indices for the 12 main categories of goods and services are disseminated on the first Thursday of each month" (CyStat CPI general information document).

reports.title: Household Budget Survey
reports.publisher: Statistical Service of Cyprus (CyStat), Republic of Cyprus
reports.description: The 2023 publication — the twelfth in the series since 1966 — states the survey is "conducted by the Statistical Service on a regular basis, usually every 5 years," and lists among its objectives "Updating private consumption data for national accounts."
reports.cadence_note: Every five years: "conducted by the Statistical Service on a regular basis, usually every 5 years" (CyStat HBS 2023).

reports.title: Labour Force Survey (LFS)
reports.description: Eurostat's Cyprus LFS national reference metadata explains why Cyprus's national accounts do NOT draw on this survey: "LFS data is collected from private households only...while National Accounts data take into consideration employment from all different sources." That is a documented negative, recorded in _dropped rather than a missing edge.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly; Eurostat's Cyprus LFS metadata gives "Quarterly (4x), Yearly (1x), Ad hoc module (1x)."

reports.title: Vísitala neysluverðs — Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Statistics Iceland states: "Hagstofa Íslands reiknar vísitölu neysluverðs, vísitölu framleiðsluverðs og skyldar verðvísitölur mánaðarlega" (Statistics Iceland calculates the consumer price index, production price index and related price indices monthly), and — the fact that makes this index unusually load-bearing — "Vísitölu neysluverðs er fyrst og fremst mælikvarði á verðbólgu en hún er einnig notuð til verðtryggingar" (the CPI is primarily a measure of inflation but is also used for price-indexation), the mechanism behind Iceland's indexed loans.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly, per the fetched Hagstofa Íslands price-statistics page: "...mánaðarlega".

reports.title: Samræmd vísitala neysluverðs — Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices, Iceland
reports.description: Iceland is in the European Statistical System via the EEA rather than EU membership, and transmits an HICP like a member state. Eurostat's Iceland national reference metadata states "HICP is a monthly statistics" and gives the two-tier weighting: "The sources of the weights are the National Accounts for household consumption at the 4-digit ECOICOP level. The weights for the 5-level are subdivided by using the household expenditure survey." URL REPAIRED 2026-09-15 (ECOICOP target audit): the node's own `url` was Eurostat's Icelandic HICP metadata page. Statistics Iceland's own HICP page is named inside that document at §10.3 ("HICP - Statistics Iceland") and §10.2 confirms the series is maintained there — "A special press release of HICP is not published in Iceland but data are updated on the website, statice.is". Verified 200 with the page title 'HICP - Statistics Iceland'. No press release is not no publication; that distinction is what separated Iceland from the Türkiye refusal.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly: "HICP is a monthly statistics", disseminated "usually between 15 and 18 days after the end of the reference month" (Eurostat prc_hicp_esmshi3_is).

reports.title: Rannsókn á útgjöldum heimilanna — Household Budget Survey
reports.description: Statistics Iceland states: "Megintilgangur rannsóknarinnar er að afla gagna í grunn fyrir vísitölu neysluverðs" (the main purpose of the survey is to gather data as a basis for the consumer price index), adding "Einnig er hún notuð til að reikna út kaupmátt, verðtryggðan sparnað og fjárskuldbindingar" (it is also used to calculate purchasing power, index-linked savings and financial obligations), on a sample of "1.222 heimili".
reports.cadence_note: RECURRING, publication cadence unconfirmed — not a one-off instrument. Fieldwork is continuous ("Rannsókn á útgjöldum heimilanna er framkvæmd allt árið um kring") but the page states no release frequency for results. releases_per_year omitted rather than guessed.

reports.title: Vinnumarkaðsrannsóknin — Labour Force Survey
reports.description: Statistics Iceland's labour-market page states "Rannsóknin gefur áreiðanlegar upplýsingar um stöðu fólks á vinnumarkaði, svo sem atvinnuþátttöku, fjölda starfandi, atvinnuleysi og vinnutíma" (the survey provides reliable information about people's position in the labour market, such as labour-force participation, number employed, unemployment and working hours). Iceland is the one country in this round with NO Eurostat LFS metadata page at all (employ_simslfs_is.htm 404s), which is why its national-accounts link is deferred rather than settled.
reports.cadence_note: RECURRING, cadence unconfirmed — not a one-off instrument. The fetched overview page is navigation/summary content and states no publication frequency; two deeper Hagstofa URLs returned nav/error pages. releases_per_year omitted rather than guessed (quarterly is the commonly known cadence but nothing fetched said so).

dependencies.basis: RE-CITED 2026-09-05 (ESMS pass) to Eurostat's national reference metadata for the PL HICP, section 18.1.1 weights; previously cited https://stat.gov.pl/dla-mediow/komunikaty-prasowe/wskaznik-cen-towarow-i-uslug-konsumpcyjnych-pot-inflacja,100,1.html. GUS's own CPI press-release page states the index weights come from the household survey: "Wagi pochodzą z Badania Budżetów Gospodarstw Domowych (BBGD) – cyklicznego badania ankietowego mierzącego wydatki i dochody ok. 37 tys. gospodarstw domowych." Eurostat's Poland national reference metadata confirms the split from the other side: "the system of weight for CPI is based on data from Household Budget Survey."

dependencies.basis: Eurostat's Poland HICP national reference metadata states: "The main source of HICP weights are National Accounts while the system of weight for CPI is based on data from Household Budget Survey," adding that "Where necessary data obtained from NA is disaggregated into lower level based on HBS data." Re-fetched and confirmed verbatim by the orchestrating session before minting.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Where necessary data obtained from NA is disaggregated into lower level based on HBS data.

dependencies.basis: Eurostat's Poland HICP metadata documents GUS's compilation responsibilities as including "transmitting data to Eurostat via Programming, Coordination of Statistical Surveys and Registers Department (several datasets within the HICP and REALEST domains: weights, indices and information (HICP-AP and metadata))," i.e. the Polish national HICP is an input to the Eurostat aggregate. Re-fetched and confirmed verbatim by the orchestrating session.

INS's own IPC methodological notes state: "Ponderile utilizate pentru calculul IPC sunt obţinute din Ancheta Bugetelor de Familie (ABF)" (the weights used to calculate the Consumer Price Index are obtained from the Household Budget Survey).
dependencies.evidence_quote: Ponderile utilizate pentru calculul IPC sunt obţinute din Ancheta Bugetelor de Familie (ABF)

dependencies.basis: Eurostat's Romania LFS national reference metadata states "Country uses LFS as the only source for employment in national accounts" and "In NA: LFS is the main data source" — Romania's national-accounts employment estimates are built from the AMIGO Labour Force Survey.

SCB's official 'Statistikens framställning' document for KPI 2024 states "Underlag för vägningstalen är i första hand Nationalräkenskaperna" (the basis for the weights is primarily the National Accounts).

SCB's KPI production-of-statistics document states "KPI är också utgångspunkt för beräkningen av det EU-harmoniserade måttet Harmoniserat Index för Konsumentpriser (HIKP)" (KPI is also the starting point for calculating the EU-harmonised measure HIKP); SCB's HIKP page separately states "It is the same price material that forms the basis for HIKP in Sweden as for CPI and other price indices SCB calculates."
SCB's 'more about the Labour Force Survey' page states "LFS is also used in the work of Statistics Sweden, partly for national accounts work, partly for labour force analyses and prognoses."

SCB's HIKP page states "HIKP for all EU countries plus Iceland, Norway, Switzerland and the United Kingdom is also published monthly by Eurostat after the individual countries have submitted their respective indices" — a first-party statement that Sweden's HIKP is transmitted to and aggregated by Eurostat.

RE-CITED 2026-09-05 (ESMS pass) to Eurostat's national reference metadata for the BE HICP, section 18.1.1 weights; previously cited https://statbel.fgov.be/en/themes/consumer-prices/consumer-price-index. Statbel's CPI methodology page states "Weights are determined based on the household budget survey," and the HBS page states reciprocally "The survey is also the main source to compile the consumer price index" and "The choice of representative items and their weights in the basket are deeply reviewed every two years based on the most recent HBS."
dependencies.evidence_quote: Regional weighting information is obtained from the household budget survey.

dependencies.basis: Statbel's Household Budget Survey page states the HBS serves "as input for updating the index basket and for estimating household consumption expenditure in the national accounts."

The National Bank of Belgium's labour-market statistics methodology page states "The Labour Force Survey (LFS) is used only to estimate hours worked by the self-employed," listing the "labour force survey (LFS) (used to estimate hours worked by the self-employed)" among its data sources — a narrow but explicit dependency; overall employment figures rely mainly on NSSO/NISSE administrative records.

Statbel's health index page states the consumer price index "forms the basis of another index: the health index," calculated by removing "alcoholic beverages (bought in a shop or consumed in a bar), tobacco products and motor fuels except for LPG" from the CPI basket.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The consumer price index, which takes into account price trends of all goods and services, forms the basis of another index: the health index.

dependencies.basis: Eurostat's HICP metadata states "National HICPs are produced by National Statistical Institutes (NSIs), while European aggregates (EU, EA and EEA) are produced by Eurostat," that "HICP data, both indices and weights, are provided by the NSIs," and that "The country-group indices for the euro area, EU and EEA... are calculated by Eurostat using the HICP data provided by the countries." EVIDENCE CAVEAT: this is the general all-NSI statement, not a Belgium-specific transmission sentence — no Belgium-specific one was found this round, so this edge rests on weaker evidence than the country-specific ones elsewhere in this slice.

The joint VPI/HVPI standard documentation states: "Die Gewichtung des Warenkorbes basiert auf den Ergebnissen der jeweils rezent vorliegenden Konsumerhebung sowie auf aktuellen Daten über den privaten Konsum aus den Volkswirtschaftlichen Gesamtrechnungen." Re-fetched and confirmed verbatim by the orchestrating session before minting.

The same standard documentation states the weighting draws on "aktuellen Daten über den privaten Konsum aus den Volkswirtschaftlichen Gesamtrechnungen," and specifies "So werden für die Abteilungen, Gruppen und Klassen die Werte des privaten Konsums der VGR ... verwendet." Re-fetched and confirmed verbatim by the orchestrating session.

RE-CITED 2026-09-05 (ESMS pass) to Eurostat's national reference metadata for the AT HICP, section 18.1.1 weights; previously cited https://www.statistik.at/fileadmin/shared/QM/Standarddokumentationen/VW/std_v_vpi_hvpi.pdf. The standard documentation covers both indices and states the basket weighting "basiert auf den Ergebnissen der jeweils rezent vorliegenden Konsumerhebung sowie auf aktuellen Daten über den privaten Konsum aus den Volkswirtschaftlichen Gesamtrechnungen," while confirming VPI and HVPI "verwenden dieselben Preisdaten werden aber mit unterschiedlichen Gewichten berechnet" — both indices weight from the same Konsumerhebung/VGR sources.

As above: the standard documentation covering both indices states weighting uses "aktuellen Daten über den privaten Konsum aus den Volkswirtschaftlichen Gesamtrechnungen" and that "für die Abteilungen, Gruppen und Klassen die Werte des privaten Konsums der VGR ... verwendet" werden.

Eurostat's HICP methodology metadata states "HICP data, both indices and weights, are provided by the NSIs" and "The country-group indices for the euro area, EU and EEA, as well as special aggregates are calculated by Eurostat using the HICP data provided by the countries"; Statistik Austria describes its HVPI as "die europäische Vergleichsgröße" used "u. a. der Bewertung der Geldwertstabilität innerhalb der Euro-Zone," and publishes it "am selben Tag mit Eurostat." EVIDENCE CAVEAT: the transmission sentence is the general all-NSI one, not Austria-specific.

The pattern edge minted for 17 other countries in this round is correctly absent for Cyprus.

Destatis's own quality-report extract states what it is for: 'The consumer prices recorded are used to calculate the HICP which is in turn used for the calculation of an inflation standard to measure price stability in the economy of the euro area ... The HICP is one of the convergence criteria on which the decision on including a given Member State in the euro area is based.' dependencies.basis: SELF-DECLARED: ESA 2010's own Annex A, Chapter 2, on the classification of local KAUs into industries — the document is Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, published by ESA 2010's own publisher, the European Parliament and the Council. This CLOSES a lead open since the esa2010-methodology-stack round, which recorded the edge `no-node-yet` because no NACE node existed; `nace-rev2` was minted in the Poland round on 2026-09-11 and the note is rewritten `resolved` in that file. The quote chosen is Annex A 2.147's flat statement rather than Annex A 1.22 ('The ESA 2010 contains EU-specific classifications, e.g. ... NACE Rev. 2 for industries'), which the live `esa-2010 -> cpa` edge already cites and which qualifies its own claim with a parenthetical about harmonisation. Relationship type is `methodology_depends_on` rather than the `legal_basis` the sibling `esa-2010 -> cpa` edge carries: NACE is the classification ESA's industry accounts are built on, not the act ESA rests on. ROUTE: EUR-Lex answers this container with an AWS WAF challenge (HTTP 202, zero bytes) on every legal-content URL tried, so the act was read from CELLAR, the Publications Office's own repository. The cited URL is the one an `Accept: application/xhtml+xml` + `Accept-Language: eng` negotiation on `publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/<CELEX>` RESOLVES to — a `resource/cellar/<uuid>/DOC_1` document a plain GET reads with no header at all, which is what a later grader run will issue. First-party publisher, direct read, no archive in the chain; `playbook/corpus-route.md`'s B cap is for archived snapshots and does not apply. QUOTE SHAPE, AND WHY IT IS TWO FRAGMENTS: the second fragment alone graded B `artefact-named-elsewhere-in-document` at coverage 1.0. `nace-rev2`'s title-lead is 'NACE Rev. 2', which `tokenise` reduces to three tokens, and the run rule needs about seven contiguous words of the full title — so a window carrying only the short name cannot name the target however clearly a reader sees it. The first fragment is Annex A 1.19's statement that the ESA employs the classification, and it carries the statutory name in full. WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ANYONE RE-READS THIS: ESA 2010 writes that name as 'Statistical classification of economic activities in the European UNION', while the node carries 'European COMMUNITY', which is Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006's own wording and the right title for the node. The run rule clears the 60% bar on the eight words the two spellings share, so the mismatch costs nothing here — but a future edge resting on a shorter span of that name may land on the wrong side of it. Both fragments are from the same act and neither is doing work the other could not check: the first names the artefact, the second states what ESA uses it for. Graded A, `quote-found-artefact-named`, on a live re-fetch 2026-09-15.

All four were fetched and read in full this round. THREE OF THE FOUR ACTS ARE ALREADY IN THE CORPUS AS THE CLASSIFICATION NODE ITSELF, and minting them again would manufacture the exact duplicate-node defect `notes/bps-url-repair-probe-2026-09-15.md` recorded on the other side of the corpus. The evidence is each node's own `url` field: `esa-2010` carries `eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2013/549` and its description opens 'enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013' and quotes that act's Article 1(2); `cpa` carries `eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2008/451`, is `kind: instrument`, is published by 'European Parliament and Council of the European Union' and quotes Article 1(1) in its description; `nace-rev2` carries `CELEX:32006R1893` and its description opens 'established by Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006'. A separate `eu-reg-549-2013` node would be a second node for one document, pointed at the same URL, competing for the 117 in-edges `esa-2010` already holds. THE ECOICOP PRECEDENT DOES NOT TRANSFER, and the difference is worth stating because it is what makes ECOICOP the exception rather than the template: ECOICOP is one ANNEX of Regulation (EU) 2016/792, and that act does a great deal besides carrying it — it is the whole HICP framework, and 34 nodes cite it as their legal basis without citing ECOICOP. Annex A of Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 IS the ESA 2010 methodology and the act does almost nothing else. Same for 1893/2006 and NACE, and for 451/2008 and the CPA. WHAT THE FETCHES BOUGHT INSTEAD, and it was not nothing: the ESA act closed `esa-2010 -> nace-rev2`, open as a lead since the esa2010-methodology-stack round, and the EBS act gave `eu-reg-2019-2152` the first out-edge it has ever had. 223/2009 is the fourth act and is already a node, correctly — it is a framework statute that no classification is an annex to. It yielded nothing new: its only upstream candidates are the European Statistics Code of Practice, refused on the record in esa2010-quality-reporting.json for language the Code itself chose ('COMPLEMENTS the extensive legal framework'), and the UN Fundamental Principles, which recital 9 says 'should also be taken into account' — hortatory, and §7a's assertion-only shape.

_dropped.edge: a Turkish HICP node, and `tr-* -> eu-ecoicop`
_dropped.why: REFUSED, and the reason is a property of Türkiye rather than of the evidence. `HANDOFF.md` §3 item 2 said Türkiye 'is the same shape' as Germany — ESMS page read and quotable, national CPI node in the corpus, two edges waiting on a harmonised node being minted. It is not the same shape. Eurostat's Turkish HICP metadata, section 10.1, says it outright: 'However, no separate news release is published for the HICP. HICP data are transmitted directly to Eurostat, which disseminates the figures on its own platform according to the established release calendar.' TurkStat publishes no Turkish HICP — the series exists only as Eurostat output — so a node carrying the publisher's own title for the artefact (§7a) cannot be minted, because the putative publisher publishes no such artefact. That is `unpublishable-source` by its own definition. Germany is the opposite case and is why the two were worth separating: Destatis gave the German HVPI its own topic page on 10 September 2026, five days before this round. WIRING `tr-cpi` INSTEAD WAS CONSIDERED AND REFUSED for the reason the 2026-09-14 round refused it: the node is the national CPI and the page describes the HICP. The closest the page comes is section 6.1's 'HICP indices for Türkiye are calculated at the ECOICOP 5-digit level ... as Türkiye's national CPI is also compiled at the same level of detail', which states a shared level of detail and leaves the national index's own classification to be inferred. §7a does not allow that, and it does not need to be: `tr-cpi -> un-coicop-2018` is already live and answers the classification question for the national index.

_dropped.edge: CORRECTION to the 2026-09-14 round's claim about Türkiye's section 6.1
_dropped.why: `notes/eu-classification-statute-2026-09-14.md` §2 records, and `HANDOFF.md` §3 repeats, that Türkiye's ESMS page 'does NOT carry the 2016/792 sentence — that was the single failure when all 32 pages were checked, and it is a real difference in the document.' THE PAGE DOES CARRY THE REGULATION; what it does not carry is the template WORDING. Re-fetched 2026-09-15, section 6.1 reads: 'The Harmonised Indices of Consumer Prices (HICPs) are harmonised measures of inflation required under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). The legal basis for the establishment of a harmonised methodology for compiling HICPs is provided by Regulation (EU) 2016/792 of the European Parliament and of the Council.' The other 31 pages say 'Regulation (EU) 2016/792 ... (OJ L 135) sets the legal basis for establishing a harmonised methodology for the compilation of the HICP and the HICP-CT'. Türkiye's page is written fresh rather than from the template — it also adds a national paragraph on Statistical Law No. 5429 — and a check that searched for the template span would report it missing. The finding changes nothing this round, because the refusal above is about the SOURCE node and not the evidence, but a future round should not re-derive it: the correct statement is 'Türkiye's page is not template text', not 'Türkiye's page omits the regulation'. Bears on rule 16 generally — an ESMS field can be present and unrecognisable to a span search at the same time.

PROPOSED THIS ROUND AND REFUSED BY RULE 14, which is the rule working exactly as written. Romania is one of the four countries wired to ECOICOP and to the framework regulation while missing the feed edge, and Eurostat's Romanian metadata carries a clean country-specific sentence for it: 'The indices are transmitted to Eurostat and published each month, according to the pre-announced schedule, in general between 14 and 16 days after the month in question.' The edge was NOT minted because eu-national-chains-2026-08-28.json already carries a `no-node-yet` note saying why: 'Romania's IAPC (Indicele Armonizat al Preturilor de Consum) is a distinct series from the national IPC and is what Eurostat aggregates, but no IAPC node could be minted'. `ro-ins-ipc` is the national IPC. The older note has the better information and the edge would have had the wrong target. ROUTE UPDATE, because the older note's blocker has decayed and the replacement is not what it expected: it recorded 'insse.ro returned ROBOTS_DISALLOWED / robots.txt ConnectTimeout on roughly 8 of 14 attempts' and advised a retry. Re-probed 2026-09-15 from two machines. The cloud container cannot reach insse.ro at all — the egress proxy closes the tunnel mid-exchange on every attempt, curl exit 35, which is a statement about this container and not about the site. THOMAS'S CHROME REACHES IT AND RENDERS IT: `insse.ro/cms/ro/content/ipc-serii-de-date` returned its real article text on the first try. Two guessed paths for the IAPC's own page 404'd, so the node still needs someone to find the right page, but the host is no longer the obstacle and the browser is the route. WHAT THIS OPENS, and it is bigger than one edge: if Romania publishes the IAPC as a series distinct from the IPC, then `ro-ins-ipc -> eu-ecoicop` and `ro-ins-ipc -> eu-reg-2016-792`, both minted 2026-09-14 off a metadata page that describes the HARMONISED index, may sit on the wrong node — the same mismatch that made this round refuse to wire `de-destatis-cpi` and `tr-cpi`. Rule 13 says caveat and defer rather than override, so neither edge is touched here. The question is how many of the 31 national ECOICOP edges point at a national CPI node whose harmonised index is a separate published series; it is a measurement, not a round, and it is in `HANDOFF.md` §3.

The other two of the four countries wired to ECOICOP without a feed edge. Both ESMS pages were fetched and read in full on 2026-09-15 and NEITHER carries a country-specific transmission sentence. The only occurrence of 'Eurostat' in a transmission context on either page is the common all-NSI boilerplate — 'In line with the Community legal framework and the European Statistics Code of Practice Eurostat disseminates European statistics on Eurostat's website' — which is about dissemination by Eurostat, not transmission to it, and is on all 32 pages. The Czech page's one sub-index sentence is a NEGATIVE ('Sub-indices that may account for more than one part in thousand not produced and transmitted, because exact information is not available'), which the grader's A bar would read as presence and which §6 already records as a way it has gone wrong once. The 2026-08-28 Austrian edge shows the alternative — fall back to the general all-NSI sentence and caveat it — and that was not repeated here: a generic sentence supports a generic claim. Both need the NSI's own page, the way Sweden's edge was taken off SCB's HIKP page. Not blocked, just not done.

Looked for while minting the German HICP node, because the Austrian pair records the relationship on its node ('Die beiden Indizes VPI und HVPI verwenden dieselben Preisdaten werden aber mit unterschiedlichen Gewichten berechnet') and the German pair is the same arrangement. Destatis's HICP page says the two indices SHARE A PRICE COLLECTION, not that one feeds the other: 'The consumer prices recorded are used to calculate the HICP', and, on the weighting change, 'Due to the differences in the calculation formulas between CPI and HICP, the use of the 3-year average for the CPI remains in place.' A shared input is not a dependency between the two publications — the price collection is the common upstream of both, and it is not itself a published release. The honest shape would be two edges from a price-collection node that does not exist and could not be minted (`unpublishable-source`), which is why nothing is drawn. Worth knowing before someone re-proposes it from the Austrian precedent: Austria's sentence says the two indices use the same price data, which is the same fact, and the Austrian node does not carry that edge either.
