reports.title: Reporting of Government Deficits and Debt Levels (EDP Notification, Luxembourg)
reports.publisher: STATEC (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)
reports.description: Luxembourg's Article 9 Excessive Deficit Procedure (EDP) notification tables, submitted under Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 as amended by Commission Regulation (EU) No 220/2014. Read directly this session (April 2026 notification, dated 31/03/2026): the document's own header states "Reporting of Government Deficits and Debt Levels in accordance with Council Regulation (EC) N° 479/2009, as amended by Commission Regulation (EU) No 220/2014", identifies "Member State: Luxembourg" and "Notification: April 2026 notification in format April/October 20xx", and reports general-government net lending/borrowing (B.9) and consolidated gross debt in "ESA 2010" terms. Hosted on Eurostat's central EDP notification-tables document repository (the standard hosting pattern for every member state's own submitted notification), not a Eurostat commentary about Luxembourg. Replaces the previously-rejected candidate (STATEC's Note de Conjoncture N°1-2026), which reported the same underlying figures but named no framework -- this document is the actual Article 9 notification itself.
reports.cadence_note: Semi-annual EDP notification, per the document's own "Notification: April 2026 notification in format April/October 20xx" -- transmitted each April and October per Regulation 479/2009's Article 3 timetable.

reports.title: Household Budget Surveys in the EU — Methodology and Recommendations for Harmonisation (2003)
reports.description: Eurostat's handbook coordinating the voluntary EU-wide Household Budget Survey (HBS) exercise -- no EU regulation compels national HBS, so this handbook is the actual harmonisation instrument member states cite. Confirmed by Statistics Sweden's own SCBDOK 3.2 methodology documentation for HUT (2012 edition, section 0.9 "EU-reglering"), which names it explicitly: "Eurostat publicerat handboken 'HOUSEHOLD BUDGET SURVEYS IN THE EU Methodology and recommendations for harmonization 2003'" and states Sweden has reported consumption by COICOP purpose "enligt Eurostats rekommendationer" (according to Eurostat's recommendations) since 1999. Independently confirmed via Eurostat's own publication catalogue (product code KS-BF-03-003): "Household budget surveys in the EU - Methodology and recommendations for harmonisation 2003", published 2004-02-10.
reports.cadence_note: One-off methodology handbook (2003/2004), not a recurring release -- the EU-wide HBS exercise it governs is voluntary and coordinated rather than regulation-driven, and no revised edition was found.

dependencies.basis: lu-edp-inventory is the Article 9 methods inventory Regulation 479/2009 requires; lu-govfin is the actual notification tables data it describes the compilation of. Same pattern as every other EU member state's edp-inventory -> govfin edge in this corpus.
The notification's own tables are headed "Data are in millions of Euros ESA 2010", stating the figures are compiled on an ESA 2010 accounting basis.
The document's own title states it is compiled "in accordance with Council Regulation (EC) N° 479/2009, as amended by Commission Regulation (EU) No 220/2014."

Eurostat's EDP notification-tables collection centrally hosts and aggregates each member state's own Article 9 submission, including Luxembourg's -- same pattern already established for cz-govfin/nl-govfin/dk-govfin/it-govfin/etc. in this corpus.

Eurostat's ESMS metadata page for dataset nama_10_pe ("Population and employment - national accounts"), Poland's national submission, section 18.1 Source data: "The main source for EMP data that is used in Poland is the Labour Force Survey (LFS). However, in order to ensure both completeness and high quality of Polish EMP NA and RA data, the combination of various data sources are used: quarterly survey - the Labour Force Survey (LFS); results from the annual 'Report on persons employed, wages, salaries and working time' ('Z-06' form); and the secondary survey 'Persons employed in the national economy'." Corroborated in section 11.1 (Quality assurance): "The main data source for Polish EMP NA and RA data is the LFS, which assures the harmonization, the comparability and the reliability of all data concerning labour market." Supersedes the round-1 deferred finding, which had looked at the wrong Eurostat dataset code (na10/nama_10_gdp instead of the employment-specific nama_10_pe).

Eurostat's ESMS metadata page for dataset nama_10_pe ("Population and employment - national accounts"), Greece's national submission, section 18.1 Source data: "The source that is widely used by almost all the EU countries is the Labour Force Survey (LFS). This survey is addressed to households and aims to measure the labour supply... Regarding quarterly employment (persons) the main data source is the Labor Force Survey (LFS)", with LFS data (persons employed by NACE Rev.2 2-digit division) named as the basis for quarterly employment figures. Section 18.5 (Data compilation) adds that total-hours-worked figures are also "calculated mainly by using LFS data". Supersedes the round-1 no-document finding, which had guessed the wrong URL (na10_esms_el.htm, which 404s) instead of the correct employment-specific dataset page (nama_10_pe_esms_el.htm).

SCB's own methodology documentation for HUT (SCBDOK 3.2, 2012 edition, section 0.9 "EU-reglering"): "Undersökningar om Hushållens utgifter genomförs i alla EU-länderna. För att få jämförbarhet mellan de olika ländernas undersökningar har Eurostat publicerat handboken 'HOUSEHOLD BUDGET SURVEYS IN THE EU Methodology and recommendations for harmonization 2003'" (Household expenditure surveys are conducted in all EU countries. To achieve comparability between the different countries' surveys, Eurostat has published the handbook...), and "Från och med 1999 redovisas konsumtionen även efter ändamål enligt Eurostats rekommendationer, den så kallade COICOP-indelningen" (From 1999, consumption is also reported by purpose according to Eurostat's recommendations, the COICOP classification). Distinct from the already-closed CPI/HICP-weights question (HUT is confirmed NOT the source of Swedish CPI/HICP weights, which come from national accounts instead) -- this is a separate, genuine methodology-alignment dependency: survey design and classification, not price-index weighting.

reports.title: EDP Notification Tables (Government Deficit and Debt)
reports.description: Harmonised tables in which EU Member States report their planned and actual government deficit and debt levels to Eurostat under the excessive deficit procedure (EDP). Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009, Article 3(1): 'Member States shall report to the Commission (Eurostat) their planned and actual government deficits and levels of government debt twice a year, the first time before 1 April of the current year (year n) and the second time before 1 October of year n.' Eurostat's own page: 'In April and October of each year, Eurostat publishes the notification tables as transmitted by EU Member States in accordance with EU regulation 479/2009.'
reports.cadence_note: Live-verified against both the Regulation text and the Eurostat page's own current release listing -- 'April 2026' and 'October 2025' dated release blocks visible on the live page.

entries.covers: October 2026 EDP notification (government deficit and debt data)

release_schedule.note: Eurostat's April 2026 EDP notification press release (22 April 2026) explicitly states 'Next release: 21 October 2026' for the following EDP notification. This matches the publisher's stated pattern that EDP notification tables are published in April and October each year, per Council Regulation 479/2009 which requires Member States to report EDP data at end of March and end of September. The April 2026 release has already occurred, so the next expected release is the confirmed 21 October 2026 date.

reports.title: Report on the Quality of Fiscal Data Reported by EU Member States
reports.description: Article 8(3) of Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 (as amended): 'The Commission (Eurostat) shall report regularly to the European Parliament and to the Council on the quality of the actual data reported by Member States.' Eurostat's own page characterizes the resulting output as annual reports and currently lists 'Staff working document reporting to the European Parliament and the Council on the quality of fiscal data reported by Member States (MS) in 2025'. Note: the Regulation's own text says 'regularly', not 'annually' -- the annual framing is Eurostat's own practice, not a statutory requirement.
reports.cadence_note: Live-verified on Eurostat's own quality page; current edition assesses 2025 data. Statutory basis says 'regularly', not 'annually' -- recorded as a distinction, not resolved.

entries.covers: Quality of fiscal data reported by Member States in 2022
Quality of fiscal data reported by Member States in 2024
Quality of fiscal data reported by Member States in 2025
Quality of fiscal data reported by Member States in 2026 (projected next edition)

release_schedule.note: Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 (as amended) requires the Commission (Eurostat) to report 'regularly' -- not on a fixed statutory date -- to the European Parliament and Council on fiscal data quality. In practice, Commission Staff Working Documents in this series have been transmitted to the Council each year in April: SWD covering 2022 data was dated/received ~14-18 April 2023 (Council doc ST-8410-2023-INIT); SWD covering 2024 data was dated 30 April 2025 (ST-8500-2025-INIT); SWD(2026)127 final covering 2025 data was dated 28 April 2026 and transmitted to Council 20 May 2026 (ST-8895-2026-INIT). This confirms the corpus's existing cadence_note: the statutory language is 'regularly,' not a fixed annual mandate, but observed practice has been one edition per year, released in April. Since the 2025-data edition already appeared in April 2026, the next expected edition (covering 2026 data) would be around April 2027.

That is the closest thing to a genuine EU-internal statistics-to-statistics edge this branch has found -- every prior EU finding has been about the asymmetry between the supranational and national layers, not a dependency running entirely within the EU statistical system itself.

reports.title: Farm Structure Survey (FSS)
reports.description: Eurostat's recurring survey of the structure of agricultural holdings across the EU, run in one form or another since 1966. Eurostat's own metadata page states: 'The data describe the structure of agricultural holdings providing the general characteristics of farms and farmers and information on their land, livestock and labour force. They also describe production methods, rural development measures and agro-environmental aspects... The aggregated results are disseminated through statistical tables.' Legally re-founded by Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 ('on integrated farm statistics'), which fixed the current data collections at reference years 2020, 2023 and 2026 -- a census in 2020, sample surveys in 2023 and 2026 -- each covering at least 98% of the EU's utilised agricultural area and livestock units. Eurostat's own metadata states the FSS 'provid[es] a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data' -- see _dropped.
reports.cadence_note: Currently fixed at reference years 2020, 2023, 2026 by Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 Article 5 -- a 3-year interval, with results 'disseminated 2 years after the reference year' (Eurostat metadata page, 'Frequency of dissemination'). Historically (1989/1990 through 2016) reference years averaged roughly one every 2.6 years on a 10-year agricultural-census cycle with 2-3 intermediate sample surveys between censuses. See _open_questions.

release_schedule.rule: Regulation (EU) 2018/1091, Article 5: 'Member States shall collect and provide the core structural data ... for the reference years 2020, 2023 and 2026.' Article 12 sets Member State transmission deadlines of 12 months after the end of the 2023/2026 reference years (15 months for 2020). Eurostat's own metadata for this dataset (ef_sims.htm, Accuracy/Timeliness section) states: 'Results are disseminated 2 years after the reference year.'
release_schedule.note: FSS is run on a 3-year cycle mandated by Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 (reference years 2020 [census], 2023, 2026); the regulation as currently in force does not specify years beyond 2026. As of the current date (2026-08-11) the 2026 reference-year survey is the cycle underway; per Eurostat's own metadata, results for a given reference year are disseminated about 2 years later, so 2026-reference-year results are expected around 2028 (exact month not published). This matches the releases_per_year=0.33 (~once every 3 years) already on file.

reports.title: Farm Sustainability Data Network (FSDN)
reports.publisher: European Commission (Directorate-General for Agriculture and Rural Development)
reports.description: The EU's annual farm-level accountancy and sustainability survey, and the other end of the one genuine EU-internal statistics-to-statistics edge this branch has found. DG AGRI's own page describes it as "an EU survey that gathers annual data about farms" which has "collected farm economics data from an annual sample of around 75 000 farms across the EU for more than 60 years", a sample that "represents 3.5 million farms and 90% of the EU's agricultural production". Selected through national liaison agencies from market-oriented farms. Its outputs are a public database of aggregated results, farm-economy dashboards at EU, country and sector level, and analytical briefs. RENAMED, and the old name is the one most documents still use: this is the former Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN), renamed and re-scoped by Regulation (EU) 2023/2674 amending Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009. As of 2025 the collection expanded beyond economics to "environmental and social sustainability performance", including quantities of fertilizers, pesticides, feed and antimicrobials. Current implementing instruments named on DG AGRI's page: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2746 (variable definitions, farm selection methodology, data-sharing), Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1417 (income determination and sustainability analysis) and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2499. Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 Article 5(3) caps the sample: "the maximum number of returning holdings shall be 105 000 for the Community". MINTED 2026-08-09 (cheap-check pass). The blocker recorded in this file's `_open_questions` and `_dropped` was site access, and it is gone: agriculture.ec.europa.eu served both the FADN and FSDN pages as ordinary fetchable HTML this session, so the title, cadence, sample and URL now come from the network's own authoritative site rather than only from the legal instruments.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, stated as such by DG AGRI ("an annual sample of around 75 000 farms", "gathers annual data about farms"). Note this is the cadence of the data collection; the dashboards and analytical briefs built on it are published on their own schedules, which were not established this session.

entries.covers: Transmission deadline for reporting year 2025 farm returns to the Commission

release_schedule.rule: Farm returns shall be transmitted to the Commission by 15 December, after the end of the reporting year in question (Article 11(4) of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/220, as amended by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2746 of 25 October 2024, laying down rules for application of Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 / the FSDN legal framework). Germany has a derogation allowing transmission within 15 weeks after this deadline.
release_schedule.note: This is the Member States' legal deadline for transmitting annual farm return data to the Commission, not a publication date for a public-facing report or dashboard. No published calendar of FADN/FSDN public database updates or DG AGRI 'Standard Results' publication dates was found; those downstream products (public database, standard results, analytical briefs) appear to be released some time after this input deadline but on no publicly stated fixed date. This complements, rather than contradicts, the existing cadence_note (annual data collection of ~75,000 farms).

dependencies.basis:
VERIFIED DIRECTLY BY THIS SESSION (2026-08-09) -- Eurostat's 'Farm structure (ef)' metadata page re-fetched first-hand, and the sentence now pinned to its section: it sits in section 3.4, Statistical concepts and definitions. "Both the censuses and the sample surveys are aimed at producing a variety of information on specific CAP targets, as well as providing a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data." Direction is FSDN -> FSS, as the original lead reasoned: a ~75 000-farm sample capped by Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 Article 5(3) at "105 000 for the Community" needs a population framework to extrapolate to the 3.5 million farms it claims to represent, and this record says the FSS supplies it. Typed `methodology_depends_on` rather than `uses_data_from`: what passes is a weighting/extrapolation framework, not FSS observations feeding into FSDN records. TWO CAVEATS, both stated rather than smoothed over. First, the evidence is ONE-SIDED: it is Eurostat asserting what its survey is used for, and DG AGRI's own FSDN page -- read in full this session -- names neither the Farm Structure Survey, nor integrated farm statistics, nor Regulation (EU) 2018/1091, nor Eurostat anywhere. The producer of the dependent product has not been found stating the dependency. Second, the quoted sentence still says FADN, the network's pre-2023 name; the node is minted under its current name, FSDN, so the edge crosses a rename. Nothing found this session suggests the extrapolation arrangement itself changed with the rename, but nothing found confirms it either -- a successor should look for the same statement in FSDN-era methodology (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2746 is the obvious place, since DG AGRI's page says it carries the farm-selection methodology).

CORROBORATED FROM THE RECEIVING SIDE, 2026-08-09 (closing G.64.md cheap check 3 / this file's own _open_questions item 4). The first caveat above -- that only Eurostat, the supplying side, had been found stating this dependency -- no longer holds. FSDN's own implementing regulation, Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2746 of 25 October 2024 ('laying down rules for the application of Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 setting up the Farm Sustainability Data Network...'), fetched directly from EUR-Lex (CELEX:32024R2746), states in Annex III ('Models and methods for selection plan preparation'): 'all relevant types and sizes of farming represented in the integrated farm statistics (IFS) census or survey are to be covered at the level of detail which provides representative results on important farm groups, within the limits of the sample size.' 'Integrated farm statistics' is the Farm Structure Survey's own legal name -- Regulation (EU) 2018/1091, which this node's own description cites as its re-founding instrument, is titled 'on integrated farm statistics'. Recital (5) of 2024/2746 cross-references the same instrument directly: 'These standard outputs need to be established by product and should align with the list of core structural data variables set out in Annex III to Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 of the European Parliament and of the Council.' So the FSDN sample-selection methodology names the FSS/IFS census as the population it must represent, on its own side of the relationship, independent of Eurostat's own metadata page. The second caveat (the edge crosses FADN's rename to FSDN) is unaffected -- 2024/2746 is itself an FSDN-era instrument and does not use the name FADN, so it does not help there either way.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Both the censuses and the sample surveys are aimed at producing a variety of information on specific CAP targets, as well as providing a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data.

Whatever denied the original session was transient or environmental, not a property of the site -- worth knowing before another EU lead is parked on 'unreachable'. ONE SUBSTANTIVE CHANGE the original entry could not have known: the network has been RENAMED. The node is minted under the current name; the Eurostat sentence the edge rests on still says FADN, and that crossing is flagged in the edge's own `basis` rather than papered over. ORIGINAL ENTRY BELOW. THE BEST LEAD THIS SLICE PRODUCED. Eurostat's own 'Farm structure (ef)' metadata page states: 'Both the censuses and the sample surveys are aimed at producing a variety of information on specific CAP targets, as well as providing a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data.' Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 Article 5(3) caps FADN's sample at 'the maximum number of returning holdings shall be 105 000 for the Community' -- a sample that needs a population framework to extrapolate to the whole farming sector, which is what this record says the FSS supplies. Direction, if minted: FADN depends on FSS (methodology_depends_on), because FSS is the structural/weighting framework, not FADN's raw accountancy data. NOT MINTED because FADN itself has no independently-verified title, cadence or URL from its own authoritative site -- agridata.ec.europa.eu and agriculture.ec.europa.eu were both unreachable this session (browser tool denial, cause not established). The identification is documented after all -- by definitional property rather than by acronym, which is why three prior searches for the string 'IPCN' missed it. Eurostat's own methodological annex to the Joint Index, 'Remuneration and Pensions Calculation of the Joint Index in accordance with Annex XI of the EU Staff Regulations' (ec.europa.eu/eurostat/cache/metadata/Annexes/prc_colc_tot_esms_an_2.pdf, fetched in full this session), names the Luxembourg component as "the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) in the case of Luxembourg", sourced from "the Luxembourg national statistical office (Statec)", and then defines it: "The current Luxembourg national index of consumer prices came into effect in 1997. It complies with the HICP except that its weighting structure excludes the consumer spending of non-residents on Luxembourg territory." STATEC's own methodology document 'L'indice des prix a la consommation (IPC)' (statistiques.public.lu, /fr/methodologie/methodes/economie-finances/Prix/ipc/IPC-description.pdf, fetched in full this session) gives that exclusion as the SOLE difference between its two indices, and assigns it to the IPCN: "l'IPCN exclut les depenses de consommation finale effectuees par des non-residents sur le territoire economique luxembourgeois alors que l'IPCH les inclut", and "L'IPCN et l'IPCH sont etablis selon les memes principes methodologiques. Les deux indices se distinguent sur le seul point de leur couverture geographique." Since the two indices differ on exactly one property, and Eurostat states that property, the identification is unique: the Joint Index's Luxembourg CPI is the IPCN, not the IPCH. STATED LIMIT, per sec.3: no document read writes 'IPCN' and 'the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) in the case of Luxembourg' in the same sentence. This is an identification by matching definitions across two primary sources, not a citation. Recorded as such rather than as a quoted equivalence. MINOR DATE TENSION, logged not resolved: Eurostat dates the current national index to 1997, while STATEC writes that "le Luxembourg a decide, en janvier 2000, de reintroduire l'indice national pour les besoins de l'<<echelle mobile des salaires>>" -- consistent if the index existed from 1997 and was adopted for wage indexation in 2000, but neither document says so.

reports.title: Annual Consolidated Balance Sheet of the Eurosystem
reports.description: The consolidated year-end balance sheet of the Eurosystem (the ECB and the euro area national central banks), with intra-Eurosystem claims and liabilities netted out. Governed by Annex VII to Guideline (EU) 2024/2941 of the European Central Bank (ECB/2024/31): 'the consolidated annual balance sheet of the Eurosystem' (Article 26(3)(c)). ECB's own landing page lists one dated entry per year, unbroken, from 1999 to 2025.
reports.cadence_note: 27 consecutive years of linked publication (1999-2025) confirmed directly on the ECB's own landing page, each dated in February for the preceding year-end -- e.g. '26 February 2026 -- Consolidated balance sheet of the Eurosystem as at 31 December 2025'.

reports.title: Weekly Financial Statement of the Eurosystem
reports.description: The consolidated weekly financial statement of the Eurosystem, published under Annexes V and VI to Guideline (EU) 2024/2941 (ECB/2024/31): 'the published consolidated weekly financial statement of the Eurosystem after quarter end' and '... during the quarter' (Article 26(3)(a)-(b)). ECB's own landing page: 'The weekly financial statements of the Eurosystem are published on a Tuesday, and they relate to the preceding Friday.'
reports.cadence_note: Stated directly by the ECB: published every Tuesday, relating to the preceding Friday, except the first statement of each quarter, which 'will normally be a Wednesday (instead of Tuesday) in order to allow more time to complete the quarterly revaluation of assets and liabilities'. The fastest-cadence node in the EU branch, faster than eurostat-hicp's monthly cadence.

release_schedule.rule: The weekly financial statements of the Eurosystem are published on a Tuesday, and they relate to the preceding Friday, except the first statement of each quarter, which will normally be a Wednesday (instead of Tuesday) in order to allow more time to complete the quarterly revaluation of assets and liabilities. Publication dates may also shift when TARGET system closures occur during the statement preparation period.
release_schedule.note: Confirmed via ECB site fetch: standard weekly Tuesday cadence with quarterly-first-statement Wednesday exception (e.g. 7 Jan 2026, 9 Apr 2026 [shifted to Thursday due to Easter Monday TARGET closure], 8 Jul 2026, 7 Oct 2026 are the 2026 quarter-first-statement dates). As of 2026-08-11 (a Tuesday, not a quarter-first date), the immediate entries follow the plain weekly rule.

_slice: Canadian federal benefit, tax and statistical programmes
_note: This slice covers the Canadian federal parameter-setting machinery: the annual and quarterly decisions that turn statistical series into dollar amounts people actually receive or pay. Its shape is a narrow funnel. Almost everything ultimately rests on just two Statistics Canada series - the Consumer Price Index and the average weekly earnings of the industrial aggregate from the Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours - and the connections are unusually well documented because most of them are written into statute rather than administrative practice. The Employment Insurance Act s. 4(5) and the Canada Pension Plan s. 18(5) both name the industrial aggregate average weekly earnings in nearly identical language, which is why the EI maximum insurable earnings and the CPP Year's Maximum Pensionable Earnings move together; Income Tax Act s. 117.1(4) and s. 122.61(5) both name the Consumer Price Index for Canada and both use a 12-month period ending 30 September, while CPP uses 12 months ending 31 October and OAS uses rolling three-month averages, so the same index is read on three different clocks. The most valuable finding is what feeds the CPI itself, which the graph previously showed as a source with no inputs: the annual basket-update paper (catalogue 62F0014M) states plainly that basket weights are derived primarily from the national Household Final Consumption Expenditure series, supplemented by the Survey of Household Spending for low-level and geographic detail. That makes the Canadian CPI a downstream product of the national accounts, which is the reverse of how it is usually pictured. The one genuinely two-stage structure in the slice is EI: the regional unemployment rates come from the Labour Force Survey via s. 17 of the EI Regulations, and they then determine both the best-weeks divisor in the benefit calculation and the number of weeks payable, so labour market statistics enter the benefit amount twice over.

reports.title: Survey of Household Spending (SHS)
reports.description: Annual national household survey collecting detailed information on what Canadian households spend on food, shelter, clothing, transportation and other categories. Its principal downstream use is to supply the expenditure detail used to construct Consumer Price Index basket weights, particularly at low levels of product and geographic aggregation. Results are released as Table 11-10-0222-01 and associated Daily articles.

release_schedule.note: StatCan's own survey metadata (IMDB, SDDS 3508) states the Survey of Household Spending is conducted 'Every 2 years' (reference years 2019, 2021, 2023, 2025, ...), so data collection follows a fixed 2-year cycle. However, there is no published release calendar and the actual publication lag after each reference year has been highly irregular: 2019 reference-year data was released 2021-01-22 (~13 months after year-end), 2021 data was released 2023-10-18 (~22 months after year-end), and 2023 data was released 2025-05-21 (~17 months after year-end) — see The Daily releases dq210122b, dq231018a, and dq250521a. Because both the exact release month and the lag length vary substantially cycle to cycle, no specific next release date can be reliably computed. 2025 reference-year data collection ran through roughly February 2026 per StatCan's respondent portal, so the next release (for 2025 data) is expected at some point in 2026-2027, but no concrete date or calendar entry has been published by StatCan as of 2026-08-11.

reports.title: Household Final Consumption Expenditure (HFCE)
reports.description: The household final consumption expenditure series of the Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts, measuring total spending by the household sector on goods and services by detailed product category. Since the 2019 CPI basket update it has been the primary source of Consumer Price Index basket weights, replacing the Survey of Household Spending in that role. Published quarterly with annual benchmarks.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly series with annual benchmark levels; CPI basket updates use the annual national HFCE series for a single calendar reference year.

entries.covers: Second quarter 2026 - Gross domestic product, income and expenditure accounts (includes Household final consumption expenditure)
Third quarter 2026 - Gross domestic product, income and expenditure accounts

release_schedule.note: HFCE (table 36-10-0107-01) is released as part of Statistics Canada's quarterly National Income and Expenditure Accounts / GDP by income and expenditure release (The Daily), published roughly 60 days after each reference quarter ends. Most recent release was May 29, 2026 (Q1 2026); next is Q2 2026 on August 28, 2026 per StatCan's 2026-2027 major economic releases schedule.

reports.title: An Analysis of the Consumer Price Index Basket Update
reports.description: Annual analytical and methodological paper (catalogue 62F0014M) describing the composition of the CPI basket and the changes introduced with each basket update, including the expenditure weights by major component and the data sources used to derive them. It is the document of record for what feeds the Canadian CPI's weighting structure. The 2026 update is based on 2025 expenditures.

entries.covers: An Analysis of the 2027 Consumer Price Index Basket Update, Based on 2026 Expenditures

release_schedule.note: Statistics Canada publishes this analytical piece annually, one per year, timed to the annual CPI basket update. No published release calendar or stated rule was found, but recent editions show a consistent mid-June release: 2022-06-15, 2023-06-20, 2024-06-18, 2025-06-17, 2026-06-15 (earlier editions were less regular: 2021-07-21, 2019-02-27). The 2026 edition (current corpus record) was already released on 2026-06-15, so the next expected edition is projected for mid-June 2027 based on the recent pattern; exact day is not knowable in advance.

reports.title: Employment Insurance Premium Rate (Canada Employment Insurance Commission annual rate setting)
reports.publisher: Canada Employment Insurance Commission / Employment and Social Development Canada
reports.description: Each September the Canada Employment Insurance Commission sets the Employment Insurance premium rate for the following calendar year, expressed in dollars per $100 of insurable earnings for employees, with employers paying 1.4 times the employee rate and a separate lower rate applying in Quebec. The rate is legislatively required to be the seven-year break-even rate forecast by the EI Senior Actuary. For 2026 the rate was set at $1.63 (employee) and $2.28 (employer).
reports.cadence_note: Announced by mid-September each year for the following calendar year, alongside the maximum insurable earnings.

release_schedule.rule: Employment Insurance Act, s.66(1): the Canada Employment Insurance Commission shall, on or before September 14 in a year, set the premium rate for the following year (subject to a maximum year-over-year change of 0.05 percentage points, per s.66(1.1)/(7)).
release_schedule.note: In practice the Commission has announced the rate a couple of days before the September 14 statutory deadline (e.g., the 2026 rate was announced September 12, 2025). The computed 'next' date of 2026-09-14 is the statutory deadline for setting the 2027 rate; the actual press-release date may fall slightly earlier.

reports.title: Actuarial Report on the Employment Insurance Premium Rate
reports.publisher: Office of the Chief Actuary, Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
reports.description: Annual statutory report by the EI Senior Actuary forecasting the seven-year break-even premium rate that would balance the Employment Insurance Operating Account, together with the projected maximum insurable earnings, premium revenues and benefit expenditures. It is the binding technical input to the Commission's rate-setting decision. Accompanied in recent years by an addendum reflecting policy announcements made after the main report was finalised.

entries.covers: 2027 Actuarial Report on the Employment Insurance Premium Rate (public release deadline)

release_schedule.rule: Employment Insurance Act s.66.3: the Chief Actuary shall, on or before August 22 in a year, provide the Canada Employment Insurance Commission with the actuarial report setting out forecasts/estimates for the premium rate. The Commission must then make the report and its summary available to the public on or before September 14 of that year (the Minister subsequently tables it in Parliament within 10 sitting days of publication).
release_schedule.note: September 14 is the statutory latest date for public availability; actual publication in recent years has occurred slightly earlier (e.g. the 2026 report, covering the 2026 premium rate, was published 2025-09-12 against an Aug 22 deadline for delivery to the Commission). The report title year is one year ahead of the calendar year it is published in (the '2026' report was published in Sept 2025), so the next edition, for the 2027 rate, is expected on or before 2026-09-14.

reports.title: Employment Insurance Maximum Insurable Earnings (MIE)
reports.publisher: Canada Employment Insurance Commission / Employment and Social Development Canada
reports.description: The annual ceiling on earnings on which EI premiums are payable and on which EI benefits are calculated, announced each September for the following year. It is set by a formula in section 4 of the Employment Insurance Act driven by Statistics Canada's Average Weekly Earnings of the Industrial Aggregate, and is rounded down to the nearest $100. The 2026 MIE is $68,900, up from $65,700 in 2025.

entries.covers: 2027 Employment Insurance Maximum Insurable Earnings notice/effective date

release_schedule.rule: Employment Insurance Act, s.4: the maximum yearly insurable earnings for a year is 52 times the average, for the 12-month period ending April 30 of the year immediately before that year, of the Average Weekly Earnings of the Industrial Aggregate in Canada (as published by Statistics Canada) for each month in that period, adjusted by the year-over-year percentage change in that average, and rounded down to the nearest multiple of $100. The resulting amount takes effect January 1 of that year, and CEIC/ESDC publishes an updated 'Maximum Insurable Earnings' notice each year (historically via a September/October news release; more recently as an updated canada.ca notice page, e.g. the 2026 notice was published 2025-10-31) ahead of the January 1 effective date.
release_schedule.note: The 2026 MIE ($68,900, up from $65,700 in 2025) was published on the corpus's current URL (dated 2025-10-31, effective 2026-01-01). The 2027 figure has not yet been published as of 2026-08-11; it is computed under the statutory formula using average weekly earnings data through April 30, 2026, and by pattern (2013-2025 news releases/notices) is expected to be published in fall 2026, effective 2027-01-01.

reports.title: Indexation adjustment for personal income tax and benefit amounts
reports.description: The CRA's annual publication of the federal indexation factor and the resulting indexed values of federal tax bracket thresholds, non-refundable credit amounts, the OAS repayment threshold, the Canada child benefit, the Canada workers benefit and other income-tested amounts. Tax bracket and credit changes take effect on 1 January; income-tested benefit amounts such as the CCB take effect on 1 July to align with the benefit year. The 2026 indexation increase was 2.0%.

release_schedule.note: The CRA's page (last updated March 2026) does not state a formal publication schedule. However, multiple past editions show the agency updates/announces the indexation figures for the upcoming tax year in mid-to-late November of the prior year: 2012 amounts on 2011-11-22, 2023 amounts around 2022-11-16, and 2026 amounts around late November 2025 (media coverage dated 2025-11-27 referencing 'this week' CRA released the figures). The next release, for 2027 amounts, is projected to follow this pattern in November 2026. The underlying indexation factor itself is calculated using Statistics Canada CPI data per the page's own statement: 'Each year, certain personal income tax and benefit amounts are indexed to inflation using the Consumer Price Index data as reported by Statistics Canada.'

reports.title: Employment Insurance monthly regional rates of unemployment
reports.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada / Service Canada

reports.title: Canada Pension Plan annual benefit adjustment (Pension Index)
reports.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada / Service Canada
reports.description: The annual cost-of-living adjustment applied to all Canada Pension Plan benefits in payment - retirement, disability, survivor, children's and death benefits - effective each January. Benefits never decrease: a negative calculation leaves amounts unchanged. The January 2026 increase was 2.0%.

release_schedule.rule: CPP amounts are adjusted once a year in January. The adjustment percentage is the percentage increase in the average CPI (All-Items) for the 12-month period ending October 31, over the average CPI for the previous 12-month period, as legislated under the Canada Pension Plan.

_dropped.edge: ei-actuarial-report-premium-rate -> Finance Canada economic and fiscal projections
_dropped.why:
RE-CHECKED 2026-08-09, still open. Re-read the live 2026 actuarial report (both the OSFI landing page and the underlying PDF) specifically looking for a titled Finance Canada publication behind the Minister-of-Finance attribution. Neither source names one: both give the attribution in general terms only - 'Assumptions and forecasts provided by the Minister of Finance in accordance with section 66.2 of the EI Act' - and section 66.2 of the Employment Insurance Act is a statutory requirement that the Minister of Finance supply these forecasts to the Commission, not a citation of a Finance Canada publication. So the underlying assumptions may come from an internal or unpublished Finance Canada projection, or from the same forecasts Finance Canada uses in the federal Budget and Fall Economic Statement without those documents being named - there is no way to tell from the actuarial report which. Confirms the original finding rather than changing it: no document names a specific publication, and there is still no Finance Canada economic and fiscal projection node in the graph to point at. Original entry follows.

The actuarial report is explicit that several of its most influential assumptions come from the Department of Finance - section 4.2.2 says of the unemployment rate 'This assumption is provided by the Minister of Finance', and Table 2 footnotes the increase in average employment income the same way. But it names no specific published Finance Canada document, and there is no Finance Canada economic and fiscal projection node in the graph to point at, so there is nothing to attach the edge to.

Household final consumption expenditure benchmarking plausibly draws on the Survey of Household Spending, but the CPI basket-update paper treats HFCE and SHS as two parallel sources and says nothing about one feeding the other. No StatCan methodology document I found states the relationship, so the edge is not recorded.

The 2026 basket-update paper states that 'the use of retail scanner data was expanded with the 2025 basket and is now the primary data source for the food from stores component weights'. This is a real and documented input, but retail scanner data is a commercial data feed rather than an official report or statistical release, so it does not qualify as a node in this graph.

The two are announced in the same September news release and multiply together to give the published maximum annual contribution, but the premium rate is set by the seven-year break-even forecast and the MIE by the section 4 average-weekly-earnings formula. No document states that the rate depends on the MIE, so this is co-publication rather than dependency.

Tax indexation depends on the level of the CPI, which in turn depends on the basket weights, but the indexation authority (Income Tax Act s. 117.1(4)) refers only to 'the Consumer Price Index for Canada, as published by Statistics Canada' and no document connects the indexation factor to the basket-update paper. The path runs through statcan-cpi and is already captured there.

The OAS recovery tax repayment threshold appears in the CRA indexation table ($95,323 for 2026) while OAS benefit amounts are indexed quarterly by ESDC on a different CPI reference period. The two are separate mechanisms indexed off the same source index, and no document says the OAS payment adjustment uses the CRA factor, so no edge.

The Chief Actuary's triennial Actuarial Report on the Canada Pension Plan projects the YMPE, but s. 18 of the Canada Pension Plan makes the YMPE a purely mechanical function of the Statistics Canada Wage Measure with no actuarial input. The actuarial report governs the contribution rate, not the YMPE, so the edge would misstate the relationship.

reports.title: Enquête mensuelle de conjoncture auprès des ménages (Camme)
reports.description: INSEE's monthly household economic-sentiment survey (Consommation des Ménages / Camme), part of the European Commission's harmonised joint business and consumer survey programme. reports.title: Loi organique N°001/2014 du 14/06/2015 relative à la décentralisation
reports.publisher: Journal Officiel de la République Gabonaise / Présidence de la République
reports.description: Gabon's organic decentralization law, published in the Journal Officiel de la République Gabonaise, N°260 du 7 juillet 2015, and signed by President Ali Bongo Ondimba ("Fait à Libreville, le 15 juin 2015"). Defines a commune as "une personne morale de droit public distincte de l'Etat, dotée de la personnalité juridique et de l'autonomie administrative et financière." Classifies communes by population and own-resources: "Article 5 : Les communes de première catégorie sont celles ayant plus de 15 000 habitants ou des ressources propres supérieures ou égales à 150 millions de francs CFA. Article 6 : Les communes de seconde catégorie sont celles dont la population est comprise entre 5000 et 15 000 habitants ou ayant des ressources propres comprises entre 50 et 150 millions de francs CFA." Article 216 requires that competence transfers from the State to communes and départements identify the resulting financial charges, and states the general principle: "Le transfert des compétences s'accompagne du transfert des ressources correspondantes." Establishes State transfers to local government: "Article 238 : Les transferts de l'Etat, sous forme de dotations ou de transferts d'impôts, visent à compenser l'accroissement des charges de la collectivité locale du fait de la décentralisation et de l'insuffisance de ses ressources propres. Article 239 : ... -de la dotation globale de fonctionnement destinée au fonctionnement courant de la collectivité locale ; -des dotations et subventions d'équipement destinées à l'investissement de la collectivité locale ; -de la dotation liée à l'accroissement des charges résultant des transferts des compétences ; -de la dotation visant à compenser le manque à gagner résultant des dégrèvements et exonérations consentis par la loi." Also creates a named equalisation fund: "Article 250 : Il est institué un fonds de péréquation des collectivités locales chargé de fournir aux collectivités locales des ressources additionnelles... Article 252 : Le Fonds de péréquation des collectivités locales est alimenté par : -un prélèvement d'office opéré sur le budget général de l'Etat dont le taux est fixé annuellement dans la loi de finances ; -la contribution respective des collectivités locales dont le taux... tient compte de la capacité contributive de chaque collectivité locale." CAVEAT: a December 2020 secondary news report (Gabonreview, not independently quotable) suggested the Fonds de péréquation's operational status was still "under study" as of that date; no 2021-2026 primary document confirms current operational status, and the implementing décret referenced in Article 253 ("Ses attributions et son organisation sont fixés par les statuts approuvés par décret") could not be located this round.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, currently in force (JO-listed date 14/06/2015; signature block dated 15 juin 2015 — a 1-day internal discrepancy in the source document).

reports.title: Loi n°037/2018 du 11 juin 2019 portant réglementation du secteur minier en République Gabonaise
reports.publisher: Journal Officiel de la République Gabonaise / Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (douanes.ga)
reports.description: Gabon's Mining Code, published in the Journal Officiel de la République Gabonaise, N°28 Bis, 24 juillet 2019. Article 234 establishes a state/local-government split of mining-related tax revenue: "Les droits, taxes et impôts directs, à l'exception de l'impôt sur les sociétés, doivent être libérés par les titulaires des autorisations et des titres miniers en deux bordereaux distincts, l'un destiné à l'Etat et l'autre à la collectivité locale abritant l'autorisation ou le titre minier, conformément aux dispositions de la loi des finances." The split percentage itself is deferred to the annual Loi de Finances, not stated in the Code. CAVEAT: Article 1 explicitly excludes hydrocarbons from the Code's scope ("la présente loi... détermine le régime juridique... de l'exercice des activités ou opérations du secteur minier... à l'exception de celles relatives aux hydrocarbures liquides ou gazeux et aux eaux"), so this is a mining-only (not oil-and-gas) revenue-split mechanism; no Gabonese Code des Hydrocarbures primary text with a parallel provision could be located this round.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, currently in force.

reports.title: Loi de Finances 2025 — ligne budgétaire 712 "Péréquation Collectivités" (Article 21)
reports.publisher: Journal Officiel de la République Gabonaise / Présidence de la République
reports.description: Gabon's FY2025 Finance Law, published in the Journal Officiel de la République Gabonaise (66e année, N°51 Bis Spécial, 20 janvier 2025). Article 21, p.31 (Chapitre 4), sets prélèvements au profit des collectivités locales for 2025 at 29,058,048,393 FCFA and itemises them by line code, including: "712 | Péréquation Collectivités | 369 385 095 [LFI 2024] | 402 261 680 [LF 2025] | 32 876 585 [écart] | 9% [écart %]" — i.e. a named, code-bearing 'Péréquation Collectivités' beneficiary funded at 402,261,680 FCFA for 2025, up 9% from 369,385,095 FCFA in LFI 2024. This confirms the fund named in Articles 250-252 of the 2014/2015 organic decentralization law now has a real annual appropriation, not merely a paper statute. CAVEATS: (1) accessed via a third-party mirror (directinfosgabon.com), not the .gouv.ga domain directly, because journal-officiel.ga's own search interface is non-functional/JS-rendered and returned no result for this instrument this round; the PDF's own masthead unambiguously identifies it as the official Journal Officiel, so the document itself is treated as primary despite the indirect access route. (2) An appropriation is not the same fact as a disbursement: no Cour des Comptes execution report (2022 or 2023 edition) isolates péréquation-specific spending from the aggregate 'collectivités locales' transfer total, so whether this line was actually paid out to communes in 2025 is NOT confirmed by any primary document located this round — see ga-courcomptes-relf-2022 and the _dropped RELF 2023 entry in this file. (3) A June 2026 ministerial statement (Interior Minister Adrien Nguema Mba, via gouvernement.ga) separately confirms the fund 'a été mis en place' (has been established) but describes its funding sources — a share of state own-revenue plus oil/forestry/mining-sector resources — only in the conditional ('devrait être alimenté'), suggesting the funding mechanism was still being finalised as of that date even though this FY2025 line already exists. (4) A July 2026 secondary-only report (two Gabonese news outlets, not government-authored, sourced to an unnamed internal compte rendu not locatable on gouvernement.ga) claims an interministerial committee found the fund's 'inopérabilité prolongée' (prolonged non-operability) as of July 23, 2026, directly contradicting the June 2026 ministerial claim; this is recorded here as an unresolved tension in the evidence, not adjudicated either way.
reports.cadence_note: One-off annual budget-law entry for FY2025; the enclosing Loi de Finances itself recurs annually but no cadence is asserted for this specific line item's continuation or amount.

dependencies.basis: The organic decentralization law's Article 250 institutes the 'fonds de péréquation des collectivités locales' and Article 252 states it is funded by 'un prélèvement d'office opéré sur le budget général de l'Etat dont le taux est fixé annuellement dans la loi de finances' — i.e. the organic law itself designates the annual Finance Law as the instrument that sets the fund's actual take rate/amount each year. The FY2025 Finance Law's Article 21 line item 712 ('Péréquation Collectivités', 402,261,680 FCFA) is exactly that designated annual act: it is not merely citing the fund for context, it is the yearly mechanism Article 252 names as the fund's funding source, applied. That is a genuine data/figure dependency (the budget line's existence and legal basis flow from Article 252's designation) rather than a loose contextual reference, so uses_data_from is chosen over cites. _note: Thomas, 2026-09-06: 'chase all of the round 3 leads'. The corpus carried no UK census statute at all — an odd gap next to Australia's Census and Statistics Act 1905 (minted in round 2), Ireland's Statistics Act 1993 and the UK's own Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007. Every UK census runs on a two-step statutory chain: a permanent Census Act, plus a Census Order made afresh for each census. This slice mints both steps for all three UK census jurisdictions and wires the three census nodes to them. Every edge is A, and each rests on two independent readings: the census publisher's own document naming the instrument by title, and the instrument's own enacting recital. Northern Ireland is a separate legal system and section 10(2) of the 1920 Act says so verbatim ('This Act shall not extend to Ireland'), so nir-census-2021 hangs off the Census Act (Northern Ireland) 1969 instead — a distinction that would have been easy to get wrong. Every url and evidence_url was raw-verified HTTP 200 and every quote re-fetched and substring-checked against the live cited URL after this file was written.

reports.title: Census Act 1920
reports.description: The permanent statute authorising the taking of a census in Great Britain. Section 1(1) provides that it is lawful for His Majesty by Order in Council from time to time to direct that a census be taken for Great Britain or any part of it, and that such an Order may prescribe the census date, the persons by and about whom returns are made, and the particulars to be stated. Section 2(1), as amended by the Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007, places the duty to carry out the census on the Statistics Board in relation to England and Wales and on the Registrar General for Scotland in relation to Scotland. Section 10(2) provides that the Act does not extend to Ireland, so it is not the basis for the Northern Ireland census.
reports.cadence_note: Section 1(1) proviso (i) sets a minimum interval, not a fixed decennial requirement: an Order may not require a census in any part of Great Britain in a year unless at least five years have elapsed since the year the last census was taken there.

reports.title: The Census (England and Wales) Order 2020
reports.publisher: His Majesty in Council, on the recommendation of the Minister for the Cabinet Office
reports.description: The Order in Council directing Census 2021 in England and Wales (SI 2020 No. 532), made 20 May 2020. It recites that it is made in exercise of the powers conferred by section 1(1) of the Census Act 1920, following consultation with the Welsh Ministers. Article 2 defines census day as 21 March 2021 and article 3 directs that a census is to be taken for England and Wales on that date; article 4(3) requires returns in the form prescribed by regulations made under section 3 of the Act.

reports.title: The Census (Scotland) Order 2020
reports.publisher: His Majesty in Council, approved by resolution of the Scottish Parliament
reports.description: The Order in Council directing Scotland's census (SSI 2020 No. 76), made 11 March 2020 and extending to Scotland only. It recites that it is made under sections 1(1) and 8(1A)(b) of the Census Act 1920 and was approved by resolution of the Scottish Parliament. As made it set census day at 21 March 2021; the Census (Scotland) Amendment Order 2020 (SSI 2020/436, made 16 December 2020) substituted 20 March 2022 in both article 2 and article 3, so this Order as amended is the operative directing instrument for Scotland's Census 2022.

reports.title: Census Act (Northern Ireland) 1969
reports.description: The permanent statute authorising the census in Northern Ireland, which is a separate legal system from Great Britain — the Census Act 1920 expressly does not extend to it. Section 1(1), as amended, provides that the First Minister and deputy First Minister acting jointly may by order direct that a census of population be taken in Northern Ireland, and section 1(4) requires a draft of that order to be laid before and approved by resolution of the Assembly. Section 2(2) names the Registrar General for Northern Ireland as the officer who must make the arrangements for taking a census.
reports.cadence_note: Section 1(3)(a) sets the same five-year minimum interval as the 1920 Act: an order may not require a census in Northern Ireland in a year unless at least five years have elapsed since the year the last one was taken.

reports.title: The Census Order (Northern Ireland) 2020
reports.publisher: The First Minister and deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland
reports.description: The statutory rule directing Census 2021 in Northern Ireland (SR 2020 No. 83), laid before the Assembly in draft, made 5 May 2020 and in operation from 6 May 2020. Its opening recital states that the First Minister and deputy First Minister acting jointly make the Order under section 1(1) of the Census Act (Northern Ireland) 1969. Article 2 defines census day as 21 March 2021 and article 3 directs that a census be taken for Northern Ireland on that date; its Schedule lists the topics for the census questionnaire.

reports.title: Government Expenditure and Revenue Scotland
reports.publisher: Scottish Government (Office of the Chief Economic Adviser)
reports.description: Accredited official statistics estimating the revenue raised in Scotland and the cost of the public services provided for Scotland; the 2024-25 edition is the thirty-second in the series. Revenue is constrained to UK outturn from ONS public sector finances and apportioned to Scotland stream by stream; expenditure uses Scottish Government accounting data together with HM Treasury's Public Expenditure Statistical Analyses and its Country and regional analysis.

reports.title: GDP Quarterly National Accounts, Scotland
reports.description: Scotland's quarterly national accounts: GDP by the output, income and expenditure approaches, household sector income and expenditure accounts, and quarterly public sector revenue. The published methodology states that a full set of national accounts comparable with ONS UK output is neither practical nor conceptually possible for Scotland, so QNAS produces a defined subset, mixing top-down Scottish shares of UK results with bottom-up Scottish sources.

reports.title: Scotland's Census 2022
reports.description: The decennial census of the Scottish population, taken on 20 March 2022 after being moved from 2021 because of COVID-19. The Registrar General for Scotland takes the census under the Census Act 1920, with each census requiring a further Census Order and Census Regulations; the Census (Scotland) Order 2020 and Regulations 2020 governed this one. First results were published in September 2023 and the statistics were designated accredited official statistics.
reports.cadence_note: Decennial. Scotland's Census 2022 was taken on 20 March 2022, a year later than the rest of the UK because of COVID-19.

reports.title: Mid-year population estimates, Scotland
reports.description: Annual accredited official statistics estimating the usually resident population of Scotland at 30 June each year, by age and sex. The census provides the base population, which is rolled forward each year for births, deaths, net migration and other changes such as armed forces and prison populations. NRS rebased the 2011-2022 series in June 2024 following Scotland's Census 2022 and revised it again in January 2025.

reports.title: Scotland's Economic and Fiscal Forecasts
reports.description: The Scottish Fiscal Commission's official forecasts of the Scottish economy and of devolved tax revenues and social security spending, published alongside the Scottish Budget. The Commission states it does not produce official statistics but voluntarily applies the UK Statistics Authority's Code of Practice for Statistics, and its forecast comparison tables set its figures against the OBR, NIESR, the Bank of England and HM Treasury.

reports.title: Census 2021, Northern Ireland
reports.publisher: Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency (NISRA)
reports.description: The 2021 census of population and households in Northern Ireland, conducted by NISRA; first population and household estimates were published on 24 May 2022. The census results are the benchmark to which Northern Ireland's population statistics are anchored and from which subsequent mid-year estimates are rolled forward.
reports.cadence_note: Decennial. Census day for the 2021 Northern Ireland census was 21 March 2021.

reports.title: Mid-Year Population Estimates for Northern Ireland
reports.publisher: Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency (NISRA)
reports.description: Annual accredited official statistics estimating the usually resident population of Northern Ireland at 30 June each year, produced by the cohort component method. Births and deaths come from General Register Office registrations; migration inflows and outflows are estimated from the Medical Card Register, with flows to Great Britain constrained to figures agreed between NISRA, ONS and National Records of Scotland.

reports.title: Northern Ireland Composite Economic Index
reports.publisher: Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency (NISRA)
reports.description: A quarterly measure of economic activity in Northern Ireland, broadly equivalent to the output measure of GDP produced by ONS. It combines the NI Index of Services, Index of Production, Quarterly Construction Enquiry, Quarterly Employment Survey public sector jobs and unpublished agricultural output, weighted using ONS regional balanced GVA by industry and aggregated by annual chain-linking, with self-employment estimates drawn from the Labour Force Survey.

reports.title: Northern Ireland Labour Force Survey
reports.publisher: Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency (NISRA)
reports.description: A survey of households at private addresses in Northern Ireland providing the information used to develop, manage and evaluate NI labour market policy. It is the Northern Ireland component of the UK Labour Force Survey, managed by NISRA's Central Survey Unit while ONS Social Surveys manages the GB component, and it applies standard International Labour Organisation definitions of economic status. It is the largest social survey in Northern Ireland.

reports.title: Labour market overview, Wales
reports.description: A monthly Welsh Government release summarising the latest statistics on the Welsh labour market, drawing on HMRC Pay As You Earn Real Time Information and the Labour Force Survey. It reports headline employment, unemployment and economic inactivity rates for Wales alongside payrolled employment and earnings, with Welsh Government commentary on LFS data quality.

reports.title: Mid year estimates of the population, Wales
reports.description: An annual Welsh Government statistical bulletin presenting the ONS mid-year population estimates for Wales by local authority, age and sex. The underlying estimates are produced by ONS to methods set out in the ONS England and Wales methods guide; Welsh Government statisticians quality-assure the Welsh figures before publication. The bulletin notes that statistical uncertainty is lowest immediately after a census and grows as estimates are rolled forward.

reports.title: Consumer price inflation, UK
reports.description: The UK's monthly consumer price inflation bulletin, carrying the Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers' housing costs (CPIH), the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) and the Retail Prices Index (RPI). The index the Government's 2% inflation target is defined on.

reports.title: Living Costs and Food Survey
reports.description: The UK's household budget survey: an annual survey of household spending, which with national accounts household final consumption expenditure underpins the calculation of the consumer price inflation weights. ONS's own Consumer Prices Indices Technical Manual names it as one of the two major sources of information for the weights.

reports.title: Labour Force Survey
reports.description: The UK's continuous household survey of labour market activity, and the source of the International Labour Organization measure of unemployment that the monthly labour market bulletins are built on. Its own QMI: "The main labour market statistics are published in our monthly Labour market overview, UK bulletins".
reports.cadence_note: Continuous survey; datasets released quarterly, with the headline estimates carried monthly by the Labour market overview bulletin.

reports.title: Labour market overview, UK
reports.description: The UK's monthly headline labour market bulletin — employment, unemployment, economic inactivity and earnings — first published in April 1998. Draws its unemployment measure from the Labour Force Survey rather than the administrative Claimant Count.

reports.title: United Kingdom Balance of Payments — The Pink Book
reports.description: The UK's annual balance of payments compendium: current account, capital and financial accounts and the international investment position. Produced in accordance with the IMF's Balance of Payments Manual sixth edition and in line with the UK Statistics Authority's Code of Practice for Statistics.

reports.title: Public sector finances, UK
reports.description: The UK's monthly public sector finances bulletin — borrowing, debt and the main fiscal aggregates — produced jointly with HM Treasury. All statistical aggregates in the bulletin are defined using national accounts concepts and rules, compiled with reference to ESA 2010 since 2014.

reports.title: Monetary Policy Report
reports.description: The Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee's quarterly report on inflation and the outlook for monetary policy, setting out the Committee's projections against the Government's 2% target for the 12-month increase in the Consumer Prices Index.

reports.title: Code of Practice for Statistics
reports.description: The statutory code the UK Statistics Authority is required by section 10 of the Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007 to prepare, adopt and publish; official statistics assessed against it are designated National Statistics. UK statistical releases state compliance with it as their quality basis.
reports.cadence_note: Revised occasionally rather than on a cadence — s.10(2) of the Act: 'The Board may at any time revise the Code'. Edition 2.1 is the current text.

reports.title: Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007
reports.description: The Act that established the UK Statistics Authority as a non-ministerial department and set the statutory framework for UK official statistics, including the requirement at section 10 that the Board prepare, adopt and publish a Code of Practice for Statistics.

reports.title: Public Expenditure Statistical Analyses
reports.description: HM Treasury's annual accredited official statistics on UK government spending, bringing together recent outturn, estimates for the latest year and plans for the rest of the spending review period. It presents spending on both the budgeting framework (DEL/AME) and the Total Expenditure on Services framework, broken down by department, function, economic category and sector of government; chapters 9 and 10 carry the country and regional analysis. Outturn comes from the ONS public sector accounts and forward-year plans from the OBR's Economic and fiscal outlook.

reports.title: Country and regional analysis
reports.description: HM Treasury's annual statistical estimates allocating identifiable public sector expenditure between the four UK countries and the nine English regions. It is compiled from a data collection exercise across departments, devolved administrations, local authorities and public corporations, using a mix of actual regional spending and statistical apportionment on a 'who benefits' basis, and is presented within PESA as chapters 9 and 10.

reports.title: Country and regional public sector finances, UK
reports.description: An annual ONS release presenting public sector revenue, expenditure and net fiscal balance for each country of the UK and each region of England. It is distinct from the monthly Public sector finances bulletin: it takes the UK public sector finances as its control totals and apportions them to countries and regions using indicator datasets, HM Treasury's country and regional analysis being the main expenditure basis. It does not present debt or financial account data sub-nationally.

reports.title: Economic and fiscal outlook
reports.description: The Office for Budget Responsibility's five-year forecast for the UK economy and the public finances, presented to Parliament under section 8 of the Budget Responsibility and National Audit Act 2011. It covers the economic outlook, the fiscal outlook, the effects of announced government policy and the risks around the central forecast. What it must contain is set by the Charter for Budget Responsibility; the March 2026 edition was published on gov.uk by HM Treasury on the OBR's behalf.

reports.title: GDP quarterly national accounts, UK
reports.description: The ONS quarterly bulletin giving the third estimate of quarterly UK gross domestic product with the output, expenditure and income approaches balanced together, plus the quarterly sector accounts and real household disposable income per head. It is distinct from the annual UK National Accounts, The Blue Book, which is the point of annual reconciliation and supply-and-use balancing, and is compiled in line with ESA 2010.

reports.title: UK trade
reports.description: The ONS monthly bulletin on UK total trade in goods and services on a balance of payments basis, published about 40 days after the reference period. Trade is measured from over 30 sources, with HM Revenue and Customs the largest source for trade in goods at over 90% of its value; trade in services draws on ONS surveys including the International Trade in Services Survey and the International Passenger Survey.

reports.title: UK overseas trade in goods statistics
reports.description: HMRC's monthly accredited official statistics on UK trade in goods, giving aggregated and detailed data for over 9,500 commodities and around 200 partner countries. They are compiled on an International Merchandise Trade Statistics basis from customs declarations and, for Northern Ireland-EU movements, the Intrastat survey, and are the component ONS adjusts to produce trade in goods on a balance of payments basis.

reports.title: Budget Responsibility and National Audit Act 2011
reports.description: The Act that establishes the Office for Budget Responsibility and sets its main duty, to examine and report on the sustainability of the public finances. Section 4 requires the Office to prepare fiscal and economic forecasts on at least two occasions each financial year and, at least annually, an assessment of the fiscal mandate, an assessment of the accuracy of its previous forecasts and an analysis of fiscal sustainability. It also requires the Charter for Budget Responsibility.

reports.title: Charter for Budget Responsibility
reports.description: The Charter setting out the UK government's approach to fiscal policy and management of the public finances, including its fiscal objectives, the fiscal rules that deliver them and how the Office for Budget Responsibility operates in relation to them. It is required by the Budget Responsibility and National Audit Act 2011 as amended by the Budget Responsibility Act 2024, and is approved by Parliament; it determines what each Economic and fiscal outlook must contain.
reports.cadence_note: Revised occasionally rather than on a cadence, and approved by Parliament each time. The Autumn 2025 update changed the frequency at which the OBR assesses performance against the fiscal rules.

reports.title: Average weekly earnings
reports.description: The lead monthly measure of average weekly earnings per employee in Great Britain, published as the 'Average weekly earnings in Great Britain' bulletin and as the EARN datasets. AWE is the ratio of estimated total pay for the whole economy to the total number of employees, calculated from the Monthly Wages and Salaries Survey, whose sample is drawn from the Inter-Departmental Business Register; pay for employees of businesses below the MWSS size threshold is estimated from the Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings. Published for total pay and regular pay, and in real terms deflated by consumer price inflation. Excludes the self-employed, HM armed forces and government-supported trainees.

reports.title: Workforce jobs
reports.description: The quarterly measure of the number of jobs in the UK and ONS's preferred measure of short-term employment change by industry, published as the workforce jobs element of the 'Vacancies and jobs in the UK' bulletin and as the JOBS datasets. WFJ is the sum of employee jobs, self-employment jobs, government-supported trainees and HM forces. Employee jobs come from the Quarterly Business Survey and the Quarterly Public Sector Employment Survey and are benchmarked annually to the Business Register and Employment Survey; self-employment jobs and the England government-supported-trainee component come from the Labour Force Survey; the public-sector boundary is the one defined by the UK National Accounts.

reports.title: Inter-Departmental Business Register
reports.description: The comprehensive list of UK businesses used across government for statistical purposes, and the main sampling frame for business surveys run by ONS and other departments. Its two main inputs are VAT and PAYE records from HMRC, supplemented by Companies House, Dun and Bradstreet and ONS business surveys; it covers around 2.7 million businesses, and because the two tax sources have thresholds, very small businesses below them are generally not included. ONS states it is fully compliant with EC Regulation No 177/2008 on the harmonisation of business registers for statistical purposes.
reports.cadence_note: A continuously maintained register rather than a periodic release; releases_per_year is nominal, so that its absence would keep meaning 'one-off' (types.ts). ONS publishes from it annually — 'UK Business: Activity, Size and Location' and 'Business Demography' — alongside a data analysis service and a disclosive-microdata route through the Microdata Release Panel.

reports.title: Price Paid Data
reports.description: HM Land Registry's dataset of all property sales in England and Wales sold for value and lodged for registration, published in text and CSV form under the Open Government Licence and updated on the 20th working day of each month. It carries address data processed against Ordnance Survey's AddressBase Premium, and is the price source the UK House Price Index is built from.
reports.cadence_note: HM Land Registry: 'We update the data on the 20th working day of each month.'

reports.title: UK House Price Index
reports.description: The monthly index of residential property price change for the UK, produced from administrative land-registration records rather than a survey and published by HM Land Registry on behalf of a joint production with Registers of Scotland, Land & Property Services Northern Ireland and ONS. It combines price data with property-attribute data in a hedonic regression model, with the attributes for England and Wales taken from the Valuation Office Agency's Council Tax Valuation List. Data run from 1995 for England and Wales, 2004 for Scotland and 2005 for Northern Ireland. ONS places house prices outside the scope of consumer price inflation, so this index is not a CPIH input.

reports.title: Price Index of Private Rents
reports.description: The monthly measure of private rental price inflation across the whole privately rented stock, new and existing tenancies, published in the 'Private rent and house prices, UK' bulletin from March 2024 and extended to the whole UK from March 2025. It replaced the Index of Private Housing Rental Prices, ONS's lead measure of rental price change before that. It is built from administrative rental data collected by Rent Officers at the HMRC Valuation Office, the Scottish and Welsh Governments and the Northern Ireland Housing Executive, and the same rental data construct the owner-occupiers' housing costs component of CPIH under the rental equivalence approach.
title_aliases: Index of Private Housing Rental Prices

reports.title: Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings
reports.description: The annual survey of the levels, distribution and make-up of employee earnings and paid hours in the UK, published as the 'Employee earnings in the UK' bulletin. It is based on a 1% random sample of employee jobs drawn from HMRC Pay As You Earn records, with employers supplying the earnings and hours information; the drawn sample is matched against the Inter-Departmental Business Register for employer contact details, and returned data are weighted to UK population totals from the Labour Force Survey. It does not cover the self-employed or employees not paid in the reference period.

reports.title: Business Register and Employment Survey
reports.description: The annual business survey giving employee and employment estimates at detailed industrial and geographical levels, which ONS regards as the definitive source of official employee statistics by industry. Its sample of roughly 87,000 businesses is drawn from the Inter-Departmental Business Register, stratified by SIC 2007, country and register employment size; NISRA collects the same information independently in Northern Ireland and the two are combined for UK estimates. BRES results are also fed back to update the employment data held on the IDBR.
