reports.title: UK Shared Prosperity Fund: prospectus and allocations
reports.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
reports.description: The prospectus, technical notes and per-authority allocations for the £2.6 billion UK Shared Prosperity Fund, the UK government's domestic successor to EU structural funding, allocated to lead local authorities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. The ministerial foreword states, VERIFIED DIRECTLY (gov.uk, 2026-08-07): 'This is our vision and ambition for the new £2.6 billion UK Shared Prosperity Fund (UKSPF), which succeeds the old EU structural funds.' The companion FAQ, same publication series, holds the other framing of the same relationship, also VERIFIED DIRECTLY: 'The UKSPF is not a direct replacement for EU structural funds.' Both quotes are current gov.uk text and the conflict is recorded rather than adjudicated, per this project's convention.
reports.cadence_note: First published 13 April 2022 as a prospectus; maintained as a recurring release rather than a one-off. The gov.uk publication's own update history (read 2026-08-07) shows nine dated updates through 17 December 2025, including '13 December 2024: Added 2025-26 Technical Note and allocations documents', '4 March 2025: Added 2025-26 additional information and indicators' and '17 December 2025: Updated sections on expenditure deadline extension' — an annual technical-note/allocations rhythm plus in-year amendments. Publisher shown on gov.uk as MHCLG together with its predecessor name, Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities, which published the 2022 original. Nine dated updates 2022-2025 (~2 a year), including annual technical-note and allocations additions; treated as the release rate since the page is the publication.

release_schedule.note: The UK Shared Prosperity Fund itself closes on 31 March 2026 (no UKSPF funding for activity after that date; project activity must complete by 30 September 2026). From 1 April 2026 it is being replaced by two new programmes — the Pride in Place Programme and the Local Growth Fund (see Fundability.org.uk analysis and feweek.co.uk 'Fewer share prosperity when UKSPF ends in March'). The gov.uk prospectus page's update history (verified 2026-08-11) still shows its most recent update as 17 December 2025 (expenditure deadline extension), consistent with the corpus's existing cadence_note describing an annual technical-note/allocations rhythm through 2025-26. However, since the fund itself is winding down with no 2026-27 allocations cycle announced, there is no basis to project a further recurring update to this specific page going forward — reclassifying from an assumed continuing ~2/year cadence to irregular/terminal is warranted, though the existing releases_per_year=2 and cadence_note remain a defensible description of 2022-2025 history and are not being flagged as an error since they describe the past record, not a forward guarantee.

reports.title: Common Provisions Regulation (EU) No 1303/2013 (ERDF, ESF, Cohesion Fund, EAFRD, EMFF)
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: The framework regulation for the 2014-2020 European Structural and Investment Funds — the instrument that constitutes 'the Structural Funds' the UKSPF succeeded in the UK. Full title, VERIFIED DIRECTLY (legislation.gov.uk, 2026-08-07): 'Regulation (EU) No 1303/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 December 2013 laying down common provisions on the European Regional Development Fund, the European Social Fund, the Cohesion Fund, the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development and the European Maritime and Fisheries Fund and laying down general provisions on the European Regional Development Fund, the European Social Fund, the Cohesion Fund and the European Maritime and Fisheries Fund and repealing Council Regulation (EC) No 1083/2006.' Article 1 as adopted, VERIFIED DIRECTLY, defines the term this case turns on: Part Three 'lays down the general rules governing the ERDF, the ESF (together referred to as the "Structural Funds")'. NOTE ON SOURCE: verified from legislation.gov.uk's retained-EU-law copy (whose current revised text is amended post-Brexit — the as-adopted version carries the original Article 1); EUR-Lex, the canonical publisher, was unreachable through this session's fetch proxy (persistent HTTP 429) — see _dropped.
reports.cadence_note: Consolidated regulation, re-made each seven-year Multiannual Financial Framework programming period — Council Regulation (EC) No 1083/2006 (2007-2013, repealed by this instrument's own title), Regulation (EU) No 1303/2013 (2014-2020), Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 (2021-2027) — and amended within-period (legislation.gov.uk shows the retained copy last modified 29 July 2025, revised as of 29 December 2020). Modelled at the per-programming-cycle rate, the same convention as other versioned framework instruments in this corpus. 1303/2013 rather than 2021/1060 is the correct target here because the UK left the framework under the 2014-2020 cycle: it is the ERDF/ESF programmes under this regulation that the UKSPF succeeded.

release_schedule.note: Confirmed via legislation.gov.uk (fetched 2026-08-11): Regulation (EU) No 1303/2013 remains in force, last modified 29 July 2025, 'up to date with all changes known to be in force on or before 11 August 2026'. It has no calendar or stated periodic-release rule of its own -- it is a one-time consolidated instrument for the 2014-2020 MFF cycle that gets amended irregularly (Article 151 'Review' provision exists but specifies no fixed date). It was already superseded for its own programming cycle by Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 (2021-2027 MFF), so there is no further future 'next edition' of 1303/2013 itself to compute a date for -- the existing cadence_note's per-cycle framing (releases_per_year 0.14) is a reasonable modeling convention for the corpus but does not correspond to an actual upcoming publication event for this specific instrument. No source states or implies a concrete next release/amendment date, so 'irregular' (empty entries) is the accurate classification rather than a fabricated stated-rule date.

relations.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY by the minting session (2026-08-07, all four documents WebFetched live), converting the `no-node-yet` entry in uk-local-government-finance.json's `_dropped` array on the day the project owner decided the case. THE OPERATIVE QUOTE, the UKSPF prospectus's ministerial foreword: 'This is our vision and ambition for the new £2.6 billion UK Shared Prosperity Fund (UKSPF), which succeeds the old EU structural funds.' The prospectus body corroborates continuity in its allocation method ('This ensures that all places get an allocation that allows for significant continuity with EU structural funds') and names the ESF directly ('Lead local authorities should take account of the Adult Education Budget and remaining European Social Fund investments, which operate at larger geographies'). THE RECORDED CONFLICT, unchanged and still live on gov.uk (FAQ, same publication, updated 17 December 2025, re-verified this session): 'The UKSPF is not a direct replacement for EU structural funds.' Two primary UK-government documents in the same publication series hold different framings of the same relationship; per this project's convention the conflict is reported, not adjudicated — 'succeeds' (the foreword's word, and this schema's relation_type) asserts temporal succession, which both documents are compatible with; 'not a direct replacement' denies equivalence of design, which this relation does not assert. WHY THE TARGET IS REGULATION 1303/2013: neither gov.uk document names ERDF or ESF as the predecessor programmes, but two council documents, both previously subagent-read only and both RE-VERIFIED FIRST-HAND this session, do. Orkney Islands Council, Policy and Resources Committee, 'Replacement of Previous EU Structural Funding', 20 September 2022 (https://www.orkney.gov.uk/media/gyfbbbcr/item-20-replacement-of-previous-eu-structural-funding.pdf): 'The UK Shared Prosperity Fund, alongside the Levelling up Fund (LUF), is intended to replace EU funding provided through the European structural and investment funds, namely European Regional Development Fund (ERDF), and European Social Fund (ESF).' North East Lincolnshire Council, 'Council to submit investment plan to Government', 21 July 2022 (https://www.nelincs.gov.uk/council-to-submit-investment-plan-to-government/): 'The UKSPF is allocated to local authorities to replace the "European Structural Funds" programmes, ERDF and ESIF which this area has previously benefited from.' Regulation (EU) No 1303/2013's Article 1 as adopted is the instrument that defines exactly those two programmes as the term the foreword uses — the ERDF and 'the ESF (together referred to as the "Structural Funds")' — and it governed the 2014-2020 programmes still winding down in the UK when the UKSPF launched. The council documents are corroboration inside this basis rather than edges of their own: neither is a corpus node, and 'replaces' is not a dependency.

reports.title: Strategy Paper on Index-Linking LEAP Benefits to Inflation
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance (Ghana), with the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (direct fetch of the strategy paper itself). States the indexation formula precisely: 'LB_t+1 = LB_t(1 + inf_t)' where inf_t is 'the 12-month annual average inflation from October of previous year to September of current year estimated from Ghana Statistical Service (GSS) Consumer Price Index release', with annual adjustments 'capped at 50%'. States the mechanism 'will be backed by legislation to enhance its effectiveness and continuity... through the proposed Social Protection Bill' -- a forward reference to an unnamed future bill, not a citation of Act 1148 by number (Act 1148 did not yet exist). On funding: 'The primary source of funding the LEAP Programme should be GoG resources. However, opportunities for alternative funding support, particularly from development partners, should be identified and explored.' Cites the World Bank's Social Protection Public Expenditure Review as a data source for its own figures. Independently corroborated as actually implemented (not merely proposed) by Ghana's Graphic Online, reporting the mechanism 'will take effect from this month to enable an automatic adjustment of grants', introduced through 'collaborative work between the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP), and the Ministry of Finance (MoF), after increasing the allowances paid to beneficiaries by 100 per cent in 2023', with a further GH₵720 million committed in the 2024 budget for an additional 12% increase.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (Ghana Statistical Service)
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via GSS's own CPI Technical Methodology Manual (v5, published October 2020) and its own recent press releases. The v5 manual: 'GSS uses 13 out of the 15 Divisions as distinguished by the COICOP manual', organised into '44 Groups, 98 Classes, 156 Subclasses, and 307 Item-level observations', and 'to order products into these different categories, GSS uses the United Nations Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018 manual.' Elementary aggregates: 'GSS uses the unweighted Jevons Index... the geometric mean of price relatives.' The v5 manual describes the then-current series on 'the whole year of 2018 as the price reference period' with 'weights based on the Ghana Living Standard Surveys 7 (GLSS7) from 2016/2017', and credits input from 'Statistics Denmark, and the International Monetary Fund (IMF)' plus ILO CPI-manual guidance. GSS has since rebased: the September 2025 press release (published 1 October 2025) states 'the price reference period has been updated to 2021 (2021=100)' with the weight reference period still 2017 -- confirmed independently, distinct from and more current than the v5 manual's own 2018=100 description. The rebase's own dedicated methodology note (as opposed to a press-release mention) was not located this session.

release_schedule.note: GSS publishes CPI/inflation monthly, consistently in 'Week 1' (occasionally week 2) of the month following the reference month. Observed 2026 releases: May 2026 CPI released ~June 4, 2026; June 2026 CPI released July 1, 2026; July 2026 CPI released Aug 6-7, 2026 (inflation 4.6%). GSS's own 2025 Statistical Product Release Calendar PDF confirms CPI is scheduled in Week 1 (or Week 2) of each month, but states the calendar 'will be updated quarterly' and no 2026 edition with exact dates was found online, so the September 2026 (for August 2026 data) date is inferred from the pattern rather than a published calendar entry.

reports.title: Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP)
reports.description: Ghana's flagship cash-transfer programme. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via MoGCSP's own LEAP background page: established under Ghana's Growth and Poverty Reduction Strategy II (GPRS II), 'first disbursement in March 2008 to 1,654 pilot households across 21 districts.' Now indexed to inflation via the mechanism described in gh-mofep-leap-indexation-strategy, per Graphic Online's reporting that the indexation mechanism 'took effect' following the 2023 strategy paper. Development-partner support (World Bank, UNICEF, UK Government/FCDO) is acknowledged on the programme's own page without a stated funding split; see gh-gpsnp2-worldbank for the current primary World Bank financing instrument and its own stated split (GoG now the larger share).

reports.title: Social Protection Act, 2025 (Act 1148)
reports.description: Ghana's framework social-protection statute. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session against judy.legal's hosted text (an Akoma Ntoso-identified official-text mirror, the same convention used by Kenya Law for ke-social-protection-act-2025) and independently corroborated by the import's round: passed by Parliament 31 July 2025, 'assented to on 14 August 2025' and 'commenced on 14 August 2025' as Act 1148. Section 1 (Application) covers 'chronically poor', 'economically at-risk', 'socially vulnerable', and persons 'affected by a national or a local emergency'. Section 2 (Object): to 'reduce poverty and vulnerability', 'promote the well-being' of those groups, and foster 'sustainable livelihoods and decent work'. Secondary reporting (MoGCSP, news coverage) states the Act establishes a Social Protection Fund and explicitly covers LEAP and the Ghana School Feeding Programme by name, but the free public preview only exposes Sections 1-2 -- no operative indexation clause was independently readable. The implementing Legislative Instrument (LI) was, per MoGCSP, submitted to Parliament and expected in force by June 2026. See gh-mofep-leap-indexation-strategy for the earlier (2023) formula this Act may or may not put on statutory footing, and _note for why no edge connects the two documents.

reports.title: Ghana Productive Safety Net Project 2 (GPSNP2)
reports.description: The World Bank/IDA project currently financing LEAP, effective January 2022. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session, quoting the project's own text: development objective 'to expand and enhance social safety nets that improve the incomes and productivity of the poor in Ghana.' Component 3 'supports the continuation, expansion, and strengthening of the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) program through increased coverage, improved targeting, higher benefit levels, and enhanced capacity of decentralized implementation structures', delivering 'bimonthly cash transfers to poor households using digital payment systems and targeting based on the Ghana National Household Registry data.' Financing: IDA credit US$100.0 million, Government of Ghana counterpart US$157.0 million; Component 3 (LEAP) specifically allocated US$177 million total (US$20 million IDA, US$157 million GoG) -- i.e. Ghana's own government is now the majority funder of the LEAP component, distinct from the earlier Ghana Social Opportunities Project and first GPSNP (2010s), which per the import's round carried GBP 21 million in FCDO co-financing. This is the direct evidentiary counterpart to Ethiopia's SEASN/PSNP5 project financing (et-psnp5-worldbank-seasn), confirming a comparable donor-financing-instrument-names-the-programme-it-funds shape for a second country in this branch.

reports.title: SSNIT Pension Indexation Rate (annual review and announcement)
reports.publisher: Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT)
reports.description: SSNIT's annual review of pensions in payment, published as a dedicated press release each year. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via SSNIT's own 2025 Pension Indexation Rate press release, which cites its legal basis as 'Section 80 of the National Pensions Act, 2008 (Act 766)' and quotes the statutory standard: 'The Trust shall annually review the pension payment which shall be indexed to wage inflation rates of active contributors or another rate determined by the Trust in consultation with the Board of the Authority.' The same press release lists the factors SSNIT considered for the 2025 rate: 'Average salary of active contributors from the previous year', 'Annual average Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the previous year', 'Affordability and the impact of indexation on the cost of pensions to the Scheme', and 'The effect of indexation on the long-term sustainability of the Scheme' -- CPI is a named, explicit input but one of four, not a standalone formula; the statute's own default reference is wage inflation, with CPI and other factors used in the Trust's alternative-rate determination. Act 766's own text was not independently fetchable this session (the government registry copy blocks automated access); this description rests on SSNIT's own quotation of its governing section. the import's round adds an unverified-by-this-session 2026 example: an overall 10% indexation (fixed 6% plus a redistributed flat GH₵91.56), against SSNIT's own stated ~5.4% end-2025 inflation figure -- i.e. the review outcome is deliberately not a pure pass-through of CPI, consistent with the four-factor statutory language.

entries.covers: 2025 pension indexation rate announcement (announced Jan 6, 2025 at 12%)
2026 pension indexation rate announcement (announced Jan 8, 2026 at 10%)

release_schedule.note: SSNIT has no published release calendar or statutory fixed date for the indexation announcement, but it has consistently announced the new year's pension indexation rate (approved by its Board) in the first half of January each year: 2023 (Jan 13), 2024 (January), 2025 (Jan 6), 2026 (Jan 8). This is an observed annual pattern, not a stated rule, hence next occurrence is projected as January 2027.

reports.title: District Assemblies Common Fund — 2026 Allocation (under the 2026 Appropriation Act)
reports.description: Verbatim: "The total allocation to the Fund for the 2026 fiscal year is based on five per cent of the projected total revenue for the year," totaling GHC8,769,707,900 (up from a prior allocation, per the Herald's own headline framing it as a raise). reports.title: Auditor General's Report on Kanifing Municipal Council Financial Statements (Period Ended 1 April 2017 to 31 December 2019)
reports.description: The National Audit Office (Gambia)'s Auditor-General's report on Kanifing Municipal Council's financial statements for the period 1 April 2017 to 31 December 2019, transmitted 3 December 2020 (Ref: HC 93/475/01/PART IV(11), signed by Bakary Trawally, For: Auditor General, copied to the Permanent Secretaries of the Ministry of Local Government and Lands and the Ministry of Finance). States KMC's governing accountability framework: "Management is responsible for the preparation and fair presentation of these financial statements in accordance with Local Government Finance and Audit Act, 2004, Financial and Accounting Manual For Local Government Authorities Chapter 9 on cash basis, and for such internal control as management determines is necessary..." — the first of two independent primary confirmations found this round that a distinct "Local Government Finance and Audit Act, 2004" exists and governs municipal financial accountability, the law anticipated (but not enacted) by the 2002 Local Government Act's own Section 130: "The financial affairs of a Council shall be regulated in accordance with a Local Government (Finance and Audit) law to be enacted by the National Assembly." A companion passage names the fuller compliance stack: financial statements must comply "with the provisions of the Government Budget Management and Accountability Act, Financial and Accounting Manual for Local Government Authorities, Local Government Act, and the Finance and Audit Act." The audited Revenue and Expenditure Statement for FY2019 (with FY2018 comparatives) records Total Revenue of D180,415,062 (2019) vs D142,473,020 (2018), broken into Licences, Taxes, Rents & Fees, Rates, Other Income, and Interest and Dividend; Note 5 ("Other Income") itemizes a "Grants And Subventions - Government" line of D500,000.00 for 2019 versus D2,317,300.00 for 2018 — a documented, audited, named-council-specific central-government transfer figure, though the year-on-year decline is stark. CAVEAT (OCR): the source PDF has no embedded text layer (pdftotext returned zero characters; it is a set of 150dpi scanned-image pages per pdfimages) — all quotes above were extracted via local OCR (tesseract) rather than standard text extraction, and should be treated as OCR-derived, not directly machine-extracted, text. CAVEAT (audit opinion): NAO issued an overall Adverse Opinion on KMC's FY2019 financial statements due to unrelated unexplained balances (accumulated funds, suspense account, etc.), so the underlying financials should be treated as officially contested/unreliable in aggregate even though the specific quoted lines are as NAO itself published them.

reports.title: Ley Fundamental de Guinea Ecuatorial (Constitución)
reports.publisher: República de Guinea Ecuatorial (official constitutional text, hosted by FAOLEX)
reports.description: Equatorial Guinea's constitution. Artículo 3, apartados 4-5: "4. Se divide para los fines administrativos y económicos en Regiones, Provincias, Distritos y Municipios. 5. La ley determina los límites y las denominaciones de las regiones, provincias, distritos y municipios." Título Cuarto, "De las Corporaciones Locales," Artículo 131: "Las Corporaciones Locales son instituciones con personalidad jurídica propia, encargadas del gobierno y administración de las regiones, provincias, distritos y municipios. Promueven los planes y programas de desarrollo económico y social de sus respectivos territorios de acuerdo a la ley." Artículo 132.2: "La ley determina las competencias, el funcionamiento, la jurisdicción y la composición de las Corporaciones Locales." The Constitution itself establishes Municipios as one of four administrative/economic-division tiers and gives Corporaciones Locales legal personality, but explicitly delegates all finance/competency detail to ordinary law rather than stating a mechanism itself — the implementing law is Ley Número 1/2003 (see gq-ley-1-2003-administracion-local). Independently downloaded and text-extracted via pdftotext, not AI-summarized. Equatorial Guinea's official BOE portal (boe.gob.gq) could not be reached this round (503 Service Unavailable) to cross-verify against a more-authoritative host; the FAOLEX copy was used and is treated as reliable.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument (a constitution).

reports.title: Ley Número 1/2003, de fecha 28 de Febrero, Reguladora de la Administración Local
reports.publisher: República de Guinea Ecuatorial — Boletín Oficial del Estado / Presidencia del Gobierno de Guinea Ecuatorial
reports.description:
UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF lead-chase round, gq-leadchase-finance-tax.json): the "Ley 1/2013" variant flagged as an unresolved discrepancy below is now confirmed an ERRONEOUS alternate citation, not a genuinely distinct law. FAOLEX's own hosted primary-source PDF (independently downloaded and pdftotext-verified this round; same URL already cited as this node's evidence) gives the title page as "ley Núm. 1/2.003, de fecha 28 de Febrero, Reguladora de la Administración Local," and its own Exposición de Motivos names the law it reforms as "la Ley Núm. 12/1.984, de fecha 20 de junio, Reguladora de la Administración Local" — both readings consistent with 2003, neither with 2013. No primary source (government-hosted or FAOLEX) supports a 2013 enactment date for this title; guineaecuatorialpress.com's "Ley Número 1/2013" citation (see the unresolved-discrepancy note retained below) is treated as a secondary-source transcription error rather than evidence of a distinct law. The corpus keeps this node as "Ley 1/2003" — no ID rename, since renaming would break existing edges. Original entry follows.

The organic law implementing the Constitution's Artículo 132.2 delegation, and the primary text establishing Equatorial Guinea's municipal finance categories. Título Cuarto "De los Ingresos Municipales," Capítulo Primero, Artículo 241.1: "La Hacienda de los Municipios estará constituida por los siguientes recursos: a) Los productos de su patrimonio, b) El rendimiento de servicios y explotaciones, ... d) Las exacciones municipales, y e) Las participaciones en impuestos estatales o de ingresos mediante transferencias directas a los Municipios." Item (e) explicitly names direct state-to-municipality transfers as a legally recognized municipal revenue category, though no percentage or formula is specified anywhere in the readable text (unlike comparable Mozambique/Angola precedents already in this corpus). Artículo 242-243 establishes a further, sub-municipal fiscal tier: "La Hacienda de los Consejos de Poblados se formará con [los] recursos a que se refieren los apartados a), b) y c) del artículo 241 anterior, en cuanto se aprueben con pertenencia privativa y, además, con la participación en los conceptos que constituyen la imposición municipal, en la cuantía necesaria para atender los servicios que sostengan, en caso de que no los preste el Municipio respectivo." Independently downloaded and pdftotext-extracted (scanned/OCR'd Boletín Oficial del Estado document; OCR is noisy in places — item (c) of Art. 241 is garbled beyond legibility and was not quoted). The law's own Exposición de Motivos states it reforms an earlier "Ley Núm. 12/1.984, de fecha 20 de junio, Reguladora de la Administración Local" — not independently located this round. A later government-portal reference (guineaecuatorialpress.com, 23 June 2017) names an amending law, "Ley Número 5/2017," as modifying a "Ley Número 1/2013, de fecha 28 de febrero, reguladora de la administración local" — same day/month as this 2003 law but a different year, and its own primary text was not located this round. This is a genuine unresolved discrepancy, flagged rather than force-reconciled (see _dropped).
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational/organic law.

reports.title: Ley Nº 6/2012, de fecha 15 de noviembre, por la que se reforma la Ley número 3/1.990, de fecha 15 de mayo, sobre las Entidades Locales Menores en la República de Guinea Ecuatorial
reports.publisher: República de Guinea Ecuatorial — Boletín Oficial del Estado / Presidencia del Gobierno
reports.description: Confirms Consejos de Poblado — the below-municipio local entities also referenced in Ley 1/2003's Artículo 242-243 — draft and approve their own budgets: "d) Elaborar y aprobar los presupuestos de ingresos y gastos del Consejo de Poblado. e) Acordar los créditos necesarios que deben solicitarse del Gobierno y demás instituciones financieras, para la promoción vecinal." A second passage in the same law states that appeals involving "obligaciones económicas o financieras... con cargo a los presupuestos nacionales o municipales" [economic or financial obligations charged to national or municipal budgets] are excepted from a default-approval rule requiring Ministerial sign-off — confirming these entities' spending is charged against national OR municipal budgets rather than an independent local tax base. Independently downloaded via FAOLEX and pdftotext-extracted; OCR quality fair-to-poor in places (the cover page itself gives the law's date inconsistently as both "15 de noviembre" and "16 de Noviembre"), and the quotes above are drawn only from clearly legible passages.

reports.title: Ley Número 8/2022, de fecha 13 de octubre, de los Presupuestos Generales del Estado para el Ejercicio Económico 2023 (LPGE 2023)
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Hacienda, Economía y Planificación — Dirección General de Presupuestos y Contabilidad Pública, República de Guinea Ecuatorial
reports.description: Equatorial Guinea's annual national budget law, and the primary document that actually funds and reports on the municipal tier the Ley Fundamental and Ley 1/2003 only frame. Its own Exposición de Motivos, Sección I, states: "Los Presupuestos Generales del Estado para el Ejercicio Económico 2023 han sido elaborado teniendo en cuenta la Ley Fundamental de Guinea Ecuatorial, la Ley de Finanzas Públicas, la Ley Tributaria, la Agenda Guinea Ecuatorial 2035 y el Decreto 136/2019 por el que se adopta el Memorándum sobre Políticas Económicas y Financieras, resultante de las negociaciones entre el Gobierno y el FMI," and separately names "la estrategia de ajuste regional de la CEMAC" and "las Recomendaciones del FMI en el marco de la Misión del Artículo IV de 2022" as framework inputs. Artículo 32, "Sección 15 - Interior y Corporaciones Locales," appropriates named local-government lines: "64212 Corporaciones Locales ... 2.500.000.000 [FCFA] / 64212 Municipios de Nueva Creación y Distritos Urbanos ... 250.000.000 / 64221 Gobiernos locales ... 1.185.000.000, De los cuales, Apoyo a los Jefes Tradicionales, Consejos de Poblados y Comunidad de Vecinos 600.000.000" (the disaggregated account-code table elsewhere in the same document confirms the correct codes are 64211 for Corporaciones Locales and 64212 for Municipios de Nueva Creación y Distritos Urbanos — the Article-32 summary table appears to duplicate "64212" for both lines as a transcription typo). Anexo VIII, "Escala y Complementos Salariales 2023," table "CONCEJALES AYUNTAMIENTOS," sets a national, centrally-funded six-tier municipal councillor salary scale by category — e.g. "5ª.- Municipios. 100 000 [FCFA/mes] 146 [concejales] 14 600 000 [total mensual] 204 400 000 [total anual]" — for 506 councillors nationwide (1,075,200,000 FCFA/year total), unambiguous primary evidence that municipal councillor compensation is entirely centrally funded and set by category rather than locally budgeted. The same Anexo also sets named-location civil-servant salary supplements ("COMPLEMENTO DE DESTINO") by provincial capital and district — e.g. "ANNOBON 150 000 ... MALABO 60 000 ... BATA 70 000 ... RIABA 90 000" — across 6 provincial capitals and 13 districts. A further detailed table in the Ministerio del Interior section breaks out operating allocations by named province/region column (Wele-Nzas, Kie-Ntem, Centro Sur, Djibloho, etc.) alongside a specific Corporaciones Locales column. Independently downloaded via curl (not WebFetch) and pdftotext-extracted, 285 pages, full text searched.
reports.cadence_note: Annual national budget law; this is the Ejercicio Económico 2023 edition. A later LPGE 2026 draft (ahoraeg.com) was located in secondary search but not independently downloaded/full-text-searched this round.

_slice: City of Grande Prairie — the municipal template
_note: The first genuinely municipal nodes in the graph. Grande Prairie is mapped in full rather than broadly because the point is the pattern: budget, tax rate bylaw, assessment, municipal census, audited financial statements and the FIR filing are the same six documents in every Alberta municipality, published under the same statute. Establishing the shape here is what makes the other ~330 a replication job with per-instance URL verification, rather than 330 separate research problems. The tax rate bylaw is the keystone — by statute it must state the assessment it levies against and the requisitions it collects on behalf of others, so it names its own inputs in a way most municipal documents do not.

reports.title: Property Tax Bylaw (Rates of Taxation)
reports.description: Annual bylaw setting the mill rate for each property class, passed under section 353 of the Municipal Government Act. States the assessment base it levies against and every requisition it collects on behalf of another body — the Alberta School Foundation Fund, opted-out school boards, the seniors housing management body and the designated industrial property requisition.

entries.covers: 2027 Property Tax Bylaw (Rates of Taxation / Mill Rate) adoption

release_schedule.rule: Each year, Council sets the Mill rates (tax rates) in late April or early May to meet our community's needs.
release_schedule.note: The City adopts a new Property Tax Bylaw annually via Council resolution, historically in late April or early May (e.g., Bylaw C-1460 in May 2023, C-1473 in May 2024, C-1493 adopted May 11, 2026). No fixed calendar date is published; the exact adoption date varies year to year within that window based on Council's meeting schedule and budget finalization.

reports.title: City Budget Report
reports.description: Annual operating and capital budget, adopted as the detailed estimates of revenue and expenditure that the tax rate bylaw is then set to fund. Names its population and demographic sources, its provincial and federal capital grant amounts, and the inflation measure it benchmarks spending against.

entries.covers: 2025 Budget ratified at Dec 2, 2024 Council meeting
2026 Operating & Capital Budget approved at Dec 8, 2025 Council meeting
2027 Budget Report, expected approval by Council

release_schedule.note: No published budget calendar or statutory fixed date was found on cityofgp.com. Observed pattern: City Council approves/ratifies the annual Budget Report (Operating + Capital) at a Council meeting in early December of the year preceding the budget year (e.g., 2025 Budget ratified Dec 2, 2024; 2026 Budget approved Dec 8, 2025), and the Budget Report PDF is published to cityofgp.com around the same time. Council also gives 'in principle' approval to multi-year budgets (e.g., 2027-2029 Operating Budget was given preliminary approval alongside the Dec 8, 2025 2026 budget approval), but the report itself is finalized/republished annually in December.

reports.title: Municipal Census
reports.description: Municipal population count conducted under the Municipal Government Act, giving population, private dwellings and median age between federal census years. Run at the municipality's discretion rather than on a fixed cycle; Grande Prairie's most recent was 2024.
reports.cadence_note: Not annual. Conducted at the city's discretion — 2024 was the most recent. The enum has no bucket for an irregular multi-year count; releases_per_year carries the truth.

release_schedule.note: City of Grande Prairie conducts a municipal census only when Council directs it (e.g., to support provincial/federal funding claims), not on a fixed cycle. Confirmed census years found: 2016, 2018, and 2024 (a 2-year gap followed by a 6-year gap), with no census found in 2019 or 2021 (Wikipedia's list of 2019 and 2021 Alberta municipal censuses does not include Grande Prairie). No calendar or stated statutory rule for timing was found on cityofgp.com; Alberta's Municipal Government Act allows but does not require municipalities to conduct their own census at intervals of the municipality's choosing. As of 2026-08-11, no announcement of a next census date was found.

reports.title: Property Assessment Roll
reports.description: Annual valuation of every assessable property in the city, prepared under the Municipal Government Act and mailed to owners as assessment notices in the first week of March. Reassessed annually to track market movement; each property inspected on roughly a five-year cycle. The base every property tax rate in the city is levied against, and the data the province audits to set the equalized assessment.

release_schedule.rule: Assessment Notices are typically mailed out the first week of March every year.
release_schedule.note: Publisher states notices are 'typically' mailed the first week of March; exact date varies year to year and no dated calendar is published. The 2026 mailing (first week of March 2026) has already passed relative to today (2026-08-11), so the computed next entry rolls forward to the first week of March 2027.

reports.title: Consolidated Audited Financial Statements
reports.description: Annual audited statements of financial position, operations and cash flow, required of every Alberta municipality by the Municipal Government Act and due to Municipal Affairs by May 1. Reports the year's tax levy against the adopted budget and discloses each requisition collected on another body's behalf.

entries.covers: FY2026 (year ended December 31, 2026) Consolidated Audited Financial Statements

release_schedule.rule: The Municipal Government Act requires that each municipality prepare annual audited financial statements and a financial information return; both must be returned to Alberta Municipal Affairs by May 1 of each year (covering the fiscal year ended December 31 of the prior year).
release_schedule.note: In practice the City of Grande Prairie's Council has approved the statements shortly before the May 1 deadline (e.g., FY2024 statements posted to the city's website in May 2025; FY2025 statements were approved by Council on April 27, 2026, per council meeting highlights). The FY2025 statements are already released as of today (2026-08-11), so the next expected release is the FY2026 statements, due by May 1, 2027.

reports.title: Designated Industrial Property Requisition
reports.description: Annual provincial requisition recovering the cost of centrally assessing designated industrial property. The province assesses this class itself rather than leaving it to local assessors, and bills municipalities a rate against that assessment to fund the work.

entries.covers: 2027 Designated Industrial Property Requisition Tax Rate (Ministerial Order)

release_schedule.note: No published calendar or statutory deadline found; timing is governed by an annual Ministerial Order (Municipal Affairs) that sets the DIP tax rate/requisition for the year. Past orders were issued: MAG:005/23 on 2023-03-13, MAG:006/24 on 2024-03-25, MAG:004/25 on 2025-03-26, MAG:003/26 on 2026-03-27 (source: open.alberta.ca publication pages for each order, e.g. https://open.alberta.ca/publications/ma-mag-003-26). This is a consistent mid-to-late March pattern, not a stated rule. The 2026 order has already been issued as of the current date (2026-08-11), so the next expected instance is the 2027 order, projected for March 2027 based on the pattern; exact day is not predictable from public sources.

reports.title: Public Sector Accounting Standards (CPA Canada Public Sector Accounting Handbook)
reports.publisher: Public Sector Accounting Board, CPA Canada
reports.description: The accounting standards every Canadian government and government organisation prepares its financial statements under, set by the Public Sector Accounting Board and published in the CPA Canada Public Sector Accounting Handbook. Not a government body and not a statistical release — a standard that determines what the financial statements of every municipality, province and territory are permitted to say.
reports.cadence_note: The Handbook is amended continuously through exposure drafts and annual improvements rather than issued as a dated edition. Filed as annual because that is the rhythm at which preparers absorb changes.

release_schedule.note: Rolling agenda, but once a standard is finalized PSAB publishes a real mandatory effective date. The 2026-04-01 entry has already passed as of this audit; kept for context alongside the 2029 date.

dependencies.basis: Bylaw C-1486 recites that 'the City of Grande Prairie has prepared and adopted detailed estimates of the municipal revenue and expenditures as required' before setting any rate. The mill rate is the budget divided by the assessment base; the bylaw is the arithmetic of the budget landing on property.
dependencies.evidence_quote: the City of Grande Prairie has prepared and adopted detailed estimates of the municipal revenue and expenditures as required

dependencies.basis: Bylaw C-1486 authorises the Chief Administrative Officer 'to levy the following rates of taxation on the assessed value of all property as shown on the assessment roll of the City of Grande Prairie', then tabulates the assessment behind each class — $7.2 billion of low density residential, $2.96 billion non-residential, and so on.
dependencies.evidence_quote: to levy the following rates of taxation on the assessed value of all property as shown on the assessment roll of the City of Grande Prairie

dependencies.basis: Bylaw C-1486 levies a Designated Industrial Property Requisition of 0.0701 against $246,988,150 of assessment. The city collects it; the province sets it and keeps it.

Bylaw C-1486 levies a separate Alberta School Foundation Fund rate on residential and non-residential assessment, plus a matching rate for opted-out school boards. The city collects these amounts on the province's behalf; the requisition sets them.

The budget report's community profile attributes population, private dwellings and median age to the 2024 Municipal Census by name, and the per-capita spending metric Council is asked to judge the budget by is computed from that population.
The same community profile attributes median household income to the 2021 Federal Census by name. The municipal census does not collect income, so the federal one fills the gap.

Local Government Fiscal Framework funding appears as a named capital funding source in the 2026 budget at $8,401,000, 18.4% of the capital plan, and is carried forward at $8,317,000 a year across the five-year capital forecast. Named road rehabilitation programs are funded from it directly.

The budget benchmarks ten years of tax increases and per-capita spending against Alberta CPI, quoted at 25.9% cumulatively. Context for the fiscal argument rather than a computational input, hence a citation rather than a calculation.

Note 1 states plainly: 'Property tax revenues are based on property tax assessment values provided by the City of Grande Prairie.' The largest revenue line in the statements is the assessment roll multiplied by the rates.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Property tax revenues are based on property tax assessment values provided by the City of Grande Prairie.

dependencies.basis: Every statement of operations in the document carries a Budget column beside the actual — net municipal property taxes of $129,935,024 budgeted against $131,071,106 collected. The statements are in part a report card on the budget, so they carry it.

Schedule 3 nets the Alberta School Foundation Fund requisition of $30,181,579 out of gross property taxes to arrive at net municipal property taxes. The notes further explain that over-levies and under-levies against the requisition are accrued and corrected in the following year's requisition rates.

The auditor's report and note 1 both state the statements are prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards as established by the Public Sector Accounting Board. The standards decide what the statements are permitted to recognise, which is why this is a methodology dependency rather than a data one.
dependencies.evidence_quote: In our opinion, the accompanying consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the consolidated financial position of the City as at December 31, 2024, and the results of its consolidated operations, its consolidated remeasurement gains and losses, changes in its consolidated net financial assets and its consolidated cash flows for the year then ended in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards.

dependencies.basis: Municipal Affairs states that the Municipal Government Act requires each municipality to prepare both annual audited financial statements and a financial information return, both returned by May 1, and that 'the completed FIR should be submitted with the signed and dated copy of the audited financial statements'. The FIR is the same year's audited figures restated in the province's standard schedule.
dependencies.evidence_quote: the completed FIR should be submitted with the signed and dated copy of the audited financial statements

dependencies.basis: The Recording and Reporting Information for Assessment Audit and Equalized Assessment Manual describes an annual submission of data from municipalities to Municipal Affairs containing 'the information about every assessable property in the municipality for the purposes of conducting the annual audit and for determining the equalized assessment'. The province divides the municipality's taxable assessment by its audited assessment level to reach 100% of market value.
dependencies.evidence_quote: the information about every assessable property in the municipality for the purposes of conducting the annual audit and for determining the equalized assessment

dependencies.basis: The population list's own usage note: 'The information in the lists is based on municipal census results (Alberta municipalities may choose to conduct a census in any year) or federal census counts. Municipalities that choose to conduct a census are required to report the results to Municipal Affairs by September 1 of that year, and those results are reflected in the population lists.'

RESOLVED 2026-08-09 (cheap-check pass), and the node-rule question `G.63.md`'s secondary observations flagged is now answered: THE FUND IS NOT A NODE, and the edge as proposed cannot be minted -- but not for the reason the flag anticipated. The flag's worry was that a federal fund is a funding programme rather than a 'real, named, recurring official release', UNLESS it publishes its own periodic allocation report. It does publish one. 'Canada Community Building Fund Municipal Allocations' is a real dataset on open.canada.ca (dataset b61755fd-824b-469d-b75c-3448e31deb89), custodian the Department of Housing, Infrastructure and Communities, first published 2017-07-20, last updated 2026-03-29, maintenance frequency stated as "Annually", described as "funding allocations provided to municipalities under Infrastructure Canada's Canada Community Building Fund program". That is titled, cadenced and published -- it clears sec.4's point 2 and the cadence test outright. IT FAILS ON POINT 1, which is the binding one: no document read names it as an input. Grande Prairie's 2026 budget names the FUND as a capital revenue source at $5,160,000 -- the programme, not the allocation dataset. That is the same gap as `AGENCY ONLY` in a different key: naming the money's source is not citing a release. Minting `ccbf-municipal-allocations` off this budget line would be inventing the citation. So the entry closes as a `note` rather than staying an open lead: the edge is not blocked on research, it is not documented. `ccbf-municipal-allocations` remains a clean node CANDIDATE for whenever federal-to-municipal transfers are worked properly, at which point the question is which document cites it, not whether it qualifies. ONE FURTHER OBSERVATION, logged not pursued: Housing, Infrastructure and Communities Canada's own CCBF page states that provinces and territories must "report financial activities annually and outcomes/results every five years to Infrastructure Canada". Two real recurring reporting obligations with two real cadences and NO titles given for either -- textbook `AGENCY ONLY` under Research.1.md sec.6, and not minted for that reason. If a province's own CCBF report turns out to have a title, that is the better node and it would sit between this budget and the federal fund. ORIGINAL ENTRY BELOW. The 2026 budget names the Canada Community-Building Fund as a capital source at $5,160,000. The federal fund itself has not been researched as a node yet, so the edge has nothing to point at. Dropped for now rather than half-defined.

reports.title: Department of Statistics (DoS)

reports.title: Central Administration of Statistics (CAS)

reports.title: Central Statistical Bureau (CSB)

reports.title: Constituição da República da Guiné-Bissau — Capítulo VI, "Do Poder Local" (Artigos 105.º–118.º)
reports.description: Guinea-Bissau's constitutional chapter establishing the country's local-government tier, verified directly from the FAOLEX-hosted text (chapter heading notes "Nova redacção dada pela Lei Constitucional n°1/96"). Art. 105(1): "A organização do poder político do Estado compreende a existência das autarquias locais, que gozam de autonomia administrativa e financeira." Art. 106 defines the tier: "As autarquias locais são os municípios, secções autárquicas e juntas locais" and "Nos sectores funcionarão os municípios, nas secções administrativas funcionarão as secções autárquicas e nas juntas locais funcionarão as juntas de moradores" — i.e. municípios map 1:1 onto "sectores". Art. 107 sets the territorial hierarchy ("o território nacional divide-se em regiões, subdividindo-se estas em sectores e secções"), deferring "a organização e o funcionamento das regiões administrativas" to ordinary law. Art. 110 grants autarquias "património e finanças próprios" and states "o regime das finanças locais, a estabelecer por lei, deverá visar a justa repartição dos recursos públicos pelo Estado e pelas autarquias locais e a necessária correcção de desigualdades entre as autarquias" — a delegation clause with no numeric formula in the constitutional text itself. Art. 118 grants a further, separately delegated share: "As autarquias locais participam, por direito próprio e nos termos definidos pela lei, nas receitas provenientes dos impostos directos." The ordinary laws these articles delegate to (Lei 5/96, Lei 7/96, Lei 6/97) could not be retrieved in full text this round — see _dropped.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument; text as revised by Lei Constitucional n.º 1/96.

reports.title: Decreto n.º 6/2018 — Regulamento Geral da Lei da Terra, Artigo 94.º ("Participação nas receitas e consignação")
reports.description: Guinea-Bissau's General Regulation of the Land Law, published in the Boletim Oficial (Suplemento) of 27 November 2018 and currently in force, contains a real, quantified revenue-sharing formula for the Imposto Fundiário (land tax) — verified by direct PDF download and pdfplumber extraction of the two-column-layout source. Art. 94(1): "O produto de cobrança do Imposto Fundiário constitui receita do Estado e reverte, nas proporções abaixo indicadas, a favor das seguintes entidades: a) 60% a favor do Tesouro Público; b) 20% a favor das comunidades locais; c) 10% a favor das autoridades administrativas regionais e setoriais; d) 10% a favor das comissões fundiárias." Art. 94(3) further splits the regional/sectoral share: "A repartição de fundos referidos na alínea c) do número 1 entre as autoridades administrativas regionais e setoriais efetua-se na proporção de 25% e 75%, respetivamente." Art. 94(4) restricts the funds' use: "As autoridades administrativas regionais e setoriais devem utilizar os valores resultantes da cobrança do Imposto Fundiário na realização de ações de ordenamento e gestão de território, de infra-estruturas de saneamento básico, abastecimento de água, rede elétrica, rede viária e tratamento de lixo." The beneficiary class named here ("autoridades administrativas regionais e setoriais") is the deconcentrated regional/sectoral administrative tier, not explicitly equated in this text to the constitutionally-defined "autarquias locais" (municípios/secções/juntas) — see _dropped for why no edge is drawn to the Constitution node on this basis alone.
reports.cadence_note: One-off regulatory instrument, in force since 27 November 2018.

reports.title: Orçamento Geral do Estado (OGE) 2022 [Proposta] — Ministério da Administração Territorial e Poder Local, Transferências às Regiões
reports.publisher: Ministério das Finanças da Guiné-Bissau — Direção-Geral do Orçamento (DGO)
reports.description: Guinea-Bissau's FY2022 state budget proposal, sourced from CABRI-SBO's budget-transparency repository (SIGFiP-generated document, footer reads "Editado por: DGO... Editado em: 02/12/2021"), itemizes an identical transfer line for each of the country's eight named administrative regions under Título 11 ("Ministério da Administração territorial e Poder local"), Título 4 ("Transferências"): "6411 - Região de Cacheu ... 8,500 ... / 6412 - Região de Oio ... 8,500 ... / 6413 - Região de Biombo ... 8,500 ... / 6414 - Região de Bolama Bijagós ... 8,500 ... / 6415 - Região de Quinara ... 8,500 ... / 6416 - Região de Tombali ... 8,500 ... / 6417 - Região de Bafata ... 8,500 ... / 6418 - Região de Gabu ... 8,500 ..." (figures in thousand FCFA under "Financiamento Interno"; "Total do Capitulo : 361110201 ... 118,000"). Each of the eight regions (Cacheu, Oio, Biombo, Bolama Bijagós, Quinara, Tombali, Bafatá, Gabú) receives an identical 8,500 thousand FCFA (≈USD 14,000 at 2021-22 rates) — a flat, non-differentiated administrative transfer, not a needs- or population-based formula. Bissau, administered as the "Sector Autónomo de Bissau" rather than as a "região," receives no line in this table. The same figures also appear in the whole-of-government "ANEXO III – Despesa Global" annex of the same document.
reports.cadence_note: Annual state budget (OGE); this edition is the FY2022 proposal ("[PROPOSTA]"), not confirmed as the final enacted text.

reports.title: Lei n.º 7/96, de 9 de Dezembro — "Autonomia Financeira e Patrimonial das Autarquias" (Lei das Finanças Locais)
reports.description: Guinea-Bissau's operative municipal-finance law, confirming and quantifying the delegation Constitution Art. 110 makes to ordinary law ('o regime das finanças locais, a estabelecer por lei'). Verbatim text (Preâmbulo plus Arts. 1-6) reached this round via an unpaywalled preview at vlex.pt: "PREÂMBULO Inicia-se com o presente diploma o lançamento das bases financeiras com o propósito de permitir as Autarquias Locais caminharem em vista aos objectivos plasmados com a sua criação... ARTIGO 1º (Autonomia financeira e patrimonial das Autarquias) Os Municípios, Secções Autárquicas e Juntas Locais têm património e finanças próprias cuja gestão compete aos respectivos órgãos... ARTIGO 6º (Contribuição do FEF) O montante global do FEF é repartido pelos Municípios através da aplicação dos seguintes critérios: 50% igualmente por todos os Municípios; 25% na razão directa do número de habitantes; 25% na razão directa da área. A lei do OGE fixa em cada ano um montante não inferior a 10% da receita tributária executada no ano transacto..." (text cut off by the platform's paywall after this point) — a real, quantified Fundo de Equilíbrio Financeiro (FEF) inter-municipal transfer formula: 50% split equally across all municípios, 25% by population, 25% by area, funded by a minimum 10% share of the prior year's executed tax revenue set annually in the OGE (state budget) law. CAVEAT on sourcing: vlex.pt (https://vlex.pt/vid/financeira-patrimonial-autarquias-dezembro-36574017) is a commercial third-party legal-publishing platform, not a Guinea-Bissau government domain — but the quoted text is a verbatim reproduction of the government-authored statute, not vlex's own paraphrase or summary, so it is treated as usable primary-source text under this branch's established convention for verbatim-government-text-via-third-party-hosting (the same tier already applied to droit-afrique.com and WIPO Lex mirrors elsewhere in this project), with the third-party-hosting caveat recorded explicitly rather than silently. Independent corroboration reached this round from a genuinely government-hosted source, mef.gw's Kontaktu tax portal (https://kontaktu.mef.gw/legislation, a Ministério da Economia e Finanças subdomain), which confirms the law's short title "Lei das Finanças Locais" and its citation as "Lei n°7/96, de 9 de dezembro" in its own text: "Transitoriamente fica o Governo central autorizado a lançar a derrama prevista na alínea c) do n°1 do art.3° da Lei n°7/96, de 9 de dezembro (Lei das Finanças Locais)." RESOLVES A PRIOR AMBIGUITY: this round confirms Lei n.º 5/96 ("Lei de Bases das Autarquias Locais", the framework/organic law, still not located in full text — see gw-g23-municipal.json's _dropped block) and Lei n.º 7/96 (this finance law) are DISTINCT instruments, not two labels for the same text — vlex.pt's own text of Lei 7/96 is self-contained, dated 9 December 1996, and titled exactly "Autonomia financeira e patrimonial das Autarquias", separately from the framework law's own "Lei de Bases" title. OPEN CAVEAT ON CURRENT FORCE: the Kontaktu page's own markup shows the derrama-rate sub-provision of Art. 3º n.º1 c) (a flat 1% derrama rate) has been struck through / superseded — "Redação atribuída pelo art. 9º da Lei nº 1/2021", replacing it with a reference to "A taxa da derrama prevista no artigo 206º, da Lei nº 5/2018, de 7 de agosto, relativa ao Código da Administração Autárquica, é de 2%." This confirms only that ONE narrow sub-provision (the derrama rate) has been superseded, by Lei nº 5/2018 (Código da Administração Autárquica) as amended by Lei nº 1/2021 — it does NOT establish that the whole of Lei 7/96 is repealed, and in particular the Article 6 FEF formula quoted above is NOT confirmed to remain in force by anything found this round; its current-force status should be treated as unconfirmed rather than assumed, pending a future round checking whether Lei 5/2018's Código da Administração Autárquica recasts the FEF mechanism as well.

_dropped.why: RESOLVED 2026-08-30: a fresh, independently-verified fetch of the same vlex.pt page (confirmed by two separate readers, not just re-trusting the earlier round) found the citation this entry said was absent, right in the preamble: 'no uso dos poderes Constitucionais definidos nos artigos 86º, alínea b) e 1l0º [110º], o seguinte' -- Article 110 is exactly the finance-regime delegation article this branch concerns. Wired gw-lei-7-96-financas-locais -> gw-constituicao-poder-local (cites) in gw-autarquias-locais-laws-2026-08-30.json. The earlier round's 'paywall cuts the text off before any article number' explanation does not match what a fresh fetch of the same URL shows -- the citation is in the preamble, before any paywall could plausibly cut in. Original entry follows. Topically this law implements Constitution Art. 110's delegation ('o regime das finanças locais, a estabelecer por lei'), and Art. 1's title ('Autonomia financeira e patrimonial das Autarquias') echoes Art. 110's own wording almost exactly — but the vlex.pt preview text of Lei 7/96 reached this round (Preâmbulo plus Arts. 1-6) never cites the Constitution by article number, and the paywall cuts the text off before any later article might. Per the evidence-strict citation rule, no documented edge is drawn despite the strong topical relationship; recorded here as a proximity note rather than an edge, per the task's own instruction to prefer a note over an unsupported edge.

Both instruments concern sub-national revenue-sharing formulas (Lei 7/96 Art. 6's FEF inter-municipal split; Decreto 6/2018 Art. 94's land-tax split), and both are FCFA-denominated Guinea-Bissau fiscal-transfer mechanisms, but the two texts as retrieved never cross-cite each other and their beneficiary classes differ (Lei 7/96's FEF distributes among 'Municípios'; Decreto 6/2018 Art. 94 distributes to 'comunidades locais' and 'autoridades administrativas regionais e setoriais', a different, deconcentrated tier — the same non-equation already flagged in gw-g23-municipal.json's _dropped block for that decree). No textual citation basis for an edge; recorded as topical proximity only, per the task instruction.

_dropped.edge: gw-lei-7-96-financas-locais -> Lei nº 5/2018 (Código da Administração Autárquica), as amended by Lei nº 1/2021
_dropped.why: Confirmed this round to exist and to be in force via mef.gw's Kontaktu tax portal (https://kontaktu.mef.gw/legislation), which documents that Lei nº 5/2018's Art. 206 (as further amended by Art. 9º of Lei nº 1/2021) now sets the derrama rate previously fixed at 1% by Lei 7/96 Art. 3º n.º1 c) — the tax portal's own markup shows that sub-provision of Lei 7/96 struck through/superseded. This is genuine, real, and named evidence that a later, more comprehensive municipal-administration code (the 'Código da Administração Autárquica') exists and may supersede more of Lei 7/96 than just the single derrama-rate sub-provision confirmed this round — most importantly, whether it recasts or replaces the Article 6 FEF (Fundo de Equilíbrio Financeiro) formula that is this node's core quantified finding. Full text of Lei nº 5/2018 (and of the amending Lei nº 1/2021) was not located this round — a real, named, documented lead for a future round to resolve the FEF formula's current-force status.
