Note that the Order also names the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951 in the same breath; that statute has no corpus node and is recorded in `_dropped` as a lead.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY. FC16 names the constituting Order by its Gazette number in Volume I para 1.2 -- "the President of India constituted the FC-16 vide Notification S.O. 5533(E) dated 31 December 2023 (Annexure 1.1)" -- and then reproduces the Order's terms of reference in full, introducing them at para 1.8 with "As per the order constituting the FC-16, its ToR is as follows: 'The Commission shall make recommendations as to the following matters, namely: …'", with the Order itself carried as Annexure 1.1. `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`: the Order does not merely authorise the Commission, it fixes the questions the Report must answer and the award period it must cover, and the Report's structure follows those terms directly -- the Order supplies the scope the Report's method is built to satisfy. That is the same distinction `br-ipca-fpe.json` draws between a statute that grants authority (`cites`) and one that determines what must be computed (`methodology_depends_on`).

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, and closes BRICS/G.1's open lead. FC16 names the Census as its population source repeatedly and operatively. Volume I para 8.85, on the Population criterion carrying a 17.5 per cent weight: "In keeping with the longstanding practice ... we continue to include population among the criteria. In conformity with the uniform recommendation by nearly all States, we implement this criterion by awarding each State an allocation based on its share in the Census 2011 total population of the twenty-eight States. We assign a weight of 17.5 per cent to this criterion. We note here that whenever any of our variables are combined with population, we rely on the 2011 Census figures. In this respect, we have fully transitioned from the 1971 Census population to the 2011 Census population data." The Technical Note states it inside the formula itself: "Denoting by Nk the population of State k (k = 1, 2, … 28) as per the 2011 Census, we have, (ii) C1j = …". The Demographic Performance criterion depends on it too, para 8.88: "we set the per capita devolution to a State in proportion to the inverse of its population growth between 1971 and 2011 Censuses. We convert this per capita devolution into total by multiplying it by the 2011 population." And a table source line reads "Source: Reports of FC-11 to FC-15; Census of India 2001 and 2011." `uses_data_from` rather than `calculated_from`: the census figures are a direct published input to two weighted criteria, but the devolution shares are the output of a multi-criterion formula rather than a mechanical derivation from population alone.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY. The Explanatory Memorandum exists to record the Government's action on the Commission's recommendations and cites the Report by internal reference throughout: "The formula for horizontal devolution and weights assigned to various criteria as recommended by the Commission are given in Table 8.8 of the Report. The shares of States in horizontal devolution for the award period are given in Table 8.9 of the Report." Further references run to "Volume I of the Report", "para 10.100 of Volume I of the Report" and "Chapter 13 of Volume I". `cites` rather than `uses_data_from`: the memorandum states what the Government accepts or modifies and points at where each recommendation lives, rather than taking the Report's figures as a computational input -- the document that does the latter is the Receipts Budget, whose edge is typed accordingly.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, and the sibling that establishes this as a recurring documentary relationship rather than a one-off. Verbatim: "The Final Report of the Commission covering the financial years 2021-22 to 2025-26 ... together with this Explanatory Memorandum on the action taken on the recommendations of the Commission, is being laid on the Table of the House, in pursuance of Article 281 of the Constitution." and "The Commission has recommended that 41 per cent of the net proceeds of Union taxes should be shared with the States." -- the second sentence restating FC15's headline vertical-devolution recommendation as already recorded on `in-fc15-report`, which confirms the memorandum is acting on this specific report rather than on the Commission generically.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, and the strongest breadth edge found for India this round -- the dependent document both NAMES the source and REPUBLISHES its numbers. The footnote to ANNEX-4's "Share (Per cent)" column reads: "* As per accepted recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission, the States' share has been fixed at 41% of the net proceeds of shareable Central Taxes." The column it annotates reproduces FC16 Volume I Table 8.9 digit for digit: "Andhra Pradesh 4.217 | Arunachal Pradesh 1.354 | Assam 3.258 | Bihar 9.948 | Chhattisgarh 3.304 | Goa 0.365 | Gujarat 3.755 | Haryana 1.361 | Himachal Pradesh 0.914 | … | Uttar Pradesh 17.619 | Uttarakhand 1.141 | West Bengal 7.215" against FC16's own "Andhra Pradesh 4.217 / Arunachal Pradesh 1.354 / Assam 3.258 / Bihar 9.948 / Chhattisgarh 3.304 / Goa 0.365 / Gujarat 3.755 / Haryana 1.361 / Himachal Pradesh 0.914 / Jharkhand 3.357 / Karnataka 4.131 / Kerala 2.382 / Madhya Pradesh 7.347 / Maharashtra 6.441 …". `uses_data_from` rather than `cites`: the shares are literal computational inputs to the state-wise distribution the annex publishes, not a background reference. This is also the edge that makes the Indian chain load-bearing rather than merely documentary -- it connects a Commission recommendation to the money actually appropriated.
dependencies.evidence_quote: * As per accepted recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission, the States' share has been fixed at 41% of the net proceeds of shareable Central Taxes.

dependencies.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, from FC16's own data-sources appendix in Volume II, which names the RBI study by title and edition years as the source for a specific series across a specific period: "Total Grants — 1952-53 to 1989-90: RBI Bulletins of various years. … 1990-91 to 2022-23: RBI Study on State Finances 2014, 2023, 2024. Appendix 2. The data for 2023-24 is taken from Statement 18 of Union Budget". This is a titled-publication citation with a named appendix, not an agency-level reference, which is what makes it edge-qualifying where most of this round's near-misses were not. Note the reciprocity: `in-rbi-state-finances` cites FC15 in the other direction (see the edge below), so these two documents genuinely depend on each other across different vintages -- an unusual and legitimate shape, not a modelling error, since the RBI study of one year draws on an earlier Commission and a later Commission draws on that study.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, from the same FC16 Volume II data-sources appendix, which names Statement 18 twice and explains why it turned to it: "2016-17 to 2023-24: Statement 18 of Expenditure Profile of Union Budget as IPFS reports were discontinued" and "The data for 2023-24 is taken from Statement 18 of Union Budget". A named statement within a named annual publication, cited as the source for a stated period, is a document-level citation. Worth recording that the dependency runs ONLY in this direction: Statement 18's own text does not cite the Finance Commission, carrying merely the budget-head label "Finance Commission Grants", which is why no reverse edge is minted (see `_dropped`).

VERIFIED DIRECTLY. The RBI study cites the Fifteenth Finance Commission in its own analytical text -- "…the States can raise more revenues through higher stamp duty and registration fees, as pointed out by the Fifteenth Finance Commission (FC-XV)." -- and carries a table built on the Commission series: Table III.3, "States' Share in the Divisible Pool of Central Taxes Recommended by Finance Commissions", with rows "Eleventh 29.5 | Twelfth 30.5 | Thirteenth 32.0 | Fourteenth 42.0 | Fifteenth 41.0" and the source line "Sources: Various Finance Commission Reports; and Reddy and Reddy (2019)." The "Fifteenth 41.0" row is FC15's headline recommendation as recorded on `in-fc15-report`. `cites` rather than `uses_data_from`: the source line names a CLASS ("Various Finance Commission Reports") rather than a single titled report, and the in-text reference is analytical commentary -- so the edge rests on the combination of the two, which supports a citation relationship but not a claim that FC15's figures are a computational input to the study.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY. The CAG audits state finances explicitly against the Commission's projections, naming it in its own analytical findings: "The actual devolution of State's share of Union taxes and duties was greater than the projections made by the Fifteenth Finance Commission (XV FC) for the years 2021-22 to 2023-24." and "Fifteenth Finance Commission Grants — Transfers from GoI to the State during 2023-24 on the recommendations of XV FC are given in Table 2.10". The report's own scope statement makes the dependency structural rather than incidental: "The analysis is also carried out on recommendations of the Finance Commission (FC), in the context of Tamil Nadu State Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (TNFR Act), best practices and guidelines of the Government of India." `cites` rather than `uses_data_from`: the Commission's projections are the benchmark the audit measures outturn against, which is a reference relationship rather than a computational input.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The actual devolution of State's share of Union taxes and duties was greater than the projections made by the Fifteenth Finance Commission (XV FC) for the years 2021-22 to 2023-24.

dependencies.basis: VERIFIED, BUT WITH A WEAKNESS STATED EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN SILENTLY UPGRADED -- read this basis before relying on the edge. BRICS/G.1 scoped `in-rbi-act-45za` deliberately narrowly, to only what Section 45ZA's own text establishes, because it could not verify the notified target behind an RBI bot-wall and a CAPTCHA-gated gazette search. This round did NOT retrieve the literal signed gazette instrument either (S.O. 2088(E) -- see `_dropped` for the full record of attempts). What it did retrieve is the same statement from TWO INDEPENDENT PRIMARY GOVERNMENT-OF-INDIA PUBLISHERS. Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Finance, 5 August 2016: "Under sub-section (1) of section 45ZA of the RBI Act, the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, determines the inflation target in terms of the Consumer Price Index (CPI), once in every five years. This target would be notified in the Official Gazette." and "Determination and notification of Inflation Target — In exercise of the powers conferred by section 45ZA of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the Central Government, in consultation with RBI, has fixed the inflation target … Inflation Target: Four per cent. Upper tolerance level: Six per cent. Lower tolerance level: Two per cent." And the Reserve Bank's own Monetary Policy Overview: "Under Section 45ZA, the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, determines the inflation target in terms of the Consumer Price Index (CPI), once in five years and notifies it in the Official Gazette." THE MECHANISM IS ALSO CURRENT, which matters for tense: "In its second review, on March 25, 2026, the Central Government retained the inflation target and the tolerance band for the next 5-year period – April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2031." TWO EXPLICIT LIMITS ON THIS EDGE: (1) the citation comes from the Government's own explanatory statements ABOUT section 45ZA, not from the section's four corners nor from a retrieved gazette instrument; (2) the "(Combined)" qualifier is NOT evidenced anywhere reachable and is deliberately absent from this basis and from the node -- every primary text retrieved says "Consumer Price Index (CPI)" without it. `cites` rather than `uses_data_from` precisely because of limit (1): a stronger type would assert a computational relationship the retrieved documents do not themselves state.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Under sub-section (1) of section 45ZA of the RBI Act, the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, determines the inflation target in terms of the Consumer Price Index (CPI), once in every five years. This target would be notified in the Official Gazette.

_dropped.edge: in-fc16-explanatory-memorandum / in-fc15-explanatory-memorandum -> Article 281 of the Constitution
_dropped.why: Two clean, verbatim, in-text citations with nothing to point at. Both Explanatory Memoranda state the Article 281 laying mechanism in their own words -- "…together with this Explanatory Memorandum on the action taken on the recommendations of the Commission, is being laid on the Table of the House, in pursuance of Article 281 of the Constitution." -- which is exactly the citation shape this corpus requires, naming the article by number in the dependent document's own body. The corpus has `in-constitution-art280` but no Article 281 node, so the edges are stranded. This is the cheapest high-value fix available to the next Indian round: minting `in-constitution-art281` from the same constitutional source `in-constitution-art280` was built from would immediately close TWO fully evidenced edges. Not minted here because this session did not fetch and verify Article 281's own text, and this corpus does not mint a node on the strength of documents that cite it -- the same rule that keeps the Budget Report's detail annex out of the Chinese slice.

SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-08-17 (BRICS/G.3): still refused AT THIS NODE, but India's national accounts are now attached to SNA 2008 elsewhere in the corpus. G.3 found a current, non-obsolete MoSPI document that names the edition — the National Accounts Division's GDP base-year-revision sub-committee report (Feb 2026), whose Chapter 2 opens 'As per recommendations of System of National Accounts (SNA)-2008, NAD industry-wise estimates of GDP are compiled using institutional sector approach.' It is minted as `in-mospi-gdp-base-revision-2026` with a `methodology_depends_on` edge to `sna-2008` in `in-g3-international-standards.json`. The edge is NOT attached to `in-mospi-nas`, because the NAS publication's own release text still says only 'in alignment with the United Nations System of National Accounts (SNA)' with no year — attaching it here would put a citation in this node's mouth that its own document does not make. ORIGINAL REASONING, kept: A real citation of the UN System of National Accounts that names no EDITION, and is therefore not minted -- the same decision made for China's COICOP citation in `cn-g2-budget-law-equalization.json`, and made for the same reason, so the two branches stay consistent. The NAS-2025 release says only: "These estimates are presented at current and constant (2011-12) prices and are based on the methodologies in alignment with the United Nations System of National Accounts (SNA)". The string "SNA 2008" does NOT appear in it. It does appear in OTHER MoSPI documents about the same estimates -- a 2026 GDP FAQ, and a 2015 methodology volume which is itself watermarked OBSOLETE -- but under this project's rule the dependent document's own text must name the target, and combining two documents to establish which edition is meant is inference. Recorded rather than quietly minted because the temptation is real: everyone knows India's national accounts follow the 2008 SNA, and that is exactly the kind of ambient knowledge this corpus refuses to encode as evidence. CONTRAST WORTH KEEPING: the Chinese national-accounts instrument DOES name 《国民账户体系2008》 by edition, and therefore does get its edge to `sna-2008` -- the difference between the two cases is entirely in what the documents say, which is the standard working as intended. RESOLVABLE: the NAS publication itself (as opposed to its press release) very likely names the edition in its methodology chapter.

_dropped.edge: in-fc16-report -> a specific titled MoSPI GSDP publication (behind the 42.5% Per Capita GSDP Distance criterion)
_dropped.why: NOT FOUND, and this round settles BRICS/G.1's open lead as a genuine negative rather than leaving it open. FC16 Volume I (17,998 lines) and Volume II (8,985 lines) were both read in full text, INCLUDING the Technical Note that defines the devolution formula. FC16 never names a titled MoSPI GSDP publication anywhere -- it uses a dataset label with no corresponding release. This matters because Per Capita GSDP Distance carries 42.5 per cent, by far the largest single weight in the entire devolution formula, so the corpus's largest Indian dependency by economic significance has no documentary target. That is a real finding about how the Commission sources its most important input, not a search failure: the Commission cites MoSPI repeatedly for GDP and GSDP without ever pointing at a publication, exactly as `br-fpe-dn-tcu` names IBGE for its per-capita household income column without naming a release. Two BRICS federations, the same gap, in the same place in the same kind of formula.

_dropped.edge: in-union-budget-expenditure-profile-stmt18 / Budget at a Glance / FRBM Fiscal Policy Statements -> in-fc16-report
_dropped.why: REJECTED deliberately, and this is the round's clearest application of the discipline BRICS/G.1 established. All three are unambiguously recurrent annual Union Budget publications and good nodes (Statement 18 is minted; Budget at a Glance and the FRBM statements are left for a future round). But their ONLY reference to the Commission is a budget-head LABEL -- "II. Finance Commission Grants" in Statement 18 and Budget at a Glance, and in the FRBM statements an institutional reference with figures attached: "(v) Finance Commission Grants — 30. In BE 2026-27, the Finance Commission grants are estimated at ₹1.29 lakh crore. … Thus, total resources shared, tax devolution and FC Grants, with States through the Finance Commission route are estimated at ₹16.56 lakh crore in BE 2026-27." A BUDGET HEAD NAMED AFTER AN INSTITUTION IS NOT A CITATION OF A DOCUMENT, and neither is a spending figure routed through that institution. The Receipts Budget's ANNEX-4 footnote is the one that clears the bar, by naming the Commission's accepted recommendations and reproducing its table -- and that is where the edge is drawn instead. Recorded at length because this round ALSO overturned one G.1 rejection (the FC16-to-Article-280 edge), and the two outcomes must not be read as one lesson: the standard did not move, the evidence did.

_dropped.edge: in-rbi-act-45za -> the literal Gazette notification S.O. 2088(E) fixing the inflation target, and the "Consumer Price Index (Combined)" wording
_dropped.why: PARTIALLY RESOLVED but recorded honestly as still open on its own terms. The SUBSTANCE is now verified from two independent primary Government publishers and supports the minted `in-rbi-act-45za -> in-mospi-cpi` edge (see that edge's basis). The literal signed gazette instrument was NOT retrieved. Every attempt, recorded so the next round does not repeat them: `egazette.nic.in` has NO DNS RECORD AT ALL and simply does not exist -- a different failure from the .gov.in host, and previously conflated with it. `egazette.gov.in` was recovered from its TLS failure to HTTP 200 by the trust-bundle fix in this file's `_note`, and contrary to G.1's note the LANDING PAGE HAS NO CAPTCHA -- but its search is a stateful ASP.NET session plus `__VIEWSTATE` postback flow, and a bare GET with a fabricated session token returns 500; completing it needs a real browser session. The RBI Discussion Paper PDF that reproduces the notification history sits behind the TSPD bot-wall on `/rdocs/PressRelease/PDFs/`, the one path the cookie-plus-Referer method does not defeat (it returned `curl: (52) Empty reply from server`, also on `--http1.1`). `r.jina.ai` returned a Cloudflare 403, so no TIER B was available. `dea.gov.in` was reachable but the notification was not located on it. SEPARATELY AND IMPORTANTLY: the "(Combined)" qualifier is NOT ASSERTED anywhere in this file. No reachable primary source contains the string "Consumer Price Index (Combined)" in the notification text; every one says "Consumer Price Index (CPI)". What IS verifiable is that the MoSPI series is published as a Combined series -- its release carries the column headers "Rural | Urban | Combined" and "Annexure IV: All India Combined (General) level index and inflation" -- but that is MoSPI's structure, not the notification's wording, and the two are kept apart deliberately. A browser session against egazette.gov.in would close this.

Plausible but judged too weak, and left out rather than minted at a confidence the evidence does not carry. FC16 Volume I uses the table source line "Source: States' Finance Accounts, States' Budgets, CAG Audit Reports on State Finances", and para 1.31 states "Disaggregated details of the divisible pool of taxes were obtained from the office of the CAG." The first names a CLASS of reports rather than a specific one, and the second names the OFFICE rather than a publication -- neither reaches the standard the forward edge (`in-cag-state-finances-audit-report -> in-fc15-report`) clears comfortably. Contrast with the RBI study, where FC16's appendix names the publication AND its edition years AND the specific appendix within it, which is why that reciprocal edge WAS minted and this one was not. A future round reading FC16's per-state annexures may well find a specific State Finances Audit Report named by number, at which point this becomes available.

_dropped.edge: in-fc16-report -> Economic Survey (Table 1.6 of Economic Survey 2024-25), and the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951
_dropped.why: Two precisely named instruments with no corpus node, both cited verbatim in documents this file mints, and both easy wins for a future round. (1) FC16's Volume II data-sources appendix cites the Economic Survey with table-level precision: "GDP — Table 1.6 of Economic Survey 2024-25". The Economic Survey is a well-known annual Government of India publication and would be a strong node; its URL was not verified this round, so it is flagged as a lead rather than asserted. Note this is the CLOSEST thing found to a titled source for FC16's macroeconomic denominators, and may be worth testing against the unresolved 42.5% GSDP-criterion question above. (2) The Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951 (Act No. 33 of 1951) is named alongside Article 280 in BOTH the constituting Order and FC16 Volume I para 1.2 -- "In pursuance of clause (1) of Article 280 of the Constitution of India and the provisions of the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951 (Act No. 33 of 1951)…" -- so two fully evidenced edges are waiting on a node that indiacode.nic.in, already proven reachable at TIER A for the GST Compensation Act, would almost certainly supply. Also recorded from the same FC16 appendix, for completeness: "GRR — Database on Indian Economy, RBI. The figure is derived as a sum of Gross Tax Revenue and Gross Non-tax Revenue taken from HBS Table 93 (Central Government Receipts- Major components) of DBIE" and "Net Proceeds — Data on divisible pool is taken from the CAG certificates for respective years".

_dropped.edge: in-gst-compensation-act-2017 -> in-fc15-report / in-fc16-report, in either direction
_dropped.why: NOT FOUND, and structurally impossible in one direction. The Act is a 2017 statute and cannot cite FC15 (reporting 2020) or FC16 (reporting 2025). In the reverse direction, both Commissions discuss GST and GST compensation substantively, but no verbatim citation of THIS ACT BY NAME AND NUMBER was located in the FC passages read this round, so none is asserted. The node is minted as a node-only contribution: a standing statute defining a real method (a fourteen per cent per annum projected growth rate over a 2015-16 base year), currently unconnected. Worth flagging for whoever picks this up: the Act's compensation mechanism operated over a defined "transition period", so before any future round writes a present-tense dependency on it, the tense question this project's own hand-off spec insists on should be settled -- a past-tense arrangement is not a live dependency.

_status: NEW 2026-08-17. India's third slice, and the one that connects the Indian branch to the rest of the graph for the first time. After BRICS/G.2, India had fifteen corpus nodes and ZERO edges to any non-Indian node -- the largest fully disconnected island in the corpus. This round asks REPORTS.md's secondary-objective question of India: which supranational bodies issue a standard that an Indian statistic is documented as methodologically dependent on? Answer: five, across eight edges. THE MOST SATISFYING RESULT NEEDED NO NEW RESEARCH AT ALL -- `in-mospi-cpi`'s own release text, quoted in that node's description since BRICS/G.1, states verbatim that the series "is aligned with the United Nations' Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018". The edition is named, the citation is in the dependent document's own text, and the edge was available for two rounds without being drawn. It is drawn here, directly from the existing node. Five new Indian source nodes carry the rest: the MoSPI expert-group report defining the CPI 2024 series, the GDP base-revision sub-committee report that finally names SNA 2008 in current non-obsolete text, NIC 2025, the Ministry of Finance's external-debt status report, and the RBI's balance-of-payments methodology. An eighth edge runs from `in-fc15-report` to the IMF's World Economic Outlook, which matters structurally out of proportion to its strength: FC15 sits inside India's main eleven-node component, so that single citation is what attaches the Finance Commission cluster itself to the international layer. Refusals are recorded in `_dropped`, including one where a verified-looking result was rejected because the host could not be reached for raw verification.
_note: ACCESS AND VERIFICATION. Sources are TIER A -- plain curl, genuine HTTP 200, real document bytes on the issuing agency's own host -- with ONE DELIBERATE EXCLUSION described below. The Indian trust-store fixes from BRICS/G.2 were reused and confirmed: `dea.gov.in` chains to Let's Encrypt intermediate YR1, absent from the container store, fixed by fetching `http://yr1.i.lencr.org/`, converting DER to PEM and appending to the system bundle -- verified cleanly with no `-k`. `censusindia.gov.in` needs the eMudhra emSign intermediate the same way. The diagnostic trap from G.2 is restated because it is easy to fall into twice: running `openssl s_client` DIRECTLY shows the egress gateway's own certificate and verifies cleanly, which is misleading -- it must be run THROUGH the proxy to see the real upstream chain. `www.rbi.org.in` serves plain HTML fine; only `rbidocs.rbi.org.in` is behind the F5/Shape TSPD bot-wall, and `/rdocs/PressRelease/PDFs/` remains impassable even with the cookie-plus-Referer method that works for `/rdocs/Publications/PDFs/`. `r.jina.ai` remains Cloudflare-403, so no TIER B fallback exists. THE DELIBERATE EXCLUSION, recorded because it is a live application of this project's own hardest-won lesson: the GASAB standard IGFRS 1 contains what appears to be an excellent IPSAS dependency, but `gasab.gov.in` returns `curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` on both the document and the site root, and 503 over plain HTTP. The research agent reached the content only through WebFetch, on a different egress. Since AF/G.24 established that WebFetch has fabricated plausible content for unreachable URLs, and since no independent raw verification was possible from here, THE EDGE IS NOT MINTED -- see `_dropped`. Every `basis` below is this session's own read of the underlying research; full research log in `BRICS/G.3-research/india.md`.

reports.title: Expert Group Report on Comprehensive Updation of Consumer Price Index
reports.publisher: Price Statistics Division, National Statistics Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India
reports.description: The 258-page expert-group report, dated January 2026, that defines the methodology of India's CPI 2024=100 series -- and the document that ties India's CPI to two international instruments by name and edition. On classification, §3.3 (Summary of Key Recommendations): "To enhance credibility and to ensure global comparability of Indian CPI, the latest structure of Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018 will be adopted in the CPI 2024 series." Corroborated at §2.3: "CPI 2024 – The latest classification framework is COICOP 2018. The CPI 2024 series is mostly aligned with COICOP 2018 with 12 Divisions, 43 Groups, 92 Classes and 162 Sub-classes." and at §4.1.5: "EG recommended for mapping HCES items as per COICOP 2018 in CPI 2024." On method, the IMF manual is used NORMATIVELY rather than decoratively -- §4.6.5: "The procedure is fully consistent with the principles of the IMF CPI Manual (2020) and supports a smooth, stable, and operationally feasible implementation of the chain-base CPI."; §5.3.2: "This is one of the three methods prescribed in the Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods 2020 (page 35) in case, if the price of social security transfers decreases from some positive amount to zero."; and §5.4.2 quotes the manual's text directly: "In this regard, the IMF's CPI Manual Concepts and Methods 2020 para 2.60 may be seen below: 'The expenditure on social transfers in kind is incurred by the governments or nonprofit institutions that pay for them, and not by the households that consume them....'" The report also records the PREDECESSOR series' classification lineage -- §4.1.1: "In India, in the CPI (2012=100) series COICOP 1999 was adopted with some deviations" -- which is deliberately not turned into an edge; see `_dropped`. Fetched TIER A from mospi.gov.in as a real 5.2MB PDF.
reports.cadence_note: A one-off expert-group report rather than a recurring release, qualifying as a standing instrument that defines a method -- it is the document that fixes the classification structure and index formulae of the CPI 2024=100 series. Comparable in role to `ru-rosstat-cpi-methodology-915` on the Russian side, which is why the two are typed the same way.

reports.title: Report of the Sub-Committee for Incorporation of New Data Sources, Rates and Ratios — For base year revision of GDP (2011-12 to 2022-23)
reports.publisher: National Accounts Division, National Statistics Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India
reports.description: The National Accounts Division's base-year-revision sub-committee report, constituted under the Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics (ACNAS) and published on mospi.gov.in on 24 February 2026 -- and the document that resolves BRICS/G.2's open India question by naming the SNA edition in CURRENT, non-obsolete text. Chapter 2 opens: "As per recommendations of System of National Accounts (SNA)-2008, NAD industry-wise estimates of GDP are compiled using institutional sector approach. All resident institutional units are allocated to one and only one of the following five institutional sectors: i. The non-financial corporation sector; ii. The financial corporation sector; iii. The general government sector; ..." -- "NAD" being the National Accounts Division, the compiler of `in-mospi-nas`. This matters because G.2 had to refuse the NAS-to-SNA-2008 edge: the NAS publication's own press release says only "in alignment with the United Nations System of National Accounts (SNA)" with no year, and the only documents naming "SNA 2008" were a FAQ and a 2015 methodology volume watermarked OBSOLETE. This report is neither -- it was checked for an OBSOLETE watermark and carries none. A FORWARD-LOOKING SIGNAL is recorded and deliberately NOT turned into an edge: §1.6 lists "v. Sub-Committee for SNA 2025 Update" among the five sub-committees constituted for the revision. That names an internal committee, not a published Indian statistic compiled on SNA 2025, so no `sna-2025` edge is drawn -- but when that sub-committee reports, the edge may become real. Fetched TIER A from mospi.gov.in as a real 32MB PDF, re-verified with a range request.
reports.cadence_note: A one-off sub-committee report tied to a specific base-year revision, qualifying as a standing methodological instrument rather than a recurring release. India's GDP base-year revisions occur roughly once a decade, so a successor document is expected rather than scheduled.

reports.title: National Industrial Classification 2025 (NIC-2025)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India
reports.description: India's national industrial classification, published on mospi.gov.in on 18 November 2025, and an unusually clean instance of a national classification stating that its own structure IS the international one. Introduction: "The classification aligns with the International Standard Industrial Classification (ISIC Rev. 5) while addressing specific features of the Indian economy such as the informal sector, agriculture, renewable energy, and the growing digital economy." And under Salient Features: "Based on ISIC Rev. 5: NIC-2025 is aligned with the latest international standard, ISIC Revision 5, ensuring structural and conceptual comparability up to the 4-digit class level." The document also records the lineage of its predecessors in a table of national-versus-international versions -- "NIC 2008 | ISIC Rev 4 (2008) | Sections 21, Divisions 88, Groups 238, Classes 403, Sub-Classes 1304" -- and notes that "The Indian Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) fully adopted ISIC Rev.1 at the division level", so the dependency is a documented sixty-year pattern rather than a one-off alignment. A NODE-IDENTITY NOTE, checked before minting: the corpus's `isic` node is deliberately the unversioned FAMILY node ("the acknowledged parent of most national industrial classifications"), not a revision-specific node, so pointing an ISIC Rev. 5 citation at it raises no edition problem -- unlike SNA and COICOP, which the corpus does split by edition. Fetched TIER A from mospi.gov.in as a real 5.1MB PDF.
reports.cadence_note: A standing classification, revised generationally rather than on a cadence -- SIC 1962, then NIC 2008, now NIC 2025, each tracking a successive ISIC revision.

reports.title: India's External Debt: A Status Report
reports.publisher: External Debt Management Unit, Economic Division, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
reports.description: The Ministry of Finance's annual external-debt status report -- the 2024-25 edition, September 2025, 114 pages -- and the best Indian-hosted, Indian-authored primary text naming the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standard. Annex "II. Dissemination of External Debt Statistics in India" states: "India has also been disseminating data on external debt under the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standards (SDDS) and Quarterly External Debt Statistics (QEDS) database jointly developed by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund." and "The external debt statistics of India are disseminated with a lag of three months from the end of the reference quarter in both the country-specific and SDDS format and are accessible at www.finmin.nic.in and www.rbi.org.in." The report also names the IMF's External Debt Statistics Guide as its compilation basis -- Annex (vi): "The external debt statistics are compiled using the methodology and practices prescribed in the 'External Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users' brought out by the IMF", with §2.15 confirming operative use: "the data on India's external debt is presented according to the IMF format (as per the IMF's 2013 EDS Guide format), classified by debtor sectors." That Guide has no corpus node yet; see `_dropped`, along with the reason its footnoted mentions of SNA 2008 and BPM6 are NOT turned into edges. Fetched TIER A from dea.gov.in once the Let's Encrypt YR1 intermediate was supplied to the trust bundle.
reports.cadence_note: Annual -- one status report per financial year, the verified instance being 2024-25 published September 2025. The underlying statistics are quarterly, disseminated "with a lag of three months from the end of the reference quarter" per the report's own Annex II.

reports.title: Developments in India's Balance of Payments (RBI Bulletin quarterly article and associated BoP statistics)
reports.description: The Reserve Bank's quarterly balance-of-payments publication, and a first-person statement that India's BoP is compiled and presented on BPM6. The article's opening paragraph: "The data on India's Balance of Payments (BoP) are compiled and published by the Reserve Bank on a quarterly basis with a lag of one quarter. The compilation of BoP data is based on the IMF guidelines set out in its Balance of Payments Manual (BPM) which is revised from time to time. IMF has recently brought out the Sixth Edition of BPM, i.e., BPM6 which has suggested revised compilation procedure as well as new format of standard presentation of BoP statistics. ... Accordingly, from this quarter (Q4 of 2010-11), BoP data are presented in the revised format as per BPM6." Annex 2 records the Indian decision instrument behind the switch: "The Report of the Working Group on Balance of Payments Manual for India (Chairman: Shri Deepak Mohanty), released by the RBI on its website ... on November 23, 2010, had recommended that the BoP data for India should be presented in the new format of standard presentation of BoP as suggested by the IMF's Balance of Payments Manual (Sixth Edition), i.e., BPM6." The statistical tables are themselves headed "Statement I: Standard Presentation of BoP as per BPM6 (US$ million)", with a table note reading "Changes in Reserve Assets are included under the Financial Account as recommended by the BPM 6." A DATING WEAKNESS is stated rather than hidden: the verified article is the Q4 2010-11 transition issue, so it documents ADOPTION rather than confirming present practice -- however every later RBI BoP statement is still headed "as per BPM6", and the Ministry of Finance's September 2025 external-debt report independently confirms BPM6 as the live framework. A current quarterly BoP press release would strengthen this; those live behind the `rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/PressRelease/PDFs/` bot-wall that this round could not pass. Fetched TIER A as plain HTML from www.rbi.org.in.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly, stated in the publication's own first sentence: "compiled and published by the Reserve Bank on a quarterly basis with a lag of one quarter."

dependencies.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY from the node's OWN release document, and available since BRICS/G.1 without being drawn -- the single cheapest edge in this round. The July 2026 CPI press release, which is `in-mospi-cpi`'s own url, states verbatim: "The CPI (Base: 2024=100) series is aligned with the United Nations' Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018, comprising 12 Divisions, 43 Groups, 92 Classes and 162 Subclasses." That sentence names the classification, its issuing body, AND the edition -- satisfying the edition rule outright, with no companion document required and no inference. It has been quoted in the `in-mospi-cpi` node description since G.1; what was missing was the edge, not the evidence. `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`: COICOP 2018 supplies the index's own classification structure down to the sub-class level, which is method, not reference. Corroborated independently by MoSPI's expert-group report (see the next edge). WEAKNESS STATED: the release says "aligned with", and the expert-group report elaborates that the series is "mostly aligned" -- India uses 12 Divisions against COICOP 2018's 15, with documented mapping compromises where household-survey items could not be mapped unambiguously. The dependency is real and named; the conformance is partial, and this corpus has no relationship type expressing partial conformance, so the qualification is recorded here.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, edition named repeatedly. §3.3: "To enhance credibility and to ensure global comparability of Indian CPI, the latest structure of Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018 will be adopted in the CPI 2024 series." §2.3: "CPI 2024 – The latest classification framework is COICOP 2018. The CPI 2024 series is mostly aligned with COICOP 2018 with 12 Divisions, 43 Groups, 92 Classes and 162 Sub-classes." §4.1.5: "EG recommended for mapping HCES items as per COICOP 2018 in CPI 2024." This is the methodology document that DECIDES the classification the CPI release then reports using, so the two edges into `un-coicop-2018` are complementary rather than duplicative -- one records what the published index is built on, the other records the instrument that chose it. `methodology_depends_on` on the same reasoning as the release-level edge.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, with the edition named and the manual applied NORMATIVELY rather than cited for colour -- it supplies the menu of options from which MoSPI picks its treatment. §4.6.5: "The procedure is fully consistent with the principles of the IMF CPI Manual (2020) and supports a smooth, stable, and operationally feasible implementation of the chain-base CPI." §5.3.2 and §5.3.4 go further and take a decision from it: "This is one of the three methods prescribed in the Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods 2020 (page 35) in case, if the price of social security transfers decreases from some positive amount to zero." followed by the three methods and MoSPI's choice, "Method 1: To use a zero price and adjust the weight during next update. (Proposed for new series of CPI)". §5.4.2 quotes the manual's paragraph 2.60 verbatim. The full title and year are given, with page and paragraph references (p.35, paras 2.60, 2.72). NODE IDENTITY CHECKED before minting: the `cpi-manual` node's own description identifies it as the 2020 edition updating the 2004 ILO-managed predecessor, matching what the Indian document names -- had the node been the 2004 edition, the edition rule would have required refusing this edge. Note the pleasing symmetry with the Russian side of this round: `ru-rosstat-cpi-methodology-915 -> cpi-manual` rests on the same manual, named with the same year, in a document of the same kind.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, edition named, and it closes the question BRICS/G.2 had to leave open. Chapter 2's opening sentence: "As per recommendations of System of National Accounts (SNA)-2008, NAD industry-wise estimates of GDP are compiled using institutional sector approach. All resident institutional units are allocated to one and only one of the following five institutional sectors: i. The non-financial corporation sector; ii. The financial corporation sector; iii. The general government sector; ..." The edition is explicit, the compiler named is the National Accounts Division itself, and the claim is about how India's GDP estimates ARE compiled rather than how they might be. `methodology_depends_on`: "as per recommendations of" introduces the sectoral framework actually used. THE SCOPE LIMIT IS THE REASON THIS EDGE IS MINTED FROM A NEW NODE RATHER THAN FROM `in-mospi-nas`: the quote is from a companion methodology report of the National Accounts Division, not from the body of the National Accounts Statistics publication, whose own release text still says only "System of National Accounts (SNA)" with no year. Attaching the edge to `in-mospi-nas` would put a citation in that node's mouth that its document does not make -- so the report is minted as its own node instead, exactly as the Russian side handles `ru-rosstat-osm-233-household-accounts`. Secondary corroboration in the same PDF (§1.1, "consistent with the System of National Accounts (SNA) guidelines") is unversioned and would not support an edge alone.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A. NIC-2025's Introduction: "The classification aligns with the International Standard Industrial Classification (ISIC Rev. 5) while addressing specific features of the Indian economy such as the informal sector, agriculture, renewable energy, and the growing digital economy." And under Salient Features: "Based on ISIC Rev. 5: NIC-2025 is aligned with the latest international standard, ISIC Revision 5, ensuring structural and conceptual comparability up to the 4-digit class level." `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`: the national classification's structure IS the international one to four digits, which is as strong as a classification dependency gets. NODE-IDENTITY CHECK, and the reason no edition problem arises: the corpus's `isic` node is deliberately the unversioned FAMILY node -- its own description calls it "the acknowledged parent of most national industrial classifications, including ANZSIC and its two predecessors" -- so it is designed to receive citations of any revision, unlike `sna-2008`/`sna-2025` and `un-coicop-2018`/`un-coicop-hbs-1999`, which are edition-split. Recorded because a future round may reasonably propose splitting `isic` by revision, at which point this edge would need re-pointing to a Rev. 5 node, and NIC 2008's separately documented dependency on ISIC Rev. 4 would become mintable as well.

SELF-DECLARED: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, from an Indian-authored, Indian-hosted primary document -- which is what the evidence standard requires, an IMF-side claim of Indian coverage would not qualify. Annex II: "India has also been disseminating data on external debt under the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standards (SDDS) and Quarterly External Debt Statistics (QEDS) database jointly developed by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund." and, operatively: "The external debt statistics of India are disseminated with a lag of three months from the end of the reference quarter in both the country-specific and SDDS format and are accessible at www.finmin.nic.in and www.rbi.org.in." NO EDITION PROBLEM: SDDS is a single named standard rather than an edition series, and the Indian text names it by full title. `methodology_depends_on` because the standard governs the dissemination FORMAT and periodicity actually used -- the dependency is on SDDS's dissemination dimension, stated plainly here rather than implied to be broader.
dependencies.evidence_quote: India has also been disseminating data on external debt under the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standards (SDDS) and Quarterly External Debt Statistics (QEDS) database jointly developed by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.

dependencies.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, first-person and edition-named. "The compilation of BoP data is based on the IMF guidelines set out in its Balance of Payments Manual (BPM) ... IMF has recently brought out the Sixth Edition of BPM, i.e., BPM6 which has suggested revised compilation procedure as well as new format of standard presentation of BoP statistics. ... Accordingly, from this quarter (Q4 of 2010-11), BoP data are presented in the revised format as per BPM6." The RBI's own statistical tables carry it in their headings -- "Statement I: Standard Presentation of BoP as per BPM6 (US$ million)" -- and a table note reads "Changes in Reserve Assets are included under the Financial Account as recommended by the BPM 6." `methodology_depends_on`: BPM6 supplies both the compilation procedure and the presentation format of India's published BoP. TENSE WEAKNESS STATED HONESTLY, since this project's own spec insists on it: the verified article is the Q4 2010-11 transition issue, so its central sentence documents the moment of adoption. That is a PAST-tense event, and on its own would be exactly the kind of past arrangement this corpus refuses to treat as a live dependency. It is minted because two independent present-tense confirmations exist: the RBI's statistical statements are still headed "as per BPM6", and the Ministry of Finance's September 2025 external-debt report treats BPM6 as the current framework. A current RBI quarterly BoP press release would remove the caveat entirely and is a clean lead -- blocked only by the `rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/PressRelease/PDFs/` bot-wall.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, and structurally the most important edge in this file: `in-fc15-report` sits inside India's main eleven-node component, so this single citation is what attaches the whole Finance Commission cluster -- Constitution, Commission reports, Explanatory Memoranda, Union Budget, RBI State Finances, CAG -- to the international layer. FC15 Volume I cites the WEO in two footnotes supporting its macroeconomic narrative: "1 World Economic Outlook, October 2020" and "4 World Economic Outlook October 2020, International Monetary Fund". `uses_data_from` rather than `methodology_depends_on`, deliberately: the WEO supplies comparator data and growth figures the Commission reasons from; it is not a standard the Commission's methodology conforms to. ON THE EDITION QUESTION, which the research flagged and which is worth settling here as a corpus rule: `imf-weo` is NOT edition-split and should not be, because the WEO is a RECURRING PUBLICATION, not a standard with successor editions held as separate nodes. This corpus models a recurring release as one node covering all its issues -- `br-ipca` covers every month, `cn-nbs-statistical-communique` every year -- so citing the October 2020 issue is like citing a particular month of a monthly index, and points at the series node correctly. That is a different situation from SNA 2008 versus SNA 2025, which are successive STANDARDS deliberately held apart. WEAKNESS STATED: this is a footnote citation, the weakest form of dependency in this project's taxonomy. A third mention (the source line of Figure 2.2, "Sources: IMF, World Economic Outlook, and staff calculations") is unversioned and would not qualify alone.
dependencies.evidence_quote: 1 World Economic Outlook, October 2020

_dropped.edge: in-gasab-igfrs-1 -> ipsas (GASAB's IGFRS 1 residual dependency on IPSAS)
_dropped.why: REFUSED FOR LACK OF RAW VERIFICATION, and recorded at length because it is a live application of this project's hardest-won methodological rule rather than a routine access failure. The apparent evidence is excellent: GASAB's *IGFRS 1 – Presentation of Financial Statements* reportedly states "Where relevant IGFRSs on specific accounting transactions are not available, the Government entity shall follow relevant International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), till an appropriate IGFRS is formulated" -- a RESIDUAL NORMATIVE dependency, which is the strongest possible form: IPSAS is the operative rule wherever no Indian standard exists. It also reportedly names IPSAS 1 and IPSAS 2 by number. THE PROBLEM: `gasab.gov.in` cannot be reached from this environment at all. Verified this session, twice, with a browser User-Agent: both `https://gasab.gov.in/gasab/pdf/IGFRS-1.pdf` and `https://gasab.gov.in/` return `curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` (000/0), and plain HTTP returns 503. The content above was obtained by the research agent through WebFetch, on a different egress, and could not be independently confirmed. AF/G.24 established that WebFetch has FABRICATED plausible content for unreachable URLs rather than reporting failure, and this corpus's standing rule is to raw-verify before trusting any fetched quotation. The quotations may well be genuine -- they read entirely plausibly -- and that is precisely why the rule exists. NO EDGE, NO NODE. This is the highest-value single lead for a future round: one successful fetch of IGFRS 1 from a network that can reach gasab.gov.in mints a node and an edge, and connects India's public-sector accounting to the same `ipsas` node Brazil's `br-mcasp` already reaches.

REFUSED as transitive, on this project's own "comparable with is not a dependency" rule. Both editions ARE named, in one sentence, in a footnote to the external-debt report: "The concepts set out in the IMF's External Debt Statistics (EDS) Guide 2013 are harmonized with those of the System of National Accounts (SNA) 2008 and the sixth edition of the IMF's Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual (BPM6) published in 2009." But read carefully, that sentence asserts a property of the EDS GUIDE, not a dependency of India's statistics: it says the Guide is HARMONIZED WITH SNA 2008 and BPM6. India's own stated dependency, in Annex (vi), is on the Guide -- "compiled using the methodology and practices prescribed in the 'External Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users' brought out by the IMF" -- so any dependency on SNA 2008 or BPM6 from this document is INDIRECT, running through the Guide. REPORTS.md states plainly that "comparable with"-type language is not a dependency, and "harmonized with" is the same shape. Minting these would also double-count: India's BPM6 dependency is separately and directly evidenced from the RBI, and is minted from there. The honest fix is to mint the EDS Guide as its own node and edge this report to it -- see the next entry.

_dropped.edge: in-mof-external-debt-status-report -> IMF External Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users (2013)
_dropped.why: A fully evidenced, edition-named dependency on an international manual the corpus does not hold. §2.15 states operative use: "the data on India's external debt is presented according to the IMF format (as per the IMF's 2013 EDS Guide format), classified by debtor sectors", and a further footnote pins the same 2013 edition alongside BPM6. Target would be *External Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users* (2013), IMF et al., `https://www.imf.org/external/np/sta/ed/guide.htm`. Would be `methodology_depends_on` at STRONG confidence. NOTE AN EDITION SUBTLETY for whoever mints it: the same Indian report ALSO cites the 2003 edition, for a different purpose -- the definition of external debt -- so two editions are in play in one document and a corpus that splits them will need both, exactly as it splits SNA. Note also that Annex (vi)'s statement gives the Guide's title UNVERSIONED; the 2013 year comes from §2.15 and the footnote, so the edge depends on reading the document as a whole.

STILL REFUSED at the NAS publication level, and the refusal is unchanged from BRICS/G.2 even though the SNA 2008 edge now exists elsewhere in the corpus. The NAS release's own text says only: "These estimates are presented at current and constant (2011-12) prices and are based on the methodologies in alignment with the United Nations System of National Accounts (SNA)." -- no year. Under the edition rule that cannot select between `sna-2008` and `sna-2025`. What CHANGED this round is that a current, non-obsolete MoSPI document naming "System of National Accounts (SNA)-2008" was found and minted as `in-mospi-gdp-base-revision-2026`, so India's national accounts are now attached to SNA 2008 in the graph -- just not from this node, because this node's document does not say it. Recorded so a future session does not read the new edge and conclude the NAS-level one was an oversight.

_dropped.edge: in-mospi-cpi -> un-coicop-hbs-1999 (via the predecessor CPI 2012=100 series)
_dropped.why: REFUSED on two independent grounds, both worth recording. MoSPI's expert-group report does name an edition for the OLD series: "In India, in the CPI (2012=100) series COICOP 1999 was adopted with some deviations to classify the items into different groups, subgroups and sections", and "The series was partially aligned with UNSD endorsed classification system i.e. Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 1999." GROUND ONE: the dependent is the CPI 2012=100 series, which the corpus does not hold -- `in-mospi-cpi` is the 2024=100 series, a different index with a different classification, so attaching this to it would be a wrong-target error. GROUND TWO: the Indian text says plain "COICOP 1999" (UNSD), whereas the corpus node id `un-coicop-hbs-1999` reads as the *Household Budget Surveys* variant -- these may be different publications, and that identity question should be settled before any edge is drawn to that node from anywhere. The relationship is also expressly superseded. If a future round wants an `in-mospi-cpi-2012` node, this is a ready edge subject to ground two.

NOT FOUND for the specific existing nodes. The State Finances Audit Report does not name IPSAS, nor ISSAI 300 (Performance Audit Principles) or ISSAI 400 (Compliance Audit Principles) -- the two INTOSAI nodes the corpus happens to hold. Separately, CAG's *Auditing Standards 2017* WERE found to cite INTOSAI's ISSAI framework, but not those two instruments, so forcing that citation onto `intosai-issai-300`/`intosai-issai-400` would be a wrong-target error of the same kind refused for the ICLS resolution on the Russian side of this round. Minting CAG's Auditing Standards as a node, together with whichever ISSAIs it actually names, is a clean and well-scoped lead for a future round -- and would give India's audit tier an international attachment matching the one Brazil's `br-mcasp -> ipsas` already provides.

NOT FOUND, and a genuine surprise worth recording rather than passing over. The UN's *Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses* is the obvious international standard for a national census, the corpus already holds it as `un-census-principles`, and India's census is among the largest statistical operations in the world -- yet no reachable Census of India document naming it was located this round. This may well be a search limitation rather than an absence: census methodology is spread across administrative manuals and instruction booklets rather than a single methodology volume, and `censusindia.gov.in` required a trust-store fix to reach at all. Recorded as an open lead rather than a settled negative.

NOT FOUND. India's Union Budget documents do not name GFSM 2014, IPSAS or the SNA. This is consistent with the pattern BRICS/G.2 found in the same documents -- their only reference to the Finance Commission was a budget-head label -- and with the broader observation that Indian budget documents are presentational rather than methodological. Recorded so a future round does not re-search them. The Indian government-finance-statistics dependency, if one is documented anywhere, is more likely to sit with the Controller General of Accounts or GASAB than in the Budget itself.

NOT FOUND, and notable as a contrast with its own predecessor. FC15 cites the IMF World Economic Outlook by name and issue -- the edge minted in this file -- whereas the Sixteenth Finance Commission's Volume I names no international standard or international publication at all. WEAKNESS IN THE NEGATIVE, stated so it is not over-read: only Volume I (Main Report) was scanned for this question; Volume II (Annexures) was not, and it is Volume II that carried FC16's richest data-source citations in BRICS/G.2 (the RBI State Finances study, Statement 18, the Economic Survey). A future round should scan Volume II before treating this as settled.

_dropped.edge: Indian constitutional and statutory instruments -> any international standard
_dropped.why: NOT FOUND, expected, and recorded once for completeness so no future round spends effort on it. `in-constitution-art280`, `in-rbi-act-45za`, `in-gst-compensation-act-2017`, `in-fc16-tor-order`, `in-fc16-explanatory-memorandum` and `in-fc15-explanatory-memorandum` are constitutional, statutory and executive instruments, and Indian primary legislation does not as a drafting convention incorporate foreign or supranational statistical standards by reference. WEAKNESS STATED: this is asserted from document type plus the FC16 full-text sweep, not from a full-text sweep of each instrument individually.

UNRESOLVED rather than NOT FOUND -- the distinction matters. The RBI publication landing page resolves (HTTP 200, foreword text confirmed present) but the report PDF links are injected client-side and resolve to `rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/Publications/PDFs/...`, which this round could not enumerate from the returned HTML. BRICS/G.2 did retrieve this PDF using the cookie-plus-Referer method, so it is reachable in principle and a future round should simply reuse the URL recorded in `in-g2-finance-commission-chain.json`. A priori a GFSM citation is unlikely -- the publication is analytical rather than a compilation manual -- but that is a prediction, not a finding.

_dropped.edge: PEFA Framework for assessing public financial management (2016), and the RBI Working Group on Balance of Payments Manual for India (2010), as nodes
_dropped.why: Two further named instruments surfaced this round with no corpus node. (1) FC15 Volume I cites the PEFA Framework with a full methodological description -- "PEFA is a methodology for assessing public financial management performance. It identifies ninety-four characteristics (dimensions) across thirty-one key components of public financial management (indicators) in seven broad areas of activity (pillars)." PEFA is a real international assessment framework and the corpus already holds one PEFA-derived African document (`bf-pefa-ouagadougou-2021`), so a PEFA Framework node would serve more than one branch. (2) The *Report of the Working Group on Balance of Payments Manual for India* (Chairman: Deepak Mohanty), RBI, released 23 November 2010, is the Indian instrument that DECIDED the BPM6 adoption and would be the cleanest possible source node for an `-> imf-bpm6` edge -- better than the transition-quarter bulletin article minted here, because it is a standing decision document rather than a dated news item. It was named but not retrieved this round.

reports.title: The Collection of Statistics Act, 2008
reports.publisher: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation / Parliament of India
reports.description: Principal legislation facilitating the collection of statistics on economic, demographic, social, scientific and environmental aspects. Empowers appropriate governments (Central, State, UT, local) to direct statistical surveys, appoint statistics officers, and impose duties on informants. Repealed the Collection of Statistics Act, 1953. Enforced from 11 June 2010. Rules under the Act include the Collection of Statistics Rules, 2011 (superseded) and Collection of Statistics Rules, 2024.

reports.title: The Census Act, 1948
reports.publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs / Parliament of India
reports.description: Legal framework providing for the taking of the population census in India. Empowers the Central Government to take the census, appoint census staff, and imposes obligations on the public and local authorities. Census is Entry 69 of the Union List. Rules framed under the Act include the Census Rules, 1990 (as amended).

reports.title: National Accounts Statistics
reports.publisher: National Statistics Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
reports.description: Annual comprehensive publication presenting detailed estimates of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Gross Value Added (GVA), consumption, savings, capital formation and related macroeconomic aggregates at current and constant prices. Aligned with the United Nations System of National Accounts (SNA). Includes sectoral breakdowns, institutional sector accounts and time series. The 2025 edition covers Final Estimates for FY 2022-23 and First Revised Estimates for FY 2023-24 (2011-12 series at the time of that release). Base-year revision to 2022-23 underway with new series release targeted for early 2026.

reports.title: Index of Industrial Production (IIP)
reports.publisher: National Statistics Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
reports.description: Monthly index measuring changes in the volume of production in the industrial sector. New series with base year 2022-23 launched June 2026 expands coverage beyond Mining, Manufacturing and Electricity to include Gas Supply, Water Supply, Sewerage and Waste Management; adopts NIC-2025 classification and Output PPI as deflator (replacing earlier WPI-based series). Quick Estimates released approximately 28 days after the reference month. Key high-frequency input into quarterly GDP estimation.

reports.title: Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)
reports.publisher: National Statistics Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
reports.description: Primary source of data on employment and unemployment in India. Launched in 2017. Provides estimates of Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) under both Usual Status (ps+ss) and Current Weekly Status (CWS). From January 2025 the sampling design was modified to generate monthly and quarterly estimates for both rural and urban areas under CWS, in addition to the annual report. Annual Reports and Monthly/Quarterly Bulletins are released regularly.

reports.title: Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES)
reports.publisher: National Statistics Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
reports.description: Large-scale household survey collecting information on consumption of goods and services. Generates estimates of Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE) and its distribution for rural and urban sectors, States/UTs and socio-economic groups. Two consecutive surveys conducted post-COVID: HCES 2022-23 (August 2022–July 2023) and HCES 2023-24 (August 2023–July 2024). Results used for poverty analysis, CPI weighting, and national accounts consumption estimates. Fact sheets and detailed reports released by MoSPI; unit-level data disseminated via microdata portal.

reports.title: Census of India
reports.publisher: Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India (Ministry of Home Affairs)
reports.description: Decennial population and housing census providing the most comprehensive demographic, social and economic profile of the population. Conducted under the Census Act, 1948. Last completed census was 2011. Census 2021 postponed; Census 2027 announced and under preparation (Houselisting Operations scheduled 2026, Population Enumeration to follow). Primary source for population totals, literacy, workforce, housing and many derived indicators used across the statistical system.

reports.title: Sample Registration System (SRS) Statistical Report

_note: Continues the [Agent] todo 'India's NSDP, from a new direction' (HANDOFF.md). The IMF's own dsbb list endpoint gives dea.gov.in/sites/default/files/nsdp.htm as India's NSDPUrl -- confirmed dead again this round from three networks (cloud sandbox curl: connection reset; the linked device's own network: connection refused; WebFetch alone reached it but the page it returned never mentions SDDS or the IMF at all, so even a working route to it would not have helped). Followed the todo's own lead instead: searched mospi.gov.in and rbi.org.in directly rather than retrying dea.gov.in. mospi.gov.in's own NSDP announcement page (https://www.mospi.gov.in/announcements/summary-data-real-sector-nsdp-sdds-0) is a Drupal JS shell that returns 2.7KB of chrome and no body text to a plain fetch -- consistent with the standing note that mospi.gov.in needs a live browser to render, not pursued further this round since RBI's route worked cleanly. RBI hosts its own NSDP under classic server-rendered ASP.NET (no JS-shell problem): its 'Sources of Information' page (https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/SDDSview.aspx, raw-verified via cloud-sandbox curl, HTTP 200, 67,519 bytes) states RBI's SDDS role directly and links onward, labelled 'National Summary Data Page', to https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_NSDPDisplay.aspx -- also raw-verified, HTTP 200, 172,361 bytes, live data dated September 2026 (Date of Publish: Sep 04, 2026; table rows dated as late as August 28, 2026), structured exactly per SDDS categories (Reserves Template, International Investment Position, External Debt, Advance Release Calendar) and headed in its own markup 'SDDS-NATIONAL SUMMARY DATA PAGE-INDIA'. This is a live, current, first-party NSDP that the IMF's own dsbb record for India (a dead dea.gov.in link) does not surface -- the standing lead's 'somewhere other than dea.gov.in' is this page. Node minted from BS_NSDPDisplay.aspx (what the NSDP IS); evidence_url and evidence_quote instead point to SDDSview.aspx, the companion RBI page that names SDDS and NSDP together in the same two sentences and links directly to the NSDP page by that label -- chosen over the NSDP page's own table-header labels because the two mentions of 'SDDS' sit inside the same sentence as the declarative claim, guaranteeing they land in the same grading window, rather than relying on a data-table heading several thousand characters from any full sentence. No id or evidence-URL collision found against the whole corpus (research + seed files) for in-nsdp, rbi.org.in/scripts/SDDSview.aspx or rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_NSDPDisplay.aspx.

reports.title: National Summary Data Page — India
reports.description: India's National Summary Data Page as hosted by the Reserve Bank of India, the single page of macroeconomic and financial data the IMF's SDDS prescribes and monitors on the Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board. The IMF's own dsbb list endpoint points to a dead dea.gov.in URL for India (confirmed unreachable across three networks this round and in round 8/9); this is the live, current alternative RBI itself hosts and updates (data dated September 2026 at the time of research), reached via RBI's 'Sources of Information → SDDS' page rather than the IMF's stale pointer. Coverage, periodicity and timeliness of every category on it are set by the standard, which is what the edge to imf-sdds records.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated data page with no discrete editions: the standard prescribes a periodicity and a timeliness per data category, and the page is refreshed as each category releases. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7) — a nominal releases_per_year so the pulse reads as continuous rather than one-off; 250 encodes business-day updating. It is a statement of continuous flow, not a claim of counted editions.

This section provides the data released by the Reserve Bank of India under SDDS requirements.' and immediately below that sentence links, labelled 'National Summary Data Page', to https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_NSDPDisplay.aspx -- the node this edge is drawn from. meta.source: research round 2026-09-16 — India, the NSS sampling-frame layer. Thomas: “honestly i doubt there is value in india, look for new edges and nodes anyway”.
meta.note:
INDIA, AND THE DOUBT WAS HALF RIGHT. RESULT: 1 node, 10 dependencies, 3 dropped notes.

WHY THE COVERAGE CHART OVERSELLS INDIA. It showed 37 zero-edge nodes. TWENTY-EIGHT of those carry their publisher's BARE HOMEPAGE as their own url, so they are not research waiting to happen, they are the August 2026 import's url-and-granularity defect wearing a research job's clothes. Only 8 orphans carry a real document url. That part of Thomas's doubt was correct and is why this round did not touch the state-level layer at all.

WHERE THE VALUE ACTUALLY WAS, and it was not in the orphan list. The National Sample Survey family — PLFS, HCES, ASUSE and the NSS health round — publishes a full study description per survey on MoSPI's own microdata portal, and every one of them states its sampling frame in the same sentence: Urban Frame Survey blocks for urban, the Census 2011 village list for rural. The corpus already held the rural half and had never held the urban half. Minting `in-ufs` turned one node into four in-edges immediately, and the same four pages paid the Census 2011 node four more — eight edges off four fetches, which is the yield shape this project wants. Two further edges came from the IIP and ASI pages: the IIP's manufacturing weights are built on ASI results, and the ASI is conducted under the Collection of Statistics Act 2008.

THREE ORPHANS STOPPED BEING ORPHANS: `in-mospi-nss-health`, `in-mospi-asi` and `in-collection-of-statistics-act-2008` all had zero edges in either direction before this round.

ONE DIRECTION CORRECTION. The August import recorded `in-collection-of-statistics-act-2008 -> in-mospi-asi`, the Act depending on the survey. That is backwards and the note is rewritten `resolved` against the edge minted here.

THE ROUTE FINDING, which is worth more than this round. microdata.gov.in and censusindia.gov.in BOTH answer only with `curl -k`; a plain fetch gets nothing. So does mahades.maharashtra.gov.in, which a 2026-08-30 note records as 'fails DNS resolution'. These are certificate-chain gaps, not walls, and re-probing on that basis moved India's reachable-orphan count from the handful that round implied to 19 of 37. Details in notes/india-nss-frames-2026-09-16.md.

Every quote was verified against the exact `stripHtml` output the grader reads before the slice was written.

reports.description: The urban half of the sampling frame behind every National Sample Survey. NSO's own microdata portal publishes it under this title with survey ID DDI-IND-NSO-UFS. It is minted here because four separate NSS survey pages — PLFS, HCES, ASUSE and the NSS health round — each name the UFS block list as the frame for their urban first-stage units, in the same sentence that names Census 2011 as the rural one: the corpus held the rural half (`in-census-2011`) and not the urban half. Minted 2026-09-16.
reports.cadence_note: UFS runs in roughly five-year cycles — ASUSE's own page names the live ones as 'UFS 2017-22 or UFS 2022-27', which is the only cadence statement any of the four pages makes, and 0.2 is that rate written as a number. The portal's own page carries no release schedule.

_dropped.why: A real, cleanly stated dependency with no node to point at. ASUSE's own study description: 'Auxiliary information such as number of workers, etc. available from Sixth Economic Census (EC) frame was used for stratification, sub-stratification and selection of FSUs in rural areas (except Kerala).' The Economic Census is a distinct NSO product and the microdata portal lists it as a collection, but no catalog study page for it was found in the listing this round, so there is no first-party url to carry a node. One page find closes this. Recorded rather than minted because a node needs the publisher's own page, not a mention inside another survey.

BOTH documents read this round cite NIC-2008 and the corpus has only NIC-2025 (`in-mospi-nic-2025`). The IIP page apportions weights 'at the 2-digit, 3-digit- and 4-digit level of the National Industrial Classification (NIC)' and the ASI page strata are 'State x District x Sector x 3 digit NIC-2008'. NOT WIRED TO `in-mospi-nic-2025`, which would be the wrong target: NIC-2008 and NIC-2025 are different editions of the classification and these surveys name the 2008 one. Minting NIC-2008 needs MoSPI's own page for it, and mospi.gov.in is a JavaScript single-page application that serves an identical 2,657-byte shell for every path this container requests — the classification volume is not reachable by curl. A browser round closes it.
