reports.title: Statistics Act (통계법)
reports.description: Framework law governing the production, dissemination and use of official statistics in the Republic of Korea. Wholly amended in 2007 (Act No. 8387) and subsequently revised. Establishes the purpose of statistics as a public resource for rational decision-making, requires scientific methods to ensure accuracy, timeliness, consistency and impartiality, and provides the legal basis for designated statistics, statistical agencies and coordination by the Commissioner of Statistics Korea.
reports._notes: Foundational legal node, parallel to Japan’s Statistics Act 2007. Continuously cited as the authority for the reliability and coordination of official statistics. Qualifies under the expanded definition as a static instrument that is recurringly referenced in the operation of the entire statistical system.
_referenced_by: KOSTAT methodological documents and designation of official statistics
KOSIS portal and official statistical programmes
International assessments of Korea’s statistical system (IMF SDDS, OECD, UN)

reports.title: Statistics Korea (KOSTAT) — national statistical office
reports.description: Central government agency responsible for producing, coordinating and disseminating official statistics. Operates the KOSIS (Korean Statistical Information Service) portal, conducts major censuses and surveys, and designates official statistics under the Statistics Act.
reports._notes: Institutional node. KOSTAT is the primary producer of demographic, labour, price, household and many economic statistics and the coordinator of the national statistical system.
_referenced_by: All KOSTAT survey and census releases
National accounts and other agencies that rely on KOSTAT source data

reports.title: Population and Housing Census (인구주택총조사)
reports.description: Decennial (with inter-censal updates and register-based elements) complete enumeration of population, households and housing. Provides the benchmark for population estimates, sampling frames and a wide range of demographic and social statistics.
reports._cadence_original: null (primarily every 5–10 years with continuous updates)
reports._notes: Core demographic foundation. Used for population projections, electoral apportionment, sampling frames for household surveys, and as the reference for ageing and household-structure analysis. Parallel to Japan’s Population Census node.
reports._cadence_evidence: url not retrievable - kostat.go.kr blocks WebFetch (robots.txt fetch failed); retried, same result.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (소비자물가지수)
reports.description: Monthly measure of changes in the prices of a fixed basket of consumer goods and services. Official inflation indicator used for monetary-policy assessment, indexation and real-income analysis.
reports._notes: Primary price indicator. Continuously watched by the Bank of Korea, markets and policy makers. Base-year revisions and methodological updates are documented and cited in subsequent releases.

reports.title: Economically Active Population Survey (경제활동인구조사)
reports.description: Monthly household survey that measures the labour force, employment, unemployment and non-participation, with detailed breakdowns by age, sex, industry, occupation and employment status. Korea’s official labour-force statistics.
reports._notes: Core labour-market indicator. Provides the official unemployment rate and employment figures used in macroeconomic analysis, social policy and international comparisons (ILO concepts). Parallel to Japan’s Labour Force Survey.

reports.title: Household Income and Expenditure Survey (가계동향조사 / related household income surveys)
reports.description: Periodic household survey measuring income, expenditure, consumption patterns and living conditions. Source for distributional analysis, poverty-related indicators and the weights of the CPI basket.
reports._notes: Key source for living standards, inequality and consumption analysis. Complements the labour-force and price series and feeds into national-accounts household-sector estimates.
reports._cadence_evidence: url not retrievable - kostat.go.kr blocks WebFetch (robots.txt fetch failed); retried, same result.

reports.title: Korean System of National Accounts / GDP and related aggregates (국민계정)
reports.description: Quarterly and annual national accounts compiled by the Bank of Korea in accordance with international standards (SNA). Includes GDP by production, expenditure and income approaches, institutional-sector accounts, and related aggregates.
reports._notes: Core macroeconomic framework. BOK is the primary compiler of the Korean System of National Accounts. Continuously used for growth analysis, fiscal and monetary policy, and international comparisons. Parallel to Japan’s JSNA (CAO/ESRI) node.
reports._cadence_evidence: bok.or.kr/eng retrieved, but its release listing (Apr 2026) contains no national accounts / GDP item, no stated periodicity and no link to a publication calendar; nothing to count.

reports.title: Balance of Payments and International Investment Position
reports.description: Monthly / quarterly balance-of-payments statistics and related external accounts compiled according to BPM6. Includes current account, capital and financial account, and international investment position.
reports._notes: Primary external-sector statistics. Closely watched given Korea’s export-oriented economy and large current-account swings. Links to trade statistics and to national-accounts external transactions.
reports._cadence_evidence: BOK release list shows 'Balance of Payments during February 2026 (preliminary)' published 8 April 2026 - one release per reference month.

reports.title: Monthly Survey of Mining and Manufacturing (광업제조업동향조사) / Industrial Production Index
reports.description: Monthly survey of production, shipments and inventories in mining and manufacturing, used to compile the Index of Industrial Production and related short-term indicators.
reports._notes: Key short-term activity indicator for Korea’s manufacturing-heavy economy (semiconductors, autos, shipbuilding, etc.). Parallel to Japan’s Current Survey of Production / IIP cluster.

reports.title: KOSIS — Korean Statistical Information Service (국가통계포털)
reports.description: Central online portal and dissemination platform for official statistics produced by KOSTAT and other agencies. Provides searchable access to time series, census results, and statistical publications.
reports._notes: Infrastructure node analogous to Japan’s e-Stat. The practical gateway through which most official Korean statistics are accessed and cited.
reports._cadence_evidence: kosis.kr/eng is a live dissemination portal with continuously refreshed indicator tiles (e.g. '24.10 employment, '24.09 industry) and search/history features; no discrete edition and no stated release frequency.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7) and applied 2026-08-19: a nominal releases_per_year so that absence keeps meaning 'one-off instrument' only - 250 encodes business-day updating (the live corpus's daily-FX convention), 365 genuinely all-days monitoring. It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

reports.title: Bank of Korea (한국은행) — statistical function
reports.description: Central bank with primary responsibility for national accounts, flow of funds, balance of payments, monetary and financial statistics, and related macroeconomic indicators. Complements KOSTAT in the production of official economic statistics.
reports._notes: Institutional node. In Korea the division of labour between KOSTAT (many survey-based and demographic statistics) and BOK (national accounts, BOP, monetary) is a defining feature of the statistical system, parallel to the SBJ–BOJ / CAO division in Japan.
_referenced_by: Korean System of National Accounts releases
Balance of Payments and monetary statistics
Monetary-policy reports and financial-stability assessments that rely on BOK statistical series

reports.title: Producer Price Index (생산자물가지수)
reports.description: Monthly index of prices received by domestic producers for their output. Complements the CPI as the main producer-side inflation measure.
reports._notes: Important for national-accounts deflation, margin analysis and understanding cost-push pressures in Korea’s export-oriented manufacturing sector. Parallel to Japan’s CGPI.

reports.title: Trade Statistics (수출입무역통계) — Korea Customs Service / MOTIR
reports.publisher: Korea Customs Service / Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources (MOTIR)
reports.description: Monthly and annual customs-based merchandise trade statistics by commodity, partner country, and enterprise characteristics. Primary source for Korea’s export and import performance, including the high concentration in semiconductors and other key items.
reports._notes: Core external-trade series for an economy whose growth is heavily export-driven. Continuously cited in BOP analysis, industrial policy and FTA impact assessments. Complements BOK Balance of Payments with detailed commodity and partner matrices.

reports.title: Financial Statement Analysis (기업경영분석) — Bank of Korea
reports.description: Annual (with related quarterly elements) analysis of the financial statements of Korean corporations, covering sales, profitability, stability, growth and financial ratios by industry and firm size. Long-running series (published since 1960) that provides the empirical basis for assessing corporate-sector health, including large business groups.
reports._notes: Key corporate-sector statistics. Directly relevant to analysis of Korea’s concentrated industrial structure (large enterprises / business groups). Complements the Mining & Manufacturing Survey and national accounts with accounting-based measures of profitability, leverage and investment. Parallel to Japan’s Financial Statements Statistics of Corporations.
reports._cadence_evidence: bok.or.kr/eng retrieved but shows no Financial Statement Analysis release, no stated frequency and no release calendar.

reports.title: Vital Statistics — Births, Deaths, Marriages, Divorces (인구동향조사 / 출생·사망통계)
reports.description: Annual (with monthly/quarterly provisional) statistics on live births, deaths, marriages and divorces, including the total fertility rate (TFR), crude rates and age-specific rates. Documents Korea’s ultra-low fertility (TFR recently around 0.7–0.8) and rapid demographic transition.
reports._notes: Core demographic series that quantifies one of Korea’s most distinctive features — the world’s lowest total fertility rate. Main technique: Korea's statistical agency (KOSTAT, now reorganized as the Ministry/National Data and Statistics, mods.go.kr) publishes '통계정보보고서' (Statistical Information Reports) and '정기통계품질진단' (Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis) reports for each official statistic, which explicitly state the international manual/standard each statistic follows and/or the other Korean statistic it draws its sampling frame or source data from; every edge below was minted only after fetching the actual PDF/press release and locating the exact quoted sentence. Yield: 20 verified edges wiring 15 of the 32 unlinked nodes (about 47%). Several additional leads (PPI, Wage Structure Survey, Housing Price Survey, Financial Stability Report/Basel) were checked but not minted because the fetched document either lacked an explicit, unambiguous statement or (for BOK's Basel appendix) could not be retrieved due to a signed-URL/CDN fetch failure; these are recorded in _dropped for follow-up. UPDATE 2026-08-29 (import follow-up, raw-verified by the orchestrating session): closed the kr-financial-stability -> bis-basel-framework lead — the signed bok.or.kr download URL that failed the first attempt succeeded on a retry (281,837 bytes, matching).

dependencies.basis: Official KOSTAT-affiliated newsletter (통계의 창, published by the National Statistics Human Resources Development Institute) states, in its feature on the 2025 Agricultural, Forestry and Fishery Census: "농림어업총조사는 국제연합(UN) 식량농업기구(FAO)의 세계농업총조사 권고안에 따라 국제적으로 130여 개 국가가 수행하는 범세계적인 센서스이다." ("The Agricultural, Forestry and Fishery Census is a worldwide census conducted by roughly 130 countries in accordance with the recommendations of the UN Food and Agriculture Organization's World Programme for the Census of Agriculture.") This directly ties Korea's agriculture/fishery census methodology to the FAO WCA framework.

KOSTAT's own classification-standards portal (kssc.kostat.go.kr), in its official history of the Korean Standard Classification of Diseases (KCD) used to compile Korea's cause-of-death and health statistics, states: "세계보건기구(WHO)가 작성한 국제질병분류(ICD) 체계를 근간으로 한국표준질병‧사인(死因)분류(KCD)를 작성하여 왔다" ("[Korea] has compiled the Korean Standard Classification of Diseases (KCD) on the basis of the International Classification of Diseases (ICD) system prepared by the World Health Organization (WHO)"), and specifically for the 3rd revision: "제43차 세계보건총회(1990년)에서 제10차 국제질병분류를 개정하여 회원국에 적용토록 권고함에 따라 이를 기초로 한국표준질병‧사인(死因)분류를 3차 개정하여 1995.1.1.부터 시행하였다" ("Following the WHO's 43rd World Health Assembly (1990) recommendation that member states adopt the 10th revision of the ICD, Korea's 3rd revision of the KCD was based on it and took effect 1995.1.1."). This is the classification underlying Korea's cause-of-death/health statistics.
dependencies.evidence_quote: 세계보건기구(WHO)가 작성한 국제질병분류(ICD) 체계를 근간으로 한국표준질병‧사인(死因)분류(KCD)를 작성하여 왔다

dependencies.basis: Government Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report on Korea's Monetary and Financial Statistics (통화금융통계, 2023) states: "우리나라의 통화금융통계는 IMF의 「통화금융통계 매뉴얼 및 편제 가이드」에 따라 작성되고 있는 것으로 확인되었다." ("Korea's monetary and financial statistics were confirmed to be compiled in accordance with the IMF's 'Monetary and Financial Statistics Manual and Compilation Guide.'") and separately "IMF의 통화금융통계 매뉴얼을 준수하고 있으며" ("[BOK] complies with the IMF's Monetary and Financial Statistics Manual"). This is the exact manual represented by the corpus node imf-mfsmcg-2016.

Government Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report on Korea's Flow of Funds (자금순환표, 2020) states: "자금순환표는 국제기준인 국민계정체계(SNA)에 따라 매분기 동일하게 작성되어... 동 기준의 개정(SNA1953→SNA1968→SNA1993→SNA2008)으로 인해 체계별로는 형태, 부문 분류가 상이" ("The Flow of Funds table is compiled quarterly according to the international standard, the System of National Accounts (SNA)... due to revisions of that standard [SNA1953→SNA1968→SNA1993→SNA2008], the form and sector classifications differ by vintage"), and elsewhere confirms the current vintage: "2014년 : SNA2008에 따른 개편 완료" ("2014: reform based on SNA2008 completed").

Government Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report on Korea's R&D Activity Survey (연구개발활동조사, 2015) states: "연구개발활동조사는 연구개발활동 현황에 대한 국가 간 비교가 작성 목적의 한 부분이기 때문에 통계의 개념 및 작성방법, 조사기준 등을 OECD의 '연구개발 조사를 위한 표준지침(Frascati Manual)'에 기초하여 설계하고 있다." ("Because international comparability is part of the survey's purpose, the concepts, compilation methods and survey standards of the R&D Activity Survey are designed based on the OECD's 'Standard Guideline for R&D Surveys (Frascati Manual).'")

Government Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report on Korea's Input-Output Tables (산업연관표, 2019) states: "산업연관표는 국민계정 편제를 위한 국제기준인 2008 SNA(System of National Accounts)와 동일한 기준에 따라 작성되며" ("The Input-Output Tables are compiled according to the same standard as 2008 SNA (System of National Accounts), the international standard for compiling national accounts.")

dependencies.basis: Government Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report on Korea's Trade Statistics (무역통계, Korea Customs Service, 2018) states: "무역통계는 수출입 신고 업무처리 절차를 기초로 수집한 자료를 품목분류번호(HS Code), 관세청분류체계(성질별·신성질별), 국가별, 세관별 등 여러가지 기준에 따라... 집계" and "'92년 이후 HS 8단위 수준까지 통계를 작성하고 있으며" ("Trade statistics classify data collected via customs declarations by item classification number (HS Code)... and since 1992 have compiled statistics down to the HS 8-digit level").

Government Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report on the Bank of Korea's Financial Statement Analysis (기업경영분석, 2022) states, in the section on standard classification usage: "업종별 분류체계는... 통계청의 「제10차 한국표준산업분류」를 사용" ("The industry classification system uses the 10th Korean Standard Industrial Classification issued by Statistics Korea"), and: "제10차 한국표준산업분류는 국제표준산업분류 기준을 반영하고 있어 국제기준에 부합" ("The 10th Korean Standard Industrial Classification reflects the International Standard Industrial Classification standard, and thus conforms to international standards.")

Government Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report on the Domestic Construction Order Trend Survey (국내건설수주동향조사, 2019) lists its main uses: "통계청에서 발표하는 건설경기동향조사(수주, 기성), 지역GDP(GRDP)에 활용" ("Used in Statistics Korea's Construction Business Trend Survey [orders, completions] and in Regional GDP (GRDP)"), i.e. Korea's regional accounts (GRDP) draw on this construction survey's data.

The same Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report on the Domestic Construction Order Trend Survey states, in the same list of main uses: "한국은행에서 발표하는 건설투자, GDP 등 관련 지표에 활용" ("Used in the Bank of Korea's published construction-investment, GDP and related indicators"), i.e. BOK's national accounts (construction investment component of GDP) use this survey's data.

Government Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report on the Service Industry Survey (서비스업동향조사, 2021) states, describing the sampling frame for the online-shopping/mail-order component: "전국사업체조사 결과를 표본추출틀로 이용하여 추출" ("[the sample is] extracted using the National Business Survey (전국사업체조사) results as the sampling frame"), and more broadly, for other components: "○ 표본추출틀로 사용되는 자료의 출처... 통계명: 년 기준 경제총조사" tying the survey's population to the Economic Census / National Business Survey system.

The same Service Industry Survey quality report states, describing the Korean Standard Industrial Classification it applies: "통계법에 의거하여 통계자료의 정확성 및 국가 간의 비교성을 확보하기 위하여 유엔에서 권고하고 있는 국제표준산업분류를 기초로 작성한 통계목적분류임" ("Pursuant to the Statistics Act, and to ensure accuracy and international comparability, [KSIC] is a statistical-purpose classification prepared on the basis of the International Standard Industrial Classification recommended by the United Nations.")

Government Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report on the Survey of Business Activities (기업활동조사) states, defining its survey population and sampling frame: "전국사업체조사 결과로 구성된 기업모집단" ("the enterprise population is constructed from the results of the National Business Survey") and "표본추출틀로 사용되는 자료의 출처 및 주기: 통계명 전국사업체조사를 기초로 구성된 기업체 모집단" ("source of the sampling-frame data: the enterprise population built on the basis of the National Business Survey").

The same Survey of Business Activities quality report states, describing its industry classification: "통계법에 의거하여 통계자료의 정확성 및 국가 간의 비교성을 확보하기 위하여 유엔에서 권고하고 있는 국제표준산업분류를 기초로 작성한 통계목적분류임" ("Pursuant to the Statistics Act, and to secure accuracy and international comparability, [the Korean Standard Industrial Classification applied to this survey] is prepared on the basis of the International Standard Industrial Classification recommended by the United Nations.")

Government Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report on the Small Merchant/Small Business Survey (소상공인실태조사, 2019, KOSTAT) states: "표본추출틀은 전사체 전국사업체조사(통계청, 2018년 기준)자료를 사용하며" ("The sampling frame uses the complete National Business Survey (Statistics Korea, 2018 base year) data") and "표본추출틀은 매년 통계청에서 구축 및 갱신, 전국사업체조사 연간통계로 매년 현장조사" ("The sampling frame is built and updated annually by Statistics Korea from the National Business Survey's annual field enumeration").

The official 2025 edition of '북한의 주요통계지표' (Statistical Indicators of North Korea), published by Korea's national statistics agency, sources its comparative population figures: "출처: (북) 국가데이터처 「북한인구추계('23.8월)」, (남) 국가데이터처 「장래인구추계('23.12월)」" ("Source: [North] National Data and Statistics Agency's 'North Korea Population Projections' (Aug 2023); [South] the same agency's 'Population Projections' (Dec 2023)"), directly citing KOSTAT's Population Projections (장래인구추계, kr-population-projections) as the source for the South Korean figures presented in this compilation.

The same 2025 '북한의 주요통계지표' publication sources its North Korea GDP/economic-growth figures to the Bank of Korea: "출처: 한국은행 ... 주: 2020년 기준년 자료, UN의 국민계정체계(SNA: System of National Accounts)를 적용하여 추정. 북한 경제성장률은 UN의 국민계정체계(SNA)를 적용하여 추정" ("Source: Bank of Korea ... Note: 2020 base-year data, estimated by applying the UN System of National Accounts (SNA). North Korea's economic growth rate is estimated by applying the UN SNA framework"), i.e. the North Korea GDP/growth data in this compilation comes directly from BOK's national-accounts estimation work.

The official press release for '기업특성별 무역통계' (Trade Statistics by Enterprise Characteristics) states: "본 통계는 통계청의 기업통계 자료와 관세청의 무역통계 자료를 연계하여 기업규모별, 산업별, 종사자규모별 등 상세 무역 현황을 파악하기 위한 것입니다." ("This statistic links Statistics Korea's enterprise data with the Korea Customs Service's Trade Statistics data to capture detailed trade conditions by enterprise size, industry, and employment size.") and notes it differs slightly from "관세청 무역통계" (kr-trade-statistics) only due to specific exclusions, confirming it is calculated from that base trade dataset.

UPDATE 2026-08-29 (import follow-up, raw-verified by the orchestrating session — the same signed bok.or.kr fileDown.do URL that failed for the prior agent succeeded on retry: 281,837 bytes, byte-identical to the import's reported size). BOK's own Financial Stability Report (June 2024), appendix "참고 7. 주요국의 바젤Ⅲ 최종안 도입 현황 및 시사점" (Reference 7: Status and Implications of Major Countries' Basel III Final Package Adoption), states: "바젤은행감독위원회(BCBS)가 2017년 12월 발표한 바젤Ⅲ 최종안(잔여규제 개혁안)의 이행시기(2023년 1월)가 지난 가운데 미국, 유럽연합 등 주요국의 바젤Ⅲ 도입 작업이 진행 중이다. 우리나라를 포함한 일부 회원국은 이미 바젤Ⅲ 최종안을 도입･시행 중이나..." ("...Korea, among other member states, has already adopted and is implementing the Basel III final package...") and "2023년 11월 기준 BCBS 회원국(27개) 중 캐나다, 중국, 인도네시아, 일본, 한국, 사우디아라비아 등 6개국이 바젤Ⅲ 최종안 도입을 완료하였다" ("as of Nov 2023, 6 of 27 BCBS members — including Korea — have completed Basel III final-package adoption"). This is BOK's own Financial Stability Report describing Korea's completed Basel III implementation as the basis for the bank-resilience chapter's assessment. REPOINTED 2026-09-04 (Thomas ruling) from bis-basel-framework to basel-iii: BOK names 바젤Ⅲ throughout the appendix and never names the consolidated Basel Framework. Note for the grader: this edge does NOT reach A on the repoint alone, because namesTarget tokenises 바젤Ⅲ as the single token 바젤iii (U+2162 decomposes to III under NFKD) and both the title-run rule and the single-token CJK rule miss it — the latter reads only the English title and its character class excludes Hangul. Recorded in the round note as a measured proposal, not fixed here.

_dropped.why: Fetched the 2019 Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report for 고용형태별근로실태조사 (Survey on Labor Conditions by Employment Type, the modern successor to the old Wage Structure Survey). Its sampling frame is drawn from a different, non-corpus survey (사업체노동실태현황조사), and the only international references found were generic comparisons to Japan's wage-structure survey and to ILO/OECD statistics ('국외통계로는 일본의 임금구조기본통계조사, ILO나 OECD에서...') rather than an explicit statement that its own methodology/data depends on a specific corpus node. Did not mint given no unambiguous quote.

Fetched the 2022 Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report for 생산자물가조사 (Producer Price Survey). It confirms PPI is classified by the Korean Standard Industrial Classification (한국표준산업분류) and its Input-Output-table-based weights, but does NOT restate the 'KSIC is based on ISIC' boilerplate found in the Financial Statement Analysis/Service Industry Survey/Survey of Business Activities reports. The only explicit IMF-manual reference in the document ('IMF의 XMPI 매뉴얼을 참고') is under the Export/Import Price Index section, not the PPI section itself, so the link would be inferential rather than directly evidenced. Dropped rather than forced.

Fetched the 2020 Regular Statistical Quality Diagnosis report for 전국주택가격동향조사 (National Housing Price Trend Survey, ~100 pages). Found only generic language about applying 'domestic or international standards' for terminology and no explicit statement tying its methodology or source data to CPI, SNA, or any other specific corpus node. No usable quote found within the time budget.

The Trade-by-Enterprise-Characteristics press release names the linked business-side data source as '기업통계(기업생멸행정통계 및 기업통계등록부)' (enterprise statistics: business-demography administrative statistics and the Business Register), not literally the '전국사업체조사' (National Business Survey) that is the corpus node's exact title. These are related but distinct KOSTAT products; equating them would overstate the evidence, so only the unambiguous kr-trade-statistics dependency was minted for this node.

The 2025 북한의 주요통계지표 publication states North Korea's GDP/growth is estimated by BOK 'UN의 국민계정체계(SNA: System of National Accounts)를 적용하여' but never names a specific SNA vintage (1993 vs 2008). Rather than guess which SNA-edition node to attach, only the more specific and unambiguous kr-national-accounts-bok (BOK as the cited source) edge was minted.

reports.title: Auditor General's Report on Compliance Audit of the Nimba County Social and County Development Funds, For the Fiscal Periods July 1, 2018 to December 31, 2023
reports.description: The General Auditing Commission's compliance audit of Nimba County Administration's Social Development Fund (SDF) and County Development Fund (CDF) expenditure and operations, signed by Auditor General P. Garswa Jackson, FCCA, CFIP, CFC (cover dated October 2025; transmittal letter to the Speaker of the House and President Pro-Tempore of the Senate dated March 2026), conducted per Section 2.1.3 of the GAC Act of 2014. Verified via two independent OCR passes of the scanned/image-only PDF (cross-checked against a third OCR pass of the same source pages on disk this round). Background section (PDF p.11) on the Arcelor Mittal Social Development Fund, established via Article 22 Section 3 of the Mineral Development Agreement (MDA) between the Government of Liberia and Mittal Steel Holding Liberia (Arcelor Mittal), passed into law May 7, 2007: "The Act that created the Mineral Development Agreement between the Arcelor Mittal and the Government of Liberia requires that the amount of US$3,000,000.00 be contributed to the social and community development of three counties including Bong, Nimba and Grand Bassa annually for 25 years... Nimba County's 50% equaled US$1,500,000.00, Grand Bassa County's 33.3% equaled US$999,000.00 and Bong County's 16.7% equaled US$501,000.00." A second, related SDF stream (also Article 8.2(b) MDA, passed into law September 2010) is quoted on the same page: "the amount of US$400,000.00 be contributed to the social and community developments of the three (3) counties, Bong, Nimba and Grand Bassa annually. The three (3) counties received a proportional distribution of thirty-three percent (33.3%) each. Nimba County's share... is US$133,333.33." Separately (PDF p.12, "County Development Fund (CDF)" section), a second and independent named-county fiscal figure: "The County Development Fund (CDF) was initiated in 2006 by the Government of Liberia to fast track national development in the leeward counties. In 2018/2019 to 2023, US$12,564,505.86 was appropriated to Nimba County." NOTE: this is the strongest available pattern in the branch for municipal/county-tier evidence — a national oversight body's primary document naming three specific counties with exact percentage/dollar allocation formulas, plus a second independent county appropriation figure, all for named fiscal periods.
reports.cadence_note: Ad hoc compliance audit covering a multi-year period (FY2018–2023); not a recurring annual publication in the way a national budget is, though GAC issues comparable named-county compliance audits on an ongoing basis per its own sitemap listing.

_dropped.why: The audit's own cited legal authorities are the GAC Act of 2014 (Section 2.1.3, for the audit's mandate) and the Mineral Development Agreement Act (Article 22 §3 / Article 8.2(b), for the SDF formula itself) — the Local Government Act of 2018 is never named or quoted in the audit text as located and OCR'd this round. No textual basis for a citation edge to lr-local-government-act-2018; both nodes concern Liberian county-tier fiscal transfers but via entirely separate legal instruments, so no edge is drawn per the evidence rule requiring a documented textual basis.

This extends the existing ls-cpi-formula-unconfirmed open question with a confirmed negative result rather than resolving it. Lesotho's own CPI is used as a downstream input by two independent regional bodies documented elsewhere in this corpus: SADC's HCPI newsletter (sadc-hcpi-newsletter, af-sadc-hub.json) and a SACU Secretariat HCPI press notice (sacu-harmonised-cpi-notice, ls-g23-municipal.json) — neither of which is cited by BOS's own release in the other direction. Lesotho's official monthly Consumer Price Index release. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via Report No. 3:2026 (January 2026 edition): base period 'rebased using the price reference period as the yearly average, so that 2022 = 100'; weights reflect 'expenditure and shopping patterns from the 2017/2018 Household Budget Survey'; classification uses 'COICOP (Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose)... organized into 12 divisions, with further breakdowns into groups and classes'; scope covers 'all the expenditures on goods and services in Lesotho by private households' using 'cash prices typically paid by the reference population'. The report states the annual inflation rate as 'the change in the CPI for all items of the relevant month of the current year compared with the CPI for all items of the same month in the previous year expressed as a percentage', but does not name a specific elementary-aggregate index formula (see _open_questions).

reports.title: Local Government Act 1996 (Act No. 6 of 1997) — Part V: Finance
reports.publisher: Government of the Kingdom of Lesotho
reports.description: Lesotho's foundational local-government statute. Part V "Finance" (ss.47-63) establishes each council's own treasury: "Every Council for its general financial purposes shall establish a Council Fund, (hereinafter referred to as \"the Fund\")." (s.47(1)). The Fund's constituent revenue sources include "(b) subject to any special appropriation made by the Minister all grants allocated to the Council by the Minister;" "(c) all rates, taxes, duties, fees and other charges levied under the authority of this Act;" and "(i) all sums and all sources or revenue, from time to time, appropriated or made order [sic] to the Council by the National Assembly, whether by resolution or otherwise." On the grant-allocation mechanism (s.55(1)-(4)), the Act sets up a discretionary, application-based process rather than a fixed revenue-sharing formula: "A Council may, in order to implement its development programme, as recommended by the District Development Co-ordinating Committee, make a written application to the Minister for the allocation of a grant"; "The Minister shall evaluate the merits of such application having regard to the development priorities of that district, and recommend such application to the Minister responsible for Finance"; "Where the Minister of Finance considers such application and allocates a sum of monies by way of grant... such monies shall be credited to the Fund of the Council." The Act also grants councils a rating power (s.56(1)): "A local authority may subject to such limitations, qualifications and conditions as may be prescribed by the Minister, impose and levy a rate on any property situated within its jurisdiction," and imposes a bi-annual audit requirement (s.63(1)): "The accounts of every Council shall be audited during each half of the financial year by the Government Auditor or by such other professionally qualified auditor as may be appointed by the Minister." Text recovered as clean OCR from an FAO/FAOLEX mirror of the scanned Government Gazette (Adobe Acrobat 8.0 Paper Capture); the Government's own hosted copy (via an aceproject.org mirror) is an un-OCR'd image scan with no extractable text. Minor OCR artifact noted in s.47 ("made order" likely "made over") — recommend spot-checking against the Gazette if exact character fidelity is required.

reports.title: Public Financial Management and Accountability Act, 2011 (Act No. 12 of 2011)
reports.publisher: Government of the Kingdom of Lesotho
reports.description: Lesotho's public financial management statute, which explicitly folds local-government finance into the national accountability chain. Its interpretation section cross-references the Local Government Act 1997's own Council Fund provision by name: "'council funds' means the funds referred to in section 47 of the Local Government Act, 1997" (s.2). It assigns local-authority audit to the national Auditor-General: "The Auditor General shall undertake audit of the financial statements of local authorities" (s.39). And it routes local-authority accountability through Parliament: "A local authority shall submit audited annual reports to the minister responsible for local government, who shall table the reports before Parliament and shall furnish copies of the reports to the Minister" (s.34(3)). CAVEAT: lesotholii.org is behind a Cloudflare managed JS challenge — direct curl access to both the HTML act page and its /source.pdf variant returned HTTP 403 ("Just a moment..." interstitial). These quotes were obtained via a WebFetch tool that reached real rendered content, but could not be independently byte-verified against raw HTML/PDF this round; treat as high-confidence but not independently cross-verified verbatim text pending a manual browser-session re-check.

reports.publisher: Government of the Kingdom of Lesotho
reports.description: Governs discipline of local-government officers, including the officers responsible for council finances. reports.title: Report of the Auditor-General on the Consolidated Financial Statements of the Government of Lesotho for the Year Ended 31 March 2024
reports.publisher: Office of the Auditor-General, Kingdom of Lesotho
reports.description: The single cleanest primary-source statement of Lesotho's local-government reporting tier structure (s.2.2): "The Government of Lesotho (GOL) is composed of the Central Government, Local Governments, Extra-Budgetary Entities, Public Financial Corporations and Public Non-Financial Corporations. Central Government includes all Ministries, Departments and Agencies whilst Local Governments are all the District Councils, Urban Councils and the Maseru City Council." Near-identical wording independently recurs in the FY2023 edition of this same report (auditorgeneral.org.ls/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/REPORT-OF-THE-AUDITOR-GENERAL-ENDED-MARCH-2023.pdf), confirming it is a stable, repeated institutional definition rather than a one-off. On community-level fund execution: "Community Councils have maintained infrastructure through the Development Fund for Community Councils. Additionally, solid waste budget was executed up to 90%." "Table 2: Controlled entities excluded from consolidation" (p.44) gives the fullest national-report roster of named lower-tier units found this round: under "Local Government," Maseru City Council is listed alongside named District Councils (Berea, Botha-Bothe, Mafeteng, Mokhotlong, Quthing, Qacha's Nek, Thaba-Tseka, Maseru, Leribe, Mohale's Hoek) and named Urban Councils (Berea, Botha-Bothe, Mafeteng, Mokhotlong, Quthing, Qacha's Nek, Thaba-Tseka, Semonkong, Hlotse, Mohale's Hoek, Maputsoe). reports.title: SACU Harmonised Consumer Price Index (HCPI) Press Notice 02/2019
reports.description: SACU (Southern African Customs Union, of which Lesotho is a founding member)'s regional harmonised CPI, built from member states' own national HCPIs. Methodological note: "It is against this background that COMESA and SADC jointly developed a harmonised measure of consumer inflation, the Harmonised Consumer Price Index or HCPI. The HCPI for the SACU region builds on the HCPIs of the individual Member States, the latter following the harmonised rules agreed by COMESA and SADC. The HCPI for the SACU region is a weighted average of the HCPIs for the individual SACU Member States." "The Member States HCPIs are produced by the respective Member States using the agreed harmonised methodologies, while the SACU HCPI is compiled by the SACU Secretariat." Table 1 gives a Lesotho-specific data row: "Lesotho 12.3 5.4 4.0 4.3 3.9 3.9 3.2 3.1 0.0" (12.3% weight; February 2019 annual inflation rate 3.1%, monthly rate 0.0%). Document is dated 15 April 2019. CAVEAT: this notice does not explicitly name "Lesotho Bureau of Statistics" by name — it refers only to "the respective Member States" as HCPI producers, with Lesotho named individually only in the country list and Table 1 data row, not paired with its national statistics office's name.
reports.cadence_note: Titled a numbered press notice (02/2019); publication frequency of the SACU HCPI series is not established from this single document — recorded as a one-off primary source, not assumed periodic.

reports.title: Indice des prix à la consommation harmonisé (IPCH)
reports.publisher: Service central de la statistique et des études économiques (STATEC)
reports.description: Luxembourg's own contribution to the EU's harmonised consumer price framework. Règlement grand-ducal du 20 décembre 1999, Art. 1er: 'Le Service central de la statistique et des études économiques, dénommé ci-après STATEC, établit chaque mois un indice des prix à la consommation conformément aux dispositions du Règlement (CE) n° 2494/95 du Conseil du 23 octobre 1995 relatif aux indices des prix à la consommation harmonisés et des règlements du Conseil et de la Commission pris en son exécution.'
reports.cadence_note: Règlement grand-ducal du 20 décembre 1999, Art. 1er: STATEC 'établit chaque mois' [establishes each month] the index.

entries.covers: August 2026 IPCH/IPCN (indice des prix à la consommation harmonisé)

release_schedule.rule: Règlement grand-ducal du 20 décembre 1999, Art. 1er: STATEC 'établit chaque mois' [establishes each month] the index (IPCN/IPCH).
release_schedule.note: The grand-ducal regulation mandates a monthly index with no fixed day-of-month specified. In practice STATEC's STATNEWS press releases (e.g. stn01-26-ipc, published 2026-01-07 for December 2025 data, which itself announced that the January 2026 index would be released 2026-02-09) show releases occurring roughly on the 7th-10th of each month for the prior month's data. Following that observed cadence, the July 2026 index was likely already released around 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-11 (right around/just before the corpus's current date of 2026-08-11), so the next not-yet-occurred release is for August 2026 data, expected in the first half of September 2026; exact day could not be confirmed because the relevant STATEC pages (statistiques.public.lu) returned 403 errors on direct fetch and no specific September 2026 date was found via search.

reports.title: Indice des prix à la consommation national (IPCN)
reports.publisher: Service central de la statistique et des études économiques (STATEC)
reports.description: Luxembourg's national-only consumer price index, published alongside the IPCH but scoped to resident consumption only. Règlement grand-ducal du 20 décembre 1999, Art. 1er: 'En complément à l'indice des prix à la consommation harmonisé (IPCH), le STATEC établit un indice des prix à la consommation national (IPCN), qui se conforme aux mêmes principes et concepts méthodologiques. Toutefois, la couverture géographique de l'IPCN se limite à la seule population résidante; elle exclut la consommation des non-résidants.' Named as the input to Luxembourg's own wage/salary indexation mechanism at Art. 4(1) of the same regulation: 'Pour les besoins de l'échelle mobile des salaires et traitements, l'indice national des prix à la consommation (IPCN)... est raccordé à la base 100 au 1er janvier 1948.'
reports.cadence_note: Same monthly cadence as lu-statec-ipch -- both established by the same Art. 1er, 'chaque mois'.

release_schedule.note: STATEC's official 'Calendrier de diffusion' (release calendar, last updated 2026-07-31) lists a monthly entry 'Indice des prix à la consommation (CPI)' with a specific day-of-month release date for each reference month; this entry covers the joint monthly IPCN/IPCH press release. Dates are explicitly labeled by STATEC as provisional ('dates prévisionnelles de diffusion et sont susceptibles d'être modifiées'). The most recent past release (Aug 5, 2026, covering July 2026 data) has already occurred as of the 2026-08-11 reference date; the next release is Sep 4, 2026 (August 2026 data).

dependencies.basis: MUTUAL 2026-09-05: companion edge eurostat-hicp -> lu-statec-ipch (Eurostat's aggregate uses the Luxembourg IPCH as an input; this edge says the IPCH's methodology is prescribed by the harmonised-index framework). Règlement grand-ducal du 20 décembre 1999, Art. 1er: STATEC 'établit chaque mois un indice des prix à la consommation conformément aux dispositions du Règlement (CE) n° 2494/95 du Conseil du 23 octobre 1995 relatif aux indices des prix à la consommation harmonisés' [establishes monthly a consumer price index in accordance with the provisions of Council Regulation (EC) No 2494/95 of 23 October 1995 on harmonised indices of consumer prices]. Same shape as de-destatis-national-accounts -> esa-2010: a binding EU regulation supplies the definitions and methodology a national release conforms to, not figures. eurostat-hicp's own description states it is 'calculated according to a harmonised approach and definitions as laid down in Regulations and Recommendations' -- the same regulatory framework named here. Not extended to lu-statec-ipcn: Art. 1er says the IPCN merely 'se conforme aux mêmes principes et concepts méthodologiques' [conforms to the same methodological principles and concepts] as the IPCH, without itself being subject to Regulation 2494/95 -- a Research.1 §5a 'comparable with' shape, not a documented dependency, so no edge is drawn for the IPCN side.
dependencies.evidence_quote: établit chaque mois un indice des prix à la consommation conformément aux dispositions du Règlement (CE) n° 2494/95 du Conseil du 23 octobre 1995 relatif aux indices des prix à la consommation harmonisés

_note: Libya's own statistics homepage (bsc.ly) is misleading if read alone: its front-page widget still displays a stale December 2023 figure on the old 2008 base, which is exactly the outdated, Tripoli-only series the IMF's 2025 Article IV report describes as having 'a significant downward bias due to methodological deficiencies.' The actual current release sits in the site's archive, not the homepage, and shows a genuine methodological relaunch: 'The Bureau of Statistics and Census (BSC) has recently introduced a new CPI -- based on the new household spending survey -- that covers the entire country,' with IMF technical assistance (METAC) dated from a January 2022 roadmap mission through a January 2025 CPI-development mission. The IMF's own Data Adequacy Assessment rates Libya's price statistics 'B' (broadly adequate) even as national accounts, government finance, external-sector and inter-sectoral-consistency data are all rated 'D' -- CPI is the one bright spot in an otherwise weak national statistical system, the opposite of the 'too thin to source' framing carried forward unchecked since G.7. On social protection, Libya's Basic Pension Benefit is a flat, minimum-wage-pegged transfer with a documented benefit-adjustment rule that is explicitly NOT CPI-linked -- the ISSA country profile states plainly 'Not legally mandated. Indexed based on changes in civil servant salaries,' the same 'real mechanism, non-CPI' shape already found for Rwanda, Uganda, Morocco and Tunisia this batch.

reports.title: Report about Inflation and Consumer Price Indices
reports.publisher: Bureau of Statistics and Census (BSC), Ministry of Planning, Libya
reports.description: Libya's official monthly Consumer Price Index report. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via the June 2026 edition and the BSC's own online archive, which shows an unbroken monthly run from December 2024 to June 2026 -- 18+ consecutive months, each on the new 'Base Year 2024.' Per the IMF's 2025 Article IV report: 'The Bureau of Statistics and Census (BSC) has recently introduced a new CPI -- based on the new household spending survey -- that covers the entire country. The reported inflation from the new series stood at 1.2 percent in 2025 Q1. However, the new index could have a significant downward bias due to methodological deficiencies.' A 12-group classification table (Food and Beverages, Tobacco, Clothing and Footwear, Housing/Water/Electricity/Gas, Furniture and Household Equipment, Health, Transport, Communication, Recreation and Culture, Education, Restaurants and Hotels, Miscellaneous Goods and Services) is structurally close to standard COICOP divisions, though no document read this session names COICOP explicitly. The BSC's own homepage widget still displays a stale December 2023 figure on the superseded 2008 base -- the current series lives in the site's archive, not the front page.

release_schedule.note: The BSC prices page (bsc.ly/economic_statistic/prices/) lists monthly 'Report on inflation and consumer price index numbers' (تقرير حول التضخم والأرقام القياسية لأسعار المستهلك) plus separate base-year (2024=100) comparison reports and quarterly group-comparison reports, but publishes no dated release calendar and states no explicit release-day rule. As of 2026-08-11 the most recent posted monthly report covers June 2026, with reports appearing roughly monthly at a lag of about 6-8 weeks after the reference month (May, April, March 2026 editions posted in sequence before it). This is a consistent monthly cadence inferred from the sequence of past editions, not a published calendar or a stated rule, so it is classified as observed-pattern; the next report(s) are projected forward from that pattern rather than read off a calendar.

reports.title: Law No. 15 of 1981 on the Salary System for [National] Employees (قانون رقم 15 لسنة 1981م بشأن نظام المرتبات للعاملين)
reports.publisher: Libyan government, 1981 enactment (General People's Congress era) — current text hosted by Ministry of Justice (وزارة العدل), Government of National Unity
reports.description: Major upgrade from a previously 'not located' open question in the corpus (ly-civil-service-salary-schedule-not-located, in ly-cpi-social-protection.json) to a named, dated, readable law. VERIFIED via the current Ministry of Justice legislation portal (aladel.gov.ly), full law text. Article 3(a) sets scope, explicitly covering municipal employees: 'تسري أحكام هذا القانون على جميع العاملين الوطنيين في الجهات الآتية: أ) الأمانات واللجان الشعبية للبلديات والأجهزة والتقسيمات التنظيمية التابعة لأي منهما...' — 'The provisions of this law apply to all national employees in: (a) the secretariats and popular committees of the municipalities (baladiyat) and organs/divisions affiliated with them...' Article 4: 'يتحدد الإطار العام لمرتبات كافة العاملين الوطنيين ... وفقاً لما هو محدد بالجدول رقم (1) المرفق' — 'The general framework for salaries of all national employees is determined per attached Table No. (1)...' Effective January 1, 1982 (Jamahiriya-era terminology: People's Congress / General People's Committee). Structure: a base Grade Table No. 1 plus nine substitute tables (police, customs guard, armed forces, judiciary, Jamahiriya Security, Central Inspection apparatus, universities, municipal guard). CAVEAT: the numeric pay tables themselves were not rendered in the page-text extraction read this round (may sit in an attached PDF/image not captured); the law's operative articles were read in full, but whether the numeric tables are separately downloadable from this page was not confirmed. A separate, non-governing 21 November 2015 document on the same domain (a Ministry of Justice announcement of an Audit Bureau workshop on a proposed replacement salary schedule) is deliberately NOT treated as evidence this law was amended or repealed — see _dropped for why.

_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Morocco is the second of three North Africa countries researched this session (AF/G.9 priority 1) -- Algeria and Tunisia alongside it. Researched by a subagent this session against the branch's full Research.1.md discipline, reading HCP's own methodological note directly plus the full 19-article text of the 2021 social-protection framework law. Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review, following the established DRAFT-then-import pattern.
_note: Morocco's CPI methodology note is the most self-documenting of the three North Africa countries researched this session: it names COICOP (without a version), states its release calendar follows the IMF's SDDS (independently confirmed by the IMF's own 2022 Morocco SDDS Annual Observance Report, which lists 'Price index: Consumer prices' as an SDDS-monitored category), and states its missing-price imputation method follows 'le manuel du FMI' -- the only country in this batch whose own CPI document names an IMF manual directly, even without a full title. On social protection, Morocco shows the same 'real mechanism, not CPI-based' shape already found for Rwanda's actuarial trigger and Uganda's Minister-set NSSF rate: the CMR's civil-service pension statute (Loi 011-71, Art. 44 bis) automatically ties pension increases to the civil-service base-salary scale, and the CNSS's founding statute (Dahir 1-72-184, Art. 68) ties discretionary pension revaluation to a wage-level gap -- both real, both statutory, neither CPI-linked. The 2021 social-protection framework law (Loi-cadre 09-21), read in full across all 19 articles, uses the aspirational phrase 'soutenir le pouvoir d'achat des familles' twice but specifies no indexation formula, trigger, or review cycle anywhere.

_open_questions.question: HCP's methodological note names 'COICOP' as the CPI's classification but never states a version (no 'COICOP 2018' anywhere in the document, and no web search for 'HCP Maroc COICOP 2018' surfaced one). The `un-coicop-2018` edge below should be treated as version-unconfirmed pending a document that states the vintage explicitly.

Loi n° 58-23 (establishing Morocco's Aide Sociale Directe direct cash-support programme) exists on ANSS's own site only as a non-OCR'd Arabic-language scan; no French version could be located. Whether the law itself contains any inflation/CPI-adjustment provision is genuinely unconfirmed, not a documented silence -- official secondary sources (ANSS's own site, the government portal maroc.ma) describe benefit increases as driven by budget sustainability and the 'Chantier Royal' rollout schedule, not inflation, but this is not a reading of the statute itself.

A trade-association news article (CGEM) attributes a 2020 CNSS pension-revalorisation decree to 'l'article 9' of Dahir 1-72-184, but Article 9 as read this session governs the fund's conseil d'administration, not pensions -- the substantively relevant provision is Article 68. Possibly a citation error in the secondary source; not resolved this session.

reports.title: Indice des Prix à la Consommation (IPC), Base 100 : 2017
reports.description: Morocco's official monthly Consumer Price Index. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via HCP's own methodological note. 'Le premier IPC basé sur la nouvelle référence 100 : 2017 a été publié le 27 avril de l'année 2020.' Formula: 'une formule de Laspeyres en chaîne combinée à une moyenne géométrique pour le premier niveau d'agrégation.' Classification: 'classifiés selon la nomenclature COICOP' (version unstated -- see _open_questions). Missing-price imputation: 'la méthode d'imputation est appliquée conformément au manuel du FMI, sauf pour les produits dont les prix sont fixés par l'État... où la méthode du report est utilisée.' Release calendar: 'conformément au calendrier établi selon les normes spéciales de diffusion des données (NSDD)' -- the French name for the IMF's SDDS.

release_schedule.rule: Per HCP's official Calendrier des publications (embedded Google Sheets calendar), the Indice des Prix à la Consommation (IPC) is published Mensuelle (monthly), with reference release day of the 20th, 21st, or 22nd of the month following the reference period ("Référence: 20, 21 ou 22").
release_schedule.note: The stated rule gives a range (20th-22nd) rather than one fixed day; actual 2026 editions were consistently released on the 22nd of the following month (April 2026 data released 22/04/2026, May 2026 data released 22/05/2026, June 2026 data released 22/07/2026), so 2026-08-22 (for July 2026 data) is used as the computed next date. Source calendar: https://www.hcp.ma/Calendrier-des-publications_r630.html

reports.title: Enquête nationale sur les dépenses et la consommation des ménages (2013-2014)
reports.description: The national household expenditure and consumption survey named by HCP as 'la principale source' of the CPI's expenditure weights, supplemented for the rent group by the 2014 General Population and Housing Census and for pharmaceuticals by 2016 drug-expenditure data.

reports.title: Loi n° 011-71 instituant un régime de pensions civiles (Chapitre II bis : Revalorisation, Article 44 bis)
reports.publisher: Caisse Marocaine des Retraites (CMR) / Trésorerie Générale du Royaume
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (consolidated text hosted by the Trésorerie Générale du Royaume). Article 44 bis, inserted by Loi n° 06-89: 'Les pensions de retraite et les pensions d'ayants cause concédées au titre de la présente loi sont majorées de toute augmentation affectant le traitement de base afférent aux grade, échelle et échelon ou classe effectivement détenus à la date de radiation des cadres.' A real, mandatory ('sont majorées') indexation mechanism -- but tied to the civil-service base-salary scale, not to CPI or inflation.

reports.title: Dahir portant loi n° 1-72-184 relatif au régime de sécurité sociale
reports.publisher: Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (CNSS), Morocco
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Founding statute of Morocco's private-sector social security fund. Article 68: 'Lorsque l'écart entre le niveau des salaires sur la base desquels ont été liquidées les pensions d'invalidité, de vieillesse et de survivants et le niveau des salaires en cours le justifie, ces pensions peuvent être revalorisées par décret pris sur proposition du ministre chargé du travail.' A real but discretionary ('peuvent être') mechanism, triggered by a wage-level gap, not a price index.

reports.title: Loi-cadre n° 09-21 relative à la protection sociale
reports.publisher: Royaume du Maroc / Chef du Gouvernement
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session -- full text (Articles 1-19) read via Bulletin Officiel n° 7132 du 6 octobre 2022. Morocco's 2021 framework law for generalizing social protection (AMO, family allocations, pension coverage, unemployment benefit) over a five-year rollout. Uses the aspirational phrase 'soutenir le pouvoir d'achat des familles' twice (Préambule; Article 4, on the flat-rate family allocations) but specifies no indexation formula, trigger, or review cycle anywhere in the law.

reports.publisher: Agence Nationale du Soutien Social (ANSS) / Royaume du Maroc

Primary text available on ANSS's own site only as a non-OCR'd Arabic scan -- could not be read this session (see _open_questions). Reopened per PLAYBOOK-CORPUS.md §7d and ruled 2026-09-08: no document in this family names a COICOP edition/revision at all -- the source text says bare 'COICOP' or 'nomenclature COICOP' with no year, no 'Rev.', no '2018'. Reading '2018' onto that silence is the researcher's inference, not the document's statement -- exactly the inference the corpus's own IMTS-Revision-2 refusal (round5-little-things-2026-09-06.json _dropped) exists to block, and the same standard that required un-coicop-hbs-1999 and un-coicop-2018 themselves to only be minted where a country's own document spelled out the edition by name (CAPMAS's 'COICOP-HBS 2000/1999', South Africa's 'the 2018 version of ... COICOP'). Morocco's document carries no divisional structure evidence either way -- it is silence alone, which is enough on its own under the edition-inference rule. Dropping rather than keeping the caveated wire: three rounds converging on the same 'wire with a vintage caveat' shape doesn't make it consistent with the rule those rounds were themselves trying to honour.

reports.title: Loi organique n° 111-14 relative aux régions
reports.description: Adopted late January 2015 / dated 7 July 2015 depending on source ("adoptée fin janvier 2015" per one region's own PDR; "du 7 juillet 2015" per a legal-summary secondary source — both cited, discrepancy not resolved this round). Establishes Morocco's 12 regions — Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceïma, l'Oriental, Fès-Meknès, Rabat-Salé-Kénitra, Béni Mellal-Khénifra, Casablanca-Settat, Marrakech-Safi, Drâa-Tafilalet, Souss-Massa, Guelmim-Oued Noun, Laâyoune-Sakia El Hamra, and Dakhla-Oued Ed Dahab — and, per a secondary summary, "définit la composition et les attributions du conseil régional" and "les compétences propres, partagées et transférées des régions, ainsi que les règles budgétaires et financières applicables." The same secondary source states regions receive "une quote-part de la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée" (a VAT share) and "une part de l'impôt sur les sociétés" (a corporate-tax share) — Morocco's version of the federal-to-region fiscal transfer already documented differently for Nigeria (FAAC), Kenya (CRA), Ghana (DACF), Ethiopia (subsidy proclamation) and DR Congo (40% retrocession) this round — though no specific article number for that funding provision was independently verified this round.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument (an organic law).

reports.title: Programme de Développement Régional (PDR), Région Casablanca-Settat
reports.description: Dated March 2017, covering the region representing (per the document) 20.3% of Morocco's national population and 32.4% of GDP. Verbatim citation of the organic law: "La loi organique 111-14, adoptée fin janvier 2015, prévoit de nouvelles prérogatives et attributions dévolues aux régions. L'article 83 de cette loi précise l'obligation pour le Conseil Régional de définir une stratégie de développement régionale durant la première année de son mandat" — a direct statement that this very document exists BECAUSE Article 83 requires it, one of the cleaner statutory-basis citations found in this branch. Does not cite HCP or CPI data by name, checked directly and confirmed absent.

reports.title: Monthly Survey of Manufacturing (MSM)
reports.description: Monthly survey of Canadian manufacturing sales, inventories, unfilled orders and capacity utilisation, IMDB record 2101. Named as an indicator source by the monthly GDP-by-industry programme for most manufacturing industries, and named alongside the IPPI in the deflation rows of that programme's source table. The target population is drawn from the Business Register and classified by NAICS: 'The target population for the MSM consists of all statistical establishments on the Business Register that are classified to the manufacturing sector (by NAICS), which are categorized into over 156 industries.' Sales for low-revenue establishments are derived from GST files rather than collected, which is an administrative input with no publication behind it.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly. Record 2101 states 'Frequency: Monthly'. Two things about the historical record are worth keeping: the MSM was benchmarked to the Annual Survey of Manufacturing and Logging only 'up to and including 2003', so that specific arrangement has not held for two decades, and the present-tense relationship in the other direction is stated by the annual survey's own record rather than by this one.

release_schedule.note: Dates taken from Statistics Canada's official 2026-2027 major economic releases calendar (PDF), verified by direct download and text extraction. The publisher notes: 'In exceptional circumstances, some release dates may be modified during the year.' The corpus's existing url field (the IMDB survey definition page, SDDS 2101) is a good stable landing page for the survey itself; the actual dated calendar lives at the source_url above and is republished annually.

reports.title: Annual Survey of Manufacturing and Logging Industries (ASML)
reports.description: Annual census-and-sample survey of establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing and logging, IMDB record 2103. It is the annual anchor for the manufacturing side of the Canadian accounts and it names its own consumers in its own words: 'Within Statistics Canada, the data are used by the Canadian System of National Accounts, the Monthly Survey of Manufacturing (record number 2101) and Prices programs.' That sentence is the only present-tense statement of the ASML-to-MSM relationship found; the MSM's own record describes the arrangement in the past tense and dates it to 2003. Survey data are substituted with T1, T2, T3010 and T5013 tax data under the Integrated Business Statistics Program, which is an administrative input with no publication behind it. The IPPI's own record 2318 names the 2019 ASML as one of two weighting sources, which is why this node is worth more than a manufacturing statistic normally would be.
reports.cadence_note: Annual. Record 2103 states 'Frequency: Annual'. Reference year, published with a lag; the lag is not stated in the quoted passages and has not been verified.

entries.covers: Annual Survey of Manufacturing Industries, 2022 (reference fiscal period)
Annual Survey of Manufacturing Industries, 2025 (projected next release)

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar entry was found for the next (2025 reference year) release. StatCan's IMDB survey page (SDDS 2103) states the survey is annual, with data collected April-August of the year following the reference period and a one-year revision policy, but gives no specific release date. However, The Daily has released 'Annual Survey of Manufacturing Industries' results in mid-to-late December for three consecutive years (Dec 20 2023 for 2022 data, Dec 18 2024 for 2023 data, Dec 18 2025 for 2024 data), so the next release (2025 reference-year data) is projected for mid-December 2026 based on this consistent pattern. The IMDB page also separately lists detail-table releases (products produced/sold, raw materials) for Dec 18 2025 and Mar 27 2026, which are companion product-level breakdowns tied to the same annual cycle.

reports.title: National Occupational Classification (NOC) 2021 Version 1.0
reports.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada / Statistics Canada
reports.description: The Canadian occupational classification standard, and the occupational counterpart to NAICS. Jointly maintained: 'The NOC has been developed and maintained as part of a collaborative partnership between Employment and Social Development Canada and Statistics Canada.' As of 10 August 2021 it is 'the departmental standard for data collection and dissemination for occupations at Statistics Canada'. Its own introduction names what a revision reaches: 'the redesign of the NOC can have significant implications for several Surveys, such as the Labour Force Survey (LFS), and ESDC programs such as the Temporary Foreign Worker Program and Employment Insurance program.' Note what it does NOT support: the classification is described as 'comparable to' ISCO, and the same passage records that 'certain conceptual differences between the NOC 2021 Version 1.0 and ISCO-08 limit comparability' — comparability is not derivation, so no edge to ISCO exists here.
reports.cadence_note: Two clocks, and the validator corrected which field takes which. Content updates are roughly annual and structural revision is decennial: 'NOC structural revisions are planned every 10 years and content was updated every 5 years to respond to labour market changes. Starting in 2017, the NOC 2016 has undergone content updates approximately every year.' A new version of the classification appears about once a year, so that is releases_per_year; the structure — the thing a dependent's methodology actually tracks — moves about once a decade, so that is changes_per_year. The first attempt had these reversed and the validator's changes-cannot-exceed-releases rule caught it, which is the rule earning its keep on a node type it was not written for.

entries.covers: NOC 2026 Version 1.0 (structural revision superseding NOC 2021 Version 1.0)

release_schedule.note: NOC 2021 Version 1.0 was published September 14, 2021 (StatCan's index page cites 'Release date: September 28, 2021' for the September 2021 NOC 2021 V1.0 index; StatCan text also notes the release marked the 30th anniversary of the standard occupational classification system). NOC undergoes a full structural revision on roughly a 10-year cycle (NOC 2011, 2016, 2021, and next 2026); within a cycle, content is updated approximately annually (e.g., NOC 2021 V1.0 -> V1.1 -> V1.2, etc.) without a new 'Version 1.0'. Because the tracked report is specifically 'NOC 2021 Version 1.0' (the initial structural release of the 2021 cycle), the next comparable event is the next structural revision, NOC 2026 Version 1.0, which Statistics Canada's consultation results report states explicitly: 'The NOC for 2026 will be released in December of 2026.' Exact day within December was not published.

reports.title: North American Product Classification System (NAPCS) Canada 2022 Version 1.0
reports.description: The product-side counterpart to NAICS, approved as a departmental standard on 24 September 2021. It is a trilateral standard by origin — 'a joint project of the national statistical agencies of Canada, Mexico and the United States' — developed after NAICS 'to serve the same purpose but for product statistics'. Two relationships it is commonly assumed to have and does not: it is parallel to NAICS rather than derived from it, and it is explicitly NOT compatible with the UN Central Product Classification ('NAPCS Canada is not fully compatible with the CPC'). Its live connection to the accounts runs through the Supply and Use Product Classification, which its introduction states is 'largely embedded at the level of NAPCS Canada' — that is a containment relationship rather than a dependency, and the SUPC is not yet a node.
reports.cadence_note: Nominally a five-year revision cycle moving toward continuous update: 'Since the creation of this product classification, NAPCS Canada, has been revised on a 5-year cycle, in 2012, 2017 and 2022. NAPCS Canada was also revised in 2018 with NAPCS Canada 2017 Version 2.0, as Canada has started evolving towards adopting a permanent "evergreen" practice with regards to NAPCS, which means the updating of NAPCS Canada on an as-needed basis, with version updates between the standard 5-year revision milestones.' Four versions are named across roughly a decade — 2012, 2017, 2017 V2.0 in 2018, and 2022 — so releases_per_year is 0.4 counting published versions. changes_per_year 0.2 is the structural five-year cycle the document states.

release_schedule.rule: NAPCS Canada revisions are planned to occur every five years; the next version, NAPCS Canada 2027 Version 1.0, is scheduled for public release in February 2027.
release_schedule.note: Statistics Canada's consultation page for the NAPCS Canada 2027 revision (and the 2026 'What We Heard Report') both explicitly state a public release target of February 2027, with a preceding public notice of final approved proposals planned for February 2026 and a November 2025 notice of proposed changes. This is a documented target date (not merely a computed 5-year projection), though it is still a forward-looking schedule for a not-yet-released edition. The introduction page for NAPCS Canada 2022 (https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/subjects/standard/napcs/2022/introduction) states revisions are 'planned to occur every five years,' consistent with the 2012->2017->2022->2027 cadence, though StatCan also issued an off-cycle Version 2.0 update in 2018 for cannabis legalization, showing the 5-year cycle is a planning target rather than a rigid rule.

reports.title: CRA payroll deduction (PD7) accounts
reports.description: The administrative remittance records behind SEPH, and the first terminus in the graph. IMDB record 2612 names them as the primary input: 'Administrative information for total gross monthly payrolls and the total number of employees for the last pay period in the month are obtained from payroll deduction (PD7 form) accounts maintained by Canada Revenue Agency.' SEPH is a census of these records rather than a survey of employers, so the entire monthly payroll estimate — which four federal and provincial benefit formulas are calculated from — rests on a remittance form. There is no PD7 publication, no release schedule and no url: what exists is a form employers file and an agency that holds the results.
reports.cadence_note: A terminus has no publication cadence, so this number is the collection rhythm rather than a release rate: PD7 remittances are monthly, and record 2612 describes the payroll figure as covering 'the last pay period in the month'. Read it as how often the data behind this node changes, not as how often anything appears.

reports.title: Goods and Services Tax (GST) administrative files
reports.description: GST remittance records, used to avoid surveying small manufacturers. IMDB record 2101: 'Managing response burden is an ongoing challenge for Statistics Canada. In an attempt to alleviate response burden, especially for small businesses, the MSM derives sales data for low-revenue establishments from Goods and Service Tax (GST) files using a ratio estimator.' So part of the monthly manufacturing sales figure — which the monthly GDP programme uses as its indicator for most manufacturing industries — is not collected at all but estimated from tax remittances.
reports.cadence_note: A terminus has no publication cadence. GST filing frequency is set by the filer's revenue — monthly, quarterly or annually — and record 2101 does not state which vintage the MSM reads. 4 is the middle case and is a guess, flagged as such rather than left to look measured.

release_schedule.note: The corpus's existing url (StatCan IMDB SDDS=2101) actually resolves to the unrelated 'Monthly Survey of Manufacturing' record, not a GST administrative-data survey. The closest identifiable publicly-released product matching 'GST administrative files' from CRA is the annual 'GST/HST Statistics' series (CRA's own description: 'Detailed profiles of goods and services tax/harmonized sales tax (GST/HST) registrants'), published via canada.ca and the Open Government Portal. No fixed release calendar or stated rule was found; editions have appeared once per year but the month has drifted earlier each cycle (June 2024 -> May 2025 -> March 2026), so the next edition (likely '2026 Edition', covering 2020-2024) is expected roughly Q1-Q2 2027 but no specific date can be confirmed from published sources as of 2026-08-11.

reports.title: T1, T2, T3010 and T5013 tax data (Integrated Business Statistics Program)
reports.description: Four named corporate and unincorporated tax returns that substitute for survey responses across the Integrated Business Statistics Program. IMDB record 2103 states both the mechanism and the motive: 'A strategy to replace survey data with tax data has been introduced to reduce the respondent burden and survey costs... As part of the Integrated Business Statistics Program (IBSP), T1 tax data are used for unincorporated businesses, T2 tax data for incorporated businesses, T3010 tax data for registered charities and T5013 tax data for partnerships. Data replacement may be used to correct outliers or to replace partially or completely missing data. Tax data may also be used to reconcile survey data.' Worth noting how thoroughly record 2103 discloses while naming nothing citable — the fed-h15 pattern arriving in a manufacturing survey. Named here for the ASML specifically, but the IBSP spans most StatCan business surveys, so this node will gain in-degree as the corpus grows rather than staying a leaf.
reports.cadence_note: A terminus has no publication cadence. Annual tax filings; the number is the filing rhythm, not a release rate.

release_schedule.note: The corpus URL (StatCan IMDB SDDS=2103) is the survey page for the Annual Survey of Manufacturing and Logging Industries (ASML), one of several annual business surveys under the Integrated Business Statistics Program (IBSP). That page carries the exact boilerplate passage matching this report's title: 'As part of the Integrated Business Statistics Program (IBSP), T1 tax data are used for unincorporated businesses, T2 tax data for incorporated businesses, T3010 tax data for registered charities and T5013 tax data for partnerships.' This same administrative-tax-data description appears generically across many IBSP survey pages (it describes a data-collection method, not a standalone dated publication), so there is no single dedicated 'tax data' release calendar. The dated releases actually shown on this page (for 2024 reference-year data: December 18, 2025 and March 27, 2026) both fall before today (2026-08-11). Reference-period collection runs April-August of the year after the reference year, with a first release the following December and a revision the following March -- an annual pattern. Projecting that pattern forward gives an expected release around December 2026 (for 2025 reference-year data) with a follow-up revision around March 2027. These are inferred/projected dates, not dates published on a forward-looking calendar.

reports.title: Business Payrolls Survey (BPS)
reports.description: Monthly collection instrument for the Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours, IMDB record 2614. Statistics Canada's own record: the BPS is 'the collection instrument for the Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours (SEPH) (record number 2612)'; BPS results are merged with administrative data to produce SEPH's monthly estimates of earnings, jobs and hours worked by industry at national, provincial and territorial levels. Minted 2026-08-09 (sweep session, Tier-2 item #12) closing a `no-node-yet` lead: record 2612 itself names the BPS as a live input ('The Business Payrolls Survey (BPS) conducted monthly, is used to collect SEPH variables not available from administrative sources'), and this session retrieved the BPS's own IMDB record confirming a monthly cadence.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly. Statistics Canada's own record 2614 states 'Frequency: Monthly'.
