release_schedule.note: The Business Payrolls Survey (BPS, SDDS 2614) is a component survey that feeds into the combined Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours (SEPH, SDDS 2612), published monthly via Statistics Canada's 'The Daily' under the title 'Payroll employment, earnings and hours, and job vacancies.' The BPS's own IMDB page (SDDS 2614) states data release specifics are covered under record 2612 and does not itself carry a release calendar. The July 30, 2026 Daily release (covering May 2026 data) explicitly states: 'June 2026 data for SEPH and JVWS will be released on August 27, 2026.' The subsequent two entries (Sept 24, Oct 29) are taken from a search-indexed 2026 StatCan release-schedule PDF and are consistent with the observed ~2-month reference-lag, last-Thursday-of-month pattern seen across Jan-May 2026 releases, but were not independently re-verified against the primary PDF page-by-page, hence marked implied.

dependencies.basis: Record 2612, Data sources: 'The statistics compiled by SEPH are based on a census of administrative records for all in-scope establishments with employees that can be found on the Business Register. Administrative information for total gross monthly payrolls and the total number of employees for the last pay period in the month are obtained from payroll deduction (PD7 form) accounts maintained by Canada Revenue Agency.' A census of these records rather than a sample of employers, which makes this the strongest available characterisation short of calculated_from. Held at uses_data_from because SEPH applies estimation on top — the same record describes model groups and a Business Payrolls Survey filling gaps — so the payroll figure is not arithmetic on the remittances alone.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Administrative information for total gross monthly payrolls and the total number of employees for the last pay period in the month are obtained from payroll deduction (PD7 form) accounts maintained by Canada Revenue Agency.

dependencies.basis: Record 2101, Use of Administrative Data: 'In an attempt to alleviate response burden, especially for small businesses, the MSM derives sales data for low-revenue establishments from Goods and Service Tax (GST) files using a ratio estimator.' The word 'derives' plus a named estimator is a direct-input claim; it applies to a stated subset of establishments rather than the whole, which is why this is uses_data_from and not calculated_from.
dependencies.evidence_quote: In this methodology, a model that describes the relationship between estimated sales coming from the MSM and sales coming from the Goods and Services Tax (GST) data at a small level of geography is combined with traditional estimates obtained from the weighted MSM sample.

dependencies.basis: Record 2103, Data sources: 'As part of the Integrated Business Statistics Program (IBSP), T1 tax data are used for unincorporated businesses, T2 tax data for incorporated businesses, T3010 tax data for registered charities and T5013 tax data for partnerships. Data replacement may be used to correct outliers or to replace partially or completely missing data. Tax data may also be used to reconcile survey data.' Three distinct uses in one passage — substitution, outlier correction and reconciliation — all of which are the target's figures entering the source.
dependencies.evidence_quote: As part of the Integrated Business Statistics Program (IBSP), T1 tax data are used for unincorporated businesses, T2 tax data for incorporated businesses, T3010 tax data for registered charities and T5013 tax data for partnerships. Data replacement may be used to correct outliers or to replace partially or completely missing data. Tax data may also be used to reconcile survey data.

dependencies.basis: IMDB record 1301, the monthly GDP-by-industry programme, states its indicator sources by name: 'Data from the Monthly Survey of Manufacturing are used as indicators for most manufacturing industries. Data from the Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours are used for many service industries.' The same sentence is the basis for the already-existing edge to statcan-seph, so `uses_data_from` follows that precedent. Corroborated independently by the programme's own source table, which names 'Monthly Survey of Manufacturing, Record no. 2101' in the gross-output rows for manufacturing industries — the same table and the same rows that produced the IPPI edge in V0.11.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Data from the Monthly Survey of Manufacturing are used as indicators for most manufacturing industries. Data from the Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours are used for many service industries.

dependencies.basis: Stated by the annual survey rather than by the monthly one, in the present tense. IMDB record 2103: 'Within Statistics Canada, the data are used by the Canadian System of National Accounts, the Monthly Survey of Manufacturing (record number 2101) and Prices programs.' This is a reverse-direction disclosure — the target naming its consumers — and it is the only present-tense statement available. Record 2101's own account of the relationship is past tense and expired: 'Up to and including 2003, the MSM was benchmarked to the Annual Survey of Manufactures and Logging (ASML)', which is recorded in the `_dropped` block rather than used here, because a benchmarking arrangement that ended in 2003 is not a live dependency.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Within Statistics Canada, the data are used by the Canadian System of National Accounts, the Monthly Survey of Manufacturing (record number 2101) and Prices programs.

dependencies.basis: Record 2101 states it twice, in the target population and in the estimation method. Target population description: 'The target population for the MSM consists of all statistical establishments on the Business Register that are classified to the manufacturing sector (by NAICS), which are categorized into over 156 industries.' Estimation description: 'The estimation system generates estimates using the NAICS.' `methodology_depends_on` matches the type on every other NAICS edge in the graph.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The target population for the MSM consists of all statistical establishments on the Business Register that are classified to the manufacturing sector (by NAICS), which are categorized into over 156 industries.

dependencies.basis: Record 2103, target population: 'The target population of the Annual Survey of Manufacturing and Logging (ASML) comprises all establishments primarily engaged in manufacturing and logging activities. The data are classified by industry based on the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS). Under the NAICS, logging establishments are classified to NAICS code 1133 and manufacturing establishments to NAICS sectors 31, 32 and 33.' Restated in the sampling description: 'Prior to the selection of a random sample, enterprises are classified into homogeneous groups (i.e., groups with the same North American Industry Classification System codes and same geography) based on the characteristics of their establishments.'
dependencies.evidence_quote: The data are classified by industry based on the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS).

dependencies.basis: THE WEAKEST EDGE IN THIS SLICE, and flagged rather than buried. The NOC 2021 introduction states: 'It is important to note that the redesign of the NOC can have significant implications for several Surveys, such as the Labour Force Survey (LFS), and ESDC programs such as the Temporary Foreign Worker Program and Employment Insurance program.' This is a statement that a revision reaches the LFS, not a statement that the LFS uses the NOC, and the direction has to be read out of it rather than off it. It is taken on the precedent already set for boc-prime-rate -> boc-policy-rate, which rests on the Bank of Canada's word 'affects' and was accepted as `uses_data_from` on exactly that reasoning. It is also corroborated structurally by NOC being 'the departmental standard for data collection and dissemination for occupations at Statistics Canada' as of 10 August 2021. The clean version of this edge is a passage in the LFS's own record 3701 saying it codes occupation to NOC; that passage has not been retrieved, and the `_dropped` block records it as the lead to close.

Record 2612 names the Business Payrolls Survey as a live input in its own words: 'The Business Payrolls Survey (BPS) conducted monthly, is used to collect SEPH variables not available from administrative sources.' Held at uses_data_from rather than calculated_from because the BPS supplies only the variables the PD7/administrative sources cannot, i.e. a supplementary rather than arithmetic input.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Other key variables, including number of hours worked, are collected by the Business Payrolls Survey (BPS) which collects monthly data directly from a sample of establishments drawn from the BR.

_dropped.why: Record 2612's Quality evaluation section says 'Prior to the release, comparisons with independent sources such as the Labour Force Survey are performed.' A comparison against an independent source is the opposite of a dependency claim — the word 'independent' is doing the work. This is the third recorded instance of the 'comparable with is not a dependency claim' family, after record 1301's 'more comparable with' and H.15's 'are equivalent to'.

_dropped.edge: an IMDB page can date its own arrangement in the past tense
_dropped.why: Not a dropped edge — the edge exists, on other evidence. Recorded because record 2101 describes the relationship in the past tense and dates its end: 'Up to and including 2003, the MSM was benchmarked to the Annual Survey of Manufactures and Logging (ASML). Benchmarking was the regular review of the MSM estimates in the context of the annual data provided by the ASML.' Taking that quote as the basis would have put a 2003 arrangement in the graph as a live dependency. The edge is instead sourced to record 2103's present-tense 'the data are used by'. New corpus rule implied: an IMDB methodology page can describe a superseded arrangement in the same register as a current one, and the tense is the only signal.

Record 2103's quality section says 'The survey estimates are also analyzed with trends observed in related Statistics Canada data series (e.g., Monthly Survey of Manufacturing (record number 2101), sub-annual manufacturing commodity surveys).' Analysis against a related series is a validation check, not an input, and reading it as an edge would have created a false mutual pair with the real ASML edge — which matters more than usual now that mutual pairs are known to move the ranking.

The single most tempting edge in this slice and the document refuses it. NOC 2021's introduction: 'The NOC is comparable to the International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO) published by the International Labour Organization (ILO).' The same passage then limits it: 'certain conceptual differences between the NOC 2021 Version 1.0 and ISCO-08 limit comparability. For instance, differences in the classification criteria and classification structure exist between NOC 2021 Version 1.0 and ISCO-08. Additionally, subsistence occupations included in ISCO are not part of the NOC.' The relationship is parallel development with cross-team communication in the 1980s, not derivation. A correspondence table 'will be developed and published' — a concordance between two standards is not a dependency of either on the other.

NAPCS is NAICS's sibling, not its dependent. The introduction: 'The NAPCS project followed the adoption by the three countries of a common industry classification, the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) in 1997. The purpose of the NAICS project was to develop a standard that allowed comparisons of industry data among the three participating countries. The development of NAPCS was meant to serve the same purpose but for product statistics.' Same programme, same participants, same purpose, different axis. Historical sequence is not derivation.

An explicit documented non-dependency, and the strongest kind. NAPCS's introduction: 'NAPCS Canada is not fully compatible with the CPC. In order to do so, it would have been necessary for the most detailed categories of NAPCS Canada to coincide with, be grouped or be subset of, the most detailed categories of the CPC. This would have required changes to the national classification not possible at this time.' The document states the relationship does not hold and says why.

RE-CHECKED 2026-08-09 (sweep session, Tier-2 item #12), still blocked. Searched specifically for a dedicated SUPC publication page (title, publisher statement, revision cadence). Statistics Canada's own 'Industry, product and final demand classifications' guide (13-607-x) mentions SUPC only in passing — identifying it as the product classification used in supply and use tables and noting it is 'anchored to' NAPCS and the Harmonized System — with no publisher statement, formal title page or stated revision cadence of its own. Nothing else searched surfaced a dedicated SUPC record either. Confirms the original blocker rather than resolving it: SUPC appears only ever as a component described inside other classifications' own documentation (NAPCS's introduction, the supply-and-use accounts guide), never as a document with its own publication facts to cite. Original entry follows.

LEAD, and the best one in this slice. The Supply and Use Product Classification is what actually connects NAPCS to the accounts, and NAPCS's introduction states both halves. The dependency: 'The Supply and Use Product Classification (SUPC) is the basis for the commodity accounts' and 'the Supply and Use Product Classification (SUPC) used for the production of input-output tables is largely embedded at the level of NAPCS Canada.' The containment: 'The SUPC has been integrated into NAPCS Canada at the class level (5-digit) where conceptually and practically feasible... More than 80% of the remaining categories of NAPCS classes coincide with those of SUPC.' So the honest model is a statcan-supc node with part_of set to napcs and an edge from statcan-sut to it — the second use of part_of, and the first between two classifications. Blocked on publication facts for the SUPC: no title page, publisher or revision cadence has been retrieved. Deliberately NOT shortcut into a statcan-sut -> napcs edge, because that would justify an edge with a quote about a different release, which is the substitution error V0.11 refused an Equalization edge for.

_dropped.edge: the LFS-side passage that would strengthen statcan-lfs -> noc
_dropped.why:
RE-CHECKED 2026-08-09 (sweep session, Tier-2 item #12), still open. Searched for LFS variable/classification documentation naming NOC directly (as opposed to the NOC's own introduction naming the LFS, which is the weak direction already wired). Results returned only LFS output tables cross-tabulated by 'National Occupational Classification for Statistics (NOC-S)' — confirming the LFS does code occupation to some NOC-derived scheme in its published output, but not a methodology or variable-documentation passage stating that the LFS's own occupation variable is built on the NOC standard, which is the specific passage this entry wants. Confirms the original finding rather than changing it. Original entry follows.

A lead, not a dropped edge — the edge exists, weakly, on the NOC's own wording, and this is the passage that would make it strong. IMDB record 3701's Data sources section was retrieved and describes only collection method: 'Data are collected directly from survey respondents... by in-person interview; by telephone interview; or by self-completed electronic questionnaire.' It names no classification and no release at all. The passage wanted is in the LFS's variable or classification documentation rather than its Data sources block, and it has not been retrieved.

RESOLVED 2026-08-09 (sweep session, Tier-2 item #12). The BPS's own IMDB record (SDDS 2614) was retrieved: title 'Business Payrolls Survey (BPS)', publisher Statistics Canada, frequency monthly, and its own description confirms it as 'the collection instrument for the Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours (SEPH) (record number 2612)'. Minted as statcan-bps, releases_per_year 12, and wired statcan-seph -> statcan-bps, uses_data_from. Original entry follows.

LEAD. Record 2612 names the Business Payrolls Survey as a live input in its own words: 'The Business Payrolls Survey (BPS) conducted monthly, is used to collect SEPH variables not available from administrative sources.' That is a clean uses_data_from with a stated monthly cadence. Blocked only on publication facts for the BPS — its own IMDB record number has not been retrieved and inventing a URL for it is not acceptable.

_dropped.edge: statcan-seph -> provincial, territorial and federal payroll records
_dropped.why: The second administrative input in record 2612, and the one that stays dropped: 'Information for general government services is provided to SEPH on a monthly basis by the provincial, territorial and federal governments in the form of electronic files extracted from their payroll records.' Unlike the PD7 accounts — now a terminus node — this names no instrument at all, only a transfer of files from an unspecified number of governments. A terminus still has to be one identifiable thing that a document names; 'electronic files extracted from their payroll records' across fourteen governments is not one thing, and inventing a node for it would be inventing the boundary.

A confirmed and useful absence. Record 3701's Data sources section names no publication of any kind: 'Statistics Canada collects LFS information from the working-age population aged 15 and older... Data are collected directly from survey respondents.' The Labour Force Survey is a primary collection with no upstream release, which is a fact about the programme and not a gap in the research. This is exactly the case the determination field and the disclosure ratio exist to render, and it is a cleaner worked example than fed-h15 because there is nothing unpublishable behind it either — there is simply nothing behind it.

_dropped.edge: statcan-cchs (Canadian Community Health Survey) as a node
_dropped.why:
RECORD NUMBER FOUND 2026-08-09 (sweep session, Tier-2 item #12) for the missing half of this entry. Statistics Canada's IMDB lists Canadian International Merchandise Trade under two separate record numbers depending on basis, neither of which is 3226: SDDS 2201 for 'Canadian International Merchandise Trade (Customs Basis)' and SDDS 2202 for 'Canadian International Merchandise Trade (Balance of Payments Basis)' (a third, related record, SDDS 5295, covers 'Canadian international merchandise trade by industry for all countries'). Not independently re-verified against either record's own page this session — only located via search — so treat as a lead on where to look, not a confirmed replacement citation. Does not change the CCHS finding itself (record 3226 is still confirmed as the Canadian Community Health Survey) or the standing-alone-nodes blocker, which remains open. Original entry follows.

LEAD, and a record-number correction. IMDB record 3226 was requested as Canadian International Merchandise Trade and is actually 'Canadian Community Health Survey - Annual Component (CCHS)', annual. Its Data sources section names no release — collection is by EQ, CATI and CAPI, with linkage to 'the personal tax records (T1, T1FF or T4) of respondents'. So the CCHS would enter the graph as an island: a real annual programme, in health, with no documented upstream release and no documented downstream consumer yet found. Deferred pending the standing-alone-nodes decision, since under the current loader an island node is dropped from every build. The record number for Canadian International Merchandise Trade remains unknown and was not guessed at.

_dropped.edge: classification standards as an entry strategy
_dropped.why: A correction to EXPANSION-V1's stated plan, from the first attempt at executing it. The plan said to enter new territory through its classification hub, on the grounds that a classification is a hub by construction. Half right: NAICS gained two incoming edges from this slice, but NOC and NAPCS between them produced one weak edge and four documented non-dependencies, because a classification document describes alignment, comparability and concordance rather than derivation. The hub is a hub because other documents name it, not because it names things. So the entry move is not 'read the classification', it is 'find the programmes coded on it and read their methodology pages' — which is what produced every NAICS edge in the corpus, including both of this slice's.

_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Mali researched as part of a push into WAEMU/Sahel territory the branch's source docx had only described in undifferentiated bloc-level prose without naming individual countries. Mali is notable as AFRISTAT's headquarters and as a country whose statistics have operated under real political strain (2012 crisis, 2020/2021 coups, ECOWAS sanctions period) -- researched directly rather than assuming either a functioning or a collapsed system. Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review.
_note: AFRISTAT's own site states plainly it is headquartered in Bamako, Mali, and independently documents leading the WAEMU-wide IHPC renovation project with INSTAT Mali's own Director General chairing a November 2024 Bamako workshop validating the draft base-2023 regulation (also attended by AFRISTAT, BCEAO and IMF staff) -- the strongest institutional AFRISTAT-country linkage found anywhere in this branch. AFRISTAT itself is still not minted as a node (an institution without a titled publication, per this corpus's own rule), but a UEMOA Commission document describing the WAEMU-wide harmonised CPI framework -- including a named, numbered regulation (Reglement N 03/2017/CM/UEMOA) -- was independently opened and quoted, giving this branch its first genuinely-researched bloc-level document. It describes the base-2014 generation of the WAEMU harmonised CPI; Mali's own INSTAT page shows the country has since rebased to base 2023, and the Bamako workshop confirms a base-2023 successor regulation was still in draft, not yet Council-of-Ministers-adopted, as of November 2024 -- so the edge below is recorded as a citation to the WAEMU framework generally, not a current-methodology dependency, and flagged accordingly. On social protection, Mali's flagship cash-transfer programme (Jigisemejiri) is the most concrete finding: two independent World Bank documents show a flat monthly amount increased once, in 2018, explicitly 'on account of inflation and currency devaluation' but with no formula -- and the programme itself formally closed 30 June 2023, with no confirmed successor located.

_open_questions.question: If AFRISTAT (or a specific titled AFRISTAT publication, e.g. the numbered newsletter 'La Lettre d'AFRISTAT') is ever minted as a node, should country be 'ML' (AFRISTAT's own text: "AFRISTAT, qui a son siege a Bamako au Mali") or 'INT' (AFRISTAT's own text also self-describes as an international organisation founded by treaty among 14 African Franc Zone states)? Both are documented and defensible; not resolved this session.

A November 2024 Bamako workshop (opened by INSTAT Mali's own Director General) validated a draft UEMOA regulation adopting the base-2023 IHPC, ahead of submission to the Council of Ministers -- no later document confirming formal Council-of-Ministers adoption was found, even though Mali's own INSTAT page already publishes on base 2023 today. Sequencing between national implementation and Union-wide legal adoption is unresolved.

Mali's Jigisemejiri cash-transfer programme formally closed 30 June 2023 per its own World Bank technical paper. A November 2022 news article discussed a planned 'deuxieme generation' from 2023, but no document confirming what (if anything) replaced Jigisemejiri as of 2026 was located.

Mali's 2025 Article IV Consultation report references 'Annex VIII. Data Issues' (p.50), which very likely contains a formal SDDS/GDDS characterization and CPI-specific commentary, but the annex itself could not be retrieved this session (blocked by an Akamai edge response on direct download; WebFetch returned only the table-of-contents reference).

reports.title: Indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation (IHPC)
reports.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique du Mali (INSTAT)
reports.description: Mali's harmonised consumer price index, base 2023 (replacing base 2014, itself replacing base 2008 and the original 1996 rollout). "Cet indice est harmonise car la methodologie utilisee pour sa production est identique dans les huit pays membres de l'Union Economique et Monetaire Ouest Africaine (UEMOA)." Formula changed at the 2023 rebasing from Laspeyres to a chained Young index ("un indice de Young chaine"); basket now 766 varieties across 4,927 points of sale, roughly 30,150 monthly price observations, versus ~650 varieties and 3,344 outlets under the outgoing base-2014 methodology.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly bulletin archive on INSTAT's own site runs unbroken (all twelve months listed per year) from 2009 through 2025, plus January-June 2026 as of this session's check -- including full coverage through the 2012 crisis year and both 2020/2021 coup years.

release_schedule.note: No dated release calendar or stated publication rule found for IHPC specifically (the site's only 'Calendrier de diffusion' PDF is a general SSN calendar dated 2021). Instead, the monthly bulletin PDFs' own embedded CreationDate metadata was checked directly for the six most recent 2026 releases, giving the publication lag after each reference month: Jan-2026 data -> published 2026-02-12 (ihpc0126_pub.pdf); Feb-2026 -> 2026-03-11; Mar-2026 -> 2026-04-10; Apr-2026 -> 2026-05-19; May-2026 -> 2026-06-10; Jun-2026 -> 2026-07-10 (ihpc0626_pub.pdf, the latest posted as of this check). This is a consistent ~day-10-to-19-of-next-month pattern. As of 2026-08-11, no July-2026 bulletin (ihpc0726_pub.pdf, checked directly, returns 404) or press release page has appeared yet, so the next release is projected in the 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-19 window by this observed lag, not a published date.

reports.title: Indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation (IHPC) au sein de l'UEMOA
reports.region: WAEMU (8 member states, incl. Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal)
reports.description: The UEMOA Commission's own descriptive note on the Union-wide Harmonised CPI (dated avril 2023, published mai 2023), describing the then-current base-2014 generation: "Ce dernier indice a ete valide par le reglement N 03/2017/CM/UEMOA portant adoption des modalites d'elaboration et de calcul de l'Indice Harmonise des Prix a la Consommation au sein des Etats membres de l'UEMOA (IHPC base 100 en 2014)." States the index is Laspeyres-type, weights from national consumption/poverty surveys fielded 2011-2014, classified under NCOA-IHPC (a WAEMU-specific nomenclature "derivee de la COICOP"). Independently opened and quoted by two separate country-level research passes this session (Mali and Côte d'Ivoire) -- this branch's first bloc-level WAEMU/UEMOA document to be directly researched rather than only referenced in secondary summaries. Describes the base-2014 generation; both Mali and Côte d'Ivoire have since rebased nationally to base 2023, and a successor Union-wide regulation was still in draft, not confirmed adopted, as of a November 2024 validation workshop.

dependencies.basis: INSTAT Mali's own IHPC methodology page: "...les ponderations proviennent de l'enquete harmonisee sur les conditions de vie des menages « EHCVM 2021 »".

WEAK/COMPOSITE EVIDENCE, kept and flagged rather than dropped, per this branch's own precedent for low-confidence-but-real findings (see au-cgc-gst-relativities). No single document states this Mali-specific link directly: INSTAT Mali's own page states its methodology "est identique dans les huit pays membres de l'UEMOA," and this UEMOA note separately states the Union-wide IHPC (of which Mali is one of the eight producing states by treaty membership) "a ete valide par le reglement N 03/2017/CM/UEMOA." The regulation this note describes covers the base-2014 generation; Mali's live IHPC is now base 2023, and the base-2023 successor regulation was still in draft as of November 2024 (see ml-uemoa-base2023-regulation-adoption-unconfirmed). Downgraded from methodology_depends_on to cites to reflect both the compositional and generational gaps.

AFRISTAT itself is an institution without a titled publication and fails this corpus's node rule. Two independent World Bank documents describe Mali's flagship cash-transfer safety net (Jigisemejiri) paying a fixed monthly amount (FCFA 10,000, later FCFA 15,000) with no stated indexation formula. The one documented increase (2018) is explicitly attributed to 'inflation and currency devaluation' as a rationale -- "The resources allowed for an increase in both the number of transfer beneficiaries as well as the transfer amount, on account of inflation and currency devaluation" -- but is a one-off, refinancing-linked adjustment, not a rule. No node minted for Jigisemejiri itself (a programme, not a titled recurring publication); the programme formally closed 30 June 2023 with no confirmed successor (see ml-jigisemejiri-successor-unconfirmed).

reports.title: Central Statistical Organization (CSO) institutional core
reports.description: Primary national statistical office responsible for censuses, surveys, national accounts, prices, labour, demographic and multi-domain socio-economic statistics. Publishes the Statistical Yearbook and participates in the IMF enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS).
reports._notes: Foundational institutional node for the Myanmar statistical system. Data continuity and coverage are constrained relative to many peers.
reports._cadence_evidence: CSO site advertises the Myanmar Statistical Yearbook as its flagship, latest edition 2025, one per year. The site also lists Selected Monthly Economic Indicators (monthly) and a Quarterly Statistics Bulletin, but the newest SMEI shown is January 2021 and the newest quarterly bulletin is 2022-2023, so only the annual yearbook is still current; 1 reflects the yearbook.

reports.title: Population census and estimates
reports.description: Official population census and subsequent estimates. Population is approximately 55 million; the age structure remains relatively young.
reports._notes: Core demographic node. Population ~55 million.
reports._url_evidence: MMSIS (Central Statistical Organization) 'Census Reports' page listing the 2014 Myanmar Population and Housing Census volumes (Union Report Vol 2-B/2-C, thematic reports on mortality, gender, disability, older population) and the 2014-2050 population projections report.
reports._cadence_evidence: MMSIS population file list shows only 2014 census thematic outputs (e.g. thematic report on population projections 2014-2050), all with the same entry date of 2018-03-22. No periodicity is stated and there is no second census cycle on the page to count from.

reports.title: National Accounts of Myanmar (GDP)
reports.description: Official national accounts (GDP). Central macro-output series for an economy heavily shaped by agriculture, extractives, informal activity and political-institutional constraints.
reports._notes: Primary macroeconomic output node. Interpretation requires care given data gaps and informal activity.
reports._url_evidence: MMSIS 'National income' indicator page for Gross Domestic Product (At Current Producers' Prices), showing a 2012-2023 series in Kyat million (125,338,951.9 for 2022) broken into agriculture, industry and services.
reports._cadence_evidence: MMSIS GDP indicator is a single annual series (GDP at current producers' prices by sector) with one observation per year from 2012 to 2023; no sub-annual periods and no stated update frequency. Series is effectively dormant - it ends at 2023 with no later period posted.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index and inflation statistics
reports.description: CPI and inflation rates. Inflation has been elevated and volatile in recent years under exchange-rate pressures and supply disruptions.
reports._notes: Core high-frequency price node under elevated-inflation conditions.
reports._url_evidence: MMSIS/CSO 'Inflation Reports' series page listing monthly inflation report PDFs; note the series visibly stops at December 2020, so it is a dormant post-coup product page rather than a current one.
reports._cadence_evidence: MMSIS CPI file list is a run of monthly 'Inflation Report (Month Year)' items - March 2020 through December 2020 on the first page, with further pages of earlier months. Series is dormant: the newest edition is December 2020, so nothing has been posted for five years, but the cadence while running was monthly.

reports.title: Balance of Payments and external accounts
reports.description: BOP and external-sector statistics. Current-account dynamics, limited FDI, and large errors and omissions reflecting informal and unrecorded cross-border activity are recurring features.
reports._notes: External-accounts node under constrained data and institutional conditions.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved and read: Myanmar Statistical Yearbook 2024, Part 3 (Central Statistical Organization). It contains Chapter 13 'Foreign Trade and Investment', whose Table 13.15 is 'Balance of Payments' for FY2019/2020 to FY2023/2024, with current-account items (exports f.o.b., imports f.o.b., trade balance, services, primary income, secondary income) and financial-account components. This is an official national BOP presentation, obtained after the NSDP's designated URL (cbm.gov.mm/content/3905) again failed - cbm.gov.mm returns HTTP 503 on robots.txt for both www and bare hostnames.
reports._url_route: successor publisher - CSO publications index (csostat.gov.mm) after the NSDP-designated CBM page stayed unreachable
reports._cadence_evidence: The linked file is Myanmar Statistical Yearbook 2024 Part 3 (foreign trade and investment chapter); the yearbook is an annual CSO volume and its methodology sheets give dissemination frequency as 'Yearly' for these tables.

reports.title: Agriculture production statistics
reports.description: Official and compiled statistics on crop and livestock production. Agriculture remains a large share of employment and rural livelihoods; rice is the dominant staple and a material export crop.
reports._notes: Core primary-sector production node. Data coverage is incomplete relative to pre-2021 benchmarks.
reports._url_evidence: MMSIS/CSO 'General Reports' page whose listing is dominated by the Myanmar Agricultural Statistics series, most recent edition covering 2016-2017 to 2024-2025.
reports._cadence_evidence: MMSIS lists successive editions of Myanmar Agricultural Statistics, each covering a rolling set of fiscal years - 2012-13 to 2020-21 (entered 2023-01-03), 2013-14 to 2021-22 (2023-04-28), 2014-15 to 2022-23 (2024-03-22), and two newer volumes entered 2026-06-19. Roughly one new edition per year; no explicit frequency statement.

reports.title: Exchange-rate regime and parallel-market statistics
reports.publisher: Central Bank of Myanmar / parallel-market trackers
reports.description: Official and parallel-market exchange rates for the kyat. Multiple rates and a persistent parallel-market premium are structural features under currency controls, limited FX availability and elevated inflation.
reports._notes: Critical price and external-constraint node. Parallel-market premium is a key signal.
reports._url_evidence: MMSIS 'Foreign Exchange Rates' indicator page showing the official monthly kyat rate against USD and EUR from Aug 2021 to Jul 2022 (1,684-1,850 kyat/USD). reports.title: Arrêtés Conjoints portant répartition de la taxe sur le tonnage débarqué — Communauté Urbaine de Nouakchott et ses 9 communes membres (Recueil des Textes 2017, DGCT)
reports.publisher: Direction Générale des Collectivités Territoriales (DGCT), Ministère de l'Intérieur, avec l'appui de la Coopération française — compilant des Arrêtés Conjoints du Ministère de l'Intérieur, des Postes et Télécommunications (MIPT) et du Ministère des Finances (MF)
reports.description: DGCT's compiled 'Recueil des Textes 2017' (avec l'appui de la Coopération française) reproduces two joint ministerial arrêtés governing the split of the taxe sur le tonnage débarqué between the Communauté Urbaine de Nouakchott (CUN) and its 9 member communes. Arrêté Conjoint n°R884/MIPT/MF du 02 décembre 2001 (internal/PDF page 122), Article 4: "Le produit de la taxe sur le tonnage débarqué, telle que prévue aux termes de l'Ordonnance n° 90-04 du 6 février 1990, est réparti entre la Communauté Urbaine de Nouakchott et les neuf Communes membres, dans les proportions ci-après - Communauté urbaine de Nouakchott : 60 %; - Communes membres 40 %". Arrêté Conjoint n°R1198/MIPT/MF du 18 octobre 2002 (internal pages 124-125), "portant répartition de la part du produit de la taxe sur le tonnage débarqué revenant aux communes de l'agglomération de Nouakchott entre celles-ci", Article Premier: "le montant de la taxe sur le tonnage débarqué revenant aux communes de l'agglomération de Nouakchott est partagé en trois parts à raison de 50% pour la première part, 30% pour la seconde part et 20% pour la troisième part. La première part est répartie à part égale entre les neufs Communes. La deuxième part est répartie en fonction de la population communale constatée au recensement général des populations 2001. La troisième part est répartie de manière décroissante en fonction du produit de la taxe communale par habitant..." — followed by a named-commune allocation table (illustrative, base-year 2001 recensement) giving each commune's 'Part forfaitaire 50%', 'Part proportionnelle à la population 30%', and 'Part inversement proportionnelle au produit fiscal par habitant 20%', e.g. "Riyad 55,56 34,95 93,05 183,56 18,36" and "Tevragh Zeina 55,56 20,61 0,87 77,04 7,70", covering all 9 Nouakchott communes by name: Toujounine, Teyarett, Tevragh Zeina, Sebkha, Riyad, Ksar, El Mina, Arafat, Dar Naim. Both arrêtés are jointly issued by MIPT and MF; as of the 2017 compiled edition reviewed, no repeal is noted in the excerpt.

reports.title: Local Government Act 2011 (Act No. 36 of 2011), Section 83 — Grants to Municipal City Council, Municipal Town Council or District Council
reports.publisher: Attorney-General's Office, Mauritius (Revised Laws of Mauritius)
reports.description: Mauritius's national local-government statute, as consolidated in the Revised Laws of Mauritius (page marked "L18 – 52"). Section 83, "Grants to Municipal City Council, Municipal Town Council or District Council": "(1) (a) In every financial year, there shall be paid to the Municipal City Council, a Municipal Town Council or a District Council a grant from the Consolidated Fund of an amount calculated according to such formula as may be prescribed. (b) The formula for the payment of grants under this section shall operate for such period and on such conditions as may be prescribed." This is the enabling statutory clause — a Consolidated-Fund grant per a prescribed formula — not a document naming a specific council or a dollar figure; Sections 84 ("Release of grants") and 85 ("Annual estimates") are companion provisions. Sections 132–133 ("Obligation to prepare financial statements" / "Contents and form of financial statements") separately require every local authority other than a Village Council to produce audited financial statements within 3 months of the financial year end, and are the statutory basis the Municipal City Council of Port Louis cites for its own annual report (see mu-portlouis-citycouncil-annualreport-2017-18).
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, currently in force per the Revised Laws version fetched.

reports.title: Ministry of Local Government and Disaster Risk Management — Annual Report 2023-2024
reports.publisher: Ministry of Local Government and Disaster Risk Management, Mauritius

Moreover, funds to the tune of Rs 10.5M have been released to the Municipal Council of Port Louis for payment to Victoria Station Ltd (VSL) and compensation to Pick N Eat Rs 4.6 M. Rs 7.4 M to the District Council of Grand Port to meet its obligations towards Arbitration for Mahebourg Market." Companion data from Sections 6.1–6.3 (pages 37, 40): Vote 5-1 "Local Government" was budgeted at Rs 5,364,000,000 for FY2023-2024 (Rs 4,494,600,000 recurrent / Rs 869,400,000 capital), and "Grants Recurrent (Local Authorities)" made up 85.64% of the Ministry's Vote 5-1 actual expenditure per the report's own pie chart. Only the Municipal Council of Port Louis and the District Council of Grand Port are named individually with Rs figures in this document; Beau Bassin-Rose Hill, Curepipe, Quatre Bornes, and Vacoas-Phoenix are not individually named with figures here.

The Council was established in 1830 by Ordinance No 16," and "The financial statements of the City Council of Port Louis have been prepared in compliance with Section 132 and 133 of the Local Government Act 2011 and the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), with effect from 1st July 2017." reports.title: National Audit Office -- Audit Report on the Accounts of the Rodrigues Regional Assembly
reports.description: Series node folding two editions (FY2014, FY2019-20) of NAO's Rodrigues Regional Assembly audit series -- editions are never their own node (Midvamp Sec 2.1); each edition's specific findings stay in the citing edges' own basis text. Section 2.3 "Rodrigues Consolidated Fund (RCF) - Transfer from RCF to cater for Shortfall" (page 14): "RRA received a grant of some Rs 3,898 million from the Central Government in 2019-20. Revenue totalling some Rs 38 million were collected by the RRA, bringing the total inflow to some Rs 3,936 million. Total expenditure for 2019-20 amounted to Rs 3,955 million. Some Rs 20.9 million were transferred from RCF to cater for the shortfall." A three-year "Government Grant" comparison table in the same section: "3,681,490,778 [2019-20] / 3,575,000,000 [2018-19] / 3,425,000,000 [2017-18]" with corresponding "Additional Contribution 216,490,000 / 30,000,000 / -". Section 4.2, "Detailed Statement of Revenue of the Rodrigues Consolidated Fund" (Table 4, in Rs million): "Government Grant 3,897.98 [2019-20] / 3,605.00 [2018-19] / 3,425.00 [2017-18]," with: "Revenue of the RRA comprises principally of Grants/Contributions from the Central Government and internally generated revenue which consists of receipts from licence fees, social contributions, property income, sales of goods and services, incidental sales by non-market establishment, miscellaneous sales of goods and services, fines and miscellaneous revenue." CAVEAT: the report itself flags an internal accounting inconsistency — "An inconsistent accounting treatment of the item 'Grant - Contribution from Central Government'... The total Grants figure was wrongly stated as Rs 3,918,936,526" — a Rs 20,955,748 discrepancy between how the grant vs. RCF-transfer figures were classified in RRA's own accounts that year; the exact-rupee Table 2 figure (Rs 3,681,490,778) and the Table 4 Rs-million figure (3,897.98M, which appears inclusive of the Additional Contribution) do not reconcile cleanly and both should be treated as reported by the auditors rather than as a single unambiguous total.
reports.cadence_note: Annual audit report; part of NAO's dedicated Rodrigues Regional Assembly report series.

dependencies.basis: The Ministry's Annual Report 2023-2024 documents actual Grant-in-Aid disbursements (Rs 215M additional grant-in-aid; Rs 10.5M to the Municipal Council of Port Louis; Rs 7.4M to the District Council of Grand Port) that are payments under the same Consolidated-Fund grant-to-local-authorities mechanism the Local Government Act 2011's Section 83 establishes ("there shall be paid to the Municipal City Council, a Municipal Town Council or a District Council a grant from the Consolidated Fund of an amount calculated according to such formula as may be prescribed"). The Annual Report does not cite Section 83 by number, so this is recorded as a general institutional cites relationship rather than a stronger calculation dependency.

Port Louis's own financial statements state directly: "The financial statements of the City Council of Port Louis have been prepared in compliance with Section 132 and 133 of the Local Government Act 2011 and the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), with effect from 1st July 2017" — a direct 'our preparation methodology IS mandated by this Act' claim, naming the same Act (Local Government Act 2011) that mu-lga-2011-s83-grants represents.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The financial statements of the City Council of Port Louis have been prepared in compliance with Section 132 and 133 of the Local Government Act 2011 and the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), with effect from 1st July 2017

dependencies.basis: The NAO's audit report is on the accounts of the Rodrigues Regional Assembly, the body established by and operating under the Rodrigues Regional Assembly Act 2001, and its Section 2.5.1 quantifies the central-government grant that funds RRA's budget within the statutory framework (the Rodrigues Consolidated Fund, Section 42 of the Act) that mu-rodrigues-regional-assembly-act-2001 quotes. _status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Malawi is part of the AF branch's Southern Africa expansion (G.7-G.8). No raw docx entries exist for this country; every document below was located and verified from scratch this session via WebSearch + WebFetch, no import round used. Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review, following the established DRAFT-then-import pattern.
_note: The Social Cash Transfer Programme Strategic Plan is the most explicit, most self-critical 'denied' finding in this whole batch, more direct even than Eswatini's: the Government of Malawi's own strategic plan states in its own words that 'there is no systematic arrangement for adjusting the level of transfers for inflation', that 'the adjustment of transfer levels has been arbitrary and irregular: between 2006 and 2020 transfer levels were adjusted only three times', and commits to fixing it going forward -- 'A mechanism for regular adjustment of transfers will be instituted to account for inflation.' The same recommendation-reveals-absence shape as Botswana's 2020 Recovery Plan (G.7) and Tanzania's National Social Protection Policy 2023 (G.6), but stated even more bluntly, with a specific count of how rarely adjustment has actually happened.

_open_questions.question: This session confirmed only the CPI's base period ('Dec 2021=100', from an NSO news release) and monthly cadence. Weights survey, COICOP classification and index formula were not located after several attempts (NSO's own consumer-price-index page returned no methodology text on two different URLs; a direct Stats Flash PDF was not successfully located). Worth a dedicated retry, possibly via cms.nsomalawi.mw's document API (found in search but not explored) rather than the public-facing nsomalawi.mw pages tried this session.

The Strategic Plan (2022) commits to instituting a regular inflation-adjustment mechanism as a priority action. Whether that mechanism has actually been implemented in the four years since (2022-2026) was not checked this session -- a natural follow-up given how explicit the Plan's own admission of past failure is.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (Stats Flash)
reports.description: Malawi's official monthly Consumer Price Index release, published as a 'Stats Flash' bulletin. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via the NSO's October 2024 CPI news release: base period stated in-table as 'Overall CPI (Dec 2021=100)'. Monthly cadence confirmed (a Stats Flash is issued for each reference month). Weights survey, COICOP classification and index formula were not located this session despite multiple attempts -- the thinnest-documented CPI methodology in this Southern Africa batch (see _open_questions); NSO's public-facing CPI page returned no methodology text on two separate URLs tried.

release_schedule.note: NSO Malawi publishes a monthly CPI/inflation report ("Stats Flash"), typically released 15-19 days after the reference month ends (e.g. May 2026 CPI released 2026-06-19; June 2026 CPI released 2026-07-15). No published release calendar with exact future dates was found on the NSO site, so the next date is inferred from this recurring pattern rather than a stated calendar. July 2026 CPI was not yet found published as of 2026-08-11.

reports.title: Malawi Social Cash Transfer Programme Strategic Plan 2022-2027
reports.publisher: Government of Malawi, Ministry of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare
reports.description: The Government of Malawi's own strategic plan for its Social Cash Transfer Programme (SCTP), 2022. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Current transfer levels are fixed nominal Kwacha figures by household size (MK4,000 for one member up to MK8,000 for four, plus MK1,000/MK2,000 primary/secondary school bonuses, averaging MK9,000/household). On adjustment, the Plan is explicit and self-critical: 'Despite a recent ad hoc increase, there is no systematic arrangement for adjusting the level of transfers for inflation,' and historically, 'the adjustment of transfer levels has been arbitrary and irregular: between 2006 and 2020 transfer levels were adjusted only three times.' The Plan commits to a fix: 'A mechanism for regular adjustment of transfers will be instituted to account for inflation,' naming this a 2022 priority action.

_dropped.why: The Plan states outright: 'there is no systematic arrangement for adjusting the level of transfers for inflation' and that adjustments have happened only three times between 2006 and 2020. An explicit, self-critical denial from the implementing government itself, not an inference from silence.

_note: Mexico — Round 7 — browser/curl unblock of the access-blocked backlog, 2026-08-29. Every edge here closes a lead that an earlier round recorded as unreachable. The blocks were largely artefacts of the fetch tool, not the sites: mnd.gov.tw is fully readable to plain curl (its 'ROBOTS_DISALLOWED' verdict was WebFetch obeying robots.txt); gob.mx serves its /cms/uploads/attachment/file/ PDFs to curl while Akamai-challenging its HTML; BPS Indonesia's signed web-api.bps.go.id download host is not Cloudflare-walled even though every *.bps.go.id page is. dependencies.basis: INEGI's monthly IGAE boletín carries a full FICHA METODOLÓGICA in plain text, which states the indicator follows the international national-accounts guidelines of the 2008 SNA. Verbatim: "Además, se consideran los lineamientos internacionales sobre contabilidad nacional del Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales 2008 y del Manual de Cuentas Nacionales Trimestrales 2017." The round-2 diagnosis that inegi.org.mx/temas/igae/ is a JavaScript shell was correct — it is a 4,267-byte React shell — but the boletín PDF is the route around it, and the same sentence appears in an independent second issue (igae2025_07.pdf).

The same IGAE ficha metodológica states that volume indices are computed for 664 activity classes of SCIAN 2018 — the Mexican national version of NAICS — which the sector and subsector aggregates of the 'por actividad' breakdown are built from. Verbatim: "Se calculan índices de volumen físico para 664 clases de actividad económica del Sistema de Clasificación Industrial de América del Norte (SCIAN) 2018." The SCIAN-as-national-NAICS identification is the corpus's own, recorded in the naics node's description.

The IGAE ficha's Fuentes row names ENOE among the monthly INEGI statistics that feed the indicator. Verbatim: "Estadísticas mensuales que elabora el Instituto, como la Encuesta Mensual de la Industria Manufacturera (EMIM), Encuesta Nacional de Empresas Constructoras (ENEC), Encuesta Mensual sobre Empresas Comerciales (EMEC), Encuesta Mensual de Servicios (EMS), estadística de la Industria Minerometalúrgica (EIMM) y la Encuesta Nacional de Ocupación y Empleo (ENOE), los índices nacionales de precios y los registros administrativos, así como las estadísticas económicas y sociales compiladas por el Instituto."

The Secretaría de Bienestar's Informe Anual sobre la Situación de Pobreza y Rezago Social 2026 for Tuxtla Gutiérrez (07101) lists ENIGH 2024 as source footnote [2], carrying the municipal figures for indigenous self-ascription, indigenous-language speakers, literacy, employment by sector, total employed population and basic-basket access. Verbatim: "[2] Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (INEGI), con base en la Encuesta Nacional de Ingresos y Gastos de los Hogares (ENIGH) 2024." Note the document carrying the dependency is published by Bienestar, not by INEGI/CEIEG as the node's publisher field currently says.

dependencies.basis: Acapulco's own Plan Municipal de Desarrollo Urbano opens its socio-demographic diagnosis by taking the municipality's population count directly from the 2020 census. Verbatim: "El Censo de Población y Vivienda del Instituto Nacional de Estadística, Geografía e Informática (INEGI) (2020) contabilizó una población de 779,566 habitantes en el municipio de Acapulco de Juárez, que representan el 22.0% de la población estatal". Independently corroborated by the Bienestar municipal profile for Acapulco de Juárez (https://www.gob.mx/cms/uploads/attachment/file/1061187/12001_AcapulcoDeJuarez_2026.pdf), whose footnotes carry the identical census citations. Additionally, pMDU section 4.5.3 (Población Económicamente Activa) — the section round 2 could see only in the table of contents — derives Acapulco's PEA, employed and unemployed counts from the 2020 census and INEGI's occupation tabulations. Verbatim: "Del Censo de Población y Vivienda (2020) y de los Tabulados de INEGI, se señala que para el municipio de Acapulco la PEA3 representa el 66% de la población total de más de 15 años; el 98% de la PEA corresponde a la población ocupada con 377,351 personas y el 2% a población desocupada corresponde a 7,626 acapulqueños". The section's Table 27 source line reads "Fuente: Elaboración propia CONURBA, 2021; con base en Tabulados de Ocupación, INEGI; Censo de Población y Vivienda INEGI, 2020".

reports.title: Ley del Sistema Nacional de Información Estadística y Geográfica (LSNIEG)
reports.publisher: Congreso de la Unión / Estados Unidos Mexicanos
reports.description: Foundational 2008 statute (with subsequent reforms) that creates the autonomous INEGI and the entire Sistema Nacional de Información Estadística y Geográfica (SNIEG). It is the permanent legal basis for virtually all official Mexican statistics and is cited recurringly in methodology documents, publication calendars, and institutional descriptions as the source of INEGI’s mandate and of ‘Información de Interés Nacional’.

_variants.description: Foundational 2008 statute (last major reform DOF 14-11-2025) that creates the autonomous INEGI and the entire Sistema Nacional de Información Estadística y Geográfica (SNIEG). Regulates Information of National Interest, the rights/obligations of informants, and INEGI’s organisation and powers. Static instrument with no independent publication cadence of its own.
_variants.notes:
Classic pure recurring-citation node under the new rule. Every major INEGI methodology synthesis opens by grounding itself in this Law.

Contextual quote from Censo Agropecuario 2022 methodology (INEGI):
"El Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (INEGI), con el propósito de ofrecer estadísticas actuales, completas y oportunas de las actividades agropecuarias y forestales en México y con fundamento en las atribuciones que le confiere la Ley del Sistema Nacional de Información Estadística y Geográfica (LSNIEG), realizó el Censo Agropecuario 2022. El presente documento es una síntesis metodológica que da sustento y transparencia a los procedimientos conceptuales, operativos, de procesamiento, análisis de datos y difusión de resultados..."

Contextual quote from Censo de Población y Vivienda 2010 Síntesis metodológica:
"El Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (INEGI), con fundamento en lo dispuesto por la Constitución Política de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos en su Artículo 26, apartado B, y en el ejercicio de las atribuciones que la Ley del Sistema Nacional de Información Estadística y Geográfica le confiere, realizó el Censo de Población y Vivienda 2010. ... Bases legales. Para la generación de información estadística y geográfica, el INEGI se rige por lo dispuesto en la Ley del Sistema Nacional de Información Estadística y Geográfica (Ley del SNIEG) que tiene fundamento en lo dispuesto en el artículo 26, apartado B de la Constitución Política de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos."

The Law itself states (Art. 1): it is of public order, social interest and general observance throughout the Republic, and has as its object the regulation of the SNIEG, the rights and obligations of Informants, the organisation and functioning of INEGI, and administrative offences.
