reports.title: Wet waardering onroerende zaken (Wet WOZ)
reports.description: The national law requiring every Dutch municipality to determine an annual market value ('WOZ-waarde') for every real-estate object in its territory, executed by the municipal college van burgemeester en wethouders. Functions in this corpus the way `esa-2010` or `sna-2008` do — a legally-established methodology standard other documents cite as their valuation basis, rather than a periodical release. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: wetten.overheid.nl BWBR0007119 downloaded and parsed for the operative articles.
reports.cadence_note: Art. 22 lid 2: the value fixed by a municipality's beschikking 'geldt voor een kalenderjaar' (applies for one calendar year) — an annual valuation cycle.

release_schedule.rule: Wet WOZ, artikel 24 lid 1: "De beschikking wordt genomen binnen acht weken na het begin van het kalenderjaar waarvoor zij geldt." (The WOZ-beschikking [property value assessment notice] must be issued within eight weeks after the start of the calendar year for which it applies.) Article 18 lid 2 sets the valuation reference date (waardepeildatum) as one year before the start of that calendar year.
release_schedule.note: The 2026-cycle deadline (8 weeks after 1 January 2026, i.e. ~26 February 2026) has already passed relative to today (2026-08-11), so the next occurrence shown is the 2027 cycle. In practice nearly all municipalities issue the WOZ-beschikking combined with the annual municipal tax bill (gemeentelijke belastingaanslag) before 1 March each year, consistent with this 8-week statutory deadline. No published multi-year calendar of exact dates exists; the date above is computed from the statutory rule, not read off a calendar.

reports.title: Basisregistratie Kadaster (BRK)
reports.description: The Dutch national land registry base registration — cadastral designations, rights, parcel boundaries and owner information, one of the ten mandatory Dutch basisregistraties. A continuously-maintained authentic register rather than a periodical release, the same category as Ontario's Spatial Data Infrastructure terminus in this corpus — Kadaster's own materials describe what data the BRK contains but state no publication cadence or edition structure. reports.title: Forskrift om rapportering fra kommuner og fylkeskommuner mv. (KOSTRA-forskriften)
reports.description: Regulation of 18 October 2019 no. 1412, issued under kommuneloven (Act of 22 June 2018 no. 83) § 16-1 and IKS-loven § 42, prescribing what economic and service data municipalities, county authorities and inter-municipal companies must report and requiring that all KOSTRA reporting be made electronically to Statistics Norway. In force 1 January 2020. The Norwegian functional equivalent of the Dutch BBV/Iv3 reporting rules (nl-bbv) in this corpus.

release_schedule.note: This is a regulation (forskrift) governing when Norwegian municipalities/county municipalities must report data into KOSTRA each year, not a statistical publication itself. The `legislation.govt.nz` blocker described above is RESOLVED and the slice's load-bearing statutory chain has been re-read first-hand from the current consolidation, replacing the Wayback and FAOLEX proxy reads. The chain therefore terminates in the XRB by statutory definition, as `G.1.md` claimed, and the claim no longer rests on a proxy read of any kind. reports.title: Financial Statements of the Government of New Zealand
reports.description: The audited annual financial statements of the whole New Zealand government reporting entity, presented to Parliament as paper B.11. New Zealand's analog of Canada's Public Accounts. Prepared under the Public Finance Act 1989 and NZ GAAP as defined in the Financial Reporting Act 2013, on Public Sector PBE Accounting Standards Tier 1. The Treasury also publishes interim (monthly, year-to-date) financial statements through the year; `releases_per_year` counts the audited year-end set only.
reports.cadence_note: One audited year-end set (B.11), plus roughly eleven interim monthly year-to-date sets on the same basis; `releases_per_year` counts the audited set only, since the interim statements are the same document unaudited rather than a separate release.

entries.covers: Financial Statements of the Government of New Zealand for the Year Ended 30 June 2026

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar or statutory fixed date found on Treasury's site (legislation.govt.nz was inaccessible to confirm any Public Finance Act deadline). However, the audited year-end financial statements (B.11) have consistently been signed/issued in the first half of October each year: 5 Oct 2022 (FY2022), 5 Oct 2023 (FY2023), 10 Oct 2024 (FY2024), 9 Oct 2025 (FY2025). reports.title: Budget Economic and Fiscal Update
reports.description: The Treasury's Budget-day economic and fiscal forecasts, parliamentary paper B.3, required by the Public Finance Act 1989. Its forecasts become the 'Budget 20XX' comparatives in the following year's Financial Statements of the Government. A Half Year Economic and Fiscal Update (HYEFU) on the same statutory footing appears each December, and a Pre-election Update in election years; `releases_per_year` counts BEFU alone.
reports.cadence_note: BEFU annually in May; the companion HYEFU each December makes two statutory Updates a year, three in election years.

entries.covers: Budget 2027 BEFU (projected, exact Budget Day not yet announced)

release_schedule.note: BEFU is published annually alongside the government's Budget under the Public Finance Act 1989 (s26O), which requires a Budget Economic and Fiscal Update to accompany each year's Budget, but the Act does not fix a specific calendar date — Budget Day is set by the government each year. In practice Budget Day (and thus BEFU) has fallen in late May in every recent year observed (2024: 30 May; 2025: 22 May; 2026: 28 May, per Treasury's BEFU publication pages and Wikipedia's 2026 New Zealand budget article). No official date for Budget 2027 / BEFU 2027 had been announced as of 2026-08-11.

reports.title: Government finance statistics (general government)
reports.description: Stats NZ's annual consolidation of central and local government financial activity on the IMF's GFS framework — the direct counterpart of Australia's `au-abs-gfs`. Its own DataInfo+ metadata sets out a two-source split that is unusually explicit for this corpus: central government from the Treasury's CFISnet database, local government from the annual Local Authority Census supplemented by individual councils' annual reports.

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ publishes this annual report each November covering the fiscal year ended the preceding June. The Year ended June 2025 edition was released 27 November 2025 and explicitly stated: "Government finance statistics (general government): Year ended June 2026 will be released in November 2026." No exact day was given, only the month.

reports.title: Local authority statistics (quarterly)
reports.description: Quarterly income and expenditure statistics for New Zealand's 11 regional councils and 68 territorial authorities, collected through the Quarterly Local Authority Survey (QLAS, questionnaire BS/QS/01). Provisional until benchmarked against the annual Local Authority Census, and fed forward into the national accounts and into Government finance statistics as the provisional local-government estimate.

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ releases this report quarterly (March, June, September, December quarters). The March 2026 quarter release (published 10 June 2026, per its Mirage News mirror at https://www.miragenews.com/local-authority-statistics-march-2026-quarter-1689315/, which republishes the Stats NZ press release verbatim including the standard 'Next release' line) states: 'Local authority statistics: June 2026 quarter will be released on 7 September 2026.' The official stats.govt.nz page at the URL above corresponds to this same March 2026 quarter edition (confirmed reachable) but its full body text (including the next-release line) could not be extracted via the fetch tool, so the exact date is corroborated via the Mirage News mirror instead.

reports.title: Local Authority Census / Local Authority Financial Statistics
reports.description: The annual census of all city, district and regional councils and their non-market council-controlled organisations, and the Local Authority Financial Statistics (LAFS) compiled from it — the more comprehensive, less timely annual counterpart to QLAS. Stats NZ's own metadata states that LAFS is 'no longer published in the information release format used for 2009-13' and directs users to Infoshare instead, so the release exists as a data update rather than as a titled information release; kept as one node for that reason.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, released around May for the June year ending 11 months earlier. Distributed via Infoshare rather than as a titled information release since the 2009-13 series ended.

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ publishes 'Local authority financial statistics' (formerly 'Local Authority Census') annually. No published forward release calendar entry was found for this specific release, but three consecutive years show a consistent pattern: released in mid-to-late May, covering the local government financial year ended the preceding 30 June (roughly an 11-month lag). Projected next release (Year ended June 2026 data) is therefore expected around May 2027; exact day not yet published.

reports.title: National accounts (income, saving, assets, and liabilities)
reports.description: Stats NZ's quarterly institutional-sector accounts, including the net operating surplus series that the Treasury uses to uplift company tax estimates in the Financial Statements of the Government. Named in FSGNZ 2025 by its exact release URL rather than by title — the most specific Treasury-to-Stats-NZ citation found this session.

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ states this experimental series has been 'published on a quarterly basis since the first release for the March 2021 quarter.' There is no published release calendar with exact future dates for this specific series, but recent editions show a consistent lag of roughly 13 weeks (92-93 days) after quarter-end (slightly longer, ~107 days, for the September 2025 quarter release). Next edition should cover the June 2026 quarter and is projected for around early October 2026, extrapolated from this pattern.

reports.title: Local authority annual reports
reports.description: The audited annual report every local authority must adopt under Local Government Act 2002 s.98, containing the information required by Part 3 of Schedule 10 (including, per clause 29, audited financial statements, and per clause 30A the district's rating-unit count and total capital and land values). Held as a class node — the exact counterpart of Australia's `au-la-annual-statements` — because Stats NZ, the LGFA and MBIE all name the class rather than any one council's report. `nz-wellington-annual-report` is this slice's specific exemplar.
reports.cadence_note: One per local authority per financial year, adopted within four months of 30 June (LGA 2002 s.98(3)).

release_schedule.rule: Annual report adopted within 4 months of the end of the financial year (Local Government Act 2002 s.98(3)); financial year ends 30 June.
release_schedule.note: This report's own url field pointed to DLM172329 (a section about combining consultations), not the deadline provision — corrected to DLM172354 (s.98) as part of this audit.

reports.title: Wellington City Council Annual Report (Te Pūrongo ā-Tau)
reports.description: This slice's exemplar council annual report, Volume 2 (Financial Statements) of the 2024/25 report. Chosen over Auckland and Christchurch on availability grounds: Auckland Council's site returns HTTP 406 and Christchurch's HTTP 403 to every non-browser client tried, while wellington.govt.nz serves the PDF to plain curl. Its Statement of Compliance and its Note 1 together close the New Zealand accounting-standard chain from the council's own side — see the `nz-pbe-ipsas-1` edge, and contrast Brisbane's refusal to name AASB 1049 in `au-government-finance.json`.

entries.covers: Annual Report 2025/26 (year ended 30 June 2026) statutory adoption deadline

release_schedule.rule: Under the Local Government Act 2002 (s98(3)), a local authority's annual report must be completed and adopted, by resolution, within 4 months after the end of the financial year to which it relates. Wellington City Council's financial year ends 30 June, so the Annual Report is due by 31 October each year.
release_schedule.note: The 2024/25 Annual Report (year ended 30 June 2025) was adopted by Council on 8 October 2025, within the statutory 4-month window. The next edition (2025/26, year ended 30 June 2026) is due to be completed and adopted by 31 October 2026 under the same statutory rule; the exact council meeting date is not yet published.

reports.title: Wellington City Council rating valuations and rates
reports.description: Wellington City Council's own published account of how its rates are struck on rating values — the New Zealand counterpart to `au-georges-river-rates`. States that values are determined by Quotable Value on a three-yearly cycle, that the process is governed by the Rating Valuations Act 1998 and audited by the Office of the Valuer-General, and that the council sends building-consent details to QV between revaluations. NOTE: the page writes 'Rating Valuation Act 1998', dropping the 's' from the Act's actual short title 'Rating Valuations Act 1998' — quoted verbatim in the edge basis rather than silently corrected.
reports.cadence_note: Rates are set annually; the underlying rating valuation behind them is revised three-yearly (latest effective 1 September 2024, next 2027).

entries.covers: Next triennial rating revaluation (effective date inferred from the 3-year cycle and prior 1 September 2024 effective date; exact 2027 date not yet published)

release_schedule.rule: Rating valuations are conducted every 3 years; the current valuation (effective 1 September 2024) 'will be the basis for rates calculations until the next valuation in 2027, regardless of any change in the market.'
release_schedule.note: Rates themselves are set annually (each 1 July, e.g. current valuations used for rates from 1 July 2025), but the underlying rating valuation that rates are calculated from is only revised triennially. Corpus's releases_per_year=1 with existing cadence_note reflects this annual rates-setting cadence built on the triennial valuation base.

reports.title: District valuation roll (general revaluation)
reports.publisher: New Zealand territorial authorities; certified by the Valuer-General
reports.description: The roll of every rating unit in a territorial authority's district, prepared and maintained under Rating Valuations Act 1998 s.7 and revalued in full at intervals of not more than three years under s.9. The rating equivalent of the Netherlands' WOZ beschikking and NSW's Valuer-General land values. Its statutory gate is unusually hard: s.11(2) forbids assessing any rate on the proposed values until the Valuer-General has certified approval of the general revaluation.
reports.cadence_note: Three-yearly per territorial authority (RVA 1998 s.9(1)), staggered across the 66 territorial authorities, so several fall due nationally each year.

entries.covers: Ruapehu District and Mackenzie District general revaluation implementation
Waitaki District, Waikato, Kapiti Coast, Marlborough District, Rangitikei District general revaluation implementation
Kaipara District, Invercargill, Stratford District general revaluation implementation
Masterton and Tauranga general revaluation implementation
Timaru and Westland District general revaluation implementation
Tasman District, South Wairarapa, Carterton, Clutha District general revaluation implementation

release_schedule.note: New Zealand's district valuation roll general revaluation is not a single national event: each territorial authority (TA) revalues on its own three-yearly cycle (Rating Valuations Act 1998 / LINZ guidance: 'valuations occur at least every three years'), certified by the Valuer-General. QV (Quotable Value), which conducts most councils' revaluations, publishes a rolling implementation calendar showing which TAs are due next. The image 'Revaluation_Calendar_2026_V1.jpg' fetched from the QV schedule page on 2026-08-11 lists the current tranche of upcoming TA implementation dates, September 2026 through April 2027, soonest first. Entries below group TAs by implementation month exactly as published; only some of the ~67 TAs are shown (those in the currently-published near-term tranche).

reports.title: Rating Valuations Act 1998
reports.publisher: Parliamentary Counsel Office (administered by Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand)
reports.description: The Act creating the Valuer-General (s.3), setting the Valuer-General's standard-setting, monitoring and certification functions (s.4), empowering the Rating Valuations Rules (s.5), requiring each territorial authority to keep a district valuation roll (s.7), requiring three-yearly general revaluation (s.9) and forbidding rates to be assessed on uncertified values (s.11(2)). Structural counterpart of New South Wales' `au-vola1916`, minted on the same convention that a periodically reprinted statute is a node when downstream documents cite it by name.
reports.cadence_note: A consolidated statute, reprinted on amendment rather than published on a schedule; version read this session is 'as at 23 December 2023'.

release_schedule.note: This corpus entry is the statute text itself (Rating Valuations Act 1998) on legislation.govt.nz. The consolidated 'as at' version is only reprinted when an amending Act or regulation takes effect — there is no periodic publication calendar or stated rule for revising/reprinting the Act's text. The current consolidated version is 'as at 23 December 2023' (last amendment date), and next reprint depends on whenever Parliament next amends it — unpredictable. Note: the Act's own Section 9 ('General revaluation of rolls at 3-yearly intervals') states that territorial authorities must generally revalue rating valuation rolls every 3 years, but that rule governs the underlying property-valuation rolls process (administered locally, staggered by council per QV's rolling revaluation calendar), not the timing of updates to this Act's text — so it isn't a valid stated-rule for this specific report/URL.

reports.title: Rating Valuations Rules 2008 (LINZS30300)
reports.publisher: Office of the Valuer-General, Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand
reports.description: The Valuer-General's secondary legislation prescribing what the district valuation roll must contain, how sale details must be captured and coded, and the statistical rules a proposed revaluation must satisfy against market sales evidence (rule 5.5.1: coefficient of dispersion ≤ 12, median value price ratio 0.9–1.1, price related differential 0.98–1.03). Version date 1 October 2010; LINZ's own review page (fetched 2026-08) says replacement rules were expected to go to formal consultation in 2026, so this node's edition is likely to move.
reports.cadence_note: Amended rarely — Version 3.0 (2002), 3.1 (2003), 2008 issue, 31 March 2009 issue, 1 October 2010 issue. A review was under way as at July 2025.

release_schedule.note: LINZS30300 is secondary legislation (Rating Valuations Rules 2008) made under the Rating Valuations Act 1998, not a periodic statistical release. It was amended with a version dated 1 October 2010 (see https://www.linz.govt.nz/regulatory/30300). LINZ and the Valuer-General are currently conducting a phased review of the rules during 2025, intending to produce a draft for formal public consultation 'expected in 2026' (per https://www.linz.govt.nz/guidance/property-valuation/valuation-rules-guidelines-and-publications/rating-valuations-rules-review, last updated 2025-07-07). No specific consultation date, calendar, or fixed rule for future amendment cycles was found, so no computable 'next' date exists.

reports.title: XRB A1 Application of the Accounting Standards Framework
reports.description: The XRB standard that allocates every reporting entity to a tier and to a for-profit / public-benefit-entity track, and defines 'public sector PBE' by cross-reference to the Public Audit Act 2001. THE FINDING OF THIS SLICE LIVES HERE: XRB A1 never uses the words 'local authority' or 'Local Government Act' anywhere in its 43 pages (grep of the full extracted text, 0 hits) — like Australia's AASB 1049 and unlike the Netherlands' BBV or the UK's CIPFA Code, the standard does not name local government in its own scope.
reports.cadence_note: Issued 10 December 2015; compiled version read this session 'incorporates amendments to 31 March 2024'.

release_schedule.note: XRB A1 is an accounting standard, not a periodic statistical release. It is amended irregularly whenever the XRB conducts a targeted review or issues consequential amendments following changes to other standards (e.g. PBE IPSAS 50). Amendment history: issued Dec 2015; amended Oct 2017; May 2019; Feb 2020; Mar 2024 (PBE tier sizes); compiled to Feb 2025 (current version, effective for periods beginning on/after 1 Jan 2026); next compiled version through Jun 2026 effective 1 Jan 2027 (PBE IPSAS 50 consequential amendments). No fixed schedule or stated periodic-review rule with a computable next date was found.

reports.title: PBE IPSAS 1 Presentation of Financial Reports
reports.publisher: New Zealand Accounting Standards Board / External Reporting Board (XRB)
reports.description: The presentation standard for Tier 1 and Tier 2 public benefit entities, which is what New Zealand councils report under. Like XRB A1, it names no local authority: grep of its full 54 pages returns 0 hits for 'local authority', 'Local Government Act' and 'Public Audit Act'. The only local-government hook in its text is the word 'ratepayers' in the list of users of general purpose financial reports (para 3), which is not a scope binding. The binding is achieved instead by a statutory chain outside the standard — see the `nz-wellington-annual-report` edge.
reports.cadence_note: Issued September 2014; version read this session incorporates amendments to 31 January 2022 with further amendments effective 1 January 2026.

release_schedule.note: PBE IPSAS 1 is an accounting standard (not a periodic statistical report). XRB amends it irregularly via omnibus amendment packages as IPSASB updates the underlying international standard or NZ policy changes require it. Original issue November 2014; most recent substantive update is the October 2024 omnibus amendments (compiled to March 2025), effective for periods beginning 1 January 2026, with a prior amendment in May 2023 (audit fee disclosures). The XRB website states no fixed review cycle or forthcoming release date. The releases_per_year=0.2 figure on file (implying a ~5-year cadence) is not supported by any stated rule; amendment timing is genuinely irregular and driven by IPSASB/policy developments, not a fixed schedule.

reports.title: LGFA Annual Report
reports.publisher: New Zealand Local Government Funding Agency (LGFA)
reports.description: The annual report of the joint council-and-Crown-owned agency that raises debt on behalf of New Zealand councils — an institution with no direct Australian, Dutch or UK counterpart in this corpus. Names councils' own statutory planning documents as the material it monitors against its lending covenants. NEGATIVE FINDING recorded here: grep of the full 77-page 2025 report returns 0 hits for 'Statistics New Zealand', 'Stats NZ' and 'census' — LGFA's covenants are defined on accounting aggregates, not on any named statistical release.

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar or stated statutory deadline was found on LGFA's site. However, LGFA has released its 'Full Year Result and Annual Report' via NZX announcement in the last week of August each of the past three years (28 Aug 2023 for FY23, 29 Aug 2024 for FY24, and the FY25 report was 'authorized for issue' 28 Aug 2025), consistently ~8 weeks after its 30 June fiscal year end. The next (FY26) release is projected for late August 2026 based on this pattern; as of today (2026-08-11) it has not yet appeared.

reports.title: Funding Assistance Rates (FAR) Policy
reports.description: The policy that sets, once per three-year National Land Transport Programme, the share of each council's land transport programme the National Land Transport Fund co-invests. New Zealand's closest structural analog to the funding-formula technical annexes that anchored the Netherlands, UK, Ontario and Tasmania slices — and it is DELIBERATELY ISOLATED in this graph, because it names none of its four inputs to a titled source. See this slice's `_dropped` array for the verbatim negative. The isolation is the finding, on the convention `EU/G.47.md` established for `nordic-statistics-database` and `AU/G.1.md` reused for `au-brisbane-financial-statements`.
reports.cadence_note: Normal FARs are recalculated once per three-year NLTP cycle; the policy page itself is a living document (issued February 2021, last updated August 2023).

release_schedule.rule: FARs are reviewed every three years, before each NLTP.
release_schedule.note: NZTA states FARs are recalculated once per three-year NLTP cycle. The current NLTP (2024-27) runs 1 July 2024 - 30 June 2027; the next NLTP (2027-30) must be adopted by 31 August 2027 per NZTA's published NLTP timeline, so the corresponding FAR review/recalculation is expected before that date. No exact day is published for the FAR review itself.

reports.title: Accommodation Data Programme
reports.description: MBIE's monthly commercial-accommodation guest-night series, collected from accommodation providers and reported at territorial-authority level. Successor to the Stats NZ Accommodation Survey. Named by exact title in the Tourism Infrastructure Fund's assessment process as the source of the guest-night half of its eligibility ratio.

release_schedule.note: MBIE's Data Release Calendar (mbie.govt.nz/.../data-release-calendar, live-fetched, page 'last updated 03 July 2026') lists confirmed ADP release dates of 27 May 2026 (April 2026 data), 24 June 2026 (May 2026 data), and 29 July 2026 (June 2026 data) — all falling on the last Wednesday of the month, consistent with the programme's long-running (since 2020) monthly cadence of releasing roughly 4 weeks after month-end. Projected forward, the next release would be ~26 August 2026 (July 2026 data). Caveat: as of this check, the calendar page does NOT list any ADP entries for August through December 2026, even though it explicitly lists sibling monthly series (Tourism Volumes and Flows, Monthly Regional Tourism Estimates) through December 2026 — raising the possibility the programme's future beyond July 2026 is under review, paused, or simply not yet populated on the calendar. No explicit announcement of discontinuation, review, or schedule change was found via web search. Given 6+ years of unbroken monthly history and no confirming announcement of a change, this is reported as an observed-pattern (implied) rather than irregular, but the gap on the live calendar should be monitored.

reports.title: Tourism Electronic Card Transactions (TECTs)
reports.description: MBIE's monthly estimates of tourism spending derived from electronic card transaction data, published by territorial authority and region. Named by exact title and acronym in the Tourism Infrastructure Fund's assessment process as the source of the regional tourism-revenue eligibility test.

release_schedule.note: Tourism Electronic Card Transactions (TECTs) has been discontinued. It was an interim COVID-era measure (used roughly April 2020 to early 2023, with historical data available through 2024/2025) that has now been fully replaced by the resumed Monthly Regional Tourism Estimates (MRTEs) series. MBIE's own TEIC page states: 'The Monthly Regional Tourism Estimates (MRTEs) has resumed, and has replaced the Tourism Electronic Card Transactions (TECTs)' and 'No further updates or releases will be made moving forward.' MBIE's tourism-electronic-card-transactions reference page similarly says the series is 'Retained for reference only and not comparable with current tourism spending statistics.' There is therefore no future release to schedule for this report under its current name — ongoing monthly tourism spend statistics now continue under the MRTE report instead.

reports.title: Annual Report of the Controller and Auditor-General
reports.publisher: Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand (Office of the Auditor-General / The Audit Office)
reports.description: The Auditor-General's statutory annual report to the House of Representatives, required by section 37 of the Public Audit Act 2001. Minted 2026-08-06 to close the branch's highest-value single gap: the corpus held no node for the New Zealand Auditor-General's own recurring output, which is what blocked the Tokelau half of the export-of-institution finding. The report is where the office states, in its own words and every year, the extent of its mandate, including the two jurisdictions outside New Zealand it serves.
reports.cadence_note: Annual and statutory. Public Audit Act 2001 s 37(1): "As soon as practicable after the end of each financial year, the Auditor-General must prepare and present an annual report to the House of Representatives in accordance with section 43 of the Public Finance Act 1989." s 37(2) requires it to include "an account of the implementation of the annual plan required under section 36" and "a list of entities audited by the Auditor-General under an arrangement in accordance with section 19". The 2024/25 edition is 108 pages.

entries.covers: 2022/23 Annual Report presented to House of Representatives

release_schedule.note: Public Audit Act 2001 s37(1) only requires the report 'as soon as practicable after the end of each financial year' (NZ financial year ends 30 June) — this rule has no fixed/computable date, so it cannot support a stated-rule entry. In practice, actual presentation/publication dates cluster in late September to mid-October each year: 2022/23 report presented to the House 26 Sep 2023; 2023/24 report signed 30 Sep 2024; 2024/25 report published 14 Oct 2025. The 2025/26 report (covering FY ending 30 June 2026) is projected for the same Sep-Oct 2026 window based on this pattern.

reports.title: Public Audit Act 2001
reports.publisher: Parliamentary Counsel Office (administered by the Office of the Auditor-General)
reports.description: The statute that constitutes the Auditor-General, defines 'public entity', and requires the annual plan (s 36) and the annual report (s 37). Minted 2026-08-06 because it was already load-bearing in this corpus without a node: XRB A1 defines 'public sector PBE' by cross-reference to it, Wellington City Council self-classifies under it, and the Tokelau audit mandate turns on it. Schedule 2, 'Specific public entities not falling within any class' (s 5(1)(d)), lists "Tokelau Administration" by name. A full-text search of the current consolidation returns one occurrence of 'Tokelau' and zero of 'Niue' — which is the sharpest single piece of evidence for the export-of-institution finding, because it shows New Zealand statute reaching into Tokelau and being silent on Niue, whose Constitution instead reaches out.
reports.cadence_note: A consolidated statute, reprinted on amendment rather than published on a schedule. Version read 2026-08-06 is the current consolidation on legislation.govt.nz, which carries amendments through the Taranaki Maunga Collective Redress Act 2025 in Schedule 2.

release_schedule.note: This is a piece of primary legislation (Public Audit Act 2001, No 10), not a periodic statistical release. The New Zealand Legislation site republishes it as an updated 'reprint' each time an amending Act or regulation changes its text, e.g. as at 23 December 2023, 30 June 2024, 01 October 2024, 27 October 2024, 27 August 2025, and 01 January 2026. These reprint dates are driven by unpredictable parliamentary amendment activity, not by any calendar or stated periodic-review rule, and show no consistent time-of-year pattern.

reports.title: Public Finance Act 1989
reports.publisher: Parliamentary Counsel Office (administered by The Treasury)
reports.description: The statute governing the use of Crown financial resources. Minted 2026-08-07 on Thomas's decision (planning/Decisions-2026-08-07.docx, option A: mint on arrival, and the minting session adds every edge it can verify with a direct quote in the same session, no cap, nothing minted on inference), closing a lead three prior sessions had deferred as 'probably the right next statute to mint' (NZ/G.4.md, following the Tokelau/Public Audit Act 2001 work). s 1A(1): "The purpose of this Act is to consolidate and amend the law governing the use of public financial resources." Requires the Treasury to prepare the annual consolidated Financial Statements of the Government (s 27) and the twice-yearly economic and fiscal updates (s 26O). Also supplies the other half of a bidirectional statutory cross-reference with the Public Audit Act 2001: s 2(1), "Office of Parliament means the Parliamentary Commissioner for the Environment (and that Commissioner's office), the Office of Ombudsmen, and the Auditor-General" -- naming the Auditor-General as one of only three Offices of Parliament this Act recognises -- and s 2(1) again, "Auditor-General has the meaning given to it by section 4 of the Public Audit Act 2001." Each Act defines a term the other Act's own scope provisions rely on.
reports.cadence_note: A consolidated statute, reprinted on amendment rather than published on a schedule. Version read this session (2026-08-07) is 'Latest version as at 01 July 2026', carrying amendments through the Public Finance Amendment Act 2026 (2026 No 9).

release_schedule.note: This is the Public Finance Act 1989 itself (NZ primary legislation), not a periodic statistical report. The legislation.govt.nz page is a consolidated 'reprint' that is updated only when Parliament passes an amending Act into force (currently shown 'as at 13 November 2025'). There is no published release calendar and no statutory rule specifying when the next amendment/update will occur — changes depend entirely on the parliamentary legislative agenda, so the update cadence is genuinely irregular.

reports.title: Local Government (Auckland Council) Act 2009
reports.publisher: Parliamentary Counsel Office (administered by the Department of Internal Affairs)
reports.description: The statute that amalgamated Auckland's eight prior local authorities into a single unitary authority -- the corpus's first documented instance of the 'second exemplar council' pass (NZ/G.4.md priority 2) turning up a genuinely different statutory layer rather than confirming the Wellington shape. s 3 (Purpose): "The purpose of this Act is-- (a) to establish the Auckland Council as a unitary authority for Auckland; and (b) to set out the matters in relation to the Council's structure and functions, duties, and powers that differ from the general provisions applying to local authorities under the Local Government Act 2002 and certain other enactments; ... and (g) to set out requirements relating to substantive council-controlled organisations." s 4(1) defines 'substantive council-controlled organisation' -- 'means a council-controlled organisation that is either wholly owned or wholly controlled by the Council and either-- (i) is responsible for the delivery of a significant service or activity on behalf of the Council; or (ii) owns or manages assets with a value of more than $10 million' -- and 'Auckland water organisation means Watercare Services Limited, and includes any subsidiary of Watercare Services Limited'. Minted 2026-08-07, found via Auckland Council's own Volume 3 financial statements naming it as one of three governing statutes.
reports.cadence_note: A consolidated statute, reprinted on amendment rather than published on a schedule. Version read this session is 'Latest version as at 06 June 2026', which includes s 57A, inserted 1 July 2025 by the Local Government (Water Services Preliminary Arrangements) Act 2024 -- an active amendment stream, not a settled text.

release_schedule.note: This is an Act of the New Zealand Parliament (the constitutional/foundational statute establishing Auckland Council), administered online by the Parliamentary Counsel Office, not a recurring statistical or periodic publication. The PCO's legislation.govt.nz version is updated (reprinted) only when Parliament passes amending legislation affecting it, which happens irregularly and unpredictably as needed — there is no calendar, no stated periodic-release rule, and no consistent yearly pattern. A releases_per_year value of 1 does not reflect how this kind of instrument works; it likely should not be treated as having a fixed release cadence at all. (Attempted to re-verify directly against legislation.govt.nz during this session but the site returned a 403 error to automated fetch; classification is based on the well-documented nature of this report as a NZ Act of Parliament rather than a periodic release.)

reports.title: Auckland Council Annual Report (Volume 3 – Financial Statements)
reports.description: This slice's second exemplar council annual report (NZ/G.4.md priority 2), chosen because it is New Zealand's only unitary 'super city' authority and carries a substantial council-controlled-organisation structure Wellington does not. STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE FROM WELLINGTON, itself a finding: Auckland's annual report ships in four volumes -- Volume 1 (Overview and Service Performance), Volumes 2.1-2.21 (one per local board), Volume 3 (Financial Statements, the volume this node's edges are drawn from), and Volume 4 (Climate Statement) -- rather than Wellington's single consolidated document. Basis of preparation: "The financial statements have been prepared: in accordance with New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP), the LGA 2002, the LGACA 2009 and the Local Government (Financial Reporting and Prudence) Regulations 2014 and comply with PBE Accounting Standards." "Auckland Council is a local authority domiciled in New Zealand and governed by the following legislation: Local Government Act 2002 (LGA 2002); Local Government (Auckland Council) Act 2009 (LGACA 2009); and Local Government (Rating) Act 2002." "the council has designated itself and the group as public benefit entities (PBEs) and applies New Zealand Tier 1 PBE Accounting Standards."

entries.covers: Annual Report 2025/2026 (year ended 30 June 2026), including Volume 3 - Financial Statements

release_schedule.rule: Section 98(3) of the Local Government Act 2002: each annual report (which contains the audited financial statements, including Volume 3) must be completed and adopted by resolution within four months after the end of the financial year that it relates to. Auckland Council's financial year ends 30 June, so the statutory deadline is 31 October.
release_schedule.note: In practice Auckland Council has adopted/published recent Annual Reports somewhat ahead of the statutory deadline: the 2023/2024 report was before the Governing Body around 26 September 2024, and the 2024/2025 report was published/announced around 25 September 2025 (OurAuckland article dated September 2025). The statutory backstop under LGA 2002 s98(3) is 31 October (4 months after the 30 June financial year end); actual adoption has recently occurred in late September.

reports.title: Auditor-General's Observations on Councils' Long-Term Plans
reports.publisher: Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand (Office of the Auditor-General / The Audit Office)
reports.description: The Auditor-General's recurring report on the audits of councils' three-yearly long-term plans (LTPs), published once per LTP cycle rather than annually. Minted 2026-08-08, closing part of the lead recorded against Watercare and the LGFA edge below. Title varies release to release: the 2022 edition, on the 2021-31 LTPs, was titled 'Matters arising from our audits of the 2021-31 long-term plans'; the 2025 edition, on the 2024-34 LTPs, was retitled 'Observations from our audits of councils' 2024-34 long-term plans' — 'This report describes the audit results and trends from the 58 long-term plans that councils adopted between June and October 2024.' Both editions independently confirmed live this session at the office's current domain (ao.parliament.nz, which oag.parliament.nz now redirects to — the HTTP 403 a prior session hit was against the retired domain, not a live block).
reports.cadence_note: Once per statutory three-year LTP cycle (Local Government Act 2002 ss 93, 93A). Observed record: 2022 edition (2021-31 LTPs) and 2025 edition (2024-34 LTPs), roughly 2.6 years apart in publication date, consistent with a 3-year LTP cycle plus a variable post-adoption audit lag.

entries.covers: Matters arising from audits of the 2021-31 long-term plans
Observations from audits of councils' 2024-34 long-term plans
Projected Auditor-General's Observations on councils' 2027-37 long-term plans

release_schedule.note: OAG has published LTP audit observations reports at roughly 3-year intervals tied to the statutory LTP cycle, with publication dates ranging from December of the adoption year up to July of the following year (Dec 2012, Dec 2015, Feb 2019, Jul 2022, Feb 2025). No fixed calendar date or stated statutory deadline for the observations report itself exists (only councils' LTP adoption deadline is statutory). The next LTP cycle covers 2027-37 (councils adopt LTPs by ~30 June 2027 per LGA s93), so the next observations report is projected between roughly mid-2027 and mid-2028 based on the historical lag pattern; exact date not yet published.

reports.title: Local Government Act 2002
reports.publisher: Parliamentary Counsel Office (administered by the Department of Internal Affairs)
reports.description: The general statute governing New Zealand's territorial and regional local authorities -- the statutory floor every council-level node in this slice sits on, cited well over a hundred times inside nz-lgaca-2009 alone. Minted 2026-08-08 on Thomas's ruling (Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx Q3, 'mint and follow precedent'), on the same logic as the Public Finance Act 1989 mint (NZ/G.5.md): every edge this session could verify with an already-extracted direct quote, no cap. s 98 requires every local authority to prepare an annual report; Schedule 10 Part 3 sets its required content, including audited financial statements (clause 29) and the district's rating-unit count and total capital and land values (clause 30A). s 111 requires that information under Schedule 10 'be prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting practice', and s 5 defines that term 'the same meaning as in section 8 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013' -- a chain independently VERIFIED DIRECTLY against a FAOLEX mirror of the PCO reprint in an earlier session, preserved in this file's own _dropped block on the XRB A1 / PBE IPSAS 1 entry. NOT DONE THIS SESSION, flagged rather than assumed complete: a full direct read of the Act's own cross-reference structure (s 5 interpretations, in both directions) parallel to what produced the Public Finance Act 1989's reverse edge into the Public Audit Act 2001 -- legislation.govt.nz's plain-text extractor returns nothing for this site (NZ/G.4.md, reconfirmed this session) and a browser session was not available this turn. This mint rests on quotes already extracted, first-hand, by documents that cite the Act -- not on a fresh read of the Act itself.
reports.cadence_note: A consolidated statute, reprinted on amendment rather than published on a schedule, same convention as this slice's other Acts (nz-public-finance-act-1989, nz-public-audit-act-2001, nz-lgaca-2009). Version not re-confirmed this session; the standard 'latest version' URL is used.

release_schedule.note: The Local Government Act 2002 is a New Zealand statute maintained on legislation.govt.nz as a consolidated 'as at' version (currently 'as at 15 January 2026'). It is updated only when Parliament passes amendment Acts (e.g. Local Government Act 2002 Amendment Act 2019, Local Government (Electoral Legislation and Māori Wards and Māori Constituencies) Amendment Act 2024) that come into force, which happens on no fixed schedule. There is no published release calendar, no stated periodic-update rule, and no consistent yearly pattern -- amendments are driven by the parliamentary legislative agenda, so this is genuinely irregular rather than a periodic release.

dependencies.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (Local Government (Rating) Act 2002, version as at 27 November 2025, read from the Parliamentary Counsel Office's own PDF replayed byte-for-byte through the Wayback `id_` endpoint because legislation.govt.nz's WAF returns HTTP 202 with zero bytes to non-browser clients; pypdf-extracted, 129 pages). The chain is entirely in statute, in four hops. s.13(3): "For the purposes of this section, the rateable value of the land— (a) must be— (i) the annual value of the land; or (ii) the capital value of the land; or (iii) the land value of the land; and (b) must be identified in the local authority's funding impact statement as the value for setting a general rate." s.5 pins each of those three to the other Act: "capital value has the meaning set out in section 2(1) of the Rating Valuations Act 1998" (identically for annual value and land value). s.27(4): "The database must include, in relation to each rating unit within the local authority's district,— (a) all information that relates to the unit that is included in the district valuation roll for the district". s.5 again: "district valuation roll means,— (a) in relation to a territorial authority, a roll prepared for a district under section 7 of the Rating Valuations Act 1998 and approved under section 11 of that Act". This is New Zealand's exact counterpart to NSW Local Government Act 1993 s.498's cross-Act citation of the Valuation of Land Act 1916.

dependencies.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (both documents read this session — RVA 1998 as above; Rating Valuations Rules 2008 LINZS30300 version date 1 October 2010, the official linz.govt.nz PDF replayed through Wayback `id_`, pypdf-extracted, 79 pages). RVA s.7(1) requires the roll to be maintained "in accordance with rules made under this Act" and s.7(2) that "Each roll must contain the information in respect of each rating unit within the district that is required by the rules"; s.9(3) requires each general revaluation to "comply with rules made by the Valuer-General for the purpose". The Rules then set the content (rule 2.1), the sale-detail capture (rule 4.4.2: "The territorial authority must enter sale details in the DVR supporting information, as set out in rule 2.2, within 15 working days of receiving the necessary documentation") and the acceptance test (rule 5.5.1: "Where capital values or only land values are assessed, the proposed values, when compared to the market sales evidence, must satisfy the following statistical rules where appropriate: (a) coefficient of dispersion, which must be equal to or less than 12, (b) median value price ratio, which must be within the range 0.9 to 1.1, (c) price related differential which must be within the range 0.98 and 1.03, and (d) comparison of average value changes between sold and unsold properties, which must be equal to or less than 5 %.").

dependencies.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (same PDF and fetch as above, this session). Reporting entity: "Auckland Council is a local authority domiciled in New Zealand and governed by the following legislation: Local Government Act 2002 (LGA 2002); Local Government (Auckland Council) Act 2009 (LGACA 2009); and Local Government (Rating) Act 2002." Basis of preparation: "The financial statements have been prepared: in accordance with New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP), the LGA 2002, the LGACA 2009 and the Local Government (Financial Reporting and Prudence) Regulations 2014 and comply with PBE Accounting Standards." The Act shapes the accounts substantively, not just nominally -- footnoted directly against the group's own consolidation and debt disclosures: "Section 4(1) of the LGACA 2009 defines substantive CCOs as a CCO that is either wholly owned or wholly controlled by Auckland Council and either is responsible for the delivery of a significant service or activity on behalf of Auckland Council or owns or manages assets with a value of more than $10 million," and "Pursuant to section 57A of the LGACA 2009, the Auckland water organisation must repay all outstanding debt owed to the council." Both provisions independently confirmed against the Act's own text this session (legislation.govt.nz, DOM extraction against div.prov): s 4(1) 'substantive council-controlled organisation' matches word for word; s 57A 'Auckland water organisation must repay debt to Auckland Council' matches, and its own amendment note shows it was "inserted, on 1 July 2025, by section 110 of the Local Government (Water Services Preliminary Arrangements) Act 2024 (2024 No 31)" -- a live legislative change during the reporting year, not settled background law.

The class node's own defining statute. LGA 2002 s.98 requires every local authority to prepare an annual report; Schedule 10 Part 3 sets its required content -- clause 29 requires audited financial statements, clause 30A requires 'the number of rating units within the district or region of the local authority at the end of the preceding financial year' and total capital and land values. Already the basis for this node's own description before nz-lga-2002 existed as a node to point at.

Wellington's own Statement of Compliance: "Wellington City Council's Governing Body and management team confirm they have complied with all of the statutory requirements in relation to the Annual Report, as outlined in Schedule 10 of the Local Government Act 2002 (LGA 2002), including the requirement to comply with New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP)..." Distinct from the existing nz-wellington-annual-report -> nz-pbe-ipsas-1 edge (which is about which accounting standard applies) and the existing nz-wellington-annual-report -> nz-public-audit-act-2001 edge (which is about audit arrangement and self-classification) -- this edge is about the annual report's own required content and structure, Schedule 10 specifically.

Auckland's own Basis of preparation: "The financial statements have been prepared: in accordance with New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP), the LGA 2002, the LGACA 2009 and the Local Government (Financial Reporting and Prudence) Regulations 2014 and comply with PBE Accounting Standards." Same reporting-entity clause already carries the existing nz-auckland-annual-report -> nz-lgaca-2009 edge; this is the parallel edge into the general Act named in the same sentence.

LGACA 2009 s 3(b) defines its own purpose relative to the general Act: "to set out the matters in relation to the Council's structure and functions, duties, and powers that differ from the general provisions applying to local authorities under the Local Government Act 2002 and certain other enactments." LGACA 2009 is structured as a set of departures from LGA 2002's baseline, not a free-standing statute -- the same shape of dependency as an amending regulation on its parent Act. Closes the lead this file's own _dropped block opened on 2026-08-08 and left unminted pending this decision.

_dropped.why: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (the official NZTA page replayed through Wayback `id_` raw bytes after nzta.govt.nz returned HTTP 403 to direct curl). This is the New Zealand equivalent of the document that carried the Netherlands, UK, Ontario and Tasmania slices — a national formula deciding how much central money each council gets — and it names none of its inputs to a titled release. Verbatim, the whole of its "Inputs" section: "Inputs for each approved organisation are: centreline kilometres, which provide a measure of the length of the road network to be maintained and services to be available to all transport users / capital value, which is used by most local authorities to set rates, and provides a measure of the asset base from which local authorities raise their local share / inverse of rating units, which identifies local authorities that have the smallest number of ratepayers from which to source their local share / index of deprivation, a demographic index published by the University of Otago and used by the Ministry of Health, which provides a measure of the relative wealth of communities / total cost of all activities for a recent period, which is the actual total costs incurred by approved organisations for the last 3 to 5 years." And "Setting normal FARs": "A year before the start of each NLTP, we recalculate the normal FAR for each approved organisation by inputting the latest available information. The changes in FARs, if any, will reflect movements in centreline kilometres, capital values, rating units and the index of deprivation." Two publishers are named for the deprivation index and no title; the other three inputs are sourced anonymously, even though 'capital value' and 'rating units' are exactly the figures LGA 2002 Schedule 10 clause 30A makes councils publish. `nz-nzta-far-policy` is therefore minted and left isolated, on the `au-brisbane-financial-statements` convention — the absence is the result.

_dropped.why: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (both standards downloaded from xrb.govt.nz with plain curl and pypdf-extracted in full, then grepped). LGACA 2009 s 4(1): "Auckland water organisation means Watercare Services Limited, and includes any subsidiary of Watercare Services Limited." s 56A(1): the Council "has no right, title, or interest (legal or equitable) in the assets, security, debts, or liabilities of an Auckland water organisation" and "must not receive any equity return, directly or indirectly, from an Auckland water organisation." s 57A, inserted 1 July 2025 by the Local Government (Water Services Preliminary Arrangements) Act 2024 (2024 No 31): the water organisation "must repay" its existing debt to the Council "no later than the close of the day that is 5 years after this section comes into force." Strong candidate for a dedicated session -- New Zealand's water-sector reform is itself a live story (the Local Government (Water Services Preliminary Arrangements) Act 2024 is only just over a year old and s 57A/57B are self-repealing five years after commencement).

reports.title: Gross domestic product (quarterly)
reports.description: Stats NZ's quarterly GDP information release, New Zealand's official measure of economic activity, compiled per the 'Quarterly gross domestic product: Sources and methods' (fifth edition). The quarterly series is benchmarked annually to annual accounts whose industry data comes largely from the Annual Enterprise Survey: the sources-and-methods document states that new annual data is incorporated once a year at the September-quarter release. Minted as the corpus's representative of the 'national accounts' family the AES metadata names as its principal consumer; the legacy product titles that metadata lists (Production/Industry Accounts, Institutional Sector Accounts, Inter-Industry Study, Provisional National Accounts) are predecessors of the current GDP and national-accounts release set.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly, roughly 11 weeks after the reference quarter. Annual benchmark data is incorporated once a year: "The new annual data is incorporated into the quarterly accounts once a year for the September quarter information release, published in December."

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ's release calendar (filter by month = September 2026) lists '17 Sep Gross domestic product: June 2026 quarter'. This is consistent with the on-file cadence_note (quarterly, ~11 weeks after reference quarter end). The most recently published edition was the March 2026 quarter, released 18 June 2026.

reports.title: Regional gross domestic product
reports.description: Stats NZ's annual geographic breakdown of national GDP by region and industry, published for years ended March. Its own introduction page states, in one sentence, all four of its main inputs by name: the Annual Enterprise Survey, Linked Employer-Employee Data, the Crown Financial Information System, and the Local Authority Census — two of which are already nodes in this corpus, making this the most efficiently documented node in the New Zealand slice.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, for years ended March; editions verified for 2016, 2018, 2022 and 2024.

Its DataInfo+ metadata describes it as providing "a picture of the role tourism plays in New Zealand, with information on the changing levels and impact of tourism activity", published annually. Its published methodology derives industry output and scales household tourism expenditure using Annual Enterprise Survey data, which is the edge that brought it into this corpus.

reports.description: Stats NZ's periodic satellite account of the non-profit sector's contribution to GDP, supplementing the New Zealand System of National Accounts. Three editions exist — for the 2004 year (published 2007), 2013 and 2018 — which the 2018 edition itself confirms: "the NPISA, first published in 2007 and presenting statistics for the 2004 year". release_schedule.note: Stats NZ's Non-profit institutions satellite account (NPISA) page (2018 edition, published 2020-03-27) has no 'next release' date, no related release-calendar entry, and no stated periodicity rule anywhere in the page's structured content. Only three editions have ever been published (2004, 2013, 2018), each covering the NZ System of National Accounts year roughly 5-9 years apart. reports.title: Business price indexes
reports.description: Stats NZ's quarterly producer-side price release. Its DataInfo+ metadata states: "The BPI release includes the PPI, CGPI, and farm expenses price index (FEPI)." The PPI measures output and input price change for industries, the CGPI capital goods prices. Named by exact title in the AES's own metadata as a consumer of AES data, but no product-side document reachable this session corroborates that (see _dropped); the node instead anchors a documented inbound edge from the quarterly GDP release, whose sources-and-methods uses PPI sub-indexes for inventory revaluation.

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ does not publish a long-range dated calendar reachable via automated fetch (release-calendar page is JS-rendered), and no explicit 'next release' statement was found on individual release pages via fetch. However, past editions show a very consistent quarterly pattern: released on/around the 18th-20th of the second month after quarter-end -- March 2025 quarter released 19 May 2025; June 2025 quarter released ~19 Aug 2025; September 2025 quarter released 19-20 Nov 2025; December 2025 quarter released 18-19 Feb 2026; March 2026 quarter released 19 May 2026. Projecting forward, the June 2026 quarter release is expected around 19 August 2026 and the September 2026 quarter release around 19 November 2026.

reports.title: New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification (NZSIOC)
reports.description: The New Zealand-only output classification layered on top of ANZSIC 2006, and the level at which Stats NZ actually designs its business surveys and compiles the national accounts -- "NZSIOC is an output view of the ANZSIC classification designed for the production of aggregated industry statistics" (Stats NZ to the UN Committee of Experts on ISIC, 2022). Four hierarchical levels: Level 1, "16 categories at this level. They match with the ANZSIC division level, except for three categories which combine two divisions together"; Level 2, "31 categories at this level which generally match with the ANZSIC division level, except that agriculture and manufacturing are split"; Level 3, "55 categories at this level. This level generally matches an ANZSIC subdivision or consists of several smaller subdivisions combined together"; Level 4, "118 working industries" where the National Accounts are compiled. Stats NZ built it because ANZSIC 2006's structure "does not always mirror the New Zealand economy" -- specifically, "because of the significance of agriculture and its downstream industries, users require more information about agriculture and primary food product manufacturing than what is provided at the ANZSIC group level". TITLE VARIANT, on file so it is not rediscovered: Stats NZ's own 2010 implementation paper expands the acronym as "New Zealand Standard Industry Output Categories", while its 2022 and 2025 papers to UN classification bodies and the Annual Enterprise Survey's DataInfo+ metadata use "New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification". The later and more widely used form is taken as the title here. MINTED 2026-08-09 on Thomas's ruling, after a cheap-check pass established that NZSIOC has no defining publication of its own -- no edition, no catalogue number, no version -- and is distributed as downloadable classification tables. Three Stats NZ-authored sources describe it and none names a founding instrument; Stats NZ's 2022 UN paper says outright that NZSIOC "was created as an afterthought" whose "purpose and/or need was not actually considered during the ANZSIC06 review". The ruling was that `Research.1.md` sec.4's bar is named + titled, which NZSIOC meets, and that the volumes `anzsic` and `isic` happen to have were never a requirement.
reports.cadence_note: Evergreen; `releases_per_year` deliberately absent, per sec.4's one-off foundational-instrument shape and the precedent of `eu-reg-2016-2304`. There is no observed revision interval to derive a rate from: NZSIOC has no published edition sequence at all. Forward-looking caveat from Stats NZ's 2025 ECLAC workshop paper -- "There has been no review of ANZSIC since the commencement of the revision in 2006 and it is heavily out of date and difficult to use", and New Zealand is "contemplating adopting ISIC Rev 5 either as is or with a few minor class adjustments" -- so NZSIOC's parent may be replaced rather than revised, which would force a decision about this node rather than a routine update.

They match with the ANZSIC division level, except for three categories which combine two divisions together"; Level 2 "31 categories at this level which generally match with the ANZSIC division level, except that agriculture and manufacturing are split"; Level 3 "55 categories at this level. This level generally matches an ANZSIC subdivision or consists of several smaller subdivisions combined together"; Level 4 "118 working industries" where the National Accounts are compiled. (c) Stats NZ's own paper to the 2022 UN Committee of Experts on ISIC (UNCEISC 2022, Session 3c, 'New Zealand ANZSIC-ISIC Issues', unstats.un.org, fetched this session): "NZSIOC is an output view of the ANZSIC classification designed for the production of aggregated industry statistics", and "Stats NZ uses the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial 2006 (ANZSIC06) as the framework...supplemented through the use of the New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification (NZSIOC)" -- and, notably against the existence of any founding instrument, that NZSIOC "was created as an afterthought" whose "purpose and/or need was not actually considered during the ANZSIC06 review". NONE of the three names a defining publication, an edition, a catalogue number or a version for NZSIOC; all three describe it as a set of categories Stats NZ publishes as downloadable classification tables (Excel) alongside the releases that use it. The working conclusion is that NZSIOC has no front matter to read, rather than that this session failed to find it -- which converts the blocker from access to a node-rule question. That question is Thomas's and is flagged for him rather than decided here: does a classification with a title, a documented derivation and a documented structure, but no defining publication of its own, qualify under `Research.1.md` sec.4 on the same footing as `anzsic` (catalogue no. 1292.0, signed Preface) and `isic` (numbered revisions), both of which do have volumes? Left `deferred` pending that ruling rather than minted, per sec.3. Second, a naming discrepancy worth not rediscovering: Stats NZ's own 2010 implementation paper expands NZSIOC as 'New Zealand Standard Industry Output Categories', while its 2022 and 2025 UN papers and the AES DataInfo+ item expand it as 'New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification'. Both expansions are Stats NZ's own usage; if the node is minted, the title field needs a decision on which is current. Third, forward-looking and relevant to cadence if it is minted: Stats NZ's 2025 ECLAC workshop paper states "There has been no review of ANZSIC since the commencement of the revision in 2006 and it is heavily out of date and difficult to use" and that New Zealand is "contemplating adopting ISIC Rev 5 either as is or with a few minor class adjustments" -- so NZSIOC's parent may be replaced rather than revised, and NZSIOC itself has no observed revision interval to derive a `releases_per_year` from. ORIGINAL ENTRY BELOW. NZ/G.4.md cheap check 4, attempted and blocked by access, not by evidence. The NZSIOC DataInfo+ item (nz.govt.stats/0381a627-927b-4d60-bce3-bba549bf5a2d) was located but datainfoplus.stats.govt.nz, after serving three items early in this session, began returning robots-disallowed for every URL in both /Item/ and /item/ casings, including robots.txt itself; the data.govt.nz catalogue mirror is behind Incapsula. G.4's 'DataInfo+ is fetchable' should be read as 'intermittently fetchable'. What was obtained instead, from Stats NZ's own presentation to the 2025 UN ECLAC classifications workshop (Andrew Hancock, 'Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC)', unstats.un.org, fetched this session): ANZSIC "Is supported by an output classification (NZSIOC) and forms the basis of the Business Industry Classification (BIC)"; "In the New Zealand context it has become a minor input classification as NZSIOC is used for sample survey design and all outputs"; "In addition to assist implementation, a separate New Zealand Standard Industrial Output Classification (NZSIOC) was created for all aggregated data such as working or published industries of the National Accounts". That supports the NZSIOC-on-ANZSIC relationship but is a one-off conference paper, not the classification's defining document, and the branch rule since 2026-08-06 is that the corpus should not carry a node whose front matter nobody has read. One successful fetch of the DataInfo+ item closes this.

reports.title: Ontario Budget
reports.description: Annual provincial budget document presenting the government's economic outlook, fiscal plan, revenue and expense projections, borrowing program, and policy measures. Includes the multi-year path to balance, net debt-to-GDP projections, and detailed fiscal tables. Most recent: 2026 Ontario Budget: A Plan to Protect Ontario (tabled March 2026). Supplemented intra-year by First Quarter Finances and other quarterly updates.
reports.cadence_note: Annual (typically spring); supplemented by Fall Economic Outlook and Fiscal Review and quarterly finances updates

reports.title: Public Accounts of Ontario
reports.publisher: Treasury Board Secretariat / Ontario Ministry of Finance (audited by Auditor General of Ontario)
reports.description: Annual audited consolidated financial statements of the Province of Ontario for the fiscal year ended 31 March, including the Annual Report, Consolidated Financial Statements, Ministry Statements and Schedules, and Detailed Schedules of Payments. Prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards and compared against the Budget plan.
reports.cadence_note: Annual (within 180 days of fiscal year-end)

reports.title: Ontario Financing Authority
reports.publisher: Ontario Financing Authority (agency of the Province of Ontario)
reports.description: Crown agency that conducts borrowing, investment and financial risk management for the Province, manages the provincial debt, and executes the long-term public borrowing program set out in the Ontario Budget. Publishes annual reports, financial statements, borrowing program status, and investor presentations. Directly implements the funding requirements and debt-management strategy of the Budget.
reports.cadence_note: Continuous operational reporting; Annual Report and financial statements yearly

reports.title: Financial Accountability Office of Ontario
reports.publisher: Financial Accountability Office of Ontario (independent officer of the Legislative Assembly)
reports.description: Independent office established by the Financial Accountability Officer Act, 2013. Provides non-partisan analysis to the Legislative Assembly on the state of the Province’s finances (including the Budget), trends in the provincial and national economies, expenditure estimates, and the financial costs/benefits of public bills or proposals. Issues Budget Notes, Economic and Budget Outlook reports, and annual reports.
reports.cadence_note: Multiple reports per year; Annual Report

reports.title: City of Toronto Operating and Capital Budget
reports.description: Annual tax- and rate-supported operating budget and multi-year capital budget and plan adopted by City Council (Mayor's proposed budget under City of Toronto Act). Includes property-tax levy requirements, service-area allocations, and 10-year capital plan. Most recent: 2026 Operating Budget ($18.9 billion) and 2026–2035 Capital Budget and Plan ($63.1 billion).
reports.cadence_note: Annual (adopted February)

reports.title: City of Toronto Consolidated Financial Statements / Annual Financial Report
reports.publisher: City of Toronto (Finance & Treasury; audited by external auditor)
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements (including sinking funds and trust funds) prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards (PSAB). Accompanied by the Annual Financial Report providing narrative and statistical context. Most recent complete: 2024 statements approved 2025; 2025 draft statements available 2026.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of Toronto Tax Levy By-law
reports.description: Annual by-law enacted under the City of Toronto Act setting the municipal tax ratios, general local municipal levy, additional rates for budgetary increase and City Building Fund, and resulting tax rates by property class. Generates the property-tax revenue authorized by the adopted budget. Example: By-law 133-2026 (Tax Levy By-law for 2026).
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of Toronto Long-Term Financial Plan
reports.description: Multi-year framework for longer-term financial decision-making, strategies and key actions to support integrated, strategic budgeting. Updated Long-Term Financial Plan adopted September 2023; subsequent status updates appear in annual budget processes and Annual Financial Reports. Provides the roadmap that informs the annual Operating and Capital Budgets.
reports.cadence_note: Periodic major updates (most recent 2023) with annual status reporting

reports.title: City of Ottawa Operating and Capital Budget
reports.description: Annual tax- and rate-supported operating budget and capital budget adopted by Council under the Municipal Act. Must be balanced. Includes property-tax levy, transit levy, water/sewer rates, and multi-year capital authority. Example: 2025 Adopted Budget; 2026 draft presented late 2025.
reports.cadence_note: Annual (typically adopted December)

reports.title: City of Ottawa Consolidated Financial Statements / Annual Report
reports.publisher: City of Ottawa (Finance and Corporate Services; audited by external auditor)
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards (PSAB) as required by the Municipal Act, accompanied by the Annual Report containing financial statement discussion and analysis and statistical schedules. Most recent: 2024 Annual Report (released 2025); 2025 statements presented 2026.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of Ottawa Tax Policy and Annual Tax Rate Bylaws
reports.description: Council-approved tax ratios by property class and subclass, together with the annual bylaws that establish municipal tax rates based on the adopted budget levy requirement and MPAC assessment. Equivalent function to Toronto’s Tax Levy By-law. Includes small-business subclass, multi-residential ratio path, and capping/clawback parameters.
reports.cadence_note: Annual (ratios and rates set each year)

reports.title: Ontario Education Tax Rates (O. Reg. 400/98 as amended)
reports.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Finance (Minister of Finance)
reports.description: Annual regulation under the Education Act prescribing the tax rates for school purposes that every municipality must levy and collect on rateable property. Rates are set by the Minister of Finance (most recent update O. Reg. 297/25 for 2026). Municipalities apply these rates to MPAC assessments alongside their own municipal rates. Education portion typically ~20-25% of a residential tax bill.
reports.cadence_note: Annual (regulation updated each year)

reports.title: City of Toronto Municipal Land Transfer Tax (MLTT) and Municipal Non-Resident Speculation Tax
reports.description: Municipal Land Transfer Tax levied on property conveyances in Toronto (Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 760) plus the Municipal Non-Resident Speculation Tax (10% on eligible foreign buyers, effective 2025). Graduated rate structure for high-value residential properties updated 2026. Significant own-source revenue tool referenced in the Long-Term Financial Plan and annual budgets.
reports.cadence_note: Rates and structure updated by bylaw as needed; ongoing administration

reports.title: City of Mississauga Budget
reports.description: Annual operating and capital budget adopted by Council. Includes City portion of property tax levy (Region of Peel and education are separate). Most recent: 2026 Budget adopted January 2026.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of Mississauga Consolidated Financial Statements / Financial and Sustainability Report
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with Public Sector Accounting Board standards as required by the Municipal Act, 2001, accompanied by the Financial and Sustainability Report.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of Mississauga Tax Ratios and Rates By-law
reports.description: Annual by-law establishing tax ratios and levies for the year (e.g. By-law 0061-2026). Property tax calculated as MPAC assessment × combined City + Region of Peel + education rates.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of Hamilton Tax & Rate Budget
reports.description: Annual tax-supported operating and capital budget plus rate-supported (water) budget. Adopted under Municipal Act / Strong Mayor powers. Includes Property Tax Levy By-law.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of Hamilton Consolidated Financial Statements
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements and statistical information prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of Brampton Budget
reports.description: Annual operating and capital budget. City portion of property tax; Region of Peel and education collected on behalf of others. 2026 Budget featured 0% increase on City portion.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of Brampton Consolidated Financial Statements / Financial Report
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards / PSAB, published in the annual Financial Report.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of London Multi-Year Budget
reports.description: Multi-year (currently 2024–2027) property-tax and rate-supported budget with annual updates. Sets the tax levy requirement used to calculate rates.
reports.cadence_note: Multi-year with annual updates

reports.title: City of London Consolidated Financial Statements / Financial Report
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Public Sector Accounting Standards, published in the annual Financial Report.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of London Tax Rates and Codes
reports.description: Annual tax rates and codes set by Council after budget adoption. Calculated from the tax levy requirement and MPAC assessments; education rates applied as prescribed by the Province.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of Guelph Multi-Year Budget / Confirmed Budget
reports.description: Multi-year budget (e.g. 2024–2027) with annual confirmed updates. Sets the City tax levy requirement used for rate calculation. Includes local boards and shared services and hospital levy components.
reports.cadence_note: Multi-year with annual confirmation

reports.title: City of Guelph Consolidated Financial Statements
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards / Municipal Act requirements. Clean (unqualified) audit opinions routinely received.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of Guelph Property Tax Rates
reports.description: Published annual tax rates by property class combining City levy, hospital levy (where applicable), and provincial education rates applied to MPAC assessment.

reports.title: City of Kingston Operating and Capital Budgets
reports.description: Annual operating and capital budgets proposed under Strong Mayor powers and adopted by Council. Includes tax levy requirement.

reports.title: City of Kingston Consolidated Financial Statements
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: City of Kingston Tax Levy By-law

reports.title: Town of Caledon Budget
reports.description: Annual operating and capital budget. Includes property tax increase plus dedicated infrastructure levy. Lower-tier municipality within Region of Peel.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: Town of Caledon Consolidated Financial Statements
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards as required by the Municipal Act.
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: Town of Caledon Tax Rates / Levy

reports.title: Town of Cobourg Tax Rates
