reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: The Canadian Consumer Price Index Reference Paper
reports.description: Authoritative methodology document explaining the conceptual, structural and methodological basis of the Canadian CPI: scope, classifications, sample strategy, price collection, index calculation, quality adjustment, basket weights and updates, reliability, and history. Updated periodically (2023 edition is the current comprehensive reference).
reports.cadence_note: Periodic (major updates)

reports.title: City of Toronto Councillor / Mayor Remuneration – CPI Adjustment
reports.description: During the term of Council, remuneration paid to the Mayor and Councillors is adjusted annually to the Statistics Canada Consumer Price Index (CPI) for Toronto, as calculated by the Deputy City Manager and Chief Financial Officer based on the previous year’s average (Council policy originating 2006, with subsequent reviews).
reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.title: Public Service Pension Plan (PSPP) Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) Methodology
reports.description: Formal formula for annual COLA applied to PSPP pensions in pay. Escalation factor is calculated from the average Statistics Canada Consumer Price Index over two consecutive 12-month periods ending 30 September. Maximum annual increase 8%; excess carried forward. Applied each January. Primary provincial mechanism that directly indexes a major compensation stream to CPI.
reports.cadence_note: Annual calculation; methodology standing

reports.title: MPP Pension and Compensation Act, 2025
reports.publisher: Legislative Assembly of Ontario / Government of Ontario
reports.description: Legislation that ended the multi-year MPP salary freeze. Sets base MPP salary at 75% of the federal Member of Parliament sessional allowance (effective with the 2025 election), with subsequent annual increases tied to federal MP salaries. Also establishes a new pension arrangement integrated with the Public Service Pension Plan plus a supplemental benefit for members with at least six years of service (effective 1 January 2026).
reports.cadence_note: One-time statute; annual salary adjustments thereafter

reports.title: Ontario Works Policy Directives
reports.publisher: Ministry of Children, Community and Social Services / Government of Ontario

reports.cadence_note: Standing directives; rates updated by regulation

reports.title: Ontario Guaranteed Annual Income System (GAINS) Benefit Rates
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance / Government of Ontario
reports.description: Official rate tables for the Guaranteed Annual Income System, a provincial top-up for low-income seniors receiving federal Old Age Security and Guaranteed Income Supplement. reports.cadence_note: Periodic (rate tables)

reports.title: City of Toronto Property Tax & Utility Relief Programs for Low-Income Seniors and Persons with Disabilities
reports.description: Municipal programs providing property tax increase cancellation or deferral, water rebate, and solid waste relief for eligible low-income seniors and low-income persons with disabilities. reports.cadence_note: Annual application cycle

reports.title: City of Mississauga Property Tax Rebate for Low-Income Seniors and Persons with Disabilities

reports.cadence_note: Annual

reports.cadence_note: annual

reports.title: Postsecondary Operating Grants and Strategic Mandate Agreements

reports.title: Ontario Tuition Framework for Publicly Assisted Colleges and Universities

reports.title: Property Assessment Notice and Assessment Roll (Current Value Assessment)
reports.description: Ontario's single province-wide property assessment, prepared by a not-for-profit corporation funded by all Ontario municipalities rather than by a government department. This is the structural difference from Alberta, where each municipality prepares its own roll and the province must then run an explicit equalization step to make them comparable. Ontario needs no equalization because there is one assessor. The standard is Current Value, defined in the Assessment Act s. 1(1) as 'the amount of money the fee simple, if unencumbered, would realize if sold at arm's length by a willing seller to a willing buyer'. MPAC states it uses 'one of three approaches to value properties: direct comparison approach, income approach, cost approach', with the direct comparison approach 'the most commonly used' and the choice depending on 'property type, and the number of recent comparable sales of similar properties in the area'. The returned roll and its household counts are what the Ontario Municipal Partnership Fund allocates against.
reports.cadence_note: The roll returns annually; the values in it have not been re-based since 2016, and the gap between those two facts is the point. The Assessment Act s. 19.2(1) sets a four-year cycle by schedule, and para 4 assigns 1 January 2016 to 'the four taxation years from 2017 to 2020'. MPAC states the schedule has been suspended: 'On August 16, 2023, the Ontario government filed a regulation to amend the Assessment Act, extending the postponement of a province-wide reassessment through the end of the 2021-2024 assessment cycle. Property assessments for the 2026 property tax year will continue to be based on fully phased-in January 1, 2016 current values.' So `releases_per_year` 1 counts the returned roll, which does move for new construction, demolition and change of use; `changes_per_year` 0.25 is the statutory reassessment cycle, which is the rate at which the valuation basis is supposed to move and has not moved in ten years. Both numbers are true and neither alone describes this node.

entries.covers: 2023 Property Assessment Notices mailed (Nov) and Assessment Roll returned (Dec 12, 2023)
2024 Property Assessment Notices mailed (Nov, 627,000+ notices) and Assessment Roll returned (Dec 10, 2024)
2025 Property Assessment Notices mailed and Assessment Roll returned (fact sheet dated Dec 9, 2025)
Projected 2026 Property Assessment Notices and Assessment Roll return, based on the consistent Nov-Dec annual pattern

release_schedule.note: MPAC delivers an assessment roll annually to Ontario municipalities each Nov-Dec (with Property Assessment Notices mailed to owners with changed assessments in November, and the roll formally 'returned' in early-mid December: Dec 12 2023, Dec 10 2024, ~Dec 9 2025). This annual notice/roll cycle is distinct from the province-wide Current Value Assessment (CVA) base-year update: Ontario's Assessment Act nominally requires reassessment on a 4-year cycle, but the government has repeatedly postponed it by regulation since 2020 (most recently confirmed through the 2026 tax year), so assessed values remain frozen at January 1, 2016 current values with no announced date for the next province-wide reassessment. The annual roll-return/notice cycle, however, has continued on schedule every year regardless of the reassessment freeze.

reports.title: Ontario Municipal Partnership Fund — Allocations and Technical Guide
reports.description: Ontario's main unconditional transfer to municipalities, described in its own Technical Guide as 'the Province's main general assistance grant to municipalities'. The 2026 programme provides 'a total of $600 million in unconditional funding to 388 municipalities' through four core grant components plus Transitional Assistance. It earns a place in this graph for a reason unrelated to its size: the Technical Guide carries an Appendix F headed 'Data sources', a literal table of every data element the allocation formula consumes and where each one comes from. Documents that name their own inputs in a table are the strongest evidence class this project recognises, and they are rare outside statute.

entries.covers: 2027 OMPF allocations and technical guide (projected next edition)

release_schedule.note: The Ontario Ministry of Finance does not publish a fixed release calendar or a statutory deadline for OMPF allocations/technical guide. The ministry states only that 'OMPF allocations are announced annually in time to support the municipal budget planning process' (per the 2026 technical guide page). Observed history: 2024 guide published 2023-10-20; 2025 guide published 2024-10-30; 2026 guide published 2025-10-31 — a consistent late-October release each year for the following calendar year's allocations. The next edition (2027 OMPF) is therefore projected for late October 2026, but no exact day is confirmed.

reports.title: Financial Information Return (FIR)
reports.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing
reports.description: Ontario's mandatory annual municipal financial return — the direct counterpart of `ab-municipalaffairs-fir`, already a node in this graph for Alberta. The FIR portal describes it as 'a standardized reporting of a municipality's financial activities in the previous fiscal year (January to December)', collecting data on assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses and statistical information drawn from each municipality's audited financial statements. Mandatory under the Municipal Act s. 294(1): 'the treasurer of a municipality shall in each year provide the Minister with a return containing information designated by the Minister with respect to the financial affairs of the municipality.' Named directly in the OMPF Technical Guide's Appendix F: 'PIL Weighted Assessment | 2023 or 2024 | Municipal FIR (Financial Information Return)'. Minted 2026-08-09 (corpus-wide `_dropped` sweep, Tier-1 item #7).
reports.cadence_note: Annual, deadline 31 May per the FIR portal's own description of the submission cycle; collected since 1978 (covering 1977 financial data), with complete province-wide datasets from 1988 onward per the portal's own historical archive.

release_schedule.rule: The deadline for the completion of the [year] Financial Information Return (FIR) is May 31 of the following year (e.g., "The deadline for the completion of 2025 FIR is May 31, 2026"), per the FIR Instructions issued by the Ontario Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing under Municipal Act s.294(1).
release_schedule.note: The 2025 FIR deadline of May 31, 2026 has already passed as of 2026-08-11; next occurrence is the 2026 FIR, due May 31, 2027, following the same annual pattern. Deadline is stated in the annual FIR Instructions document (page 9, 'Deadline for Completion' section) rather than a fixed statutory date, but has been consistently May 31 in recent years.

reports.title: Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI)
reports.description: The geographic reference database behind Statistics Canada's published boundary and road-network products, named directly in the OMPF Technical Guide's Appendix F ('Municipal Land Area is based on the Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI) from Statistics Canada and excludes bodies of water') but never itself released. Statistics Canada's own Illustrated Glossary describes it as 'an internal maintenance database that is not disseminated outside of Statistics Canada. A THIRD STATUTE THAT ANTICIPATES ITS OWN SUSPENSION, and the submitted artifact had the outcome right and the mechanism wrong. It attributed the 2016 valuation date for the 2026 taxation year to 'successive postponements', citing nothing. The Act's own schedule says something narrower. Assessment Act s. 19.2(1) para 4: 'For the period consisting of the four taxation years from 2017 to 2020, land is valued as of January 1, 2016', and para 5 provides that after 2020 each four-year period is valued as of 'January 1 of the year that precedes the period by two years'. Read alone, the Act does not put 2016 anywhere near 2026. The bridge is s. 19.2(5): 'Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of the valuation of land for a taxation year after 2004 if the Minister prescribes a different day as of which land is valued for that year.' MPAC confirms that is what happened — a regulation filed 16 August 2023. So the statute contains a clause permitting its own timetable to be set aside, and that clause has now been used to hold a valuation date six years past the schedule it was written into. This belongs with the Canada Pension Plan Act's splice clause and the Oil Sands Royalty Regulation's provision for the day the Bank of Canada stops publishing an exchange rate: three instances now, and enough to call it a pattern rather than a curiosity. Legislation about numbers routinely writes in what to do when the number stops behaving, and the graph has no way to show it. READ 2026-08-09 — still correct, no change.

The submitted material does not do that: `calgary-tax-bylaw` carries `url: null`, so the keystone document is not cited at all, and the edge from it to the education requisition is evidenced by a City newsroom press release. That release is also the source given for 'Calgary's 2026 education requisition rose ~20% to over $1.2 billion', a figure which does not appear on the alberta.ca page the artifact cites for it and which was not verified anywhere. Three of the artifact's Alberta nodes duplicate existing ones outright — `ab-equalized-assessment` shadows `ab-municipalaffairs-equalized-assessment`, `ab-education-property-tax` shadows `ab-education-property-tax-requisition`, and `ab-regulated-property-guidelines` is an exact id collision that the loader would have silently dropped under first-wins, losing the differing content without a warning. READ 2026-08-09 — out of this file's own scope (Alberta municipal work, not Ontario/StatCan); no new information, no change.

PROCESS FINDING, recorded because the format question was settled in V0.9 and this is the first regression. V0.9 established that a second reader extracts and this project adjudicates: no verdict field, verbatim quotes, `AGENCY ONLY` where only an institution is named. Three rounds in V0.10 under that format produced zero adjudication errors. This artifact arrived in the pre-V0.9 shape — 17 finished report objects and 24 finished edges with `relationship_type` already chosen and `basis` written as paraphrase rather than quotation. Two edges of the twenty-four survived. The paraphrasing is what did the damage: not one of the twelve Equalization bases contains a quoted string, so there was nothing to check against the source except the section number, and the section numbers were the ones already known to be wrong. Where the artifact did quote — the Appendix F rows, the Assessment Act current-value definition — it was accurate, and those are the parts that became edges. The rule holds and has now been tested from the other side: a verbatim quote is checkable in minutes, a paraphrase is not checkable at all. It also under-reported its own best source. Appendix F names twelve data elements; the artifact used three of them, ignored Municipal FIR, OPTA and Ontario Parcel entirely, and spent its effort on the six Statistics Canada rows that name no release. READ 2026-08-09 — still correct; worth noting that this session's own mints (FIR, SDI terminus, OPTA terminus) are exactly the three the artifact 'ignored entirely', confirming the process finding's point that quoted, tabular sources are more productive than a paraphrasing reader's own judgement calls.

2026-08-07: this file used to carry a deliberately-superseding copy of ab-education-property-tax-requisition -> ab-municipalaffairs-equalized-assessment, relying on the V0.8 last-wins rule and on this slice registering after alberta-municipal.json. That made the winning basis depend on import order (flagged in the 2026-08-07 review). The better-evidenced copy now lives in alberta-municipal.json itself, where the edge belongs; the override is gone and the duplicate-edge report is empty again.

reports.title: Fiji Bureau of Statistics
reports.description: Fiji's national statistical office, established under the Statistics Act and Census Act, responsible for compiling and publishing the country's official economic and social statistics.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
reports.description: Monthly official consumer price index tracking changes in the prices of a basket of goods and services in Fiji; the index weights are derived from the Household Income and Expenditure Survey.

reports.title: Fiji Gross Domestic Product (GDP) / National Accounts
reports.description: Official annual estimates of Fiji's gross domestic product (production, expenditure and income approaches), compiled following the 2008 System of National Accounts.

reports.title: Household Income and Expenditure Survey (HIES)
reports.description: Nationwide household survey conducted every five years by the Fiji Bureau of Statistics; used to update CPI weights, the poverty rate, and inputs to the national accounts.

reports.title: National Statistical Office of Papua New Guinea
reports.description: Papua New Guinea's national statistical office, established under the Statistical Services Act 1980, responsible for producing and coordinating official statistics across government.

reports.title: Solomon Islands National Statistics Office
reports.description: Solomon Islands' national statistical office, operating under the Statistics Act 1970 and Census Act 1959, responsible for compiling official economic and social statistics.

reports.title: Vanuatu Bureau of Statistics
reports.description: Vanuatu's national statistical office (formerly named the Vanuatu National Statistics Office, VNSO), responsible for CPI, national accounts, trade and census statistics.

reports.title: Samoa Bureau of Statistics
reports.description: Samoa's national statistical office, responsible for compiling and disseminating official economic and social statistics and for hosting Samoa's IMF e-GDDS National Summary Data Page.

reports.title: Tonga Statistics Department
reports.description: Tonga's national statistical office, responsible for producing official economic and social statistics including the census, CPI and national accounts.

reports.title: Kiribati National Statistics Office
reports.description: Kiribati's national statistical office, established under the Statistics Act 1997, responsible for producing official statistics including CPI, GDP and trade data.

reports.title: Nauru Bureau of Statistics
reports.description: Nauru's national statistical office, sitting within the Ministry of Finance, responsible for producing the country's Consumer Price Index and other official statistics.

reports.title: Tuvalu Central Statistics Division
reports.description: Tuvalu's official statistical agency, governed by the Statistics Act 1978, responsible for national accounts, census and other official statistics.

reports.title: Pacific Community (SPC) — Statistics for Development Division
reports.description: One of SPC's technical divisions, based in Noumea and Suva, that strengthens the capacity of Pacific Island countries' national statistical systems through technical assistance, training workshops and staff attachments covering national accounts, CPI, censuses and other official statistics.

reports.title: Pacific Financial Technical Assistance Centre (PFTAC)
reports.description: IMF regional technical assistance centre established in 1993, a collaborative venture between the IMF, member countries and donor partners, providing capacity-development support on macroeconomic and financial statistics and policy to sixteen Pacific Island countries.

reports.title: Encuesta Nacional de Hogares (ENAHO) / National Household Survey
reports.description: Continuous household survey that is the official source for living conditions, monetary poverty, multidimensional poverty, income and expenditure, education and health access. National coverage with departmental disaggregation.
reports._notes: Central social survey of Peru. Continuous since 2003 (earlier quarterly from 1995). Primary microdata source for poverty measurement and for a wide range of living-conditions indicators. Quarterly living-conditions reports and annual poverty results are the main public products.

reports.title: Pobreza monetaria / Monetary poverty
reports.description: Official income/expenditure-based poverty and extreme-poverty incidence. Calculated by comparing household per-capita expenditure (from ENAHO) with nationally defined poverty lines. Annual publication with urban/rural and departmental breakdowns.
reports._notes: Headline social indicator. 2025: monetary poverty 25.7% (down 1.9 pp from 27.6% in 2024); extreme poverty 4.7%. Urban–rural gap remains large (urban ~23.4%, rural ~35.5%). Series supervised by the Comisión Consultiva.

reports.title: Líneas de pobreza total y extrema
reports.description: Monetary values of the total and extreme poverty lines (per capita and for reference households), updated with price information and differentiated by geographic domain.
reports._notes: Direct input into the poverty measurement. 2025 total poverty line ~S/ 462 per person; extreme (basic food basket) ~S/ 260 per person.

reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) / Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index measuring changes in the prices of a representative basket of goods and services. National and major-city coverage.
reports._notes: Flagship price statistic. Direct input into monetary-policy analysis by the Banco Central de Reserva and into the updating of poverty lines.

reports.title: Cuentas Nacionales / National Accounts of Peru
reports.description: System of national accounts producing GDP by production, expenditure and income. Quarterly and annual releases.
reports._notes: Core macroeconomic statistical system. INEI is the primary compiler of the real-sector accounts.

reports.title: Encuesta Permanente de Empleo Nacional (EPEN) / Permanent National Employment Survey
reports.description: Continuous employment survey providing labour-force indicators (employment, unemployment, underemployment, informality) at national and major-domain levels.
reports._notes: Primary high-frequency labour survey. Complements the longer-running ENAHO on labour-market dimensions and feeds the quarterly living-conditions reports.

reports.title: Censos Nacionales de Población y Vivienda / National Population and Housing Census
reports.description: Decennial population and housing census. Provides the demographic baseline, sampling frames for household surveys, and small-area population estimates.
reports._notes: Foundational demographic product. Continuously cited by ENAHO/EPEN design, poverty analysis and departmental statistical work.

reports.title: Condiciones de Vida en el Perú (quarterly technical report)
reports.description: Quarterly technical report synthesising ENAHO and EPEN results on living conditions, employment and related welfare indicators.
reports._notes: Regular public synthesis product. Bridges the continuous survey data to a widely used quarterly narrative on welfare and the labour market.

reports.title: Producción Nacional / Monthly GDP (PBI)
reports.description: Monthly estimate of national production (PBI) by economic activity. Principal high-frequency real-activity indicator.
reports._notes: Core short-term activity product. 2025 full-year growth ~3.4%; Q1 2026 ~3.5%. Construction, commerce and manufacturing have been recent drivers.

reports.title: PBI Manufactura / Manufacturing production
reports.description: Volume and value indicators of manufacturing production, split into primary and non-primary manufacturing. Monthly and annual series.
reports._notes: Manufacturing contributes ~12% of GDP. 2025 growth ~2.7% (primary +4.9%, non-primary +1.9%). Export-oriented manufacturing has been a notable contributor.

reports.title: Balanza de Pagos / Balance of Payments
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
reports.description: Quarterly and annual balance of payments covering the current account, capital/financial account and changes in reserve assets.
reports._notes: Core external-accounts product. Recent years have shown current-account surpluses driven by strong traditional exports (mining, fishing, gas). Net international investment position and reserve adequacy are regularly reported.

reports.title: Estadísticas de Comercio Exterior / Merchandise Trade
reports.description: Monthly and annual statistics of exports and imports of goods, classified as traditional (mining, fishing, agriculture, oil/gas) and non-traditional.
reports._notes: Trade data feed both the BOP and the national accounts. Mining remains the dominant traditional export; manufacturing exports have shown strong recent growth.

reports.title: Reporte de Inflación (BCR)
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
reports.description: Periodic Inflation Report of the central bank. Explains recent inflation, the outlook, and the implications for the reference interest rate under the explicit inflation-targeting regime.
reports._notes: Flagship policy communication product. Complements the monthly monetary-programme statements. Central reference for the 1–3% inflation target band.

reports.title: Tasa de interés de referencia / Policy interest rate
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
reports.description: Main monetary-policy instrument of the BCR Board. The rate at which the central bank signals the monetary stance and steers interbank rates.
reports._notes: Operational policy rate. Held at 4.25% for an extended period in 2025–2026 after the earlier easing cycle. Path is the primary signal of the monetary stance.

reports.title: Reservas Internacionales Netas (RIN)
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
reports.description: Stock of net international reserves managed by the central bank. Published at high frequency and analysed in the BOP and annual reports.
reports._notes: Key external-buffer indicator. End-2025 RIN ~USD 90 bn (~26% of GDP), covering multiple months of imports and a high multiple of short-term external debt.

reports.title: Marco de metas de inflación (1–3%) — BCR
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
reports.description: Operational monetary-policy framework: explicit inflation targeting with a 1–3% annual CPI band (centre 2%). In place since 2002.
reports._notes: Core policy-framework node. Continuously cited as the reference against which inflation outcomes and policy actions are evaluated.
_referenced_by: Every Inflation Report and monetary-programme statement
IPC and inflation analysis that refers to the target band
Market and academic commentary on Peruvian monetary policy

reports.title: Producción y exportaciones mineras / Mining production & exports
reports.publisher: INEI / Ministerio de Energía y Minas / BCR
reports.description: Statistics of metallic and non-metallic mining production and exports (copper, gold, zinc, silver, etc.). Structural component of traditional exports and of GDP.
reports._notes: Mining is the backbone of traditional exports and a major GDP contributor. Copper and gold dominate the export basket; production and export volumes are high-frequency inputs into the BOP and national accounts.

reports.title: Producción y exportaciones pesqueras / Fishing & fishmeal
reports.description: Statistics of fishing catch, fishmeal and fish-oil production and exports. Important traditional export and source of short-term volatility in manufacturing and GDP.
reports._notes: High-volatility traditional sector. Anchovy/fishmeal cycles drive large swings in primary manufacturing and in the goods trade balance. Regularly highlighted in monthly production and BOP analysis.

reports.title: Lima Metropolitana — capital statistical identity
reports.description: Capital metropolitan area and largest urban economy. Primary high-frequency domain for ENAHO, EPEN and many price/activity series. Intermediate monetary-poverty incidence relative to the national average.
reports._notes: Dominant metro node. 2025 monetary poverty in Lima Metropolitana ~27.3% (close to the national 25.7%). Continuously published as a distinct geographic domain in poverty and living-conditions reports.

reports.title: Departamento de Cajamarca — highest-poverty contrast
reports.description: Andean department with the highest monetary-poverty incidence in the 2025 results. Tests the statistical hierarchy under persistent high poverty despite mining presence.
reports._notes: Poverty-contrast department. 2025 monetary poverty 41.0% (highest); also among the highest in extreme poverty. Has remained in the top poverty group for many consecutive years.

reports.title: Departamento de Loreto — high-poverty Selva contrast
reports.description: Amazonian department with the second-highest monetary-poverty incidence. Completes the periphery contrast alongside Cajamarca and Puno.
reports._notes: 2025 monetary poverty 40.1%. Illustrates the Selva high-poverty cluster under a common national measurement framework.

reports.title: Departamento de Puno — high-poverty Sierra contrast
reports.description: Southern Andean department ranking among the highest in monetary and extreme poverty.
reports._notes: 2025 monetary poverty 37.5%. Part of the persistent high-poverty Sierra group.

reports.title: Departamento de Ica — low-poverty contrast
reports.description: Coastal department with the lowest monetary-poverty incidence in the 2025 results.
reports._notes: 2025 monetary poverty 4.5% — lowest of the departments. Completes the low-poverty pole opposite Cajamarca/Loreto/Puno.

reports.title: Pobreza monetaria por departamento (INEI)
reports.description: Official departmental tabulations of monetary poverty and extreme poverty. Primary source for the inter-departmental poverty gradient.
reports._notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2025 ranking (selected): Cajamarca 41.0%, Loreto 40.1%, Puno 37.5%, … Ica 4.5%, Madre de Dios 7.3%, Moquegua 7.8%. National average 25.7%.

reports.title: Presupuesto del Sector Público / National Budget (MEF)
reports.description: Annual public-sector budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues and expenditure of the central government and transfers.
reports._notes: Operational fiscal framework. 2026 budget ~S/ 257.6 bn. Education, health, transport and security absorb a large share of the functional allocation.

reports.title: Estadísticas de educación / Education statistics & budget
reports.description: Enrolment, attainment and learning-outcome indicators together with the education functional budget. Complements ENAHO education modules.
reports._notes: Education is a major budget priority. ENAHO provides household-side attainment and access data; administrative systems and learning assessments supply the supply-side picture.

reports.title: Estadísticas de salud / Health coverage & expenditure
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Salud / SIS / INEI / MEF
reports.description: Health-insurance coverage (SIS and other schemes), health-service access and the health functional budget. Complements ENAHO health modules.
reports._notes: Health is a major and growing budget function. SIS (Seguro Integral de Salud) is the principal public insurer for the uninsured population; ENAHO tracks affiliation and access.

reports.title: Café — producción y exportaciones
reports.publisher: MIDAGRI / Junta Nacional del Café / SUNAT / INEI
reports.description: Statistics of coffee production and exports. Leading traditional agricultural export, produced mainly by smallholders in Andean and Amazonian foothill regions. Peru is a major organic-coffee exporter.
reports._notes: Signature soft-commodity export. 2025 exports reached record levels (reports in the USD 1.7–1.8 bn range). Produced in 16 regions; main producers include San Martín, Cajamarca, Junín, Cusco and Amazonas. Continuously cited in agro-export and rural-economy analysis.

reports.title: Agroexportaciones / Non-traditional agricultural exports
reports.description: Broader statistics of agricultural and agro-industrial exports (fresh produce, processed foods, coffee, cocoa, etc.). Complements the mining-dominated traditional-export basket.
reports._notes: Non-traditional agro-exports have been a diversification success story. Coffee is the largest single traditional agricultural line; blueberries, grapes, avocados and asparagus are major non-traditional lines.

reports.title: Sierra — natural-region statistical domain
reports.description: Andean highlands natural region used as a standard geographic domain in ENAHO poverty and living-conditions analysis. Highest rural poverty incidence.
reports._notes: Key natural-region domain. Sierra rural recorded the highest monetary poverty in 2025 (~38.8%). Hosts much of the coffee and highland agricultural production as well as important mining districts.

reports.title: Selva — natural-region statistical domain
reports.description: Amazonian natural region used as a standard geographic domain in ENAHO analysis. Elevated rural poverty and important coffee/cocoa producing zones.
reports._notes: Selva rural poverty remains elevated (~30.7% in 2025). Contains major coffee-producing departments such as San Martín and parts of Amazonas.

reports.title: Costa — natural-region statistical domain
reports.description: Coastal natural region used as a standard geographic domain. Lowest poverty incidence among the three natural regions; hosts the capital and the bulk of non-traditional agro-exports.
reports._notes: Costa urbana has the lowest poverty rates. Completes the three natural-region domains (Costa–Sierra–Selva) that structure much of Peruvian social and agricultural analysis.

reports.title: Departamento de San Martín — coffee-producing Andean–Amazon transition
reports.description: Major coffee-producing department in the Andean–Amazon transition zone. Important for both agricultural-export and rural-poverty analysis.
reports._notes: One of the leading coffee regions. Links the commodity (coffee) to the departmental and natural-region poverty/production geography.

reports.title: Canon minero y regalías mineras
reports.publisher: MEF / Ministerio de Energía y Minas
reports.description: Mining canon and royalty transfers from central government to producing regions and local governments. Major sub-national fiscal mechanism linking mining production to territorial budgets.
reports._notes: Critical sub-national fiscal node. Directly links the mining production and export statistics to departmental and municipal budgets, especially in the Sierra and mining corridors.

reports.title: Departamento de Moquegua — low-poverty mining contrast
reports.description: Southern mining department with very low monetary-poverty incidence. Completes the mining-department contrast alongside Ica.
reports._notes: 2025 monetary poverty ~7.8%. Hosts major copper operations; illustrates that mining presence can coincide with low measured poverty under the national framework.

dependencies.basis: San Martín is one of the principal coffee-producing departments.

_note: Philippines — Round 7 — browser/curl unblock of the access-blocked backlog, 2026-08-29. Every edge here closes a lead that an earlier round recorded as unreachable. The blocks were largely artefacts of the fetch tool, not the sites: mnd.gov.tw is fully readable to plain curl (its 'ROBOTS_DISALLOWED' verdict was WebFetch obeying robots.txt); gob.mx serves its /cms/uploads/attachment/file/ PDFs to curl while Akamai-challenging its HTML; BPS Indonesia's signed web-api.bps.go.id download host is not Cloudflare-walled even though every *.bps.go.id page is. dependencies.basis: The Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028 results matrix (Chapter 12, Infrastructure, PDF p.313) names "DOE Power Statistics" in its MEANS OF VERIFICATION column for the indicator "Share of renewable energy in the power generation mix increased (%)" (baseline 22.40, 2021), with DOE as responsible agency. Adjacent rows in the same block name "Department of Energy (DOE) Annual Report", confirming the column lists per-indicator sources and that Power Statistics is a distinct named product. _dropped.why:
DECISION (Thomas, 2026-08-30): declined -- an information system (EBEIS) does not stand in for the statistics it produces; the target must be a named publication. Do not re-raise. Original entry follows.

Evidence found and verified, but held on a node-identity question rather than an access problem. The PDP results matrix (PDF p.313-314, https://pdp.depdev.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Philippine-Development-Plan-2023-2028.pdf) names "Enhanced Basic Education Information System (EBEIS), Department of Education (DepEd) data" in its MEANS OF VERIFICATION column for the classroom-to-pupil ratio indicator (baseline 1:32, 2021), with the short form "EBEIS, DepEd data" recurring on six further rows. The objection: that names an information SYSTEM and 'DepEd data', not a named publication, whereas ph-basic-ed is 'Basic education statistics (DepEd)'. The bridge between the two is DepEd Order No. 52 s.2016, titled 'Data Collection of Basic Education Statistics in the Learner Information System and Enhanced Basic Education Information System' — but deped.gov.ph returns a 345-byte WAF 403 to curl on every path, so that title is a fetch-tool paraphrase with no verbatim bytes behind it. If the project's bar allows an information system to stand for the statistics it produces, this edge is ready; if the target must be a named publication, it is a genuine no.

Reclassified from unreadable-source on real bytes. The node's own listed PDF is retrievable by plain curl (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 358,199 bytes, 5 pages) — the HTML site being a Nuxt SPA no longer matters because the statistical artefact itself reads fine. Its notes block, verbatim: "Notes: / p Preliminary data. / The 2024 and 2025 data are all preliminary and subject to final evaluation. / Source: Department of Migrant Workers - Management Information and Technology Service. / Processed by: Strategic Planning and Management Service". The only stated source is DMW's own internal unit, which is not a corpus node. Separately, ph-dmw appears in the PDP only in the RESPONSIBLE AGENCY column for the documented-Overseas-Filipinos indicator, whose MEANS OF VERIFICATION names "Department of Foreign Affairs report" — an agency role, not a source.

Reclassified from unreadable-source; the source is not unreadable, it simply states no lineage. cpa.gov.ph serves fine to curl (189 KB homepage). Its /the-cebu-port-system/statistics page body is empty apart from a heading but embeds a Google Drive folder, which was enumerated (https://drive.google.com/embeddedfolderview?id=1SlDazoEzRPXS6Y0Vm2XHVqOwQ0M5DDfw): two subfolders, 'Quarterly & Annually Statistical Report' with year folders 2000-2026 of per-quarter .xlsx, and 'Datasets'. Downloaded and text-extracted '2025 CPA Performance at a Glance.pdf' (11,228,972 bytes, all 3 pages): 146,527 shipping traffic, 19.64M passengers, 75.87 MMTs cargo throughput, 993.75 TTEUs containers — with no source line, no methodology note and no reference to PPA, PSA or any other report. /news-and-publications is HR announcements and /transparency-seal is COA financial reports. Also checked: in the PDP, CPA appears only among a dozen RESPONSIBLE AGENCY entries against indicators whose MEANS OF VERIFICATION reads 'Agency reports', which names no CPA product. Containment note in passing: CPA's own page states 'The Cebu Port System is composed of the Cebu Baseport and its subports... There are five subports within the jurisdiction of Cebu Port Authority, namely: Mandaue, Danao, Sta. Fe, Toledo and Argao' (https://www.cpa.gov.ph/the-cebu-port-system) — containment of the subports inside the Cebu system, saying nothing about CPA rolling into PPA's national totals, which reinforces the earlier rejection of ph-port-cebu -> ph-ports.

Reclassified from unreadable-source as a SOURCE. deped.gov.ph returns HTTP 403 to curl on every path tried (/, /resources/facts-and-figures/, /wp-content/uploads/, and the DO 52 s.2016 PDF), with a 345-byte body consisting of a bare img tag pointing at depedwesiteblobstorage.blob.core.windows.net/.../403.png — an intentional WAF block, not robots.txt. WebFetch does retrieve the order PDF, which names only DepEd's own Learner Information System and EBEIS as data sources — internal administrative systems, not corpus nodes. SETTLED, and the round-2 premise was wrong in two ways. The '2025 SNA' phrase comes from a PSA-authored deck — 'An Overview of the Philippines' Experience in Measuring the contribution of Digital Economy', Gerald Junne L. Clariño, Chief Statistical Specialist, Satellite Accounts Division, delivered 07 April 2026 at the 'Webinar on Digitalization in the 2025 System of National Accounts' — reachable at https://www.unsiap.or.jp/sites/default/files/doc/2026-04/11_Philippine's%20Experience.pdf (8,402,284 bytes, 27 pages) because psa.gov.ph itself is Cloudflare-walled. On page 26, under the heading 'Ways forward', it reads verbatim: "1. Adoption of the 2025 System of National Accounts recommendations, particularly in covering activities i.e., content creation and trade on digital platforms (free and fee-based) including the non-traditional work arrangements." That is an aspiration, in the same register as the held vn-monetary-indicators -> imf-mfsmcg-2016 case, and it supports no edge in either direction: not to sna-2008 (wrong vintage, and the deck never says PDESA currently follows 2008 SNA), and not to a 2025-SNA node either. The second correction: sna-2025 ALREADY EXISTS in international-standards.json, so the modelling question was never 'does the corpus need a new node'. Two leads from the same deck for whoever revisits ph-digital-economy: pages 17-18 list LFS among PDESA's data sources, and page 8 states the digital-enabling-infrastructure component 'is based on the sectors identified in the ICT sector definition of International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC), Revision 4'. Page 3 also confirms the earlier oecd-digital-suts-handbook rejection was right — it names OECD and BEA as institutional precedents, never the Handbook.

Still unreadable for verbatim purposes, but the reason has changed and is worth recording. DOE rebuilt its site: https://doe.gov.ph/energy-statistics/philippine-power-statistics now returns HTTP 200 but renders '404 — Page Not Found' inside the Next.js RSC payload, and the new navigation has no statistics section at all. The statistics live on legacy.doe.gov.ph, which fails from the cloud container with curl exit 56 (the egress proxy logs connect_rejected — organization policy) and from the user's device with curl exit 6 (DNS); web.archive.org returns '403 Blocked by egress policy'. WebFetch can reach legacy.doe.gov.ph and returns a page listing six 2024 Power Statistics documents, but it contains no data-sources statement — only a contact line for the EPIMB Power Planning and Development Division. Geothermal appears there as a technology row under Renewable Energy in the installed-and-dependable-capacity table, which is the weakest form of containment evidence and is NOT sufficient to set part_of. Strong prior that the underlying answer is no-document.
