reports.title: Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) institutional core
reports.description: Primary national statistical office created by the Philippine Statistical Act of 2013 (merger of NSO, NSCB, BLES, BAS). Produces censuses, surveys, national accounts, prices, labour, poverty and multi-domain statistics. Attached to NEDA for policy coordination.
reports._notes: Foundational institutional node for the entire Philippine statistical system.
reports._cadence_evidence: psa.gov.ph is the agency portal, not a single publication: it fronts an Advance Release Calendar and the OpenSTAT open-data platform (PC-Axis) with a live STATWATCH panel dated 06 Aug 2026; no discrete release for the node itself.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7) and applied 2026-08-19: a nominal releases_per_year so that absence keeps meaning 'one-off instrument' only - 250 encodes business-day updating (the live corpus's daily-FX convention), 365 genuinely all-days monitoring. It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

reports.title: Census of Population (and related mid-year estimates)
reports.description: Official population census and subsequent estimates. 2024 Census recorded 112,729,484 persons. Provides the demographic base for all per-capita and planning indicators.
reports._notes: Core demographic node. Population ~112.7 million (2024 Census).
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA population-and-housing page documents 2020 CPH and 2024 POPCEN as the recent enumerations (no explicit periodicity statement); census rounds land about every five years.

reports.title: National Accounts of the Philippines (GDP / GRDP)
reports.description: Quarterly and annual national accounts (GDP by industry and expenditure) and Gross Regional Domestic Product. Central macro-output series.
reports._notes: Primary macroeconomic output node.
_referenced_by: BSP Monetary Policy Report and economic assessments
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA National Accounts release calendar lists 4 quarterly releases (29 Jan 2026 Q4+Annual 2025, 07 May, 07 Aug, 09 Nov 2026) plus a separate Revised Annual National Accounts release on 08 Apr 2026.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index and inflation statistics
reports.description: Monthly CPI and inflation rates by major commodity group and region. High-frequency price signal used in monetary policy and welfare analysis.
reports._notes: Core high-frequency price node.
_referenced_by: BSP inflation targeting and Monetary Policy Report

reports.title: Labor Force Survey (LFS)
reports.description: Quarterly (and more frequent) labour-force statistics: employment, unemployment, underemployment, labour-force participation. Central labour-market barometer.
reports._notes: Primary labour-market statistical product.
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA 2026 Calendar of Releases lists Labor Force Survey with 12 scheduled release dates (monthly); LFS page shows consecutive monthly editions (e.g. June 2026 released 06 Aug 2026) with month-on-month comparisons.

reports.title: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) institutional and reporting core
reports.description: Central bank responsible for monetary policy, financial stability, external accounts and key macro-financial statistics. Publishes the Monetary Policy Report, Balance of Payments, International Reserves and related series.
reports._notes: Central-bank institutional counterpart to PSA.
reports._cadence_evidence: bsp.gov.ph is the central bank portal; its Statistics section is described as 'Monetary, banking, financial industry data visualization and other statistics and their release schedule' — a continuously maintained data hub, not one publication.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7) and applied 2026-08-19: a nominal releases_per_year so that absence keeps meaning 'one-off instrument' only - 250 encodes business-day updating (the live corpus's daily-FX convention), 365 genuinely all-days monitoring. It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

reports.title: Balance of Payments and International Investment Position
reports.description: Quarterly BOP and related external-sector accounts, including the large role of remittances (OFW) in the current account.
reports._notes: External-accounts node with strong remittance linkage — a defining Philippine feature.

reports.title: Gross International Reserves
reports.description: Monthly official reserve assets. Key external-buffer indicator expressed in months of import cover.
reports._notes: High-frequency external-buffer node.

reports.title: Official poverty statistics (and related thresholds)
reports.description: Official poverty incidence, poverty thresholds and related indicators derived from the Family Income and Expenditure Survey (FIES) and other sources. High policy salience.
reports._notes: Core welfare measurement node.
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA poverty release index shows full-year official poverty statistics roughly every three years (2021 full year released Aug 2022, 2023 full year released Jul 2024) with first-semester and sectoral/SAE releases in between (Dec 2023, Aug 2024, Mar 2025, Feb 2026) — about one poverty release per year.

reports.title: Mining and quarrying production statistics
reports.description: Official statistics on metallic and non-metallic mineral production. Nickel is the standout commodity (Philippines ranks among the world’s top producers); gold, copper and others complete the main metallic output.
reports._notes: Core mining statistical product. Nickel gives the Philippines a distinctive position in global battery/EV mineral supply chains.
reports._url_evidence: MGB 'Mineral Statistics' page listing Philippine Metallic Mineral Production, employment of operating mines and quarries, and directory of operating mines.
reports._cadence_evidence: MGB Mineral Industry Statistics page lists annual products — 'Philippine Metallic Mineral Production', 'Annual Employment of Operating Metallic Mines and Quarries Per Region', 'MGB Annual Revenue Collection Report per Region'; no sub-annual series stated.

reports.title: Nickel production and export statistics
reports.description: Focused statistics on nickel output and trade. The Philippines has been the second-ranked global producer in recent years, making nickel a high-centrality commodity node.
reports._notes: High-centrality commodity uniqueness node (parallel to Indonesian nickel but different institutional and policy context).
reports._url_evidence: MGB table titled 'PHILIPPINES NICKEL ORE PRODUCTION VOLUME AND VALUE 1998-2023' with annual DMT volumes and peso values.
reports._cadence_evidence: The MGB nickel table gives one row per calendar year, 1998-2023, and is filed under Philippine_Metallic_Mineral_Production/2023 with an 'as of 07 March 2024' cut-off in the filename — an annually refreshed series table.

reports.title: Fisheries and aquaculture production statistics
reports.description: Official volume and value of production for capture fisheries and aquaculture (milkfish, tilapia and other species prominent). Complements the broader agriculture and food-security cluster.
reports._notes: Primary fisheries/aquaculture statistical product.
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA Fisheries Situation Report editions are quarterly: Apr-Jun 2026 (06 Aug 2026), Jan-Mar 2026 (06 May 2026), Oct-Dec 2025 + annual 2025 (28 Jan 2026).

reports.title: Port and shipping statistics (cargo, containers, passengers)
reports.description: Operational statistics on cargo throughput (MMT), container volume (TEUs), shipcalls and passenger traffic at Philippine ports. Captures both domestic inter-island and foreign trade flows.
reports._notes: Core maritime-logistics node for an archipelagic economy.
reports._url_evidence: PPA official page reporting 2025 national port statistics: 308.5 MMT cargo throughput, over 8 million TEUs, 664,817 shipcalls; PPA's /content/statistics-1 landing page is blocked to WebFetch by robots/SSL errors.
reports._cadence_evidence: PPA page carries a single full-year performance release dated 16 Jan 2026 covering 2025 cargo (308.5 MMT), containers (8M+ TEUs), 664,817 shipcalls and RoRo traffic against 2024 — an annual performance summary.

reports.title: MSME establishment and structure statistics
reports.description: Official counts and structure of micro, small and medium enterprises. MSMEs constitute the overwhelming majority of registered establishments (recently >99 %) and a large share of employment.
reports._notes: Core enterprise-structure node. Complements the formal manufacturing (ASPBI) and IT-BPM series.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved PSA product page '2022 Annual Survey of Philippine Business and Industry (ASPBI) - All Establishments by Employment Grouping: Preliminary Results'. Page gives 281,825 establishments split micro 196,607 (69.8%), small 77,857 (27.6%), medium 3,244 (1.2%), large 4,118 (1.5%), plus employment shares by size class - i.e. official MSME establishment structure. DTI's own MSME statistics pages (dti.gov.ph/dti-knowledge-hub/dti-statistics/dti-msme-statistics) remain robots-disallowed, so the PSA source was used instead.
reports._url_route: publisher on-site/product page via targeted search (psa.gov.ph); DTI still robots-blocked
reports._cadence_evidence: ASPBI is described on the page as an annual designated statistical activity — the 2022 round was 'conducted nationwide in April 2023 with 2022 as reference period'; establishment/employment counts come from that annual cycle.

reports.title: Women and Men in the Philippines / Core GAD indicators
reports.description: Official gender statistics and Philippine Core Gender and Development (GAD) indicators covering population, education, health, labour, political participation and related domains.
reports._notes: Core gender-statistical product.
_referenced_by: Labour Force Survey and OFW gender composition
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA Gender and Development page states the Factsheet on Women and Men in the Philippines is issued annually (latest 30 Apr 2026, ref 2026-132) and that Core GAD Indicators are monitored 'through the annual updating of the Factsheet'.

reports.title: Housing and household characteristics statistics
reports.description: Housing stock, tenure, access to basic services and related household characteristics drawn from census and household surveys. Links to construction, urbanisation and welfare analysis.
reports._notes: Housing densification of the social and construction clusters.
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA page treats population and housing as one integrated collection ('Census of Population and Housing', 2020 CPH and 2024 POPCEN) — housing characteristics come out with the roughly five-yearly census rounds.

reports.title: Department of National Defense / AFP budget statistics
reports.description: Official budget allocations for the Department of National Defense and the major services (Army, Navy, Air Force). Provides the resource base for defence and security analysis.
reports._notes: Core defence-resource node.
reports._url_evidence: DBM General Appropriations Act FY2026 page; the agency listing includes Department of National Defense with Office of the Secretary, Philippine Army, Air Force, Navy and PVAO budget documents.
reports._cadence_evidence: The DBM page is the General Appropriations Act FY 2026, i.e. Republic Act No. 12314 dated 06 January 2026 — a single enacted law with a document behind it, not a statistical series (DBM does enact a new GAA each fiscal year).

reports.title: Irrigation development and status statistics
reports.description: Official status of irrigation development — area irrigated, systems, and related indicators. Critical for rice production and agricultural resilience.
reports._notes: Core irrigation/water-for-agriculture node.

reports.title: Science, technology and R&D statistics
reports.description: Official statistics on research and development expenditure, personnel and related S&T indicators. Provides the innovation and knowledge-generation base.
reports._notes: Core R&D / S&T statistical product.
reports._url_evidence: DOST download page for 'Survey Results of the 2019-2020 R&D Expenditures and Human Resources', filed under the Compendium of S&T Statistics.
reports._cadence_evidence: DOST Compendium of S&T Statistics entry is 'Survey Results of the 2019-2020 R&D Expenditures and Human Resources' — a two-year (biennial) survey cycle; page updated 08 May 2025.

reports.title: National Tax Allotment (NTA, formerly IRA) local government finance statistics
reports.description: The principal intergovernmental transfer (40% share of national internal revenue taxes) automatically released to provinces, cities, municipalities and barangays. Renamed National Tax Allotment following the Mandanas-Garcia ruling. Critical equalisation and local fiscal-capacity instrument.
reports._notes: Core subnational fiscal equalisation node (parallel to Indonesia’s DAU/DAK).
reports._url_evidence: DBM's National Tax Allotment (NTA) page, which hosts the NTA shares of LGUs and links to the DBM NTA dashboard.
reports._cadence_evidence: The DBM National Tax Allotment page is a navigation stub: no dated NTA documents, no stated frequency, only a link to the reports.dbm.gov.ph/ira2 dashboard, which returns no substantive content or update statement.

reports.title: Geothermal power capacity and generation statistics
reports.description: Installed and dependable geothermal capacity and related generation figures. The Philippines remains one of the world’s leading geothermal producers; geothermal forms a distinctive indigenous renewable component of the power mix.
reports._notes: Distinctive renewable uniqueness node.
_referenced_by: Philippine Power Statistics and energy-mix nodes
reports._cadence_evidence: Geothermal capacity/generation figures are carried inside DOE's Philippine Power Statistics, which the DOE statistics page shows as one edition per year (2023 edition released 12 Jul 2024; 2024 edition released 15 Jun 2025).

reports.title: Renewable energy project and capacity statistics (RE Act framework)
reports.description: Summary statistics on renewable-energy projects under the Renewable Energy Act of 2008 — hydropower, geothermal, wind, solar, biomass — covering potential and installed capacity.
reports._notes: Broader renewable-energy densification.
reports._cadence_evidence: The DOE renewable-energy pages show only the legal framework (RA 9513, RA 9367), department orders and circulars — no dated statistical editions and no stated release frequency for RE project/capacity statistics.

reports.title: Philippine Development Plan (PDP) and NEDA planning framework
reports.description: The medium-term national development plan (current cycle 2023–2028) and associated progress reports. Provides the overarching policy and target frame that organises statistical monitoring across sectors.
reports._notes: High-centrality national planning frame node.
_referenced_by: Almost all major statistical and programme series
Poverty, education, health and infrastructure targets
reports._cadence_evidence: pdp.neda.gov.ph presents the PDP 2023-2028 as 'the second medium-term plan' anchored on the administration's socioeconomic agenda — a six-year medium-term plan cycle; no annual progress report schedule is stated on the page.

reports.title: Crime statistics (focus crimes and crime rate)
reports.description: Official focus-crime counts (murder, homicide, rape, physical injury, theft, robbery, vehicle theft) and overall crime-rate trends. Used in security and governance analysis.
reports._notes: Core crime/security statistical product.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved the PSA OpenSTAT PX-Web table 'Levels of Index Crimes in the Philippines: 2009 - 2015'. Metadata on the page names the Philippine National Police (PNP) as the administrative-data source and lists the focus/index crime variables: murder, homicide, physical injuries, rape, robbery, theft, carnapping, cattle rustling, in number of cases. Companion tables 0103E3D1010.px (against persons) and 0103E3D1020.px (against property) sit in the same folder. pnp.gov.ph itself still returns 403.
reports._url_route: PSA OpenSTAT database folder listing (DB__3E__GD__PH/?tablelist=true) used as discovery, then the .px table page fetched directly
reports._cadence_evidence: OpenSTAT table metadata for 'Levels of Index Crimes in the Philippines: 2009-2015' states update frequency 'Annual' (PNP administrative records; last updated 07 Aug 2018).

reports.title: Port of Manila operational statistics
reports.description: Operational statistics for the country’s primary international container gateway (Manila International Container Terminal, South Harbor, North Harbor). Handles the large majority of international container trade.
reports._notes: Primary international-gateway port node.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved 'SUMMARY PORT STATISTICS - Philippine Ports Authority 2023'. It reports shipcalls, cargo throughput (272.5m MT), container traffic (7.5m TEU), passenger and RoRo traffic, broken down by PPA district including Manila/Northern Luzon, which carries roughly 36-40% of most metrics. This is PPA's own statistical release; note it is the district aggregate rather than a MICT/South Harbor/North Harbor terminal-level page, which PPA does not publish. ppa.com.ph is intermittently unfetchable (its robots.txt fails TLS verification on many attempts) - this fetch succeeded on retry.
reports._url_route: alternate hostname (bare ppa.com.ph node page proved the site fetchable) + repeated retries on the www /sites/default/files/qtr_stat/ static PDF path
reports._cadence_evidence: The PPA file is '2023 Summary Statistics' containing all four quarterly breakdowns plus a GRAND TOTAL — a full-year compilation; Manila appears only as the aggregated 'Manila/Northern Luzon' district, with no separate MICT/South Harbor release.

reports.title: Port of Cebu operational statistics
reports.description: Operational statistics for the principal Visayas port hub — major domestic inter-island and secondary international gateway.
reports._notes: Primary Visayas port node.
reports._url_evidence: Cebu Port Authority 'Statistics' page under The Cebu Port System, the official statistics section for the Port of Cebu.
reports._cadence_evidence: Cebu Port Authority statistics page is only a landing page embedding a Google Drive folder ('Open Drive Folder, STATISTIC'); no tables, dated editions or frequency statement are exposed.

reports.title: Vital statistics (births, deaths, marriages)
reports.description: Registered births, deaths and marriages. Provides the continuous demographic flow data that complements the census and population projections.
reports._notes: Core civil-registration / vital-statistics node.
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA vital statistics page shows rolling monthly provisional releases — Birth, Marriage and Death Statistics for 2025 as of 31 May 2026 (released 31 Jul 2026) and as of 30 Apr 2026 (released 26 Jun 2026) — noting 'Civil Registration is a continuous process' with monthly cut-offs.

reports.title: BSP Monetary Policy Report
reports.description: Flagship periodic monetary-policy communication document that synthesises inflation, growth, external and financial conditions. High recurring-citation value across macro analysis.
reports._notes: High-centrality central-bank communication node.
_referenced_by: CPI, national accounts, BOP and reserves
reports._cadence_evidence: BSP Advance Release Calendar lists the Monetary Policy Report with periodicity 'Quarterly'.

reports.title: Overseas Filipino Workers stock and Survey on Overseas Filipinos
reports.description: Official estimates of the number of Overseas Filipino Workers (recently ~2.19 million) and related characteristics from the Survey on Overseas Filipinos. Captures both land-based and sea-based workers and the gender composition (female majority in recent rounds).
reports._notes: Core OFW stock node — one of the defining structural features of the Philippine economy and society.
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA Survey on Overseas Filipinos releases are annual: 2024 results (16 Dec 2025), 2023 results (13 Sep 2024), 2022 results (11 Oct 2023).

reports.title: Overseas Filipino cash remittances (total and by country)
reports.description: High-frequency and annual statistics on cash remittances from overseas Filipinos, broken down by major source country. Remittances are a major stabilising component of the current account and household income.
reports._notes: High-centrality external and household-income node. Canada is a consistently ranked source country.
reports._cadence_evidence: BSP Advance Release Calendar lists Overseas Filipinos' Remittances with periodicity 'Monthly'.

reports.title: Cash remittances from Canada
reports.description: BSP-reported cash remittances originating from Canada. Recent annual figures exceed USD 1.2 billion, placing Canada among the top source countries alongside the United States, Middle East destinations, Singapore, Japan and others.
reports._notes: Explicit Canada–Philippines financial linkage node. Reflects the large Filipino diaspora in Canada (including communities where Tagalog ranks as a major non-official language).
_referenced_by: Canada–Philippines migration and labour cooperation nodes
reports._cadence_evidence: Canada is a country line inside the BSP remittances-by-source tables, which the BSP Advance Release Calendar publishes 'Monthly'; there is no separate Canada release.

reports.title: Department of Migrant Workers institutional role and deployment statistics
reports.description: Lead agency for overseas employment policy, contract processing and worker protection. Publishes deployment / contracts-processed statistics by destination, sex and type (land-based, sea-based, new hires, rehires).
reports._notes: Policy and administrative counterpart to the statistical OFW nodes.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved DMW 'OVERSEAS EMPLOYMENT STATISTICS - Landbased Deployment per Country/Destination per Type of Hiring', 2024 through January 2025, footer 'Department of Migrant Workers - Management Information and Technology Service', processed by the Strategic Planning and Management Service. Deployment is broken out by major world region and by new hires vs rehires. The dmw.gov.ph HTML statistics landing pages (/statistics, /archives/v1/statistics, /archives/ofwstat/ofwstat.html) are still JavaScript-only shells, so the underlying static statistics PDF is the only retrievable official artefact.
reports._url_route: legacy/static archive path under dmw.gov.ph/archives/ (discovered by site-scoped search), bypassing the JS-only app
reports._cadence_evidence: The DMW table is filed at /2025/Statistics/JAN/ as 'TAB 11 - Landbased Deployment by Destination (2024 Jan 2025)', i.e. a per-month folder of preliminary deployment tables; data are cumulative-to-date and flagged 'preliminary and subject to final evaluation'.

reports.title: Family Income and Expenditure Survey (FIES)
reports.description: Major household survey providing income, expenditure and inequality data. Primary source for official poverty statistics and for understanding the household-level impact of remittances.
reports._notes: Household-income densification that links remittances to welfare outcomes.
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA FIES page carries survey years 2018, 2021 and 2023 (2023 preliminary released 15 Aug 2024) — a roughly triennial survey; no explicit frequency statement on the page.

reports.title: Underemployment and quality-of-employment indicators (LFS)
reports.description: Underemployment rates and related quality-of-employment measures from the Labor Force Survey. Complements the headline unemployment rate and is relevant to the push factors behind overseas work.
reports._notes: Labour-quality node that helps explain the scale of the OFW phenomenon.
reports._cadence_evidence: Underemployment is a headline indicator of the Labor Force Survey, which the PSA 2026 Calendar of Releases schedules 12 times in the year (monthly).

reports.title: IT-BPM / BPO industry statistics and performance
reports.description: Industry statistics on the Information Technology and Business Process Management sector — revenues (recently ~USD 40+ billion), headcount (~1.8–1.9 million FTEs), global market share, and sub-sector composition (customer experience, healthcare, IT services, etc.). Philippines ranks as the world’s second-largest IT-BPM delivery geography after India.
reports._notes: High-centrality uniqueness node. Alongside OFW remittances, IT-BPM is a defining export of Philippine services and human capital.
_referenced_by: Labour Force Survey and employment analysis
reports._url_evidence: IBPAP Knowledge Hub listing industry reports including 'The Philippine IT-BPM Industry Overview (Q2 2026)' and 'Beyond $40 Billion'; note IBPAP is the named publisher but is an industry association, not a government body.
reports._cadence_evidence: IBPAP Knowledge Hub's recurring publication is 'The IT-BPM Navigator', released quarterly (Q1, Q3, Q4 2025 and Q1, Q2 2026 editions listed); other items (ESG Report, Industry Overview) carry no stated cadence.

reports.title: National Capital Region (NCR) Gross Regional Domestic Product
reports.description: Official GRDP for the National Capital Region — the dominant services and administrative core of the Philippine economy.
reports._notes: Primary urban-core regional output node.

reports.title: CALABARZON Gross Regional Domestic Product
reports.description: Official GRDP for CALABARZON — major industrial and manufacturing belt adjacent to NCR, frequently accounting for a large share of national industry output and ranking among the largest regional economies.
reports._notes: Primary industrial-belt regional output node. Together with NCR forms the Luzon economic core.

reports.title: Agriculture and fisheries production statistics
reports.description: Official value and volume of production in agriculture and fisheries. Crops (especially rice/palay) dominate; livestock, poultry and fisheries complete the sector.
reports._notes: Core primary-sector production node.
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA 2026 Calendar of Releases lists 'Value of Production in Philippine Agriculture and Fisheries' with 4 scheduled release dates, labelled Quarterly.

reports.title: Rice / palay production statistics
reports.description: Official palay (unmilled rice) production volume and related indicators. Rice remains the central food-security crop and a politically sensitive commodity; weather, irrigation and import policy strongly affect outcomes.
reports._notes: Foundational food-security crop node.
_referenced_by: CPI food component and inflation analysis
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA palay and corn estimates are issued as the 'Palay and Corn Quarterly Bulletin'; the page shows updates for Jan-Mar 2026 (15 Apr 2026) and Apr-Jun 2026 (11 Jun and 15 Jul 2026), i.e. quarterly reference periods.

reports.title: PAGASA tropical cyclone and weather monitoring products
reports.description: Official meteorological agency products on tropical cyclones, rainfall and related hazards. Provides the scientific monitoring backbone for NDRRMC response and early warning.
reports._notes: Meteorological monitoring node tightly coupled to the disaster cluster.
reports._url_evidence: PAGASA tropical cyclone section showing the live bulletin plus its product set (advisories, severe wind and storm surge impact forecasts, TC threat potential, annual reports).
reports._cadence_evidence: The PAGASA severe weather / tropical cyclone bulletin page is a live operational feed with no stated issuance schedule — bulletins appear only while a cyclone is active, so there is no discrete periodic release.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7) and applied 2026-08-19: a nominal releases_per_year so that absence keeps meaning 'one-off instrument' only - 250 encodes business-day updating (the live corpus's daily-FX convention), 365 genuinely all-days monitoring. It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

reports.title: PEZA ecozone and investment statistics
reports.description: Statistics on approved investments, employment generation, number of ecozones and export performance under the PEZA regime. Ecozones are a principal vehicle for manufacturing and IT-BPM location.
reports._notes: Key special-zone and investment-promotion node. Complements the IT-BPM cluster.
reports._cadence_evidence: peza.gov.ph shows only a static ecozone count snapshot ('419 TOTAL' as of April 2023) with no investment, employment or export series, no dated editions and no stated reporting frequency; the statistics sub-pages are not retrievable.

reports.title: Merchandise trade by major partner country
reports.description: Export and import values by principal trading partners. United States, Japan, China, Hong Kong, Korea and ASEAN partners recur as leading markets and sources; electronics dominate the commodity mix.
reports._notes: Partner-side densification of the external-trade cluster.
_referenced_by: National accounts and BOP goods account
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA International Merchandise Trade Statistics are monthly (2026 Calendar of Releases lists 12 IMTS dates); page shows Apr 2026 (29 May), May 2026 (30 Jun), Jun 2026 (30 Jul) preliminary editions with partner-country tables.

reports.title: Electronics and semiconductor trade statistics
reports.description: Trade statistics focused on electronic products — the single largest merchandise export category and a major import category as well, reflecting the country’s role in regional electronics value chains.
reports._notes: Commodity-specific trade node that links the Philippines into East Asian electronics networks.
reports._url_evidence: PSA monthly international merchandise trade release stating electronic products were the top export in June 2026 at USD 5.25 billion, 59.9 percent of total exports.
reports._cadence_evidence: Electronic products are a commodity line inside the monthly Highlights of the Philippine Export and Import (June 2026 edition: electronics 59.9% of exports, 34.8% of imports); no separate electronics release exists.

reports.title: Philippine Power Statistics (generation, capacity, consumption)
reports.description: Official statistics on installed and dependable capacity, gross generation by technology, electricity sales and consumption, and system peak demand. Coal remains the largest single source; natural gas, geothermal, hydro, solar, wind and oil-based plants complete the mix. Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao grids reported separately.
reports._notes: Core power-system statistical product. Coal-dominant with significant renewable (especially geothermal) contribution.
_referenced_by: National accounts and industrial energy analysis
reports._cadence_evidence: DOE Philippine Power Statistics appears as one edition per year — 2023 edition released 12 July 2024, 2024 edition released 15 June 2025.

reports.title: Electricity generation and capacity mix by technology
reports.description: Breakdown of installed/dependable capacity and generation by fuel/technology — coal, natural gas, oil-based, geothermal, hydro, solar, wind, biomass, storage. Highlights both the coal lock-in and the sizeable indigenous geothermal resource.
reports._notes: Structural energy-mix node.
reports._url_evidence: DOE Philippine Power Statistics page listing 'Installed and Dependable Capacity per Grid and per technology, 2003-2024' and 'Gross Generation per Grid and per technology, 2003-2024'.
reports._cadence_evidence: The capacity/generation-by-technology breakdown is part of Philippine Power Statistics on the DOE energy-statistics page, which lists only the 2023 (rel. 12 Jul 2024) and 2024 (rel. 15 Jun 2025) editions — annual.

reports.title: Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) statistics
reports.publisher: Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD)
reports.description: Official performance and coverage statistics for the national conditional cash-transfer and human-capital program. Tracks household beneficiaries, self-sufficiency exits, education and health outcomes of monitored children.
reports._notes: Flagship social-protection node. Institutionalised by RA 11310.
reports._cadence_evidence: DSWD publishes the 4Ps Program Implementation Report quarterly — e.g. 'Second Quarter Program Implementation Report' (Apr-Jun 2025, published Jul 2025) and Fourth Quarter PIR, with quarter-on-quarter comparisons.

reports.title: Higher education statistics (enrolment, institutions, graduates)
reports.description: Official statistics on higher-education institutions, enrolment, graduates and faculty. Provides the human-capital supply side that feeds both the domestic labour market and the OFW / IT-BPM talent pipelines.
reports._notes: Core higher-education statistical product.
_referenced_by: Labor Force Survey and skills analysis

reports.title: Basic education statistics (DepEd)
reports.description: Enrolment, completion and related indicators for elementary and secondary education. Complements the higher-education series and links to 4Ps education conditions.
reports._notes: Foundational basic-education node.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved a DepEd page that loads and reports official basic education enrolment: 27,232,095 enrolled in formal basic education as of 15 Nov 2021, +3.83% year on year, with public/private transfer flows and Alternative Learning System enrolment (239,616). Caveat: this is DepEd's own enrolment statistics announcement, not a standing statistics product - deped.gov.ph's actual data pages (/resources/facts-and-figures/, /category/facts-and-figures/datasets/, /enrollment/, and all /wp-content/uploads/ PDFs) still return 403, and only dated post URLs are fetchable.
reports._url_route: alternate URL shape on deped.gov.ph - dated post paths (/YYYY/MM/DD/...) are served while category, resource and wp-content paths return 403
reports._cadence_evidence: The URL is a single dated DepEd press release (18 November 2021) on SY 2021-2022 enrolment; it promises 'a more granular enrolment analysis after November 30' but states no regular publication schedule.

reports.title: PhilHealth coverage and claims statistics
reports.description: Membership, coverage, claims and financial performance statistics of the national health-insurance programme. Central instrument of health financing and universal-health-coverage policy.
reports._notes: Core health-financing node.
reports._cadence_evidence: PhilHealth 'Stats and Charts' exists in a full-year and a first-semester edition each year (SNC 2023, SNC 2023 1st Sem, SNC 2024 covering 1 Jan-31 Dec 2024 updated 23 May 2025, SNC 2024 1st Sem, SNC 2025) — two editions per year.

reports.title: Key health and nutrition indicators
reports.description: Official indicators on child nutrition (stunting, wasting, underweight), vaccination, maternal care, mortality and leading causes of death. Provides the outcome side of the health system.
reports._notes: Outcome-side health and nutrition node.
reports._cadence_evidence: The node bundles NDHS, National Nutrition Survey and vital-statistics indicators from PSA/DOH/FNRI; the PSA NDHS page gives no survey years and no stated periodicity, and no single frequency covers the bundle.

reports.title: BARMM (Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao) economic and statistical profile
reports.description: Regional accounts, growth and sectoral performance for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region. Captures the distinctive political-economy and development trajectory of the autonomous region within Mindanao.
reports._notes: Key autonomous-region node. Distinct institutional and development path inside the Philippine archipelago.
reports._url_evidence: PSA RSSO-BARMM Regional Accounts (GRDP/GRDE) page showing the 2025 BARMM GRDP infographic and the release 'BARMM's economy expands by 5.0 percent in 2025'.
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA-BARMM regional accounts page shows one GRDP release per year — 'BARMM's economy expands by 5.0 percent in 2025' dated 23 April 2026, with a 2025 GRDP infographic; the PSA 2026 calendar lists Regional Accounts with 1 release date (Annual).

reports.title: National Government fiscal operations and budget statistics
reports.publisher: Department of Budget and Management / Bureau of the Treasury
reports.description: Official statistics on national government revenues, expenditures, financing and fiscal balance. Core public-finance series used in macro and debt analysis.
reports._notes: Primary fiscal-operations node.
reports._url_evidence: Bureau of the Treasury 'National Government Cash Operations' page with revenue, expenditure, financing, debt service and cash budget assessment tables back to 1986.
reports._cadence_evidence: Bureau of the Treasury National Government Cash Operations Report is published monthly (latest posting July 2026 for June 2026 data; page last updated 23 July 2026) alongside annual aggregates back to 1986.

reports.title: National Government outstanding debt statistics
reports.description: Outstanding domestic and external debt of the national government, with periodic updates on composition and ratios. High-visibility macro-fiscal indicator.
reports._notes: Core public-debt node.
reports._url_evidence: Bureau of the Treasury 'National Government Debt' page with NG outstanding debt (monthly 1993-2025, annual 1986-2025) and NG debt indicators in Excel and PDF.

reports.title: Annual Survey of Philippine Business and Industry – Manufacturing
reports.description: Detailed structural statistics on manufacturing establishments, employment, revenue and expenses from the ASPBI. Complements the national-accounts manufacturing GVA series.
reports._notes: Structural manufacturing densification node.
reports._cadence_evidence: The Annual Survey of Philippine Business and Industry is an annual designated statistical activity (2022 round conducted April 2023 with 2022 as reference period); manufacturing is one of its sector volumes.

reports.title: Tourism statistics (arrivals, receipts, TDGVA)
reports.description: International visitor arrivals, tourism receipts and Tourism Direct Gross Value Added. Captures both foreign tourists and returning overseas Filipinos (balikbayans).
reports._notes: Core tourism statistical product. Canada appears among notable source markets.
reports._url_evidence: PSA Philippine Tourism Satellite Account page reporting 2025 TDGVA of PhP 2.27 trillion, 8.1 percent of GDP, and tourism employment.
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA tourism page shows the Philippine Tourism Satellite Account / TDGVA released once a year — 2023 data (18 Jun 2024), 2024 data (19 Jun 2025), 2025 data (28 May 2026); no monthly arrivals series is published here.

reports.title: Philippine financial system resources and structure
reports.description: Total resources of banks and non-bank financial institutions, with breakdowns by universal/commercial, thrift, digital, rural/cooperative banks and NBFIs. Provides the size and structure of the formal financial system.
reports._notes: Core financial-system size and structure node.
reports._cadence_evidence: BSP Advance Release Calendar lists 'Total Resources of the Philippine Financial System' with periodicity 'Monthly'.

reports.title: Construction statistics and GVA
reports.description: Construction-sector output, employment and related indicators. Important cyclical and investment-related series.
reports._notes: Construction densification of the industry cluster.
reports._url_evidence: PSA 'Construction Statistics from Approved Building Permits' series landing page with the latest monthly release, Excel tables and technical notes.
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA Construction Statistics from Approved Building Permits is monthly — May 2026 edition (20 Jul 2026), April 2026 (18 Jun 2026), each comparing May 2025r, April 2026r and May 2026p.

reports.title: Gross Fixed Capital Formation statistics
reports.description: Investment-side national-accounts series covering construction, durable equipment and other capital formation. Links fiscal, private investment and growth analysis.
reports._notes: Primary investment/GFCF node.
reports._cadence_evidence: Gross Fixed Capital Formation is the expenditure side of the National Accounts, whose release calendar has 4 quarterly dates (Jan/May/Aug/Nov) plus a revised annual national accounts release (08 Apr 2026).

reports.title: CPI by major commodity group and regional inflation
reports.description: Detailed CPI breakdowns (food, housing, transport, etc.) and regional inflation rates that complement the headline CPI series.
reports._notes: Price-detail densification.
_referenced_by: Headline CPI and BSP inflation targeting

reports.title: Philippine Digital Economy Satellite Account (PDESA)
reports.description: Official satellite account measuring the size and contribution of the digital economy (digital infrastructure, e-commerce, digital content/media, government digital services). Recent figures put digital GVA around 9–10 % of GDP and employment in the tens of millions.
reports._notes: High-value digital-economy measurement node. Complements the IT-BPM industry statistics.

reports.title: E-commerce component of the digital economy
reports.description: E-commerce share of digital-economy output and especially employment (largest employment component in recent PDESA releases).
reports._notes: Employment-heavy digital sub-node.
reports._url_evidence: PSA Philippine Digital Economy Satellite Account page showing total E-commerce at 32.2 percent of digital economy GVA and 75.8 percent of digital economy employment in 2025.
reports._cadence_evidence: The Philippine Digital Economy Satellite Account, which carries the e-commerce component, is released once a year in late April — 2023 data (25 Apr 2024), 2024 data (29 Apr 2025), 2025 data (30 Apr 2026).

reports.title: External debt statistics
reports.description: Outstanding external debt (public and private), by creditor type and maturity. Complements the national-government debt series and the BOP/IIP.
reports._notes: External-debt densification of the external-sector cluster.

reports.title: Monetary aggregates and banking statistics
reports.description: Money supply, credit and related banking indicators that complement the financial-system resources series and feed monetary-policy analysis.
reports._notes: Monetary densification of the central-bank cluster.
reports._cadence_evidence: BSP Advance Release Calendar lists the Depository Corporations Survey (money supply/credit aggregates) with periodicity 'Monthly'.

reports.title: International Investment Position
reports.description: Stock measure of external financial assets and liabilities. Complements the flow BOP and the external-debt series.
reports._notes: Stock-side external-accounts node.

reports.title: Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and climate-policy framework
reports.description: Philippine NDC under the Paris Agreement, targeting substantial GHG reduction relative to business-as-usual. Continuously cited in energy, transport, agriculture and LULUCF policy discussions.
reports._notes: Core climate-policy frame node.
reports._url_evidence: The Philippines' NDC as submitted to the UNFCCC, stating a 75 percent GHG emissions reduction and avoidance for 2020-2030 (2.71 percent unconditional, 72.29 percent conditional).
reports._cadence_evidence: The document is the Philippines' Nationally Determined Contribution communicated to the UNFCCC on 15 April 2021 covering 2020-2030 — a single submitted instrument under Decision 1/CP.21, not a periodic statistical release.

reports.title: Greenhouse gas inventory and emissions statistics
reports.description: National GHG inventory results by sector (energy dominant; LULUCF as net sink). Provides the empirical base for NDC tracking.
reports._notes: Emissions-side climate node.
reports._url_evidence: Climate Change Commission NICCDIES GHG inventory page describing the Philippine GHG Inventory Management and Reporting System and the sectoral inventories (energy, IPPU, AFOLU, waste).
reports._cadence_evidence: NICCDIES GHG inventory page lists national inventories for 2010 (completed 2019), 2015 and 2020 (completed 2023, published early 2024) — five-year inventory years, feeding the first Biennial Update Report.

reports.title: Forest cover and forestry sector statistics
reports.publisher: Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR)
reports.description: Land classification, forest cover, production/protection forest, and related forestry production and management statistics. Forests are treated as a net carbon sink in the NDC.
reports._notes: Core forest/LULUCF statistical node.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved PSA release (20 Dec 2024, ref 2024-203) reporting Philippine forest cover from the Land Asset Accounts under the SEEA 2012 Central Framework: 6.91 million ha open plus closed forest in 2020 = 23.4% of land area, +2.9% on 2015; closed forest 2.22m ha (+9.3%), open forest 4.69m ha (+0.1%), built-up 1.03m ha (+20.6%), with regional contributions and links to five SDG forest indicators. DENR's forestry.denr.gov.ph still fails robots.txt with a TLS certificate-verification error on every path tried.
reports._url_route: substitute official publisher (PSA land/forest accounts) after DENR FMB remained TLS/robots-blocked
reports._cadence_evidence: The 20 December 2024 release (ref 2024-203) states it 'marks the PSA's first attempt to compile the Land Asset Accounts of the Philippines' — a one-time pilot study output with no announced repeat schedule.

reports.title: Population projections
reports.description: Official population projections (recently to 2035, with national total approaching ~124 million). Provides the forward demographic frame for planning, labour and social-protection analysis.
reports._notes: Forward-looking demographic node.
reports._cadence_evidence: PSA projection rounds are census-based and issued once per census: 1995 CBPP (08 Dec 2006), 2000 CBPP (04 Apr 2006), 2010 CBPP (09 Aug 2016), 2015 CBPP (04 Oct 2019), 2020 CBPP (13 Jan 2026) — roughly every five years.

_status: verified
_note: Deepest wiring pass yet on the Philippines' unlinked-node backlog (61/68 unlinked as of this round's start). PSA's technical-notes pages were unusually forthcoming about classification standards (PSIC/ISIC, PSCC/HS, PCOICOP/COICOP) and SNA 2008 adoption; BSP's own primer PDFs supplied the BPM6/SDDS/WEO bridges. Two new classification nodes minted (PSIC, PSCC) since PSA's own industrial and commodity classifications sit between the national series and the UN standards they're patterned after. meta.source: research round 2026-09-11 — Poland. Thomas: “read the handoff and then begin to Research Poland and add as many nodes and edges as you can.”
meta.note:
POLAND, FIRST ROUND OF ITS OWN. RESULT: 25 nodes, 30 dependencies, 1 relation, 5 dropped notes.

WHY THE STARTING POINT WAS NOT WHAT THE COVERAGE WORKBOOK SUGGESTED. HANDOFF 085 filed Poland under “narrow and complete” — 8 nodes, zero orphans, the EU-chain rounds having wired every node they minted. That reading held up: the Eurostat ESMS chain for Poland (HICP hi4, LFS employ_simslfs, national accounts na10 and nama_10_gdp) is genuinely finished, and a probe of 26 further Eurostat dataset codes under three national-metadata suffixes found NOTHING ELSE PUBLISHED for PL. So the yield was never going to come from Eurostat. It came from three places the corpus had not opened at all: NBP (no node before this round), the classification layer (PKD, KZiS, PKWiU, PKOB, KST — and, behind them, NACE Rev. 2 and ISCO-08, which the corpus did not have either despite 21 EU countries in the graph), and the statutory layer (four Polish Acts, plus the annual survey programme that Article 18 of the 1995 statistics law produces).

THE ROUTE, AND IT IS THE REUSABLE PART OF THIS ROUND. Every Polish host is 403 at the container's egress proxy and the bridge VM has no network at all, so the only way in was Thomas's Chrome. Chrome reads HTML fine but the extension is refused on the built-in PDF viewer (“Permission denied for reading page content on this domain”), and most of what matters here is PDF. What works: on a page of the publisher's own origin, a same-origin `fetch` of the PDF into a Blob plus a synthetic `<a download>` click puts the bytes in the user's Downloads folder, which `device_request_folder_access` then makes readable to `pdftotext` and `pypdf` on the bridge VM. THE TRAP: Chrome allows ONE automatic download per tab per origin and silently blocks the rest — no error reaches the tool, the JS reports 200 and the right byte count, and the file simply never lands. A fresh tab per PDF fixes it. Second trap: the download must be the LAST action in a browser_batch, because a `navigate` immediately after tears down the blob before the save commits. Six PDFs came across this way, the largest 23 MB.

THE OTHER READING LESSON, and it changed which quotes are gradeable: the Statistical Yearbook is bilingual in FACING COLUMNS, and `pdftotext -layout` interleaves Polish and English on every output line, so every English sentence looks shattered. `pypdf` reads it in column order and the English comes out whole. Both readings were taken; every span quoted from that volume was checked against the pypdf one. This is the “a PDF is read THREE ways and the best reading wins” rule meeting a layout rather than a line break.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. The COICOP citation in the yearbook's general notes names no edition and is dropped `no-document`, matching Thomas's 2026-09-08 ruling rather than re-opening it. The PKWiU upstream is dropped for the same class of reason — “international classifications and nomenclatures” names nothing. The Ministry of Finance layer is untouched because www.gov.pl is refused by the Chrome extension and unreachable everywhere else; that is a routing fact, not a corpus fact, and it is written up in `_dropped`. The Foreign Trade Statistics node is one verified title away and is the single highest-value thing left on the table.

reports.title: NACE Rev. 2 — Statistical Classification of Economic Activities in the European Community
title_aliases: Statistical Classification of Economic Activities in the European Community
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: The EU's statutory industry classification, established by Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006 and derived from ISIC. Every EU member state's national activity classification is built on it; Poland's PKD 2007 is the first one wired here. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round — the corpus had ISIC, NAICS, ANZSIC and CPA but no NACE node at all, despite 21 EU countries in the graph.
reports.cadence_note: Revised about once a generation (Rev. 1 1990, Rev. 1.1 2002, Rev. 2 2006, Rev. 2.1 2023); 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO-08)
reports.description: The ILO's occupational classification, fourth iteration after ISCO-58, ISCO-68 and ISCO-88, published 2008. National occupational classifications are routinely built on it; Poland's KZiS is the first one wired here. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Revised roughly every twenty years; 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: Classification of Types of Constructions (CC)
reports.publisher: Statistical Office of the European Communities (Eurostat)
reports.description: Eurostat's classification of building and civil-engineering works, issued 1997/1998 and adopted as the basis for several national construction classifications, Poland's PKOB among them. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round. Eurostat's RAMON page for it is gone; the URL is the Commission's own Interoperable Europe catalogue entry.
reports.cadence_note: Not revised since issue; 0.05 is the nominal once-a-generation rate the corpus uses for standards.

reports.title: OECD Benchmark Definition of Foreign Direct Investment 2008: Fourth Edition
title_aliases: OECD Benchmark Definition of Foreign Direct Investment
reports.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
reports.description: The OECD's standard for compiling foreign direct investment statistics, fourth edition, aligned with BPM6. Named by NBP as one of six international standards the Polish balance of payments is compiled to. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Four editions since 1983; 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: External Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users (2013)
reports.publisher: Inter-Agency Task Force on Finance Statistics / International Monetary Fund
reports.description: The TFFS external-debt compilation guide, 2013 edition, superseding the 2003 edition and updated for BPM6. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round off NBP's standards footnote, which cites it as “External Debt Statistics 2014” — a year the IMF's own page does not carry, which is why the Polish edge is B.
reports.cadence_note: Two editions, 2003 and 2013; 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: International Reserves and Foreign Currency Liquidity: Guidelines for a Data Template
reports.description: The IMF's reserves data template guidelines, the standard behind the SDDS reserves template. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round off NBP's standards footnote.
reports.cadence_note: Revised occasionally (2001, 2013); 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: Combined Nomenclature (CN)
reports.description: The EU's goods nomenclature for customs and external-trade statistics, built on the WCO's Harmonized System and reissued each year by a Commission Implementing Regulation under Council Regulation (EEC) No 2658/87. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round; Statistics Poland groups foreign-trade goods by it.
reports.cadence_note: A new annual version is published each autumn for the following calendar year.

reports.title: Regulation (EU) No 692/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council concerning European statistics on tourism
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: The EU instrument defining tourism statistics and the transmission programme for them. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round: the Statistical Yearbook's tourism chapter takes its definition of “tourism” from it by name.

reports.title: Directive 2009/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on statistical returns in respect of carriage of goods and passengers by sea
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: The EU instrument governing maritime transport statistics. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round: the Statistical Yearbook says its seaport cargo, ship-traffic and passenger tables follow it.

reports.title: Ustawa z dnia 29 czerwca 1995 r. o statystyce publicznej
title_aliases: ustawy z dnia 29 czerwca 1995 r. o statystyce publicznej
reports.description: Poland's law on official statistics (Dz.U. 1995 nr 88 poz. 439, consolidated Dz.U. 2026 poz. 851). It constitutes the official statistics service, defines statistical confidentiality, and in Article 18 is the enabling provision for the annual Programme of Statistical Surveys of Official Statistics. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.

reports.title: Ustawa z dnia 29 sierpnia 1997 r. o Narodowym Banku Polskim
reports.description: The Act on Narodowy Bank Polski (Dz.U. 1997 nr 140 poz. 938, consolidated Dz.U. 2022 poz. 2025). Article 3 sets price stability as NBP's basic objective and adds financial-stability tasks; the Act also obliges NBP to compile the balance of payments and the international investment position and to report on them to Parliament and the Council of Ministers. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round. The English alias is the name NBP itself uses in its own English publications, which is where it was read.

reports.title: Ustawa z dnia 27 lipca 2002 r. Prawo dewizowe
reports.description: Poland's Foreign Exchange Act (Dz.U. 2002 nr 141 poz. 1178, consolidated Dz.U. 2022 poz. 309). Together with the Act on NBP it is the source of the reporting obligation that feeds the Polish balance of payments. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round; both aliases are read in NBP's own English methodological notes.

reports.title: Ustawa z dnia 23 grudnia 1994 r. o Najwyższej Izbie Kontroli

Article 7(1)(1) obliges NIK to submit to the Sejm an analysis of the execution of the state budget and monetary policy guidelines. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round; the English alias is NIK's own title for its English translation of the Act.

reports.title: Polska Klasyfikacja Działalności 2007 (PKD 2007)

reports.cadence_note: Successive versions track the NACE revisions (PKD 2004, PKD 2007, PKD 2025); 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: Klasyfikacja Zawodów i Specjalności (KZiS)
reports.publisher: Minister Pracy i Polityki Społecznej / Główny Urząd Statystyczny (GUS)
reports.description: Poland's classification of occupations and specialisations, derived from ISCO-08 and introduced on 1 January 2015 by the Regulation of the Minister of Labour and Social Policy of 7 August 2014. Used to group councillors, paid employees and their earnings, and the unemployed. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round off the Statistical Yearbook's general notes.
reports.cadence_note: Reissued when ISCO is revised or the occupational structure changes; 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

title_aliases: Polish Classification of Goods and Services
reports.description: Poland's product classification, introduced on 1 January 2016 by the Regulation of the Council of Ministers of 4 September 2015, replacing PKWiU 2008. The Statistical Yearbook says only that it was compiled on the basis of international classifications and nomenclatures without naming one, so no upstream edge is minted from that sentence. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Successive versions roughly every seven years (2004, 2008, 2015); 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.cadence_note: Not revised since introduction; 0.05 is the nominal once-a-generation rate the corpus uses for standards.

reports.title: Klasyfikacja Środków Trwałych 2016 (KŚT 2016)

reports.cadence_note: Reissued about once a decade (KST 2010, KST 2016); 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

title_aliases: Statistical Yearbook of the Republic of Poland
reports.description: Poland's flagship annual statistical compendium, bilingual Polish/English, running to about 745 pages. reports.title: Narodowy Spis Powszechny Ludności i Mieszkań 2021

reports.cadence_note: Decennial (2002, 2011, 2021); 0.1 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: Flash estimate of the consumer price index

title_aliases: Programme of statistical surveys of public statistics
reports.description: The annual Programme of Statistical Surveys of Official Statistics, issued each year as a Regulation of the Council of Ministers under Article 18 of the 1995 law on official statistics. It enumerates every survey Polish official statistics will run in the year, its data sources and its respondents — which is why Eurostat's Polish national accounts metadata points at it for the detailed source list. Editions 2012 to 2027 are published on GUS's BIP. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: One programme per calendar year, adopted the preceding December and amended in-year by further regulations.

reports.title: Balance of payments
reports.description: Poland's balance-of-payments statistics, compiled by the central bank from direct reporting by resident entities supplemented by Statistics Poland's surveys and administrative data. NBP publishes a monthly balance of payments and a fuller quarterly one; this node is the monthly series. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round off NBP's own methodological notes.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly. NBP: “Monthly b.o.p. is published 44 working days following the end of a respective month.” A fuller quarterly balance of payments follows three months after the reference quarter.

reports.title: Inflation Report
reports.publisher: Narodowy Bank Polski (NBP) — Monetary Policy Council
reports.description: The Monetary Policy Council's assessment of macroeconomic developments influencing inflation, carrying the NECMOD-based projection of inflation and GDP prepared by NBP's Economic Analysis and Research Department. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Three times a year — March, July and November.

reports.title: Financial Stability Report
reports.publisher: Narodowy Bank Polski (NBP) — Financial Stability Department
reports.description: NBP's systemic-risk assessment of the Polish financial system, with stress tests and recommendations, published under the financial-stability task the Act on NBP gives the bank. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Twice a year — June and December.

reports.title: Monetary Policy Guidelines
reports.publisher: Narodowy Bank Polski (NBP) — Monetary Policy Council
reports.description: The monetary policy guidelines the Monetary Policy Council adopts each year and presents to the Sejm alongside the Council of Ministers' draft Budget, as Article 227(6) of the Constitution requires. They set the inflation target and the strategy for the year ahead, and their execution is what NIK audits alongside the state budget. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, adopted in September for the following calendar year.

reports.title: Analysis of the execution of the state budget and monetary policy guidelines
reports.publisher: Najwyższa Izba Kontroli (NIK) / Supreme Audit Office
reports.description: NIK's annual analysis of how the state budget and the monetary policy guidelines were executed, presented to the Sejm by the President of NIK and required of it by Article 7(1)(1) of the Act on the Supreme Audit Office. It is submitted together with NIK's opinion on discharging the Council of Ministers. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Annual; presented to the Sejm in June for the preceding budget year.

relations.basis: The Act on the Supreme Audit Office, Article 7(1)(1), makes the monetary policy guidelines one of the two things NIK's annual analysis reports on: “The Supreme Audit Office shall submit to the Sejm: 1) analysis of the execution of the state budget and monetary policy guidelines”. NIK's own parliament-relations page says the same from the other side: “Every year NIK President presents the Sejm with the Analysis of the execution of the state budget and monetary policy guidelines and the NIK activity report.” Recorded as a relation rather than a dependency because assurance is not derivation — the guidelines gain no content from being audited. The state-budget half of the same obligation has no node to point at: the Council of Ministers' budget-execution report is published on gov.pl, which was unreachable from every route this session had.

_dropped.why: The Statistical Yearbook's General Note 7(4) names COICOP as one of the classifications it groups by — “the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP), on the basis of which final consumption expenditure of products (goods and services) of the households sector as well as expenditure on consumer goods and services of households (also adopted for compiling price indices) are grouped” — and names NO EDITION. That is exactly the case Thomas closed on 2026-09-08 when he dropped iq-cpi, tn-ins-cpi and ma-hcp-ipc -> un-coicop-2018 for the same reason, and PLAYBOOK 7d records it as a decided call. Recorded here rather than wired so the next Poland round does not re-derive it: the citation is real, the edition is not stated, and the corpus models COICOP editions as separate nodes.

PKWiU 2015 is the one Polish classification in the Statistical Yearbook's General Notes whose derivation is stated without a target: “PKWiU 2015, compiled on the basis of international classifications and nomenclatures, was introduced on 1 January 2016”. PKWiU is in fact built on the EU's CPA, which IS in the corpus as `cpa` — but the yearbook does not say so, and knowing it is not evidence. A round with the PKWiU introducing regulation (Dz.U. 2015 poz. 1676) in hand should close this; its enacting formula and explanatory notes are the place the CPA link would be stated.

NBP's methodological notes name the largest single input to the Polish current account by a title that is NBP's, not GUS's: “The main source of data on goods in the Polish balance of payments is Foreign Trade Statistics (FTS) compiled by the Statistics Poland on the basis of INTRASTAT declarations (for intra-European Union trade) as well as from the Single Administrative Documents, SAD (for extra EU trade)”. The sentence is first-party, exact and would carry an A — what is missing is the node, and minting one titled “Foreign Trade Statistics” would break the rule that a node carries the PUBLISHER's own title for the artefact. GUS's English foreign-trade pages redirected to its new portal (new.stat.gov.pl) mid-session and the release's own title was not read, so the node was not minted. _dropped.why: ROUTING FINDING, worth recording because it shaped what this round could do. Of the Polish hosts, nbp.pl, stat.gov.pl, bip.stat.gov.pl, www.nik.gov.pl, isap.sejm.gov.pl and ec.europa.eu were all reachable in Thomas's Chrome; www.gov.pl and finanse-arch.mf.gov.pl were refused by the extension with “Navigation to this domain is not allowed”. Neither the cloud container nor the bridge VM has egress to any Polish host at all — the container's proxy answers 403 to CONNECT for every one of them and the bridge VM has no network. So the whole Ministry of Finance layer is unresearched rather than absent: the Public Finance Sector Debt Management Strategy, the state budget execution report NIK audits, and the Medium-Term Fiscal-Structural Plan are all on www.gov.pl. A future round needs either a gov.pl permission in the Chrome extension or a different network.

Neither half reaches the naming bar on its own, and PLAYBOOK 7a's chart-caption rule turns on the SOURCE LINE, which here is agency-only. The full phrase “Labour Force Survey” appears nowhere in the report; grep confirmed. A B edge could be argued for; it was left out rather than argued.

dependencies.basis: The Municipal Affairs Population List is based on municipal census results or federal census data, and federal census counts are used where a municipality has not run its own census.
Alberta's municipal population estimation model is built on a standard methodology drawing on provincial administrative data together with federal government sources, specifically the federal census.

LFS population control totals start as a base estimate derived from the census, then updated monthly for births, deaths and migration. Every five years the entire series back to the previous census is re-weighted on the new counts.

Base instruction grants are allocated from an averaged enrolment figure for each school authority — a three-year Weighted Moving Average up to 2024/25, replaced by the Adjusted Enrolment Method from 2025/26.

_slice: Alberta provincial social and benefit programs
_note: Alberta's income-tested social programmes turn out to have a much tidier shape than expected, because in 2025-26 the province collapsed almost all of its benefit indexation onto a single parameter. From 2023 to 2025, AISH, Income Support and the Alberta Seniors Benefit were each separately indexed to the Alberta all-items CPI published by Statistics Canada, with an explicit October-to-September averaging formula written into each policy manual. Bill 32 (Financial Statutes Amendment Act, 2024) replaced that with the 'Alberta escalator' defined in s. 44.2 of the Alberta Personal Income Tax Act - the lesser of 2% and the same Alberta CPI change - and then had the AISH Act, the Income and Employment Supports Act and the Seniors Benefit Act all point at that one definition. The result is a hub-and-spoke pattern: statcan-cpi feeds the Alberta escalator, which feeds AISH/ADAP rates, Income Support core essential and core shelter rates, the Alberta Child and Family Benefit parameters, and the Alberta Seniors Benefit cash benefit, with the 2% cap biting in both 2025 and 2026. Two things sit outside that hub and are the more interesting findings. First, accommodation charges are deliberately carved out of every benefit's escalator and pinned instead to the maximum charge set under the Continuing Care Act, so the AISH modified living allowance, Income Support for continuing care residents, and the Seniors Benefit Supplementary Accommodation Benefit all depend on an Alberta Health price table. Second, the Seniors Benefit Act escalates its non-deductible income amount by the federal Canada Pension Plan Pension Index, not the Alberta escalator, and writes federal OAS and GIS maximums directly into its benefit formulas. Health-side programmes (Alberta Adult Health Benefit, Alberta Aids to Daily Living) are the opposite case: their income thresholds carry no documented indexation rule at all, and the AAHB table has not moved since 2015 - those non-edges are recorded in _dropped. This slice runs slightly above the suggested edge count because the escalator reform gave several programmes two separately documented indexation edges (the pre-2026 direct CPI rule and the post-2026 escalator rule); both are kept because both are stated in the source documents.

Indexing was introduced under Bill 26 starting January 2019, paused 2020-2022, and restored beginning January 2023 under the Inflation Relief Act; the January 1, 2026 adjustment raised the maximum AISH living allowance from $1,901 to $1,940/month.

reports.title: Alberta Escalator (Alberta Personal Income Tax Act indexation factor)
reports.description: The annual indexation factor defined in section 44.2 of the Alberta Personal Income Tax Act and published each year by Treasury Board and Finance alongside the personal income tax bracket table. For years after 2025 it is either a percentage prescribed by regulation before January 1, or, absent a prescription, the lesser of 2% and the year-over-year change in the Alberta Consumer Price Index over the 12 months ending September 30. It is the single escalator that now drives Alberta tax brackets and credit amounts, the Alberta Child and Family Benefit, and AISH/ADAP benefit rates.
reports.cadence_note: One factor per taxation year, effective January 1; published in the personal income tax bracket table and in the Budget tax plan.

release_schedule.rule: If no percentage is prescribed by regulation by January 1, a CPI-derived formula (capped at 2%) applies automatically.
release_schedule.note: A 2026 amendment to this section exists but is not yet in force as of this audit — worth rechecking before relying on this rule going forward.

The benefit year runs July to June and payments are issued quarterly by the CRA on Alberta's behalf.

entries.covers: ACFB maximum amounts and thresholds for benefit year July 2025-June 2026
ACFB maximum amounts and thresholds for benefit year July 2026-June 2027
