release_schedule.note: The alberta.ca ACFB page currently publishes maximum benefit amounts and income thresholds for two consecutive 'benefit years' (July 2025-June 2026 and July 2026-June 2027), with different dollar figures for each, showing the figures are updated annually to coincide with the start of each new benefit year on July 1. No explicit indexation statute or fixed publication calendar was found on the page itself, so this is inferred from the observed year-over-year pattern rather than a stated rule. Payment dates (the quarterly disbursement schedule of Aug/Nov/Feb/May) are a separate, unrelated cadence from the annual update of maximum amounts/thresholds, which is what this corpus entry tracks.

reports.title: Alberta Seniors Benefit maximum benefit amounts, income thresholds and phase-out rates
reports.publisher: Alberta Assisted Living and Social Services (Seniors Financial Assistance)
reports.description: The annual schedule of maximum Alberta Seniors Benefit amounts by accommodation category and marital status, the income guideline thresholds, and the phase-out rates applied per dollar of non-deductible income. It also governs the Supplementary Accommodation Benefit for seniors in continuing care homes. Amounts take effect at the start of each July-to-June benefit year and are calculated from the applicant's previous calendar year income as reported to the Canada Revenue Agency.
reports.cadence_note: Benefit year runs July 1 to June 30 (the current schedule is stated as 'Effective July 1, 2026'); benefits are paid monthly.

release_schedule.note: No published forward calendar and no statute text specifying exact review dates was found on alberta.ca; the schedule is inferred from the Open Government dataset's release history, which shows new editions of the 'Alberta Seniors Benefit thresholds rates and percentages' document released consistently around January 1 and July 1 each year since at least 2023 (and July-only in 2020-2022, January-only in 2019). The alberta.ca program page confirms current thresholds are stated 'as of July 1, 2026'. The July 2026 edition (created 2026-07-09 on open.alberta.ca) is the current/active one as of the 2026-08-11 research date, so the next expected editions are January 2027 and July 2027. Occasional additional interim updates have also occurred (e.g. April 2024, April 2026), so mid-cycle revisions are possible.

reports.title: Alberta Income Support core benefit rate schedule (core essential and core shelter)
reports.publisher: Alberta Assisted Living and Social Services
reports.description: The schedule of Income Support core essential payments (including the comforts allowance) and core shelter payments by household composition, set under the Income and Employment Supports Act and the Income Support, Training and Health Benefits Regulation, together with the supplementary benefit maximums. Rates apply to both the Expected to Work (ETW) and Barriers to Full Employment (BFE) client streams and are revised effective January 1 each year through the 'Benefit Rate Adjustments' policy in the Income and Employment Supports Policy Manual.
reports.cadence_note: Rate adjustment takes effect January 1 each year; the manual's Core Shelter Rate Adjustment and Core Essential Rate Adjustment pages carry the year-specific tables.

entries.covers: Annual indexation of Core Essential and Core Shelter benefit rates

release_schedule.rule: Core Essential and Core Shelter benefit amounts are indexed annually, effective January 1 each year, to the Alberta Consumer Price Index (with increases capped at a maximum of 2 per cent under Alberta's indexation legislation, the "Alberta Escalator"). Note: Core Shelter-Social Housing rate increases instead take effect at each recipient's individual Annual Rent Review rather than on January 1.
release_schedule.note: Alberta resumed CPI indexing of income supports effective Jan 1, 2023; most recently confirmed indexation events occurred Jan 1, 2024 (4.25%) and Jan 1, 2026 (2%, per Maytree). New provincial legislation caps annual indexation at a maximum of 2%. The base URL alberta.ca/income-support itself has no calendar or rate table; rate figures and the indexing rule are documented on secondary/advocacy sites citing Alberta government sources (Maytree, enoughforall.ca) rather than a single official calendar page.

reports.title: Continuing Care Resident Accommodation Charges (maximum charges, types A and B)
reports.description: The table of maximum daily resident accommodation charges that type A and type B continuing care homes may charge, set by the Alberta government under the Continuing Care (Ministerial) Regulation. It also fixes the Alternate Level of Care charge for hospital patients awaiting a continuing care space. These charges are the accommodation component of the AISH/ADAP modified living allowance and of Income Support benefits for clients in continuing care, and they set the ceiling for the Alberta Seniors Benefit Supplementary Accommodation Benefit.
reports.cadence_note: Adjusted annually for inflation; the 2026 adjustment took effect August 1, 2026 (a 1.8% increase) rather than on the previous April 1 cycle, so the effective date has moved between years.

release_schedule.rule: Effective August 1 [each year], the maximum accommodation charges will increase ... to reflect the annual inflation adjustment.

entries.covers: Annual inflation adjustment to maximum resident accommodation charges (Type A and B)

release_schedule.note: Alberta.ca states the current August 1, 2026 adjustment already took effect (1.8% increase, 'annual inflation adjustment'), confirmed by Alberta Continuing Care Association news post stating 'the annual adjustment to the maximum accommodation charges will take effect August 1, 2026.' Since today (2026-08-11) is after that date, the next occurrence is projected to August 1, 2027 following the same annual pattern. A separate April 1, 2026 effective date is also shown on the page for the 'current' rate table, but the recurring adjustment cycle publisher describes as annual is the August 1 inflation adjustment.

reports.title: Health Benefits: Qualifying Income Levels Ministerial Order (Alberta Adult Health Benefit and Alberta Child Health Benefit)
reports.publisher: Alberta Assisted Living and Social Services
reports.description: The Ministerial Order made under the Income and Employment Supports Act that sets the maximum qualifying income levels by household type for the Alberta Adult Health Benefit (dental, optical, prescription drug, ambulance and diabetic supply coverage) and the Alberta Child Health Benefit. Financial eligibility at application and at annual renewal is tested against total combined household net income plus non-taxable child support. The order is reproduced in the Income and Employment Supports Policy Manual.
reports.cadence_note: Amended by Ministerial Order rather than on a fixed calendar. The qualifying income level table in the policy manual is still dated July 1, 2015, so in most years the order is re-affirmed rather than re-issued; the AAHB benefit period itself runs October 1 to September 30 with an automated annual renewal.

release_schedule.rule: Income Support, Training and Health Benefits Regulation (Alta Reg 122/2011), ss. 87-90: a household is financially eligible for the Alberta Adult Health Benefit / Alberta Child Health Benefit if its assessed income is equal to or less than 'the qualifying income level as determined by the Minister.' The Regulation does not specify any fixed interval at which the Minister must set or revise that level.
release_schedule.note: This is not a recurring statistical publication but a discretionary ministerial determination embedded in regulation (most recently amended by AR 97/2026, current-as-of-July-2026 consolidation). No dated release calendar or fixed-interval rule for updating the dollar qualifying-income-level table was found on alberta.ca, the King's Printer regulation text, or open.alberta.ca. The alberta.ca program page and a 2009 predecessor fact sheet both state that individual recipients' financial eligibility is 'reviewed annually' / confirmed 'every September' against CRA income data - but that describes re-verifying an existing recipient's continued eligibility against the current threshold, not a commitment to reissue or change the threshold table itself on that date. Alberta Ombudsman's 2024 investigation into AAHB/ACHB flagged systemic problems including thresholds that had gone without update for extended periods, which is more consistent with ad hoc/irregular ministerial revisions than a fixed annual release. Given this, releases_per_year=1 in the corpus is not well supported by direct evidence; if anything the evidence points to this being an irregular, discretion-driven instrument rather than a fixed-cadence release, though I could not find a citation strong enough to assert a specific correct replacement number.

reports.title: Alberta Aids to Daily Living cost-share amounts and cost-share exemption income thresholds
reports.publisher: Alberta Health (Alberta Aids to Daily Living)
reports.description: The published cost-share rules for the Alberta Aids to Daily Living programme: clients pay 25% of the cost of most benefits up to a maximum of $500 per family per benefit year, and the taxable-income thresholds below which a client is exempt. It also lists the provincial income programmes whose recipients may be exempt from cost-sharing. The benefit year runs July 1 to June 30.
reports.cadence_note: Cost-share maximum and exemption thresholds are stated per benefit year (July 1 to June 30) and revised when Alberta Health changes them; the 25%/$500 structure has been stable for years while the exemption thresholds move.

release_schedule.note: The alberta.ca cost-sharing page presents the 25%/$500 maximum cost-share and income exemption thresholds as static figures with no stated review cycle, effective date, or calendar. The most closely related governing document (AADL Program Manual Section GN - general policy and procedures) has been revised at irregular intervals (Sep 2024, Sep 2023, Jan 2023, Jul 2022, Feb 2021, Dec 2020, Feb 2020, Sep 2017, Jan 2017...) rather than on a fixed annual schedule, and no source states a rule (e.g. 'reviewed every X months') governing when cost-share amounts/income thresholds themselves change. No evidence of a published calendar or a consistent annual pattern specific to this parameter was found.

dependencies.basis: The archived 2023-2025 version of the 'Indexing of Benefits' policy in the Alberta AISH policy manual (retained on the current Benefit Rate Adjustments page) states: 'AISH benefits are adjusted annually using the Alberta Consumer Price Index (CPI) starting on January 1, 2023 ... Annual benefit rate changes are calculated using the Alberta CPI (All-items, not seasonally adjusted). The Alberta CPI is published monthly by Statistics Canada and measures the change in price for goods and services bought by Albertans.' It sets out the formula X = A/B - 1, where A is the sum of the monthly Alberta CPI indexes for the 12 months ending September 30 before the adjustment date and B is the sum for the preceding 12 months. From January 1, 2026 the dependence on Alberta CPI is mediated by the Alberta escalator, which is capped at 2%.

dependencies.basis: Alberta Personal Income Tax Act, RSA 2000 c A-30, s. 44.2(0.1)(b) defines the Alberta escalator, absent a prescribed percentage, as the lesser of 2% and the amount determined by the formula A/B - 1, 'where A is the Consumer Price Index for Alberta for the 12-month period that ended on the last September 30 before that year, and B is the Consumer Price Index for Alberta for the 12-month period immediately preceding'. Subsection 44.2(3) then defines that index explicitly: 'the Consumer Price Index for Alberta for any 12-month period is the result arrived at by (a) aggregating the Consumer Price Index for Alberta, as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act (Canada) ... for each month in that period, (b) dividing the aggregate ... by 12'.

dependencies.basis: Alberta Personal Income Tax Act, RSA 2000 c A-30, s. 44.2(2): 'Where the base taxation year ... in relation to a particular month is after 2024, each of the amounts expressed in dollars in section 30.2(2), except the amount of $2760, is to be adjusted so that the amount to be used under that subsection for the month is the total of (a) the amount that would, but for subsection (4), be the amount used under section 30.2(2) for the month that is one year before the particular month, and (b) the product obtained by multiplying (i) the amount referred to in clause (a) by (ii) the Alberta escalator for the taxation year following the base taxation year.' Section 30.2(2) is the Alberta Child and Family Benefit formula, containing the per-child base and working component amounts and the net income phase-out thresholds. The $2,760 working-income entry threshold is expressly excluded from indexation.

The Seniors Benefit Act (RSA 2000 c S-7) Schedule puts federal OAS and GIS amounts directly inside the Alberta formulas. Schedule s. 9(2)(b)(ii) sets the special needs component income test as 'the sum of (A) the single senior non-deductible income amount under section 8 for the benefit adjustment year, plus (B) an amount equal to the maximum annual amount, not including retroactive payments and not adjusted for deferral, of the monthly pension payable to a single senior under the Old Age Security Act (Canada) in the calendar year that ended before the commencement of the benefit adjustment year.' Schedule s. 7(4) defines term C of the supplementary accommodation assistance formula as 'the combined maximum annual amount ... of Old Age Security, not adjusted for deferral, and Guaranteed Income Supplement payable to a single senior and the maximum benefit payable to a single senior under section 4, in the previous calendar year.' The programme page corroborates that receipt of OAS is an eligibility condition and that lines 11300 (OAS) and 14600 (net federal supplements: GIS and Allowance) are deducted in arriving at non-deductible income (https://www.alberta.ca/alberta-seniors-benefit).
dependencies.evidence_quote: the sum of (A) the single senior non-deductible income amount under section 8 for the benefit adjustment year, plus (B) an amount equal to the maximum annual amount, not including retroactive payments and not adjusted for deferral, of the monthly pension payable to a single senior under the Old Age Security Act (Canada) in the calendar year that ended before the commencement of the benefit adjustment year.

dependencies.basis: Seniors Benefit Act, RSA 2000 c S-7, s. 1(a.21): "'Alberta escalator' means the Alberta escalator as defined in section 44.2 of the Alberta Personal Income Tax Act". The Schedule, s. 2 ('Calculation of adjusted benefit amounts'), then provides: 'A benefit or an amount used to calculate a benefit or eligibility for a benefit that is to be adjusted under section 2.1(3)(b), (3.1)(b) or (5)(a)(ii) or 2.2(3)(b) or (5)(b) of this Act must be adjusted by an amount equal to (a) the benefit amount or amount as of December 31 of the previous calendar year, including any increase to that amount made under this Act or the regulations, multiplied by (b) the Alberta escalator.' So the Alberta Seniors Benefit annual cash benefit and the amounts used to calculate eligibility for it move with the same 2%-capped escalator as AISH, Income Support and the ACFB.

Seniors Benefit Act Schedule, s. 8: '(1) The non-deductible income amount is (a) $23 020 for single seniors, and (b) $34 460 for senior couples. (2) Effective the benefit adjustment date of each benefit adjustment year, the non-deductible income amount is the non-deductible income amount in the previous benefit adjustment year increased annually by a percentage equivalent to the Pension Index under the Canada Pension Plan (Canada) that was applicable for the calendar year that ended before the commencement of the benefit adjustment year.' Subsection (3) adds a fallback: the Minister, in consultation with the Minister responsible for the Financial Administration Act, determines the adjustment 'if (a) the method of calculating the Pension Index is modified by the Government of Canada, or (b) the change in the Pension Index cannot be determined for any reason.' This is a rare case of an Alberta benefit threshold being escalated by a federal index rather than the Alberta escalator.

Section 11 in full: '11(1) In this section, “Alberta CPI” means the monthly All-items Consumer Price Index for Alberta, not seasonally adjusted, published by Statistics Canada. (2) The maximum amount of the accommodation charge set by the Minister under section 9(4) of the Act in respect of each type of accommodation must be adjusted annually on August 1 by the lesser of the following: (a) the percentage increase in the Alberta CPI for the 12-month period ending on February 28 of that year, rounded to the nearest $0.05; (b) 3.8%.' reports.title: Encuesta Permanente de Hogares Continua (EPHC)
reports.description: Continuous household survey that is the primary source for labour-market indicators, household income, and income-based poverty and inequality measurement. National coverage with urban/rural and departmental domains.
reports._notes: Central social and labour survey. Official source for both labour statistics and monetary poverty. Annual poverty results and quarterly labour bulletins are the main public products.

reports.title: Pobreza monetaria / Monetary poverty
reports.description: Official income-poverty and extreme-poverty incidence, calculated by comparing household per-capita income (from EPHC) with nationally defined poverty lines updated by the IPC. Published with urban/rural and departmental breakdowns.
reports._notes: Headline social indicator. 2024: total monetary poverty 20.1% (down 2.2 pp from 22.3% in 2023); extreme poverty 4.1%. Large urban–rural gap, especially in extreme poverty (rural much higher).

reports.title: Líneas de pobreza total y extrema
reports.description: Monetary values of the total and extreme poverty lines (per capita), differentiated for urban and rural areas and updated with the IPC produced by the Banco Central.
reports._notes: Direct input into the poverty measurement. Basket structures derived from income-and-expenditure surveys; annual updating uses the BCP IPC.

reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) / Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index measuring changes in the prices of a representative basket of goods and services. Produced by the central bank (distinct from the pure INE model in some neighbouring countries).
reports._notes: Flagship price statistic. Produced by the BCP rather than INE. Direct input into monetary-policy analysis and into the updating of poverty lines.

reports.title: Cuentas Nacionales / National Accounts of Paraguay
reports.description: System of national accounts producing GDP by production, expenditure and income. Quarterly and annual releases.
reports._notes: Core macroeconomic statistical system. BCP plays the central role in compilation and dissemination.

reports.title: Informe de Política Monetaria (IPoM)
reports.description: Periodic Monetary Policy Report of the central bank. Explains recent inflation, the outlook, and the implications for the policy rate under the inflation-targeting regime.
reports._notes: Flagship policy communication product. Complements higher-frequency monetary-policy decisions.

reports.title: Censo Nacional de Población y Viviendas / Population and Housing Census
reports.description: Decennial population and housing census. Provides the demographic baseline, sampling frames for household surveys, and the basis for updated population projections.
reports._notes: Foundational demographic product (2022 census). Continuously cited by EPHC design, poverty analysis and the 2025 population-projection revision.

reports.title: Índice de Pobreza Multidimensional (IPM)
reports.description: Official multidimensional poverty index capturing deprivations across multiple dimensions beyond income. Complements the monetary-poverty series.
reports._notes: Complementary structural poverty measure. Published annually for several consecutive years; series updated with the new population projections from the 2022 census.

reports.title: Balanza de Pagos / Balance of Payments
reports.description: Quarterly and annual balance of payments covering the current account, capital/financial account and changes in reserve assets.
reports._notes: Core external-accounts product. Current-account outcomes swing with commodity cycles and energy exports; goods trade is typically strong when soy and beef perform well.

reports.title: Reporte de Comercio Exterior / Merchandise Trade
reports.description: Monthly and annual statistics of exports and imports of goods, including registered trade, re-exports and other flows. Key traditional exports: soy and derivatives, beef, electricity, maize.
reports._notes: Primary high-frequency trade product. 2025 total exports ~USD 16.7 bn. Soy, beef, maize and electricity dominate; re-exports and maquila are material secondary flows.

reports.title: Tasa de Política Monetaria (TPM) / Policy interest rate
reports.description: Main monetary-policy instrument of the BCP under the inflation-targeting regime.
reports._notes: Operational policy rate. Recent levels around 5.5%. Adjusted to steer inflation toward the target band.

reports.title: Reservas Internacionales / International reserves
reports.description: Stock of international reserve assets managed by the central bank. Published at high frequency and analysed in the BOP and monetary reports.
reports._notes: Key external-buffer indicator. Continuously monitored alongside the net international investment position.

reports.title: Marco de metas de inflación — BCP
reports.description: Operational monetary-policy framework: explicit inflation targeting. The BCP sets a target (historically 4%, more recently centred near 3.5%) with a ±2 pp tolerance band and uses the TPM as the primary instrument.
reports._notes: Core policy-framework node. Continuously cited as the reference against which inflation outcomes and policy actions are evaluated.
_referenced_by: IPC and inflation analysis that refers to the target band
Market and academic commentary on Paraguayan monetary policy

reports.title: Soja y derivados — producción y exportaciones
reports.description: Statistics of soybean and soybean-product production and exports. Single most important merchandise export and the backbone of the agricultural economy.
reports._notes: Structural export leader. Often 30–40%+ of registered export value in strong years. Continuously cited in trade, BOP and rural-economy analysis.

reports.title: Carne bovina — producción y exportaciones
reports.description: Statistics of beef production and exports. Major traditional agro-export alongside soy.
reports._notes: Signature traditional export. Paraguay is a significant regional and global beef exporter; volumes and values are high-frequency trade indicators.

reports.title: Exportaciones de energía eléctrica (Itaipú / Yacyretá)
reports.description: Statistics of electricity exports from the binational hydroelectric plants (Itaipú with Brazil, Yacyretá with Argentina). Unique and material component of Paraguay’s external accounts.
reports._notes: Distinctive structural feature of the Paraguayan economy. Electricity sales to Brazil (and to a lesser extent Argentina) are a recurring and large line in the trade and current-account statistics.

reports.title: Itaipú Binacional — institutional and statistical identity
reports.description: Binational hydroelectric entity shared with Brazil. Generates the bulk of Paraguay’s electricity export revenue and is a foundational infrastructure and fiscal-revenue node.
reports._notes: Foundational binational instrument. Continuously cited in energy, trade and public-finance analysis; the treaty and compensation arrangements are recurring reference points.

reports.title: Asunción — capital statistical identity
reports.description: Capital city and primary urban economy. Core domain for EPHC labour, income and poverty analysis. Lowest departmental poverty incidence.
reports._notes: Dominant metro node. Continuously published as a distinct geographic domain. 2025 total monetary poverty ~6.0% — the lowest among departments.

reports.title: Departamento Central — core metropolitan periphery
reports.description: Department surrounding Asunción. Intermediate-to-low poverty and the largest absolute urban population mass outside the capital.
reports._notes: Completes the greater Asunción statistical geography. 2025 poverty ~9.9% — among the lowest.

reports.title: Departamento de Concepción — highest-poverty contrast
reports.description: Northern department with among the highest poverty incidence in the 2024–2025 departmental results.
reports._notes: Poverty-contrast department. 2025 total poverty ~28.7%; frequently ranks at or near the top of the departmental poverty ranking.

reports.title: Departamento de San Pedro — high-poverty contrast
reports.description: Northern/interior department with elevated poverty incidence. Completes the high-poverty northern set.
reports._notes: 2025 total poverty ~24.8%. Frequently cited alongside Concepción and Caazapá among the highest-poverty departments; also features heavily in district-level poverty maps.

reports.title: Departamento de Caazapá — high-poverty contrast
reports.description: Southern-interior department with elevated poverty incidence.
reports._notes: 2025 total poverty ~25.1%. Completes the high-poverty departmental set.

reports.title: Pobreza monetaria por departamento (INE)
reports.description: Official departmental tabulations of monetary poverty. Primary source for the inter-departmental poverty gradient.
reports._notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2025 ranking extremes: Concepción, Caazapá, San Pedro highest; Asunción and Central lowest. National total poverty fell to ~16.0%.

reports.title: Presupuesto General de la Nación / National Budget
reports.description: Annual national budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues and expenditure of the central government.
reports._notes: Operational fiscal framework. Links tax and other revenues (including energy royalties) with functional spending on education, health, social protection and investment.

reports.title: Gasto público en educación y salud
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / MEC / MSPyBS
reports.description: Public expenditure on education and health as reflected in the national budget and related functional statistics. Complements household-survey education and health modules.
reports._notes: Education and health are major functional allocations (education often the largest single share of the budget). Continuously tracked in budget execution and social-policy analysis; health coverage gaps remain a recurring policy issue.

reports.title: Royalties y compensación por cesión de energía (Itaipú)
reports.description: Fiscal transfers from Itaipú to the Paraguayan state under the Treaty Annex C: royalties and compensation for energy ceded to Brazil. Major non-tax revenue stream distributed to the central government, departments and municipalities.
reports._notes: Structural fiscal node unique to Paraguay. Hundreds of millions of USD annually (e.g. ~USD 400–500 mn range in recent full years). Part funds the national budget; part is transferred to subnational governments and social funds (e.g. FONAE for school feeding).

reports.title: Deuda pública / Public debt statistics
reports.description: Stock and flow statistics of central-government and public-sector debt (external and domestic). Key sustainability indicator.
reports._notes: Critical fiscal-sustainability node. Mid-2026 stock around USD 22 bn (~34% of GDP in recent readings). Continuously monitored in macroeconomic and policy analysis.

reports.title: Subsecretaría de Estado de Tributación (SET) — tax collection
reports.description: National tax administration. Publishes tax collection by type of tax (income tax, VAT, etc.) and performance against annual targets.
reports._notes: Primary non-energy revenue-side fiscal statistic. Complements customs revenue and the energy royalty stream.

reports.title: Ingresos fiscales del Estado / Consolidated fiscal revenues
reports.description: Consolidated view of central-government revenues including tax, customs, energy royalties/compensation and other non-tax income.
reports._notes: Operational revenue dashboard. Links the real-side economy (taxes, trade) and the binational energy complex to the financing of the national budget.

reports.title: Ley 60/90 — Régimen de promoción de inversiones
reports.description: General investment-promotion law granting tax and customs benefits for declared investment projects (capital-goods import exemptions, etc.).
reports._notes: Core horizontal investment-incentive framework. Continuously cited alongside the maquila regime as a reason firms locate in Paraguay.

reports.title: REDIEX — Red de Inversiones y Exportaciones
reports.description: National investment and export promotion network/agency. Publishes investor guides, sector profiles and trade intelligence.
reports._notes: Institutional interface between the incentive regimes (maquila, Law 60/90, free zones) and private investors and exporters.

reports.title: Departamento de Alto Paraná — industrial & border hub
reports.description: Eastern border department containing Ciudad del Este. Major commercial, industrial and re-export hub; intermediate poverty relative to the northern departments.
reports._notes: Completes the economic-geography set. Hosts significant maquila and commercial activity; poverty lower than the northern interior but higher than Asunción/Central.

reports.title: Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS) — social-security coverage
reports.description: Main social-security institution covering pensions, health insurance and other benefits for formal workers. Major formal-employment and social-protection actor.
reports._notes: Central formal-employment and social-protection node. Cotizante counts and benefit statistics complement the EPHC labour series; health coverage remains a major policy issue (large share of population without formal insurance).

reports.title: Fondo Nacional de Alimentación Escolar (FONAE)
reports.description: National school-feeding fund financed in part by Itaipú energy-compensation transfers. Links the energy-fiscal stream to a core social programme.
reports._notes: Illustrative social-programme node. Receives a large share of the Itaipú compensation-for-energy-cession resources under the current distribution law.

reports.title: Ministerio de Educación y Ciencias (MEC) — education statistics and budget
reports.description: Ministry responsible for the formal education system. Publishes enrolment, attendance and institutional statistics; major functional allocation in the national budget (constitutionally prioritised).
reports._notes: Core education node. Budget share is large (often the single largest functional category). Attendance rates from EPHC are high in primary ages but fall in the upper secondary range (~87% for 15–17). Rural–urban gaps persist.

reports.title: Tasa de asistencia escolar (EPHC)
reports.description: School-attendance rates for the school-age population derived from the continuous household survey. Key education-outcome indicator complementary to administrative enrolment data.
reports._notes: High overall attendance (~95% for 5–17) but clear age and rural–urban gradients. Complements the MEC administrative series and links education outcomes to the household-survey system.

reports.title: Cobertura de seguro médico / Health-insurance coverage
reports.description: Share of the population with formal health insurance (IPS or private). Complementary indicator to public-health service statistics.
reports._notes: Structural coverage gap. Roughly 70% of the population lacks formal insurance and depends on the public system; rural coverage is substantially lower than urban. Recurring policy and inequality theme.

reports.title: Cuentas de Salud / National Health Accounts
reports.description: Satellite accounts of health expenditure (public and private) relative to GDP and total current health spending.
reports._notes: Links the health system to the macroeconomic accounts. Public health spending has risen but remains below regional and OPS benchmarks; private out-of-pocket spending is material.

reports.title: Departamento de Itapúa — southern agricultural hub
reports.description: Southern department with significant agricultural production and intermediate-to-higher poverty relative to the capital region.
reports._notes: Completes the departmental set. Frequently appears in both poverty rankings and agricultural-production geography.

reports.title: Departamento de Caaguazú — central interior
reports.description: Central-interior department with elevated poverty incidence and significant rural population.
reports._notes: High-poverty interior department. Completes the set of departments that test the statistical hierarchy under elevated deprivation.

reports.title: Coeficiente de Gini / Income inequality
reports.description: Official Gini coefficient of income inequality calculated from EPHC income data. Companion indicator to the monetary-poverty series.
reports._notes: Structural inequality measure. Complements the poverty headcount and is published alongside the annual poverty results.

reports.title: Ley 7548/2025 — Nuevo régimen de incentivos fiscales para la inversión
reports.description: Updated general investment-promotion law (successor to Law 60/90). Grants tax and customs benefits for declared national and foreign investment projects.
reports._notes: Core horizontal investment-incentive framework. Replaced Law 60/90 in September 2025. Continuously cited alongside the maquila regime as a primary reason firms locate in Paraguay. (Supersedes the earlier py-ley-60-90 node conceptually; keep both for lineage if needed.)
_referenced_by: Project-approval documentation under the new regime

reports.title: Política Automotriz / ACE 13 sector automotor
reports.description: Automotive-sector policy and the bilateral ACE 13 regime with Argentina governing preferential trade in vehicles and auto parts, including regional-content rules and quotas.
reports._notes: Sector-specific industrial and trade instrument. ACE 13 with Argentina remains the operational preferential framework for vehicles and auto parts; Law 4838/12 provides domestic tax benefits for automotive investment.
_referenced_by: MIC origin-certification guidance for auto parts

reports.title: Consejo Nacional de Industrias Maquiladoras de Exportación (CNIME)
reports.description: Governing body of the maquila regime. Approves programmes, monitors operations and publishes sector statistics.
reports._notes: Institutional parent of the maquila system. Continuously cited in maquila export, employment and programme-approval statistics (~35k direct jobs; exports in the USD 1+ bn range).

reports.title: Consejo Nacional de Zonas Francas (CNZF)
reports.description: Governing body of the free-zone regime under Law 523/95. Supervises concessions and the special tax/customs treatment (0.5% single tax on third-country exports).
reports._notes: Institutional parent of the free-zone system. Complements the maquila regime; large-scale projects (e.g. pulp/industrial) have used free-zone concessions.

reports.title: Inversión Extranjera Directa / FDI statistics
reports.description: Statistics of foreign direct investment flows and stocks by sector and country of origin. Published as part of the external accounts and specialised BCP studies.
reports._notes: Core FDI statistical product. Cumulative net inflows on the order of USD 10 bn over 2008–2024; recent flows concentrated in non-financial services (commerce, telecoms, transport, real estate) alongside manufacturing and agro-industry.

reports.title: Ley 5542/2015 — Invariabilidad de la tasa impositiva
reports.description: Law allowing tax-rate invariability (stability) for up to 20 years for qualifying investment projects. Complements the general investment-incentive regime.
reports._notes: Stability instrument that reduces fiscal-policy risk for long-horizon investments. Continuously cited alongside Law 7548/2025 and the maquila/free-zone regimes.

py-carne's own part_of is py-comercio-exterior (invalid target). BCP's foreign-trade methodology note names DNIT/Aduanas as the primary trade-data source, and Cámara Paraguaya de Carne only for freight-cost estimates, not export-volume figures. No SENACSA/ARP institutional-source statement found.

py-soja's own part_of is py-comercio-exterior (invalid target). Same BCP methodology note names CAPECO only in the freight-cost-consultation context, not as the source of soybean export/production figures.

MIC's maquila24 regime page and a 2025 MIC Maquila presentation deck cite legal instruments and describe an inter-agency review process, but neither states a data/methodology dependency on any existing corpus report.
MEF's Zona Franca page states zona-franca users can additionally benefit from incentives under Ley 60/90 — a benefits cross-reference between two legal regimes, not a data/methodology dependency.

mspbs.gov.py and its DIGIES subsite yielded no accessible page naming a source institution or methodology (OPS/SHA framework) with citable text; WebSearch quota was exhausted mid-task, worth a follow-up pass.

py-ied's own part_of is py-bop (invalid target). A legal-analysis summary of Ley 5542/2015 treats the tax-rate-invariability law as a distinct, separate mechanism from Ley 60/90, with no stated cross-applicability.

py-reservas's own part_of is py-bop (invalid target). BCP's Gestión de las Reservas Internacionales page cites only an internal Board-approved investment policy, not another report/standard in the corpus.

py-set's own part_of is py-ingresos-fiscales (invalid target, the only natural one). DNIT's (SET's successor agency) statistics page lists many revenue/taxpayer bulletins but states no data source or cross-reference to Zonas Francas, CNZF, CNIME, or the Budget Law.

reports.title: Plan budgétaire (Budget du Québec)
reports.description: The annual multi-year Budget Plan of the Government of Quebec, presenting the fiscal framework, revenues (own-source and federal transfers), portfolio expenditures, debt service, accounting balance, Balanced Budget Act balance after Generations Fund deposits, economic outlook assumptions, and new measures. Tabled with the budget speech, typically in mid-March for the fiscal year beginning 1 April.
reports.cadence_note: annual

reports.title: Le point sur la situation économique et financière du Québec
reports.description: In-year update of Quebec's economic and financial situation, revising revenue, expenditure and deficit forecasts against the tabled Plan budgétaire, and updating the multi-year framework. Typically released in the fall (e.g., November).
reports.cadence_note: at least annual (mid-year / fall update)

reports.title: Bilan démographique du Québec
reports.publisher: Institut de la statistique du Québec
reports.description: Annual comprehensive demographic report for Quebec covering population estimates and change, natural increase (births and deaths), international and interprovincial migration, age structure, fertility and mortality. Draws on vital statistics and collaborates with Statistics Canada population estimates.
reports.cadence_note: annual

reports.title: Décret de population des municipalités
reports.publisher: Gouvernement du Québec (Conseil des ministres / Ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation)
reports.description: Annual order-in-council establishing the official population of every local municipality, northern village and borough for the application of laws, regulations and government programs. Explicitly based on estimates produced by the Institut de la statistique du Québec as of 1 July of the prior year.
reports.cadence_note: annual (late December for the following calendar year)

reports.title: Rapport financier consolidé (états financiers audités) de la Ville de Montréal
reports.description: Annual audited consolidated financial statements and financial accountability report of the City of Montreal, presenting operating results for tax purposes, surplus/deficit by local and agglomeration responsibilities, capital investments, debt ratios and other disclosures under Public Sector Accounting Standards.
reports.cadence_note: annual (typically June for the prior calendar year)

reports.title: Budget de fonctionnement de la Ville de Québec
reports.description: Annual balanced operating budget of the City of Quebec, presenting revenues (taxes and compensations in lieu, transfers, services rendered, imposition of rights), expenditures, investment budget, and tax-rate decisions for the fiscal year, with reconciliation to Public Sector Accounting Standards.
reports.cadence_note: annual

reports.title: Rapports financiers des organismes municipaux (sommation et base de données)
reports.publisher: Ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation
reports.description: Annual compilation and public release of the audited financial reports and complementary information submitted by all local municipalities, RCMs, metropolitan communities, intermunicipal boards and public transit bodies in Quebec. Includes aggregate summations by organism type and open-data extracts used for provincial monitoring and fiscal analysis.
reports.cadence_note: annual

reports.title: Manuel de la présentation de l'information financière municipale
reports.publisher: Ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation
reports.description: Authoritative provincial manual prescribing the form, content and accounting treatments for municipal financial reports and fiscal-purpose reconciliations in Quebec. Aligns presentation with Canadian Public Sector Accounting Standards while incorporating Quebec-specific legislative requirements for taxation and debt.
reports.cadence_note: updated as needed (latest December 2025 edition)

reports.title: Richesse foncière uniformisée (RFU) des municipalités
reports.publisher: Ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation
reports.description: Annual provincial dataset and complementary guide measuring each municipality's equalized assessment (richesse foncière uniformisée). Computed from the values on the municipal real-estate assessment roll multiplied by the comparative factor for that roll, plus selected non-taxable values. Serves as the fiscal-capacity measure for municipal equalization, intermunicipal cost-sharing and metropolitan community allocations.
reports.cadence_note: annual

reports.title: Manuel d'évaluation foncière du Québec (MEFQ)
reports.publisher: Ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation
reports.description: Official provincial manual that prescribes the methodology, data standards, valuation techniques and legal requirements for preparing and maintaining municipal real-estate assessment rolls (rôles d'évaluation foncière). Updated periodically; the edition in force governs all rolls coming into force in a given year. Provides the uniform basis from which the richesse foncière uniformisée is derived.
reports.cadence_note: updated as needed (annual editions for successive roll years)

reports.title: Produit intérieur brut réel par industrie au Québec
reports.publisher: Institut de la statistique du Québec
reports.description: Monthly estimates of real GDP by industry for Quebec as a whole (seasonally adjusted, annualized, basic prices). Produced using the net-production method preferred under national-accounts conventions, with indicator methods where necessary. Released approximately 2.5 months after the reference month.
reports.cadence_note: monthly

reports.title: Produit intérieur brut régional par industrie au Québec
reports.publisher: Institut de la statistique du Québec
reports.description: Annual estimates of GDP by industry for Quebec's 17 administrative regions and selected census metropolitan areas, in current dollars at basic prices. Derived by allocating provincial industry totals (from the Comptes économiques) using fiscal and census-based allocators.
reports.cadence_note: annual

reports.title: Taux de taxes de la Ville de Montréal
reports.description: Annual schedule of property-tax rates (taxe foncière générale, water, road, ARTM contribution, borough service taxes, etc.) adopted by the City of Montreal for the fiscal year. Rates vary by property category, value bracket and borough; applied to the values on the current triennial assessment roll after any phasing measures.
reports.cadence_note: annual

reports.title: Loi sur l'équilibre budgétaire
reports.publisher: Assemblée nationale du Québec / Éditeur officiel du Québec
reports.description: Provincial statute that defines the budgetary balance for the purposes of the Balanced Budget Act, excludes Generations Fund transactions from the balance, and requires a multi-year return-to-balance plan when a deficit is recorded. The Plan budgétaire presents both the accounting balance and the balance 'within the meaning of the Balanced Budget Act'.
reports.cadence_note: legislation (amended as needed)

reports.title: Rôles d'évaluation foncière de l'agglomération de Montréal (triennal)
reports.publisher: Ville de Montréal (Direction de l'évaluation foncière)
reports.description: Triennial real-estate assessment rolls for the 16 municipalities of the Montreal agglomeration. Deposited every three years (most recent 2026-2027-2028 deposited September 2025), they inventory every immovable, its characteristics and its real value as of the statutory valuation date (1 July of the year preceding the first year of the roll). Form the legal base for municipal and school property taxes and for the calculation of richesse foncière uniformisée.
reports.cadence_note: every three years

reports.title: Règlement sur l'imposition des taxes et des compensations (Ville de Québec)
reports.description: Annual by-law (most recent R.V.Q. 3492 for fiscal year 2026) that sets the general property-tax rates by property category, water/sewer and residual-materials tariffs, and other compensations for the City of Quebec. Applied to the values on the current assessment roll.

reports.title: Fonds des générations (revenus consacrés et solde)

reports.title: Projections démographiques du Québec et de ses régions

reports.description: Annual update of population projections for Quebec and its administrative regions (and selected CMAs) under multiple scenarios. reports.title: Proportions médianes des rôles et facteurs comparatifs

The document states: "Une première répartition s’effectue sur la base de la population inscrite au Décret de population et de l’ indice de vitalité économique (IVÉ) de la municipalité."
dependencies.evidence_quote: Une première répartition s’effectue sur la base de la population inscrite au Décret de population et de l’ indice de vitalité économique (IVÉ) de la municipalité.

dependencies.basis: ISQ population estimates that feed the Décret are produced in collaboration with Statistics Canada and rest on the adjusted census counts and intercensal estimates published by StatCan. The document states: "Les estimations de la population sont produites par Statistique Canada, avec la collaboration de l’Institut de la statistique du Québec (ISQ) et de plusieurs ministères et organismes. Elles ont comme base les comptes de population des recensements"

Municipal financial statements in Quebec, including Montreal's audited consolidated report, are prepared in accordance with the Canadian Public Sector Accounting Standards (Normes comptables pour le secteur public). The document states: "Les organismes municipaux préparent leurs documents financiers en s’appuyant sur les Normes comptables pour le secteur public telles qu’elles sont établies par le Conseil sur la comptabilité dans le secteur public de CPA Canada."

The form, content, fiscal-purpose reconciliations and required schedules of every municipal financial report submitted to and compiled by MAMH are prescribed by the Manuel de la présentation de l'information financière municipale. The document states: "Le Manuel a pour but de fournir aux administrateurs municipaux et à toutes les personnes actives dans le domaine municipal les éléments de base pour assurer une présentation adéquate et uniforme de l'information financière. ... dependencies.basis: Federal equalization payments form a material component of Quebec's total revenues in the multi-year financial framework presented in the Plan budgétaire; the budget tables and narrative report the amounts received under the federal program. The document states: "Transferts fédéraux 30 577 ... Sources: Institut de la statistique du Québec, Statistics Canada and Ministère des Finances du Québec."

The economic outlook and nominal/real GDP forecasts underlying the revenue projections in the Plan budgétaire rely on Statistics Canada provincial economic accounts and related national-accounts data, as explicitly sourced in the budget documents. The document states: "Sources: Institut de la statistique du Québec, Statistics Canada and Ministère des Finances du Québec."

ISQ demographic estimates and the Bilan démographique are anchored on the adjusted census counts from Statistics Canada's Census of Population. The document states: "Elles ont comme base les comptes de population des recensements, mais ont pour objectifs : 1) de corriger les résultats des recensements afin de tenir compte du sous-dénombrement net et des réserves partiellement dénombrées"

The population levels, components of growth and intercensal estimates published in the Bilan démographique are produced jointly with, and rest on, Statistics Canada's population estimates program. The document states: "Les estimations de la population sont produites par Statistique Canada, avec la collaboration de l’Institut de la statistique du Québec (ISQ)"

Municipal equalization eligibility and payment amounts under the Règlement sur le régime de péréquation are determined by comparing each municipality's richesse foncière uniformisée per capita (and average housing value) to provincial medians; the RFU dataset is the direct source of those figures. The document states: "Elle sert aussi de base de répartition d’une partie du programme de péréquation municipale."
dependencies.evidence_quote: Elle sert aussi de base de répartition d’une partie du programme de péréquation municipale.

dependencies.basis: The values that enter the RFU calculation are the values inscribed on the municipal assessment roll; those rolls are prepared and maintained strictly according to the methodology, data standards and valuation techniques prescribed by the Manuel d'évaluation foncière du Québec. The document states: "Les évaluations sont uniformisées en les multipliant par le facteur comparatif approuvé par la ou le ministre des Affaires municipales pour l’année en cours. ... Comme les rôles triennaux des municipalités ne sont pas tous déposés la même année..."

The monthly real GDP-by-industry series is compiled according to the production approach and concepts of the System of National Accounts (basic-price valuation, net production method preferred). The document states: "Mesure l'activité économique générée par un secteur ou une industrie. Il estime, en dollars constants, la contribution du secteur ou de l'industrie à la production. Pour produire ces estimations, la méthode dite de la production nette est l'approche privilégiée."

The Plan budgétaire presents both an accounting balance and a distinct 'budgetary balance within the meaning of the Balanced Budget Act' that excludes Generations Fund deposits; the Act itself defines that balance and the required return-to-balance plan. The document states: "Le solde budgétaire pour une année financière est formé de l’écart entre les revenus et les dépenses établis conformément aux conventions comptables du gouvernement. Il ne comprend pas: 1 ° les revenus et les dépenses comptabilisés au Fonds des générations"
dependencies.evidence_quote: Le solde budgétaire pour une année financière est formé de l’écart entre les revenus et les dépenses établis conformément aux conventions comptables du gouvernement. Il ne comprend pas: 1 ° les revenus et les dépenses comptabilisés au Fonds des générations

dependencies.basis: Regional allocation of industry value-added uses commuting matrices and place-of-work data derived from Statistics Canada census (and National Household Survey) special tabulations. The document states: "elles sont transformées en données selon le lieu de travail au moyen des tableaux de navettage résidence-travail par industrie (SCIAN). Ces matrices sont construites à l’aide de compilations spéciales de Statistique Canada faites à partir des données de l’Enquête nationale auprès des ménages (ENM) de 2011 ... et du recensement de 2016"

Property-tax rates published for a given year are applied to the assessed values appearing on the current triennial assessment roll (after any statutory phasing of value changes). The document states: "Le rôle d’évaluation sert de base au calcul des taxes municipales et scolaires."

The RFU for Montreal-area municipalities is computed directly from the values inscribed on the agglomeration's triennial assessment rolls, multiplied by the applicable comparative factor. The document states: "La RFU d’une municipalité comprend l’évaluation uniformisée de tous les immeubles imposables situés sur son territoire... Les évaluations sont uniformisées en les multipliant par le facteur comparatif"

The annual tax-and-compensation by-law implements the taxation decisions contained in the City's adopted operating budget for that fiscal year. The document states: "Ce règlement prévoit l’imposition des taxes et des compensations pour l’exercice financier de 2026."

The Balanced Budget Act explicitly excludes revenues and expenditures recorded in the Generations Fund from the statutory budgetary balance and requires the Fund's dedicated revenues to be used solely for debt reduction. The document states: "Il ne comprend pas: 1 ° les revenus et les dépenses comptabilisés au Fonds des générations institué par la Loi sur la réduction de la dette et instituant le Fonds des générations"

Uniformization of assessed values for RFU purposes is performed by multiplying the values on each municipal roll by the comparative factor derived from that roll's median proportion relative to market. The document states: "Les évaluations sont uniformisées en les multipliant par le facteur comparatif approuvé par la ou le ministre des Affaires municipales pour l’année en cours."

The annual population-projection update incorporates the latest observed fertility, mortality and migration components published in the Bilan démographique and related demographic estimates. The document states: "The new projections take into account the most recent data on migration, fertility and mortality."

The annual calculation and approval of each roll's median proportion and comparative factor are governed by the specific statistical rules set out in the Règlement sur la proportion médiane du rôle d'évaluation foncière. The document states: "Le Règlement sur la proportion médiane du rôle d’évaluation foncière prescrit la façon d’établir la proportion médiane de chacun des rôles d’évaluation."
dependencies.evidence_quote: Le Règlement sur la proportion médiane du rôle d’évaluation foncière prescrit la façon d’établir la proportion médiane de chacun des rôles d’évaluation.

reports.title: Nordic Statistics database
reports.description: Joint statistical database maintained by the Nordic Council of Ministers, drawing on the five Nordic NSIs, the Nomesco-Nososco health/welfare committees and international sources including Eurostat and the OECD.
reports.cadence_note: Roughly monthly, skipping January and July — confirmed via the publisher's own news archive showing distinct dated update posts in the other 10 months across 2023-2025.

release_schedule.note: The Nordic Statistics database is not a discrete annual report but a continuously maintained database. The publisher's news archive (nordicstatistics.org/news) shows a consistent multi-year pattern of roughly monthly 'X update' releases in Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov and Dec of each year from 2022-2025, with no updates posted in January or July. The 'About' page states only that 'Data is updated regularly over the year' without a fixed calendar. Exact day-of-month varies (e.g. August updates landed on 2024-08-22 and 2025-08-29), so entries use month precision. As of 2026-08-11 no 2026 monthly-update news posts have yet been published this year (only one topical article dated 2026-06-03), so all listed occurrences are projected from the historical pattern.

reports.title: Defence Expenditure of NATO Countries
reports.description: NATO's annual compilation of Allied defence spending against an agreed NATO definition of defence expenditure, distinct from national budget definitions.

release_schedule.note: NATO has no published release calendar or stated rule for this report; it publishes an annual updated compendium of member defence-spending tables/PDF/Excel each year, timed loosely around early summer (often near the NATO summit), though the exact month has varied: 2014-2021 edition issued 11 Jun 2021, 2014-2022 edition issued 27 Jun 2022, 2014-2023 edition issued ~Jun 2023 with a revised edition on 14 Mar 2024, 2014-2024 edition issued 17 Jun 2024, 2014-2025 edition issued 28 Aug 2025 (data cut-off 3 Jun 2025), and the 2014-2026 edition issued 7 Jul 2026. Given this Jun-Aug spread, the next (2014-2027) edition is projected for roughly June-August 2027; no exact date can be cited.

reports.title: Manual on measuring Research and Development in ESA 2010
reports.description: Eurostat's 2014 manual implementing R&D as capital formation under ESA 2010, cited by INSEE as the basis for its own R&D capitalisation methodology.
reports.cadence_note: Published 2014, no stated revision schedule. Modelled at the same nominal rate as sna-2008 and other versioned methodological standards in this corpus (roughly once a generation) rather than as a one-off, since it functions as an ongoing methodological reference cited by name, not a single-use document.

release_schedule.note: This is a one-off methodological manual (KS-GQ-14-004), published 2014-08-01, approved by the Eurostat Group of Directors of Macroeconomic Statistics in December 2013, guiding Member States on recognizing R&D as capital formation under ESA 2010. The publisher's own product page shows no revision schedule, no release calendar, and no stated update rule. There is no evidence of periodic re-issuance; it functions as a static reference tied to the ESA 2010 standard rather than a recurring publication.

reports.title: Frascati Manual — Guidelines for Collecting and Reporting Data on Research and Experimental Development
reports.description: OECD's standard for R&D statistics collection, cited by the EU's own R&D manual and, through it, by INSEE as the basis for French R&D expenditure statistics used in national accounts.

release_schedule.note: The Frascati Manual is a methodological guidelines document, not a periodic statistical release. Past editions were published in 1963, 1970, 1976, 1980, 1993, 2002, and 2015 (7th, current edition) — gaps between editions have ranged from 4 to 13 years, with no fixed cadence. OECD's own 'Continuing development of the OECD Frascati Manual' page and a 2024 NESTI document (DSTI/STP/NESTI(2024)3/REV2) explicitly state that NESTI 'does not envisage undertaking a wholesale revision of the Frascati Manual' at this time; instead it is producing supplementary 'complementary guidance' as an OECD Technical Paper annexed to the still-current 2015 edition. There is no calendar, no stated rule, and no consistent periodicity — the releases_per_year value of 0.2 (implying a 5-year cycle) does not match the actual historical pattern (roughly one edition every 8-13 years on average since 2002), and given the explicit 'no revision planned' statement, no fixed number is really appropriate here.

reports.title: Gross National Income Inventory (ESA 2010), 2010, The Netherlands

release_schedule.rule: Per Council Regulation (EU, Euratom) governing GNI harmonisation for own-resources purposes (as summarized by Eurostat): "Member States shall transmit the GNI Inventory to the Commission (Eurostat) by 31 December 2021. Subsequent updates of the GNI Inventory shall be made and transmitted to the Commission (Eurostat) within 12 months after any major change of sources or methods for compiling GNI. In any case, the GNI Inventory shall be updated at least every 5 years."
release_schedule.note: This specific report is the 2010-reporting-year edition of CBS's GNI Inventory (a benchmark-revision snapshot published March 2017); it will not itself be reissued, but CBS publishes updated GNI Inventory editions as part of the same recurring series (1995 ed. published 2016, 2010 ed. published 2017, 2015 ed. published 2021, 2021 ed. published 2025). Observed gaps between successive editions have been ~4-5 years, consistent with the EU regulatory minimum of updating at least every 5 years (or within 12 months of a major methods change). Next edition's exact date is not yet announced by CBS/Eurostat; computed date is an estimate based on the 5-year rule applied to the most recent (2021) edition's July 2025 publication, and the ~4-year historical cadence.

release_schedule.rule: L'échelle mobile des salaires se déclenche automatiquement lorsque la moyenne mobile semestrielle de l'indice national des prix à la consommation dépasse de 2,5 % son niveau au précédent déclenchement (loi modifiée du 27 mai 1975 concernant l'échelle mobile des salaires et des traitements). release_schedule.note: This is not a scheduled publication but an automatic trigger: whenever the 6-month moving average of Luxembourg's CPI exceeds the level at the previous trigger by 2.5%, wages/pensions/social parameters are indexed +2.5%. STATEC's central forecast (June 2026 report, reaffirmed 24 June 2026) projects the next trigger in Q2 2027, with no second 2026 tranche expected given ~2.2% inflation for 2026 and the 'Resilienzpak 2026' energy-price-capping measures. STATEC itself flags this could move earlier (as early as Q3 2026) if inflation accelerates (e.g., from an oil-price shock), so the Q2 2027 date is a rolling forecast, not a fixed date.

_note: How the policy rate reaches the rates people actually pay. The Bank of Canada's own explainer states the chain in plain words: the target for the overnight rate is 'the starting point for setting many of the interest rates in the economy that matter for Canadians', and it names the prime rate of commercial banks as one of them. Two edges of very different strength come out of this — the Bank Rate is arithmetic, and the prime rate is influence — which makes it a useful test of whether the relationship types are doing real work.

dependencies.basis: Pure arithmetic on the target. The Bank's explainer works the example: 'if the Bank sets the policy interest rate at 2.25% ... the lower end of the range is 2.20%—our deposit rate; the higher end of the range is 2.5%—our bank rate.' The offsets are policy choices that change rarely — the deposit rate moved from equal to the target to 5 basis points below it in January 2025 — but between such changes the band is a fixed spread and nothing else.

dependencies.basis: The Bank names this transmission directly: the policy rate 'is the starting point for setting many of the interest rates in the economy that matter for Canadians', and 'by encouraging financial institutions to borrow and lend among themselves at close to the policy rate, the Bank affects interest rates on all kinds of other borrowing in the economy, including the prime rate of commercial banks (used for loans such as mortgages and lines of credit)'. Deliberately not calculated_from: no bank is obliged to move prime, and the Bank's own word is 'affects'. The spread has been stable for years by convention, not by rule.

reports.title: Financial Statements of the Government of the Cook Islands
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM), Cook Islands
reports.description: The audited whole-of-government financial statements of the Cook Islands, prepared by the Treasury under the Ministry of Finance and Economic Management Act 1995-96. Reports on IPSAS and cites individual standards by number (IPSAS 17, 21, 35, 36, 39, 40 all appear). Audited by the Cook Islands' own Audit Office under the Public Expenditure Review Committee and Audit (PERCA) Act 1995-96 — not by New Zealand, unlike Niue and Tokelau. SEVERE ARREARS: the most recent full set located this session covers FY2018 and was signed by the Financial Secretary and audited by the Director of Audit on the same day, 30 November 2020 — a twenty-nine-month lag. `releases_per_year` records the statutory intent; the cadence note records the practice.
reports.cadence_note: Statutorily annual. In practice heavily lagged: the FY2018 statements were authorised for issue and audited on 30 November 2020. The 2018 audit opinion is qualified on four matters, including inability to confirm taxation revenue.

release_schedule.note: As of June 2026, the Cook Islands Government's audited consolidated financial statements are severely backlogged, so there is no fixed or computable 'next' release date. Per a June 2026 Climate Finance Capacity Support Programme (CFCSP) article, in 2024 the government was 5 years behind (most recent completed/audited accounts were for FY ending June 2019 -- consistent with the corpus's current url, which links to the '2018 Cook Islands Government Financial Statements Final B' edition). MFEM's Treasury Management Division, with an embedded CFCSP-funded Financial Reporting Specialist, completed and submitted FY2020-FY2022 consolidated IPSAS-compliant statements to the Cook Islands Audit Office (CIAO) for audit by April 2026, narrowing the arrears to 3 years behind (as of 3 April 2026). The FY2023 statements were in final consolidation stages and expected to be submitted to CIAO by June 2026, after which work on FY2024 and FY2025 would begin 'at a slower pace.' No publisher calendar or statutory-deadline text was found (the site only states statements must comply with the MFEM Act 1995-96, without a quotable numeric deadline), and given the multi-year catch-up program in progress, any single projected 'next' date would likely be stale or wrong within months. MFEM's own Annual Financial Reports listing (https://www.mfem.gov.ck/crown-financial-reporting) still shows 2019 as the most recent published edition as of this research (11 Aug 2026), corroborating the backlog.

reports.title: Cook Islands Government Budget Estimates
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM), Cook Islands
reports.description: The annual appropriation estimates and commentary, Book 1. Punctual where the audited statements are not — the 2026/27 edition is dated May 2026, with the Minister's Statement of Responsibility dated Thursday 21 May 2026. Contains the economic forecasts, a forecasting model built with Asian Development Bank technical assistance, and an explicit statement that the fiscal information follows the IMF's Government Finance Statistics Manual 2014.

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar or explicit statutory deadline date was found on MFEM's or Parliament's site. However, multiple years show a consistent pattern: the Budget Estimates (Book 1/Book 2) are finalized and tabled in Parliament in May, ahead of the Cook Islands fiscal year start of 1 July, with parliamentary debate/passage sometimes extending into June (e.g. the FY2022/23 Budget Book 1 PDF is dated 17 May 2022 per its filename '...FINAL-20220517...'; a Public Accounts Committee 'Budget Review 2024-2025' report is dated 10 June 2024, implying the budget itself was tabled earlier that May; multiple Cook Islands News/RNZ articles on the '2025/26' and '2026/27' National Budgets appeared in the May-June window of 2025 and 2026 respectively). As of 2026-08-11, the FY2026/27 Budget has already been passed (RNZ: 'Cook Islands: $3 million boost for social welfare in record 2026/27 National Budget'; Cook Islands News: 'Parliament approves massive $375m budget'), so the next edition expected is the FY2027/28 Budget Estimates, projected for around May 2027 based on the observed pattern. Could not fetch MFEM/Parliament pages directly this session (WebFetch tool was rate-limited), so this is based on WebSearch result titles/snippets and known document filenames rather than a directly-read calendar page.

reports.title: Cook Islands Government Half-Year Economic and Fiscal Update

Carries its own Accounting Policies chapter for the forecast financial statements, whose Statement of Compliance names the IPSASB and — unusually candidly — points at a list of IPSAS standards the Government does not yet comply with.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, published in December: the 2023/24 edition is dated 14 December 2023 and the 2024/25 edition 10 December 2024.

entries.covers: 2026/27 Half-Year Economic and Fiscal Update (projected next release)

No statute or publisher rule stating an exact deadline was found; the pattern is a consistent mid-December release, roughly 6 months into the July-June fiscal year, so the 2026/27 edition is projected for mid-December 2026 (exact day not yet published as of 2026-08-11).

reports.title: National Accounts — Annual (Gross Domestic Product)
reports.description: The Cook Islands' annual GDP release, compiled mainly from VAT data on the production approach. Names SNA 2008 as its conceptual framework. NOTE THE INTERNAL CONFLICT this node resolves: the Statistics Office's own 'National Classifications' methodology page still describes the national accounts as 'largely based on' SNA68 with a series published 'from the year 1982-2001', while this release names SNA 2008 and carries data to 2024. Both are live on the same site. The methodology page is treated as stale and the release as current — see this slice's `_dropped` array, where the conflict is recorded rather than silently resolved.
reports.cadence_note: Annual release (the 2024 edition published 31 December 2025); quarterly GDP is also produced and is what the Budget forecasts from.

release_schedule.note: From the Cook Islands Ministry of Finance and Economic Management '2025-2026 Statistics Publication Calendar' PDF, which lists National Accounts (annual GDP by sector/industry) target release dates by reference calendar year: CY2025 -> May 2026, CY2026 -> May 2027 (the calendar explicitly states these are target dates and actual releases may occur before or after). As of today (2026-08-11) the National Accounts landing page (https://stats.gov.ck/national-accounts/) still shows 2024 as the latest completed annual edition (released 2025-12-31 per the 2024 report page), so the CY2025 annual report (targeted May 2026) appears overdue/delayed but not yet superseded by a later scheduled entry; it is kept as the first (soonest) entry rather than skipped, since it has not actually been published yet.

reports.publisher: Cook Islands Statistics Office (Ministry of Finance and Economic Management)
reports.description: The quarterly GDP release, split out from `ck-national-accounts` on 2026-08-06 because the Budget's forecasting model takes the quarterly series and not the annual one. Note that the Cook Islands Statistics Office attaches an identical 'More information on National Accounts' methodology block to both the quarterly and the annual release page, and that block is written for the quarterly series; see `_dropped`.
reports.cadence_note: Four releases a year, each roughly eight to nine months after the quarter it reports. The annual release is a separate publication on the same programme, dated 31 December 2025 for reference year 2024.

entries.covers: March Quarter 2025 and June Quarter 2025 GDP (both released together)
September Quarter 2025 and December Quarter 2025 GDP (both released together)
March Quarter 2026 and June Quarter 2026 GDP (projected next batch release)

release_schedule.note: No release calendar with future dates and no stated rule were found; the publisher's own '2025-26 Publication and Dissemination Calendar' PDF (https://stats.gov.ck/download/54/resources/6939/2025-26-publication-and-dissemination-calendar.pdf) lists nominal quarterly target months (Jul 2025, Oct 2025, Jan 2026, Apr 2026) but these targets are explicitly caveated ('reports may be released prior to or after the dates stated') and were badly missed in practice.
