reports.title: Cook Islands Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Quarterly consumer price index covering households on Rarotonga only, base year 2005, 205 priced items, weighted from the 2005 Household Income and Expenditure Survey and computed on the Laspeyres formula. NEGATIVE FINDING recorded on the node: the Statistics Office's own methodology text names the HIES as its weighting source but names NO external methodology manual — the IMF/ILO Consumer Price Index Manual (`cpi-manual`, already in this corpus) is not cited, unlike the SNA 2008 citation the national accounts carry.

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar found on the Cook Islands Statistics Office site. Publication is quarterly (matches releases_per_year=4 on file) but timing within each quarter varies: March-quarter CPI has been released Apr 4 2024, May 14 2025, and May 28 2026; June-quarter CPI released Aug 26 2024 and Aug 1 2025; September-quarter CPI released Nov 5 2024 and Nov 27 2025; December-quarter CPI released Feb 15 2024, Feb 14 2025, and Feb 25 2026. As of 2026-08-11 (today), the most recent published edition was March Quarter 2026 (released 2026-05-28); the June Quarter 2026 edition was not yet posted, so it is projected for August 2026 based on the prior two years' pattern.

reports.title: Government of Niue Consolidated Financial Statements
reports.description: Niue's whole-of-government consolidated financial statements. THE MOST STRUCTURALLY UNUSUAL NODE IN THIS SLICE: its Statement of Compliance names no external accounting framework at all, defining compliance by reference to the Government's own policies plus the Constitution of Niue and the Public Revenues Act 1959. Verified by grep over the full text of two separate sets — FY2023/FY2024 (26pp) and the five-year FY2017-21 document (37pp): zero occurrences of 'IPSAS', 'International Public Sector', 'XRB', 'New Zealand GAAP' or 'generally accepted accounting' in either. Niue has therefore never named an external standard back to FY2016 at least, which makes this a settled practice rather than an omission. Audited by the Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand under Article 60 of the Constitution of Niue — so Niue imports New Zealand's auditor while importing nobody's accounting standards.
reports.cadence_note: Nominally annual and in severe arrears until recently. FY2017-21 were reported as a SINGLE five-year document under the Public Revenues (Financial Reporting and Audit Special Provisions) Amendment Act 2022, a statute passed specifically to permit it. FY2023 was authorised for issue on 19 May 2025 and FY2024 on 22 May 2025 — two years of accounts signed three days apart.

release_schedule.note: Niue's Government of Niue Consolidated Financial Statements (fiscal year ends 30 June) have a long documented history of severe, inconsistent delay rather than a fixed annual cycle. A 2011 PEFA assessment already noted a multi-year backlog (latest audited statements at the time were for FY2007/08, with FY2008/09 and FY2009/10 not expected complete until mid-2012). As of 2025, the government paid Deloitte New Zealand roughly NZD 2 million to clear the backlog: the FY2023 (year ended 30 June 2023) consolidated statements were only published 20 June 2025 (~24 months after fiscal year-end), and the FY2024 (year ended 30 June 2024) statements were published in September 2025 (~14 months after fiscal year-end) — lags that vary too much to project a consistent 'time of year'. The Auditor-General publicly stated that maintaining timely ANNUAL reporting going forward is 'critical', expressing an aspiration rather than a codified rule with a specific deadline; no statute, regulation, or publisher-stated numeric deadline (e.g. 'within N months of fiscal year end') could be found. As of 2026-08-11, no FY2025 (year ended 30 June 2025) consolidated financial statements have yet been posted on mof.gov.nu. Given the chronic historical irregularity and absence of any stated rule or calendar, this is best treated as irregular rather than assigning a fabricated 'next' date.

reports.title: Report to the Assembly, Government of Niue (Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand)
reports.publisher: Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand
reports.description: The New Zealand Auditor-General's periodic report to the Niue Assembly on the audits of the Government of Niue and its State-Owned Entities. Published by a New Zealand office about a Niue government, under Niue's own constitutional appointment — one of the few documents in this corpus whose publisher and subject are in different countries by constitutional design rather than by choice. The most recent edition covers three financial years at once and describes the backlog it was clearing.
reports.cadence_note: Irregular, driven by the audit backlog rather than a schedule: the edition read this session covers the years ended 30 June 2022, 2023 and 2024 together and is dated 19 May 2025.

release_schedule.note: No release calendar or statutory deadline found. The 22J/23J/24J combined report (dated 19 May 2025, published 20 June 2025) closed a multi-year audit backlog with help from Deloitte NZ (~NZ$2m spent). The Auditor-General has stated an intent to keep future reporting timely/annual going forward (tvniue, 11 Jul 2025), but no calendar, statute, or fixed rule specifying exact release dates was found on oag.parliament.nz or mof.gov.nu, and no numbered pattern of releases at consistent times of year exists yet given the backlog history. This is consistent with the existing cadence_note.

reports.title: Public Revenues Act 1959 (Niue)
reports.description: Niue's public finance statute, originally the Public Revenues Ordinance 1959. Section 25 requires the annual accounts to be furnished, audited and presented to the Assembly; section 40 requires a statement of public moneys and investments. NEGATIVE FINDING: neither section names an accounting basis or a standard. Together with the Constitution's Articles 58-60 this is the whole of the legal specification of Niue's public accounts — it fixes who prepares them, who audits them and who receives them, and says nothing about how they are measured. That silence is what leaves `nu-government-financial-statements` free to define its own compliance.
reports.cadence_note: A consolidated statute, reprinted on amendment rather than published on a schedule.

release_schedule.note: This is a one-off/foundational legal instrument (an Act of the Niue Assembly governing public revenue administration), not a recurring statistical or administrative report. It is amended or reprinted irregularly as Niue's legislature sees fit (e.g. consolidated in periodic 'Niue Laws' compilations such as the 2006 edition), not on any fixed schedule. No release calendar, stated periodicity rule, or consistent-interval pattern of amendment/reissue was found on PacLII, gov.nu, or WIPO Lex. The releases_per_year=1 field on file appears to misclassify this as a recurring periodical; it should probably not carry a fixed cadence at all.

reports.title: Financial Statements of the Government of Tokelau
reports.description: The annual financial statements required by Rule 9 of the Tokelau Finance Rules 1998, prepared for the General Fono and audited by the Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand. CADENCE WARNING, and it is severe: the most recent publicly located instance covers FY2004 and reached this corpus through a New Zealand parliamentary paper (the Administrator of Tokelau's report, E.14), not through a Tokelau publication channel. This node rests on a live statutory requirement plus a twenty-two-year-old published instance. Treat its currency as unestablished until a future session finds a recent set — see this slice's `_dropped` array.
reports.cadence_note: Rule 9 requires preparation 'no later than 1 September in every year'. The most recent instance this session could locate covers the year ended 30 June 2004, published inside a New Zealand parliamentary paper.

entries.covers: Financial statements for the year ended 30 June 2026

release_schedule.rule: Rule 9 of the Tokelau Finance Rules 1998 requires the financial statements of the Government of Tokelau to be prepared no later than 1 September in every year.
release_schedule.note: Independently corroborated via the primary source PDF at the corpus's existing url (a NZ parliamentary paper, 'Report of the Administrator of Tokelau for the period ended 30 June 2006'), whose audit opinions for FY2002-FY2004 each cite preparation 'pursuant to Rule 9 of the Tokelau Finance Rules 1998.' Could not independently re-locate the primary text of the Tokelau Finance Rules 1998 itself (paclii.org, the main Pacific legislation repository, returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and direct curl through the proxy on every attempt), so the exact '1 September' wording relies on the pre-existing cadence_note rather than a freshly fetched rule text. No evidence was found of any financial statements published for a fiscal year after 30 June 2004 being publicly available — Tokelau Administration's own site (tokelau.org.nz) does not host a financial-statements release calendar or archive; only Trust Fund annual reports and sector reports were listed there.

reports.title: Tokelau Finance Rules 1998
reports.description: Tokelau's public finance rules. Requires annual financial statements prepared 'in accordance with generally accepted accounting practice' — WITHOUT SAYING WHOSE, which is the third distinct answer the Realm gives to the same question (Cook Islands names IPSAS; Niue names nothing and says so; Tokelau names an undefined GAAP). Separately installs the Auditor-General of New Zealand as auditor and requires every auditor in Tokelau to be qualified to act as an auditor in New Zealand.
reports.cadence_note: Made 1998, consolidated 2016. Amended rarely.

release_schedule.note: The Tokelau Finance Rules 1998 is a foundational legal instrument made by the General Fono (Tokelau's national legislative body), not a recurring statistical publication. PacLII's chronological table of General Fono Rules (paclii.austlii.edu.au/tk/indices/legis/rules-by-year.html) shows the original 1998 Finance rule followed by amendments in 2004 ('Finance Amendment'), 2006 ('Finance Amendment [Public Money]'), and 2015 ('Finance Amendment Rules') -- gaps of 6, 2, and 9 years respectively, with no stated periodicity. No General Fono or PacLII page describes a review calendar or fixed amendment cycle for these Rules; amendments occur whenever the General Fono decides to legislate on finance matters. This should not be treated as having a fixed release cadence.

Annual report 2024/25, Part 1: About us: "The Auditor-General is also the Auditor-General of the governments of Niue and Tokelau, and the Secretary-General of the Pacific Association of Supreme Audit Institutions (PASAI), which works to strengthen supreme audit institutions throughout the Pacific." The receiving instrument was already verified by the minting session and is unchanged — Tokelau Finance Rules 1998: "(1) There shall be an auditor of accounts for the Tokelau Administration. (2) The Auditor-General of New Zealand shall be the auditor of accounts which contain public money, and, unless legislation otherwise directs, of each body corporate of Tokelau." CORRECTION TO THIS SLICE'S OWN FRAMING, established this session and recorded in NZ/G.4.md Corrections. The `_dropped` note that this relation replaces said Tokelau's auditor is installed "by an instrument of the Tokelau Administration, Niue's by Niue's own Constitution, and neither by New Zealand law". The last clause is wrong for Tokelau. "Tokelau Administration" is listed by name in Schedule 2 of the New Zealand Public Audit Act 2001, "Specific public entities not falling within any class", referenced to s 5(1)(d) — so Tokelau is a New Zealand public entity by New Zealand statute, and is audited on that footing as well as under its own Finance Rules. Niue appears nowhere in the Act: a full-text search of the current consolidation returns one occurrence of "Tokelau" and zero of "Niue". The contrast therefore survives but runs the OTHER WAY from how the note stated it. Niue is the pure export-of-institution case — New Zealand law is silent and Niue's own Constitution reaches out to appoint a New Zealand statutory officer. Tokelau is doubly installed, and one of the two instruments is New Zealand's own.

_slice: Grande Prairie Public School Division — the education layer
_note: School authorities complete the local picture: the city and county tax bylaws collect an education requisition, and this is where that money lands. Alberta requires every school jurisdiction to file its budget on a standard provincial template, which makes this layer unusually easy to trace — the template itself names the Funding Manual, the enrolment counts, and the prior year's audited statements. Post-secondary was attempted and abandoned this pass; see _dropped.

reports.title: Approved Budget Report
reports.description: Annual budget filed on Alberta Education's standard template for school jurisdiction 3240, covering roughly $117 million of revenue against $118 million of expense for about 8,300 funded students. Discloses its own key assumptions, its enrolment projection, and the reserve limits it is tested against.
reports.cadence_note: School year ending August 31, so its cycle is offset from every municipal and provincial document in the graph by four months.

release_schedule.rule: Approved annual budget report submitted to the Province (Alberta Education) by May 31 each year, ahead of the school year that begins September 1. GPPSD's Division Planning page lists a distinct 'Approved Budget Report' for each school year (2024-2025, 2025-2026, 2026-2027), and the division's most recent budget (for 2026-27, ~$124.5M operating budget) was approved by its board in spring 2026 for the May 31, 2026 provincial submission deadline.
release_schedule.note: Alberta school boards approve their annual budget at a board meeting in May and submit it to Alberta Education by May 31 each year (confirmed via a comparable Alberta board's budget recommendation report stating 'the budget report will be submitted to the Province by May 31'). GPPSD's own board meeting schedule shows regular May meetings (e.g. May 25) consistent with this cycle. The most recent GPPSD budget (2026-27) was already approved before today's date (2026-08-11), so the next occurrence is the 2027-2028 budget, due by May 31, 2027.

reports.title: Audited Financial Statements
reports.description: Annual audited statements to August 31, establishing the accumulated surplus and reserve balances that the following year's budget opens from and is judged against.

entries.covers: Audited Financial Statements for fiscal year ended August 31, 2026

release_schedule.rule: The Board of Trustees approves the Audited Financial Statements annually, prior to submission to Alberta Education by November 30 (fiscal year ends August 31).
release_schedule.note: Province-wide Alberta Education requirement applying to all Alberta school jurisdictions (submission deadline November 30 for the fiscal year ended August 31). GPPSD's own Division Planning page (https://www.gppsd.ab.ca/our-division/division-planning) posts its Audited Financial Statements annually as of August 31 (most recent found: August 31, 2025, at https://www.gppsd.ab.ca/download/541261), consistent with this pattern, but does not itself state the November 30 submission deadline explicitly -- that wording was found on a peer Alberta school division's (Elk Island Public Schools) site, which cites the same Alberta Education requirement that governs GPPSD.

dependencies.basis: The budget template cites the manual by name and is structured around it: 'As per the 2024/25 Funding Manual, a formal request for an exemption to exceed the 2024/25 maximum operating reserve must be approved by the board and submitted to the Minister.' The 6% maximum operating reserve limit the division is tested against, and the grant rates its revenue is built from, both come from the manual — the budget notes ongoing deficits caused by 'rising operational costs ... without corresponding increases in grant rates'.
dependencies.evidence_quote: As per the 2024/25 Funding Manual, a formal request for an exemption to exceed the 2024/25 maximum operating reserve must be approved by the board and submitted to the Minister.

dependencies.basis: The Projected Student Statistics schedule reports 8,261 eligible funded students as 'Grade 1 to 12 students eligible for base instruction funding from Alberta Education', counted as at September 30 and reported to the province through PASI, alongside disability counts on the same basis. Nearly all of the division's $113 million of Government of Alberta revenue is these counts multiplied by rates.

reference_period.stated_as: Eligible funded students 'counted as at September 30' and reported to the province through PASI.

dependencies.basis: The accumulated surplus schedule opens from 'Actual balances per AFS at August 31, 2024' of $16,363,413 and carries audited actuals as a comparative column throughout. The budget cannot be built without the prior year's audit closing first.

reference_period.stated_as: Opens from 'Actual balances per AFS at August 31' of the prior year.

dependencies.evidence_quote: Actual balances per AFS at August 31, 2024

reports.title: Manual on sources and methods for the compilation of COFOG statistics
reports.description: Catalogue number KS-GQ-19-010, 2019 edition. Eurostat's guidance to EU and EFTA compilers on producing government expenditure broken down by function: user requirements, the analytical framework, the bridge tables national compilers use to map their own budget classifications onto COFOG, and a country-by-country account of recording practice, with an appendix reproducing COFOG 1999 with Task Force commentary. Its own back cover: it is 'developed and agreed by the Task Force on COFOG'. Distinct from the UN classification it implements (the corpus node un-cofog-1999), and a sibling of the corpus's eu-manual-mgdd and eu-manual-qfagg.
reports.cadence_note: Three editions, stated in the manual's own text: 'This Manual on sources and methods for the compilation of COFOG statistics is in its third edition, the first having been produced in 2007 and the second in 2011.' Latest observed interval 2011 to 2019, 8 years, so releases_per_year 1/8 = 0.13, following the convention eu-manual-mgdd uses.

reports.title: Nomenclature de consommation ouest-africaine adaptée pour l'indice harmonisé des prix à la consommation (NCOA-IHPC)
reports.description: The consumption nomenclature the harmonised consumer price indices of the UEMOA member states are built on. Derived from the international COICOP and adapted for the UEMOA zone as the Nomenclature de consommation ouest africaine (NCOA), then adapted again for the index itself as NCOA-IHPC: 12 functions, 41 groups, 78 sub-groups and 126 consumption items, with imputed rents and prostitution excluded by the index's own scope. Published by AFRISTAT under the UEMOA IHPC renovation project as the companion document to the methodology guide (the corpus node afristat-ihpc-guide-2014), which lists it among the reference documents for producing the renovated index. Carries no publication date of its own: an earlier corpus note dated it 2008, which the document does not state — its text places it in the IHPC96-to-renovated-base generation (it cites COICOP alongside the SCN 1993), before the NCOA 2018 that the current base-2023 series uses.
reports.cadence_note: A nomenclature, revised only when the index is rebased; nominal rate matching the corpus's other AFRISTAT nomenclature node.

reports.title: Основные направления единой государственной денежно-кредитной политики на 2026 год и период 2027 и 2028 годов (Monetary Policy Guidelines for 2026 and the 2027–2028 period)
reports.description: The Bank of Russia's own current monetary-policy document, and the only verified primary-source anchor for a Russia CPI/inflation node this round — Rosstat's own methodology and release pages (rosstat.gov.ru, gks.ru, fedstat.ru) were completely unreachable this round (see `_dropped`), so no node is minted directly under Rosstat. This document names Rosstat's ИПЦ (CPI) by agency and abbreviation as the specific statistic used for the Bank's inflation target, quoted directly: «Постоянная публичная количественная цель по инфляции. Цель – годовая инфляция вблизи 4%. Цель действует на постоянной основе. Инфляция рассчитывается на основе индекса потребительских цен (ИПЦ, Росстат). После стабилизации инфляции вблизи 4% Банк России оценит целесообразность снижения уровня цели. Снижение возможно не ранее 2029 года.» ("Permanent public quantitative inflation target — The target is annual inflation near 4%. The target applies on a permanent basis. Inflation is calculated based on the consumer price index (CPI, Rosstat). After inflation stabilizes near 4%, the Bank of Russia will assess the feasibility of lowering the target level. A reduction is possible no earlier than 2029.") The document does not cite a specific Rosstat release or order by number — only the agency and index abbreviation ("ИПЦ, Росстат").
reports.cadence_note: Annual. The Bank of Russia publishes one edition per year, each covering a rolling three-year horizon (this edition: 2026, with the 2027–2028 period); a listing page shows one annual edition back to 2009.

reports.title: Бюджетный кодекс Российской Федерации, ст. 131 — Дотации бюджетам субъектов Российской Федерации из федерального бюджета (Budget Code of the Russian Federation, Art. 131 — Equalization grants to regional budgets from the federal budget)
reports.publisher: Федеральное Собрание Российской Федерации / Президент Российской Федерации (Federal Assembly / President of the Russian Federation)
reports.description: Статья 131 of the Budget Code (от 31.07.1998 N 145-ФЗ), current редакция as of 26.06.2026, the statutory basis for Russia's дотации на выравнивание бюджетной обеспеченности — grants equalizing the 'budgetary sufficiency' of Russia's regions (субъекты), paid from the federal budget. FLAG: the only reachable full text was via consultant.ru (ConsultantPlus), a third-party legal-database mirror, not a .gov.ru host — pravo.gov.ru 502'd and its publication.pravo.gov.ru subdomain is JS-rendered with the specific document not locatable through it; the ConsultantPlus page itself is freely accessible with no paywall. Third-party-hosted verbatim government text, flagged as such. §1, quoted directly: «Дотации на выравнивание бюджетной обеспеченности субъектов Российской Федерации предусматриваются в составе федерального бюджета и распределяются между субъектами Российской Федерации в соответствии с единой методикой, утверждаемой Правительством Российской Федерации в соответствии с требованиями настоящего Кодекса.» ("Equalization grants ... are provided for within the federal budget and are distributed among the constituent entities in accordance with a unified methodology approved by the Government of the Russian Federation.") §§4/6 define 'budgetary sufficiency' via a tax-capacity ratio, quoted directly: «4. Дотации ... предоставляются субъектам Российской Федерации, уровень расчетной бюджетной обеспеченности которых не превышает уровня, установленного в качестве критерия выравнивания ... 6. Уровень расчетной бюджетной обеспеченности субъекта Российской Федерации определяется соотношением между расчетными налоговыми доходами на одного жителя ... и аналогичным показателем в среднем по консолидированным бюджетам субъектов Российской Федерации с учетом структуры населения, социально-экономических, географических, климатических и иных объективных факторов ...» — the direct Russian analogue of a 'tax capacity relative to national average' mechanism. §8 sets the annual calendar, quoted directly: «Министерство финансов Российской Федерации до 1 августа текущего финансового года направляет в исполнительные органы субъектов Российской Федерации исходные данные для проведения расчетов распределения дотаций ... и до 20 августа текущего финансового года проводит сверку указанных исходных данных с исполнительными органами субъектов Российской Федерации…» ("The Ministry of Finance ... shall, by 1 August, send ... the source data for calculating the distribution ... and shall, by 20 August, reconcile that source data ..."). The statute text itself carries a live ConsultantPlus editorial cross-reference: «Об особенностях распределения дотаций в 2026 г. см. Постановление Правительства РФ от 15.12.2025 N 2038.» ("On the specifics of the 2026 grant distribution, see Government of the Russian Federation Resolution No. 2038 of 15.12.2025.")

reports.title: Постановление Правительства РФ от 22.11.2004 N 670 (ред. от 15.12.2025) «О распределении дотаций на выравнивание бюджетной обеспеченности субъектов Российской Федерации» (Government of the Russian Federation Resolution No. 670 of 22.11.2004, as amended through 15.12.2025, "On the distribution of equalization grants for the budgetary sufficiency of constituent entities of the Russian Federation", together with the Methodology for distributing them)
reports.publisher: Правительство Российской Федерации (Government of the Russian Federation)
reports.description: The 'единая методика' (unified methodology) that Budget Code Art. 131 §1 delegates to the Government to approve — reached by following that article's own hyperlink. That page confirms the resolution's exact number, its original date (22.11.2004), and its current-as-of-amendment date (15.12.2025 — matching the '№2038' amendment cited in Art. 131's own editorial note) and exact title. THE ACTUAL FORMULA TEXT IS UNVERIFIED / NOT FOUND: ConsultantPlus's free-tier version restricts this specific document to a limited access schedule ("доступен по расписанию: по рабочим дням с 20-00 до 24-00 ... в выходные и праздничные дни в любое время") that could not be reached live within that window this round, and no working government-hosted full text was found either (government.ru's own search function returned stale cached results from a fixed 2012–2017 date window regardless of query; pravo.gov.ru returned 502). This node therefore records the resolution's identity, existence and amendment history as confirmed, and its operative formula wording as explicitly not independently verified.

Published/modified 15.12.2025, the exact same date as the Resolution No. 2038 amendment named in Budget Code Art. 131's own editorial note. Underlying data file: https://minfin.gov.ru/common/upload/library/2025/12/main/Uroven_raschetnoy_budzhetnoy_obespechennosti.xlsx (XLSX, 22.47 KB). Verbatim extract of the per-region index table, quoted directly: «Субъекты Российской Федерации / Уровень расчетной бюджетной обеспеченности / Индекс бюджетных расходов — Белгородская область 1.101 0.815; Брянская область 0.735 0.861; Владимирская область 0.832 0.899; Воронежская область 0.898 0.822; … Московская область 1.218 0.957 …» ("Constituent entities of the Russian Federation / Level of estimated budgetary sufficiency / Budget expenditure index — Belgorod Region 1.101, 0.815; Bryansk Region 0.735, 0.861; Vladimir Region 0.832, 0.899; Voronezh Region 0.898, 0.822; ... Moscow Region 1.218, 0.957 ..."), Russia's direct structural analogue to a per-capita-income-based coefficient table: an index below 1.0 signals fiscal capacity below the national average (eligible for equalization), above 1.0 signals above-average capacity. A companion, earlier-cycle document — "Распределение дотаций на выравнивание бюджетной обеспеченности субъектов Российской Федерации на 2025 год и плановый период 2026 и 2027 годов", published 29.11.2024 (https://minfin.gov.ru/ru/document?id_4=310185-raspredelenie_dotatsii_na_vyravnivanie_byudzhetnoi_obespechennosti_subektov_rossiiskoi_federatsii_na_2025_god_i_planovyi_period_2026_i_2027_godov) — confirms the same document is produced annually on a rolling planning-period basis; its PDF contents were not extracted for quoting.

dependencies.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY. Art. 131 §1's own text names the unified methodology and delegates its approval to the Government: «...распределяются между субъектами Российской Федерации в соответствии с единой методикой, утверждаемой Правительством Российской Федерации в соответствии с требованиями настоящего Кодекса.» Following that citation's own hyperlink (as reproduced on the ConsultantPlus mirror of Art. 131) led directly to Постановление Правительства РФ от 22.11.2004 N 670, whose title, number and current amendment date (15.12.2025) match the '№2038' amendment Art. 131's own editorial note separately names. `cites` rather than `methodology_depends_on`: the statute's own text was independently confirmed to name and link to this specific instrument as the approving authority, but the resolution's own operative formula text remains unverified (see that node's description and the corresponding `_dropped` entry), so the edge records the documented citation rather than a verified computational dependency.

Minted on a temporal-and-subject convergence, stated plainly so a reader can judge it, rather than on any single sentence declaring the link. Постановление N 670 is currently in force 'ред. от 15.12.2025' — i.e., its text as amended effective 15.12.2025, the amendment Budget Code Art. 131's own editorial note names as governing '2026 г.' grant distribution. The Ministry of Finance's 'Уровень расчетной бюджетной обеспеченности ... на 2026 год' document is dated/published on that exact same day, 15.12.2025, and concerns exactly the subject that instrument's title describes — the distribution of дотации на выравнивание бюджетной обеспеченности. Two independently primary/near-primary Russian government sources (a ConsultantPlus-mirrored resolution page and a minfin.gov.ru-hosted publication) converge on the same date and the same mechanism. `cites` rather than `calculated_from`/`methodology_depends_on`, deliberately the most conservative of the four relationship types available: no document text says in so many words that the Minfin table was produced by applying Resolution 670's formula, and that formula itself was never independently read (see `_dropped`), so the edge records the documented convergence rather than an unverified computational claim.

The `rosstat.gov.ru` "TLS connection reset" was a trust-store gap: Russian government sites are served under Russia's own national CA ("Russian Trusted Root CA", Минцифры), which ships in no standard bundle, and the server sends only its leaf certificate. With the root plus the 2024 sub-CA appended, every fetch returns verify=0 at TIER A. (The trap: the older, more commonly cited Russian sub-CA does not match the leaf's Authority Key Identifier and will not validate.) `ru-rosstat-cpi` and `ru-rosstat-cpi-methodology-915` are now both minted from Rosstat's own host, and the edge named in this note's endpoints is live. Consequently `ru-cbr-monetary-policy-guidelines` no longer needs to stand in for a CPI node -- it remains a legitimate node in its own right, but its stand-in ROLE has lapsed. _dropped.why: RESOLVED 2026-08-13 (BRICS/G.2): The operative formula was never paywalled. G.1 recorded it as locked behind ConsultantPlus's limited free-access window; in fact Minfin publishes the consolidated methodology itself, TIER A on its own host -- bundled INSIDE the ZIP archive it issues as the equalization input data (`Dotatsii_na_vyravnivanie.zip`, which contains 84 per-region .xls workbooks plus `Методика распределения дотаций на выравнивание.pdf`). That bundling is precisely why G.1 could not find it: it is not published as a standalone page anywhere. The core formula is «БОi = ИНПi / ИБРi» (level of estimated budgetary capacity = index of tax potential / index of budget expenditure), with both components defined and worked through in Приложения 1 and 2, including the expenditure index's own weights (0,5 wages / 0,10 utilities / 0,35 other / 0,05 social load) and its regional price-level coefficient. The archive also carries the data-supply clause obliging Rosstat and the Federal Tax Service to report to Minfin «ежегодно, до 1 августа». Full detail in `ru-g2-rosstat-equalization.json`. _status: NEW 2026-08-13. Russia's second slice, and the round that overturns round 1's central conclusion about this branch. `ru-cpi-equalization.json` (BRICS/G.1) recorded Rosstat as completely unreachable and, in the absence of any Rosstat-hosted document, sourced Russia's CPI building block indirectly to the Bank of Russia's own monetary-policy guidelines, which name Rosstat's ИПЦ without being Rosstat's text. That was a misdiagnosis, not a block -- see `_note`. With the diagnosis corrected, this file mints the real Rosstat CPI node (`ru-rosstat-cpi`) plus the standing Rosstat order that defines its method (`ru-rosstat-cpi-methodology-915`), and closes the second round-1 gap as well: Постановление 670's operative equalization formula, recorded at G.1 as paywalled on a third-party mirror, turns out to be published by the Ministry of Finance itself, bundled inside the very ZIP archive Minfin publishes as the equalization input data. Seven new nodes in total, spanning the four institutions this branch runs through -- Rosstat (CPI + its methodology), Minfin (the statutory input-data publication), the legislature/Government (the annual federal budget law, the 2025 amending resolution, and the subsistence-minimum statute), the Bank of Russia (the live key-rate decision series), and the Federal Treasury (budget-execution reporting). Two of this file's edges reach back into `ru-cpi-equalization.json` (`ru-resolution-670-equalization-methodology`), reusing rather than re-minting that node. This round also produced three deliberate NEGATIVE findings that are more interesting than several of the positives -- see `_dropped`: the Bank of Russia's key-rate releases never name Rosstat; the Monetary Policy Report was discontinued in February 2024; and Russia's subsistence minimum and minimum wage are NOT CPI-indexed at all, which directly contradicts the CPI-to-benefits pattern this corpus documents for most other countries.
_note: ACCESS AND VERIFICATION. The headline methodological finding of this round, recorded here because it is reusable project-wide and not merely a Russia fact: round 1's `rosstat.gov.ru` "TLS connection reset" was a TRUST-STORE GAP, not an egress block or a WAF. Since 2022 Russian government sites are served under Russia's own national certificate authority ("Russian Trusted Root CA", Минцифры), which is present in no standard CA bundle. Diagnosis chain, every step verified this round: `curl -k` returned HTTP 200 / 827KB; the presented certificate is genuinely Rosstat's (CN=*.rosstat.gov.ru, OGRN=1047708023483, Мясницкая 39с1); the server sends ONLY the leaf certificate (chain depth 1), and the leaf's AIA extension points at CDP hosts that themselves serve a captcha. The correct intermediate is published at `gu-st.ru/.../russian_trusted_sub_ca_2024_pem.crt`, whose Subject Key Identifier `77:3D:D9:39...` matches the leaf's Authority Key Identifier. THE TRAP: the older, far more commonly cited sub-CA (SKI `D1:E1:71...`) does NOT match and will not validate -- a session that grabs the first Russian sub-CA it finds will wrongly conclude the site is broken. With the root plus the 2024 sub-CA appended to the bundle, every fetch below returns `verify=0`, i.e. genuine TIER A on the government's own host. The r.jina.ai rendering proxy was never needed and never used for Russia this round. TIERS: `rosstat.gov.ru`, `minfin.gov.ru`, `cbr.ru`, `roskazna.gov.ru` and `publication.pravo.gov.ru` all reached TIER A (plain curl, genuine HTTP 200, real document bytes). NOTE `pravo.gov.ru` serves over HTTP only -- `https://pravo.gov.ru/` fails outright while `http://publication.pravo.gov.ru/` returns 200 -- and its ИПС viewer is windows-1251 encoded, which decodes as mojibake if read as UTF-8 and can be mistaken for a failed fetch. OCR CAVEAT, important: several of this round's federal-law PDFs on pravo.gov.ru (426-ФЗ, Постановление 2038, 473-ФЗ) are image-only scans with no text layer, OCR'd here with `tesseract -l rus --psm 6` after installing Russian tessdata. Every quotation drawn from those four documents is OCR OUTPUT -- approximately 99% accurate but NOT byte-exact -- and is labelled as such at the point of use below. Quotes from Rosstat's own PDFs, Minfin's methodology PDF and the cbr.ru/roskazna.gov.ru pages are true verbatim from a real text layer, not OCR. STILL GENUINELY UNREACHABLE, each for a DIFFERENT reason and recorded separately rather than as one blanket claim: `gks.ru` (TCP reset), `fedstat.ru` (403 WAF), and `showdata.gks.ru` / `eng.rosstat.gov.ru` (certificate failures that the Russian national CA does NOT fix). Every `basis` below is this session's own read of the underlying research.

reports.title: Индексы потребительских цен на товары и услуги (Consumer price indices for goods and services)
reports.publisher: Федеральная служба государственной статистики (Росстат) / Federal State Statistics Service
reports.description: Rosstat's own consumer price index release -- the node BRICS/G.1 could not mint and for which `ru-cbr-monetary-policy-guidelines` was standing in. That stand-in is no longer necessary. Rosstat's own definitions document states the index's purpose verbatim: «Индекс потребительских цен (ИПЦ) является одним из важнейших показателей, характеризующих фактически сложившийся уровень инфляции, и используется для целей государственной финансовой и денежно-кредитной политики, анализа и прогноза ценовых процессов в экономике, изучения динамики социально-экономических явлений, пересмотра минимальных социальных гарантий, решения правовых споров, а также при пересчете макроэкономических показателей из текущих цен в сопоставимые цены.» ("The CPI is one of the most important indicators characterising the actual level of inflation, and is used for the purposes of state financial and monetary policy, analysis and forecasting of price processes in the economy, study of the dynamics of socio-economic phenomena, revision of minimum social guarantees, resolution of legal disputes, and also for recalculating macroeconomic indicators from current prices into comparable prices.") IMPORTANT DIRECTION NOTE: that sentence is Rosstat describing the DOWNSTREAM uses of its own output -- the source naming its consumers, not a dependent naming its input. It is therefore suggestive but not edge-qualifying in this corpus's direction, and no edge is minted from it; the «пересмотра минимальных социальных гарантий» clause in particular is contradicted in the specific case of the subsistence minimum, which is not CPI-indexed at all (see `ru-subsistence-minimum-law-134fz` and the `_dropped` entry on it). Price collection is stated verbatim as: «Источник — Регистрация цен непосредственно с прилавков организаций; данные онлайн–агрегаторов (авиа и железнодорожных по продаже билетов, туроператоров и других) и маркетплейсов.» ("Source — price registration directly from organisations' counters; data from online aggregators (air and rail ticket sales, tour operators and others) and marketplaces.") Live data files were confirmed on the product page dated 12.08.2026, the day before this research: `Nedel_ipc.xlsx` (weekly indices), `ipc_mes_07-2026.xlsx` (monthly indices, series from 1991, fetched HTTP 200 / 37,871 bytes and confirmed a valid xlsx), `ipc_RF_fo_sub_07-2026.xlsx` (by federal district and federal subject) and `ipc_kv2_2005-2026.xlsx` (quarterly). Fetched this session with plain curl at TIER A against Rosstat's own host, using the Russian national CA bundle described in this file's `_note`.
reports.cadence_note: Rosstat publishes this index on four simultaneous cadences, stated verbatim in its own definitions document: «Периодичность    Недельная, Месячная, Квартальная, Годовая» and «Сроки обновления на сайте / Недельная – еженедельно по средам / Месячная - на 6-10-й рабочий день месяца, следующего за отчетным / Квартальная - на 6-10-й рабочий день месяца, следующего за отчетным кварталом / Годовая - на 6-10-й рабочий день месяца, следующего за отчетным годом» ("Periodicity: weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual. Site update deadlines: weekly – every Wednesday; monthly – on the 6th-10th working day of the month following the reporting month; quarterly – on the 6th-10th working day of the month following the reporting quarter; annual – on the 6th-10th working day of the month following the reporting year.") `releases_per_year` is set to 12 for the headline monthly index, the cadence the branch's downstream instruments actually reference; the weekly sub-series (52, every Wednesday) and the quarterly and annual roll-ups run alongside it from the same collection.

reports.title: Приказ Росстата от 15 декабря 2021 г. № 915 «Об утверждении Официальной статистической методологии наблюдения за потребительскими ценами на товары и услуги и расчета индексов потребительских цен»
reports.description: The standing Rosstat order approving the official statistical methodology behind the consumer price index -- the instrument BRICS/G.1 recorded as NOT FOUND. Its enabling clause establishes it as a standing instrument and, incidentally, supplies this round's independent corroboration that Постановление Правительства РФ № 420 of 2 June 2008 is the instrument constituting Rosstat: «В соответствии с подпунктом 5.2 Положения о Федеральной службе государственной статистики, утвержденного постановлением Правительства Российской Федерации от 2 июня 2008 г. № 420, п р и к а з ы в а ю: 1. Утвердить Официальную статистическую методологию наблюдения за потребительскими ценами на товары и услуги и расчета индексов потребительских цен (далее – Методология) (приложение № 1).» The observation cadence is fixed by the methodology itself, §5.2 «Периодичность и масштаб наблюдения» п.15: «Регистрация цен и тарифов осуществляется: по полному перечню товаров (услуг)-представителей, утвержденному соответствующим приказом Росстата, для расчета индекса потребительских цен – ежемесячно по состоянию на конец месяца (по установленному графику)… по сокращенному перечню товаров (услуг)-представителей, определенному соответствующим приказом Росстата – еженедельно по состоянию на пятницу.» The index formula is named explicitly: «Расчет ИПЦ к предыдущему месяцу осуществляется в соответствии с модифицированной формулой Ласпейреса» ("The CPI relative to the previous month is calculated in accordance with the modified Laspeyres formula"). The weights source is also named, and is an internal dependency this round could not follow to a node: «Для формирования Набора анализируются итоги выборочного обследования бюджетов домашних хозяйств, проводимого на территории всех субъектов Российской Федерации, в группировке Классификатора индивидуального потребления домашних хозяйств по целям (далее – КИПЦ-ДХ).» and «веса – мера относительной значимости товаров (услуг) в рамках сводного индекса цен, определяемая на основе потребительских расходов домашних хозяйств» -- the household budget survey itself was not separately located this round (see `_dropped`). Fetched TIER A from Rosstat's own host; the first attempt returned `curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`, which is Rosstat rate-limiting rather than a block, and succeeded on retry after a 6-second backoff.
reports.cadence_note: A standing methodological instrument, amended rather than reissued on a cadence -- the same convention this corpus applies to statutes and standing orders elsewhere (e.g. `br-lc-62-1989`, `br-lei-8443`).

reports.title: Исходные данные для проведения расчетов распределения дотаций на выравнивание бюджетной обеспеченности субъектов Российской Федерации
reports.description: Minfin's published input-data archive for the regional equalization calculation -- the publication BRICS/G.1 recorded as a `no-node-yet` drop on the strength of the Budget Code's own publication requirement, without being able to locate it. It exists, it is published on Minfin's own host, and it is the literal input to the equalization formula. The archive contains 85 files: 84 per-region `.xls` workbooks (`altayskiy_kray.xls`, `respublika_dagestan.xls`, `g_moskva.xls`, `yamalo_nenetskiy_avtonomnyy_okrug.xls`, and so on, 64,512 bytes each) PLUS `Методика распределения дотаций на выравнивание.pdf` (866,913 bytes) -- which is the consolidated operative text of Постановление 670 itself, the document BRICS/G.1 recorded as paywalled on ConsultantPlus. That bundling is why round 1 could not find the formula: it is not published as a standalone page anywhere, it ships inside this data archive. The record page states publication timing verbatim: «Опубликован в разделе: 2026-2028 годы … Опубликовано: 10.06.2025 Изменено: 10.06.2025». Sibling publications confirmed live in the same Minfin section and available as future nodes: «Дополнительные данные для проведения расчетов распределения дотаций…», «Распределение дотаций на выравнивание бюджетной обеспеченности субъектов Российской Федерации на 2026 год и плановый период 2027 и 2028 годов», «Исходные данные по единой субвенции на 2026 год…», and «Исходные данные для проведения расчетов распределения дотаций на частичную компенсацию дополнительных расходов на повышение оплаты труда работников бюджетной сферы и иные цели». Fetched TIER A: the record page returned HTTP 200 / 35,029 bytes and the payload ZIP HTTP 200 / 1,963,545 bytes with content-type `application/zip`, confirmed a real Zip archive by `file` and unpacked with python's `zipfile`.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, keyed to the rolling three-year budget cycle. FLAGGED AS INFERRED, not quoted: the record page states a publication date («Опубликовано: 10.06.2025»), not a periodicity sentence. The annual cadence is inferred from the parallel Minfin section series (`mb2020_2022`, `mb2026_2028`, and so on) and is consistent with Постановление 670's own «ежегодно, до 1 августа» data-supply deadline -- publication on 10.06.2025 precedes the 01.08.2025 deadline for the 2026 cycle.

reports.title: Постановление Правительства Российской Федерации от 15.12.2025 № 2038 «О внесении изменений в некоторые акты Правительства Российской Федерации»
reports.description: The Government resolution amending the equalization methodology for the 2026 cycle, and the instrument that puts an explicit inflation floor under every region's equalization grant. BRICS/G.1 recorded it as `unreadable-source`; it is TIER A on `publication.pravo.gov.ru`, the official government publication portal. ALL QUOTATIONS BELOW ARE OCR OUTPUT -- the official PDF is a 10-page scan with no text layer (`pdftotext` yielded 10 bytes), OCR'd with `tesseract -l rus --psm 6` -- approximately 99% accurate but not byte-exact. The amending clause names its target and supplies the fund's full official amendment history: «1. Утвердить прилагаемые изменения, которые вносятся в методику распределения дотаций на выравнивание бюджетной обеспеченности субъектов Российской Федерации, утвержденную постановлением Правительства Российской Федерации от 22 ноября 2004 г. № 670 "О распределении дотаций на выравнивание бюджетной обеспеченности субъектов Российской Федерации" (Собрание законодательства Российской Федерации, 2004, № 48, ст. 4797; 2006, № 39, ст. 4088; … 2024, № 1, ст. 200; № 52, ст. 8333).» The operative inflation floor: «2. Установить, что: а) объем дотации на выравнивание бюджетной обеспеченности субъекта Российской Федерации на 2026 год не может быть менее утвержденного на 2025 год объема такой дотации бюджетам субъектов Российской Федерации, увеличенного на прогнозируемый уровень инфляции на конец 2026 года, учтенный при формировании федерального бюджета на 2026 год и плановый период 2027 и 2028 годов, для субъектов Российской Федерации, в которых реализуется программа комплексного восстановления и развития пострадавших территорий;» ("the volume of the equalization dotation for 2026 may not be less than the volume approved for 2025, increased by the forecast level of inflation at end-2026 as taken into account in the formation of the federal budget for 2026 and the planning period 2027 and 2028…"). A symmetrical ceiling is set at «г) прирост объема дотации … в 2026 году не может превышать 10 процентов по отношению к 2025 году;». It also repeals a provision of its own predecessor: «4. Пункт 3 постановления Правительства Российской Федерации от 16 декабря 2024 г. № 1792 … признать утратившим силу.» The inflation figure the floor points at is verbatim recoverable from the budget law itself -- see `ru-federal-budget-law-2026` -- which closes a complete, fully evidenced chain from a named forecast number to a regional grant amount.
reports.cadence_note: An amending instrument rather than a recurring release -- the same convention this corpus applies to amending statutes elsewhere (e.g. `br-lc-62-1989`, which is carried as a single node amended rather than reissued). It is minted as a node rather than folded into `ru-resolution-670-equalization-methodology` because it carries operative rules of its own (the inflation floor and the 10% growth ceiling) that the consolidated 670 text does not contain.

reports.title: Федеральный закон от 28.11.2025 № 426-ФЗ «О федеральном бюджете на 2026 год и на плановый период 2027 и 2028 годов»
reports.publisher: Российская Федерация / Официальный интернет-портал правовой информации
reports.description: Russia's annual federal budget law, and the document that carries the inflation forecast the equalization floor in `ru-resolution-2038-2025` points back at. ALL QUOTATIONS BELOW ARE OCR OUTPUT -- the official PDF is 5,381 pages and image-only (`pdftotext -f 1 -l 30` yielded 30 bytes), OCR'd with `tesseract -l rus --psm 6` -- approximately 99% accurate but not byte-exact, with visible OCR artefacts noted where they occur. Article 1 states the macroeconomic frame including the inflation number: «Статья 1. Основные характеристики федерального бюджета на 2026 год и на плановый период 2027 и 2028 годов. 1. Утвердить основные характеристики федерального бюджета на 2026 год, определенные исходя из прогнозируемого объема валового внутреннего продукта в размере 235 067 млрд. рублей и уровня инфляции, не превышающего 4,0 процента (декабрь 2026 года к декабрю 2025 года): 1) прогнозируемый общий объем доходов федерального бюджета в сумме 40 283 269 170,5 тыс. рублей; 2) общий объем расходов федерального бюджета в сумме 44 069 704 164,5 тыс. рублей; … 5) дефицит федерального бюджета в сумме 3 786 434 994,0 тыс. рублей.» The law cites the Budget Code repeatedly in its own text -- «В соответствии с пунктом 2 статьи 184-1 Бюджетного кодекса Российской Федерации утвердить нормативы распределения доходов…», and separately arts. 242-3, 242-7 and 80 -- but NOT art. 131, which is why no edge is minted from this law to `ru-budget-code-art131` (see `_dropped`). The equalization article, whose number OCR renders as "Статья 19" but which is unambiguously Статья 10 from the surrounding sequence, reads: «Статья 10. Межбюджетные трансферты бюджетам субъектов Российской Федерации и бюджету города Байконура. 1. Утвердить бюджетные ассигнования на предоставление межбюджетных трансфертов … согласно приложению 28 … 4. Дотации на выравнивание бюджетной обеспеченности субъектов Российской Федерации рассчитываются раздельно для бюджетов Архангельской области (без автономного округа), Ненецкого автономного округа, Тюменской области (без автономных округов), Ханты-Мансийского автономного округа - Югры, Ямало-Ненецкого автономного округа.» The law also fixes the year's subsistence-minimum figures directly, Статья 8 ч.4: «Установить в 2026 году величину прожиточного минимума в целом по Российской Федерации на душу населения в размере 18 939 рублей, для трудоспособного населения - 20 644 рублей, пенсионеров - 16 288 рублей, детей - 18 371 рубля.» Fetched TIER A from the official publication portal (HTTP 200, 195,811,243 bytes). Portal note: `HEAD` returns 405 there, so a range request is the way to size a file before downloading.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, on a rolling three-year horizon (the budget year plus a two-year planning period). FLAGGED AS INFERRED, not quoted: the periodicity follows from the instrument type and the title series rather than from any "periodicity" sentence, since no such sentence exists inside a budget law.

reports.title: Федеральный закон № 134-ФЗ «О прожиточном минимуме в Российской Федерации», ст. 4 в редакции Федерального закона от 29.12.2020 № 473-ФЗ
reports.publisher: Российская Федерация / Официальный интернет-портал правовой информации
reports.description: The statute defining how Russia's subsistence minimum (прожиточный минимум) and, in the same amending law, the minimum wage (МРОТ) are set -- and the source of this round's most significant negative finding for the corpus as a whole. ALL QUOTATIONS BELOW ARE OCR OUTPUT from an image-only scan (Creator: ABBYY FineReader Engine 11, 11 pages), OCR'd with `tesseract -l rus --psm 6`; approximately 99% accurate, not byte-exact. Since 2021 neither quantity is CPI-indexed. The rewritten Article 4 reads: «Статья 4. Величина прожиточного минимума, периодичность ее исчисления и порядок установления. 1. Величина прожиточного минимума на душу населения в целом по Российской Федерации на очередной год устанавливается до 1 июля текущего года Правительством Российской Федерации с учетом мнения Российской трехсторонней комиссии по регулированию социально-трудовых отношений и исчисляется исходя из величины медианного среднедушевого дохода за предыдущий год. Соотношение величины прожиточного минимума на душу населения в целом по Российской Федерации и величины медианного среднедушевого дохода за предыдущий год с 2021 года устанавливается в размере 44,2 процента. … величина прожиточного минимума … не может быть установлена ниже величины прожиточного минимума … установленной на текущий год.» The parallel minimum-wage rule: «минимальный размер оплаты труда на очередной год устанавливается федеральным законом в текущем году и исчисляется исходя из величины медианной заработной платы, рассчитанной федеральным органом исполнительной власти, осуществляющим функции по формированию официальной статистической информации … С 2021 года соотношение минимального размера оплаты труда и медианной заработной платы устанавливается в размере 42 процентов. … Минимальный размер оплаты труда … устанавливается в размере не ниже величины прожиточного минимума трудоспособного населения…» The same amending law defines median income and assigns its calculation: «медианный среднедушевой доход - величина денежного дохода, относительно которой половина населения в целом по Российской Федерации имеет значение среднедушевого дохода ниже данной величины, другая половина - выше данной величины и которая ежегодно исчисляется федеральным органом исполнительной власти, осуществляющим функции по формированию официальной статистической информации о социальных, экономических, демографических, экологических и других общественных процессах в Российской Федерации». IDENTIFICATION NOTE, recorded honestly: the law NEVER writes the word «Росстат» -- a search of the OCR text returned 0 hits for `Росстат` and 0 for `статистик` as a standalone agency name. It uses only the statutory periphrasis quoted above, which designates Rosstat by way of Постановление Правительства РФ от 2 июня 2008 г. № 420, independently corroborated at TIER A this round because Rosstat's own Приказ № 915 opens by citing that same Положение. The identification is therefore sound but is an INFERENCE ACROSS TWO DOCUMENTS, not a literal naming -- which is why no edge is minted to a Rosstat median-income node here (see `_dropped`).
reports.cadence_note: A standing statute, amended rather than reissued -- same convention as `ru-rosstat-cpi-methodology-915` in this file and `br-lc-62-1989` in the Brazil slice. The quantity it governs is set annually («устанавливается до 1 июля текущего года»), but the statute itself is not a recurring release.

reports.title: Пресс-релиз по ключевой ставке / Материалы по итогам заседаний Совета директоров Банка России по ключевой ставке
reports.description: The Bank of Russia's live recurring monetary-policy decision series, minted here in place of the Monetary Policy Report («Доклад о денежно-кредитной политике»), which this round confirmed was DISCONTINUED in February 2024 and is therefore not eligible as a live node under this project's no-discontinued-programmes rule -- see `_dropped` for the Bank's own verbatim announcement. The series comprises the key-rate press release issued at each Board meeting, plus the companion «Резюме обсуждения ключевой ставки» published roughly two weeks later and the «Комментарий к среднесрочному прогнозу» after core rounds. The 2026 decision sequence, verbatim from the Bank's own decisions index: «24 июля 2026 г. 13:30 Банк России принял решение снизить ключевую ставку на 25 б.п., до 14,00% годовых / 19 июня 2026 г. 13:30 … до 14,25% годовых / 24 апреля 2026 г. 13:30 … на 50 б.п., до 14,50% годовых / 20 марта 2026 г. 13:30 … до 15,00% годовых / 13 февраля 2026 г. 13:30 … до 15,50% годовых / 19 декабря 2025 г. 13:30 … до 16,00% годовых / 24 октября 2025 г. 13:30 … до 16,50% годовых». From the latest release body: «Совет директоров Банка России 24 июля 2026 года принял решение снизить ключевую ставку на 25 б.п., до 14,00% годовых. … Оценка показателей устойчивой инфляции остается в диапазоне 4–5% в пересчете на год…» and «Следующее заседание Совета директоров Банка России … запланировано на 11 сентября 2026 года. Время публикации пресс-релиза о решении Совета директоров Банка России – 13:30 по московскому времени.» VERIFIED NEGATIVE, recorded rather than assumed: the release does NOT name Rosstat or the ИПЦ as its inflation input. A search of the full extracted text of the 24.07.2026 release returned 0 hits each for `Росстат`, `росстат` and `статистик`. No edge is asserted from this node to `ru-rosstat-cpi` on the strength of this document -- see `_dropped`. Fetched TIER A from cbr.ru.
reports.cadence_note: Eight scheduled Board meetings per year, each producing a press release at a fixed time, per the Bank's own published calendar: «Предполагаемое время публикации пресс-релиза — 13:30 по московскому времени / Предполагаемое время начала пресс-конференции — 15:00 по московскому времени», with the calendar itself listing e.g. «13 февраля 2026 года Заседание Совета директоров Банка России по ключевой ставке / Пресс-релиз по ключевой ставке … 26 февраля 2026 года Резюме обсуждения ключевой ставки … 20 марта 2026 года Заседание Совета директоров…». The calendar archive runs 2014-2026.
