The Financial Market Development Programme elaborates the Bank of Russia’s statutory function of developing the financial market of the Russian Federation and ensuring its stability under Federal Law 86-FZ.

Supervision and publication of key indicators of insurers form part of the Bank of Russia’s regulation, control and supervision in the sphere of financial markets under the expanded mandate of Federal Law 86-FZ.
Supervision of non-governmental pension funds and publication of their key indicators are exercised under the Bank of Russia’s financial-market regulatory powers in Federal Law 86-FZ.
Regulation and statistical monitoring of unit investment funds and management companies fall under the Bank of Russia’s financial-market supervision mandate in Federal Law 86-FZ.

The regulatory framework and statistical monitoring of the digital financial assets market are developed and published by the Bank of Russia under its financial-market development and supervision functions.
Payment-system operational statistics are compiled in the exercise of the Bank of Russia’s supervision and oversight functions under Federal Law 161-FZ on the National Payment System.
SBP transaction volumes form a major and rapidly growing component of the overall payment-system indicators published by the Bank of Russia.
BRPS funds-transfer statistics are a core table within the selected indicators on the Russian Federation’s payment system.
The quarterly List of Financial Corporations supplies the institutional-unit coverage used in the compilation of the financial accounts of the SNA for the financial-corporations sector.
The concise ‘Results in Brief’ publication summarises the same activities and statistical outcomes that are presented in greater detail in the full Bank of Russia Annual Report.
Development and pilot testing of the digital ruble platform are reported as part of the broader advancement of the national payment system and the Bank of Russia’s NPS oversight activities.

The Industrial Production Index is compiled in accordance with the Official Statistical Methodology for the formation of official statistical information on the output of goods and services and indices of physical volume of output relating to industrial production.
All official statistical information of Rosstat, including the Industrial Production Index, is formed under the legal framework of Federal Law 282-FZ on official statistical accounting.
Russian industrial-production data are among the key economic-activity indicators contributed by Rosstat to the annual BRICS Joint Statistical Publication.
The Labour Force Survey is conducted and its results disseminated as official statistical information under Federal Law 282-FZ and the Federal Plan for Statistical Works.
dependencies.evidence_quote: 0.1 Legal environment 0.1.1 Responsibility for collecting, processing, and disseminating statistics The collection of primary statistical data and the publication of official statistical information is carried out in accordance with Federal Law of November 29, 2007 No 282-FZ “On Official Statistical Accounting and the System of State Statistics in the Russian Federation”.

dependencies.basis: Employment and unemployment indicators derived from the Labour Force Survey are supplied by Rosstat to the labour-market chapters of the BRICS Joint Statistical Publication.
Producer price indices are official statistical information formed under Federal Law 282-FZ and the associated methodologies.

Merchandise trade data from the Federal Customs Service are a primary input to the goods account of the balance of payments compiled by the Bank of Russia; the Bank of Russia notes adjustments to external-trade estimates in its BOP methodology.
The socio-economic development forecast is prepared and submitted as part of the budget process governed by the Budget Code; it provides the macroeconomic parameters for the draft federal budget.
The annual Federal Law on the federal budget is adopted in accordance with the procedures and principles established by the Budget Code of the Russian Federation.
The federal budget is prepared on the basis of the socio-economic development forecast submitted by the Ministry of Economic Development together with the draft budget.
Wage statistics are closely linked to the labour-market framework; employment data from the Labour Force Survey provide the denominator context for average-wage calculations.
Official unemployment statistics are derived primarily from the Labour Force Survey conducted by Rosstat.
The agricultural-output methodology is an official statistical methodology formed under the requirements of Federal Law 282-FZ.
Industrial production indices are used as extrapolators and volume indicators in the compilation of GDP by production approach in the national accounts.
VPN-2020 was conducted and its results published pursuant to Federal Law 8-FZ, which defines the legal basis, principles and purposes of the All-Russian Population Census.
Rosstat Order 549 of 9 September 2021 explicitly implements the methodological and organizational provisions required by Federal Law 8-FZ and the Government Decree organizing the 2020 census.
Order 226 of 5 April 2017 supplies the official rules for aggregating ОБДХ microdata into the published indicators of household income, expenditure and consumption.
CPI weights are derived from consumer expenditure data collected in the Sample Survey of Household Budgets (ОБДХ); this is a standard and repeatedly documented use of the survey.
The official poverty series is calculated by comparing the distribution of average per-capita monetary incomes with the poverty line defined under Government Decree 2049 of 26 November 2021.
Poverty estimates rely on the distribution of monetary incomes derived from household survey data (including ОБДХ and related income surveys) combined with macroeconomic income aggregates.
Order 259 of 29 May 2025 is issued pursuant to Article 7 of Federal Law 282-FZ on official statistical accounting and the Rosstat statute (Government Decree 420).
The 2014 TEB methodology is an official statistical methodology adopted under the framework of Federal Law 282-FZ.
Order 353 of 23 July 2025 explicitly cites Article 7 of Federal Law 282-FZ and the Federal Plan of Statistical Works as the legal basis for the electricity balance methodology.

The 2025 methodology on the use of fuel and energy resources is stated to provide the principal information base for compiling the Fuel and Energy Balance whose framework was set by Order 229 of 2014.
The Yearbook incorporates updated population figures and structures derived from the VPN-2020 results and presents them alongside other socio-economic indicators.
The Yearbook contains sections on household incomes, expenditures and living standards that draw on the Sample Survey of Household Budgets and related income statistics.

The Regions of Russia series is an official statistical publication produced under the Federal Plan of Statistical Works and the legal framework of Federal Law 282-FZ on official statistical accounting.

Both volumes draw on the same underlying regional statistical system; the Main Characteristics volume provides a more detailed subject-by-subject presentation of indicators also summarised in the broader Socio-economic Indicators volume.
The short handbook «Moscow in Figures» is a condensed presentation of key indicators drawn from the same Mosstat data system that produces the full Statistical Yearbook «Moscow».
Krasnoyarsk Krai yearbook data feed the corresponding subject rows of the national Regions of Russia socio-economic indicators and characteristics volumes.
The concise «Krasnoyarsk Krai in Figures» handbook summarises indicators published in fuller form in the Krasnoyarsk Krai Statistical Yearbook.
Federal-district bulletins aggregate and present subject-level data that also appear in the national Regions of Russia volumes, organised by federal district.
Population and demographic structures in the Moscow yearbook incorporate results and revisions based on the All-Russian Population Census 2020 (VPN-2020).

The published VRP series by subject are calculated according to the official statistical methodology for Gross Regional Product (including the 2025 refinements on financial corporations and constant-price calculation).
VRP is the regional counterpart of GDP within the System of National Accounts; the national accounts framework and classifications underpin the regional calculation.
The Regions of Russia socio-economic indicators volume systematically presents VRP and related regional accounts indicators for every subject.
Subject-level municipal indicator publications are extracted and presented from the national Municipal Indicators Database (БД ПМО) framework.
Municipal indicators form the lowest tier that aggregates into the oblast-level socio-economic picture published in the Sverdlovsk statistical collection.
Monthly/periodic socio-economic reports provide the high-frequency data later consolidated into the annual yearbook.

Novosibirskstat's VRP workbook carries a row computing the oblast's share of the sum of all subjects' gross regional product — the Rosstat GRP-by-subject series — which cannot be produced without that federal series. dependencies.basis: The Municipal Indicators Database is an official statistical information system maintained under the Federal Law on official statistical accounting and the Federal Plan of Statistical Works.
Bashkortostan indicators in national regional compilations are consistent with the annual «in figures» handbook and operational reports of Bashkortostanstat.
Periodic main socio-economic indicator reports feed the annual handbook for the Republic of Bashkortostan.
Moscow Oblast data in national Regions of Russia volumes are consistent with the Mosstat Statistical Yearbook «Moscow Oblast».
The short handbook is a condensed presentation of key indicators from the full Moscow Oblast Statistical Yearbook.

Both the City of Moscow and Moscow Oblast yearbooks are produced by the same territorial body (Mosstat) under a coordinated regional statistical programme; they share methodological and data-collection infrastructure while remaining distinct subjects.
The concise «Tyva in figures» handbook summarises indicators published in fuller form in the Republic of Tyva Statistical Yearbook.

Both yearbooks are produced under the same territorial body (Krasnoyarskstat covering Krasnoyarsk Krai, Khakassia and Tyva); they share institutional and methodological infrastructure while remaining distinct subject-level publications, enabling direct contrast between a major industrial krai and a sparser republic.
Administrative-okrug and district indicators are published as part of, or drawn from the same data system as, the Statistical Yearbook «Moscow» and related Mosstat materials.
Intra-city municipal (district/okrug) indicators align with the national Municipal Indicators Database framework used across subjects.

_note: Two findings worth flagging above the rest. (1) Rwanda's CPI is running on stale inputs by its own donor's account: a World Bank Eastern Africa Regional Statistics Program-for-Results supervision mission (September 2024) states plainly that 'rebasing and switch to the 2018 Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) are required to achieve compliance. These changes are expected to be completed in 2025' -- but the most recent CPI bulletin actually reachable this session (June 2026, published July 2026) still carries the same 'Feb 2014=100' base and the same EICV4 (2013-14) weights as the March 2024 and July 2025 editions, meaning the 2025 target was missed. Rwanda's own separate COICOP manual confirms it is still the '"COICOP Rwanda 2014 edition"', explicitly built on the 1993 SNA rather than the 2008 SNA already carried elsewhere in this corpus. (2) A genuine bidirectional relationship was found between the CPI and the household survey series that is new to this branch: EICV4's 2013-14 expenditure data supply the CPI's weights (the ordinary direction), while EICV7's own 2025 methodological note states as one of its explicit objectives to 'serve as a key input for updating the consumer price index (CPI)' and separately describes using NISR's own 'CPI prices' to deflate household consumption to real terms -- the same two publications feeding each other in opposite directions. On social protection, Rwanda's 2024-2029 Social Protection Sector Strategic Plan comes closer than most of this branch's prior findings to naming an inflation-adjustment intervention directly -- 'a mechanism to regularly adjust benefits based on inflation and market changes' -- but frames it explicitly as a planned 2024-2029 intervention rather than an operating one, the same recommendation-reveals-absence shape already seen in Botswana, Tanzania and Malawi. Rwanda Social Security Board's mandatory pension scheme, by contrast, has a real and currently operating benefit-adjustment clause, but it runs on a five-yearly actuarial study rather than CPI.

_open_questions.question: The World Bank's September 2024 Aide Memoire stated Rwanda's CPI rebasing and COICOP-2018 switch were 'expected to be completed in 2025.' The most recent CPI edition reachable this session (June 2026, published July 2026) still shows the old Feb-2014 base and EICV4 weights, meaning the target was missed as of that edition. Whether a rebased edition has appeared since was not checked (would require a session running after this one).

The only textual link found between EICV7 and NISR's own Customized COICOP classification is a bare table column header ('COICOP') in Table 9.2, not a prose sentence naming a specific classification document or vintage. Worth checking EICV7's full methodology chapter (not just the deflation and food-conversion sections read this session) for a stronger, explicit citation.

The SSA/ISSA 'Social Security Programs Throughout the World: Africa, 2019 -- Rwanda' quote on presidential-decree benefit adjustment, and the 2017 IMF e-GDDS press release quote, were both extracted via the WebFetch tool's summarizer rather than hand-verified against raw page text by the researching session (ssa.gov and imf.org both returned access blocks to direct fetch/curl attempts). Both are independently corroborated by other primary sources already in this slice, but a session with different tooling access could re-verify the exact wording directly.

Law N deg 05/2015 Article 16 requires an actuarial study 'at least once every five (5) years' before any pension benefit increase. Whether any interim mechanism exists for the years between actuarial studies (e.g. a ministerial order, a partial top-up) was not checked -- only the base five-year mechanism itself was confirmed.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
reports.publisher: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR)
reports.description: NISR's monthly Consumer Price Index publication. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via the June 2026 edition (published July 2026), cross-checked against the March 2024 and July 2025 editions for stability of wording. 'The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is a measure of the average change over time of goods and services purchased by households. The CPI uses a Modified Laspeyres formula to calculate the index.' Base: 'Index reference period (Feb 2014=100): The period with which all other periods are compared.' Weights: 'Weights used for the index are from the Household Living Conditions Survey (EICV4) results conducted in 2013-2014 with a sample of 14,419 households.' The word 'COICOP' does not appear anywhere in any of the three editions searched, nor do 'EAC', 'IMF', 'CPI Manual' or 'SNA' -- a genuine silence on external-framework citation, unlike Tanzania's and Kenya's own CPI documents.

release_schedule.note: NISR's 2026 Advance Release Calendar lists Consumer Price Index releases on the 10th of every month. Reports are published about 40 days after the reference month ends (e.g., the June 2026 CPI report was published July 10, 2026), so the August 10, 2026 release (already past relative to today, 2026-08-11) covered July 2026 CPI, and the next release, September 10, 2026, will cover August 2026 CPI.

reports.publisher: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR)
reports.description: Household living-conditions/budget survey, 'conducted in 2013-2014 with a sample of 14,419 households' (per the CPI bulletin's own methodological notice), whose results supply the expenditure weights still used in Rwanda's CPI as of the June 2026 edition -- despite a 2024 World Bank supervision report stating a rebasing onto more current data was expected in 2025 (see rw-worldbank-pforr-aide-memoire).
reports.cadence_note: One round roughly every 3-5 years; part of the numbered EICV series (EICV1 through EICV7 to date).

entries.covers: EICV8 fieldwork (next round in the series, following EICV7 which ran Oct 2023-Oct 2024)

release_schedule.rule: NISR states the Integrated Household Living Conditions Survey (EICV) "is conducted every three years."
release_schedule.note: The report id/url is specifically for EICV4 (fieldwork Oct 2013-Oct 2014), a historical, already-completed and now-superseded edition of the series (the series has since progressed through EICV5 [2016-2017], EICV6 [2020-2021], and EICV7 [2023-2024], the current latest round). EICV4 itself will never recur under that name; the 'next' date given here is for the next round in the ongoing EICV series (would be EICV8), computed from NISR's own stated 3-year periodicity applied to the most recent completed round (EICV7, Oct 2023-Oct 2024). No official announcement of EICV8's exact dates or an EICV8-specific page was found.

reports.title: Integrated Household Living Conditions Survey 7 (EICV7) -- Methodological Note
reports.publisher: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR)
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Methodological note for the seventh EICV round (2023/24). States its own objectives include to 'serve as a key input for updating the consumer price index (CPI)' -- the reverse-direction counterpart to the CPI's own reliance on EICV4's weights (see rw-eicv4-survey). Separately, on its own deflation method: 'Anticipating the need for good-quality price data nationwide, the NISR has, since October 2023, collected data on prices of hundreds of items in markets and shops in all thirty districts. These "CPI prices" were collected with careful attention to consistency in units and quality over time and space... Where unit values and self-reported prices are not available... we use CPI prices.' A genuine two-way relationship between the same pair of recurring publications.
reports.cadence_note: One round roughly every 3-5 years; part of the numbered EICV series.

release_schedule.note: NISR's EICV survey landing page states the survey "is conducted every three years," but the actual historical round dates (EICV1 2000, EICV2 2005, EICV3 2011, EICV4 2013-14, EICV5 2016-17, EICV6 2020-21, EICV7 2023-24) show gaps ranging from 2 to 6 years, consistent with the existing cadence_note's '3-5 years' characterization. No EICV8 date or methodological-note-specific publication schedule has been announced; the methodological note itself is published only after each round's data collection and processing finish (EICV7's note appeared ~9 months after data collection ended, in July 2025), so there is no fixed/computable next date. Treating as irregular rather than forcing a stated-rule date.

reports.title: Customized Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) -- Rwanda
reports.publisher: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR)
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. NISR's own Rwanda-customized COICOP classification manual: 'COICOP is an integral part of the 1993 SNA, but it is also intended for use in three other statistical areas: household budget surveys, consumer price indices and international comparisons of gross domestic product (GDP)...' Internally described as 'the COICOP Rwanda 2014 edittion [sic]... expanded to 6 digits' -- an older, 1993-SNA-based customized vintage, not COICOP 2018 (un-coicop-2018 elsewhere in this corpus). A separate document from the CPI bulletin itself, which never names COICOP by title at all.
reports.cadence_note: A standing classification manual, not a recurring release.

release_schedule.note: This is a statistical classification manual (first published 2014), not a periodic statistical release. The document's foreword states only that 'Users of the Classification Manual are urged to make their information needs known for consideration in planning future editions' -- there is no fixed schedule, stated rule, or observed pattern of periodic revision. No evidence of a second/updated edition since 2014 was found as of 2026-08-11. The low releases_per_year (0.05, i.e. once per ~20 years) on file is consistent with this being an infrequently-revised foundational classification document rather than a recurring release.

reports.title: Data Portals: E-GDDS/SDDS -- National Summary Data Page
reports.publisher: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR)
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. NISR's own statement of its IMF dissemination status: 'Rwanda National Statistical System (NSS) under the lead of NISR began publishing the required macroeconomic data on the National Summary Data Page (NSDP) as recommended by IMF's enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS). This is the transition towards subscribing to Special Data Dissemination Standards (SDDS) in the near future.' Corroborated by a 2017 IMF press release announcing Rwanda's e-GDDS implementation and by IMF Country Report No. 24/141's Technical Memorandum of Understanding, which defines a programme monitoring variable 'consistent with the definition of the enhanced General Data Dissemination Standard (e-GDDS) template.' Places Rwanda on the same weaker dissemination tier already confirmed for Kenya, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Ghana and Uganda, rather than the stronger SDDS tier confirmed for South Africa, Egypt and Tanzania.
reports.cadence_note: A standing status page, not a recurring release.

release_schedule.note: The National Summary Data Page is a standing IMF e-GDDS/SDDS compliance data portal that aggregates and continuously updates links to Rwanda's core macroeconomic indicators (GDP, CPI, trade, etc.), each on its own schedule. NISR's page (https://statistics.gov.rw/data-portals-e-gddssdds) describes the portal's purpose but publishes no calendar or stated update rule for the page itself.

reports.title: Eastern Africa Regional Statistics Program-for-Results (PforR) and Rwanda Poverty Policy Dialogue Mission -- Aide Memoire
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (mission of 4-6 September 2024). The primary source for Rwanda's own self-reported CPI compliance gap: 'Under DLI 1.1(c) "Harmonized 5 dimensions of statistics according to applicable regional guidelines", the NISR team provided the following updates: a. Consumer Price Index: rebasing and switch to the 2018 Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) are required to achieve compliance. These changes are expected to be completed in 2025 after using the results of the 7th Integrated Household Living Conditions Survey (EICV7).' Also states: 'CPI monthly reports from September 2022 to July 2024 were submitted to EAC for publishing' under a harmonized-CPI result indicator -- Rwanda's CPI functioning as an input to an EAC-level output, not evidence that Rwanda's own CPI methodology depends on the EAC HCPI Regulations. Also: 'For CPI, NISR is reviewing the software recommended by EAC to decide on its adoption after ensuring the data's security' (AGENCY ONLY -- no titled EAC document named).
reports.cadence_note: A periodic project-supervision mission report, not a fixed annual release.

release_schedule.note: Aide memoires for this World Bank project-supervision series (P176371, Eastern Africa Regional Statistics PforR, which includes the Rwanda Poverty Policy Dialogue) are issued after each ad hoc implementation support mission (ISM), not on a fixed calendar. Observed mission dates: Sept 4-6, 2024 (Rwanda ISM, source aide memoire); mid-term review conducted 15-May-2025 per the Dec 24, 2025 Implementation Status & Results Report; a separate related ISM at STATAFRIC/Tunis Nov 3-8, 2025. These are scattered across different months (Sept, May, Nov) with no consistent seasonal pattern and no publicly stated rule governing timing -- only that missions occur periodically as needed. Project closing date is June 30, 2027 (per Dec 2025 ISR), so further missions/aide memoires are expected before then, but no next mission date is announced in any document found.

reports.title: Social Protection Sector Strategic Plan (SP-SSP) 2024-2029
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Rwanda's social protection sector strategy covering the Vision Umurenge Programme (VUP), RSSB and the Imibereho social registry. Under Outcome 6: 'Reviewing Benefit Levels: An assessment of the adequacy of current benefits will be conducted, with adjustments to ensure that benefits meet the needs of beneficiaries. This includes a mechanism to regularly adjust benefits based on inflation and market changes' -- framed as a planned 2024-2029 intervention, not an operating mechanism, and never naming NISR's CPI as its intended data source. Also states the Imibereho Social Registry Information System (SRIS) 'replaces the "Ubudehe categorisation" previously used for targeting beneficiaries of social protection and graduation programmes,' adopting 'Proxy Means Testing (PMT)' -- a targeting/eligibility mechanism, not a benefit-level-setting one. Also admits generally that 'challenges persist in achieving coverage and adequacy targets, particularly exacerbated by shocks experienced during the NST1 period, including COVID-19, inflation, and climate change impacts.'
reports.cadence_note: A multi-year strategic plan, not a recurring release.

release_schedule.note: Confirmed multi-year strategic plan tied to Rwanda's National Strategy for Transformation (NST) cycle rather than a recurring statistical release. The current SP-SSP covers 2024/2025-2028/2029 (approved by the Social Protection Sector Working Group on 11 June 2024, aligned with NST2 which runs 2024-2029). The prior SP-SSP covered 2018/19-2023/24 (aligned with NST1, which ran 2017-2024, a 7-year period). Because NST1 (7 years) and NST2 (5 years) had different lengths, the underlying planning cycle itself is not fixed-length, so no reliable next release date can be computed for a follow-on SP-SSP (would presumably follow whenever NST3 is elaborated, with no announced date). This supports the existing cadence_note that this is a multi-year strategic plan, not a recurring release.

reports.title: Law N deg 05/2015 of 30/03/2015 Governing the Organization of Pension Schemes
reports.publisher: Republic of Rwanda (Official Gazette n deg 20 of 18/05/2015)
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Statutory basis for the Rwanda Social Security Board's mandatory pension scheme. Article 16, 'Actuarial study for pension scheme': 'The public entity in charge of pension scheme shall carry out an actuarial study for pension scheme at least once every five (5) years... Basing on the findings of the actuarial study provided under the preceding paragraph, pension benefits may also be increased. A Presidential Order shall determine related implementation modalities.' A real, operating benefit-adjustment mechanism -- but actuarial and discretionary (via Presidential Order), not CPI-linked. Full text searched for 'adjust', 'index', 'revalor', 'cost of living' and 'inflation': no hits outside this actuarial mechanism. Independently corroborated by the SSA/ISSA 'Social Security Programs Throughout the World: Africa, 2019 -- Rwanda' country profile: 'Benefits are adjusted periodically by presidential decree based on an actuarial evaluation.'
reports.cadence_note: A standing statute, not a recurring release.

release_schedule.note: This is a standing statute governing pension schemes in Rwanda, published once in the Official Gazette n° 20 of 18/05/2015. It is amended only sporadically via subsequent laws/regulations (e.g. implementing Presidential Orders and Regulations from 2016-2017, and gazette notices on contribution rates as recently as 2024), not on any fixed cycle. The law itself does contain a stated rule for a related but distinct process: Article 16 requires the public pension entity to carry out an actuarial study of the pension scheme 'at least once every five (5) years' - but that governs actuarial studies, not re-issuance of this law, so it does not give this report a computable next-release date.

reports.title: Final Evaluation of 2021/2022 Imihigo
reports.publisher: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR)
reports.description: Published February 2023 by the same NISR that publishes rw-nisr-cpi already in this corpus. Imihigo are annual performance contracts, per NISR's own reports page, "signed between government officials and the Head of State since 2006... aimed at accelerating the realization of the country's development ambitions." This document scores and ranks all 27 districts by name — e.g. "Ngororero District scored 77.76%, ranking 18th among 27 districts, with an average national district score of 76.50%" (Table 5) — making it the clearest documented mechanism in this branch for how a national government holds sub-national units directly, individually accountable to centrally-set targets, distinct from every fiscal-transfer mechanism (FAAC, CRA, DACF, subsidy proclamations) covered elsewhere this round, which move money rather than grade performance.
reports.cadence_note: Annual evaluation, one edition per Imihigo cycle (this is the 2021/2022 edition; NISR's reports page lists six editions spanning 2017/18-2024/25).

reports.title: National Strategy for Transformation (NST1)
reports.description: Verbatim, from the Imihigo evaluation's own executive summary: "Rwanda made significant reforms and aspires to become a middle-income country by 2035 and High-Income Country by 2050. This will be achieved through a series of National Strategies for Transformation (NST)" and "The first National Strategy for Transformation (NST1) whose aim is to achieve high standards of living conditions for all Rwandans by 2023/2024." This is the national target-setting document districts are evaluated against every year — minted here specifically because the Imihigo evaluation report cites it as its own basis, not independently sourced from NST1's own primary text this round.

_note: Deep-research pass on Saudi Arabia's 10 unlinked nodes. Every candidate document was fetched directly (curl or WebFetch) and, where possible, re-verified with pdftotext/raw-HTML grep against the live file before use. Yield: 7 verified edges across 7 of the 10 target nodes (sa-population, sa-oil-production, sa-oil-exports, sa-oil-revenue, sa-banking, sa-education, sa-ghg), all citing GASTAT/MOF/SAMA methodology-and-quality reports or an international body's Saudi-specific filing. 3 nodes (sa-vision-2030, sa-pif, sa-health) were fully checked against their primary sources and dropped: two as genuine no-document dead ends (policy narrative with no named statistical dependency) and one (sa-pif) as deferred because the publisher's WAF blocks direct full-text download, so only partial keyword coverage of a 200+ page report was possible. UPDATE 2026-08-29 (import follow-up): sa-pif -> sa-national-accounts remains blocked on every route tried (Cloudflare on pif.gov.sa; the import's own press-release lead didn't carry the GASTAT attribution either) — still deferred, not a confirmed dead end.

dependencies.basis: GASTAT's own Methodology and Quality Report for its Population Projections and Estimates statistics states, in section 9.6 'Documentation on methodology': "Concepts, definitions, issues, and classifications are based on international standards by the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division." — immediately followed by the link https://population.un.org/wpp/Methodology/, i.e. the exact World Population Prospects Methodology document. This shows GASTAT's population estimates (sa-population) explicitly adopt the UN Population Division's WPP methodology as their conceptual/classification basis.

GASTAT's Education and Training Statistics 2025 publication states in its 'Methodology and quality' note: "This publication presents the education and training indicators based on the Education and Training Survey for the age group 5-19 years for 2025 and the population estimates from the General Authority for Statistics for 2025." This directly confirms the education/training statistics report draws on GASTAT's population estimates (the sa-population node) as an input data source.

GASTAT's Methodology and Quality Report of Oil and Gas Statistics 2025, under 'Coherence - National Accounts', states: "The Oil and Gas Statistics data are integrated with the requirements of the National Accounts through the use of approved statistical classifications and concepts, supporting the consistency of energy data with related economic indicators. In addition, some publication indicators, such as production data and foreign trade data for refined petroleum products, can be used as supporting and reference data within the framework of compiling related economic indicators." This states oil production statistics are compiled to be coherent with, and feed into, National Accounts classifications/concepts.

The same GASTAT Methodology and Quality Report of Oil and Gas Statistics 2025 (which covers this publication's export volumes) states under 'Coherence - National Accounts': "The Oil and Gas Statistics data are integrated with the requirements of the National Accounts through the use of approved statistical classifications and concepts... In addition, some publication indicators, such as production data and foreign trade data for refined petroleum products, can be used as supporting and reference data within the framework of compiling related economic indicators." The explicit mention of 'foreign trade data' ties the export-volume series specifically to National Accounts coherence requirements.

The Saudi Ministry of Finance's Budget Statement FY2026 (the document behind the sa-oil-revenue node's mof.gov.sa/en/budget/2026 URL) states in its Introduction: "The classification of the fiscal data referenced here adheres to the Government Finance Statistics Manual (GFSM 2014), published by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which provides a standardized international framework." Oil revenue is one of the fiscal-data categories (Revenues chapter) covered by this classification statement.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The classification of the fiscal data referenced here adheres to the Government Finance Statistics Manual (GFSM 2014), published by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which provides a standardized international framework.

dependencies.basis: SAMA's Rulebook section on Credit Risk Management / Prudential Treatment of Problem Assets, which defines the non-performing-loan (NPL) classification that underlies SAMA's banking asset-quality statistics, states: "Non-performing loans: As stipulated in BCBS 403 'Guidelines – Prudential treatment of problem assets – definitions of non-performing exposures and forbearance' endorsed by SAMA through circular no. 381000099757 dated 23/09/1438AH." BCBS 403 is a Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BIS) guideline, i.e. part of the Basel Framework, and SAMA states it has formally endorsed/adopted it as the basis for its own NPL definitions.

_meta: AF/G.23 (2026-08-13), continuing systematic Africa-branch municipal-fiscal-tier research. Seychelles was previously researched in AF/G.17 (see af-seychelles.json), which concluded a genuine structural absence (26 districts, no independent fiscal tier) based on secondary/academic sources only. This round obtained two new raw-verified primary documents that substantially strengthen that conclusion without overturning it: (1) a directly-extracted verbatim quote of Constitution Article 167 (a bare administrative-division enabling clause, no fiscal-autonomy language), and (2) the Ministry of Finance's 2026 Budget Estimates, which itemizes the Ministry of Local Government and Inner Islands' (MLGII) finances line-by-line and explicitly shows districts are financed 100% from the central Consolidated Fund, with even minor locally-collected receipts (burial fees, facility rentals) remitted back to the centre rather than retained. Both are minted as new nodes here; no district/municipal-tier node is minted, since none exists to document (structural absence, not a research gap). The Auditor-General's report-PDF content and a possible Victoria 'Capital City' charter/Act remain unresolved leads for a future round (see _dropped).

reports.title: Constitution of the Republic of Seychelles — Article 167 (Local Administration)
reports.description: Chapter XV ("Miscellaneous"), Article 167 ("Local Administration") of the Constitution of the Republic of Seychelles — the sole constitutional provision touching sub-national administration. Verbatim text (directly extracted from a raw-downloaded PDF, not a secondary paraphrase): "167.(1) A law may, for the purpose of facilitating the administrative functions of the State in respect of its social and economic undertakings contained in Chapter III, provide for the division of Seychelles into such number of units which shall bear such name as the law may specify. (2) A law referred to in clause (1) may provide for the composition and the functions of the units and for all other matters necessary to give effect to the provisions of that clause." This wording was independently cross-checked against a second, separately-hosted copy (constituteproject.org's PDF) and found substantively identical. Article 167 is a bare permissive/enabling clause for *administrative* division only ("administrative functions of the State") — it contains no reference to elected local government, revenue-raising power, or fiscal autonomy, corroborating from the primary constitutional text itself that no constitutionally-mandated local fiscal tier exists. No enabling Act implementing this clause was located in the National Assembly's Acts listing this round (search returned "No results found"), consistent with this branch's prior finding that the 1991 Local Government Act was suspended in 1993 and never re-enacted. ACCESS CAVEAT: the government's own domain for this text (gov.sc) and the Seychelles Legal Information Institute (seylii.org / old.seylii.org) were both bot/captcha-gated (`robocop` CAPTCHA) this round; this URL is a third-party intergovernmental mirror (ARIPO, the African Regional Intellectual Property Organization), not a Seychelles-government-controlled domain, though the text itself is independently cross-verified.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument (constitutional text, in force; text unchanged across consolidations checked).

reports.title: 2026 Budget Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure for the Fiscal Year Ended 31st December 2026 — Part 1 (Ministry of Local Government and Inner Islands chapter)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Economic Planning, Trade and Investment, Republic of Seychelles
reports.description: Republic of Seychelles national budget document; the Ministry of Local Government and Inner Islands (MLGII) chapter (printed pages ~411-416, plus a Public Sector Investment Programme annex) is the strongest primary evidence yet obtained in this branch's Seychelles research for the country's district administration having no independent fiscal tier. Table 1 ("Revenue") for MLGII: "Consolidated Fund 135,378 168,999 164,212 166,448 169,611 157,371 / Main appropriation 135,378 168,999 164,212 166,448 169,611 157,371 / Total 135,378 168,999 164,212 166,448 169,611 157,371" [SR'000s, 2024 Actual through 2028 Forecast] — i.e. 100% of MLGII's SR166,448,000 2026 appropriation is drawn from the general Consolidated Fund, not district-specific or district-raised revenue. Table 2 ("Current receipts") shows the ONLY revenue MLGII/district offices collect locally is captioned "Receipts transferred to Consolidated Fund": "Burial Services Fees 191 205 205 205 205 205 / Rent of facilities 1,801 1,700 1,700 1,700 1,700 1,700 / Rent of Offices 348 500 500 400 400 400 / Rent of Day-care centres 1,065 1,080 1,080 1,200 1,200 1,200 / TOTAL 3,405 3,485 3,485 3,505 3,505 3,505" [SR'000s] — even this minor local collection (roughly 2% of the Ministry's budget) is remitted back to the centre, not retained by district administration. The Ministry's own stated mandate: "The mandate of the Ministry of Local Government and Inner Islands (MLGII) is to oversee the affairs of the districts and to empower the local communities... as well as maintaining linkages between the central and local government" — i.e. a national ministry overseeing districts, not districts self-governing. The consolidated "SP1: District Administration" sub-programme line (SR96,291,000 in the 2026 budget, covering all 26 districts/27 District Administration Offices nationally) is not broken down per district in the summary tables, but the PSIP annex DOES itemize named-district capital projects (e.g. Cascade Community Centre, Les Mamelles Day Care Centre, Ile Perseverance 1 DA's Office, Grand Anse Praslin Day Care, Anse Aux Pins Day Care, Takamaka Day Care, Glacis Day Care, Baie St Anne Community Centre/DA's Office (La Digue), Belombre DA's Office, Au Cap Community Centre, Baie Lazare Community Centre, Anse Royale Community Centre), each financed by "GOS" (Government of Seychelles) or "GOI" (Government of India, a foreign grant/loan) codes — never a district-level or locally-raised funding source, reinforcing that districts are named capital-allocation *recipients*, not independent budget-holders. ACCESS CAVEAT: this is a large (approximately 8MB, 799-page) PDF; the WebFetch tool returned a 504 proxy timeout attempting to summarize it, and the text quoted here was obtained only by downloading the file directly with curl and extracting it with pdftotext — flagged per protocol as a large-PDF/technical-access caveat, though the resulting quotes are raw-verified, not AI-summarized.
reports.cadence_note: Annual national budget estimates; this is the 2026 edition (forecasts extend to 2028).

_dropped.why: The 2026 Budget's MLGII chapter and the Ministry's own website both cite Article 167 as their constitutional authority (per the AI-summarized-only Ministry website finding, Finding 6 in this round's raw research: "Article 167 of the Constitution of the Third Republic of Seychelles"), but the budget document ITSELF (the raw-verified PDF) does not contain a citing sentence naming Article 167 — the citation only appears on the captcha-gated, AI-summarized-only Ministry website. The Office of the Auditor General of Seychelles (oag.sc / oag.sc/reports/annual-reports-of-the-auditor-general) publishes annual reports back to 2011 (e.g. "Report of the Auditor General 2024", "Annual Report 2023") and is exactly the 'higher tier of government reporting on named lower-tier units' document type productive elsewhere in this branch (e.g. Nigeria). This round reached only the report LISTING (titles/dates), not the content of any individual report PDF — direct curl is blocked by an `sg-captcha` bot-protection gate on oag.sc, and WebFetch could not follow through to a specific report's PDF text (likely JS-rendered pagination). No node minted since no content was verified. Genuine unresolved lead for a future round, not a confirmed absence.

A currently-operating 'Mayor of Victoria' office was confirmed to exist (mayorsofficeseychelles.com; current mayor named as Mrs. Michaud-Payet, office at Revolution Avenue, Victoria) but no enabling Act, legal charter, or budget/fiscal document establishing a 'Victoria City Council' or 'Borough of Victoria' was located this round; the office's own site is described as promotional/informational only with no governance-structure documentation. victoria.gov.sc returned HTTP 421 (Misdirected Request) with no retrievable content. Appears to be a ceremonial/civic-engagement office rather than a fiscally autonomous municipal government, but this could not be confirmed either way with a primary legal document. Not minted as a node; flagged as an open lead for a future round (a WebSearch for a 'Victoria (Capital City) Act' was queued but not executed this round due to search-budget exhaustion).

reports.title: Annual Reports of the Auditor-General (Seychelles), 2022-2024 editions — District Small Projects / District Administration Budget Line
reports.publisher: Office of the Auditor-General, Republic of Seychelles
reports.description: Three consecutive annual editions of the Office of the Auditor-General's (OAG) statutory report to the National Assembly, tracking the same recurring line item — a centrally-administered budget allocation for 'district small projects' / district administration, run by the Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs — across the 2022, 2023 and 2024 reports. 2022 report (Chapter 2, para 2.44, with Ministry response at 2.46): "A budget of R20.0m was allocated for small projects implemented at district level against an actual spending of R12.2m." Ministry response: "The Ministry noted that at the time of budget finalization, the list of projects under the district small projects program is not finalized. The list is only finalized after discussions at the district levels, the result of which is consolidated by the Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs." 2023 report (Chapter 2, para 2.41), the OAG's own status-tracking cross-reference to the same line: "Lump sum budget of R20m for small projects implemented at district levels without details." This is the third consecutive year (2022, 2023, 2024) this specific line item has been tracked by the AG. 2024 report (Chapter 4 introduction, describing the Ministry's mandate): "The Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs is mandated to oversee the affairs of the 27 districts and empower the local communities. Its role is to deliver transparent, accountable and inclusive local services; provides and enhance community infrastructure and facilities, implement the local government reform programme and ensure good governance through citizen's engagement, inclusiveness and empowerment towards development." 2024 report (Chapter 2, para 2.44), documenting a restructuring of the same line item away from the prior years' undifferentiated lump sum: "A budget of SR1.0m is now allocated to each of the 26 districts." SOURCE-INTERNAL DISCREPANCY, flagged rather than resolved: the 2024 report itself states "27 districts" in its Chapter 4 introduction and "26 districts" in its Chapter 2 budget-line paragraph — both quoted verbatim as printed in the same document edition. The restructuring documented between the 2022/2023 editions (a single undifferentiated R20m lump sum, unallocated by district, with the OAG repeatedly noting the absence of a finalized project list at budget time) and the 2024 edition (a fixed SR1.0m allocated to each of the 26/27 districts individually) reinforces, rather than weakens, this branch's confirmed finding of a structural absence of an autonomous local fiscal tier in Seychelles: in both the pre- and post-restructuring form, the allocation is set, administered and consolidated centrally by the Ministry, not raised or controlled by the districts themselves — this is the THIRD independent primary source (after sc-constitution-article-167 and sc-mlgii-budget-2026) making that same point, this time from the angle of the national Auditor-General's audit of the national ministry's district-facing spending rather than from constitutional text or the budget document itself. The 2024 report also documents two named audit findings against the same Ministry in the same chapter: absence of alternative quotes obtained for air ticket purchases (SR227,539) and absence of valid procurement contracts for disaster relief meal provisions (SR608,935, described as a recurring issue). The 2020 report (a fourth edition checked this round) returned zero hits for "district" on a full-text search and appears to predate or not cover this line item — a genuine NOT FOUND for that specific document/year, not an access failure (see _dropped).
reports.cadence_note: Annual statutory report to the National Assembly; this node spans three consecutive editions (2022, 2023, 2024) tracking one recurring line item rather than minting a node per exercise-year, per this branch's convention for a finding unchanged in substance across editions.

_dropped.why: Both documents describe the same underlying phenomenon — centrally-administered, non-district-controlled district financing in Seychelles — but from different institutional angles (an Auditor-General audit of a ministry's spending vs. the Ministry of Finance's own budget estimates), and no textual citation of one document by the other was found this round. Not minted as a live edge on topical similarity alone, per instruction. Worth separately flagging: the three AG report editions (2022-2024) name the responsible body as the 'Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs', while the 2026 Budget Estimates document names it the 'Ministry of Local Government and Inner Islands' (MLGII) — either a ministry rename/reorganisation between the audited years and the 2026 budget, or an inconsistency in how the two document series refer to the same body. Not resolved this round; recorded as a note for a future session rather than assumed to be the same entity without confirmation.

The `sg-captcha` bot-protection gate on oag.sc that blocked the prior round (AF/G.23, recorded in sc-g23-municipal.json's _dropped block) from reaching individual report PDFs appears to have been specific to that round's browser-rendered/direct fetch of the listing page, not a persistent block on the domain. Worth remembering for future Seychelles research: prefer the nationalassembly.sc mirror for OAG report PDFs over a direct oag.sc fetch, and treat a captcha hit on oag.sc as possibly transient rather than a dead end.

The AG Report 2020 (https://www.nationalassembly.sc/sites/default/files/2021-11/OAG%202020%20Report.pdf) was checked this round for the same 'district small projects' line item tracked in the 2022-2024 editions. A full-text search for "district" returned zero hits. reports.title: Interim National Constitution of the Republic of the Sudan (2005) — Part Nine, State Revenue and Fiscal Allocation Provisions
reports.description: HISTORICAL — LIKELY SUPERSEDED, included as a historical primary source only, not as current law. This is the pre-2011 text of Sudan's 2005 Interim National Constitution (it still contains 'Government of Southern Sudan' provisions, predating the 2011 secession of South Sudan). Sudan's constitutional order has since been superseded multiple times (2011 post-secession amendments; 2019 Constitutional Charter; suspended by the 2021 coup; further disrupted by the 2023 civil war and subsequent 2023-2025 Constitutional Charter instruments), and no currently-operative Sudanese constitutional or statutory text with a comparable numeric state-finance formula could be located this round (the 2019 Constitutional Charter's fiscal content is limited to budget-approval procedure, not a sharing formula). Quoted for its historical value in establishing that Sudan's founding federal law DID name a specific state revenue formula: Art. 192(5) (p.66-67), oil revenue: "At least two percent of oil revenue shall be allocated to the oil producing states in proportion to output produced in the state, without prejudice to the special arrangements of Abyei Area." Art. 195 (p.69), states' own revenue sources: "The states may legislate for raising revenue or collecting taxes from the following sources:- a. state land and property tax and royalties, b. service charges for state services, c. licences, d. state personal income tax, ... f. state share of oil revenue as is set out in Article 192(5) of this Constitution..." Art. 198 (p.71), oversight body: "A Fiscal and Financial Allocation and Monitoring Commission shall be established, to ensure transparency and fairness both in regard to the allocation of nationally collected funds to the Government of Southern Sudan and the states," composed in part of "all finance ministers in all states of the Sudan" (Art. 198(3)(c)).
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational constitutional instrument (2005); status as current law is unconfirmed and considered doubtful — see HISTORICAL flag above.

Neither the Central Bank of Sudan's nor the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning's sites were found to publish any state-by-state budget breakdown this round — only the national-level aggregate documents already present in the corpus (sd-cbos-statistical-review-q4-2024, sd-mofep-budget-2026, sd-budget-2021-transfers).

_dropped.why: All three National Audit Chamber nodes now in this branch (sd-nac-secrp-audit-2021, sd-nac-sldp-audit-2021, sd-nac-ssnp-audit-2020) are outputs of the same institution using the same stated audit methodology (each opinion invokes International Standards on Auditing, ISAs) and the same follow-up boilerplate instructing the implementing agency to act on findings. This is institutional/topical similarity, not a citable dependency: none of the three documents cross-references either of the other two by name, project ID, or agreement number, so no uses_data_from or cites edge is drawn between them per the evidence rule. Recorded here as a note rather than left undocumented, so a future round does not re-propose the same tempting-but-unsourced edge without checking first whether a later-located version of any of the three documents does contain an actual cross-reference (e.g. a consolidated Audit Chamber annual report citing individual project audits by name).

RE-CONFIRMED this round, now a twice-confirmed, stable finding (first found AF/G.22): Sudan's National Audit Chamber's own domain (audit.gov.sd) is still unreachable by DNS resolution failure. Given that the underlying cause (wartime infrastructure disruption since the 2023 civil war) is structural rather than transient, and the finding has now been independently reproduced twice with the same failure mode, this is not expected to change on any short timescale — a future round should NOT spend research effort re-checking audit.gov.sd again in the near term (e.g. within the next several rounds) unless there is specific news of Sudanese government infrastructure/connectivity being restored, or of the war's status changing materially. A periodic re-check (e.g. once every several months of project time, or triggered by broader Sudan-infrastructure news) is still worthwhile precisely because of the wartime context — government sites do occasionally come back online abruptly — but treating this as an open action item for every round is not a good use of research effort. All three Audit Chamber nodes in this corpus (sd-nac-secrp-audit-2021, sd-nac-sldp-audit-2021, sd-nac-ssnp-audit-2020) continue to be sourced only via the World Bank's document-mirror/disclosure copies, not the Chamber's own site.

Because every attempt failed at the transport/rate-limit layer rather than returning a substantive 'no captures found' response, this does NOT establish that audit.gov.sd has no Wayback Machine history — it only establishes that this round could not get a conclusive answer either way. _dropped.why: [COICOP-EDITION] Malaysia's DSBB national-accounts metadata says only 'COICOP is used for household consumption' with no year/edition named. Malaysia's own CPI methodology page (DSBB CPI00) actually lists 13 COICOP divisions including standalone 'Information and Communication' and 'Insurance and Financial Services' groups -- structurally consistent with COICOP 2018, not the 1999 HBS edition the import picked -- but since no document names an edition explicitly for this country's release, per the edition-matching rule neither un-coicop-2018 nor un-coicop-hbs-1999 is minted.

[SOURCE-QUALITY] the import's only source for this claim was a Phnom Penh Post news article quoting an NIS official -- a news-summary site, disallowed as a citation under project rules. I could not find an NIS or IMF primary document independently confirming a current SNA edition: NIS's own national-accounts page (nis.gov.kh/en/national/) shows GDP tables from 2014 onward but states no methodology edition, and the only primary metadata I could find (IMF DSBB NAG00 for KHM, and UNSD's Cambodia national-accounts info page) both describe SNA 1993 with a 2000 base year and 'in progress' 2008 SNA implementation, apparently stale but not affirmatively overridden by any primary source I could locate. Genuinely ambiguous -- dropping rather than guessing.

[SOURCE-QUALITY] Proposed node was sourced only from a Phnom Penh Post article (disallowed news aggregator). No NIS or government primary page describing this specific 2014 base-year rebase could be found (NIS's technical-documents page lists only CSIC-v2 and CSCO-v1, nothing on national-accounts rebasing). Dropping the node rather than minting on an unverifiable claim.

[COICOP-EDITION] Both the 2012 TL-NA methodological volume and the current DSBB TLS/NAG00 metadata state household consumption is 'classified according to the COICOP at level 3 classes' with no year/edition named. Not enough to pick 1999 HBS vs. 2018 per the edition-matching rule, despite the document's 2012 vintage suggesting the older edition -- that reasoning alone isn't sufficient grounds to mint.

[CONTAINMENT] Verified this is a genuine primary document (Timor-Leste Ministry of Finance, National Directorate of Statistics, April 2012, 'TL-NA 2004-2010 Volume II: Methodological Notes'), but it is a methodological companion volume to the TL-NA 2004-2010 release, not a distinct recurring or one-off publication in its own right -- it documents the same report already proposed as tl-national-accounts. Used its content (cross-checked against INETL's current national-accounts page) to support the tl-national-accounts -> sna-2008 / imf-bpm6 edges instead of minting a separate node.

[SOURCE-QUALITY] the import's batch2 evidence_url (a DEPS-hosted Supply-Use-Table-Summary.pdf) does contain the SNA-2008 sentence quoted, but on inspection it is generic international boilerplate describing what Supply-and-Use Tables are worldwide ('jointly produced by the United Nations, IMF, World Bank, OECD and the EU'), not a Brunei-specific adoption statement. I still mint bn-national-accounts -> sna-2008 (and -> sna-1993) but on the stronger, country-specific DSBB NAG00 metadata quote instead ('...in accordance with 1993/2008 System of National Accounts').

reports.title: Statistics Act 1973
reports.publisher: Parliament of Singapore / Singapore Statutes Online
reports.description: Foundational legislation establishing the Singapore Department of Statistics and research and statistics units, empowering the Chief Statistician as national statistical coordinator, and providing the legal basis for data collection, processing, confidentiality and dissemination of official statistics.

reports.title: Gross Domestic Product (Advance and Quarterly Estimates)
reports.description: Advance GDP estimates released within ~2 weeks of quarter-end and full quarterly GDP (production, expenditure and income approaches) released later in the quarter; annual comprehensive revision embedded in the Economic Survey process.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Monthly CPI measuring changes in the price level of a fixed basket of goods and services consumed by resident households; includes breakdowns by household income group and detailed item indices.

reports.title: Population Trends
reports.description: Annual report presenting the latest statistics and analysis on Singapore’s population size and structure, households and housing, family formation and dissolution, fertility and mortality.

reports.title: Yearbook of Statistics Singapore
reports.description: Flagship annual compilation providing a comprehensive statistical record of key socio-demographic and economic characteristics of Singapore across ~25–27 chapters and 270+ tables.

reports.title: Economic Survey of Singapore
reports.description: Quarterly and annual survey of Singapore’s economic performance, sectoral developments, labour market, costs and prices, external trade, balance of payments and outlook; incorporates DOS national-accounts data with policy commentary.

reports.title: Official Foreign Reserves
reports.description: Monthly data on Singapore’s official foreign reserves (foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and IMF reserve position), published both in Singapore-dollar and US-dollar terms; also includes the IMF Data Template on International Reserves and Foreign Currency Liquidity.

reports.title: Monthly Statistical Bulletin
reports.description: Monthly compilation of key monetary, banking, financial-market and selected economic indicators for Singapore, including money and banking aggregates, interest rates, exchange rates and housing/bridging loans.

reports.title: Labour Market Report
reports.publisher: Manpower Research and Statistics Department, Ministry of Manpower
reports.description: Quarterly comprehensive assessment of Singapore’s labour market covering employment change (resident and non-resident), unemployment, retrenchments, re-entry into employment, job vacancies, labour turnover and hours worked. Accompanied by an advance-release version roughly six weeks earlier.

reports.title: Monthly Unemployment Situation / End Monthly Unemployment
reports.publisher: Manpower Research and Statistics Department, Ministry of Manpower
reports.description: Timely monthly release of overall, resident and citizen unemployment rates and numbers, providing the earliest signal of labour-market conditions between the fuller quarterly Labour Market Reports.

reports.title: Balance of Payments
reports.description: Quarterly statement summarising economic transactions between Singapore residents and non-residents (current account, capital and financial account, reserve assets). Compiled under the Statistics Act and released with the Economic Survey cycle.

reports.title: Merchandise Trade Statistics
reports.publisher: Enterprise Singapore (compiled from Singapore Customs data; disseminated via DOS)
reports.description: Monthly statistics on total merchandise trade, domestic exports, non-oil domestic exports (NODX), re-exports and imports, broken down by commodity and market. Primary source for external-trade chapters of the Economic Survey.

reports.title: Key Household Income Trends
reports.description: Annual paper presenting median and average household market income (employment plus non-employment sources), income growth by decile, Gini coefficients before and after government transfers, and related distributional indicators for resident households.

reports.title: Household Expenditure Survey
reports.description: Quinquennial survey-based report on household consumption expenditure patterns, online spending, ownership of consumer durables, and related socio-economic characteristics of resident households. Latest full report covers 2023.

reports.title: International Investment Position
reports.description: Quarterly statement of the value and composition of Singapore’s cross-border financial assets and liabilities (direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives, other investment, reserve assets) at a point in time. Net IIP shows Singapore as a consistent net creditor.

reports.title: Labour Force in Singapore
reports.publisher: Manpower Research and Statistics Department, Ministry of Manpower
reports.description: Annual comprehensive report on resident labour-force outcomes drawn from the Comprehensive Labour Force Survey. Covers labour-force participation, employment rates, income growth, job mobility, underemployment and structural trends (ageing, female participation). Accompanied by an advance release.

reports.title: Index of Industrial Production
reports.publisher: Economic Development Board (Research & Statistics Unit); disseminated via Singapore Department of Statistics
reports.description: Monthly index measuring real output of the manufacturing sector, broken down by major clusters (electronics, chemicals, biomedical, precision engineering, transport engineering, general manufacturing). Rebased periodically (most recently to 2025=100).

reports.title: Unit Business Cost / Unit Labour Cost Indices
reports.description: Quarterly indices tracking unit business costs and unit labour costs for the overall economy and manufacturing sector; used as competitiveness and cost-pressure indicators in the Economic Survey of Singapore.

reports.title: Singapore in Figures
reports.description: Annual (and interactive electronic) reference publication presenting key top-line economic, demographic, social and environmental indicators of Singapore in a concise, user-friendly format. Complements the more detailed Yearbook of Statistics.

reports.title: External Debt Statistics
reports.description: Quarterly gross external debt liabilities of Singapore residents to non-residents, broken down by institutional sector, original maturity (short-term / long-term) and instrument type, including inter-company lending under direct investment. Compiled on BPM6 basis.

reports.title: Foreign Direct Investment in Singapore
reports.description: Annual statistics on the stock and flows of foreign direct investment in Singapore by source economy, industry and component (equity capital, retained earnings, net inter-company lending). Principal series and detailed breakdowns published by DOS.

reports.title: Singapore’s Direct Investment Abroad
reports.description: Annual statistics on the stock and flows of Singapore’s direct investment abroad by destination economy, industry and component. Complements the FDI-in-Singapore series and feeds the international investment position.

reports.title: Household Sector Balance Sheet
reports.description: Quarterly statement of the household sector’s financial and non-financial assets (currency & deposits, shares & securities, life insurance, CPF, residential property) and liabilities (mortgages, personal loans), yielding household net worth.

reports.title: Singapore Manufactured Products & Domestic Supply Price Indices
reports.description: Monthly price indices measuring changes in prices of goods manufactured in Singapore (SMPPI) and of goods supplied to the domestic economy (DSPI — local manufactures plus retained imports). Also covers related import and export price indices.

reports.title: Retail Sales Index and Food & Beverage Services Index
reports.description: Monthly indices measuring the sales performance of the Retail Trade and Food & Beverage services industries (value and volume terms, seasonally adjusted and unadjusted). Rebased periodically (most recently to 2025=100).

reports.title: International Visitor Arrivals and Tourism Receipts
reports.publisher: Singapore Tourism Board (data disseminated via DOS / SingStat)
reports.description: Monthly international visitor arrivals by place of residence (derived from SG Arrival Cards / immigration records) and quarterly/annual tourism receipts by major component. Core tourism-sector performance indicators.

reports.title: Job Vacancies Report
reports.publisher: Manpower Research and Statistics Department, Ministry of Manpower
reports.description: Annual detailed analysis of the job-vacancy situation, covering newly created versus replacement vacancies, occupational and industry demand, skills requirements, and duration of unfilled vacancies. Complements the quarterly job-vacancy figures in the Labour Market Report.

reports.title: Supply, Use and Input-Output Tables
reports.description: Annual (and benchmark) Supply and Use Tables recording production, intermediate consumption and final demand by product and industry, together with derived Input-Output Tables used for impact analysis, multipliers and industry inter-dependence studies. Central framework for reconciling the three approaches to GDP.

reports.title: Wholesale Trade Index and Business Receipts Index
reports.description: Quarterly indices measuring short-term performance of the wholesale trade industry (Domestic and Foreign WTI) and of selected services industries (Business Receipts Index, excluding wholesale, retail, accommodation and food services). Value and volume measures.

reports.title: Services Producer Price Indices
reports.description: Quarterly price indices measuring changes in the average prices of services produced by establishments in selected priority industries (sea freight transport, warehousing & storage, cargo handling, freight forwarding, telecommunications, computer consultancy & information services, accounting, postal & courier, etc.).

reports.title: Complete Life Tables for Singapore Resident Population
reports.description: Annual publication presenting complete life tables and key trends in life expectancy at birth and at selected ages for the Singapore resident population, by sex.

reports.title: Singapore Standard Industrial Classification 2025
reports.description: National standard for classifying economic activities of economic units. Adopted framework of ISIC Rev. 5 with Singapore-specific adaptations. Used across censuses, surveys and administrative databases. One-off foundational classification instrument (updated periodically).

reports.title: Singapore Standard Occupational Classification 2024
reports.description: National standard for classifying occupations. Adopts the basic framework of ISCO-08 with national adaptations. Used in censuses, household surveys and administrative databases. One-off foundational classification instrument (updated periodically).

reports.title: Report on Wage Practices
reports.publisher: Manpower Research and Statistics Department, Ministry of Manpower
reports.description: Annual report examining employees’ wage changes and private-sector establishments’ wage practices, including nominal and real wage growth, incidence of wage increases, and adoption of Flexible Wage System components.

reports.title: Business Expectations of the Services and Manufacturing Sectors
reports.publisher: Singapore Department of Statistics (Services) / Economic Development Board (Manufacturing)
reports.description: Quarterly survey-based indicators of firms’ general business outlook for the next six months and their operating revenue/output and employment forecasts for the next quarter. Net weighted balances are the primary published metric.

reports.title: Births and Fertility Statistics
reports.publisher: Singapore Department of Statistics (rates) / Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (registration)
reports.description: Annual (and monthly/quarterly detail) statistics on live-births, crude birth rates, total fertility rate, age-specific fertility rates and related fertility indicators for the resident and citizen populations.

reports.title: Enterprise Landscape and Corporate Sector Statistics
reports.description: Annual statistics on the number, ownership (local/foreign), size (SME/non-SME) and revenue-band structure of enterprises, together with balance-sheet aggregates for the corporate sector (total assets, equity, etc.).

dependencies.basis: The quarterly and annual Economic Survey of Singapore reports contain policy statements and data; DOS’s data are acknowledged and separated from the Ministry’s policy statements. GDP estimates (advance and preliminary) are supplied by DOS for incorporation into the Survey.

The Economic Survey of Singapore incorporates Balance of Payments data compiled by DOS; the BOP figures are supplied under embargo to MTI for inclusion in the quarterly and annual Survey chapters on external accounts.

The International Investment Position is compiled on a consistent conceptual framework with the Balance of Payments (BPM6), showing the stock positions that correspond to the flow transactions recorded in the BOP financial account and reserve assets.

External debt statistics form a key component of the liabilities side of the International Investment Position and are compiled on a consistent BPM6 conceptual framework with the IIP and Balance of Payments.

_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Senegal researched as part of a push into WAEMU territory the branch's source docx had only described in undifferentiated bloc-level prose ("Francophone (WAEMU): ...Automatic indexation is rare") without naming individual countries. Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review.
_note: The standout finding: Senegal's own SDDS metadata, as submitted to the IMF (dsbb.imf.org, a page the branch expected might be an unreadable JS-rendered SPA but which rendered fully via a live browser session), names AFRISTAT directly and by name twice, in two different DQAF sub-sections, and separately names a WAEMU Commission methodological guide by exact title ("Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices in the WAEMU Member Countries -- Theory and Practice"). This is the first time in this branch that a country's own primary document has named AFRISTAT this substantively -- stronger than the three-times-failed ECOWAS HCPI guide citation. Neither AFRISTAT nor the WAEMU guide could be minted as nodes (AFRISTAT is an institution without a title; the WAEMU guide's own text was not independently located, and a differently-titled, apparently earlier-vintage AFRISTAT-authored guide found separately is not confirmed to be the same document) -- both recorded as open citations, not forced edges. On social protection, IPRES's and the FNR's pension mechanisms both read as points/wage-based rather than CPI-indexed, but the supporting quotes trace to secondary sources (CLEISS, a French government liaison body; a Senegalese news article) because Senegal's own Journal Officiel site and IPRES's own site could not be reached this session -- flagged as leads pending primary-text confirmation, not settled denials.

_open_questions.question: Senegal's own SDDS metadata names a WAEMU Commission guide by exact title ("Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices in the WAEMU Member Countries -- Theory and Practice") as its methodological reference. A differently-titled AFRISTAT guide ("Guide methodologique de l'IHPC dans la zone UEMOA") was found and read, but its evidenced base year (~2008) predates Senegal's current 2023-base IHPC, so it is very likely a superseded earlier edition rather than the document Senegal's metadata cites. The exact document Senegal cites was not located.

Senegal's own SDDS metadata page states two different monthly release dates for the same IHPC on the same page: Sections 1.1.2/4.1.2 say the 30th of month m+1; Sections 5.1.3/5.1.4 say the 10th. ANSD's own December 2025 bulletin independently supports the 10th. The 30th-day language looks like unrevised legacy text but this is not confirmed.

jo.gouv.sn (Senegal's official gazette) and budget.sec.gouv.sn did not load this session, blocking direct verification of the pension code (Loi 81-52/2002-08) and the 2018 complementary-pension law's implementing arrete. IPRES's own site (secusociale.ipres.sn) also failed to load. Findings on both pension systems currently rest on secondary sources (CLEISS, a Senegalese news outlet) pending a session that can reach these primary hosts.

reports.title: Indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation (IHPC)
reports.publisher: Agence Nationale de la Statistique et de la Démographie (ANSD)
reports.description: Senegal's official consumer price index, base 2023 ("Base 100 en 2023"). Classification stated directly as COICOP 2018 via a regional adaptation: "L'indice est structure selon la nomenclature de consommation ouest africaine (NCOA) 2018, tiree de la classification des fonctions de consommation des menages (COICOP) 2018." Formula is a Young index, explicitly not Laspeyres ("les indices de Young sont privilegies plutot que ceux de Laspeyres"). Corroborated independently by Senegal's own IMF SDDS metadata submission, which restates the same base year, classification and formula.
reports.cadence_note: ANSD's own December 2025 bulletin states publication "au plus tard le 10 du mois suivant" -- but Senegal's SDDS metadata gives a conflicting "30th of month m+1" in two sections while agreeing with "10th" in two others on the same page (see sn-release-date-conflict-10th-vs-30th). Rebased on a 5-year cycle per the SDDS metadata: "The HICP is updated every 5 years."

release_schedule.rule: ANSD's monthly IHPC bulletin states publication "au plus tard le 10 du mois suivant" (no later than the 10th of the following month) — confirmed as the operative pattern: the March 2026 IHPC note was posted to the site's 2026-04 folder, the December 2025 note was posted to the 2026-01 folder, and the July 2026 note was covered in press articles (pressafrik.com, dakaractu.com) published August 10-11, 2026, i.e. right at the 10th-of-the-following-month mark.
release_schedule.note: Most recent observed release: the July 2026 IHPC note, published on/around 2026-08-10 (per press coverage referencing it as newly published on 10-11 Aug 2026), consistent with the 'by the 10th of month m+1' rule already documented in this report's existing cadence_note (which also flags a conflicting SDDS mention of the 30th). Next release (August 2026 data) is expected by 2026-09-10.

"La pension annuelle est calculee selon la formule suivante : (Points de cotisations + points gratuits - points de minoration + points de majoration) x valeur du point", with the point value administratively set ("parametres IPRES 2025") -- CLEISS (French inter-agency social-security liaison body), describing Senegal's system. No CPI/inflation-indexation language found. Caveat: this is CLEISS's description of IPRES, not IPRES's own primary text -- IPRES's own site could not be reached this session (see sn-primary-legal-texts-unreachable); this denial should be re-verified against IPRES's own statutes.

"la modification du mode de calcul de la pension basee sur la moyenne des emoluments des trois dernieres annees" -- a Senegalese news article's account of Loi n2002-08 amending Loi n81-52. Wage-based (average of the final three years' pay), not CPI-indexed, per this source. "Modalites de gestion (indexation, rachat de cotisations, remuneration des reserves) fixees par arrete du Ministre charge des Finances" -- the law itself (per a government summary page, not the full statute) defers the indexation mechanism to a ministerial order not located this session.
