reports.title: Local Government: The Urban Government Act No. 8 of 1969
reports.description: Eswatini's (then Swaziland's) foundational urban-municipal-finance statute. Part IX ('Municipal Funds'), Section 86 ('Revenues of the council'): 'The revenues of a council shall consist of-- (a) all rates lawfully levied by the council; ... (g) all moneys paid to the council by the Government as contributions, grants, endowment or otherwise, except where such moneys are paid with a condition as to the purpose for which such moneys are paid...' -- establishing government grants as one permitted category of council revenue, though the Act itself states no allocation formula or percentage; the actual subvention/CIP-grant amounts are set by later Ministry of Housing administrative practice (see sz-mohud-annual-report-2024-25). Section 57(1) separately grants own-source fee authority: 'a council may charge fees for any service or facility provided by it or for any licence or permit issued by it.' HOSTING/QUALITY CAVEAT: this PDF is hosted by Gender Links (genderlinks.org.za), a South African NGO, not an Eswatini-government domain -- no official gov.sz/legislation portal copy could be located (the gov.sz 'ACTS' resources page does not list it). It is nonetheless authentic statutory text; its section numbering is independently corroborated by the Ministry of Housing's FY2024/25 report, which separately cites 'Section 115' and 'Section 8' of the same Act. The scanned/OCR'd PDF also has significant digit-garbling errors (e.g. '35.' for '85.', '36.' for '86.', page-footer range markers like 'ss.85-87' confirming the correct numbering despite garbled in-body digits); the quotes above are reproduced in cleaned form.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational statute (Act No. 8 of 1969), not a recurring publication.

reports.title: Implementation Completion and Results Report (IBRD-80030) on a Loan to the Government of Eswatini for the Swaziland Local Government Project (SLGP)
reports.description: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR00004807), closed December 2019. On Eswatini's dual local-government structure: 'The country has two categories of local government, namely Urban Local Governments (ULG) and Rural Local Governments, known as Tinkhundla... Formally, there are two City Councils (Manzini and Mbabane), five Town Councils and six Town Boards (five part of the Project)... The two City Councils are facing conditions of severe fiscal distress, characterized by weak revenue performance, high fixed operating costs, and ongoing deterioration in the quality of service delivery. Other Councils and Boards remain heavily reliant on central transfers to finance their expenditures... There is a total of 55 Tinkhundla or rural local governments.' On the project's limited lasting effect: 'There has been no action on the part of GOE to move towards a more stable fiscal transfer system and mainstreaming of performance-based grants (as recommended by reports produced by this project), and own source revenue in ULGs and Tinkundla remain very low.' A non-primary/context-flagged international-financial-institution report, but directly load-bearing here: Mbabane Municipal Council's own annual report explicitly states its capital-grant eligibility assessment is 'adapted from' this project (see the dependency edge below).

reports.description: CNPS's own guide to insured persons' rights (2019 edition), stating the pension calculation formula directly: "La pension de retraite est calculée en pourcentage des salaires soumis à cotisation. Il est égal au produit du salaire moyen de trois ou cinq dernières années de la carrière par le [taux] de remplacement. Ce taux qui est de 30% pour le 15 premières années est majoré de 1,2% pour chaque année supplémentaire au délà de 15ème année." A one-time, final-average-wage-based calculation with no post-award revaluation clause found anywhere in the 763-line guide.

_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Togo researched as part of a second WAEMU/CEMAC push (following G.11's Senegal/Côte d'Ivoire/Mali/Cameroon batch). Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review.
_note: This session resolves a standing branch-wide open question, carried across Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire and Mali in G.11: whether the UEMOA Council of Ministers ever formally adopted a base-2023 harmonised-CPI regulation, and if so, its number. It did: UEMOA's own Bulletin Officiel de l'Union N°123 (4e trimestre 2024) -- the Union's official gazette, obtained and OCR'd directly this session -- contains the full text of Règlement N°05/2024/CM/UEMOA du 20 décembre 2024, adopted at Bamako, effective 1 January 2025, which formally adopts the base-2023 IHPC methodological guide and abrogates both Règlement n°03/2017/CM/UEMOA (the base-2014 regulation Mali's session located and quoted secondhand) and Règlement n°08/2006/CM/UEMOA (underlying inflation calculation). Independently corroborated by BCEAO's own 20 December 2024 communiqué and by a UEMOA Commission official quoted in Niger's press. Togo's own INSEED, even in its most recent (June 2026) documents, does not itself cite this regulation by number -- the resolving document had to come from UEMOA's own gazette, not from Togo's statistics office, mirroring the pattern found for Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire in this same round.

_open_questions.question: Togo's own 2018 IMF metadata names 'Harmonized Consumer Price Index for WAEMU Member Countries – Theory and Practice' (WAEMU Commission, near-identical title to Senegal's and Burkina Faso's own citations) as the reference methodology document. Still not located as a retrievable file by any of the three countries that have now named it.

Togo's IMF DSBB CPI-specific metadata (dsbb.imf.org, CPI00 category) is dated 'Last Updated: Jul 08, 2018' and describes base year 2008 and Lomé-only coverage -- two rebasings and one coverage-expansion out of date relative to Togo's own current bulletins. Togo's e-GDDS participation status itself is confirmed current via a separate, live government data portal (togo.opendataforafrica.org), but the CPI-specific detail page has not been refreshed.

CRT's (Caisse de Retraites du Togo, civil-service pension fund) founding Loi N°91-11 du 23 mai 1991 and Décret N°91-208 du 6 septembre 1991 are listed by title on CRT's own site but their full text was not retrievable this session -- any indexation clause they may contain is unchecked.

reports.title: Indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation (IHPC) Togo
reports.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique et des Études Économiques et Démographiques (INSEED)
reports.description: Togo's monthly harmonised consumer price index under the common WAEMU/UEMOA methodology, base 2023 as of the June 2026 bulletin. "Cet indice est dit harmonisé car il repose sur une méthodologie commune, adoptée en 1996 par les huit pays membres de l'Union Économique et Monétaire Ouest-Africaine (UEMOA), puis rénovée successivement en 2008 et 2023." 810 products tracked at 4,790 points of sale, ~29,200 monthly price collections, weights from EHCVM 2021.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly bulletin.

reports.title: Règlement N°05/2024/CM/UEMOA du 20 décembre 2024 portant adoption du Guide méthodologique définissant les modalités d'élaboration et de calcul de l'Indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation au sein des États membres de l'UEMOA (IHPC base 100 en 2023)
reports.region: WAEMU (8 member states: Bénin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Guinée-Bissau, Mali, Niger, Sénégal, Togo)
reports.description: One-off foundational instrument formally adopting the base-2023 IHPC methodological guide for all eight WAEMU member states, effective 1 January 2025, replacing the base-2014 regulation. Article premier: "Est adopté le Guide méthodologique définissant les modalités d'élaboration, de calcul et de diffusion de l'indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation au sein des États membres de l'UEMOA (IHPC base 100 en 2023)..." Article 7: "L'IHPC base 100 en 2023 sert de mesure officielle des variations des prix à la consommation dans les États membres de l'UEMOA, en remplacement de l'IHPC base 100 en 2014." Article 11: "Le présent Règlement abroge le Règlement n°03/2017/CM/UEMOA du 31 mars 2017... et le Règlement n°08/2006/CM/UEMOA du 29 juin 2006..." Article 12: "Le présent Règlement prend effet à compter du 1er janvier 2025... Fait à Bamako, le 20 décembre 2024." Obtained from UEMOA's own official gazette, Bulletin Officiel de l'Union N°123 (4e trimestre 2024), via OCR of the scanned original.

dependencies.basis: Règlement N°05/2024/CM/UEMOA Article 2: "Les États membres préservent le caractère national et harmonisé de la méthodologie de calcul de l'indice... A ce titre, ils s'appuient sur la méthodologie de l'IHPC base 100 en 2023 et utilisent exclusivement le progiciel mis à leur disposition par la Commission de l'UEMOA." Togo is a named UEMOA member state bound by this regulation (cover page of the Bulletin Officiel lists all eight, including Togo, by name). Note: Togo's own INSEED documents do not independently cite this regulation by number -- the dependency is established by the regulation's own binding text, not by a Togo self-citation.

SELF-DECLARED: Togo's own government data portal (Togo Data Portal, opendataforafrica.org): "Data linked from this page correspond to data described in the International Monetary Fund's DSBB. For a fuller explanation of the DSBB and the enhanced General Data Dissemination System in which Togo participates..." lists Consumer Price Index as a live e-GDDS category. Reuses the imf-e-gdds node already minted elsewhere in this branch. This is the live, current confirmation -- distinct from Togo's CPI-specific DSBB metadata, which is stale (see tg-2018-dsbb-metadata-stale).
dependencies.evidence_quote: Data linked from this page correspond to data described in the International Monetary Fund’s DSBB. For a fuller explanation of the DSBB and the enhanced General Data Dissemination System in which Togo participates, please visit the DSBB home page.

_dropped.why: CNSS's own regulatory-texts index (cnss.tg/documentation/textes-reglementaires/) lists the full Code de Sécurité Sociale plus every 2023 AMU decree, with no revalorization instrument. A detailed secondary compendium (CLEISS) states the CNSS pension formula fully (20% of last-5-years average + 1.33%/year beyond 180 months, floor/ceiling tied to the legal minimum wage) but never mentions CPI, inflation, or periodic revalorization. Searched and confirmed absent, not merely unresearched.

CRT's own site names only Loi 91-11 and Décret 91-208 as its governing texts and states a 20%/7% contribution split on its missions page, but gives no indexation clause there. Full statutory text of Loi 91-11/Décret 91-208 was not retrievable this session (titles only, see tg-crt-founding-texts-unreadable).

An IPA (Innovations for Poverty Action) design brief states the Novissi cash-transfer amount was set as 30% of the monthly minimum wage (SMIG, 35,000 FCFA), not linked to IHPC/inflation: 'The inter-ministerial committee determined that the transfer should approximate the minimum wage.' No CPI-linkage found. This is a secondary NGO/academic brief describing the 2020 emergency launch design, not a retrieved Togolese government primary document -- novissi.gouv.tg itself returned HTTP errors on every fetch attempt this session.

INSEED's own site names AFRISTAT only in an institutional/governance context -- Togo's 2024-2025 presidency of AFRISTAT's Council of Ministers -- never as a cited methodological source for the IHPC itself. Contrast with a UEMOA Commission official quoted in Niger's press, who credits AFRISTAT as 'maître d'œuvre technique' of the regional IHPC rebasing project Togo participated in as one of the eight member states.

Togo's own 2018 e-GDDS DSBB submission states NCOA is 'derived directly from the international COICOP' -- a real methodology_depends_on candidate -- but that submission is stale (last updated 2018, still describing base-2008/Lomé-only IHPC). No 2023-era INSEED document re-confirms the COICOP linkage; the June 2026 bulletin names only 'NCOA-IHPC' without the COICOP cross-reference. Deferred rather than minted until a current-dated source is found.

reports.title: National Statistical Office of Thailand (NSO) institutional core
reports.description: Primary national statistical office responsible for censuses, surveys, national accounts coordination, prices, labour, demographic and multi-domain socio-economic statistics. Publishes the Statistical Yearbook and major survey series.
reports._notes: Foundational institutional node for the Thai statistical system.
reports._cadence_evidence: The given URL (nso.go.th root) resolves to a language-selection splash carrying only a tagline and navigation images - no publication list, no calendar. The NSO main page behind it names census programmes and refers to a 'ปฏิทินการเผยแพร่ข้อมูล' (data release calendar) but does not state a frequency for the office's own output, so no single cadence is evidenced.

reports.title: Population census and estimates
reports.description: Official population census and subsequent estimates. Population is approximately 71–72 million; Thailand is an upper-middle-income economy with advanced demographic transition and rising aging.
reports._notes: Core demographic node. Population ~71.5 million.
reports._cadence_evidence: Same nso.go.th root URL as the institutional node - a language splash with no content. The NSO main page lists a Population and Housing Census among its programmes but gives no census interval and no schedule for the intercensal population estimates, so the page does not establish a frequency.

reports.title: National Accounts of Thailand (GDP)
reports.publisher: Office of the National Economic and Social Development Council (NESDC)
reports.description: Official national accounts (GDP by industry and expenditure). Central macro-output series for a diversified upper-middle-income economy with strong tourism, manufacturing and agricultural foundations.
reports._notes: Primary macroeconomic output node. NESDC is the key national accounts compiler.
reports._url_evidence: NESDC National Account hub page: lists National Income of Thailand (NI), Quarterly GDP (QGDP), GPP, capital stock and flow-of-funds series.
reports._cadence_evidence: NESDC national accounts page groups its products under 'สถิติ/ข้อมูลที่เผยแพร่ประจำ' (regularly published statistics) and names Quarterly Gross Domestic Product (ผลิตภัณฑ์มวลรวมในประเทศรายไตรมาส) alongside annual National Income, Gross Regional and Provincial Product, capital stock, flow-of-funds and input-output tables. Quarterly GDP is the finest stated cycle, hence 4; the annual NI and the Gross Regional and Provincial Product series sit at 1 within the same page. Note: this is the only item in the Thai file pointing at NESDC - no five-item shared Gross Regional and Provincial Product page exists in this input; the repeated URLs here are nso.go.th (2 items) and bot.or.th (3 items). No release dates are printed on the page.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index and inflation statistics
reports.description: Monthly CPI and inflation rates. Thailand has generally maintained low-to-moderate inflation relative to many peers in recent years.
reports._notes: Core high-frequency price node.
reports._url_evidence: Trade Policy and Strategy Office (Ministry of Commerce) CPI/inflation landing page listing monthly CPI series, regional indices and base-year methodology notes.

reports.title: Bank of Thailand (BOT) institutional and reporting core
reports.description: Central bank responsible for monetary policy, financial stability, foreign-exchange management and key macro-financial and external statistics. Publishes monetary, banking, exchange-rate, BOP and related series.
reports._notes: Central-bank institutional counterpart to NSO/NESDC.
reports._cadence_evidence: The given URL (bot.or.th root) is a language-selection splash with no publication content. The BOT statistics section behind it states only generic timing rules across four tiers - daily published every business day, weekly on the last business day of the following week, monthly on the last business day of the following month, quarterly on the last business day of the following quarter - and assigns no cadence to the institution as a whole, so no single number is supportable.

reports.title: Balance of Payments and external accounts
reports.description: BOP and external-sector statistics. Tourism and goods exports (electronics, vehicles, agriculture) are major credits; the external accounts are a central policy focus.
reports._notes: External-accounts node with important tourism and manufacturing signatures.
reports._cadence_evidence: Same bot.or.th root splash. The external-sector statistics page that carries balance of payments prints no frequency label next to the BOP, trade or external-debt tables - it only announces a June 2026 revision to 26 external-sector tables and refers users to individual table descriptions or an email contact. Frequency not stated on the page.

reports.title: Tourism arrivals and tourism revenue statistics
reports.description: Official statistics on international visitor arrivals and tourism receipts. Tourism is a major services credit in the balance of payments; recent years show arrivals in the low-to-mid 30 millions range and revenue in the multi-trillion-baht range.
reports._notes: High-centrality services and external-earnings node. Core uniqueness for Thailand.
reports._url_evidence: Ministry of Tourism and Sports tourism statistics hub, indexing yearly international tourist arrival and tourism revenue statistics from 2008 to 2026.
reports._cadence_evidence: Ministry of Tourism and Sports category 411 is organised as one entry per year, 'สถิติด้านการท่องเที่ยว ปี X', running from 2008 through 2026 (Thai years 2551-2569), plus a few one-off dated items from 2019. The listing is an annual repository; no monthly or weekly editions appear at this level.

reports.title: Industrial production and manufacturing statistics
reports.description: Industrial production index and manufacturing output statistics. Key segments include automotive, electronics, food, rubber/plastics, petroleum products and related manufactures that underpin export performance.
reports._notes: Core high-frequency industrial activity node.
reports._url_evidence: Office of Industrial Economics 'Industrial Indices' page listing the Production Index, Shipment, Inventory, Labour and Capacity Utilisation indices with downloadable data.

reports.title: Labour force and unemployment statistics
reports.description: Labour-force participation, employment and unemployment rates from the Labour Force Survey. Unemployment is typically very low by international standards (around or below 1% in recent readings).
reports._notes: Primary labour-market statistical product. Structurally low unemployment.

reports.title: ASEAN merchandise trade statistics
reports.description: Merchandise trade with ASEAN partners. ASEAN is a core regional market and production-network partner for Thai manufacturing and agricultural exports.
reports._notes: Primary regional trade densification.
reports._url_evidence: Ministry of Commerce official trade statistics report system; provides export/import/balance data with a country-group selection covering ASEAN.
reports._cadence_evidence: MOC tradereport portal is an interactive query system - dashboards by country and product, harmonised-code search, monthly/yearly filters and API endpoints - rather than dated report releases. It links to a 'Statistic Publication Date' page but states no update frequency on this page.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7) and applied 2026-08-19: a nominal releases_per_year so that absence keeps meaning 'one-off instrument' only - 250 encodes business-day updating (the live corpus's daily-FX convention), 365 genuinely all-days monitoring. It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

reports.title: Agriculture production statistics
reports.description: Official volume and value statistics for major crops and livestock. Rice and rubber are the two highest-centrality agricultural commodities; other significant products include sugarcane, cassava, palm oil and fruits.
reports._notes: Core primary-sector production node.
reports._url_evidence: Office of Agricultural Economics data catalogue entry for 'Agricultural Statistics of Thailand' (annual): area, production, yield, farm-gate prices and land use by province.
reports._cadence_evidence: OAE data catalogue metadata for สถิติการเกษตรของประเทศไทย states 'หน่วยความถี่ของการปรับปรุงข้อมูล: ทุกปี' (update frequency unit: every year). Record last modified 2568 (2025); data last updated 24 March 2564 (2021).

reports.title: Rice production and export statistics
reports.description: Focused statistics on rice production, area and exports. Thailand is a major global rice exporter; the crop remains central to rural livelihoods and food-security framing.
reports._notes: Foundational food and export crop node.
reports._url_evidence: OAE dataset 'ปริมาณการผลิตข้าว': planted/harvested area, production and yield for wet- and dry-season rice by province from 1981; covers production only, not exports.
reports._cadence_evidence: OAE catalogue metadata for ปริมาณการผลิตข้าว (rice production quantity) gives 'หน่วยความถี่ของการปรับปรุงข้อมูล: ปี' (update frequency unit: year). Last updated 1 October 2566 (2023).

reports.title: Natural rubber production and export statistics
reports.description: Statistics on natural rubber planting area, production (dry rubber content) and exports. Thailand is among the world’s largest rubber producers and exporters; the southern region dominates production.
reports._notes: High-centrality industrial-crop and export node.
reports._url_evidence: OAE dataset for rubber (ยางพารา): standing area, tapped area, production and yield per rai by province, data from 1988 onward.
reports._cadence_evidence: OAE catalogue metadata for ปริมาณการผลิตยางพารา (rubber production volume) gives update frequency unit 'ปี' with a frequency value of 1, i.e. once a year. Record updated 12 September 2568 (2025); latest data year 2565 (2022).

reports.title: Public debt statistics
reports.publisher: Public Debt Management Office / Ministry of Finance
reports.description: Official statistics on public debt stock, composition (government, SOE, guarantees) and debt-to-GDP ratio. Recent readings place public debt in the mid-60s percent of GDP range.
reports._notes: Core public-debt stock node.
reports._url_evidence: PDMO public debt outstanding page showing monthly government, SOE, SFI and agency debt plus the debt-to-GDP ratio (63-65%).
reports._cadence_evidence: PDMO debt-outstanding page carries one entry per month in an unbroken run - September 2024 through July 2025 - covering government, state-enterprise and SFI debt plus the debt-to-GDP ratio. No schedule is stated in words; monthly cadence counted from the consecutive dated entries.

reports.title: Bangkok Gross Regional / Provincial Product
reports.publisher: Office of the National Economic and Social Development Council (NESDC)
reports.description: Official GRDP for Bangkok — the dominant primate-city economy, accounting for a very large share of national GDP through services, finance, trade, tourism and headquarters activity.
reports._notes: Primary primate-city economic node. Highest single provincial share.

_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Tunisia is the third of three North Africa countries researched this session (AF/G.9 priority 1) -- Algeria and Morocco alongside it. Researched by a subagent this session against the branch's full Research.1.md discipline, reading INS's own methodology brief directly plus the operative pension statutes for both CNRPS (public) and CNSS (private). Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review, following the established DRAFT-then-import pattern.
_note: Tunisia is the third and clearest North Africa confirmation of a now-familiar branch pattern: real, statutory, non-CPI benefit-adjustment mechanisms rather than either an explicit denial or plain silence. The CNRPS (public-sector) pension statute automatically re-adjusts pensions whenever the retiree's civil-service pay grade rises ('péréquation'); the CNSS (private-sector) decree automatically revalues pensions in payment at every increase in the SMIG (minimum wage). Both are corroborated independently by the ISSA and SSA/ISSA country profiles, which each state plainly: 'Not legally mandated. Indexed based on changes in the legal minimum wage.' Tunisia's flagship cash-transfer programme, PNAFN, shows a third shape again: no formula of any kind was found in any document reviewed, CPI-based or otherwise -- its benefit level has moved through a documented series of discrete ad hoc increases (TND 7.7 in 1987 to TND 180 in 2020) that an academic working paper compares only to the minimum wage, never to the CPI. On the CPI itself, Tunisia is confirmed on the IMF's stronger SDDS dissemination tier -- directly quoted from the IMF's own 2024 Annual Observance Report -- with a documented, quoted timeliness lapse in practice attributed to a December 2024 SDMX platform migration, worth noting as a genuine deviation rather than smoothed over.

_open_questions.question: INS's methodology brief names 'COICOP' with a 12-division structure matching the pre-2018 vintage, not the restructured COICOP 2018. The `un-coicop-2018` edge below should be treated as approximate pending a document that states the exact vintage Tunisia applies.

A secondary source (finco.tn) describes SMIG (minimum wage) increases as set via periodic government décret on a multi-year negotiated schedule, and a press commentary piece (webmanagercenter.com) states increases run 'toujours en retard sur l'inflation réelle' (always lagging behind actual inflation) -- both consistent with no automatic CPI-indexation of the SMIG itself, but the underlying Journal Officiel décret text was not reached directly this session (site access blocked).

An African Development Bank evaluation titled (in French) 'Performance of Tunisia's Social Assistance System and the Challenges of Informality' could not be retrieved this session -- the URL returned a Cloudflare bot-check page on two separate attempts. Its title suggests it may contain directly relevant material on PNAFN benefit adequacy.

Unlike Tanzania, Malawi and Eswatini (each of which has a titled national social-protection strategy/policy document explicitly discussing benefit adequacy vs. inflation), no equivalent Tunisian Ministry of Social Affairs strategy document was located this session -- only press commentary. Worth a further search specifically on social.gov.tn.

reports.title: Indice des Prix à la Consommation Familiale, Base 100 en 2015
reports.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique (INS), Tunisia
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via INS's own methodology brief. 'L'INS a finalisé la confection d'un nouvel indice des prix à la consommation familiale (IPC) base 100 en 2015, en remplacement de l'ancien indice base 100 en 2010.' Formula: elementary aggregates via 'la formule de Jevons' (geometric mean), higher-level aggregation via 'la formule de Laspeyres.' Classification: 'La classification des fonctions de consommation des ménages (Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose - COICOP)... comporte 12 fonctions' -- version unstated, structure matches the pre-2018 vintage (see _open_questions). The full 6-page brief was searched for 'FMI'/'IMF', 'manuel', 'SNA'/'comptabilité nationale', 'Arabe', 'Maghreb' -- none appear as a compliance statement.

release_schedule.note: INS Tunisia publishes a rolling release calendar (www.ins.tn/calendar) listing dated CPI releases; each release covers the prior calendar month and is issued on the 5th of the following month (e.g. July 2026 CPI released 05/08/2026, per the calendar and confirmed by the actual publication https://www.ins.tn/publication/indice-des-prix-la-consommation-fevrier-2026 dated 05/03/2026 for February 2026 data). The next four scheduled releases as listed on the calendar are given below.

reports.title: Enquête Nationale sur le Budget, la Consommation et le Niveau de vie des ménages 2015
reports.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique (INS), Tunisia
reports.description: National household budget, consumption and living-standards survey conducted 2015-2016. Per INS's own CPI methodology brief: 'La structure de pondération a été calculée sur la base des données issues de l'enquête sur le budget et la consommation des ménages effectuée par l'INS en 2015-2016.'

reports.title: Loi n° 85-12 du 5 mars 1985, portant régime des pensions civiles et militaires de retraite et des survivants dans le secteur public
reports.publisher: République Tunisienne / Journal Officiel de la République Tunisienne (JORT)
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (as amended by Loi n° 2007-43 du 25 juin 2007). Public-sector pension statute administered by the Caisse Nationale de Retraite et de Prévoyance Sociale (CNRPS). Article 37 (nouveau): 'La péréquation de la pension est effectuée lors de toute augmentation de l'un quelconque des éléments permanents de la rémunération correspondante au grade ou à la fonction sur la base de laquelle a été liquidée la pension.' A mandatory but salary-grade-linked mechanism, not CPI-linked; no mention of inflation or a price index anywhere in Articles 35-38 (all read directly).

reports.title: Décret n° 74-499 du 27 avril 1974, relatif au régime de vieillesse, d'invalidité et de survivants dans le secteur non agricole
reports.publisher: République Tunisienne / Journal Officiel de la République Tunisienne (JORT)
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Private-sector (non-agricultural) old-age, disability and survivors' pension decree administered by the Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (CNSS). Article 53 (nouveau): 'Le montant des pensions au cours de paiement est revalorisé automatiquement à chaque augmentation du SMIG.' A mandatory, automatic mechanism tied to the SMIG (minimum wage), not CPI. Also sets a pension floor at '2/3 du SMIG' -- again minimum-wage-referenced, not CPI-referenced.

reports.title: Programme National d'Aide aux Familles Nécessiteuses (PNAFN)
reports.description: Tunisia's flagship non-contributory unconditional cash-transfer programme for needy families, established 1986. Per the World Bank's own Project Information Document (P506533): 'based mainly on unconditional permanent cash transfers (PCT) to households who lack financial and family support, such as the elderly poor and individuals with disabilities.' Per an Economic Research Forum working paper, the monthly benefit has risen through discrete ad hoc increases (TND 7.7 in 1987, TND 36.3 in 2000, TND 56.7 in 2010, TND 105 in 2013, TND 180 in 2020) compared throughout only to the minimum wage (SMIG), never to CPI. No CPI-indexation formula was found in any document reviewed.

The same report documents a 2024 timeliness lapse for this category, attributed to a December 2024 SDMX platform migration -- graded as 'cites' rather than 'methodology_depends_on' because this is the IMF's own external assessment, not a first-person compliance statement in INS's own CPI documents.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Tunisia subscribed to the SDDS on June 20, 2001, and met all the SDDS requirements at the time of subscription,

_dropped.why: Full 6-page INS methodology brief searched; no mention of 'FMI', 'IMF' or 'manuel' as a compliance statement. The two-stage Jevons/Laspeyres formula matches standard CPI Manual guidance but the document never names the Manual.

The only national-accounts reference found is a use-case bullet describing the CPI as a deflator for national accounts aggregates -- the reverse direction, and no reference to the SNA 2008 standard by name.

_dropped.edge: tn-ins-cpi cites an Arab/Maghreb regional statistical body
_dropped.why: Searched INS methodology brief and web search terms for AITRS, the Arab Monetary Fund, and the Union du Maghreb Arabe -- no Tunisia-specific document naming any of these in connection with the CPI was found.

Loi n° 85-12, Article 37 (nouveau), ties 'péréquation' to increases in the civil-service salary scale, not to any price index. Corroborated by ISSA and SSA/ISSA country profiles: 'Not legally mandated. Indexed based on changes in the legal minimum wage' -- itself confirming no CPI linkage, attributing adjustment instead to minimum-wage movements (see tn-cnss-vieillesse-decret for the specific minimum-wage mechanism).

Décret n° 74-499, Article 53 (nouveau): pensions are tied to the SMIG (minimum wage), not to CPI/inflation. Corroborated independently by ISSA Country Profile: Tunisia ('Not legally mandated. Indexed based on changes in the legal minimum wage') and SSA SSPTW Africa 2019 -- Tunisia ('Benefits are indexed based on changes in the legal minimum wage').

An Economic Research Forum working paper documents a series of discrete ad hoc nominal increases (TND 7.7 in 1987 to TND 180 in 2020) compared only to the minimum wage, never to CPI. A World Bank Project Information Document discusses inflation only as macroeconomic context, with no statement connecting it to PNAFN benefit-setting in either direction. No formula of any kind was found for PNAFN.

_dropped.edge: Tunisia's SMIG (minimum wage) is automatically indexed to CPI/inflation
_dropped.why: Secondary sources describe SMIG increases as set via periodic government décret on a negotiated multi-year schedule, with one commentary piece noting increases run 'toujours en retard sur l'inflation réelle' -- implying no automatic CPI-indexation, but the underlying Journal Officiel décret text was not reached directly this session. See tn-smig-cpi-link-unverified.

Reopened per PLAYBOOK-CORPUS.md §7d and ruled 2026-09-08: no document in this family names a COICOP edition/revision at all -- the source text says bare 'COICOP' or 'nomenclature COICOP' with no year, no 'Rev.', no '2018'. Reading '2018' onto that silence is the researcher's inference, not the document's statement -- exactly the inference the corpus's own IMTS-Revision-2 refusal (round5-little-things-2026-09-06.json _dropped) exists to block, and the same standard that required un-coicop-hbs-1999 and un-coicop-2018 themselves to only be minted where a country's own document spelled out the edition by name (CAPMAS's 'COICOP-HBS 2000/1999', South Africa's 'the 2018 version of ... COICOP'). Here too the case against 2018 is stronger than silence alone: the cited brief's 12-division structure matches the pre-2018 vintage, not the restructured 2018 revision -- the evidence points away from the very target it was wired to. Dropping rather than keeping the caveated wire: three rounds converging on the same 'wire with a vintage caveat' shape doesn't make it consistent with the rule those rounds were themselves trying to honour.

TurkStat PDF 'Main Revisions Studies on Gross Domestic Product by Provinces - Explanatory Note', published by TurkStat's Directorate of National Accounts Department, Presidency of Regional Accounts Group, dated 11 December 2025. It is the official TurkStat document for the Il Bazinda Gayrisafi Yurt Ici Hasila series: it sets out data sources and calculation methods for provincial GDP at current prices and chain-linked volume indices, the 2025 main revision, ESA-2010 alignment, and states the regional GDP series have been extended back to 2000 across all 81 provinces (Annex 1 gives the full IBBS/NUTS classification). dependencies.basis: The 2025 (114年) National Defense Report's own source note, under its defence-budget-to-GDP comparison, states that the MND budget figure the report publishes is computed from the enacted (法定) FY2024 defence budget at a stated exchange rate. Verbatim (English edition): "The MND budget is calculated based on the legal budget in 2024 at an NTD to USD exchange rate of 30.651:1." The Chinese edition carries the same note: 「國防部預算」係以113年法定預算為列計基礎，按美元計畫匯率 30.651：1 換算。 This resolves the direction of the previously-deferred candidate, which ran the other way: nothing on the budget-document side says budget compilation draws on the National Defense Report.

The same source note in the 2025 National Defense Report states that the ROC GDP figure used throughout its defence-budget-to-GDP analysis is taken from DGBAS's published data, dated to a specific DGBAS release. Verbatim (English edition): "The GDP of the ROC is based on the data announced by the Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics, Executive Yuan on August 15, 2025." Chinese edition: 中華民國「GDP」係參考行政院主計總處114年8月15日公布之數據。

The 2025 National Defense Report states that the MND personnel-maintenance budget line (NT$186.9 billion for FY2025) is computed on the basis of budgeted authorised strength (預算員額), taking recruitment, retention results and recent actual payroll headcount as inputs. Verbatim (English edition): "The personnel budget is NT$186.9 billion, which is mainly calculated based on manpower and takes into account personnel recruitment, retention results, actual payroll numbers in recent years, and is reviewed on a rolling basis." Chinese edition: 人員維持 1,869 億元，主要以預算員額為核算基礎，並參考近年人員招募、留營成效、實際發薪人數等因素，滾動檢討。

The 2025 National Defense Report states that the FY2025 uplift to the service members' meal-expense budget line was set by reference to the food-class consumer price index published by DGBAS — a named CPI component series used as a direct input to a defence budget figure. Verbatim (English edition): "Due to inflation, after referencing the consumer price index for food announced by the Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics, Executive Yuan, the budget for meal expenses of service members was increased from NT$2,969-NT$4,779 to NT$3,487-NT$5,947 in 2025." Chinese edition names the series precisely as 食物類消費者物價指數, which is why the target is the CPI component series rather than the headline CPI publication.

The 2025 National Defense Report states that the All-out Defense Mobilization Integrated Information System — run by MND's All-Out Defense Mobilization Agency, secretariat of the Whole-of-Society Defense Resilience Committee — integrates strategic-supply and materials-facility information supplied across ministries and local governments into a single mobilisation resource platform. Verbatim (English edition): "The All-out Defense Mobilization Integrated Information System integrates information on civilian defense resources, supplies and facilities, strategic supplies and air defense shelters, shelters, first aid stations, and non-gratuitous rationing stations, linking central and local government mobilization information and resources."
