It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

reports.title: Cultural and language institutional statistics (Hakka Affairs Council, Council of Indigenous Peoples, cultural budgets)
reports.publisher: Hakka Affairs Council / Council of Indigenous Peoples / Ministry of Culture
reports.description: Budget, programme and output statistics of the principal cultural and language institutions. Provide the organisational backbone for the language-revitalisation and Indigenous/Hakka policy clusters.
reports._notes: Institutional densification of the cultural cluster.
reports._url_evidence: Ministry of Culture 文化統計網 with central and local cultural expenditure budget statistics, research reports and cultural statistics e-books.
reports._cadence_evidence: stat.moc.gov.tw is the Ministry of Culture statistics portal, showing rolling data updates (2026 Q1 and May 2026 figures) and 歷年文化統計資料查詢 rather than a dated publication series with a stated frequency.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7) and applied 2026-08-19: a nominal releases_per_year so that absence keeps meaning 'one-off instrument' only - 250 encodes business-day updating (the live corpus's daily-FX convention), 365 genuinely all-days monitoring. It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

reports.title: Semiconductor / IC industry production and structure statistics
reports.description: Official and industry-linked statistics on IC design, wafer foundry, IDM and packaging/testing output, global market shares, and contribution to industrial production and exports. Taiwan holds global #1 positions in pure-play foundry and OSAT and a very high share of advanced-node capacity.
reports._cadence_original: periodic / annual + high-frequency industrial production detail
reports._notes: Highest-uniqueness industrial node for Taiwan. Foundry market share ~60 %+ and advanced packaging leadership create a structural dependency that pulls industrial production, trade, BOP goods, and investment statistics into a tight cluster. Essential for force-layout cluster formation around technology/manufacturing.
_referenced_by: Industrial Production Index (electronics and electronic parts components dominate recent growth)
Customs trade statistics (semiconductor and ICT export shares)
National accounts industry detail and export-led growth analysis
CBC and external-sector commentary on technology export performance
reports._cadence_evidence: MOEA Department of Statistics publishes 工業生產統計 on the 25th and 外銷訂單 on the 20th of each month ('當月最新調查統計發布: 25日 工業生產, 20日 外銷訂單'), with dated monthly releases in July 2026.

reports.title: Vital Statistics — births, total fertility rate, crude birth rate
reports.description: Annual and monthly vital statistics on live births, crude birth rate and total fertility rate. Taiwan has recorded one of the world’s lowest fertility rates (recent crude birth rate ~4.6 per 1,000; TFR well below replacement and recently the lowest globally in some readings).
reports._notes: Demographic uniqueness parallel to (and in some metrics more extreme than) Korea. Creates strong edges into population, ageing, labour supply and social-policy nodes.
_referenced_by: Super-aged society indicators and long-term care planning
reports._cadence_evidence: MOI 統計主題專區 lists 內政統計月報 with frequency '每月'; the 月報 page shows monthly editions (latest 115年5月內政統計月報). Births/TFR are carried in that monthly report (DGBAS SDDS also gives Population periodicity 'Monthly').

reports.title: Super-aged society indicators (65+ share ≥ 20 %)
reports.description: Official tracking of the share of population aged 65 and over. Taiwan crossed the 20 % threshold and is formally a super-aged society under UN criteria. Accompanied by rising old-age dependency and declining youth share.
reports._notes: High-authority demographic status node. Links tightly to fertility, population projections and social-protection series — the same cluster pattern that strengthens Japan and Korea force structures.
reports._cadence_evidence: Age-structure indicators come from MOI household-registration statistics, published in 內政統計月報 ('每月' per the MOI 統計主題專區 listing); DGBAS SDDS Population metadata likewise states Periodicity 'Monthly', Timeliness '10 days'.

reports.title: Population Projections
reports.description: Official long-term population projections under alternative fertility, mortality and migration scenarios. Show continued population decline and rapid rise in old-age dependency under current ultra-low fertility.
reports._notes: Forward-looking demographic node that inherits strong edges from vital statistics and super-aged indicators.
_referenced_by: Education, labour-supply and pension planning documents
reports._cadence_evidence: NDC population projection system (pop-proj.ndc.gov.tw) states '本會每2年針對最新出生、死亡及遷徙狀況，更新未來長期人口推估趨勢'; latest edition released 17 October 2024, next update August 2026.

reports.title: Export Orders statistics
reports.description: Monthly statistics on export orders received by Taiwanese firms, broken down by product and destination. Leading indicator for industrial production and merchandise exports, especially in electronics.
reports._notes: High-frequency leading indicator tightly coupled to the semiconductor/electronics cycle. Strengthens short-term activity edges.
_referenced_by: Customs export statistics and short-term forecasting

reports.title: Science Park / Hsinchu and related high-tech cluster statistics
reports.region: Taiwan (Hsinchu, Southern, Central Science Parks etc.)
reports.description: Statistics on employment, sales, investment and firm counts in Taiwan’s major science parks — the geographic concentration points of the semiconductor and high-tech industries.
reports._notes: Spatial uniqueness node. Hsinchu and the other science parks are the physical loci of Taiwan’s foundry and design strength; they create regional-contrast and cluster edges.
_referenced_by: Industrial production and export performance analysis
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved and read. National Science and Technology Council statistical release 'Kexue yuanqu 2025 nian yingshou 5.8 zhao yuan, chengzhang 21.83%', dated 11 March 2026, on the NSTC's own site. It reports the three science parks' combined 2025 revenue of NT$5.80 trillion (+21.83%) with the park-level breakdown: Hsinchu NT$1.70tn (+12.25%), Central NT$1.13tn (+9.29%), Southern NT$2.97tn (+34.26%), plus a breakdown across the six park industry sectors (semiconductors, optoelectronics, computers, precision machinery, biotech, communications). NOTE: it covers sales, not employment/investment/firm counts. The full 'yuanqu tongji ziliaoku' (Science Park Statistics Database) is at https://wsts.nstc.gov.tw/stsweb/sciencepark/SciencePark.aspx?language=C - I located that exact URL from the NSTC page https://www.nstc.gov.tw/spu/ch/list/9b80b58f-56cc-4280-8ef1-a91f13fc4b1c, but the wsts/stsweb host still fails TLS (SSLV3_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE), so it is not recorded.
reports._url_route: parent ministry (nstc.gov.tw) instead of the TLS-broken stsweb/wsts subdomain
reports._cadence_evidence: NSTC publishes a once-a-year science-park results release: '科學園區2025年營收5.8兆元，成長21.83%' (更新日期 2026/03/11) and the matching '科學園區2024年營收約4.76兆元，成長20.73%' — one full-year announcement per year.

reports.title: Monetary Aggregates (M1B, M2) and Financial Conditions
reports.publisher: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
reports.description: Monthly statistics on monetary aggregates (M1B, M2), loans and investments of financial institutions, and related financial-conditions indicators. Core high-frequency monetary data released by the CBC.
reports._notes: Parallel to Korea’s M1/M2/Lf series and Japan’s monetary aggregates. Tight edges into CBC institutional node, interest-rate policy and credit conditions.

reports.title: Foreign Exchange Reserves
reports.publisher: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
reports.description: Monthly official foreign-exchange reserve holdings. Taiwan maintains one of the world’s largest reserve stocks relative to GDP, reflecting persistent current-account surpluses.
reports._notes: High-authority external-strength node. Creates strong edges from the large BOP current-account surplus into reserve accumulation.
_referenced_by: Balance of Payments and international investment position
CBC annual reports and financial-conditions releases

reports.title: Long-Term Care services and statistics (Long-Term Care Services Act framework)
reports.description: Statistics on long-term care service units (institutional, home-based, community-based), utilisation, and the policy framework established under the Long-Term Care Services Act. Number of registered units has risen sharply as Taiwan entered super-aged status.
reports._notes: Social-response node to the demographic extremes already captured. Parallel to Japan’s LTCI and Korea’s Long-Term Care Insurance series. Strengthens the ageing–care cluster.
_referenced_by: Super-aged society indicators and population projections
Ageing-society white papers and policy evaluations
reports._cadence_evidence: MOHW 高齡及長期照顧統計專區 (dep.mohw.gov.tw/dos/cp-5223-62358-113.html) aggregates tables from several agencies and shows only 最後更新日期 115-08-17 / 更新時間 115-03-30; it states no publication frequency.

reports.title: Energy Statistics Handbook / Energy balance and electricity generation mix
reports.publisher: Energy Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs
reports.description: Annual and periodic energy statistics covering primary energy supply, transformation, final consumption, and detailed electricity generation by source (coal, gas, nuclear, renewables). Nuclear share has fallen to low single digits in recent years.
reports._notes: Critical contrast node. Unlike Korea’s ~32 % nuclear share, Taiwan’s nuclear contribution has declined sharply; gas and renewables have risen. Creates a distinctive energy-cluster signature relative to both Japan and Korea.
_referenced_by: Industrial production and energy-intensive manufacturing analysis
reports._cadence_evidence: 能源統計手冊 sits under the Energy Administration's 年度刊物 (annual publications) section of the 能源統計專區 (ea01.moeaea.gov.tw/a0303/02/publication/handbook/), with one edition per year (e.g. 112年能源統計手冊).

reports.title: Nuclear power status and phase-out / life-extension policy statistics
reports.description: Statistics and policy tracking of Taiwan’s nuclear fleet capacity, generation share, and the political/regulatory trajectory of phase-out versus possible life-extension or restart debates.
reports._notes: Uniqueness node. The near-phase-out trajectory (nuclear share now ~1–4 %) is a defining energy-policy feature and produces clear edges into the broader energy and industrial-cost clusters.
_referenced_by: Energy Statistics Handbook and electricity generation mix
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved and read. 'Fadian gaikuang' (Electricity Generation Overview) in the Energy Statistics section of the MOEA Energy Administration's site. It gives the nuclear trajectory directly: nuclear's share of generation fell from 12.0% in 2016 to 1.1% in 2025, within a 2025 mix of coal 35.3%, natural gas 47.7%, nuclear 1.1%, renewables 13.3%, on total generation rising from 264.1 to 289.7 billion kWh. The companion capacity page is https://www.moeaea.gov.tw/ECW/populace/content/Content.aspx?menu_id=14438. NOTE: this covers fleet output/share; the regulator's own plant pages remain blocked - nusc.gov.tw returns 403 to WebFetch both at the root and at the deep 'nuclear plant basic data' page.
reports._url_route: parent ministry - MOEA Energy Administration (moeaea.gov.tw) instead of the 403-blocked nusc.gov.tw
reports._cadence_evidence: moeaea Content.aspx?menu_id=14437 is a standing information page on generation mix (建檔 2021-07-08, 更新 115-08-17) showing nuclear share falling 12.0% (2016) to 1.1% (2025); no publication cycle is stated.

reports.title: Family Income and Expenditure Survey / Household income statistics
reports.description: Periodic survey of household income, expenditure, savings and distribution. Source for inequality, consumption and living-standards analysis.
reports._notes: Core household survey parallel to Japan and Korea counterparts. Strengthens income–distribution and living-conditions edges.
reports._cadence_evidence: The Family Income and Expenditure Survey report system is indexed one report per year (ws.dgbas.gov.tw/win/fies/a11.asp?year=110), and DGBAS issues one 家庭收支調查 result set per survey year — an annual survey and annual report.

reports.title: Labour productivity and unit labour cost statistics
reports.description: Statistics on labour productivity and unit labour costs, particularly for the industrial and manufacturing sectors. Closely watched given the high productivity growth in electronics and semiconductors.
reports._notes: Links the semiconductor/industrial cluster to labour and cost competitiveness. Useful for force-layout connections between real-activity and cost nodes.
reports._cadence_evidence: Productivity and unit-labour-cost figures come from DGBAS 薪資與生產力統計; SDDS metadata for Labor market: Wages/Earnings states Periodicity 'Monthly', Timeliness '40 days after the end of reference month'.

reports.title: Construction and housing statistics
reports.description: Statistics on construction activity, building permits, housing stock and related real-estate indicators.
reports._notes: Supporting structural node that feeds investment and regional clusters.
reports._cadence_evidence: No release-frequency statement or countable edition list for construction/housing statistics could be found on the DGBAS pages; the MOI 住宅資訊統計彙報 appears quarterly in third-party listings but the official page states no cadence.

reports.title: Education statistics (enrolment, schools, attainment)
reports.description: Statistics on schools, student enrolment, educational attainment and related human-capital indicators. Interacts with demographic decline (shrinking school-age cohorts) and high-tech labour demand.
reports._notes: Human-capital node that bridges demographic decline and the high-tech industrial cluster.
reports._cadence_evidence: MOE Department of Statistics (depart.moe.edu.tw/ED4500) issues its statistics compilation once per school/fiscal year — 教育統計 / 'Education in Taiwan (2026-2027)' and 教育統計指標 are annual, alongside dated bulletin-board releases per 學年.

reports.title: Financial Stability Report / banking and systemic-risk statistics
reports.publisher: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) / Financial Supervisory Commission
reports.description: Periodic Financial Stability Report and underlying statistics on bank soundness, household and corporate credit, real-estate exposure and systemic-risk indicators.
reports._notes: Deepens the financial cluster. Parallel to Korea’s Financial Stability Report node.
reports._cadence_evidence: CBC publications list marks 金融穩定報告 as '年刊' (annual); editions confirm one per year every May — 第17期 112年5月, 第18期 113年5月, 第19期 114年5月.

reports.title: National R&D Expenditure and Personnel Statistics
reports.description: Annual statistics on total R&D expenditure (recently surpassed NT$1 trillion / ~4.1 % of GDP), breakdown by performing and funding sector, and R&D personnel. Private-sector and large-enterprise dominance is pronounced; science-park firms account for a rising share of business R&D.
reports._notes: High-authority uniqueness node. R&D intensity ~4.1 % of GDP is among the world’s highest and is heavily concentrated in the same large electronics/semiconductor firms that dominate industrial production and exports. Creates dense edges into the core technology cluster.

reports.title: National Greenhouse Gas Inventory Report
reports.publisher: Ministry of Environment / Climate Change Administration
reports.description: Annual national GHG inventory compiled voluntarily in line with UNFCCC / Paris Agreement transparency standards (even though Taiwan is not a formal party). Reports total and sectoral emissions, carbon sinks and net emissions from 1990 onward.
reports._notes: Core environmental statistics node. Links energy (especially the low-nuclear, high-gas/renewables mix) to climate-policy and industrial-emission edges.
_referenced_by: Energy Statistics Handbook and generation-mix data
Climate Change Response Act implementation documents

reports.title: Climate Change Response Act
reports.description: Primary domestic climate legislation that mandates the national GHG inventory, sets the legal basis for mitigation and adaptation policy, and structures institutional responsibilities.
reports._notes: Foundational recurring-citation legal node for the environmental cluster, parallel to the Statistics Act for the statistical system.
_referenced_by: Subsequent climate-policy white papers and regulations
reports._url_evidence: Ministry of Environment law system full text of 氣候變遷因應法 — 7 chapters, 63 articles, enacted 2015, amended 15 February 2023, net-zero and carbon fee provisions.

reports.title: Input-Output Tables / Inter-industry relations
reports.description: Periodic detailed input-output tables showing inter-industry transactions, value added and final demand. Critical for tracing the semiconductor and electronics supply chains within the domestic economy.
reports._notes: Structural backbone node. Parallel to Japan and Korea I-O tables; especially valuable for mapping the dense domestic linkages around electronics.
reports._cadence_evidence: DGBAS compiles 產業關聯表 on benchmark years five years apart — 編製報告 exist for 95年 and 100年 (and the series continues 105年/110年), i.e. one table every five years.

reports.title: SME / Small and Medium Enterprise statistics
reports.publisher: Ministry of Economic Affairs / Small and Medium Enterprise Administration
reports.description: Statistics on the number, employment, sales and financial conditions of SMEs, which still account for the large majority of enterprises and a substantial share of employment even while large electronics firms dominate R&D and exports.
reports._notes: Balances the large-firm / semiconductor picture. Useful for dual-economy edges.
reports._cadence_evidence: 中小企業白皮書 listing (sme.gov.tw/list-tw-2345) shows one edition per year without gaps: 2025, 2024, 2023, 2022, 2021, 2020, 2019, 2018, 2017, 2016, 2015, 2014, 2013, 2012, 2011.

reports.title: Tourism statistics (inbound / outbound)
reports.publisher: Tourism Administration / Ministry of Transportation and Communications
reports.description: Statistics on visitor arrivals, outbound travel, tourism receipts and related services-trade indicators.
reports._notes: Supporting services and external node; sensitive to cross-strait and regional travel conditions.
_referenced_by: Services trade in the Balance of Payments
reports._cadence_evidence: Tourism Administration publishes 觀光統計月報 (admin.taiwan.net.tw/businessinfo/FilePage?a=14642), whose tables were last updated 115-08-10; the 觀光統計資料庫 offers both 月表 (monthly) and 年表 (annual) reporting, with the monthly report as the regular release.

reports.title: Health and medical statistics (beyond long-term care)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Health and Welfare / National Health Insurance Administration
reports.description: Statistics on health status, medical utilisation, National Health Insurance expenditure and related system indicators.
reports._notes: Complements the long-term care node and strengthens the health–ageing cluster.
reports._cadence_evidence: MOHW Department of Statistics publishes 醫事機構服務量統計年報 once a year: 114年 (2025-07-31), 113年 (2024-07-29), 112年 (2023-07-30) — annual editions released each July.

reports.title: Wage and salary statistics / Earnings survey
reports.description: Statistics on earnings by industry, occupation, firm size and other characteristics. Source for wage-gap and labour-cost analysis.
reports._notes: Links labour, cost and household-income clusters.
_referenced_by: Labour productivity and unit labour cost series
reports._cadence_evidence: DGBAS SDDS metadata, Labor market: Wages/Earnings — Periodicity: 'Monthly'; Timeliness: '40 days after the end of reference month' (受僱員工薪資調查).

reports.title: Cross-Strait Economic Relations Statistics (Mainland Affairs Council)
reports.description: Regular official compilation of cross-strait trade, investment, and people-to-people exchange statistics. Draws on Customs, Investment Commission and immigration/tourism sources to present a coherent picture of economic interaction across the Taiwan Strait.
reports._notes: Unique institutional product. Parallel in spirit to Korea’s official North Korea statistical indicators. Creates strong, explicit edges between the ECFA node, China-partner trade, investment flows and people-exchange series.
reports._cadence_evidence: MAC 經貿交流統計 lists 兩岸經濟統計月報 and 兩岸經濟交流統計速報; the 月報 archive runs consecutively numbered monthly issues (No.399 = 115年07月, 共279筆).

reports.title: Agriculture, forestry and fishery statistics
reports.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture / Fisheries Agency / DGBAS
reports.description: Statistics on agricultural production value, farm households, fishery production and related rural indicators. Completes the primary-sector coverage alongside manufacturing and services.
reports._notes: Sectoral completion node. Also feeds the regional-contrast edges (eastern and agricultural counties are ageing faster and less dense).
_referenced_by: Regional contrast (agricultural counties vs special municipalities)
reports._cadence_evidence: 農業部統計處 統計書刊 lists 農業統計年報 as a 年報 with one edition per year, each published in early July: 114年(115/07/01), 113年(114/07/03), 112年(113/07/03) … back to 105年(106/07/03).

reports.title: Banking sector statistics (loans, deposits, soundness)
reports.publisher: Financial Supervisory Commission / Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
reports.description: Statistics on the banking system — outstanding loans and deposits, asset quality, capital adequacy and related soundness indicators. Complements the CBC monetary aggregates and Financial Stability Report.
reports._notes: Deepens the financial cluster. Strong edges into monetary, stability and real-estate/credit nodes.
_referenced_by: CBC Financial Conditions and monetary aggregates
reports._cadence_evidence: Banking Bureau 金融統計 page shows monthly series released each month — 金融統計指標 (115年6月, released 2026-08-17), 金融業務統計輯要 (115年6月, 2026-08-17) — alongside quarterly 基本金融資料 (115年第2季).

reports.title: Insurance sector statistics (life and non-life)
reports.description: Regular indicators of the insurance industry — premiums, assets, claims, solvency and related metrics for life and non-life insurers. Taiwan’s life-insurance sector is large relative to GDP.
reports._notes: Completes the major financial-institution triad (banks, insurers, securities). Relevant to household balance-sheets and ageing-society financing.
_referenced_by: Financial Stability Report and FSC overview statistics
reports._cadence_evidence: Insurance Bureau publishes 保險市場重要指標 monthly: 115年4月 (released 2026-06-30), 115年3月 (2026-05-31), 115年2月 (2026-04-30), 115年1月 (2026-03-31) — one edition per reference month across 8 pages of archive.

reports.title: Outbound and inbound investment statistics (Investment Commission)
reports.publisher: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
reports.description: Official statistics on approved outbound investment (including the large historical stock directed to Mainland China) and inbound FDI. Key source for cross-strait and global investment patterns.
reports._notes: Tightens the investment and cross-strait clusters. Historical Mainland China share of outbound investment remains large even as diversification proceeds.
reports._cadence_evidence: 經濟部投資審議司 issues 核准僑外投資、陸資來臺投資、國外投資、對中國大陸投資統計月報/速報 once per month, with releases titled by reference month (e.g. 115年6月核准…統計情形).

reports.title: Securities and capital-market statistics
reports.description: Statistics on equity-market capitalisation, trading activity, listed-company performance and related capital-market indicators. Semiconductor and electronics firms dominate market capitalisation and trading.
reports._notes: Links the high-tech industrial cluster to capital-market outcomes and household wealth.
reports._cadence_evidence: SFB 證券暨期貨市場重要指標 is published one edition per reference month (e.g. 101年12月份, 101年11月份, 101年10月份 …), each posted about 15–19 days after month end.

reports.title: Crime and justice statistics
reports.description: Official statistics on reported crime, clearance rates, prosecution and judicial caseloads.
reports._notes: Supporting social-structure node.
reports._url_evidence: Ministry of Justice Crime Prevention Research Center series page for 我國犯罪狀況及其分析, listing 46 annual editions through 2024.
reports._cadence_evidence: MOJ 犯罪防治研究中心 publication list shows one crime-analysis report per year — 2024, 2023, 2022, 2021, 2020, 2019 and continuing back over decades, one edition per calendar year.

reports.title: Broader environmental statistics (air, water, waste, protected areas)
reports.description: Statistics on air and water quality, waste generation and treatment, protected areas and related environmental indicators that complement the GHG inventory.
reports._notes: Expands the environmental cluster beyond GHG.
_referenced_by: National GHG Inventory and Climate Change Response Act
reports._cadence_evidence: MOENV's environmental-statistics section points to the 環境統計查詢網(ESDQ) query system; neither moenv.gov.tw nor the statistics site states a publication frequency or lists dated yearbook editions.

reports.title: Internal migration and household registration statistics
reports.publisher: Ministry of the Interior / Department of Household Registration
reports.description: Statistics on internal migration flows, household registration changes and related population-mobility indicators that underpin regional concentration patterns.
reports._notes: Feeds the spatial-concentration edges.
reports._cadence_evidence: Household-registration population statistics are released monthly: DGBAS SDDS Population metadata states Periodicity 'Monthly', Timeliness '10 days', and MOI lists 內政統計月報 as '每月'.

reports.title: External debt statistics
reports.publisher: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
reports.description: Statistics on external debt by sector and maturity, complementing the large FX-reserve stock and persistent current-account surplus.
reports._notes: Completes the external-vulnerability picture alongside reserves and BOP.
_referenced_by: Balance of Payments and international investment position
reports._cadence_evidence: DGBAS/CBC SDDS metadata for External debt states Periodicity 'Quarterly' and 'The preliminary quarterly external debt data are disseminated 50 days after the end of the reference quarter… the press release dates usually fall on the 20th of Feb., May, Aug. and Nov.'

reports.title: Digital / ICT industry and computer & information services statistics
reports.description: Statistics on computer programming, information services, digital-industry turnover and related ICT service activity. Complements the semiconductor hardware cluster with the software, systems-integration and digital-transformation layer.
reports._notes: Extends the technology cluster from hardware (foundry/OSAT) into software, cloud, AI-related services and digital transformation. Strengthens edges between industrial production, R&D and services trade.
_referenced_by: R&D expenditure (business-sector software and systems components)
National accounts services detail and export of ICT services
reports._cadence_evidence: moda 數位產業署 產業統計專區 publishes 電腦及資訊服務業營業額統計 每季 — 114年第1季, 第2季, 第3季, 第4季 (Q4 released 2026-02-26), i.e. four releases per year.

reports.title: Earnings structure / salary statistics (share below average, industry differentials)
reports.description: Detailed earnings statistics showing average regular earnings, the share of employees below the mean (recently >70 %), and industry differentials. Electronics and financial services sit well above the mean; education, accommodation/food and other services sit well below.
reports._notes: Deepens the dual-structure labour picture. High semiconductor/electronics earnings versus lower-service and traditional-industry earnings create clear edges into inequality and household-income nodes.
_referenced_by: Labour productivity and unit labour cost
Semiconductor and high-tech wage premium analysis
reports._cadence_evidence: DGBAS SDDS Labor market: Wages/Earnings — Periodicity: 'Monthly', Timeliness: '40 days after the end of reference month'; the monthly 薪資及生產力統計 news release carries the earnings-distribution indicators.

reports.title: Minimum wage / basic wage framework and adjustments
reports.description: Statutory minimum (basic) wage level and the periodic adjustment process. Affects a large number of workers and feeds into labour-insurance and pension contribution bases.
reports._notes: Policy anchor for the lower end of the wage distribution. Recurring citation in labour and social-policy documents.
_referenced_by: Labour insurance and pension contribution tables
reports._cadence_evidence: MOL 基本工資之制訂與調整經過 lists adjustments taking effect on 1 January of consecutive years (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 …), and notes that from 114年1月1日 基本工資 was replaced by 最低工資 under the new act — one review/adjustment per year.

reports.title: Protected areas / biodiversity conservation statistics
reports.publisher: Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency / Ministry of Agriculture / Ministry of Environment
reports.description: Statistics on national parks, nature reserves, wildlife protected areas and overall protected-area coverage (land and marine). Taiwan has designated a substantial share of its territory under various protection categories.
reports._notes: Expands the environmental cluster beyond climate/GHG into biodiversity and spatial conservation. Useful for regional and land-use edges.
reports._cadence_evidence: Forestry Agency conservation site (redirected to forest.gov.tw/Ecological) lists 年報 and a 雙月刊 among publications and a 生態調查資料庫, but gives no dated protected-area statistical editions and no explicit frequency.

reports.title: Foreign / migrant worker statistics
reports.publisher: Ministry of Labor / National Immigration Agency
reports.description: Statistics on the stock and characteristics of foreign industrial and care workers. Material to labour-supply analysis under ultra-low fertility and rapid ageing.
reports._notes: Demographic–labour bridge node. Parallel to Korea’s foreign-residents cluster and Japan’s foreign-worker statistics. Strengthens edges between ageing, care and labour supply.
reports._cadence_evidence: MOL labour statistics query system (statdb.mol.gov.tw) labels the series '(每月)' and the ministry's 統計專刊 includes 勞動統計月報; migrant-worker headcounts are updated monthly.

reports.title: Labor Insurance and Labor Pension statistics
reports.publisher: Bureau of Labor Insurance / Ministry of Labor
reports.description: Statistics on Labor Insurance coverage, benefits, and the Labor Pension system (including contribution bases linked to the minimum wage). Central pillars of the social-insurance response to ageing.
reports._notes: Social-insurance core that links wages, ageing and fiscal sustainability.
reports._cadence_evidence: Bureau of Labor Insurance statistics section states 統計月報 released '每月' (bli.gov.tw/0013086.html) and 統計年報 '每年' (0013087.html), with a 發布時間表 at 0013165.html.

reports.title: National Health Insurance statistics
reports.description: Statistics on NHI coverage, expenditure, utilisation and financial status. Universal system that interacts closely with ageing and long-term care demand.
reports._notes: Complements the broader health and long-term care nodes; central to the social-protection cluster.
reports._cadence_evidence: NHI 健保統計專區 / 重要統計資料 pages show datasets refreshed on mixed, unstated schedules (most items stamped 115.7.22; 疾病資訊 annually 114.11.19; others 114.08.28) with no declared publication frequency.

reports.title: Science and technology policy white papers / National Science and Technology Council strategic documents
reports.description: Periodic strategic documents and white papers that set R&D, semiconductor, AI and digital-economy priorities. Recurringly cited in budget, industrial and talent-policy analysis.
reports._notes: Strategic recurring-citation node that sits above the R&D and semiconductor statistical series.
reports._cadence_evidence: NSTC 出版品 list (13 items) shows 科學技術統計要覽 among the publications but states no frequency, and neither 科學技術白皮書 nor 國家科學技術發展計畫 appears with dated editions on the page.

reports.title: Detailed price statistics (CPI components, housing-related prices)
reports.description: More granular CPI component series and housing-related price indicators that complement the headline CPI and PPI.
reports._notes: Deepens the price cluster and links it more tightly to housing and living-cost edges.

reports.title: Business demography / establishment and enterprise statistics
reports.description: Statistics on the number, entry, exit and survival of establishments and enterprises by size and industry. Complements SME and large-enterprise structural views.
reports._notes: Structural foundation for firm-size dualism edges.
_referenced_by: Industrial production and employment by firm size
reports._cadence_evidence: Enterprise/establishment counts come from the 工業及服務業普查, taken every five years — the standing census plans on the statute site are 一百十五年(2026) and the preceding 110年(2021) census, a five-year interval.

reports.title: Electronic Components Industry — Production, Sales and Inventory statistics
reports.publisher: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Statistics
reports.description: Detailed monthly/annual statistics on production, sales and inventory value of the electronic components industry (the core statistical category that contains semiconductors and related devices). This series is the primary high-frequency official measure of semiconductor-related manufacturing activity.
reports._notes: Highest-frequency official semiconductor-proxy series. Recent double-digit growth driven by advanced-process and AI-related demand makes this a central pulse node for the entire technology cluster.
_referenced_by: Headline Industrial Production Index (electronics components dominate recent growth)
Export orders and customs export statistics for electronics

reports.title: Computers, Electronic & Optical Products Industry production statistics
reports.publisher: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Statistics
reports.description: Production statistics for computers, electronic products and optical products — the downstream and equipment-related layer that has been strongly boosted by AI servers, semiconductor equipment and high-performance computing demand.
reports._notes: Complements the components series. AI-server and semiconductor-equipment demand has produced extreme year-on-year growth rates, creating tight edges into the components and export-order nodes.

reports.title: Science Parks aggregate revenue, employment and firm statistics (Hsinchu, Central, Southern)
reports.publisher: National Science and Technology Council / Science Park Administrations
reports.description: Official statistics on the three major science parks: aggregate revenue (recently record levels driven by the integrated-circuit sector), number of firms, employment, and industry composition. IC sector accounts for the large majority of park revenue.
reports._notes: Geographic and organisational heart of the semiconductor cluster. Revenue now measured in trillions of NT$; IC sector dominance creates a clear high-authority sub-graph.
_referenced_by: Regional contrast and Taipei–Hsinchu axis nodes
reports._cadence_evidence: NSTC issues one aggregate science-park results release per year: '科學園區2025年營收5.8兆元，成長21.83%' (2026/03/11) and '科學園區2024年營收約4.76兆元，成長20.73%'.

reports.title: Hsinchu Science Park detailed statistics
reports.description: Detailed statistics for the original and still-core Hsinchu Science Park — firm counts, employment, sales by industry (especially IC), and investment. Remains the densest single locus of advanced semiconductor activity.
reports._notes: Core geographic node of the foundry and design ecosystem. Strengthens the Taipei–Hsinchu axis already flagged in earlier batches.
_referenced_by: Northern Taiwan regional and labour statistics
reports._url_evidence: Hsinchu Science Park Bureau 歷年統計資訊: firm counts and sales, employment by education level, R&D expenditure and patents by industry.
reports._cadence_evidence: SIPA 統計資訊/出版品 page lists 月報 (monthly statistics report) and 預算、決算書及會計月報 alongside 歷年統計資訊 — the park's statistics are issued as a monthly report.

reports.title: Southern Taiwan Science Park statistics and semiconductor expansion
reports.publisher: Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau / NSTC
reports.description: Statistics for the Southern Taiwan Science Park, which has recorded the fastest recent growth and is the principal locus of the southward expansion of the semiconductor ‘S-corridor’.
reports._notes: Captures the spatial expansion of the semiconductor cluster beyond the traditional Hsinchu core — important for regional and industrial-policy edges.
_referenced_by: Regional contrast (southward shift of high-tech activity)
reports._url_evidence: Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau 現況統計 page: revenue, import/export, employment, leasing and investment statistics.
reports._cadence_evidence: STSP statistics page lists categories (營業額, 進出口, 從業員工, 租賃, 來賓, 投資統計) with no dated releases and no stated periodicity; figures are served through linked query portals.

reports.title: Act for Industrial Innovation (產業創新條例) — including ‘Taiwan Chip Act’ provisions (Art. 10-2 etc.)
reports.publisher: Republic of China (Taiwan) / Ministry of Economic Affairs
reports.description: Core industrial-policy statute that provides the legal basis for R&D and advanced-process equipment tax incentives (the so-called Taiwan Chip Act provisions), smart-machinery and AI investment incentives, and related industrial-innovation measures. Continuously cited in semiconductor investment and tax-policy analysis.
reports._notes: Highest-value recurring-citation policy node for the semiconductor cluster. The Art. 10-2 incentives (high R&D intensity + advanced-equipment thresholds) are explicitly designed around the foundry and advanced-packaging model.
_referenced_by: Semiconductor and R&D investment decisions and announcements
MOEA industrial-policy and tax-incentive utilisation reports
reports._url_evidence: MOEA law system full text of 產業創新條例, including Article 10-2 investment tax-credit provisions for smart machinery, 5G, cybersecurity and AI.

reports.title: Semiconductor and electronic-components trade statistics (exports / imports by detailed HS)
reports.description: Detailed customs trade statistics for electronic components, integrated circuits, semiconductor devices and related products. Semiconductor-related items dominate Taiwan’s export structure and generate large trade surpluses.
reports._notes: Trade-side counterpart to the production series. Creates direct edges from the factory floor into the external-surplus and partner-concentration nodes.
_referenced_by: Headline trade statistics and BOP goods account

reports.title: Semiconductor / electronics employment and wage statistics
reports.publisher: DGBAS / Ministry of Labor / Science Park Administrations
reports.description: Employment counts and earnings levels in electronic components, computers/optical products and science-park IC firms. These segments sit well above average earnings and account for a disproportionate share of high-skill employment.
reports._notes: Labour-side of the dual structure. High electronics earnings versus the rest of the economy generate clear inequality and household-income edges.
_referenced_by: Labour productivity and unit labour cost (manufacturing)
reports._url_evidence: DGBAS 薪資及生產力統計 section (earnings and productivity statistics), the official series carrying employment and earnings by manufacturing industry.
reports._cadence_evidence: stat.gov.tw n=2712 is the 薪資及生產力統計 area; DGBAS SDDS metadata for Labor market: Wages/Earnings gives Periodicity 'Monthly' (40 days after reference month), and employment from the Manpower Survey is likewise 'Monthly' (35 days).

reports.title: United States–Taiwan Initiative on 21st-Century Trade (first agreement)
reports.description: First agreement under the Initiative (signed 2023, entered into force December 2024) covering anti-corruption, good regulatory practices, customs and trade facilitation, services domestic regulation, and SMEs. Foundation layer on which the later Agreement on Reciprocal Trade builds.
reports._notes: Foundational US–Taiwan trade instrument of the 2020s. Provides the regulatory and facilitation base that the deeper ART then expands into market access and economic-security commitments.
_referenced_by: Customs and trade-facilitation statistics and reform documents
TIFA Council and subsequent negotiation records

reports.title: AIT–TECRO Memorandum of Understanding on industrial parks, semiconductor investment and supply-chain cooperation (Jan 2026)
reports.description: MOU under which Taiwan commits to facilitate large-scale investment by Taiwanese firms into US semiconductor, AI, energy and related industrial parks/clusters, with financial support from the Taiwan side; US side provides preferential treatment considerations in Section 232 and related investigations. Explicitly links semiconductor capacity expansion in the United States to the bilateral economic-security partnership.
reports._notes: Direct bridge between the semiconductor manufacturing cluster and the sovereignty-protecting economic architecture. Large announced investment figures (hundreds of billions) make this a high-mass edge into both the chip and the US–Taiwan nodes.
_referenced_by: US–Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade fact sheets
Science-park and advanced-capacity statistics (outbound investment side)
reports._url_evidence: USTR fact sheet describing the AIT–TECRO MOU signed 15 January 2026 on industrial parks/clusters, Taiwanese semiconductor, EMS and energy investment in the US, and Section 232 preferential treatment.

reports.title: AI-related demand impact on Taiwan semiconductor production and export statistics
reports.publisher: Ministry of Economic Affairs / DGBAS / industry sources cited officially
reports.description: Statistical and official commentary linking the surge in AI server, high-performance computing and advanced-packaging demand to the record growth rates in electronic-components and computers/optical production indices, science-park IC revenue, and related export orders.
reports._cadence_original: continuous (via monthly industrial and trade releases)
reports._notes: Demand-side narrative node that explains the extreme recent growth rates. Essential for understanding why the semiconductor cluster currently carries such high centrality and authority in the graph.
_referenced_by: Electronic Components and Computers/Optical production series
Export orders and semiconductor trade statistics
reports._cadence_evidence: The underlying MOEA releases are monthly on a fixed calendar: '25日 工業生產, 20日 外銷訂單', with dated releases 2026-07-23 (工業生產) and 2026-07-21 (外銷訂單).

reports.title: Export-control and technology-security alignment with the United States
reports.description: Policy and statistical traces of Taiwan’s alignment with US-led export-control regimes on advanced semiconductors and related technologies. Appears in ART security architecture language and in domestic implementation measures.
reports._notes: Security-layer node that links the commercial semiconductor cluster to the sovereignty-protecting economic architecture.
_referenced_by: US–Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade (security provisions)
reports._url_evidence: International Trade Administration 高科技貨品管理 section covering strategic high-tech (dual-use) commodity export controls and related announcements.
reports._cadence_evidence: ITA 戰略性高科技貨品 page (trade.gov.tw nodeID=4353) carries regulatory announcements filtered by date range with a 歷史區 archive; it states no publication frequency and the postings are issued as regulatory needs arise.

reports.title: National Defense Budget (Ministry of National Defense)
reports.description: Annual and special defence budget figures, including the headline MND allocation and the broader NATO-standard measure that incorporates veterans’ payments and coast-guard expenditure. Recent budgets have been set with a target of at least 3 % of GDP; the 2026 figure reaches approximately 3.32 % under the broader measure, with large year-on-year increases and dedicated special budgets for air and sea combat capability and asymmetric forces.
reports._notes: Core fiscal-security node. Rising share of GDP and the creation of multi-year special budgets for sea/air and asymmetric capabilities create direct edges into the broader public-finance and economic-resilience clusters.
_referenced_by: Fiscal and national-accounts analysis of government expenditure
reports._cadence_evidence: MND 預算及決算書 section is organised one budget book per fiscal year (110至114年國防部所屬預算書表), matching the annual 中央政府總預算 cycle (DGBAS publishes 115年度中央政府總預算案編列情形 once per year).

reports.title: National Defense Report (國防報告書)
reports.description: Periodic official report (most recently the 2025 edition) that sets out the threat assessment, force-structure priorities, readiness posture and policy direction of the ROC Armed Forces. Continuously cited in subsequent budget, procurement and strategic documents.
reports._notes: Highest-level recurring-citation defence policy node. Functions as the strategic counterpart to the purely statistical budget series.
_referenced_by: Defence budget justifications and special-budget statutes
reports._cadence_evidence: MND 歷年國防報告書專區 shows editions two years apart in the recent series — 110年 (2021), 112年 (2023), 114年 (2025) — i.e. one report every two years.

reports.title: Indigenous naval shipbuilding statistics and programmes (Tuo Chiang-class corvettes, Indigenous Defense Submarine, light frigates)
reports.description: Official and programme-level statistics and progress reporting on domestically built naval vessels — Tuo Chiang-class catamaran corvettes (multiple hulls commissioned or under construction), the Indigenous Defense Submarine (IDS / Hai Kun class) sea trials and follow-on plans, and the next-generation light-frigate programme. These programmes are central to asymmetric and sea-denial capability.
reports._cadence_original: continuous programme updates + periodic budget lines
reports._notes: Core navy and defence-industrial node. Domestic construction of corvettes and submarines creates edges into the broader industrial base and into the asymmetric-warfare priority that now dominates procurement rhetoric.
_referenced_by: Defence budget (military investment and special-budget lines)
Domestic industrial and employment statistics linked to shipyards
reports._cadence_evidence: No MND page states a release schedule for shipbuilding-programme statistics; programme information appears in ad hoc press items and in the biennial 國防報告書 / annual budget books rather than a dedicated series.

reports.title: US Foreign Military Sales / arms-sale notifications and backlog to Taiwan
reports.publisher: US Department of State / Defense Security Cooperation Agency / Congressional notifications (tracked in Taiwan and US official and analytical series)
reports.description: Statistical tracking of notified and backlog US arms sales to Taiwan (recent packages measured in tens of billions of dollars, with a rising share of asymmetric capabilities). Forms the quantitative backbone of the security dimension of the unofficial relationship.
reports._notes: High-authority external security node. Directly links the military cluster to the US–Taiwan economic-security architecture already captured in Batch 8.
_referenced_by: National Defense Report and procurement planning
reports._url_evidence: DSCA official Major Arms Sales congressional-notification series (now an archive; the page states new notifications moved to the State Department under EO 14383). Taiwan cases were not visible on the first page of results.
reports._cadence_evidence: DSCA Major Arms Sales is a rolling feed of congressional notifications posted as cases are approved (10 notices spanning 20 Jan–6 Feb 2026 on page 1, 15+ pages of archive plus a searchable Major Arms Sales Library); the page states no publication schedule.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7) and applied 2026-08-19: a nominal releases_per_year so that absence keeps meaning 'one-off instrument' only - 250 encodes business-day updating (the live corpus's daily-FX convention), 365 genuinely all-days monitoring. It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

reports.title: Domestic defence-industry and military-investment statistics
reports.description: Statistics and programme reporting on domestic defence production, military investment expenditure, and the industrial base that supports indigenous shipbuilding, missiles, and other systems. Interacts with the broader manufacturing and high-tech industrial statistics.
reports._notes: Industrial edge of the military cluster. Creates potential links into the semiconductor and advanced-manufacturing nodes where dual-use technologies overlap.
_referenced_by: Industrial production and employment in related sectors
reports._cadence_evidence: MND's 業務統計及研究報告 section could not be read (robots-blocked) and no defence-industry statistical series with a stated frequency or countable editions was found on mnd.gov.tw.

reports.title: Special budgets for asymmetric force and defence resilience
reports.publisher: Ministry of National Defense / Executive Yuan / Legislative Yuan
reports.description: Multi-year special budget instruments dedicated to asymmetric capabilities, munitions stockpiles, C4ISR resilience, and whole-of-society defence resilience. Distinct from the regular annual defence budget and explicitly framed as responses to the current threat environment.
reports._notes: Policy and fiscal node that operationalises the shift toward asymmetric and resilient force design. High citation value in contemporary strategic analysis.
_referenced_by: Economic and social resilience special statutes
reports._url_evidence: DGBAS 特別預算 page under 政府預算 — the official central-government special-budget listing; individual plan rows load dynamically and were not rendered.
reports._cadence_evidence: The DGBAS 特別預算 page is organised by 計畫名稱 and 年度 — individually named special budgets each enacted under their own special statute (e.g. procurement special budgets), not a periodical; no recurring release cycle is stated.

reports.title: Military personnel and manpower statistics
reports.description: Statistics on active-duty strength, reserve forces, conscription/volunteer mix and related manpower indicators. Interacts with broader demographic and labour-force trends under ultra-low fertility.
reports._notes: Links the military cluster to the demographic extremes already mapped (ultra-low fertility, super-aged society).
reports._cadence_evidence: The national statistics metadata entry for MND 主計局 personnel-related statistics states 發布週期: '年' (annual) with 時效 '5個月'; MND likewise posts a yearly 統計資料發布 page (e.g. 113年統計資料發布).

reports.title: SIPRI arms-transfer statistics for Taiwan (imports)
reports.publisher: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) — widely cited in official and analytical Taiwan security literature
reports.description: SIPRI’s quantitative series on major arms imports by Taiwan. Recent five-year periods show a substantial increase, driven by the perceived threat environment and by US FMS packages. Continuously referenced in comparative security analysis.
reports._notes: International statistical counterpart to the US FMS series. Provides the long-run quantitative measure of external arms dependence.
_referenced_by: National Defense Report and procurement planning

_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Tanzania is the seventh and last country in `country afrikans.docx` to be researched (AF/G.5.md priority 1) -- only 4 raw entries (thinnest of any country in the branch), all four independently re-verified at source this session via direct fetch, no import round used. Every report below is VERIFIED DIRECTLY. Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review, following the established DRAFT-then-import pattern.
_note: Two genuine cross-source findings. (1) A three-way tension on whether Tanzania's pension benefits are CPI-adjusted: the National Social Protection Policy 2023 states plainly that 'inflation has eroded the value of benefits ... due to the absence of mechanisms to adjust benefits' (p.28); the Public Service Social Security Fund Act (Cap. 371) itself, read section-by-section this session, contains no CPI or inflation-linked adjustment provision (only a triennial actuarial valuation under s.57 and a Minister's power to adjust contribution rates 'taking into consideration of the actuarial valuation' under s.18(4)); yet the older SSA/ISSA country profile (2018-2019 vintage, the one the docx actually cited) states for old-age and disability pensions that 'Benefits are adjusted periodically based on changes in the consumer price index.' This session independently fetched the newer ISSA profile (2024-07 vintage) and found that claim is NOT repeated there -- the old-age and disability sections in the 2024 profile carry no 'Benefit adjustments' subsection at all, while the survivor-pension section (present in both vintages) consistently describes actuarial review, not CPI. Per Research.1.md S3, this is reported as a conflict rather than resolved: it reads as though the 2018-2019 profile's CPI claim was simply wrong (or described a since-discontinued arrangement) and the correction shows up silently in the profile's own next vintage, but that is inference, not confirmed. Neither ISSA/SSA profile is minted as a corpus node (same precedent as South Africa's docx entry for the same series, not minted in za-cpi-social-grants.json) -- a periodic secondary compilation, not itself something another primary document names as an input. (2) `eac-hcpi-regulations` already exists in the corpus (first minted for Kenya, ke-social-protection.json) but with only a placeholder evidence URL (https://www.eac.int/, the bare homepage -- Kenya's own session could not reach the actual PDF). This session fetched the EAC Regulations for Compiling Harmonised Consumer Price Indices (March 2022) directly and successfully, and the dependency edges below cite specific Articles (101, 2002, 109.2, 110.1) with a working PDF URL -- worth using to upgrade the existing node's evidence_url when this slice is reviewed, since it is currently backed by a non-primary link.

_open_questions.question: Tanzania's own Data Quality Assessment (Section 2.1.1) says CPI 'adhere[s] to the guidelines outlined in the EAC guidelines for compiling consumer price indices (HCPI)' -- but the EAC document this session actually fetched and quoted from is titled 'EAC REGULATIONS FOR COMPILING HARMONISED CONSUMER PRICE INDICES (HCPI)' (March 2022). A companion document literally titled 'EAC Guidelines for Compiling Harmonised Consumer Price Indices' (same March 2022 date) also turned up in search but could not be fetched this session -- WebFetch failed on eac.int for that specific URL with a certificate/robots error, while the Regulations PDF (a different URL, same domain) fetched cleanly. Unresolved whether 'guidelines' in the DQA is loose language for the Regulations, or a genuinely separate document this session simply could not reach.

Every document in this slice (NCPI, DQA, National Social Protection Policy) explicitly scopes itself to Tanzania Mainland (the NCPI names '26 mainland regions' directly). The United Republic of Tanzania is a union of Mainland and Zanzibar with a partially separate statistical and social-policy apparatus; whether Zanzibar publishes its own CPI or social-protection policy, and whether either cites these Mainland documents or is fully independent of them, was not checked this session.

The World Bank's PSSN III factsheet (March 2026, $250 million IDA credit) states the programme's development objective but not household transfer amounts or any formula for setting them. Older World Bank PSSN documentation (PSSN II, PSSN I) was not checked this session for whether earlier phases specified a transfer-setting method later dropped, or whether one was ever documented at all.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI) Release
reports.description: Tanzania's official monthly National Consumer Price Index (NCPI) release. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via the February 2026 edition, Sections 1.2-1.4 (Methodological Notes): 'The base price reference period is the average from January to December 2020' and 'the index reference period is the year 2020' (S.1.2). Weights: 'The NCPI weights are based on household monetary expenditure data from all 26 mainland regions, covering both urban and rural households. These weights are derived from the 2017/18 Household Budget Survey' (S.1.2). Classification: 'The NCPI follows the United Nations Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP), 2018 version, and is disseminated using 13 COICOP divisions' (S.1.3). Formula: 'The NCPI is compiled using the geometric mean of price relatives for elementary index aggregates and higher-level aggregates are compiled using Lowe Index formula, a type of Laspeyres index' (S.1.4). This particular release contains no statement regarding EAC HCPI guidelines/regulations or IMF CPI Manual compliance -- those citations belong to the separate Data Quality Assessment report (tz-nbs-cpi-dqa), not this monthly release, and no edge is drawn from this node to either.

release_schedule.rule: Each NCPI (National Consumer Price Index) release document includes a schedule table (e.g. Table 2, "NCPI Release Months / Release date") stating the release date for the following reference month's data; in practice NBS Tanzania publishes the CPI release for a given reference month on the 8th day of the following month (e.g. June 2026 CPI released 08 July 2026, May 2026 CPI released 08 June 2026, April 2026 CPI released 08 May 2026, March 2026 CPI released 08 April 2026).
release_schedule.note: July 2026 CPI data was already published (confirmed via third-party aggregator showing July 2026 figures) by the time of this research (2026-08-11), consistent with the observed 8th-of-following-month pattern, so the August 2026 release (due ~08 September 2026) is the next expected one. NBS's own release PDFs and the yearly topic page (https://www.nbs.go.tz/statistics/topic/consumer-price-index-2026) do not show a full forward-year calendar, only the next month's date restated in each report, so this is modeled as a stated/observed rule rather than a fully published calendar.

reports.title: Data Quality Assessment for Consumer Price Index 2023 – Tanzania Mainland
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. States the CPI programme's own methodological compliance in detail: 'CPI adhere to the guidelines outlined in the EAC guidelines for compiling consumer price indices (HCPI)' (S.2.1.1, p.15) -- see tz-eac-guidelines-vs-regulations-naming for the title mismatch against the primary EAC document actually fetched. Same section also names 'Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP) 2018' (S.2.1.1, p.15) and elsewhere 'adheres to the 2008 SNA for classifying institutional units and transactions' (S.2.3.1, p.16). Names the 'Consumer Price Index (CPI) Manual – Concept and Methods 2020' directly (S.3.3.2, p.22). States dissemination practice: 'The CPI is disseminated on monthly basis that follows the IMF data dissemination standards (Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS))' (S.4.1.1, p.25) -- placing Tanzania on the same stronger SDDS tier as South Africa and Egypt, rather than the weaker e-GDDS tier confirmed for Kenya, Nigeria, Ethiopia and Ghana elsewhere in this branch. Frames its own assessment methodology explicitly: 'The IMF Data Quality Assessment Framework (DQAF) identifies quality-related features' (Introduction, p.2), 'rooted in the UN Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics' (Introduction, p.2, not independently minted as a node this session -- a passing citation, not a load-bearing one). Weights confirmed again independently of the CPI release itself: '2017/18 Household Budget Survey' (S.3.1.1, p.18).
reports.cadence_note: An ad-hoc data-quality assessment exercise, not a fixed annual release; this one covers the 2023 reference year.

release_schedule.note: NBS Tanzania's Data Quality Assessment publications page (https://www.nbs.go.tz/publications/data-quality-assessment) lists only a single CPI data-quality assessment (for reference year 2023, published 28 June 2024), alongside one-off DQAs for other statistical domains (PPI, GFS, National Accounts) published at different, non-recurring times. There is no stated periodicity rule or published calendar, and with only one CPI DQA edition ever published, no observed pattern can be established either. This confirms the existing cadence_note's characterization as an ad-hoc exercise rather than a fixed annual release.

reports.title: National Social Protection Policy 2023
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Chapter Four (p.34) lists the governing legal instruments: 'Employment and Labour Relations Act No. 6 of 2004; the Labour Institutions Act No. 7 of 2004; the Occupational Safety and Health Act No. 5 of 2003; the Social Security Act Cap. 135; the Public Service Social Security Fund Act No. 2 of 2018 and the Persons with Disability (Rights and Privileges) Act No. 9 of 2010,' with further instruments named including 'National Social Security Fund Act Cap. 50 [R.E. 2018]' and 'the Universal Health Insurance Act of 2023.' Critically, the policy documents an admitted gap rather than a mechanism: 'Inflation has eroded the value of benefits in contributory and non-contributory social protection due to the absence of mechanisms to adjust benefits' (p.28) -- a direct, self-reported statement that no CPI-linked (or any other) adjustment process currently exists, alongside an unimplemented objective to 'ensure that the value of social insurance benefits, social assistance transfers, and support is adequate' (p.28). On the Productive Social Safety Net (PSSN), financing risk is flagged rather than a benefit-setting formula: 'The programme is limited in coverage due to inadequate resources, and high dependence on donor funding threatens its sustainability' (p.11); benefit structure is named ('a fixed transfer... vulnerable groups transfers (VGT)... and variable human capital transfers (VHCT)', p.10) but amounts are not specified in this document. NBS itself appears only as a future data-generation body (p.39): 'The bureau will generate, store and maintain adequate and up-to-date social protection statistics for planning purposes' -- not as a source the policy currently draws a benefit calculation from.
reports.cadence_note: A multi-year policy framework (November 2023), not a recurring release.

release_schedule.note: One-off multi-year policy framework published November 2023 by Tanzania's Prime Minister's Office - Labour, Employment and Relations (kazi.go.tz). No published review calendar or stated periodic-revision rule was found. A February 9, 2026 event in Arusha was the formal public launch/rollout of this same 2023 policy (alongside the new NISS informal-sector social security scheme), not a new edition or evidence of a recurring release cycle.

reports.title: Public Service Social Security Fund Act, 2018 (Cap. 371)
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (R.E. 2023 consolidated text). Tanzania's main public-service pension statute, named by the National Social Protection Policy 2023 among its governing instruments (see dependency below). Read section-by-section for any inflation/CPI adjustment mechanism: s.30 (Rates of retirement pension) sets the calculation formula but delegates specifics to regulations, with no automatic adjustment clause; s.34 (Rate of invalidity pension) likewise delegates to regulations without mentioning review; ss.25-48 (Benefits under the Scheme) cover qualification, eligibility and payment procedure with no periodic-adjustment provision; s.57 (Actuarial valuation report) requires triennial valuations directed at fund soundness, not benefit levels; s.58 (Restoration of financial soundness) addresses deficit recovery, not indexation. The one adjustment-adjacent power found is s.18(4), letting the Minister adjust contribution rates 'taking into consideration of the actuarial valuation' -- a fund-solvency lever, not a benefit-indexation one, and confined to contributions rather than paid pensions. No CPI or inflation-linked benefit-adjustment provision exists anywhere in the Act -- confirming, at primary-statute level, the Policy's own admission (tz-national-social-protection-policy-2023) that no such mechanism exists.

reports.title: Tanzania Productive Social Safety Net III (PSSN III)
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via the World Bank's own factsheet (dated 31 March 2026): '$250 million credit from the International Development Association (IDA).' Development objective: 'increase access to social protection and better jobs for targeted poor households while building a sustainable and adaptive social protection system that can respond to shocks like climate events.' No Government of Tanzania counterpart-financing figure is stated in this document (contrast Ghana's GPSNP2, majority GoG-funded, and Ethiopia's PSNP5, roughly a third GoG-funded). No statement anywhere in the factsheet ties transfer amounts to inflation, CPI, or cost-of-living -- the docx's own continent-wide typology classifies Tanzania's PSSN as 'Purely Discretionary / Project-based,' which this document does nothing to contradict.

reports.title: Data Quality Assessment Framework (DQAF)
reports.description: The IMF's framework for structured assessment of statistical output quality, named as the explicit methodological basis of Tanzania's own CPI Data Quality Assessment: 'The IMF Data Quality Assessment Framework (DQAF) identifies quality-related features' (tz-nbs-cpi-dqa, Introduction, p.2). First minted this session -- a distinct node from imf-sdds and imf-e-gdds (dissemination-standard tiers) and from cpi-manual (compilation methodology): DQAF governs how quality itself is assessed and reported, not how the index is compiled or disseminated.
reports.cadence_note: A standing framework document, revised infrequently; not an annual release.

release_schedule.note: The DQAF is a methodological framework (a set of quality-assessment templates for statistical data categories), not a periodic statistical release. IMF's Statistics Department revises individual DQAF modules occasionally as needed (e.g., the original framework and supplement date to 2001-2003; the Public Sector Debt Statistics (PSDS) DQAF module was last dated August 2024) but there is no published release calendar or stated periodicity governing when revisions occur. The DSBB/DQRS portal hosts the current framework documents but shows no update schedule.

_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED into src/data/index.ts. Round 8 of Thomas's 'go for 10 rounds' request, 2026-08-12. Tanzania is a structurally unique case in this branch: not a federation of provinces but a Union (1964) of two formerly separate states, one of which (Zanzibar) keeps its own government, statistics office, and CPI series entirely separate from the mainland's. This is the clearest documented example so far of Thomas's question about how 'provinces' relate to the nation NOT reducing to a single pattern across Africa.

reports.title: Zanzibar Consumer Price Index (ZCPI)
reports.publisher: Office of the Chief Government Statistician (OCGS), Zanzibar
reports.description: Confirmed monthly via OCGS's own CPI info page, latest listed release December 2024. Entirely separate from the already-minted tz-nbs-ncpi (Tanzania Mainland CPI, published by the National Bureau of Statistics) and tz-nbs-cpi-dqa (whose own title truncates to 'Tanzania Mainl[and]' — itself a hint of this same split, now confirmed directly). Zanzibar's own primary PDF (an April 2023 dated release) is robots-blocked to non-browser fetch, so no methodology citation could be independently checked this round — the title, publisher and cadence come from OCGS's own confirmed webpage, not the release document itself. UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.18, municipal-tier round): the SAME cpi_info page (https://www.ocgs.go.tz/cpi_info, re-checked via a different fetch path since the domain has a TLS hostname-mismatch issue that blocks direct curl but not an AI-fetch tool) does carry methodology text after all: "The CPI was constructed according to recommended international standards and the Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) Codes." Base period August 2012=100; weights from the 2009/10 Household Budget Survey; formula described as "a weighted geometric average...of the price relatives using expenditure shares" (geometric modified Laspeyres). This page names COICOP and 'international standards' generically, but — re-checked specifically this round — does NOT name EAC, SADC, or the African Charter on Statistics anywhere in its text, so the working hypothesis in this file's own _dropped note below (that Zanzibar's CPI is methodologically independent of any bloc-specific framework) is now supported by a direct, full-text-checked primary source rather than left as inference from the constitutional structure alone.
reports.cadence_note: Confirmed monthly via OCGS's own site.

reports.title: Articles of Union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, 1964
reports.publisher: United Republic of Tanzania (Vice President's Office)
reports.description: The founding instrument of the 1964 union between Tanganyika and Zanzibar. Per the Vice President's Office's own explanatory page, union matters are those "specified in the second schedule of the constitution of URT" (22 listed areas), while "The RGoZ [Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar] has exclusive jurisdiction over non union matters in Tanzania Zanzibar." This is the constitutional root of the split documented alongside it this round: statistics is treated as a non-union matter, which is exactly why Zanzibar maintains OCGS as an entirely separate statistical office from the mainland's NBS rather than a regional branch of it — a structurally different arrangement from every provincial/regional case covered elsewhere this session (Ethiopia, Nigeria, Kenya, DR Congo, Morocco, Ghana), none of which have a constitutionally separate second national government inside them.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument (a union treaty/act).

_dropped.why: OCGS's own dated CPI release PDF (checked: 'Zanzibar Consumer Price Index, April 2023') is robots-blocked to non-browser fetch, so no methodology citation to the mainland's Statistics Act or NBS could be checked. Given statistics is a non-union matter per the Articles of Union, the working hypothesis is that no such citation exists at all — Zanzibar's CPI would be methodologically independent, not derived from mainland Tanzania's framework — but this is a hypothesis from the constitutional structure, not a confirmed textual finding, so no edge (positive or negative) is minted.

Zanzibar is part of Tanzania, an EAC member, and the mainland's tz-nbs-ncpi is presumably wired (or wireable) to the EAC harmonized-CPI hub already in the corpus. Whether Zanzibar's separately-run CPI is independently obligated under the same EAC framework, or whether only the mainland/Union government represents Tanzania at the EAC level, was not checked this round — a genuinely interesting structural question left open.

_note: Uganda's own CPI documents are notably silent on every external framework this branch has come to expect a citation to: the March 2026 and July 2021 UBOS CPI releases were both searched in full for 'East African Community'/'EAC', 'IMF', and 'SNA' and none appear anywhere -- a genuine silence, not a hedge, and a contrast with Tanzania's and Kenya's CPI documents, which both name the EAC HCPI guidelines/regulations directly. The EAC's own regulation document names Uganda as a founding Partner State, but that citation runs the opposite direction (EAC naming Uganda, not Uganda naming EAC) and per the corpus's own direction rule cannot support an edge from Uganda's CPI to `eac-hcpi-regulations`. On social protection: the Senior Citizens Grant's decade-long nominal freeze (2010-2020, per the World Bank) and subsequent ad hoc increase (UGX 25,000 to UGX 35,000, reported only in secondary news coverage, for FY2026/27) is the same shape found repeatedly elsewhere in this branch -- a fixed transfer amount raised occasionally without any stated formula -- but Uganda's own government social-protection policy and strategy documents (2016 and 2025) are, unusually, completely silent on inflation/CPI/erosion language; the only explicit statement of erosion found anywhere is in a World Bank assessment, not a Government of Uganda document. That is a genuine difference in shape from Tanzania's, Malawi's and Eswatini's own admissions in their own policy documents.

_open_questions.question: The Public Service Pension Fund Act, 2025 was reported by URBRA (Uganda Retirement Benefits Regulatory Authority) and by Makerere University's own retirement benefits scheme trustees to have introduced a new contributory public-service pension scheme (5% employee / 10% employer contributions), but this session could not locate the Act's own primary text -- it appears too recent to be indexed on ULII or similar legal databases. Whether it contains any CPI/inflation-linked benefit-adjustment provision is unconfirmed.

NTV Uganda (a news outlet, not a primary source) reports the Senior Citizens Grant/SAGE amount rising from UGX 25,000 to UGX 35,000 effective FY2026/27, but gives no indication of a formula or CPI-linked rationale. No Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development or Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development budget document confirming this figure or its rationale was located this session.

The 2022-consolidated text of the National Social Security Fund Act (https://ulii.org/akn/ug/act/1985/8/eng@2022-01-07) returned a bot-verification block to every fetch attempt this session. Section 35's interest-rate mechanism was confirmed against the 2000-consolidated text and against the SSA/ISSA country profile, but whether the 2022 revision changed this provision is unconfirmed.

reports.title: Uganda Consumer Price Index (2016/17=100)
reports.description: UBOS's monthly Consumer Price Index release for Uganda (Composite) and ten urban centres. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via the March 2026 edition, cross-checked against the July 2021 edition for stability of wording. Foreword: 'The current Consumer Price Index has been rebased from 2009/2010 to 2016/2017, using weights derived from the Uganda National Household Survey (UNHS VI) that was conducted from July 2016 to June 2017.' Classification: 'The rebased CPI is classified using international standards, referred to as Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP 2018) This is a shift from the COICOP 1999 that was used in the earlier series.' Formula: 'At the elementary aggregate (EA) level, the indices are computed using the Jevons (Geometric Mean) method for all items within the elementary aggregates. The modified Laspeyres index formula is used to compute higher level indices.' Both the March 2026 and July 2021 editions were searched in full for 'East African Community'/'EAC', 'IMF', 'SNA' and 'System of National Accounts' -- none appear anywhere, a genuine silence rather than a hedge, and a contrast with Tanzania's and Kenya's own CPI documents.

release_schedule.note: UBOS could not be fetched directly (robots.txt blocked WebFetch access), so this is based on the consistent monthly pattern of UBOS CPI report pages (e.g. consumer-price-index-december-2025, -january-2026 through -july-2026, one per month, published near month-end) plus a third-party economic calendar (TradingEconomics) that lists UBOS CPI releases occurring at the end of each month and shows the next one scheduled for 2026-08-28. Exact day-of-month varies slightly (e.g. July 2026 release was on 2026-07-31); day given for the next entry is from the aggregator's calendar, not confirmed directly on ubos.org.

reports.title: Uganda National Household Survey 2016/2017 (UNHS VI)
reports.description: The sixth round of Uganda's National Household Survey, 'conducted from July 2016 to June 2017' (per the CPI release's own Foreword), whose expenditure data supply the weights currently used in the rebased Uganda CPI. A recurring, titled survey series (UNHS I-VI to date), the same node shape as Tanzania's Household Budget Survey and Kenya's rebasing-report weight source, minted here as its own node rather than folded into the CPI's description because it is independently named with its own round number and dates.
