reports.title: Encuesta Continua de Hogares (ECH) / Continuous Household Survey
reports.description: Continuous household survey that is the primary source for labour-market indicators, household income, and income-based poverty and inequality measurement. National coverage with Montevideo / Interior domains.
reports._notes: Central social and labour survey. Continuous high-frequency operation. Official source for both labour statistics and monetary poverty. Recent poverty (persons) in the mid-to-high teens percent range under the updated methodology.

reports.title: Pobreza por el método del ingreso / Income poverty
reports.description: Official income-poverty and indigency incidence, calculated by comparing household income (from ECH) with nationally defined poverty and indigency lines. Published with Montevideo / Interior and other breakdowns.
reports._notes: Headline social indicator. 2025: persons under the poverty line ~16.6–17.7% depending on semester; indigency ~1.5–1.8%. Methodology updated in recent years (new baskets and economies of scale). Uruguay records among the lower income-poverty rates in the region.

reports.title: Líneas de pobreza e indigencia
reports.description: Monetary values of the poverty and indigency lines (per capita / household), differentiated for Montevideo and the Interior and updated with price information.
reports._notes: Direct input into the poverty measurement. Separate lines for Montevideo and Interior reflect cost-of-living differences.

reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumo (IPC) / Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index measuring changes in the prices of a representative basket of goods and services.
reports._notes: Flagship price statistic. Direct input into monetary-policy analysis by the Banco Central del Uruguay and into the updating of poverty lines.

reports.title: Cuentas Nacionales / National Accounts of Uruguay
reports.description: System of national accounts producing GDP by production, expenditure and income. Quarterly and annual releases.
reports._notes: Core macroeconomic statistical system. BCU plays a central role in the compilation and dissemination of the national accounts.

reports.title: Informe de Política Monetaria (IPoM)
reports.description: Quarterly Monetary Policy Report of the central bank. Explains recent inflation, the outlook, and the implications for the monetary-policy stance under the inflation-targeting regime.
reports._notes: Flagship policy communication product. Complements higher-frequency monetary-policy statements.

reports.title: Censo de Población y Vivienda / Population and Housing Census
reports.description: Decennial population and housing census. Provides the demographic baseline and sampling frames for household surveys.
reports._notes: Foundational demographic product. Continuously cited by ECH design and poverty analysis.

reports.title: Índice de Pobreza Multidimensional (IPM)
reports.description: Official multidimensional poverty index capturing deprivations across multiple dimensions beyond income. Complements the income-poverty series.
reports._notes: Complementary structural poverty measure. Recent estimates place multidimensional poverty in the high teens percent range, with higher incidence outside Montevideo and among children and Afro-descendant populations.

reports.title: Balanza de Pagos / Balance of Payments
reports.description: Quarterly and annual balance of payments covering the current account, capital/financial account and changes in reserve assets.
reports._notes: Core external-accounts product. Recent current-account balances have been close to zero or mildly in deficit; goods and services trade is typically in surplus, offset by primary-income outflows.

reports.title: Estadísticas de Comercio Exterior / Merchandise Trade
reports.description: Monthly and annual statistics of exports and imports of goods. Key traditional exports include beef, cellulose, soybeans, dairy and other agro-industrial products.
reports._notes: Trade data feed the BOP and national accounts. Agro-industrial products (meat, cellulose, grains, dairy) dominate the export basket.

reports.title: Tasa de Política Monetaria (TPM) / Policy interest rate
reports.description: Main monetary-policy instrument of the BCU under the inflation-targeting regime. The rate at which the central bank signals the monetary stance.
reports._notes: Operational policy rate. Adjusted in discrete steps; recent path has moved from a more restrictive stance toward a more neutral/expansive one (e.g. 5.75% in early 2026 after cumulative cuts).

reports.title: Activos de reserva / International reserves
reports.description: Stock of international reserve assets managed by the central bank. Published at high frequency and analysed in the BOP and monetary reports.
reports._notes: Key external-buffer indicator. Continuously monitored alongside the net international investment position.

reports.title: Marco de metas de inflación — BCU
reports.description: Operational monetary-policy framework: explicit inflation targeting. The BCU sets a target range for annual CPI inflation and uses the TPM as the primary instrument.
reports._notes: Core policy-framework node. Continuously cited as the reference against which inflation outcomes and policy actions are evaluated.
_referenced_by: IPC and inflation analysis that refers to the target band
Market and academic commentary on Uruguayan monetary policy

reports.title: Índice de Volumen Físico de la Industria Manufacturera (IVFIM)
reports.description: Monthly physical-volume index of manufacturing production. Principal high-frequency industrial-activity indicator.
reports._notes: Core short-term industry product. Published with variants (with/without refinery, core). Companion indices track hours worked and employment in manufacturing.

reports.title: Exportaciones de carne / Beef & meat exports
reports.description: Statistics of beef and other meat production and exports. Long-standing traditional export and a major component of the agro-industrial economy.
reports._notes: Signature traditional export. Continuously cited in trade and agro-sector analysis; Uruguay is a recognised high-quality beef exporter.

reports.title: Celulosa y forestal / Pulp & forestry exports
reports.description: Statistics of pulp (cellulose) and forestry-related production and exports. Major modern agro-industrial export line.
reports._notes: Structurally important export after large-scale pulp-mill investments. Frequently among the top export products by value.

reports.title: Sector agropecuario / Agricultural & livestock statistics
reports.description: Broader agricultural and livestock production and trade statistics (beef, dairy, grains, soybeans, etc.). Backbone of the traditional export economy.
reports._notes: Primary-sector parent node. Links the commodity-level series (meat, grains, dairy) to the external accounts and to rural economic activity.

reports.title: Encuesta Anual de Actividad Económica (EAAE)
reports.description: Annual structural business survey covering value added, employment, investment and other variables across economic activities.
reports._notes: Structural complement to the high-frequency IVFIM and national accounts. Provides detailed activity-level value-added and employment data.

reports.title: Montevideo — capital statistical identity
reports.description: Capital city and primary urban economy. Core domain for ECH labour, income and poverty analysis. Higher average incomes than the Interior but also elevated poverty incidence in peripheral areas.
reports._notes: Dominant metro node. Continuously published as a distinct geographic domain (Montevideo vs Interior) in ECH income and poverty reports. Intra-city periphery carries higher poverty than the southern coastal strip.

reports.title: Departamento de Artigas — high-poverty border contrast
reports.description: Northern border department with among the highest poverty incidence in the 2025 departmental results.
reports._notes: Poverty-contrast department. Frequently ranked with Rivera and Cerro Largo among the highest-poverty departments.

reports.title: Departamento de Rivera — high-poverty border contrast
reports.description: Northern border department with elevated poverty incidence. Completes the northern border contrast set.
reports._notes: 2025 poverty ranking places Rivera among the highest-poverty departments alongside Artigas and Cerro Largo.

reports.title: Departamento de Cerro Largo — high-poverty border contrast
reports.description: Northeastern border department with elevated poverty incidence.
reports._notes: Completes the high-poverty northern/northeastern border cluster.

reports.title: Departamento de Colonia — low-poverty contrast
reports.description: Southern department with among the lowest poverty incidence in the 2025 results.
reports._notes: Low-poverty southern department. Completes the contrast pole opposite the northern border departments.

reports.title: Pobreza por departamento (INE)
reports.description: Official departmental tabulations of income poverty. Primary source for the inter-departmental poverty gradient.
reports._notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2025 extremes: Artigas, Rivera, Cerro Largo highest; San José, Maldonado, Colonia, Flores lowest. National persons under LP ~16.6%.

reports.title: Presupuesto Nacional / National Budget
reports.description: Annual national budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues and expenditure of the central government.
reports._notes: Operational fiscal framework. Links tax and other revenues with functional spending on education, health, social protection and investment.

reports.title: Gasto público en educación y salud
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / INE
reports.description: Public expenditure on education and health as reflected in the national budget and related functional statistics. Complements household-survey education and health modules.
reports._notes: Education and health are major and constitutionally prioritised functional allocations. Continuously tracked in budget execution and social-policy analysis.

reports.title: Lácteos — producción y exportaciones
reports.description: Statistics of dairy production and exports (whole milk powder, cheese, butter, etc.). Major traditional agro-industrial export and a significant rural employer.
reports._notes: Signature agro-export. 2025 export billing ~USD 965 mn (record/near-record). Whole milk powder dominates; Algeria and Brazil are leading destinations. Completes the agro-export triad with beef and cellulose.

reports.title: Instituto Nacional de la Leche (INALE)
reports.description: Sector institute that compiles and disseminates primary and commercial statistics for the dairy chain. Key analytical and policy-support body for the sector.
reports._notes: Primary statistical and analytical node for the dairy chain. Continuously cited in production, price and export analysis.

reports.title: Soja y granos — producción y exportaciones
reports.description: Statistics of soybean and other grain production and exports. Major component of the agricultural export basket alongside beef, cellulose and dairy.
reports._notes: Important traditional export line. Frequently ranks among the top merchandise exports by value.

reports.title: Dirección General Impositiva (DGI) — tax collection
reports.description: National tax administration. Publishes tax collection by type of tax and performance against annual targets.
reports._notes: Primary revenue-side fiscal statistic. Links the real-side economy to the central-government budget.

reports.title: Deuda pública / Public debt statistics
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / BCU
reports.description: Stock and flow statistics of central-government and public-sector debt (external and domestic). Key sustainability indicator.
reports._notes: Critical fiscal-sustainability node. Continuously monitored in macroeconomic and policy analysis.

reports.title: Departamento de Maldonado — low-poverty southern contrast
reports.description: Southern coastal department with among the lowest poverty incidence. Completes the low-poverty southern set alongside Colonia.
reports._notes: Low-poverty southern department; hosts important tourism and residential activity.

reports.title: Departamento de Canelones — core metropolitan periphery
reports.description: Large department surrounding Montevideo. Intermediate poverty and inequality; important demographic and economic weight in the greater capital region.
reports._notes: Completes the greater Montevideo statistical geography. Frequently cited in both poverty and inequality departmental rankings.

reports.title: Coeficiente de Gini / Income inequality
reports.description: Official Gini coefficient of income inequality, calculated from ECH income data. Published nationally and by department.
reports._notes: Companion inequality indicator to the poverty series. 2025 national Gini ~0.40. Montevideo, Salto and Canelones among the highest departmental inequality.

reports.title: Indicadores de empleo y desempleo (ECH)
reports.description: Labour-force indicators from the ECH: employment rate, unemployment rate, activity rate, and related quality-of-employment measures.
reports._notes: Primary high-frequency labour indicators. Derived from the same continuous household survey that underpins the poverty series.

reports.title: Banco de Previsión Social (BPS) — social-security coverage and finances
reports.description: Main social-security institution covering pensions, family allowances, unemployment benefits, sickness benefits and other social transfers. Major fiscal and social-protection actor.
reports._notes: Central social-protection node. 2025 benefit outlays on the order of USD 8+ bn, dominated by pensions. Continuously cited in fiscal, labour and social-policy analysis; cotizante counts are a key formal-employment indicator.

reports.title: Jubilaciones y pensiones (BPS)
reports.description: Pension and retirement benefit statistics administered by BPS. Largest single component of social-security expenditure.
reports._notes: Dominant BPS expenditure line. Hundreds of thousands of beneficiaries; major structural claim on public resources.

reports.title: Actividad de la construcción / Construction activity
reports.description: Statistics of construction activity, employment and related permits. Cyclically sensitive sector tracked via employment, permits and investment indicators.
reports._notes: Important short-term activity and employment sector. BPS cotizante counts in construction are a high-frequency formal-employment signal; unemployment benefits often concentrate in this sector in downturns.

reports.title: Turismo y hotelería / Tourism & hospitality
reports.description: Tourism and hospitality activity and employment statistics. Important services-export and seasonal employment sector, especially in coastal departments.
reports._notes: Services-side complement to the agro-export economy. Hospitality employment is a useful high-frequency signal of tourism and domestic consumption dynamics.

reports.title: FONASA / Seguro Nacional de Salud
reports.publisher: BPS / Ministerio de Salud Pública / MEF
reports.description: National health-insurance scheme financing coverage through mutualistas and the public provider (ASSE). Major component of the social-security and health-financing system.
reports._notes: Central health-financing mechanism. Linked to BPS contributions and to the public health budget; methodological parameters (e.g. CPE) are periodically reviewed.

reports.title: ASSE — Administración de los Servicios de Salud del Estado
reports.description: Public health-service provider. Complements the mutualista sector within the national health system.
reports._notes: Public provider side of the dual health system. Linked to FONASA financing and to the health functional budget.

reports.title: Departamento de Flores — low-poverty interior contrast
reports.description: Small interior department with among the lowest poverty and inequality incidence.
reports._notes: Completes the low-poverty set. Useful as a small-department contrast to the high-poverty border departments.

reports.title: Departamento de Salto — northern interior
reports.description: Northern interior department with elevated inequality and intermediate-to-higher poverty relative to the southern core.
reports._notes: Frequently appears among the higher-inequality departments. Completes the northern departmental set.

reports.title: Asignaciones familiares y transferencias (BPS)
reports.description: Family allowances and related cash-transfer programmes administered by BPS. Important social-protection instrument for households with children.
reports._notes: Key non-pension social-transfer line. Complements the pension system within the BPS benefit structure.

reports.title: Cotizantes BPS / Formal employment contributors
reports.description: Count of formal workers contributing to BPS. High-frequency formal-employment indicator complementary to the ECH labour series.
reports._notes: Useful formal-employment signal. Sectoral breakdowns (construction, hospitality, industry, agro, etc.) provide high-frequency insight into formal job dynamics.

reports.title: Régimen de Zonas Francas
reports.publisher: Dirección Nacional de Zonas Francas / MEF
reports.description: Free-zone regime offering tax and customs incentives for industrial, commercial and services activities. Strategic instrument for logistics, manufacturing and global-services investment.
reports._notes: Flagship industrial/commercial promotion instrument. ~11–14 free zones in operation. Protocol with Brazil (Additional Protocol 83 to ACE 18) allows zero-tariff entry of free-zone goods into Brazil subject to origin rules — a material industrial-competitiveness lever.

reports.title: Ley de Promoción de Inversiones / COMAP regime
reports.description: General investment-promotion regime granting tax benefits (IRAE, wealth tax, import duties, VAT credits) for declared investment projects. Administered through COMAP.
reports._notes: Primary horizontal investment-incentive framework. Recent decrees have expanded 100% IRAE exemptions for large projects meeting employment and R&D/innovation criteria. Continuously cited in investor-climate materials.

reports.title: Uruguay XXI — investment & export promotion agency
reports.description: National agency for investment attraction and export promotion. Publishes investor guides, sector profiles and trade intelligence.
reports._notes: Institutional interface between the international agreements / incentive regimes and private investors and exporters. Continuously cited in FDI and export-strategy analysis.

reports.title: Relación comercial y estratégica con China
reports.description: Strategic partnership and intensive bilateral trade relationship with China (top export destination). Includes dairy-protocol and broader economic cooperation; FTA negotiations and RCEP interest under discussion.
reports._notes: De-facto structural trade partner. Continuously cited in export-performance analysis even in the absence of a comprehensive bilateral FTA; dairy protocol and strategic-partnership language are recurring reference points.
_referenced_by: Export statistics (China often #1 destination for beef, soy, pulp)
Policy debate on Asia diversification and possible FTA/RCEP path

dependencies.basis: Income poverty is calculated from ECH household income data.
Poverty status is determined by comparing household income with the official poverty lines.
Poverty lines are updated with price information derived from the IPC.
Multidimensional poverty draws on household-survey information alongside other sources.
Artigas’s high poverty ranking is derived from the departmental poverty tabulations.
Tax collection is the primary revenue source of the national budget.
The Gini coefficient is computed from the same income distribution underlying the poverty estimates.
China is a top export destination; the bilateral relationship structures a large share of merchandise trade.

meta.note:
UZBEKISTAN, SECOND PASS, straight off the first round's own todo. RESULT: 1 node, 5 dependencies, 3 dropped notes.

WHAT IT ADDS. The first pass attached Uzbekistan to NACE through `uz-oked`. This one attaches it to the UN consumption classification through `uz-coicop`, on a sentence that states the derivation outright rather than leaving it to be assumed — 'COICOP RU 2018 ... which is based on the UN international standard'. The same two-step shape is used deliberately in both places: the statistic depends on the NATIONAL classifier and the national classifier is what is derived from the international one, so nothing is wired straight from a statistic to a UN or EU standard. `uz-national-accounts` picked up three edges from sheets already in hand — to the national COICOP, to COFOG, and to `uz-oked`, which is now a three-statistic hub.

A BROWSER SESSION ON lex.uz WAS THE FIRST ROUND'S NAMED TOP FOLLOW-UP AND IT CAME BACK NEGATIVE, which is the useful part. Searched in Thomas's own Chrome: OKED returns 91 acts that mention it and no classifier; the COICOP RU 2018 classifier returns nothing at all. Uzbek classifiers are almost certainly Uzstandard O'z DSt standards rather than legal acts, so lex.uz was the wrong place and standart.uz is the lead. Both classifier nodes therefore keep an empty `url`, and the `_dropped` note records the full search so nobody repeats it.

ONE EDGE WAS PROPOSED AND REFUSED: `uz-cpi -> the HIES`. The sheet says the HIES frame rests on the 2010 Microcensus and separately that CPI weights come from consumption expenditure data, but never joins them. That join is the reader's, not the publisher's.

meta.note:
UZBEKISTAN, FIRST ROUND. RESULT: 5 nodes, 5 dependencies, 4 dropped notes. The country had ONE node before this — `uz-ssc`, which is the statistical office itself carrying `kind: instrument`, i.e. the institution-as-a-node scaffolding the August import was supposed to strip. So this is a minting round, not a wiring one, and the coverage workbook said as much: 1 node against a category-median expectation of about 13 for a country of 37 million.

THE SEAM. stat.uz publishes ~198 English-language METADATA SHEETS, one per indicator, and they are ESMS-shaped — a common governance preamble followed by numbered indicator-specific sections that name the methodology, the classification and the legal basis. That is the same shape Eurostat's national reference metadata has, and it is the same reason it pays: several answers per fetch, from the publisher's own documents. Eight sheets were read this round.

THE EDGE WORTH HAVING is `uz-oked -> nace-rev2`. Uzbekistan's national activity classifier is stated by its own statistical office to be based on NACE Rev. 2, independently in four sheets, which attaches Uzbekistan to the EU classification spine the 2026-09-14 round built — the same shape as Poland's PKD 2007. `uz-employment` and `uz-ppi` then hang off OKED rather than off NACE directly, because the statistics use the national classifier and the national classifier is what is derived; skipping the middle would state a derivation no document states.

ONE NODE HAS NO URL ON PURPOSE. `uz-oked` is well evidenced and unpublished: no page on stat.uz carries the classifier itself and lex.uz is unreadable from here. An empty field was chosen over another publisher's page or a bare homepage, which are the two defects the last three rounds have been cleaning up. The `_dropped` entry says exactly what was tried.

WHAT WAS REFUSED: the BPM6 edge ('brought into line with' is agreement language), the UN Vital Statistics recommendations (the corpus's lookalike node is the Census one — a wrong target), and any edge off the sheets' common governance preamble, which describes the agency rather than the statistic.

dependencies.basis: SELF-DECLARED: the Committee's own CPI metadata sheet, section 2.1.1. The evidence is the Committee's own English-language metadata sheet for this indicator, one of ~198 published under stat.uz's Metadata section. They are ESMS-shaped: a common governance preamble, then numbered indicator-specific sections (2.1 Concepts and definitions, 2.2 Scope, 2.3.1 Classification/sectorization). The quote is taken from the indicator-specific half, never the preamble. WHICH EDITION, AND WHY IT IS THE 2020 ONE: the document renders the title as 'Guide to the Consumer Price Index: Theory and practice', which are the 2004 edition's words, but gives the year as 2020 and lists the six publishers as IMF, OECD, Eurostat, UNECE, World Bank and ILO. `cpi-manual` (Concepts and Methods, 2020) carries exactly that publisher set including UNECE; `cpi-manual-2004` carries 'United Nations' instead. Two of three signals — year and authorship — point at 2020 and only the translated title phrase points at 2004, so the target is the 2020 manual. THE EDGE COMPRESSES ONE LINK, stated plainly rather than hidden: the sentence runs CPI -> national Methodological Provisions (Resolution No. 33 of 27 September 2022) -> the international manual. The Provisions have no node and no retrievable url, so they are recorded in `_dropped` and this edge spans them. If the Provisions are ever minted, this edge should be split in two. ROUTE: stat.uz answers this container on a plain fetch; the metadata sheets are ordinary PDFs read with `pdftotext -layout`. Direct read of a first-party publisher, no archive in the chain. GRADE: B, `quote-found-target-not-named`, and it is the correct answer. Coverage is 1.0 but the document calls the manual 'Guide to the Consumer Price Index: Theory and practice' and the node carries its real title, 'Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods'. The grader is reporting a true fact about the document — it does not name the artefact as its publisher titles it. Nothing was done to move this: the edition reasoning above stands on the year and the six-publisher list, not on the title.

dependencies.basis: SELF-DECLARED: the Committee's own PPI metadata sheet, comparability section, on the classifier the index has been structured by since 2016. The evidence is the Committee's own English-language metadata sheet for this indicator, one of ~198 published under stat.uz's Metadata section. They are ESMS-shaped: a common governance preamble, then numbered indicator-specific sections (2.1 Concepts and definitions, 2.2 Scope, 2.3.1 Classification/sectorization). The quote is taken from the indicator-specific half, never the preamble. The scope section says the same thing operationally — observation covers enterprises whose main activity falls in OKED sections B, C, D and E. NOTE ON THE TARGET'S TITLE: this sheet renders the classifier as 'National Classification on kinds of Economic Activities of the Republic of Uzbekistan' while the employment sheet renders it 'National Classifier of Types of Economic Activities (OKED, rev. 2)'. Same classifier, two English translations of one Uzbek title; both are carried in the node's `title_aliases` so either spelling reaches it. ROUTE: stat.uz answers this container on a plain fetch; the metadata sheets are ordinary PDFs read with `pdftotext -layout`. Direct read of a first-party publisher, no archive in the chain. QUOTE TRIMMED BEFORE THE FINAL RUN: the first span began at 'Until 2016, the PPI was formed...' and graded B `partial-quote` at coverage 0.93. `pdftotext` renders the dash in 'since 2016 – in the structure' as the two characters '¬–', a soft-hyphen artefact that no normalisation in the grader folds away, so any span crossing it loses those characters. The span now starts after it and covers 1.0. Nothing about the claim changed.
dependencies.evidence_quote: in the structure of types of economic activity (according to the National Classification on kinds of Economic Activities of the Republic of Uzbekistan, based on NACE rev.2).

_dropped.edge: uz-cpi -> the Methodological Provisions (Resolution of the State Statistics Committee No. 33, 27 Sept 2022)
_dropped.why: The national instrument that sits between the Uzbek CPI and the international manual. The CPI sheet names it in full — 'Methodological Provisions for organizing monitoring of consumer prices (tariffs) for goods and services and calculating consumer price indices (approved by Resolution of the State Statistics Committee No. 33 of September 27, 2022)' — so the publisher's own title is in hand. No node, because no url is: the instrument is not on stat.uz and lex.uz's search is JavaScript-driven and returned nothing readable to this container. CONSEQUENCE, stated so it is not discovered later as a surprise: `uz-cpi -> cpi-manual` spans this instrument in one edge. When the Provisions get a node, that edge should become two.

Recorded because a node with an empty `url` looks like an oversight and this one is a decision. Four of the Committee's metadata sheets name OKED and two state its NACE derivation, so the artefact is not in doubt. What is missing is a page that PUBLISHES it. Tried and failed 2026-09-16: stat.uz's 'Statistical classifications' link resolves to /en/interactive-services/classification-of-commodities, which is a commodity-classification service and carries no OKED content; classifier.stat.uz does not resolve; two guessed stat.uz classifier paths 404'd; lex.uz answers 200 but renders its search by JavaScript and its API rejects a direct query. The alternatives were worse than an empty field — another publisher's page repeats the defect the ECOICOP audit found, and a bare homepage repeats the August-import defect. ONE BROWSER SESSION on lex.uz probably closes this.

_dropped.edge: uz-population -> UN Principles and Recommendations for Vital Statistics
_dropped.why: Found while sweeping the metadata sheets and NOT taken, because the obvious target is the wrong one. The population sheet names 'Principles and Recommendations for Vital Statistics, approved by the UN Statistical [Commission]'. The corpus holds `un-census-principles` — 'Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses' — which is a DIFFERENT UN document with a similar name. Wiring to it would be a wrong-target edge of exactly the kind rule 14 caught for Romania. The Vital Statistics recommendations need their own node, and a population node for Uzbekistan needs minting first.

_dropped.edge: uz-ssc is an agency node, not an artefact
_dropped.why: Uzbekistan's only pre-existing node is `uz-ssc`, titled 'National Committee of the Republic of Uzbekistan on Statistics' — the same string as its own `publisher` field — and carries `kind: "instrument"`. It is the statistical office, not an instrument and not a publication. The August 2026 import's own mint note says 'geography- and institution-as-a-node scaffolding stripped'; this one survived the strip. It is left alone here because retyping or retiring a node with a live edge (`uz-ssc -> imf-e-gdds`, graded A) is a ruling for Thomas, not a research decision — PLAYBOOK 7c retired the analytical meta-node sweep deliberately and says not to extend it by keyword. Flagged so the next Uzbekistan round does not build on it by accident.

reports.title: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE) — institutional statistical identity
reports.description: National statistical office. Formal producer of official demographic, social and economic statistics. Publication cadence and methodological transparency have been severely constrained for an extended period.
reports._notes: Institutional parent node. Continuously cited as the formal statistical authority, but the practical data environment for poverty, labour and living conditions has been dominated by independent sources for years.
_referenced_by: International organisations that still cite residual official series

reports.title: Encuesta Nacional de Condiciones de Vida (ENCOVI) — UCAB
reports.description: Independent multi-purpose household survey conducted by the Universidad Católica Andrés Bello. Primary source for income poverty, multidimensional poverty, labour, education, health, services and migration effects used by domestic and international analysis.
reports._notes: De-facto core household-welfare survey. Annual (or near-annual) since the mid-2010s. Continuously cited as the reference series for poverty, services access and living conditions when official publication is sparse. Recent rounds place income poverty in the high 60s % of households and multidimensional poverty around the mid-50s %.

reports.title: Pobreza de ingresos (ENCOVI)
reports.description: Income-poverty and extreme-poverty incidence derived from the ENCOVI household survey. Headline monetary-poverty indicator used in external analysis.
reports._notes: Headline social indicator under data-quality constraints. Recent ENCOVI rounds show income poverty still very high (order of 65–70% of households) with extreme poverty (inability to cover food) remaining material (order of 30%+ of households in recent readings).

reports.title: Pobreza multidimensional (ENCOVI)
reports.description: Multidimensional poverty index combining income with deprivations in employment, housing, public services and education. Complementary structural poverty measure.
reports._notes: Structural poverty measure. Has been more sticky than income poverty in recent years; public-service failures (electricity, water) weigh heavily. Recent readings around the mid-50s % of the population.

reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor / Inflation statistics
reports.description: Consumer price index and inflation measures. Official BCV series coexist with independent estimates that have been widely used during periods of high inflation and publication gaps.
reports._notes: Flagship price statistic under data-quality stress. Hyperinflation episode and subsequent high inflation made independent price tracking (and later official stabilisation) central to any reading of real incomes and poverty.

reports.title: CLAP — Comité Local de Abastecimiento y Producción (food boxes)
reports.description: State subsidised food-distribution programme delivering periodic food boxes to households. Major non-income support instrument in the crisis and post-hyperinflation period.
reports._notes: Lived social-protection node. ENCOVI and other sources consistently report very high coverage (often 80%+ of households receiving boxes at some frequency). Complements (and partially substitutes for) cash income in food access.
reports._url_evidence: Asamblea Nacional official law page for the Ley Constitucional del CLAP (sanctioned 5 Jan 2018, Gaceta Oficial 41.330), which constitutes and regulates the CLAP food-distribution committees; no Venezuelan ministry publishes a live CLAP programme/statistics landing page.

reports.title: Acceso a servicios públicos (electricidad, agua)
reports.description: Household access to continuous electricity and piped water. Core component of multidimensional poverty and of everyday living conditions.
reports._notes: Lived infrastructure failure node. Recent ENCOVI rounds indicate continuous electricity is available to only a small minority of households and continuous piped water to a minority; service interruptions are a defining feature of daily life for most.

reports.title: Migración y población residual
reports.description: Statistics and estimates of large-scale emigration and of the residual resident population. Demographic context for all household and labour analysis.
reports._notes: Structural demographic shock. Millions have left; residual population estimates (ENCOVI and others) are substantially below earlier official projections (order of 28–29 million vs earlier 34 million projections). Shapes labour supply, dependency ratios and the interpretation of all household surveys.

reports.title: Distrito Capital / Caracas — metropolitan core
reports.description: Capital metropolitan area. Primary urban domain for labour, income, services and poverty analysis.
reports._notes: Dominant metro node. Continuously appears as a distinct geographic domain in ENCOVI and residual official tabulations; service and labour conditions remain stressed even in the capital.

reports.title: Producción petrolera / Oil production
reports.description: Crude-oil production volumes. Structural backbone of the external accounts and fiscal capacity. Recent recovery from the deep trough of the late 2010s / early 2020s.
reports._notes: Core external-revenue node. Production has recovered toward the 1.0–1.2 million barrels/day range in recent readings (highest in several years) but remains far below historical peaks. Continuously cited as the primary driver of any macroeconomic rebound.

reports.title: Balanza de Pagos / Balance of Payments
reports.description: Balance of payments covering the current account, capital/financial account and reserve changes. Publication and detail have varied over the crisis period.
reports._notes: Core external-accounts product under data-quality stress. Oil exports dominate the goods account; remittances and other secondary income are material supporting flows.

reports.title: Reservas internacionales / International reserves
reports.description: Stock of international reserve assets. Key external-buffer indicator under chronic foreign-exchange pressure.
reports._notes: External-buffer node. Levels remain low relative to historical peaks and to the economy’s import and debt-service needs; exchange-market intervention draws on available reserves.

reports.title: Tipo de cambio / Exchange rate
reports.description: Official and parallel exchange rates. Central relative price in a dual (or multi) exchange-rate environment that shapes inflation, real incomes and import access.
reports._notes: Lived price signal. Large and persistent gaps between official and parallel rates have been a defining feature of the crisis; recent periods show rapid official depreciation and high inflation pass-through.

reports.title: Cobertura y asistencia escolar (ENCOVI)
reports.description: School enrolment and attendance indicators from the independent household survey. Complements residual official education statistics.
reports._notes: Lived education gap. Coverage remains below pre-crisis levels; a large absolute number of children are out of school, and irregular attendance (2–3 days/week) is widespread among those enrolled.

reports.title: Empleo y ocupación (ENCOVI)
reports.description: Labour-force participation, occupation and formal/informal employment indicators from ENCOVI. Primary labour-market window under official-data constraints.
reports._notes: Lived labour market. Occupation rates are low by regional standards; female participation is especially depressed. Formal employment share has risen from crisis lows but remains limited; self-employment and informal work absorb much of the adjustment.

reports.title: Remesas / Family remittances
reports.description: Inflows of personal transfers from Venezuelans living abroad. Major secondary-income and household-support flow.
reports._notes: Lived external support. Remittances partially offset domestic income shortfalls for receiving households; ENCOVI tracks both the share of households that receive them and changes in sending behaviour among the diaspora.

reports.title: Bonos y transferencias monetarias del Estado
reports.description: State cash bonuses and transfers that supplement household income alongside CLAP food boxes.
reports._notes: Lived social-protection node. Coverage is wide but amounts are small in real terms; ENCOVI analysis has noted that transfers are not strongly progressive (non-poor households also receive them).

reports.title: Faja Petrolífera del Orinoco — resource base
reports.description: World’s largest known extra-heavy oil resource. Geographic and geological core of Venezuela’s long-run petroleum potential.
reports._notes: Foundational resource node. Continuously cited as the physical base of proven reserves (order of 300 billion barrels) and of any sustained recovery scenario; requires specialised technology and large investment to develop at scale.

reports.title: Estado Zulia — western oil and population pole
reports.description: Western state centred on Maracaibo. Largest state population mass and a major oil-producing region. High service and living-condition stress in independent surveys.
reports._notes: Demographic and oil-geography node. Continuously appears among the highest-stress states in independent living-conditions diagnostics; large absolute population affected by service failures and poverty.

reports.title: Estado Miranda — capital-region periphery
reports.description: State surrounding and interwoven with the Caracas metro. Large population, mixed urban conditions, and high absolute poverty and service-stress counts.
reports._notes: Completes the greater Caracas statistical geography. Frequently ranked among the largest absolute poverty and service-deprivation masses.

reports.title: Estado Bolívar — southern mining and industrial
reports.description: Southern state with major mining (iron, gold, etc.) and industrial activity (Ciudad Guayana). Distinct resource and living-conditions profile.
reports._notes: Mining and heavy-industry geography. Independent diagnostics show elevated multidimensional stress; resource extraction coexists with severe service and income gaps.

reports.title: Estado Carabobo — central industrial corridor
reports.description: Central state with significant industrial and commercial activity (Valencia area). Intermediate-to-high living-condition stress.
reports._notes: Industrial-corridor node. Completes the set of major population and economic poles outside the pure oil west and the capital.

reports.title: Sistema de salud — acceso y deficiencias
reports.description: Public health-system access and reported deficiencies in infrastructure, personnel, medicines, equipment and basic services (water, electricity) at care points.
reports._notes: Lived health-system stress. Large majority rely on public facilities; independent diagnostics report widespread shortages of medicines, supplies, equipment and basic services inside those facilities. Private care is largely inaccessible by cost.

reports.title: Ingresos petroleros del Estado
reports.description: Fiscal and external revenues derived from oil exports. Primary financing source of the public sector and of foreign-exchange supply.
reports._notes: Core fiscal-revenue node. Recovery of production and commercialisation arrangements (including licensed private operators) directly shapes the government’s foreign-exchange and budget capacity. Transparency of flows remains limited.

reports.title: SENIAT — tax administration
reports.description: National tax authority. Publishes residual tax-collection statistics that form the non-oil revenue side of the budget.
reports._notes: Non-oil revenue node. Tax collection exists and is reported in residual form, but oil remains the dominant fiscal resource; the overall budget framework is characterised by limited transparency.

reports.title: Estado Anzoátegui — eastern oil and industrial
reports.description: Eastern state with significant oil and industrial activity. Intermediate-to-high living-condition stress in independent diagnostics.
reports._notes: Eastern oil/industrial geography. Completes the set of major hydrocarbon and population states.

reports.title: Régimen de sanciones de EE.UU. / OFAC Venezuela sanctions
reports.description: Comprehensive U.S. sanctions architecture targeting the Venezuelan government, PDVSA, the central bank and designated individuals/entities. Continuously amended by general licenses that carve out authorised oil, gas and related activities.
reports._notes: Dominant external constraint and enabling framework. The regime remains in force; policy has shifted toward incremental expansion of General License carve-outs rather than comprehensive lifting. Continuously cited as the binding condition for lawful commercial engagement with the oil sector.

reports.title: OFAC General Licenses (GL 46 / GL 50 and successors)
reports.description: Series of general licenses authorising named international oil companies and defined activities involving Venezuelan-origin oil, gas, petrochemicals and related investment. Core operational carve-out from the broader sanctions regime.
reports._notes: Operational enabler of the recent production recovery. Named majors are authorised to operate upstream and related activities under evolving license terms; royalty and revenue handling is subject to U.S.-controlled mechanisms.
_referenced_by: Chevron, BP, Shell, Eni, Repsol, Maurel & Prom operations

reports.title: Chevron — licensed oil operations in Venezuela
reports.description: Longest-standing U.S. major operating under successive OFAC licenses. Principal early channel for resumed commercial oil flows toward the United States.
reports._notes: Flagship licensed operator. Continuously cited as the bridge that kept a residual commercial link to the U.S. market during the tighter sanctions period and as a core participant under the broader 2026 general licenses.
reports._url_evidence: Chevron's official 'Venezuela Highlights of Operations' page, listing its PDVSA joint-venture interests (Petroboscán 39.2%, Petropiar 30%, Petroindependiente 25.2%, Petroindependencia/Carabobo 3 34%) and the Loran gas block.

reports.title: Majors licenciados (BP, Shell, Eni, Repsol, Maurel & Prom)
reports.description: Group of European and other international oil companies authorised under OFAC general licenses to conduct oil and gas operations in Venezuela alongside Chevron.
reports._notes: Expanded licensed-operator set. Their entry/return under the 2026 general licenses is a central feature of the post-transition commercial reopening of the upstream sector.

reports.title: Fondo / mecanismo de control de ingresos petroleros (EE.UU.)
reports.description: U.S.-controlled arrangements for the handling of certain Venezuelan oil-related revenues and royalty flows under the post-2026 sanctions and license architecture.
reports._notes: Critical revenue-governance node. Independent analysis tracks the share of export value that flows through U.S.-administered mechanisms versus direct government or PDVSA channels; transparency remains limited.
reports._url_evidence: OFAC's Venezuela-Related Sanctions program page; it lists the current oil-related general licences (GL 52A on PDVSA, 46C on Venezuelan-origin oil, 47A, 50B) and E.O. 14373 'Safeguarding Venezuelan Oil Revenue', the revenue-control framework described in the node.

reports.title: Relación comercial petrolera Venezuela–EE.UU.
reports.description: Bilateral oil-trade relationship reconstituted under the licensed-operator regime. United States has re-emerged as a major (in some recent months the largest) destination for Venezuelan crude.
reports._notes: Structural commercial reorientation. Share of exports going to the U.S. has risen sharply relative to the China-dominated pattern of the preceding years.
reports._url_evidence: EIA series 'U.S. Imports from Venezuela of Crude Oil (Thousand Barrels per Day)', monthly, showing values through May 2026 (471 kb/d) with release date 7/31/2026 — the official U.S. statistical series for the bilateral oil trade.

reports.title: Relación comercial y de deuda con China
reports.description: Long-standing oil-for-loans and commercial relationship. China was the dominant export destination through the mid-2020s; volumes and relative weight have declined under the post-transition commercial reorientation.
reports._notes: Legacy and residual partner. Oil-backed debt and preferential supply arrangements defined a major external relationship for more than a decade; the commercial share has fallen as U.S.-licensed channels expanded.
reports._url_evidence: China's Ministry of Commerce country guide '对外投资合作国别（地区）指南 — 委内瑞拉' (2025 edition) on mofcom.gov.cn, covering China–Venezuela bilateral trade, Chinese investment and the 2023 all-weather strategic partnership; hosted on the publisher's own domain, not a mirror.

reports.title: Public Sector Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users
reports.publisher: Inter-Agency Task Force on Finance Statistics (IMF, World Bank, BIS, OECD, Eurostat, UNCTAD, Commonwealth Secretariat, Paris Club Secretariat)
reports.description: 2011 joint international manual on the concepts, classification, compilation and dissemination of public-sector debt statistics, co-published by the IMF, World Bank and six other international bodies under the Inter-Agency Task Force on Finance Statistics. Distinct from the IMF's Government Finance Statistics Manual (GFSM) — it is the standard specifically for debt-stock statistics, cited by name and edition in Vietnam's Ministry of Finance Public Debt Bulletin as the international basis for its debt classification.

reports.title: OECD Handbook on Compiling Digital Supply-Use Tables
reports.description: OECD guidance (issued November 2023) for measuring the digital economy's contribution to GDP via Digital Supply and Use Tables (D.SUTs). Cited by name by Vietnam's General Statistics Office as the methodology it studied and applied when compiling the digital economy's value-added share of GDP/GRDP.

reports.title: IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
reports.publisher: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Task Force on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
reports.description: The IPCC's methodological standard for compiling national greenhouse gas inventories under the UNFCCC, issued across multiple cumulative editions (the Revised 1996 Guidelines, the 2006 Guidelines, and the 2019 Refinement to the 2006 Guidelines). Cited directly, across different editions, by Vietnam's Biennial Update Report and Nationally Determined Contribution as the basis for its GHG inventory and emissions-projection methodology.

IIP is the stock counterpart to the flow data vn-bop represents, compiled by the same SBV division under the single IMF manual covering both (the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, 6th ed.) — SBV's live Balance-of-Payments data page and its DSBB BOP metadata file were both blocked (WAF rejection) on repeated attempts this round, so the IIP-series metadata document, from the same division and manual family, is used as the basis instead. SELF-DECLARED: Vietnam's official National Summary Data Page (nsdp.nso.gov.vn), the IMF e-GDDS portal for Vietnam, states: "Data linked from this page correspond to data described in the International Monetary Fund’s DSBB. For a fuller explanation of the DSBB and the enhanced General Data Dissemination System in which Vietnam participates, please visit the DSBB home page." SBV is itself a designated data-provider agency on this page — its own Central Bank Survey metadata document, filed on the same NSDP and used to compile reserve-money and other monetary statistics, names "The State Bank of Vietnam" as the reporting agency ("Reserve money is compiled on a monthly basis by the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV)"). This complements the existing vn-gso -> imf-e-gdds edge: GSO and SBV are separate e-GDDS-participating agencies filing their own category's metadata within the same Vietnamese national framework.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Data linked from this page correspond to data described in the International Monetary Fund’s DSBB. For a fuller explanation of the DSBB and the enhanced General Data Dissemination System in which Vietnam participates, please visit the DSBB home page.

dependencies.basis: Vietnam's own Government Finance Statistics Manual, developed jointly by the Ministry of Finance, the World Bank and the IMF, states on its cover page: "This manual is developed by the Ministry of Finance of Vietnam, the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund," and contains a dedicated section ("Relationship between the Vietnam classification and GFSM2001/2014") mapping Vietnam's state-budget classification directly onto the IMF's Government Finance Statistics Manual framework.

The same MOF/World Bank/IMF Vietnam GFS Manual states Vietnam's state budget reports already publish deficit figures on both bases ("State budget reports publish deficits on a Government of Vietnam and GFS basis"), and that bridge tables — built during the 2012 IMF GFS mission, mapping the State budget classification (Circular No. 342/2016/TT-BTC) to the GFS2014 framework — are what produce the GFS-basis deficit figure, with any residual difference from the domestic figure to be documented in MOF's own State Budget Bulletin (SBB).

MOF's Public Debt Bulletin No. 17 (Bản tin Nợ công số 17, Debt Management and External Finance Department, Jan 2024), in its own methodology section, states its debt classification follows international standards "như được giới thiệu trong cuốn 'Thống kê nợ công: Hướng dẫn cho người sử dụng'" ("as introduced in the book 'Public Sector Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users'"), footnoting the exact 2011 joint publication by the BIS, the Commonwealth Secretariat, Eurostat, the IMF, the OECD, the Paris Club Secretariat, UNCTAD and the World Bank — distinct from imf-gfsm, which the same corpus already uses for Vietnam's budget/deficit statistics.

GSO's own December 2023 press release on compiling the digital economy's value-added share of GDP/GRDP states it studied international measurement frameworks and names OECD's handbook specifically: "Tháng 11 năm 2023 tổ chức này đã ban hành Sổ tay biên soạn D.SUTs để làm rõ hơn các khái niệm cũng như hướng dẫn chi tiết phương pháp" ("In November 2023 this organisation [OECD] issued the D.SUTs Compilation Handbook to further clarify the concepts and give detailed methodological guidance"). The same release also discusses an alternative ADB input-output framework, but names the OECD D.SUTs handbook as the guidance whose concepts it adopted.

Vietnam's 3rd Biennial Update Report (BUR3) to the UNFCCC states directly: "The national GHG inventory is carried out in accordance with the guidelines of the IPCC, including: The 2006 IPCC Guidelines for national GHG inventories ... The 2019 refinement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for national GHG inventories."

The same BUR3 states: "The General Statistics Office (GSO) under MPI is responsible for collecting/controlling the quality of data from other focal points ... to provide the DCC, MONRE with activity data and related information to implement GHG inventories," directly naming GSO as the activity-data supplier for Vietnam's national GHG inventory.

Vietnam's 2022 NDC states its 2014 baseline emissions figure is "the results of the GHG inventory ... published in the Third National Communication of Viet Nam sent to the UNFCCC in 2019." The Third National Communication is not itself a separate corpus node; it is an earlier report in the same MONRE/DCC national GHG-inventory series that vn-ghg's listed document (BUR3) continues and updates, so this is recorded as the NDC drawing on Vietnam's ongoing national GHG-inventory programme, not literally the BUR3 PDF — flagged explicitly rather than silently treated as identical documents.

The same NDC document states: "The Revised 1996 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories and the 2000 IPCC Good Practice Guidance have been used to calculate and forecast GHG emissions to 2030 ... the IPCC Good Practice Guidance for the LULUCF sector in 2003 has been used," citing an earlier IPCC edition than BUR3's 2006/2019 citation — both fall under the same corpus node (ipcc-ghg-guidelines), scoped to the IPCC Guidelines standard across its cumulative editions rather than one fixed vintage, unlike SNA/COICOP where each edition is a materially different, non-cumulative framework.

Decision 749/QD-TTg (vanban.chinhphu.vn, cross-checked against thuvienphapluat.vn) sets forward-looking targets ('digital economy accounts for 20% of GDP by 2025') but does not cite a current/baseline digital-economy GDP-share statistic sourced from GSO or any named body — reads as a pure policy target, not a data-dependency citation.

The Vietnam Logistics Report 2023 landing page (logistics.gov.vn) describes the report only in general terms ('reliable information systems and data updated from official sources') without naming vn-seaport-throughput, VIMAWA, or GSO trade statistics specifically. The parent listing page rendered as a JS-loading shell with no content, and the full report PDF itself could not be located/fetched, so its actual data-sources section was not verified.

vimawa.gov.vn/vi/thong-ke lists monthly cargo-throughput reports only as downloadable .docx/.pdf files, not renderable by the fetch tool, with no explanatory text on the page itself about data sources or classification standards. Could not confirm any HS-code citation without opening the individual report files.

No listed URL. Hai Phong Port Authority's own site (cangvuhaiphong.gov.vn) publishes no throughput statistics, only regulatory/administrative content (though it names Vietnam Maritime Administration as its oversight body). VIMAWA's own Hai Phong page is a berth/terminal directory with no throughput figures. A Hai Phong city-government figure reports standalone provincial cargo tonnage with no stated link to VIMAWA's national total. Structurally very likely a component of vn-seaport-throughput's national aggregate, but no document states that containment in words, so no part_of or edge is asserted — flagged for Thomas as a plausible but undocumented part_of candidate.

No listed URL. Saigon Newport Corporation's own site self-reports throughput ('a throughput volume of 9.7 million TEUs') without citing Vietnam Maritime Administration, GSO, or any government statistical body as validation/source. No VIMAWA or GSO document found explicitly citing Cai Mep/HCMC port figures as sourced from or feeding into vn-seaport-throughput's national aggregate — same undocumented-containment situation as vn-port-haiphong.
