reports.title: General Statistics Office of Viet Nam (GSO) institutional core
reports.publisher: General Statistics Office / National Statistics Office
reports.description: Primary national statistical office responsible for censuses, surveys, national accounts, prices, labour, trade and multi-domain socio-economic statistics. Organised vertically from central to provincial and district levels.
reports._notes: Foundational institutional node for the Vietnamese statistical system.
reports._cadence_evidence: gso.gov.vn is the agency's live portal/homepage; it carries continuously refreshed indicator tiles and links rather than one discrete publication. Item is the institution itself, not a titled series.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7) and applied 2026-08-19: a nominal releases_per_year so that absence keeps meaning 'one-off instrument' only - 250 encodes business-day updating (the live corpus's daily-FX convention), 365 genuinely all-days monitoring. It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

reports.title: Population and housing census / mid-year population estimates
reports.description: Official population census and subsequent estimates. Population reached approximately 102.3 million in 2025, ranking third in Southeast Asia. Provides the demographic base for all per-capita and planning indicators; fertility now below replacement.
reports._notes: Core demographic node. Population ~102.3 million (2025).
reports._cadence_resolution: nominal: title states mid-year (annual) estimates; GSO advance-release calendar not independently confirmed
reports._cadence_evidence: Page fetched (gso.gov.vn homepage). Targeted check found no census cycle, no mid-year estimate schedule and no advance release calendar; only monthly CPI/IIP/socio-economic items unrelated to population.

reports.title: National Accounts of Viet Nam (GDP)
reports.description: Quarterly and annual national accounts (GDP by industry and expenditure). Central macro-output series for a rapidly industrialising, export-oriented economy.
reports._notes: Primary macroeconomic output node.
reports._cadence_evidence: gso.gov.vn homepage states no periodicity for GDP/national accounts and shows no dated GDP releases to count; no advance release calendar on the page.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index and inflation statistics
reports.description: Monthly CPI and inflation rates by major commodity group. High-frequency price signal used in monetary policy and welfare analysis.
reports._notes: Core high-frequency price node.
_referenced_by: State Bank of Vietnam monetary policy

reports.title: Labour force and employment statistics
reports.description: Labour-force participation, employment, unemployment and related indicators from household and enterprise surveys. Captures the large manufacturing and services workforce that underpins export performance.
reports._notes: Primary labour-market statistical product.
reports._cadence_evidence: gso.gov.vn homepage contains no labour-force survey release dates or stated periodicity.

reports.title: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) institutional and reporting core
reports.description: Central bank responsible for monetary policy, financial stability, external accounts and key macro-financial statistics. Publishes monetary, banking and external-sector data.
reports._notes: Central-bank institutional counterpart to GSO.
reports._cadence_evidence: sbv.gov.vn homepage is a live portal: continuously updated exchange rates, interbank rates and a rolling 'banking activity this week' feed; no single discrete release for the institutional core.
reports.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7) and applied 2026-08-19: a nominal releases_per_year so that absence keeps meaning 'one-off instrument' only - 250 encodes business-day updating (the live corpus's daily-FX convention), 365 genuinely all-days monitoring. It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

reports.title: Balance of Payments and external accounts
reports.description: Quarterly and annual BOP statistics. Captures the large goods-trade surplus (especially with the United States) and FDI inflows that characterise Vietnam’s external position.
reports._notes: External-accounts node with strong goods-export surplus signature.
reports._url_evidence: SBV statistics page showing Vietnam's quarterly balance of payments table (current, capital and financial accounts, Q2 2025).
reports._cadence_evidence: Page presents the BOP table headed 'QUY II NAM 2025' (Q2 2025) with a quarter-by-quarter archive of the same table; quarterly periodicity.

reports.title: National seaport cargo and container throughput statistics
reports.description: Official statistics on total cargo throughput (million tonnes) and container throughput (TEUs) across Vietnam’s seaport system. Recent years show strong growth, with container volumes exceeding 30 million TEUs and cargo approaching or exceeding 900–960 million tonnes.
reports._notes: Core national maritime-logistics statistical product.
reports._url_evidence: Statistics section of the Vietnam Maritime and Inland Waterways Administration listing the monthly 'Khoi luong hang hoa thong qua cang bien' (seaport cargo throughput) series.
reports._cadence_evidence: vimawa.gov.vn/vi/thong-ke lists one 'Hang hoa thong qua cang' cargo-throughput item per reference month (e.g. to June 2026, to May 2025) running back to April 2024 - monthly.

reports.title: Ho Chi Minh City / Cai Mep port complex operational statistics
reports.region: Southeast / Ho Chi Minh City area
reports.description: Operational statistics for the southern gateway complex (Ho Chi Minh City Port / Cat Lai and the deep-water Cai Mep–Thi Vai cluster). Together they form Vietnam’s largest container handling concentration and rank among the world’s top container ports by volume and performance.
reports._notes: Primary southern international-gateway port node.
_referenced_by: HCMC GRDP and Southeast regional analysis

reports.title: Hai Phong port operational statistics
reports.description: Operational statistics for Hai Phong — the principal northern gateway port. Ranks among the world’s top container ports by volume and has recorded strong performance-index gains.
reports._notes: Primary northern international-gateway port node.
_referenced_by: Red River Delta and industrial-province analysis

reports.title: Ethnic minority population and composition statistics
reports.description: Official statistics on Vietnam’s 54 ethnic groups. The Kinh majority forms the large bulk of the population; ethnic minorities (approximately 15 % of the total) are concentrated especially in the Midlands and Northern Mountains and the Central Highlands.
reports._notes: Core demographic node for ethnic composition.

reports.title: Digital economy value-added and share of GDP
reports.publisher: General Statistics Office / National Statistics Office
reports.description: Official measurement of the digital economy’s contribution to GDP. In 2025 the digital economy reached an estimated 14.02 % of GDP (approximately USD 72 billion), up substantially from earlier in the decade. Distinguishes core digital sectors from the digitalisation of other industries.
reports._notes: Core digital-economy statistical product. High-centrality modernisation node.

reports.title: E-commerce and digital trade component of the digital economy
reports.description: E-commerce and digitally enabled wholesale/retail activity as a measurable component of the digital economy. Accounts for a significant share of digital-economy value added and generates rising tax revenues.
reports._notes: E-commerce densification within the digital-economy cluster.
reports._url_evidence: Publications page of MOIT's E-commerce and Digital Economy Agency listing the 'Sach trang Thuong mai dien tu Viet Nam' (Vietnam E-commerce White Book) series 2019-2023.
reports._cadence_evidence: idea.gov.vn document list shows one e-commerce white book / annual e-commerce report per year: 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023.

reports.title: National Digital Transformation Strategy framing
reports.description: Official National Digital Transformation Strategy (including the 2026–2030 strategy with vision to 2045). Sets targets for digital government, digital economy (ambitious share of GDP) and digital society, and organises policy action across ministries.
reports._notes: High-level policy frame for the digital agenda.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved the Government legal-document portal record: Decision No. 749/QD-TTg of 3 June 2020 by the Prime Minister, 'Phe duyet Chuong trinh Chuyen doi so quoc gia den nam 2025, dinh huong den nam 2030' - the official National Digital Transformation Programme, with the signed PDF attached. NOTE: the newer Decision 1266/QD-TTg of 14/7/2026 (Strategy 2026-2030, vision 2045) could not be confirmed - I walked the portal's docid range covering documents dated 30/6/2026 to 28/7/2026 (218890-219038) and it is not published there.
reports._url_route: 4 (publisher's own document portal, vanban.chinhphu.vn, browsed/probed by docid)
reports._cadence_evidence: Document is Decision 749/QD-TTg signed 3 June 2020 by the Prime Minister approving the national digital transformation programme - a single legal instrument, not a recurring publication.

reports.title: Da Nang Gross Regional Domestic Product
reports.publisher: General Statistics Office / local statistical office
reports.description: Official GRDP for Da Nang — the principal urban and services/tourism hub of the Central region. Regularly ranks among the mid-to-upper tier of provincial economies and contributes meaningfully to national growth.
reports._notes: Primary Central urban-core regional output node.
reports._url_evidence: Da Nang city portal's socio-economic report section (128 monthly/quarterly 'bao cao tinh hinh kinh te - xa hoi' reports), the official vehicle for the city's GRDP figures.

reports.title: Can Tho Gross Regional Domestic Product
reports.publisher: General Statistics Office / local statistical office
reports.description: Official GRDP for Can Tho — the largest city and commercial hub of the Mekong Delta. Complements the broader Mekong Delta agricultural and aquaculture profile with an urban services and logistics node.
reports._notes: Primary Mekong Delta urban-core regional output node.
reports._url_evidence: Can Tho city portal's socio-economic situation report series (monthly and quarterly 'Bao cao tinh hinh kinh te - xa hoi'), which carries the city's GRDP figures.

reports.title: Index of Industrial Production (IIP)
reports.publisher: General Statistics Office / National Statistics Office
reports.description: Monthly and cumulative Index of Industrial Production covering manufacturing, mining, electricity and water. Manufacturing dominates growth; electronics and related processing are major drivers.
reports._notes: Core high-frequency industrial activity node.

reports.title: Foreign Direct Investment statistics (registered and disbursed)
reports.description: Official FDI attraction figures (new projects, additional capital, capital contributions). Processing and manufacturing typically absorb the large majority of inflows. Singapore, Korea, China, Japan and others lead recent rankings; US FDI stock and flows remain strategically important.
reports._notes: High-centrality investment node. Manufacturing absorbs ~2/3 of recent FDI.
reports._url_evidence: Foreign Investment Agency (Ministry of Finance) listing of the recurring 'Tinh hinh thu hut dau tu nuoc ngoai' reports with registered, adjusted and disbursed FDI.
reports._cadence_evidence: FIA listing page carries cumulative FDI attraction reports for each successive reference period ('Thang 1', '3 thang dau nam', '6 thang dau nam', '11 thang', 'nam 2024') - one report per month.

reports.title: FDI by major partner country / territory
reports.description: Breakdown of FDI inflows by source. Singapore, South Korea, China, Japan, Hong Kong and others dominate recent flows; US FDI is smaller in annual ranking but significant in stock, technology and strategic sectors.
reports._notes: Partner-side densification of the FDI cluster. Complements the large USA export relationship.
reports._url_evidence: FIA report 'Tinh hinh thu hut dau tu nuoc ngoai nam 2024' showing the ranking of investing countries (Singapore 10.21bn USD, Korea 7.06bn, then China, Hong Kong, Japan).
reports._cadence_evidence: This is the 13 January 2025 FDI report covering full-year 2024 with the by-source-country ranking; the page identifies it as part of 'So lieu FDI hang thang' (monthly FDI data) and links prior monthly editions.
reports._part_of_evidence: RESOLVED 2026-08-29 (was flagged undocumented in unlinked-nodes-wiring-round4/vn-unlinked-wiring-2026-08-29.json): re-fetched both live pages directly (not the fetch tool's summary). vn-fdi's own List page (fia.mof.gov.vn/List/.../CatID/457641e2...) literally enumerates this exact article ('Tinh hinh thu hut dau tu nuoc ngoai nam 2024', dated Thu Hai 13/01/2025 04:08) as one of its listed entries, and both pages share the identical site breadcrumb 'Bao cao dau tu > Bao cao theo thang > So lieu FDI hang thang'. This is the primary source itself declaring the containment (the article is one entry within the listing vn-fdi represents), not a guessed CatID match -- satisfies the same evidence burden as an edge (types.ts part_of constraint 2).

reports.title: Rice production statistics
reports.description: Official volume and area statistics for rice (paddy). Vietnam remains one of the world’s top rice exporters; the Mekong Delta is the primary production basin.
reports._notes: Foundational food-security and export-crop node.
reports._url_evidence: NSO 'Agriculture, forestry and fishery' statistics topic page, which includes 'Planted area and production of paddy' series by province.
reports._cadence_evidence: nso.gov.vn agriculture section is an index of table titles ('Production of paddy by province' etc.) with no release dates, no editions to count and no stated periodicity.

reports.title: Agriculture, forestry and fishery production statistics
reports.description: Broader primary-sector output covering crops, livestock, forestry and fisheries/aquaculture. Complements the rice-focused series.
reports._notes: Core primary-sector production node.
reports._cadence_evidence: gso.gov.vn homepage gives no periodicity or dated releases for agriculture/forestry/fishery output.

reports.title: Hanoi Gross Regional Domestic Product
reports.publisher: General Statistics Office / local statistical office
reports.description: Official GRDP for the capital city. Major services, administration and industrial contributor to national growth.
reports._notes: Primary northern urban-core regional output node.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved the Hanoi Statistics Office page 'Bao cao tinh hinh kinh te - xa hoi quy IV va nam 2025' and its attached PDF (03. BC KTXH_N2025_HaNoi.Ky.pdf), which states 'Tinh chung nam 2025, GRDP cua Thanh pho uoc tinh tang 8,16% so voi nam truoc'. Publisher shown as Cuc Thong ke TP Ha Noi, under the National Statistics Office.
reports._url_route: 3 (alternate/successor hostname: thongkehanoi.gov.vn and cucthongkehanoi.gso.gov.vn fail TLS; thongkehanoi.nso.gov.vn works)

reports.title: Ho Chi Minh City Gross Regional Domestic Product
reports.publisher: General Statistics Office / local statistical office
reports.description: Official GRDP for Ho Chi Minh City — Vietnam’s largest urban economy and southern commercial/industrial hub. Together with Hanoi forms the dual-core national economic structure.
reports._notes: Primary southern urban-core regional output node.

reports.title: Electronics, computers and components trade statistics
reports.description: Trade statistics for electronics, computers and components — the single largest and fastest-growing export category. Exports have more than tripled over the past decade; imports of components remain large, reflecting assembly-oriented participation in global value chains. Dominant in the Vietnam–US trade corridor.
reports._notes: High-centrality commodity node linking industry, FDI and the USA export relationship.
reports._url_evidence: NSO trade release page whose tables include exports and imports by main commodity group (electronics, computers and components) as well as by country.
reports._cadence_evidence: Same NSO monthly export/import value tables ('data tables of months in 2025'); electronics/computers is a commodity line within the monthly trade release.

reports.title: Electricity generation and energy mix statistics
reports.description: Power generation and capacity by source. Coal remains a large share of total energy supply; hydropower, gas, solar and wind are expanding under successive Power Development Plans. Energy transition targets are progressively raising renewable shares.
reports._notes: Core energy-system node. Coal-heavy with rising renewables.
_referenced_by: National accounts and industrial energy demand
reports._url_evidence: Vietnam Electricity (EVN) annual report series landing page, listing EVN Annual Reports 2017-2025 which carry generation and capacity by source.
reports._cadence_evidence: EVN 'Bao cao thuong nien' (Annual Report) page lists one edition per year (2017, 2018, 2021, 2022, 2022-2023, 2024-2025 posted 8 Jan 2026).

reports.title: National Power Development Plan (PDP) framework
reports.publisher: Government of Vietnam / Ministry of Industry and Trade
reports.description: The successive National Power Development Plans (including PDP8 and adjustments) that set capacity targets, fuel mix trajectories and energy-transition pathways to 2030 and beyond.
reports._notes: High-level energy planning frame node.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved the portal record for Decision No. 768/QD-TTg of 15 April 2025 by the Prime Minister, 'Phe duyet Dieu chinh Quy hoach phat trien dien luc quoc gia thoi ky 2021-2030, tam nhin den nam 2050' (the adjusted PDP8), with four downloadable PDFs (768-ttg.signed.pdf plus annexes). The original PDP8, Decision 500/QD-TTg of 15/5/2023, was also confirmed at docid=207889.
reports._url_route: 4 (publisher's own document portal, vanban.chinhphu.vn, addressed by docid)
reports._cadence_evidence: Document is Decision 768/QD-TTg dated 15 April 2025 approving the adjusted Power Development Plan VIII - a single Prime Ministerial legal instrument.

reports.title: Poverty and living standards survey statistics
reports.description: Results from the Vietnam Household Living Standards Survey and related poverty-rate series. Multidimensional and income poverty have fallen sharply; remaining poverty is concentrated in northern mountainous and some ethnic-minority areas.
reports._notes: Core welfare measurement node.
reports._cadence_evidence: gso.gov.vn homepage states nothing about VHLSS or poverty-survey cycles and shows no dated poverty releases.

reports.title: Aquaculture and fisheries production statistics
reports.description: Official volume and value statistics for aquaculture and capture fisheries. Vietnam is a major global seafood exporter; the Mekong Delta dominates production.
reports._notes: Core aquaculture/fisheries statistical product.
reports._url_evidence: NSO 'Agriculture, forestry and fishery' topic page, whose Fishery section covers capture-fishing and aquaculture production by province.
reports._cadence_evidence: nso.gov.vn agriculture-forestry-fishery section is an undated catalogue of table titles; no dates or stated frequency for aquaculture/capture fisheries.

reports.title: International visitor arrivals and tourism statistics
reports.publisher: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism
reports.description: Official statistics on international tourist arrivals, source markets and related tourism indicators. Arrivals have recovered strongly and set new records in recent years.
reports._notes: Core tourism statistical product.
reports._url_evidence: Statistics section of Vietnam's Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, publishing visitor-arrival figures (international and domestic) - the tourism authority's own site is a JavaScript app that returns no content to WebFetch.
reports._cadence_evidence: bvhttdl.gov.vn/thong-ke is a news-style feed of ad-hoc provincial tourism items (Apr-Aug 2024) with no stated release schedule and no countable national visitor-arrivals series.

reports.title: Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and climate-policy framework
reports.description: Vietnam’s NDC under the Paris Agreement and associated climate-policy framing. Continuously referenced in energy, agriculture, forestry and adaptation discussions.
reports._notes: Core climate-policy frame node.
_referenced_by: Energy mix and Power Development Plan
reports._url_evidence: Viet Nam's updated Nationally Determined Contribution (2022) as recorded in the UNFCCC registry: 15.8% unconditional / 43.5% conditional reduction vs BAU by 2030.
reports._cadence_evidence: Single dated submission - Viet Nam's NDC updated 2022, submitted October 2022. The document states updates were made in 2015, 2020 and 2022 in response to calls (e.g. COP26), and gives no fixed update cycle.

reports.title: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory and statistics
reports.publisher: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment
reports.description: National GHG inventory results by sector (energy dominant, followed by agriculture and industrial processes). Provides the empirical base for NDC tracking.
reports._notes: Emissions-side climate node.
reports._url_evidence: Viet Nam's Third Biennial Updated Report to the UNFCCC containing the national GHG inventory for 2016 (316,735 ktCO2e; energy 65%, IPPU 14.6%, AFOLU 13.9%, waste 6.5%).
reports._cadence_evidence: Document is Viet Nam's Third Biennial Updated Report (BUR3); foreword cites Decision 2/CP.17 requiring biennial submission - one every two years.

reports.title: Health insurance coverage statistics
reports.description: Official coverage rates for the national health insurance scheme. Coverage has reached very high levels (above 90 % of the population in recent years).
reports._notes: Core health-financing / social-protection coverage node.
reports._url_evidence: Vietnam Social Security's official 'So lieu thong ke Nganh' (sector statistical data) disclosure section, which carries health-insurance participation/coverage reporting.
reports._cadence_evidence: Vietnam Social Security 'So lieu thong ke Nganh' page carries meeting summaries and directives (Dec 2025, Mar 2026, Apr 2026) rather than a dated statistical series; no stated publication schedule.

reports.title: Social insurance and unemployment insurance coverage
reports.description: Coverage statistics for compulsory social insurance and unemployment insurance among the labour force. Complements health-insurance coverage and forms the core of the formal social-security system.
reports._notes: Core social-insurance coverage node.
reports._url_evidence: Same VSS 'So lieu thong ke Nganh' disclosure section, covering compulsory social insurance and unemployment insurance participation.
reports._cadence_evidence: Same VSS statistics page: no stated frequency and no countable series of social/unemployment insurance coverage releases.

reports.title: Vietnam–China merchandise trade statistics
reports.description: Bilateral goods trade with China. China is Vietnam’s largest overall trading partner and dominant import source (intermediate goods, components, machinery). Vietnam runs a large structural trade deficit with China while exporting electronics, agricultural products and other goods.
reports._notes: High-centrality bilateral trade node. China is the largest import source and second export market.
reports._url_evidence: NSO trade release page including 'Imports and exports by country group, country and territory', the official series carrying Vietnam-China bilateral goods trade.
reports._cadence_evidence: Same NSO page of monthly preliminary export/import value tables, one per month of 2025.

reports.title: Vietnam–Korea trade and FDI statistics
reports.description: Bilateral trade and investment with the Republic of Korea. Korea is a top-three export market, major import source and consistently among the largest FDI sources (electronics, manufacturing, consumer industries).
reports._notes: High-centrality Korea corridor node (trade + FDI).

reports.title: Vietnam–Japan trade and FDI statistics
reports.description: Bilateral trade and investment with Japan. Japan is a top-five export market, important import source and long-standing major FDI partner (manufacturing, infrastructure, technology).
reports._notes: High-centrality Japan corridor node (trade + FDI).
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved MOFA's country dossier 'Tai lieu co ban ve Nhat Ban va quan he Viet Nam - Nhat Ban'. It carries both halves of the node: bilateral trade ('Nam 2013, Nhat Ban la ban hang thuong mai dung thu 4 cua Viet Nam voi kim ngach thuong mai hai chieu dat 25,163 ty USD', exports 13.581 bn / imports 11.582 bn) and Japanese FDI (top source in 2013 with 5.747 bn USD registered; 2,226 valid projects worth 35.5 bn USD cumulative to April 2014, ranked first). Dated - the dossier is updated to 2014 - but it is the official MOFA product.
reports._url_route: 4 (MOFA's own country-dossier page)
reports._cadence_evidence: MOFA page is a single background briefing on Japan and Vietnam-Japan relations marked 'Cap nhat den thang 3/2014'; it states no update frequency and there are no editions to count.

reports.title: China FDI in Vietnam statistics
reports.description: Registered and realised FDI from China (and Hong Kong where separately reported). China ranks among the top sources by number of new projects and has risen into the top tier by capital in recent years; manufacturing and processing dominate.
reports._notes: Investment-side densification of the China corridor. Complements the large trade relationship.
reports._url_evidence: FIA (Ministry of Finance) series of FDI attraction reports; the 2024 report in this list ranks China and Hong Kong among the top five sources of registered capital.
reports._cadence_evidence: Same FIA listing of monthly cumulative FDI attraction reports, which carry the by-source-country breakdown including China/Hong Kong.

reports.title: Vietnam–China trade structure (electronics, intermediates, agriculture)
reports.description: Commodity composition of bilateral trade. Vietnam imports large volumes of intermediate goods, components and machinery from China; exports electronics, telephones, agricultural products and other goods. Structural deficit with China is a recurring feature.
reports._notes: Commodity-structure densification of the China trade relationship.

reports.title: Vietnam–China Border Economic Zones and cross-border cooperation
reports.description: Border Economic Zones (BEZs) and Cross-Border Economic Cooperation Zones along the Vietnam–China land border (Lao Cai, Mong Cai, Dong Dang, Cao Bang and related pairs). Focus of infrastructure, trade facilitation and local economic development.
reports._notes: Spatial and institutional densification of the land-border economic relationship.

reports.title: Vietnam–China infrastructure and railway connectivity projects
reports.description: Priority cross-border infrastructure cooperation, including standard-gauge railway lines linking the two countries. Treated as strategic connectivity projects in joint statements.
reports._notes: Physical-connectivity densification of the bilateral relationship.
_referenced_by: Border Economic Zones and trade nodes

reports.title: Structure and total assets of credit institutions
reports.description: Official statistics on the structure of the credit-institution system (state-owned commercial banks, joint-stock commercial banks, foreign banks, policy banks, finance companies, people’s credit funds, etc.) and their total assets, charter capital and key ratios.
reports._notes: Core structural node for the Vietnamese banking system.
reports._cadence_evidence: sbv.gov.vn homepage gives no periodicity or dated releases for credit-institution structure / total assets.

reports.title: State-owned commercial banks (SOCBs) statistics
reports.description: Statistics focused on the major state-owned commercial banks (Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV, Agribank and related). These institutions hold a large share of system assets and play a central role in credit allocation.
reports._notes: State-owned banking densification.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved the State Bank of Vietnam's 'State-owned Commercial Banks' register, current as of 30 June 2026, giving each bank's name, address, licence number/date and charter capital in VND billion (e.g. Agribank, 51,638.6 bn VND), with links to the earlier dated versions of the list back to 2022.
reports._url_route: 4 (SBV's own site navigation; dttktt.sbv.gov.vn remains unreachable)
reports._cadence_evidence: Page shows the SOCB table 'By June 30, 2026' with a 'Related documents' archive of the same table at quarter-ends: 31/12/2023, 31/03/2024, 30/06/2024, 30/09/2024, 30/03/2025, 30/06/2026 - quarterly snapshots.

reports.title: Credit growth and outstanding loans statistics
reports.description: System-wide and sectoral credit growth rates and outstanding loan volumes. Credit expansion is a key transmission channel of monetary policy and a major driver of investment and consumption.
reports._notes: High-frequency credit-activity node.
_referenced_by: SBV monetary policy and banking-system nodes
reports._cadence_evidence: sbv.gov.vn homepage states no release frequency for credit growth / outstanding loans and shows no dated credit releases to count.

reports.title: Non-performing loans and asset-quality statistics
reports.publisher: State Bank of Vietnam / commercial bank disclosures
reports.description: System-wide and bank-level non-performing loan ratios, absolute NPL volumes and loan-loss provisioning / coverage ratios. Key indicator of banking-system health and credit risk.
reports._notes: Core asset-quality / risk node.
reports._url_evidence: SBV statistics section listing the 'Ratio of NPLs over Total Loan Outstanding' series under Performance of Credit Institutions; the underlying data pages sit on dttktt.sbv.gov.vn, which is unreachable via WebFetch.
reports._cadence_evidence: sbv.gov.vn/en/statistics lists 'Ratio of NPLs over Total Loan Outstanding' among available series but states no periodicity; the page is a navigation portal to a separate analytics platform with no dated NPL editions shown.

reports.title: Monetary aggregates and key SBV monetary indicators

_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. South Africa is the pilot country for the OPEN-THREADS Africa file (`country afrikans.docx`, raw import research covering Nigeria, Egypt, South Africa, Kenya, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Ghana -- 48 entries, none independently verified). This slice mints only the South African nodes, all independently re-verified at source this session rather than trusted from the docx's own quotes. Sitting in EU/proposals/ per that folder's promote-when-reviewed rule even though this is not an EU node -- no AF proposals folder exists yet; move to src/data/research/ once reviewed, at which point a new AF branch folder is also worth creating (see the accompanying hand-off).
_note: The docx's own framing -- that most African countries run a discretionary, not automatically CPI-indexed, benefit-adjustment model -- held up under independent verification for South Africa specifically: Social Assistance Act s.32(3) gives the Minister (with Treasury's concurrence) a Gazette-notice power to set grant amounts, not a formula. This is why the dependency structure below uses the weakest relationship type (`cites`) between the Budget Review and the CPI rather than `uses_data_from` -- the Budget Review's own text references 'a lower inflation outlook' when explaining a grant adjustment, but nothes ties the adjustment to the CPI print by a stated formula. Two Acts named 'Social Assistance' vs 'Social Security Agency' are easily confused and were confirmed as genuinely separate statutes this session (the docx's own entries did not distinguish them).

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (P0141)
reports.description: South Africa's official monthly CPI, published as statistical release P0141. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: the June 2026 edition (embargoed until 22 July 2026, released under the standard P0141 numbering) was fetched and read at source. Its own key findings: 'Annual consumer price inflation was 5,0% in June 2026, up from 4,5% in May 2026. The CPI increased by 0,7% month-on-month in June 2026' -- matching the figures in the Africa research file exactly, confirming the file's citation was accurate for this entry even though it was not independently checked before this session.

release_schedule.note: Stats SA publishes CPI monthly on a Wednesday at 10:00, roughly three weeks after month-end, via its advance schedule page (accessible from the P0141 publication page at https://www.statssa.gov.za/?page_id=1854&PPN=P0141).

reports.title: Social Assistance Act 13 of 2004
reports.description: The statute governing South Africa's social grants (old age, disability, child support, and others). VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (LawLibrary/Laws.Africa, the free legislation archive run with the African Legal Information Institute -- SAFLII's own act pages 301-redirect and were not usable). Its own text, s.32(3): 'The Minister, with the concurrence of the Minister of Finance -- (a) must determine amounts payable in respect of social assistance; and (b) may determine additional payments linked to a social grant, by notice in the Gazette.' This is the key finding for the whole slice: there is no statutory CPI-indexation formula in the Act itself. Amounts are set by discretionary Gazette notice, jointly by the Minister of Social Development and the Minister of Finance -- confirming, at the primary-source level, the general pattern the Africa research file describes across the continent (discretionary adjustment, not automatic indexation), rather than merely repeating its claim.

reports.title: South African Social Security Agency Act 9 of 2004
reports.description: A separate statute from the Social Assistance Act 13 of 2004 (same year, easily confused -- the docx's own entries did not distinguish them; this session did). Establishes the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA), the body that actually administers and pays grants. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: s.2(1), 'The South African Social Security Agency is hereby established as a juristic person'; s.3(a), the Agency's object is to 'act, eventually, as the sole agent that will ensure the efficient and effective management, administration and payment of social assistance.'

reports.title: South African Social Security Agency Annual Report
reports.description: SASSA's own annual report. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: the 2024/25 edition (RP270/2025, ISBN 978-1-83491-131-1) was fetched and read at source. Its own text confirms the reporting obligation rests on the Public Finance Management Act (PFMA, Act 1 of 1999) rather than on the SASSA Act itself -- a general public-entity reporting requirement, not a SASSA-specific one, worth recording precisely rather than assuming the establishing Act itself mandates the report.
reports.cadence_note: Annual reporting under the Public Finance Management Act, confirmed from the report's own PFMA-compliance section rather than assumed from the SASSA Act.

entries.covers: SASSA Annual Report 2025/26 (financial year ended 31 March 2026) — statutory submission deadline to executive authority

release_schedule.rule: Public Finance Management Act, 1999, Section 55(1)(d): the accounting authority for a public entity must submit the annual report, audited financial statements and auditor's report within five months of the end of a financial year to the relevant treasury, the executive authority responsible for that public entity, and (where applicable) the Auditor-General.
release_schedule.note: SASSA's financial year ends 31 March; the PFMA sets a 5-month deadline for submitting the annual report to the executive authority/treasury (i.e. by 31 August). This is the statutory submission deadline, not necessarily the date of public tabling in Parliament or website posting, which can follow somewhat later in the same cycle (the 2024/25 report, FY ended 31 March 2025, was published as static.pmg.org.za/2/SASSA_Annual_Report_2024_25.pdf). The most recent occurrence (2024/25 report, due by 31 Aug 2025) has already passed, so the computed next occurrence is the 2025/26 report due 31 Aug 2026.

reports.title: Budget Review (National Treasury)
reports.description: South Africa's annual national Budget Review, the document that sets out the social grant allocation for the coming medium term. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: the 2026 edition, Chapter 5 (Consolidated Spending Plans), fetched and read at source. Its own text: 'The social grant allocation has been adjusted down over the medium term in line with a lower inflation outlook and improved grant targeting and verification, which is expected to yield savings of R2 billion in 2026/27 and R1 billion in 2027/28.' This confirms the docx's claim, quoted independently rather than trusted from its summary.

entries.covers: 2025 Budget Review (delayed from originally scheduled 19 Feb 2025 due to coalition dispute over VAT)

release_schedule.note: The Budget Review is tabled in Parliament by the Minister of Finance alongside the annual National Budget Speech, published each year on the National Treasury site under /documents/national budget/<year>/review/. No statute fixes an exact calendar date (the Money Bills Amendment Procedure and Related Matters Act requires an annual budget but not a specific date), so timing is an observed pattern rather than a stated rule. Convention is mid-to-late February, but 2025 slipped to 12 March 2025 after the originally scheduled 19 Feb 2025 tabling was postponed amid a coalition dispute over a proposed VAT increase. A National Treasury press advisory dated 3 February 2026 ('2026 Budget lock-up Registration is Open') confirms the 2026 Budget/Budget Review was presented in February 2026, consistent with the corpus's existing Chapter 5.pdf URL for the 2026 edition. Exact day for 2026 and the projected 2027 date could not be confirmed from pages I could reach, hence month-level precision for those two entries.

dependencies.basis: Budget Review 2026, Chapter 5: 'The social grant allocation has been adjusted down over the medium term in line with a lower inflation outlook...' -- inflation is named as a factor in the allocation decision, but no formula ties the figure to a specific CPI print, so this is filed as `cites` (context) rather than `uses_data_from` (mechanical input). This absence of a formula is itself the finding, not an oversight in how the edge is drawn.

SASSA Act s.3(a): the Agency's object is 'the efficient and effective management, administration and payment of social assistance' -- 'social assistance' being the scheme the Social Assistance Act 13 of 2004 establishes and defines. The two Acts were passed the same year and name two different things (a benefits scheme and the agency that pays it); this edge records the documented link between them rather than assuming one because of the similar names.

SASSA Act s.2(1) establishes SASSA as a juristic person; the Annual Report is the Agency's own statutory report on its performance and finances as that juristic person, so its existence depends directly on the Act that creates the Agency.

_open_questions.question: Should `za-sassa-annual-report` also carry a `methodology_depends_on` edge to `za-social-assistance-act-2004`, since the report covers grant payments made under that Act?
_open_questions.answer: Not added this session -- the report's own text ties its reporting obligation to the PFMA (a general public-entity requirement) and to the SASSA Act (which establishes the reporting entity), not explicitly to the Social Assistance Act. The existing `za-sassa-act-2004 -> za-social-assistance-act-2004` edge already carries that connection one hop up; adding a second direct edge risked double-counting the same underlying fact. Worth revisiting if a future session reads the Annual Report's own text more closely for an explicit citation.

_open_questions.question: Is the Budget Review always tabled in February, or does the date move?
_open_questions.answer: Not checked this session -- `last_updated` is set to the 2026 edition's tabling date (25 February 2026) without confirming this is the fixed annual date rather than this year's specific date. `releases_per_year: 1` is safe either way; the specific day is not.

_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Extends the South Africa pilot slice (`za-cpi-social-grants.json`) after Thomas asked for three things: more nodes generally, whether any top-level node connects internationally, and how municipalities/provinces/national government actually relate. All sources below were fetched and read directly this session, not taken from `country afrikans.docx` (which does not cover fiscal federalism or international CPI standards at all -- this is new ground, not verification of an existing docx entry). Sitting in src/data/research/ alongside the existing za slice pending review, matching that file's current location rather than the EU/proposals/ convention its own header describes (the header may be stale -- worth checking with Thomas).
_note: Three findings worth stating plainly. (1) International connections are real and multiple: Stats SA's own CPI Sources and Methods document states outright that the CPI follows the IMF-ILO-OECD-Eurostat-UNECE-World Bank 2020 CPI Manual, adopted COICOP 2018 as its actual classification structure (not a side series -- this is the live basket structure since January 2025), and complies with the IMF's SDDS. All three are national-side statements, not inferred. (2) SARB's inflation target is explicitly defined in terms of Stats SA's CPI ('the headline change in the consumer price index, as calculated by Statistics South Africa') -- the same shape as the Canada/US 'CPI sets the policy rate' finding already in the graph. (3) Fiscal federalism has a real constitutional structure (Chapter 13: national/provincial/municipal equitable shares, given annual effect by the Division of Revenue Act) but it does NOT touch social grants. Grant amounts move through the National Revenue Fund directly under the Social Assistance Act's own Gazette-notice power (already documented in za-cpi-social-grants.json) -- DoRA's own conditional-grant schedules (read directly this session: infrastructure, health facilities, human settlements, roads, transport, school backlogs) do not name social assistance at all. The equitable share machinery exists for education, health, housing, roads and municipal free-basic-services -- not for the grant system this corpus is tracking. That absence is itself the finding, filed the same way the CPI/Budget Review edge already handles an absent formula.

_open_questions.question: Constitution Schedule 4 lists 'Welfare services', 'Health services' and 'Population development' as concurrent national/provincial competences, and DSD's own legislative-mandate page cites Schedule 4 alongside s.27(1)(c) as a second, distinct constitutional basis for its work -- separate from the national, exclusive cash-grant power in the Social Assistance Act. This looks like a real, documented distinction (grants vs. services) but no provincial Department of Social Development document was fetched this session to give Schedule 4 a concrete outgoing edge, so it was left out of `reports` rather than minted as a dangling node. Next session: fetch one provincial DSD annual report or budget vote (Free State's socdev.fs.gov.za and the National Treasury ENE Vote 19 Social Development document both turned up in search but were not read) to anchor this properly.

SARB's own monetary-policy page states the mandate is 'set out in the Constitution' but doesn't quote the South African Reserve Bank Act itself. The Act's actual inflation-targeting clause (if the target itself is statutory rather than a Minister-SARB agreement, which is the more likely structure per other inflation-targeting central banks) was not fetched this session.

National Treasury publishes an annual Estimates of National Expenditure, Vote 19: Social Development -- department-level budget detail distinct from both the aggregate Budget Review (already in the graph) and SASSA's own Annual Report (already in the graph). Turned up in search, not fetched. Likely candidate for a `calculated_from` or `cites` edge to za-social-assistance-act-2004 and/or za-national-treasury-budget-review, but the actual relationship between ENE and the Budget Review numbers was not verified this session.

reports.title: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996 — Chapter 13 (Finance)
reports.description: The constitutional basis for how revenue is split among South Africa's three spheres of government. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. s.213: money raised nationally goes into the National Revenue Fund, and 'a province's equitable share of revenue raised nationally' is 'a direct charge against the National Revenue Fund'. s.214(1)(a): 'An Act of Parliament must provide for... the equitable division of revenue raised nationally among the national, provincial and local spheres of government'; s.214(2) lists the factors that Act must weigh, including provinces' and municipalities' ability to 'provide basic services' and 'fiscal capacity and efficiency'. s.226 gives each province its own Revenue Fund; s.227(1)(a) entitles local government and provinces to 'an equitable share of revenue raised nationally... to provide basic services'. ss.228-229 give provinces and municipalities limited own-revenue powers (no income tax, VAT or customs duty for either).

reports.title: Division of Revenue Act 24 of 2024
reports.publisher: Parliament of South Africa / National Treasury
reports.description: The annual Act that gives effect to s.214(1)(a)'s mandate -- the actual instrument dividing nationally raised revenue among national, provincial and local government for a given financial year, plus a set of conditional grants to provinces and municipalities. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (National Treasury's own gazetted copy). Its Schedules 4-7, read directly, list conditional grants including the Education Infrastructure Grant, Health Facility Revitalisation Grant, Human Settlements Development Grant, Provincial Roads Maintenance Grant, Public Transport Operations/Network Grants, School Infrastructure Backlogs Grant, Urban Settlements Development Grant and disaster-response allocations. Social assistance/grants are not named anywhere in the Act -- the cash-grant system this corpus tracks runs through the National Revenue Fund directly under the Social Assistance Act's own Gazette-notice power (s.32(3), already in za-cpi-social-grants.json), not through DoRA's conditional-grant machinery. Worth stating precisely rather than assumed: this is a real absence, checked directly, not an oversight in scope.

entries.covers: Division of Revenue Act 24 of 2024 (for FY2024/25) — assented 28 May 2024, gazetted 3 Jun 2024 (GG 50743)
Division of Revenue Act 2 of 2025 (for FY2025/26) — gazetted 8 Aug 2025 (GG 53139)
Division of Revenue Act for FY2026/27 — Bill (B5-2026) tabled in Parliament 25 Feb 2026 alongside the Budget; corresponding Act not yet confirmed gazetted as of 11 Aug 2026

release_schedule.note: The Division of Revenue Act is passed annually by Parliament (National Treasury/Budget process) to allocate nationally raised revenue among national, provincial and local government, as required by s214 of the Constitution. There is no fixed statutory assent date — the Bill is normally tabled with the annual Budget (historically February), but final Act signing/gazetting has varied widely: Act 24 of 2024 (FY2024/25) was assented 28 May 2024 (delayed by the May 2024 general election); Act 2 of 2025 (FY2025/26) was only gazetted 8 Aug 2025 (delayed by the 2025 Budget-tabling dispute over VAT). Each main Act has also been followed later in its fiscal year by a Division of Revenue Amendment Act tied to the Adjustments Appropriation process (Amendment Act 48 of 2024 on 24 Dec 2024; Amendment Act 12 of 2025 on 11 Feb 2026). For FY2026/27, Division of Revenue Bill B5-2026 was tabled 25 Feb 2026, but no corresponding Act appears yet in the government gazette index as of 11 Aug 2026, so its exact enactment date is not yet knowable — only that it is expected sometime in 2026 based on the established annual pattern.

reports.title: National Framework for Municipal Indigent Policies
reports.publisher: Department of Provincial and Local Government (now COGTA)
reports.description: The national policy framework municipalities build their own indigent/free-basic-services policies on (confirmed as the pattern by three individual municipal indigent policies found in search -- eThekwini, Govan Mbeki, George -- though only this national framework document was fetched and read directly). VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session: 'This policy framework provides a basis for the provision of free basic services to the indigent... The policy needs to be applied in conjunction with the equitable share policy being prepared by National Treasury', and the local government equitable share is described as 'an important component of the funding to be used to subsidise the provision of free basic services to the indigent'. No formula ties a specific equitable-share rand amount to a specific municipality's free-basic-services spend in this document -- it names the equitable share as the intended funding source, not a computed input -- so the edge below is filed as `cites`, matching the same caution already used for the Budget Review -> CPI edge in za-cpi-social-grants.json.

reports.title: Monetary Policy (Inflation-Targeting Framework)
reports.description: SARB's inflation-targeting framework and the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) that sets the repo rate. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (SARB's own site): 'The SARB's mandate, set out in the Constitution, requires it to protect the value of the rand in the interest of balanced and sustainable growth... The inflation target is 3% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 1 percentage point. This target refers to the headline change in the consumer price index, as calculated by Statistics South Africa.' The exact statutory clause in the South African Reserve Bank Act itself was not fetched this session (see _open_questions) -- SARB's own page cites the Constitution, not the Act, as the mandate's source.
reports.cadence_note: MPC meets six times a year (confirmed via SARB's own public MPC-dates communications, not the monetary-policy page itself). Repo rate changes only on decision dates, so this is publication cadence, not a claim about how often the rate actually moves.

entries.covers: MPC interest rate decision / statement, September 2026
MPC interest rate decision / statement, November 2026

release_schedule.note: SARB's monetary policy page lists upcoming MPC announcement dates under 'Upcoming Announcements'; as of 2026-08-11 it shows 23 September 2026 and 19 November 2026 as the next two MPC decision dates. The page also restates that the MPC meets six times a year and the SARB publicly announces the policy rate every two months, consistent with the existing releases_per_year=6 and cadence_note on file. A dedicated MPC-dates subpage (e.g. /mpc-meeting-dates) returned 404, so this finding relies on the dates listed directly on the monetary-policy landing page.

reports.title: Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP 2018)
reports.description: The UN's standard classification for household consumption expenditure. Deliberately not minted for the Canada or US CPI slices already in the graph (`international-frameworks.json`'s own dropped notes: StatCan's CPI never uses COICOP at all, and BLS only produces a COICOP mapping as a side series for the OECD, not something the headline release rests on -- 'It should return if a document is found where COICOP governs a primary release.'). South Africa is that document: Stats SA's own CPI Sources and Methods report states 'The South African CPI adopted the 2018 version of the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP) for goods and services with effect from the January 2025 publication' -- COICOP 2018 is the actual basket structure of the live release, not a side output.
reports.cadence_note: Revised on a multi-decade cycle (prior editions predate 2018 by a similar span to SNA's revision cadence); not an annual release.

release_schedule.note: Next revision is contingent on the outcome of the separate COFOG revision process (targeted 2028) rather than its own independent schedule.

reports.title: IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS)
reports.description: The IMF's voluntary standard for the coverage, periodicity, timeliness and advance-release-calendar practices of a country's official statistics. A parallel edge for Canada (`statcan-cpi -> imf-sdds-plus`, the stricter SDDS Plus tier) was scoped and dropped in `international-frameworks.json` for lack of national-side evidence -- every document naming the obligation was IMF-side, none from StatCan itself. South Africa has the national-side evidence Canada's case lacked: Stats SA's own CPI Sources and Methods report states plainly, 'The South African CPI complies with the IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS)' -- the plain SDDS tier, not SDDS Plus, and not independently checked against South Africa's actual IMF DSBB country page this session (that page's landing view did not surface country-specific content when fetched directly).
reports.cadence_note: Standard itself revised rarely; not an annual release.

release_schedule.note: Framework reviewed 'at intervals determined by the Executive Board' — no fixed periodicity. Last review concluded 2022-03-16 per the IMF's own site. This report's own url field previously pointed to a Statistics South Africa PDF with no connection to the IMF — corrected here to the DSBB SDDS overview page. (Note: the za-statssa-cpi -> imf-sdds edge's evidence_url, the same statssa PDF, is left as-is — that citation is correct evidence for that specific edge's claim.)

dependencies.basis: DoRA is the Act s.214(1)(a) requires Parliament to pass each year; its allocation is required to weigh the factors s.214(2) lists (basic-services capacity, fiscal capacity and efficiency, economic disparities). The Constitution supplies the criteria the annual Act's formula must apply, not a computed figure itself.

The framework names the local government equitable share (s.227(1)(a)) as the intended funding source for free basic services to the indigent, but states it is 'to be applied in conjunction with' equitable share policy rather than computed from a stated formula in this document -- filed as `cites`, same caution as the existing za-national-treasury-budget-review -> za-statssa-cpi edge.

SARB's own page: the inflation target 'refers to the headline change in the consumer price index, as calculated by Statistics South Africa' -- the repo-rate decision is defined directly in terms of Stats SA's CPI print, not merely informed by it. Same shape as the Bank of Canada / CPI edge already in the graph.

_note: The most structurally important thing here isn't any single node -- it's that South Africa finally gets a genuine provincial-level node (za-western-cape-dsd-app, jurisdiction_level: provincial). Every South African node minted so far, across three prior draft files, was federal. This is the first one that answers the original 'does it run top to bottom' question with an actual document rather than a gap. Also worth flagging: the SARB inflation target turns out to have the same shape as the grant system and the UIF benefit scale -- not written into primary legislation at all, but set by an intergovernmental agreement (Minister of Finance + SARB Governor). That's now three separate South African mechanisms (grants, UIF, and now monetary policy) that could each sound like a hard rule from the outside but are actually discretionary instruments dressed as numbers. Worth stating as a pattern, not just three separate findings.

release_schedule.note: No fixed statutory date or published multi-year calendar found. The Estimates of National Expenditure (including all Vote chapters such as Vote 19: Social Development) are released by National Treasury on the same day as the annual National Budget Speech to Parliament, which by strong convention falls in February (usually a Wednesday in the second half of the month: 23 Feb 2022, 22 Feb 2023, 21 Feb 2024, 25 Feb 2026). 2025 was an anomaly: originally scheduled for 19 Feb 2025, the budget was twice postponed amid a VAT-increase dispute within the coalition government and was ultimately tabled on 21 May 2025. Absent a confirmed 2027 date, the projection is for February 2027, consistent with the pre-2025 and 2026 pattern, but the exact day is not yet announced by Treasury as of 2026-08-11.

reports.title: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996 — Schedule 4 (Functional Areas of Concurrent National and Provincial Legislative Competence)
reports.description: Lists 'Welfare services', 'Health services' and 'Population development' among the functional areas both national and provincial legislatures may make law on -- a genuinely separate constitutional basis from the national, exclusive cash-grant power under s.27(1)(c)/the Social Assistance Act (already in the graph). The National DSD Annual Report states this directly: 'Schedule 4 of the Constitution further identifies welfare services, population development and disaster management as functional areas of concurrent national and provincial legislative competence.' release_schedule.rule: Public Finance Management Act, 1999 (Act No. 1 of 1999): the accounting officer must submit the department's annual report (with audited financial statements) to the relevant treasury and Auditor-General within five months after the end of a financial year (s.40(1)(c)-(d)); the executive authority must then table the annual report in the National Assembly within one month after receiving the auditor's report, and in any event not later than six months after the end of the financial year (s.65).

No DSD-specific published release calendar was found; the date above is the PFMA s.65 outer-limit deadline (6 months after FY end) computed from the current 2025/26 fiscal year end (31 March 2026), not a date the department itself published. In practice, South African national departments' annual reports are typically tabled in Parliament in September following the March fiscal year-end.

RE-CITED 2026-09-05 (Round C): the gov.za media statement previously cited never mentions the Constitution (round 5's Section 224 quote came from the Constitution itself). The SARB's own monetary-policy page — the source node's url — states the constitutional mandate in its own words; cited and quoted from there instead. This resolves the open question left in za-fiscal-federalism.json about the SARB's statutory basis: the 3% (±1pp) numerical target itself is NOT written into the South African Reserve Bank Act 90 of 1989 (which only carries the older 'protect the value of the currency' language) -- it was set by a 2025 agreement between the Minister of Finance and the SARB Governor ('The Minister of Finance today announced a new inflation target for South Africa of 3% with a 1 percentage point tolerance band. This decision follows agreement between the Governor of the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) and the Minister.'). A third South African mechanism, after grants (Gazette notice) and UIF (Gazette notice), that turns out to be discretionary/agreement-based rather than a hard statutory formula.

_note: This is the strongest positive municipal-level finding of the batch, and by a wide margin. South Africa's municipal budgeting system explicitly and repeatedly ties itself to StatsSA's CPI: the City of Johannesburg's own 2026/27-2028/29 MTREF budget book states it is 'projecting CPI at 3.4 per cent for the 2026/27 financial year... CPI averaged 3.2 per cent in 2025 (StatsSA)', ties minor-service tariff increases and property-rates revenue growth directly to that projected figure, and pegs collective-bargained wage increases to 'the average CPI for the period... The source of CPI data is StatsSA' (with a 4-7% collar). This traces to a real institutional chain, not a coincidence: National Treasury's own annual MFMA budget circulars (independently located and opened, not just cited secondhand) mandate the CPI benchmark and the wording Johannesburg's budget book uses ('required to justify all increases more than CPI') is close to verbatim from Circular 129/132's own language. The one genuine gap: the City's own Property Rates Policy document, searched in full, contains no CPI clause at all -- the annual percentage increase is set separately each year in the budget book/Council resolution, not in the Policy. City Power's own site could not be reached (persistent SSL/robots errors) so its tariff document's CPI basis, if any, is unverified rather than denied.

_note: Two of the three findings here are the SNA-2008 and ICLS pattern repeating cleanly for a third country (Canada, US, now South Africa). The third is different in kind: the Unemployment Insurance Act's own Gazette-notice power (s.12(3)(a)) benchmarks itself against an ILO Convention by name -- a genuine treaty-level international reference sitting inside ordinary domestic labour legislation, not a statistical methodology citation. Checked separately whether South Africa has actually ratified that Convention (it has not, per the ILO's own March 2026 workshop article -- still assessing feasibility), which matters for how the edge should be read: this is a domestic statute citing an unratified international benchmark voluntarily, not a treaty obligation. Filed as `cites` rather than `methodology_depends_on` for that reason -- it's a reference point for a discretionary ministerial power, not a rule the benefit calculation is derived from.

_open_questions.question: The QLFS technical note found this session states the questionnaire was revised in Q3 2025 'to adhere to the most recent international labour statistics standards' (citing the 19th/20th/21st ICLS by name), and separately states this revision 'does not affect the measurement or definition of employment and unemployment.' That's good evidence the questionnaire follows ICLS, but doesn't by itself confirm the core definitions of employed/unemployed were ever explicitly adopted from ICLS/ILO (as opposed to being a South Africa-specific definition that happens to be broadly compatible). reports.title: Quarterly Labour Force Survey (P0211)
reports.description: South Africa's official quarterly labour force survey -- the source of the headline unemployment rate. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (the Q1 2026 release's own technical notes): the questionnaire 'was revised in Q3: 2025 in order to adhere to the most recent international labour statistics standards', naming the 19th ICLS (statistics on work, employment and labour underutilisation), 20th ICLS (statistics on work relationships) and 21st ICLS (statistics on the informal economy) by number. The same document also states the revision 'does not affect the measurement or definition of employment and unemployment' -- so headline definitions predate and are not derived from this specific revision. Following this ~3-month pattern (mid-Feb, mid-May, mid-Aug, mid-Nov), Q3 2026 is expected to be released in mid-November 2026; exact day not confirmed so month-level precision is used.

reports.title: Unemployment Insurance Act 63 of 2001
reports.description: The statute governing UIF short-term unemployment benefits, run by the Department of Employment and Labour (distinct from SASSA/DSD's social grants). VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session: benefits are calculated on a sliding Income Replacement Rate against prior daily income (Schedule 2), 'The maximum IRR is fixed at 60%. The minimum IRR is currently set at 38%', with a flat benefit above a transition income level. Confirms the same discretionary-adjustment pattern already found for social grants in za-social-assistance-act-2004: s.12(3)(a) lets 'the Minister... with the concurrence of the Minister of Finance, by notice in the Gazette... amend the scale of benefits contained in Schedule 3 in accordance with a maximum monthly rate of remuneration of a skilled manual labourer as determined by the Social Security (Minimum Standards) Convention, [1952 per ILO's own designation; the Act text as extracted this session reads '1953' -- see _open_questions, not resolved]'. No automatic CPI-indexation clause found in the Act for either benefit amounts or the contribution ceiling.

reports.title: Social Security (Minimum Standards) Convention, 1952 (No. 102)
reports.description: The ILO's foundational treaty setting minimum standards across nine branches of social security, including unemployment benefit. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session that South Africa has NOT ratified this Convention -- the ILO's own site (March 2026 workshop article) describes South Africa as still assessing the feasibility of ratification against a comparative legal analysis, not as a ratifying state. The Unemployment Insurance Act nonetheless names it by name as the benchmark for the Minister's discretionary Gazette-notice power to adjust the benefit scale (s.12(3)(a)) -- a domestic statute voluntarily referencing an unratified international instrument as a reference point, not a treaty-driven obligation. Filed with an INT country code and international jurisdiction level per the schema's existing convention for standards bodies.
reports.cadence_note: A single 1952 instrument, not revised since; releases_per_year is nominal so the pulse rate reads as near-static, matching the treatment of sna-2008 and the cpi-manual node.

release_schedule.note: This is the text of an ILO Convention (a treaty adopted in 1952, still in force) — a one-off foundational legal instrument, not a recurring statistical/government publication. The convention text itself is not re-released on any cadence. What does recur is member states' Article 22 reporting obligation: ratifying states must submit periodic reports on measures taken to give effect to the Convention, and per ILO's supervisory system, Convention 102 is classified as a 'technical convention', so reports are formally called for on a 6-year cycle, staggered across 6 alphabetical groups of member states (so different countries report on C102 in different years). There is no single global 'next release' date this produces — it's a rolling, country-by-country reporting obligation, not a dated publication event. Treating this corpus entry as having a fixed releases_per_year is therefore not really meaningful; it should probably be flagged as irregular/non-recurring rather than assigned a numeric cadence.

Whether the programme runs on policy/administrative authority alone (as Eswatini's Old Age Grant does, per sz-worldbank-social-assistance-2021) or has an unfound legal basis was not checked further.

reports.title: The Monthly (Consumer Price Index bulletin)
reports.description: Zambia's official monthly Consumer Price Index bulletin, branded 'The Monthly "Quality Statistics for Development"'. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via Volume 278 (May 2026): base period '2009 = 100'; released 'on the last Thursday of each month'; main expenditure groups named include Food and Non-alcoholic Beverages, Housing/Water/Electricity, Transport, Communication and Education. Thinner methodology documentation than Botswana's, Eswatini's or Lesotho's equivalents: the bulletin does not state the weights survey's name or year, does not explicitly name COICOP, and does not state an index formula (see _open_questions) -- the same kind of documentation gap already logged for Namibia (G.7) and, this session, Malawi and Zimbabwe.

reports.title: Social Cash Transfer Factsheet
reports.publisher: Republic of Zambia, Ministry of Community Development and Social Services
reports.description: The Zambian government's own factsheet on its Social Cash Transfer programme. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Transfer amounts are stated as fixed nominal figures: 'Beneficiary households are entitled to 200 Kwacha per month which they receive every two months as a sum of 400 Kwacha,' and 'Beneficiary households with a member with severe disability receive double the amount, i.e., 400 Kwacha per month and 800 Kwacha every two months.' No statement anywhere in the factsheet about indexation to inflation, the Consumer Price Index, or any periodic review procedure -- the amounts are presented as static figures with no stated mechanism for change.

_dropped.why: The factsheet states transfer amounts as fixed Kwacha figures with no adjustment mechanism of any kind named -- no CPI reference, no periodic-review clause, nothing. A January 2024 news report (Lusaka Times) shows beneficiaries themselves requesting increases on adequacy grounds, with no government response describing an existing formula.

_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Zimbabwe is part of the AF branch's Southern Africa expansion (G.7-G.8), and closes out the docx's original Southern Africa list (South Africa, Botswana, Namibia, Lesotho, Eswatini, Zambia, Malawi, Zimbabwe -- all eight now researched as of this session). No raw docx entries exist for this country; every document below was located and verified from scratch this session via WebSearch + WebFetch, no import round used. Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review, following the established DRAFT-then-import pattern.
_note: Zimbabwe's CPI methodology proved the hardest to document in this batch: ZIMSTAT's own CPI PDF releases failed to fetch twice (proxy/gateway errors, not a content-access refusal), a UNECE conference paper on the same topic returned a 403, and an IMF technical assistance report on national accounts mentioned the CPI only in passing. What is documented instead is a genuinely distinctive structural fact unique to Zimbabwe in this corpus so far: following the April 2024 introduction of the Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG) currency, ZIMSTAT publishes three parallel CPI series -- a ZiG index, a US dollar index, and a 'Blended Index' -- rather than the single series every other AF country publishes. On the social-protection side, no primary NSSA document was fetched this session (nssa.org.zw itself was not reached); the evidence is two news reports describing NSSA's 2026 pension increases as explicitly discretionary and ad hoc -- 'we increased by 100 percent in April, with further increases expected in July and October' toward a stated target of 'US$60 equivalent' monthly payouts, described as 'interim relief' while NSSA 'is assessing its capacity to implement a long-term pension adjustment.' Neither article is minted as a node (secondary reporting on an announcement, not a document another document names as an input), but the language -- interim relief, capacity assessment for a future long-term mechanism -- reads as the same recommendation-reveals-absence shape found explicitly in Botswana's, Malawi's and Tanzania's own primary documents, now corroborated by press coverage rather than a government document directly.

_open_questions.question: No weights survey, base year, COICOP classification or index formula was confirmed for Zimbabwe's CPI this session. ZIMSTAT's own PDF releases (zimstat.co.zw/wp-content/uploads/...) failed with proxy/gateway errors on two separate URLs and dates; a UNECE conference paper on Zimbabwe's cost-of-living indices (presented Geneva, April 2021) returned a 403. Worth a retry from a session whose tooling can reach zimstat.co.zw's PDF hosting, or via an alternative mirror (IMF Article IV consultation statistical annexes sometimes reproduce national CPI methodology in full).

The National Social Security Authority's own founding legislation (the NSSA Act) was not located or fetched this session -- only news coverage of a 2026 discretionary pension increase. nssa.org.zw itself was found in search but not fetched. This would be the natural primary source for whether any adjustment mechanism is written into NSSA's statute, the same kind of check already done for Tanzania's PSSSF Act and Namibia's National Pensions Act.

Zimbabwe's multi-currency CPI structure (ZiG/USD/Blended) is itself a documented methodological fact but its implications for benefit-setting -- e.g. whether NSSA pensions are set/paid in ZiG, USD, or a blend, and against which of the three CPI series any future 'long-term pension adjustment' mechanism might be benchmarked -- was not explored this session.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Zimbabwe's official monthly Consumer Price Index release. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session only as to structure, not full methodology: ZIMSTAT publishes 'three price indices' following the April 2024 introduction of the Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG) currency -- 'the ZiG index, US dollars Index and the Blended Index' -- with the ZiG series' own index reference period stated as 'April 2024' and month-on-month/year-on-year ZiG rates beginning May 2024 and April 2025 respectively, following 'international recommended methods' (unspecified beyond that phrase). ZIMSTAT's site lists monthly releases in both ZWG and USD through at least May 2026 and a 'July 2026 Price Statistics Release' covering 'inflation, poverty lines, producer prices, and construction-related price indices'. No weights survey, COICOP classification or elementary/aggregate index formula was confirmed this session -- see _open_questions; this is the thinnest-documented CPI methodology in the AF branch so far.

release_schedule.note: ZIMSTAT publishes a monthly 'Price Statistics Release' covering CPI/inflation. No formal release calendar is posted on the website (checked https://www.zimstat.co.zw/consumer-price-index/ and https://www.zimstat.co.zw/price-indices/, neither lists forward dates). Observed past releases cluster in the last week of the same reference month (day ~27-30), e.g. the 'JULY 2026 PRICE STATISTICS RELEASE' covering July 2026 inflation was issued Mon 28 Jul 2026 (per ZIMSTAT press-release archive, and corroborated by Xinhua/NewZimbabwe/allAfrica coverage same day). This supports the existing releases_per_year=12 on file; next release (August 2026 data) is an inferred date based on this monthly end-of-month pattern, not a published date.
